program: B Tech (All Program except CSBS, CSDS,CSDS- 311) /MBA Tech (All Program)
objectives: The main objective of this course is to equip the students with the ability to solve, assemble and test simple AC and DC electrical circuits. Further, the course also enables the student to obtain a basic understanding of the working principle and applications of electronics devices.

outcomes.text: Interpret DC circuits, theorems and time domain analysis of first order RL circuit
Solve series and parallel AC circuits and compare star/delta configurations
Explain the principles of transformer and electrical machines
Understand the construction, working principle and applications of electronics devices and logic circuits

units.title: DC Circuits
units.text: DC Circuits Electrical circuit elements (R, L and C), voltage and current sources, Kirchhoff’s current law, Kirchhoff’s voltage laws, Analysis of simple circuits with dc excitation, Superposition Theorem, Thevenin’s Theorems, Norton’s Theorems. Time-domain analysis of first-order RL circuits.

units.title: AC Circuits
units.text: AC Circuits Generation of alternating emf, instantaneous, rms, peak, average values and related other terms, vector representation of AC quantities, Steady state analysis of R, L, C series and parallel circuits, resonance. Generation of three-phase emf, star connection, delta connection, relationship between line and phase quantities.

units.title: Transformers and Electrical Machines
units.text: Transformers and Electrical Machines Construction and working of single-phase transformer Ideal and practical transformer, equivalent circuit, Losses in transformers, Generation of rotating magnetic fields, Construction and working of a three-phase induction motor, Single-phase induction motor, construction and working, DC motor construction, working and types.

units.title: Analog Electronics (no mathematical treatment and design)
units.text: Analog Electronics (no mathematical treatment and design) Half and full wave rectifiers, special purpose diodes -zener regulator, BJT and its applications, amplifier, oscillator, overview of opto-electronics devices, opto- couplers, concepts of transducer, Operational amplifier (IC-741), Inverting and Non-Inverting, Comparator, Timer (IC-555) and multivibrators.

units.title: Digital Electronics
units.text: Digital Electronics Logic gates, concept of universal logic; implementation of Boolean expressions using logic gates, application of digital circuits: e.g., adder, subtractor, multiplexer, de-multiplexer, Analog to Digital Converter, Digital to Analog Converter.

program: B Tech (All Program except CSBS, CSDS,CSDS-311) /MBA Tech (All Program)/B Tech Integrated (Mechanical/Computer)
objectives: The objective of this course is to understand the concept of Design thinking through engaging the students in projects/ assignments that illustrate the various pillars of Design thinking. Imbibe the higher order skill of Design thinking which they will be able to apply in various projects during their course, to create new products & services.

outcomes.text: Develop a human-centric approach towards problem solving
Apply design thinking principles to come up with innovative solutions to problems and challenges

units.text: Introduction to Design Thinking -Design Thinking as ‘Experience Innovation’ - Concepts of Customer Desirability, Technological Feasibility, Business Viability and their significance

units.title: Case Study
units.text: Case Study: Discussion on HBR article Design Thinking by Tim Brown (Pre-Read based analysis of all four case studies covered in article)
Mindset Creation - Growth Mindset vs. Fixed Mindset - Essential elements of Design Thinking Mindset - Case Study: Jeff Bezos-Amazon’s approach of being Customer Obsessed
- Pillars of Design Thinking - Introduction to Stages of Design Thinking based on Stanford d. School

units.title: Case Study for Application of Design Thinking
units.text: Case Study for Application of Design Thinking IDEO Shopping Cart (Case Video followed by debrief/class discussion)
Empathy [A] -Introduction to empathy -Decoding Customer Behaviour using DT (using case study method)

Empathy [B] -Tools:Understanding Consumer’s Unmet Needs & Pain Points: (Observation, Focused Interviews, Shadowing, Journey Mapping) - Rules and tips for each specific tool (Class activity based learning for each tool)

units.title: Empathy [C]
units.text: Empathy [C] Debrief of Class Activity for Journey Mapping Empathy Case Study: ‘Embrace- Infant Incubator’

Define -Analysis of data gathered from Empathy stage through tools like Clustering & Affinity Diagrams -Building Problem Statements & understanding POV -Tools: Framing problems as ‘How Might We?’ questions
Ideate -Concept of Semi-structured approach to Ideation in DT -Rules of Ideation -Tools: Brainstorming, Brainwriting, Dot Voting
Ideate -Class Activity to demonstrate Brainstorming & Dot Voting - Case Study for Out of the Box Idea Generation: Steelcase

Prototype -Introduction to concept of prototyping & basic techniques of rapid prototyping -Introduction to Low fidelity vs. High fidelity prototypes and their significance in the Design Thinking process -General information on user testing & MVPs - Case Study for Prototyping & User Testing: Nordstorm Innovation Lab

units.title: Term End Group Project
units.text: Term End Group Project Analysis of Design Thinking success stories from across various domains – Students are expected to build a presentation based on the design thinking led success story of their chosen company/organization

text_books: 1. Idris Mootee , Design Thinking for Strategic Innovation, Wily, 2014.

program: B Tech (All Program except CSBS, CSDS-311 and Civil) and MBA Tech All Program
objectives: This course gives the basic working knowledge required for the production of various engineering products. It is the backbone of the real industrial environment which helps to develop and enhance relevant technical hand skills required by the engineer working in the various engineering industries and workshops.

outcomes.text: Identify correct testing instruments and tools for various tasks
Build PCB circuits using through hole and SMD components for small applications
Make use of required electrical components for building domestic wiring circuits
Assemble PC hardware and configure network topology

units.text: Familiarization and application of testing instruments and commonly used measuring instruments and tools Multimeter, Function generator, Power supply, Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO) etc. Soldering iron, De-soldering pump, Pliers, Cutters, Wire strippers, Tweezers, Crimping tool, Hot air soldering and de-soldering.

units.title: Printed circuit boards (PCB)
units.text: Printed circuit boards (PCB) Types, Single sided, Double sided, PTH, Processing methods, schematics design using open source software and fabrication of a single sided PCB for a simple circuit with manual etching (Ferric chloride) and drilling. Soldering and Joining Processes – Introduction, Techniques and circuit assembly. Assembling of electronic circuits using SMT (Surface Mount Technology) components/stations.

Study, demonstration and identification of common electrical materials such as wires, cables, switches, fuses and connectors Wiring of fan, tube light, two-way control (staircase wiring), Earthing- Need, objectives and types – Plate, Pipe, Rod and maintenance free earthing. Understanding of electric shock, understand rating and working of Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCB), Electric Leakage Circuit Breaker (ELCB), Residual Current Circuit Breaker (RCCB) and Fuse.

units.title: Introduction to PC Hardware
units.text: Introduction to PC Hardware – Assembly of I/O peripherals, memories and storage devices, Central Processing Unit (CPU), Graphic Processing Unit (GPU), and SMPS. LAN configuration using device (MAC) address, Switch/Hub configuration (4/8 port), router configuration using GSM. Study of ARDUINO boards (uno/mega), sensors – Temperature, Humidity, LDR, Smoke, Ultrasonic etc., Shields – Motor driver, wi-fi, IO, DC gear motors, Stepper motor.

text_books: 1. R.S. Khandpur, Printed Circuit Boards: Design, Fabrication, assembly and testing, 3rd ed. Tata McGraw Hill, , 2017. 2. Dan Gookin, Troubleshooting and maintaining your PC, 3rd ed., Wiley, 2017. 3. R.P. Singh, Electrical Workshop: Safety, Commissioning, maintenance and testing of electrical equipment, 3rd ed., IK International Publishing, 2012.
reference_books: 1. John H. Watt, Terrell Croft, American Electricians' Handbook: A Reference Book for the Practical Electrical Man, 9th ed., McGraw-Hill, 2018.
lab_work: 6 to 8 laboratory exercises (and a practicum) based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech Mechanical ,Civil/ Mechatronics
objectives: The aim is to acquaint students with engineering materials like lubricants, polymers, nanomaterials and composites. Also to familiarize them with the industrial importance of water chemistry, application of fuels and concept of metal corrosion.

outcomes.text: Rationalize fundamentals of corrosion and materials
Understand basic concepts in water, combustion of fuels and polymer chemistry
Solve numerical problems based on water, fuels and combustion, lubricants

units.title: Polymers
units.text: Polymers Introduction, basic concepts of degree of polymerization, tacticity, melting and glass transition temperature and its importance. Types of polymerization (Addition, condensation and co-polymerization). Smart polymer materials, conducting polymers, liquid crystals, applications of polymers.

units.title: Lubricants
units.text: Lubricants Definition, Mechanism of lubrication, Properties- viscosity, viscosity index, flash & fire, cloud & pour points, oiliness, saponification & acid value (numericals based on saponification and acid value)

units.title: Fuels & Combustion
units.text: Fuels & Combustion Discuss the definition, classification and characteristics. Calculation of Calorific value-Theoretical & Experimental method (Bomb calorimeter). Solid Fuels: Coal, proximate and ultimate analysis, Numerical based on analysis of coal. (Dulong’s formula) and bomb calorimetry. Combustion: calculation on air and oxygen requirement. Liquid fuels: Mining of Petroleum, Cracking, Reforming, Knocking in IC engines, Octane number, Cetane number & anti-knocking agents (TEL and MTBE) Gaseous fuel: (LPG, CNG) Composition, properties and application.

units.title: Water Chemistry
units.text: Water Chemistry Concept of hardness of water, types of hardness and its determination by EDTA methods, numerical based on water hardness. Water softening processes by: Lime-soda method, ion-exchange process and reverse osmosis process. Role of water as a universal solvent.

units.title: Chemistry of Corrosion and protection
units.text: Chemistry of Corrosion and protection Introduction, types of corrosion, chemical and electrochemical theories of Corrosion and their sub-types (corrosion by oxygen and other gases and liquids), factors affecting corrosion, preventive measures for corrosion-Cathodic and anodic protection methods, use of protective coatings (galvanization, tinning, metal cladding, electroplating, organic coatings like paints and varnishes).

units.title: Chemistry of Important Engineering Materials and Nanomaterials
units.text: Chemistry of Important Engineering Materials and Nanomaterials Introduction to alloys (steels, special steels, Carbon steel, brass, bronze and applications). Introduction to composites; Classification (Polymer, Metal & Ceramic composites, Cement), applications of composites. Introduction to nanomaterials, Structural features and properties of Nanomaterials, recent advances in nanomaterials, application of nano materials in catalysis, medicine, construction chemicals, paints and pigments and heat transfer fluids.

text_books: 1. Palanna. O.G., Engineering Chemistry, Tata McGraw Hill Education. Pvt. Ltd, 1st Edition 2009.
reference_books: 1. Advance Organic Chemistry, Jerry March,7th edition ,2013 2. P. W. Atkins, Physical Chemistry, ELBS/Oxford, 9th Edition, 2010. 3. Textbook of Nanoscience and Nanotechnology, B.S. Murty, P. Shankar, Baldev Raj, B B Rath, James Murday, Springer Science, 2013

program: B Tech (All Program except CSBS, CSDS-311) / MBA Tech (All Program)/ B Tech(Civil, Mechanical, CSEDS)
objectives: The knowledge of Physics relevant to engineering is critical for converting ideas into technology. An understanding of Physics also helps engineers understand the working and the limitations of existing devices and techniques, which eventually leads to new innovations and improvements. This course aims to make students understand the basic concepts of Physics thoroughly with a view to lay foundations for the various engineering courses.

outcomes.text: Relate and interpret the relationship and interaction between the nature and the matter with a scientific outlook
Identify and apply different processes of physics that have wide applications in industrial and technological sectors
Develop creative thinking, problem solving abilities and considerable scientific skills, viz. experimental, observational, manipulative, investigatory and decision making etc.

units.title: Semiconductors Physics
units.text: Semiconductors Physics Formation of energy bands and classification of solids into conductors, semiconductors and insulators, direct and indirect band gap semiconductors, fermi levels in semiconductor, energy gap and its temperature dependence, physics of semiconductor junction, hall effect and application.

units.title: Optics
units.text: Optics Interference: Thin film interference, wedge shaped film and Newton’s rings and their applications. Diffraction: Fraunhofer and Fresnel diffraction, Fraunhofer diffraction at single slit, double slit, and multiple slits, Characteristics of diffraction grating and its applications.

units.title: LASER and Fiber optics
units.text: LASER and Fiber optics Introduction to interaction of radiation with matter, Population inversion, pumping, various modes, threshold, population inversion, Solid state LASER, Semiconductor LASER, Gas LASER, applications of lasers. Introduction, optical fiber as a dielectric wave guide, total internal reflection, numerical aperture and various fiber parameters, losses associated with optical fibers, step and graded index fibers, application of optical fibers.

units.title: Electricity and Magnetism
units.text: Electricity and Magnetism Laws and applications of electrostatics and magnetostatics, Maxwell’s equations and applications, introduction to waveguides.

units.title: Nuclear and Plasma Physics
units.text: Nuclear and Plasma Physics Introduction to nuclear physics, types of nuclear reactions, nuclear fission as a source of energy, Particle accelerators: Cyclotron, Synchrotron, Nuclear radiation counters: Geiger Muller Counter, scintillation counter. Basic concepts of Plasma physics: Plasma as a state of matter, Debye length, plasma frequency, collisions, dc conductivity, ac conductivity Applications of plasma physics.

units.title: Modern Engineering materials
units.text: Modern Engineering materials (Introduction and basic properties of each material) Nanomaterials, Superconductors, Dielectrics, metallic glasses, biomaterials.

text_books: 1. H.K Malik and A.K. Singh, Engineering Physics, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Jearl Walker, David Halliday and Robert Resnick, Fundamentals of Physics, 10th edition, Wiley India, 2013. 2. James F.Shackelford and Madanapalli K. Muralidhara, Materials Science for Engineers, 7th edition, Pearson Education, 2006. 3. Francis F. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics, Springer, 2012.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course imparts basic knowledge of construction activities and their sequence, the process of concreting from manufacturing to finishing. It aims to compare various types of flooring and their applications in different scenarios

outcomes.text: Describe various construction activities and their sequence
Explain the process of concreting from manufacturing to finishing
Discuss various types of flooring and their applications

units.title: Excavation
units.text: Excavation Manual and mechanical method of Excavation, disposal of excavated material, dewatering of trenches, shoring and strutting of Trenches, precaution while excavation, fencing – caution signs.

units.title: Foundation
units.text: Foundation Necessity and Purpose of Foundation, Shallow Foundation, Spread foundation, raft foundation, deep foundation and its types, Precast concrete piles. Modern methods of pile installation.

units.title: Masonry
units.text: Masonry Terminology, Preparation, construction procedure, post construction precautions, brick masonry stretcher bond and half brick thick masonry, hollow and solid concrete block masonry, fixing of door and window frame in masonry, block masonry. Procedure of constructing un-coursed Rubble and coursed masonry. Pointing & Plastering Necessity and types, methods of providing pointing and plastering.

units.title: Formwork and Scaffolding
units.text: Formwork and Scaffolding Types, basic factors governing selection. Erecting and removal of formwork. Scaffolding types, precautions.

units.title: Concrete
units.text: Concrete Procedure of mixing concrete, manual and machine mixing, types of mixers, transporting, laying, compacting and curing of concrete, different types of vibrators, underwater concreting.

units.title: Floors
units.text: Floors Solid ground floor, plinth fillings, floor finish with murum, brick-bat concrete, Indian patent stone, cement tiles, China mosaic, floorings for special purposes such as factories, warehouses, stables, garages, railway platforms, upper floors: jack arch construction, mezzanine floors and lofts, false flooring for control rooms.

program: B Tech (All Program except CSBS, CSDS, CSDS-311) / MBA Tech (All Program)/ B Tech Integrated (Computer, Mechanical)
objectives: The principal objective of this course is to provide a basic understanding of biological mechanisms of living organisms from the perspective of engineers. To encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools. To make them aware of the application of engineering principles in biology and engineering robust solutions inspired by biological examples.

outcomes.text: Convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are diverse
Identify and classify microorganisms while understanding molecular basis of DNA as a genetic material for information transfer
Classify enzymes and distinguish between different mechanisms of enzyme action

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Convey that Biology is as important a scientific discipline as Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry Bring out the fundamental differences between science and engineering by drawing a comparison between eye and camera, Bird flying and aircraft. Mention the most exciting aspect of biology as an independent scientific discipline. Why we need to study biology? Discuss how biological observations of 18th Century that lead to major discoveries. Examples from - Brownian motion and the origin of thermodynamics by referring to the original observation of Robert Brown and Julius Mayor. These examples will highlight the fundamental importance of observations in any scientific inquiry.

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification Convey that classification per se is not what biology is all about. The underlying criterion, such as morphological, biochemical or ecological be highlighted. Hierarchy of life forms at phenomenological level. A common thread weaves this hierarchy Classification.Discuss classification based on (a) cellularity-Unicellular or multicellular (b) ultrastructure- prokaryotes or eucaryotes. (c) energy and Carbon utilization -Autotrophs, heterotrophs, lithotropes (d) Ammonia excretion - aminotelic, uricoteliec, ureotelic (e) Habitata- acquatic or terrestrial (e) Molecular taxonomy- three major kingdoms of life. A given organism can come under different category based on classification. Model organisms for the study of biology come from different groups. E.coli, S.cerevisiae, D. Melanogaster, C. elegance, A. Thaliana, M. musculus

units.title: Genetics
units.text: Genetics Convey that "Genetics is to biology what Newton's laws are to Physical Sciences" Mendel's laws, Concept of segregation and independent assortment. Concept of allele. Gene mapping, Gene interaction, Epistasis. Meiosis and Mitosis be taught as a part of genetics. Emphasis to be give not to the mechanics of cell division nor the phases but how genetic material passes from parent to offspring. Concepts of recessiveness and dominance. Concept of mapping of phenotype to genes. Discuss about the single gene disorders in humans. Discuss the concept of complementation using human genetics.

units.title: Biomolecules
units.text: Biomolecules Convey that all forms of life has the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are as diverse as one can imagine Molecules of life. In this context discuss monomeric units and polymeric structures. Discuss about sugars, starch and cellulose. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA. Two carbon units and lipids.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes Convey that without catalysis life would not have existed on earth Enzymology: How to monitor enzyme catalyzed reactions. How does an enzyme catalyze reactions. Enzyme classification. Mechanism of enzyme action. Discuss at least two examples. Enzyme kinetics and kinetic- parameters. Why should we know these parameters to understand biology? RNA catalysis.

units.title: Information Transfer
units.text: Information Transfer The molecular basis of coding and decoding genetic information is universal Molecular basis of information transfer. DNA as a genetic material. Hierarchy of DNA structure- from single stranded to double helix to nucleosomes. Concept of genetic code. Universality and degeneracy of genetic code. Define gene in terms of complementation and recombination.

units.title: Macromolecular analysis
units.text: Macromolecular analysis How to analyses biological processes at the reductionistic level Proteins- structure and function. Hierarch in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors and structural elements.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism The fundamental principles of energy transactions are the same in physical and biological world. Thermodynamics as applied to biological systems. Exothermic and endothermic versus endergonic and exergonic reactions. Concept of Keq and its relation to standard free energy. Spontaneity. ATP as an energy currency. This should include the breakdown of glucose to CO2 + H2O (Glycolysis and Krebs cycle) and synthesis of glucose from CO2 and H2O (Photosynthesis). Energy yielding and energy consuming reactions. Concept of Energy Charge.

units.title: Microbiology
units.text: Microbiology Concept of single celled organisms. Concept of species and strains. Identification and classification of microorganisms. Microscopy. Ecological aspects of single celled organisms. Sterilization and media compositions. Growth kinetics.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech (All Programs)
prerequisites: Knowledge of vector algebra, functions, limits, differentiation and integration of functions.
objectives: This course aims at providing adequate exposure to the theory and applications of Calculus. This course will help the students achieve sound understanding of the concepts of calculus, develop problem solving skills and apply the concepts and techniques of calculus to solve problems within Engineering domain. This course will equip the students with intermediate to advanced level concepts and aligned tools to help them tackle advanced mathematics and related applications.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental concepts of differential calculus for functions of one variable, including limits, derivatives, Mean Value Theorems, Taylor and Maclaurin series, and LHospital’s rule.

Solve problems involving functions of several variables using partial differentiation, Taylor series expansion, and techniques for finding maxima and minima, including Lagrange’s method of undetermined multipliers.
Use Beta and Gamma functions to solve problems in single-variable calculus.
Compute and interpret double and triple integrals, including change of variables and coordinate transformations, and apply them to determine areas and volumes.
Examine vector functions using gradient, divergence, curl, and scalar potential and apply fundamental vector calculus theorems such as Green’s, Stokes’, and Gauss’ theorems to evaluate integrals.
Integrate concepts from differential, integral, and vector calculus to formulate and solve real- world problems in physics, engineering, and applied sciences.

units.text: Partial Differentiation Functions of several variables: Limits and continuity, Partial differentiation, Taylor’s theorem of function of two variables Maxima, Minima, Lagrange’s Method of Undetermined Multiplier.

units.title: Integral Calculus of functions of one variable
units.text: Integral Calculus of functions of one variable Improper Integrals, Special functions: Beta and Gamma functions.

units.text: Multiple Integrals Double Integral, Change of order of Integration, Change of variables, Jacobian, Application of Double Integral to find area. Triple Integral, Change of variable to spherical and cylindrical co- ordinates, Application of Triple Integral to find volume.

units.title: Vector Calculus
units.text: Vector Calculus Gradient, Directional Derivative, Divergence, Curl, Scalar Potential, Line Integral, Surface Integral. Greens Theorem, Stokes Theorem and Gauss Divergence Theorem.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech (All Program)
objectives: The knowledge of Physics relevant to engineering is critical for converting ideas into technology. An understanding of Physics also helps engineers understand the working and the limitations of existing devices and techniques, eventually leading to innovations and improvements. This course aims to help students understand the basic concepts of physics thoroughly and lay the foundations for the various engineering courses.

outcomes.text: Describe the fundamental properties of semiconductors and elucidate the operational principles of semiconductor devices.
Apply interference and diffraction principles to analyze optical phenomena and diffraction grating applications.
Explain the working principles of LASER technology and fiber optics, and apply them to real-world communication and engineering problems.
Interpret the concepts of gradient, divergence, and curl in scalar and vector fields, and recognize their applications in basic engineering problems related to electromagnetism.
Explore the properties and applications of modern engineering materials like nanomaterials, superconductors, and dielectrics.
Gauge theoretical principles through laboratory experimentation, enhancing problem- solving abilities and technical proficiency in modern physics applications.

objectives: To introduce students to modern biology with an emphasis on the evolution of biology as a multi- disciplinary field, to make them aware of the application of engineering principles in biology. Describe the mechanisms of enzyme action, enzyme-substrate interactions, and enzyme inhibition, and discuss their industrial and biological applications.
Explain the principles of metabolism and energy transactions, and categorize microorganisms based on their characteristics, growth kinetics, and applications in biotechnology and drug discovery.

outcomes.text: Recall the historical evolution of India’s democratic values, emphasizing the foundational principles of justice, equality, and liberty as enshrined in the Preamble of the Constitution.

Understand the fundamental rights enshrined in the Constitution, their permissible restrictions, and how these rights are balanced with duties, to grasp their application within societal and professional frameworks.
Apply the knowledge of the structure of India's polity and the role of the Judiciary in maintaining the basic structure of the Constitution in real-world professional contexts.

units.text: Nature, Characteristics, and Sources of the Indian Constitution

Fundamental rights and Fundamental duties – Concept of State, Right to Equality under Articles 14 and 15, Right to certain freedoms under Article 19, Right to Life and liberty under Article 21, Right to religion under Article 25 and 26, Right to remedy under Article 32 and Fundamental duties
Indian Judiciary – Concept of Supreme Court and High Courts, Appointment of Judges, Independence of Judiciary, Jurisdictions of Supreme Court and High Courts
Emergency Provisions – Concept of National Emergency under Article 352, Financial Emergency under Article 360 and President rule under Article 356 of the Constitution

program: B Tech Civil/Mechanical
objectives: This course examines the basic nature of reasoning and the fallacies which prevent good reasoning and decision making. Both the theory and practice of critical thinking are covered. Emphasis will be on understanding the logical structure of an argument and on recognizing the influence of bias and emotional persuasion on decision making.

Recognise, build and appraise arguments
Analyse contexts effectively

program: B Tech and MBA Tech (All Programs)
objectives: The main objective of this course is to equip the students with the ability to solve, assemble and test simple AC and DC electrical circuits. Further, the course also enables the student to obtain a basic understanding of the working principle and applications of electronics devices.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental concepts of DC circuits, including Kirchhoff’s laws and network theorems, (Understand- Level 2)
Interpret the principles of AC circuit analysis, including resonance and three-phase systems, (Understand- Level 2)
Illustrate the working principles of transformers and different types of electrical machines, (Understand- Level 2)
Explain the basic operation of analog electronic components, including rectifiers, transistors and operational amplifiers. (Understand- Level 2)
Make use of logic gates and Boolean expressions for digital circuits.

units.title: DC Circuits
units.text: DC Circuits Electrical circuit elements (R, L and C), voltage and current sources, Kirchhoff’s current law, Kirchhoff’s voltage law, Mesh and Nodal Analysis, Superposition Theorem, Thevenin’s Theorem, Norton’s Theorem.

units.title: AC Circuits
units.text: AC Circuits Generation of alternating emf, instantaneous, peak, average, RMS values and other related terms, vector representation of AC quantities, Steady state analysis of R, L, C, R-L, R-C, R-L-C series circuits, series RLC resonance. Three- phase emf- star and delta connections, relationship between line and phase quantities.

units.title: Digital Electronics
units.text: Digital Electronics Logic gates, concept of universal logic gates; implementation of Boolean expressions using logic gates, De Morgan’s theorems, simplification of Boolean expressions using Boolean laws, application of digital circuits: half and full adder, half and full subtractor and their K-maps.

program: B. Tech. and MBA Tech. (All Programs)
objectives: This course aims to equip students with practical skills in electronics prototyping and provides hands-on experience with essential tools, measuring instruments, PCB design, and fabrication techniques. Additionally, students will gain knowledge in PC hardware assembly, Arduino-based circuit programming, and aerial robotics, including drone assembly and flight basics.

outcomes.text: Understand and demonstrate the use of essential hand tools, measuring instruments, and prototyping equipment for circuit design and testing, (Understand - Level 2)
Design and fabricate single-sided PCBs by selecting appropriate circuit components, routing layouts using open-source software, and assembling electronic circuits, (Create- Level 6)
Analyze and troubleshoot common electrical and electronic components used in industrial applications, including wiring systems and protection devices, (Apply- Level 3)

Assemble, configure, and troubleshoot PC hardware by understanding the functionality of components such as CPU, RAM, motherboard, power supply, storage devices, and input/output peripherals, (Understand - Level 2)
Develop and implement Arduino-based projects by coding and interfacing various sensors for real-world applications, (Create- Level 6)

Assemble and configure aerial robotic systems (drones/UAVs) by understanding flight principles, selecting appropriate components, and performing test flights in a controlled environment. (Understand - Level 2)

units.text: Introduction to Electronics Workbench, Hand tools and measuring instruments- Equip with instruments for prototyping and experimenting with circuits and electronic devices- The know-how of the Multimeter, Function generator, DC Power supply, Cathode Ray Oscilloscope (CRO), Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO), Soldering iron, De-soldering pump. Hand tools for general fabrication and assembly tasks- To familiarize with the operation and safety guidelines for some handful of tools-Pliers, Cutters, Wire strippers, Tweezers, Crimping tool, Hot air soldering and de-soldering.

Hands-On Learning- Printed circuit boards (PCB)- Types, Single sided, Double sided. Design, Create and Test Single sided PCB for an electronic circuit- Circuit selection, components assembly, PCB routing using open source software such as Dip Trace/Tina Pro Software, PCB fabrication, manual etching, hand drilling, soft soldering of joints, and designed circuit testing.

Industrial Electrical and Electronic components - Identification and study of commonly used electrical material such as Wires, Cables, Connectors, Switches, Relays, heat sink, Circuit Breaker, Fuses, Buzzer, Residential wiring of Hall, Kitchen, Bedroom, use of 2-way, intermediate switches in staircase wiring, Earthing.

units.title: Introduction to PC Hardware
units.text: Introduction to PC Hardware – Step by Step PC assembling and disassembling process- Understanding PC components- Central Processing Unit (CPU), motherboard, Random Access Memory (RAM), Graphic Processing Unit (GPU), storage drives, Power supply unit (PSU), case and cooling system, Optical drive, Input and Output ports, expansion slots, The Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) or Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI). 5. Project-Based Learning (Bringing an idea to life) – Circuit design, programming, and simulation- Study of ARDUINO boards (uno/mega), Coding and interfacing of sensors to Arduino -Temperature, Humidity, Light Dependent Resistor (LDR), Smoke, Ultrasonic range sensor etc., 6. Introduction to Aerial Robotics (Drone/UAV/Sky Rover/Aerobot) Assembly and Flight Basics – Introduction to aerial robotics, overview of aerial robotics, Types of aerial robotics - Fixed-wing, rotary-wing, hybrid, Regulations and safety guidelines, Basics of aerodynamics and flight principles, Understanding Components - Frame types and materials, Motors: Brushed vs Brushless, Electronic Speed Controllers (ESCs), Propellers: Pitch, size, and thrust, Flight Controller: Role and selection, Power system: Battery types (LiPo), connectors, and chargers, Sensors: IMU, GPS, and Altimeters, Camera, Wireless communication modules (RF, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi), Hands-on Aerial Robotics Assembly - Basics of flight control software (Betaflight, Ardupilot, etc.), Configuring flight parameters, Remote control setup and binding, Hands-on test flight in a controlled environment, Basic maneuvers: Takeoff, hovering, landing

Apply relevant language usage and communication rules to listen, write, present and connect
Analyze various interpersonal scenarios towards applying appropriate communication tools and strategies in the given context
Evaluate a particular context to generate comparable and appropriate communication based solutions that are socially and ethically relevant

objectives: The course would enable students to get a brief introduction of the Indian Constitution and its principles. The students would have knowledge of concept of ‘State’ and interdependencies of its institutions vis a vis their relation with fundamental rights.

outcomes.text: understand the historic evolution of the Indian Constitution, its drafting, nature and to understand the principles mentioned in its Preamble

inculcate fundamental rights in its true sense and also the permissible restrictions upon it so as to enjoy these rights within permissible limits while simultaneously performing their duties and to apply these principles into their professional lives
ingrain the structure of our polity and role of Judiciary in maintaining the basic structure of the Constitution

attain knowledge of the Emergency provisions, when and how it is imposed, to know the additional powers the bestowed upon the Government at times of Emergency and to understand the Amendment procedure.

units.text: Nature, Characteristics and Sources of Indian Constitution

Fundamental rights and Fundamental duties – Concept of State, Right to Equality under Articles 14 and 15, Right to certain freedoms under Article 19, Right to Life and liberty under Article 21, Right to religion under Article 25 and 26, Right to remedy under Article 32 and Fundamental duties
Indian Judiciary – Concept of Supreme Court and High Courts, Appointment of Judges, Independence of Judiciary, Jurisdictions of Supreme Court and High Courts
Emergency Provisions – Concept of National Emergency under Article 352, Financial Emergency under Article 360 and President rule under Article 356 of the Constitution

demonstrate the ability to understand mathematical logic, concepts in abstract algebra and mathematical proof techniques
solve problems based on combinatorics, graph theory and abstract algebra

Describe various measuring devices and sensors
Understand the application of computer science and electrical engineering principles in real-time application

objectives: This course is designed to encourage students to inculcate human values, that will enable them to grow as a responsible human being. The course also helps students to understand how to maintain ethical conduct in discharging professional duties, which will be beneficial for them in their professional lives.

outcomes.text: Understand the engineering code of ethics and be able to apply them as necessary
Understand moral complexities in many engineering activities and decision-making processes
Understand some of the contemporary issues in the engineering professions
Effectively communicate their knowledge and understanding of engineering ethics.

units.text: Introduction to Ethics- • Concept of morals and ethics, • Study of engineering ethics; • Laws and ethics; • Personal and professional ethics.
Professional Practice in Engineering- • Common morality ASME code of ethics, • Technical codes and standards, • Accepted standards of Engineering practice and the standard of care.

Ethics as design-doing justice to moral Problem- • Discuss about ethics as a design to solve moral problems • Comparison between moral problems and engineering design problems; • Moral lessons from design problems; • Implications of the dynamic character of problem situations.

Rights and Responsibilities of Engineers- • Moral responsibilities; • Conflicts of interests; • Confidentiality, • Engineers, organizations and ethics, • Engineer-manager relationships; • loyalty; • The concept of whistleblowing.

course_name: Basics of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)-311 (VT)
objectives: Equip the student to understand and solve simple ac and dc electrical circuits. To enable the student to obtain a basic understanding of the working principle and applications of electronics devices. To impart hands-on experience in assembling and testing of circuits.

outcomes.text: Interpret the importance of electrical energy and relate its usage in various applications.
Understand and analyze AC circuits.
Comprehend the principles of electromechanical energy conversion.
Understand the construction, working principle and applications of electronics devices and logic circuits.

units.title: DC Circuits
units.text: DC Circuits Electrical circuit elements (R, L and C), voltage and current sources, Kirchhoff’s current law, Kirchoff’s voltage laws, Analysis of simple circuits with dc excitation, Superposition Theorem, Thevenin’s Theorems, Norton’s Theorems. Time-domain analysis of first-order RL circuits.

units.title: AC Circuits
units.text: AC Circuits Generation of alternating emf, instantaneous, rms, peak, average values and related other terms, vector representation of AC quantities, Steady state analysis of R, L, C series and parallel circuits, resonance. Analog Electronics (no mathematical treatment and design) Half and full wave rectifiers, special purpose diodes -zener regulator, BJT and its applications, amplifier, oscillator, overview of opto-electronics devices, opto-couplers, concepts of transducer, Operational amplifier (IC- 741), Inverting and Non-Inverting, Comparator, Timer (IC-555) and multivibrators. Digital Electronics Logic gates, concept of universal logic; implementation of Boolean expressions using logic gates, application of digital circuits: e.g. adder, subtractor, multiplexer, de-multiplexer, Analog to Digital Converter, Digital to Analog Converter.

units.title: Strategic importance of IT as a resource

Ethics in Information Systems.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)
objectives: To acquaint students with various facets of management. To sensitize students on social issues impacting society in general and business in particular.

outcomes.text: Appreciate decision-making and motivation skills
Apply management principles in everyday practice in organizations
Apply knowledge of business management for enhancing organization
Describe business Terminologies and functions
Make connections between ideas and experiences, and to apply them to new learning situations
Practice the ethical issues in corporate governance and to adhere to the ethical codes

units.text: Business System and Contemporary Business Global Environment The role of Businesses in combining human, physical and financial resources to create goods and services. Private and public sector organizations. The main business functions and their roles: human resources, finance and accounts, marketing, operations. Primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary sectors The nature of business activity in each sector and the impact of sectorial change on business activity. Forms of Business Organization including LLP. Emerging trends in business: outsourcing, service sector and e-commerce. Business in Global environment External Business Environment- Macro & Micro Environment, Understanding Management Contexts- Constraints & Challenges, PESTEL analysis. Development of Management Thought Management & Organizations, Management theories- Taylor, Fayol& Elton Mayo. Functions of Manager.

units.title: Planning and Decision Making
units.text: Planning and Decision Making Foundations of Planning, Managers as Decision makers. Process of Strategic Planning SWOT Analysis. Types of decision- Programmed and Un-programmed decisions, concept of Rationality and bounded rationality in decision making, role of intuition in decision making. Steps in an effective decision-making process.

units.title: Organizations
units.text: Organizations Formal and Informal Organization, Organization structures- mechanistic Vs Organic Structures, Types of structures Line and staff authority. Specialization, Centralization Vs Decentralization, Formalization. Structures with Narrow and wide spans.

units.title: Foundations in Accounting
units.text: Foundations in Accounting Introduction to Financial accounting, Cost accounting, Management accounting, Financial management & Finance Analytics The accounting process, preparation of financial statements for external users, techniques for analysing a basic set of financial statements, using accounting information to support management decisions. Accounting for Managerial Decisions: Understand how managerial decisions are made in corporations using accounting data. Special emphasis is given to cost classifications, cost allocation, break-even analysis, ABC costing, and budgeting decisions.

units.title: Financial Management
units.text: Financial Management Objectives & Scope of Financial management. Time Value of Money calculations. Understand differences in interest rates (due to differences in risk, horizon, and compounding) Develop a set of techniques for valuing capital investment projects in privately and publicly traded companies, develops a set of investment criterion. Examine how firms raise capital, and analyse the effect of financing choices on shareholder wealth, firm value, risk, and tax payments. Dividend Policy- What firms should do with the profits they generate given effective financial policies and decisions, the pay-out policy?

units.title: Investment management
units.text: Investment management Introduction to Stock market Use present value calculations to solve bond and stock pricing Basics of risk& return management-Portfolio Risk-combining risky and riskless securities. Introduction to Capital asset pricing model (CAPM) and the Arbitrage Pricing Theory (APT). Derivative market—Types of derivatives- forward, futures, options & swaps. The definition, use, and pricing of derivative securities

units.title: Foundations in Economics
units.text: Foundations in Economics Microeconomics: supply and demand mechanism, how markets are affected by regulation and taxation, costs of production, and how market structure affects outcomes. Macroeconomics The fundamental measures of the aggregate economy, the sources of economic growth, explaining short-run fluctuations in economic activity, and how government policies can affect these fluctuations. Fundamental economic cycles Impact of the same at both the micro and macro level(companies, investments, industries, and national economies).

units.title: Marketing Foundations
units.text: Marketing Foundations Concepts such as segmentation, targeting, positioning, customer and market analysis, and basic marketing planning Holistic Marketing, Marketing Mix, -4P’s, Need for Marketing Research- Quantitative, Qualitative, Pricing Strategies, Promotion Mix, Direct & Indirect Selling, CRM, Social Media Marketing 4 C’s of Marketing

units.title: Introduction to Major Areas of HRM and OB
units.text: Introduction to Major Areas of HRM and OB Orientation to talent management – onboarding, recruitment , selection, appraisal, training, exit. Groups Vs. teams, Types of teams, skills necessary to manage teams. Effective teams, Team Roles

units.title: Leadership and Motivation
units.text: Leadership and Motivation Leader Vs Manager, Leadership theories- Trait, Behavioural theories of Leadership. Motivation Theories and application- Maslow’s Need Theory, Mc Gregor’s Theory X and Y, Herzberg’s two factor theory, Victor Vroom, Equity theory of Motivation, Union and Management issues

units.title: Controlling
units.text: Controlling Introduction to Controlling, Control process Measuring Organization Performance-Feed forward/Concurrent/Feedback Control, Financial Controls-Budget, Information Control, Balanced Scorecard, Benchmarking, Gantt, Milestone and PERT Charts.

Introduction Business Ethics a) Business Ethics Introduction to Business Ethics: Concept and Interpretation, Importance of Business Ethics, Personal Integrity at the workplace, Ethical Issues & Dilemmas at Work, Costs Associated with Unethical Behaviours, Competitive Advantages of Ethical Organizations, Code of Ethics and a Code of Conduct b) Individual Approach to Ethics Corporate Social Responsibility- Responsibility towards stakeholders.

units.title: Management of Operations
units.text: Management of Operations Introduction to Operations Management & Productivity of Operations. Defining Operations Function, Operations Management integrated with other business functions, Operation as a process to generate ‘Goods’ and ‘Services’. Difference between ‘Goods’ and ‘Services’. Operations Management in Manufacturing and Service Providers

units.text: Introduction to Entrepreneurship Meaning and concept of entrepreneurship, role of entrepreneurship in economic development, entrepreneurship ecosystem- agencies in entrepreneurship management and future of entrepreneurship, women entrepreneurship The Entrepreneur: Meaning of entrepreneur/intrapreneur, the skills required to be an entrepreneur, the entrepreneurial decision process, and role models, mentors and support system.
Hospitality and Tourism Management

Use of Pivot charts for data visualization. Create 3D worksheets, 3D workbooks, and 3D formulas. Design and use Slicers for data filtration.

units.text: Business Automation Using Macro Programming in Excel Recording and managing macros, Accessing and understanding VBA Code for macro. Create program code using Visual Basic for Applications and the VBA editor. Create command buttons and other controls using to macros. Using controls like radio button, List and Checkbox using VBA code. Understanding use of Input box and Message box. Customizing macros as per requirements by modifying VBA Code.

Ethics in Information Systems.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)-311 (VT)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Fundamentals of Differential and Integral Calculus.
objectives: To provide sound understanding of the concepts in Calculus needed in Business and Economics. To enable students to apply the concepts of Calculus to Business and Economics.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate understanding of functions, graphs, derivatives and mathematical modelling
Solve problems based on derivatives, partial derivatives and integration
Analyse and optimize functions
Apply the techniques of calculus to business and economics

units.title: Functions, Graphs and Limits
units.text: Functions, Graphs and Limits Functions, The graph of a function, Functions used in Economics, Linear functions, Mathematical modelling, limits of functions, limits involving infinity.

units.title: Differentiation and Applications of derivatives
units.text: Differentiation and Applications of derivatives Rate of Change, Marginal analysis and approximations using increments, Implicit differentiation and related rates, Increasing and decreasing functions, relative extrema, concavity and points of inflection, Optimization, Elasticity of demand, Applications of optimization.

units.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
units.text: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions Exponential functions; Continuous compounding, Differentiation of exponential and logarithmic functions, Applications; exponential models, optimization.

units.title: Integration and Applications of Integrals
units.text: Integration and Applications of Integrals The definite integral, Average value of the function, Applications of Integration to Business and economics.

units.title: Calculus of Several Variables

objectives: This course introduces the field of human psychology by focusing on the core theoretical concepts, theories and research methodology. It also focuses on an overview of some of the pillars that form the sub-fields within the field namely biological, cognitive, developmental, mental and physical health.

outcomes.text: Describe comprehensive overview of the field of psychology as well as its various sub-fields
Explain key psychological orientations, theories, and research practices
Discerning major themes and concepts across the span of the field
Explain historical and critical psychological perspectives

units.title: An Introduction to the discipline of Psychology
units.text: An Introduction to the discipline of Psychology Psychology as a Science Research Methods in Psychology History of Psychology Issues in Psychology

units.title: Biological Bases of Behaviour

units.title: Sensation, Perception, Consciousness

Motivation and Emotion

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)-311 (VT)
objectives: To equip students with critical thinking abilities through diverse reading exercises. To enhance students’ communication skills by giving them adequate exposure in writing, listening and speaking skills. To support students’ language skills requirements such as vocabulary and grammar. To build students’ confidence in participating in formal communication such as speeches, presentations and group discussions as well as informal communication such as conversations. To help students in understanding interpersonal and group dynamics and to inculcate the principles of team work.

outcomes.text: Draft formal and academic documents as per the standard principles of written communication
Engage in effective oral communication in both formal and informal communication context
Create formal and persuasive presentation
Comprehend oral and written texts critically
Work effectively in groups with sound understanding of groups dynamics

units.title: Communication Basics
units.text: Communication Basics Introduction to human communication Communication models (Transmission and Dialogue) Communication barriers Role of context in communication Modes of communication: verbal, non-verbal, visual Understanding audiences

units.title: Reading and listening for critical comprehension
units.text: Reading and listening for critical comprehension Close and critical reading of written and oral texts such as newspaper editorials, speeches etc.

units.title: Oral Communication
units.text: Oral Communication Power point presentations Speeches Group discussions Responding to and participating in case study analysis

units.title: Group Communication
units.text: Group Communication Introduction to communication in groups and teams Characteristics of functional teams and groups Principles of group communication

units.title: Written Communication
units.text: Written Communication Principles of written communication Building blocks of all writing: Outlines, Paragraphs, Sentences and word choice, grammar 7C’s of effective communication Editing and proofreading Formats: Emails, short research articles (800 words), abstract or summary

text_books: 1. Meenakshi Raman and Sangeeta Sharma, Technical Communication, 3rd Edition, Oxford University Press, 2015.
reference_books: 1. David Bohm, On Dialogue, Routledge, 1996. 2. Anjanee Sethi and Bhavana Adhikari, Business Communication, Tata McGraw Hill, 2010. 3. Courtland Bovee and John Thill, Business Communication Today, 15th Edition, Pearson Education, 2021.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)-311 (VT)
objectives: To acquaint students with various facets of management. To sensitize students on social issues impacting society in general and business in particular.

outcomes.text: Appreciate decision-making and motivation skills
Apply management principles in everyday practice in organizations
Apply knowledge of business management for enhancing organization
Describe business Terminologies and functions
Make connections between ideas and experiences, and to apply them to new learning situations
Practice the ethical issues in corporate governance and to adhere to the ethical codes

units.text: Business System and Contemporary Business Global Environment The role of Businesses in combining human, physical and financial resources to create goods and services. Private and public sector organizations. The main business functions and their roles: human resources, finance and accounts, marketing, operations. Primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary sectors The nature of business activity in each sector and the impact of sectorial change on business activity. Forms of Business Organization including LLP. Emerging trends in business: outsourcing, service sector and e-commerce. Business in Global environment External Business Environment- Macro & Micro Environment, Understanding Management Contexts- Constraints & Challenges, PESTEL analysis. Development of Management Thought Management & Organizations, Management theories- Taylor, Fayol& Elton Mayo. Functions of Manager.

units.title: Planning and Decision Making
units.text: Planning and Decision Making Foundations of Planning, Managers as Decision makers. Process of Strategic Planning SWOT Analysis. Types of decision- Programmed and Un-programmed decisions, concept of Rationality and bounded rationality in decision making, role of intuition in decision making. Steps in an effective decision- making process.

units.title: Organizations
units.text: Organizations Formal and Informal Organization, Organization structures- mechanistic Vs Organic Structures, Types of structures Line and staff authority. Specialization, Centralization Vs Decentralization, Formalization. Structures with Narrow and wide spans.

units.title: Foundations in Accounting
units.text: Foundations in Accounting Introduction to Financial accounting, Cost accounting, Management accounting, Financial management & Finance Analytics The accounting process, preparation of financial statements for external users, techniques for analysing a basic set of financial statements, using accounting information to support management decisions. Accounting for Managerial Decisions: Understand how managerial decisions are made in corporations using accounting data. Special emphasis is given to cost classifications, cost allocation, break-even analysis, ABC costing, and budgeting decisions.

units.title: Financial Management
units.text: Financial Management Objectives & Scope of Financial management. Time Value of Money calculations. Understand differences in interest rates (due to differences in risk, horizon, and compounding) Develop a set of techniques for valuing capital investment projects in privately and publicly traded companies, develops a set of investment criterion. Examine how firms raise capital, and analyse the effect of financing choices on shareholder wealth, firm value, risk, and tax payments. Dividend Policy- What firms should do with the profits they generate given effective financial policies and decisions, the pay-out policy?

units.title: Investment management
units.text: Investment management Introduction to Stock market Use present value calculations to solve bond and stock pricing Basics of risk& return management-Portfolio Risk-combining risky and riskless securities. Introduction to Capital asset pricing model (CAPM) and the Arbitrage Pricing Theory (APT). Derivative market—Types of derivatives- forward, futures, options & swaps. The definition, use, and pricing of derivative securities

units.title: Foundations in Economics
units.text: Foundations in Economics Microeconomics: supply and demand mechanism, how markets are affected by regulation and taxation, costs of production, and how market structure affects outcomes. Macroeconomics The fundamental measures of the aggregate economy, the sources of economic growth, explaining short-run fluctuations in economic activity, and how government policies can affect these fluctuations. Fundamental economic cycles Impact of the same at both the micro and macro level (companies, investments, industries, and national economies).

units.title: Marketing Foundations
units.text: Marketing Foundations Concepts such as segmentation, targeting, positioning, customer and market analysis, and basic marketing planning Holistic Marketing, Marketing Mix, -4P’s, Need for Marketing Research- Quantitative, Qualitative, Pricing Strategies, Promotion Mix, Direct & Indirect Selling, CRM, Social Media Marketing 4 C’s of Marketing

units.title: Introduction to Major Areas of HRM and OB
units.text: Introduction to Major Areas of HRM and OB Orientation to talent management – onboarding, recruitment, selection, appraisal, training, exit. Groups Vs. teams, Types of teams, skills necessary to manage teams. Effective teams, Team Roles

units.title: Leadership and Motivation
units.text: Leadership and Motivation Leader Vs Manager, Leadership theories- Trait, Behavioural theories of Leadership. Motivation Theories and application- Maslow’s Need Theory, Mc Gregor’s Theory X and Y, Herzberg’s two factor theory, Victor Vroom, Equity theory of Motivation, Union and Management issues

units.title: Controlling
units.text: Controlling Introduction to Controlling, Control process Measuring Organization Performance-Feed forward/Concurrent/Feedback Control, Financial Controls-Budget, Information Control, Balanced Scorecard, Benchmarking, Gantt, Milestone and PERT Charts.

Introduction Business Ethics a) Business Ethics Introduction to Business Ethics: Concept and Interpretation, Importance of Business Ethics, Personal Integrity at the workplace, Ethical Issues & Dilemmas at Work, Costs Associated with Unethical Behaviours, Competitive Advantages of Ethical Organizations, Code of Ethics and a Code of Conduct b) Individual Approach to Ethics Corporate Social Responsibility- Responsibility towards stakeholders.

units.title: Management of Operations
units.text: Management of Operations Introduction to Operations Management & Productivity of Operations. Defining Operations Function, Operations Management integrated with other business functions, Operation as a process to generate ‘Goods’ and ‘Services’. Difference between ‘Goods’ and ‘Services’. Operations Management in Manufacturing and Service Providers

units.title: Introduction to Entrepreneurship
units.text: Introduction to Entrepreneurship Meaning and concept of entrepreneurship, role of entrepreneurship in economic development, entrepreneurship ecosystem- agencies in entrepreneurship management and future of entrepreneurship, women entrepreneurship The Entrepreneur: Meaning of entrepreneur/intrapreneur, the skills required to be an entrepreneur, the entrepreneurial decision process, and role models, mentors and support system.
Hospitality and Tourism Management

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)-311 (VT)
objectives: To impart knowledge about societal applications of engineering design, visual aspects of engineering design, familiarize the aspects of engineering graphics standards and computer- aided geometric design concepts.

outcomes.text: Explain societal application of engineering design and its visual aspects
Interpret and communicate drawings effectively using different types of solid models
Describe engineering design standards
Apply the design techniques using modern tools to create projections of machine components with the help of software

units.text: Introduction to Engineering Drawing & Computer Graphics Principles of Engineering Graphics and their significance; Usage of Drawing instruments; lettering; numbering. Listing the computer technologies; Demonstrating knowledge of the theory of CAD software; use of standard toolbars like Draw, Modify, Dimensions and Annotations.

units.title: Orthographic Projections
units.text: Orthographic Projections Principles of orthographic projection- Conventions; Quadrant formation and Projections of points; Conversion of orthographic views to isometric views.

units.title: Sectional Orthographic Projections
units.text: Sectional Orthographic Projections Principles of sectional orthographic projection; need of sectional views and sectional orthographic projection; types of sections; hatching of sectioned part; related rules and assumptions.

units.title: Isometric Projections
units.text: Isometric Projections Principles of isometric projection; Isometric scale, Isometric views, Conventions; Isometric views of lines, planes; Simple and compound solids; Conversion of isometric views to orthographic views.
