program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)-311 (VT)
prerequisites: Develop the logic building skill. Solve pattern-recognition based problems because it will improve the visualization of logic. It is one of the fundamental steps of computation thinking.
objectives: Enable students understand the basic concepts of Programming and help them build Programming Logic. Develop problem-solving skills using basic Programming constructs, Decision Making and Looping. Enable students solve complex problems using the knowledge of Arrays, Functions, Structures and Pointers.

outcomes.text: Formulate algorithms and draw flowcharts
Implement Decision Making, Nested Control Structures and Iterations.
Implement programs using Functions and concept of Recursion.
Implement programs using arrays, strings, structure, pointers, searching and sorting algorithms.

units.title: Introduction to Programming
units.text: Introduction to Programming Introduction to components of a computer system (disks, memory, processor, where a program is stored and executed, operating system, compilers etc.) Introduction to Algorithm & Flowchart Properties of algorithm, Developing an algorithm and Flowcharts.

units.title: The Components of a C Program
units.text: The Components of a C Program Program's Components, Variables, Data Types, Constants, Statements, Expressions and Operators.

units.title: Basic Program Control
units.text: Basic Program Control Decision Making and Branching, Switch Statements, Break and Continue Statements, Looping: For, While, Do-While, Nested Loops.

units.title: Arrays
units.text: Arrays One Dimensional Array: Concept, Declaration and Initialization, Accessing array elements of one-dimensional array. Two-Dimensional Array: Concept, Declaration and Initialization, Accessing array elements of two-dimensional array.

units.title: Program Decomposition in to modules
units.text: Program Decomposition in to modules Introduction and need of user defined functions, Defining functions in C, Function calls and declaration, Category of functions. Introduction to recursive functions.

units.title: Strings
units.text: Strings Introduction to strings, Declaring & initializing string variable, Reading & writing strings, String handling functions.

units.title: Understanding Pointers
units.text: Understanding Pointers Idea of Pointer, defining Pointers, Call by value and call by reference.

units.title: Structures
units.text: Structures Defining a Structure, Declaring structure variables, Accessing structure members, Array of Structure, Difference between Structure and Unions. Basic Algorithms Sorting Algorithms: Bubble sort, Insertion sort, Selection sort. Searching: Sequential search.

text_books: 1. Byron Gottfried, Schaum's Outline Programming with C, 3rd Edition, McGraw-Hill, 2017. 2. E. Balaguruswamy, Programming in ANSI C, 8th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Education, 2019.
reference_books: 1. Brian W. Kernighan and Dennis M. Ritchie, The C Programming Language, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall of India, 2015 2. Seymour Lipschutz, Schaum’s Outlines Data Structures, Revised 1st Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2014.

course_name: Basics of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)-311 (VT)
objectives: Equip the student to understand and solve simple ac and dc electrical circuits. To enable the student to obtain a basic understanding of the working principle and applications of electronics devices. To impart hands-on experience in assembling and testing of circuits.

outcomes.text: Interpret the importance of electrical energy and relate its usage in various applications.
Understand and analyze AC circuits.
Comprehend the principles of electromechanical energy conversion.
Understand the construction, working principle and applications of electronics devices and logic circuits.

units.title: DC Circuits
units.text: DC Circuits Electrical circuit elements (R, L and C), voltage and current sources, Kirchhoff’s current law, Kirchoff’s voltage laws, Analysis of simple circuits with dc excitation, Superposition Theorem, Thevenin’s Theorems, Norton’s Theorems. Time-domain analysis of first-order RL circuits.

units.title: AC Circuits
units.text: AC Circuits Generation of alternating emf, instantaneous, rms, peak, average values and related other terms, vector representation of AC quantities, Steady state analysis of R, L, C series and parallel circuits, resonance. Generation of three- phase emf, star connection, delta connection, relationship between line and phase quantities Transformers and Electrical Machines Construction and working of single phase transformer Ideal and practical transformer, equivalent circuit, Losses in transformers, Generation of rotating magnetic fields, Construction and working of a three- phase induction motor, Single-phase induction motor, construction and working, DC motor construction, working and types. Analog Electronics (no mathematical treatment and design) Half and full wave rectifiers, special purpose diodes -zener regulator, BJT and its applications, amplifier, oscillator, overview of opto-electronics devices, opto-couplers, concepts of transducer, Operational amplifier (IC-741), Inverting and Non-Inverting, Comparator, Timer (IC-555) and multivibrators. Digital Electronics Logic gates, concept of universal logic; implementation of Boolean expressions using logic gates, application of digital circuits: e.g. adder, subtractor, multiplexer, de-multiplexer, Analog to Digital Converter, Digital to Analog Converter.

text_books: 1. D. C. Kulshreshtha, Basic Electrical Engineering, 2nd Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2019. 2. E. Hughes, Electrical and Electronics Technology, 10th Edition, Pearson Education, 2010. 3. Boylestad R.L., Nashelsky L., Electronic Devices and Circuit Theory, 11th Edition, Pearson, 2015. 4. M. Morris Mano, Digital Logic and Computer Design, 1ST Ed. Pearson Education, 2016.
reference_books: 1. B. L. Theraja, Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering and Electronics, (LPSPE), S Chand Publishing, 2022. 2. Jacob Millman & Halkias, Electronic Devices & Circuits, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2015.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)- 311(VT)
objectives: To develop students to gain understanding and to provide working knowledge of accounting concepts, detailed procedures and documentation involved in Accounting system.

outcomes.text: Describe the framework of accounting systems and the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
Prepare necessary financial statements for understandability and relevance of stakeholders

units.title: Conceptual basis of Accounting
units.text: Conceptual basis of Accounting Need and Importance, Definition of Accounting, Accounting Process, Accounting Cycle, Users of Accounting information, Types of Accounting, Capital & Revenue Expenditure and Income.

units.title: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
units.text: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles Accounting Concepts and Accounting Conventions.

units.title: An Introduction to Financial Statements
units.text: An Introduction to Financial Statements Use basic accounting equation, Identify assets, liabilities, and stockholders' equity, Identify financial statement components, Preparation of Income statement and Retained Earnings statement and Balance sheet, Correct an incorrectly prepared balance sheet.

units.title: A Further look at Financial Statements
units.text: A Further look at Financial Statements Classify financial statement items by balance sheet classification, Classify items as current or noncurrent, prepare assets section of balance sheet, Compute liquidity, solvency and profitability ratios.

units.title: Basis Accounting Process
units.text: Basis Accounting Process Identify accounts to be debited and credited, Analyze the effects of transactions, Record journal entries, Journalize a series of transactions.

units.title: Basis Accounting Process
units.text: Basis Accounting Process Analyze transactions and determine their effect on accounts, Post journal entries and prepare a trial balance, journalize transactions, post, and prepare a trial balance, Prepare a correct trial balance.

units.title: Accrual Accounting Concepts
units.text: Accrual Accounting Concepts Preparation of Financial Statement with adjustment entries – Closing Stock, Depreciation, Prepaid Expenses, unearned Revenue, Accruals.

units.title: Merchandising Operations and Multi-Step Income Statement
units.text: Merchandising Operations and Multi-Step Income Statement Journalizing Sales transaction, Journalizing Purchase transaction, Net Purchases and Cost of goods purchased, Journalizing Perpetual inventory entries, Prepare Cost of Goods sold using Periodic system.

units.title: Reporting and Analyzing Inventory
units.text: Reporting and Analyzing Inventory Compute ending Inventory using LIFO and FIFO, Compute ending inventory using average cost, Compute inventory turnover and days in inventory, calculate ending inventory, COGS and Gross profit.

units.title: Fraud, Internal Control and Cash
units.text: Fraud, Internal Control and Cash Bank reconciliation, analyzing outstanding checks, Deposits in transit and outstanding checks, Journalize and post petty cash transactions and preparation of Cash budget.

units.title: Reporting and Analyzing Receivables
units.text: Reporting and Analyzing Receivables Record basic accounts receivable transactions, Prepare entry using percentage of receivables method, Prepare entry for credit card sale, Prepare a balance sheet presentation of receivables, Prepare entries to record allowance for doubtful accounts, Prepare journal entries for credit card and notes receivable transactions

units.title: Reporting and Analyzing Long-Lived Assets
units.text: Reporting and Analyzing Long-Lived Assets Determine the cost of land, Compute straight-line depreciation, Journalize equipment transactions for purchase, sale, retirement, depreciation, Compute depreciation under different methods

units.title: Reporting and Analyzing Liabilities
units.text: Reporting and Analyzing Liabilities Prepare entries for an interest-bearing note payable, Prepare entries for issuance of bonds, Journalize sales and related taxes, Record accrual of payroll taxes, Prepare journal entries for redemption of bonds, Prepare instalment payments schedule, journal entries for mortgage.

units.title: Reporting and Analyzing Stockholders’ Equity
units.text: Reporting and Analyzing Stockholders’ Equity Journalize issuance of par value common stock, Prepare entries for a cash dividend, Journalize issuance of common stock, Compare issuance of stock financing to issuance of bond financing, Journalize stock dividends.

units.title: Statement of Cash Flows
units.text: Statement of Cash Flows Compute net cash provided by operating activities – indirect, Determine cash received from sale of equipment, Classify transactions by type of activity, Prepare cash flow from operating activities indirect method, Prepare a statement of cash flows - indirect method.

text_books: 1. Kimmel, Weygandt and Kieso, Financial Accounting, Tools for Business Decision Making, 8th Edition, Wiley Publication, 2015. 2. Ramanathan, S., Accounting for Management: A Basic Text in Financial and Management Accounting, New Delhi, Oxford University Press, 2014 ed.
reference_books: 1. Shah, Financial Accounting for Management, 2nd Edition, Oxford University Press, 2013. 2. Harsolekar, D., Financial Accounting for Managers, 6th Edition, Mumbai edu-tech publishing, 2014.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) -311(VT)
objectives: This course provides basic orientation towards economic (micro and macroeconomic) principles and help them understand the functions of economic system. To combine elements of basic micro and macroeconomics. To familiarize with importance of economic approach in decision making. To understand the application of economic theories in day- to-day life. To understand broader aspects of the economy and its environment.

outcomes.text: Analyze and evaluate the impact of Economic Policies and its implication on the Economic Environment
Describe basic concepts of economics -Microeconomics
Orient themselves towards higher levels of learning
Handle economic data for policy purposes

units.title: Nature and Scope of Economics
units.text: Nature and Scope of Economics Introduction to Economics, Micro and Macro Economic Analysis, Positive and Normative Economics, Types of Economic Systems, Basic Economic Problems and Uses of Economic Resources-Production Possibility Curve, Recent Developments in the Field of Economics.

units.title: Analysis of Demand and Supply
units.text: Analysis of Demand and Supply Meaning and Determinants, Demand Curve and Supply Curve, Equilibrium of Demand and Supply, Shift in Demand and Supply, Demand and Supply Function, law of Demand and law of Supply, Effects of Change in Demand and Supply, Types of Elasticity of Demand, Uses of Elasticity of Demand.

units.title: Demand Estimation and Forecasting
units.text: Demand Estimation and Forecasting Meaning and Importance of Demand Forecasting, Methods of Forecasting, Introduction to Regression (Simple-bivariate) Analysis, OLS Method, Estimating and interpreting the regression Coefficients and Forecasting.

units.title: Utility Analysis
units.text: Utility Analysis Types of Utility, Cardinal and Ordinal Utility Analysis, Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility (DMU), Uses of Law of DMU in Decision Making, Indifference Curve analysis and Consumer Equilibrium.

units.title: Production Analysis
units.text: Production Analysis Meaning of Production and Productivity, Short-run and Long-run Production Function, Total-Average-Marginal Product, Law of Variable Proportions, Law of Return and Return to Scale, Classification of Isoquant Curve and Producer’s Equilibrium, Economic region of production, Production Forecasting Using Data Analysis Technique.

units.title: Cost Analysis
units.text: Cost Analysis Cost Concepts and Analysis, Relation Between Marginal Cost and Average Cost, Analysis of Short-run and Long-run Cost, U-shape and L- shape Long Run Average Cost and their Implications, Determinants of Cost, Break-even Analysis, Cost Function and Cost Model Technique.

units.title: Market Structure and Analysis
units.text: Market Structure and Analysis Introduction and Features of Market Structure (Perfect Competition, Monopoly, Monopolistic Competition, Oligopoly and Duopoly), Equilibrium Analysis of Firm, Price Discrimination and Degrees of Price Discrimination, Dumping.

units.title: Welfare Analysis and Game Theory
units.text: Welfare Analysis and Game Theory Partial and General Equilibrium, Role of Government in Socio-Economic Welfare, Consumer and Producer Surplus, Price Ceiling and Price Floor, market Failure and State Intervention, Introduction to Game Theory.

units.title: National Income Analysis
units.text: National Income Analysis Meaning-Concepts –Importance of National Income, Methods of measurement of National Income and their Limitations, Uses of National Income Data, Simple Keynesian Model of Income Determination- Circular Flow of income with Closed and Open Economy, Business Cycle- Phases and Management of Cyclical Fluctuations.

units.title: Consumption Function and Investment Function
units.text: Consumption Function and Investment Function Meaning and determinants of Consumption, Theories of Consumption, Meaning and Types of Investments, Theories of Investment, Government Policies- FDI and FIIs.

units.title: Inflation
units.text: Inflation Meaning and Types of inflation, Causes and effects of Inflation, Methods of measuring Inflation, Measures to Control Inflation, Theories of Inflation, Inflation and Money Supply, Inflation and interest Rates, Inflation and Unemployment- Philips Curve.

units.title: Analysis of Demand and Supply of Money

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) -311(VT)
objectives: To develop advanced written and oral communication skills in students that may help them cope well in contemporary professional contexts. To inculcate a sound critical and analytical bent in the students that may help them scrutinize and face contemporary challenges in a holistic manner. To develop a research and solution oriented approach in students that may prepare them for a competitive work environment and utilize their skills towards creating an improved world. outcomes.text: Communicate effectively in different range of situations with respect to cultural contexts.
Conduct academic inquiry and present their findings in the form of formal reports, case-study responses
Follow ethical practices underlying academic work
Participate effectively in professional networks
Communicate through written and oral means of communication in professional and academic settings effectively

Describe fundamental concepts of object-oriented concepts.
Develop computer programs using object oriented concepts to solve the real life problems
Design a UML diagram for a given problem statement.

objectives: To develop critical thinking skills in students in a logical sense and as it applies to thinking about real world issues.To broaden and deepen students’ understanding of the society they live in .To enhance their abilities of reasoning, articulation, expression so that they may be effective communicators and change agents

outcomes.text: Discern statements, premises, conclusions, assumptions, fallacies in any discourse and thereby think clearly for themselves
Apply critical thinking to the teaching-learning experience self reflectively
Apply the principles of critical thinking to understand contemporary society through the lenses of caste, gender, and the post-colonial experience
Attempt to transform the situation in their own ways through dialogue, critical questioning, love for humanity and participatory action

units.text: Introduction to Critical Thinking (i) What is critical thinking and why it matters; what facilitates and hinders it (ii) Elements of arguments in logic: Statements, premises, conclusions, inferences, explanations, evidence, background information, indicator words (iii) Discerning arguments in real world discourse (eg. newspapers/reports) [Reading 1: Chapters 1, 2 and 3]

Evaluating moral arguments and beliefs [Reading 1: Chapter 11]

units.title: Thinking critically about Colonialism and Post colonialism
units.text: Thinking critically about Colonialism and Post colonialism (i) Understanding India’s colonial history and how it informs our present [Excerpts: Readings 5, 6]

Apply the laws of electromagnetism and electromagnetic properties in real life challenges.
Interpret the laws of astronomy and effectively use them for sensing and monitoring applications.

Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion, Satellite orbits, Weather Satellites and Sensing Systems, Operational polar orbiting and geostationary satellites, weather sensors, Satellite data archives , Ground based sensors

objectives: To provide knowledge of the basic principles of the organization, operation and performance of computer systems and the underlying integrated circuit technologies that is used to construct computer components.

outcomes.text: Describe basic components of computer systems and its operations.
Explain the memory design architecture and related operations
Enlist the operations of control unit of the computer
Differentiate among various I/O operations and its classifications

units.title: Functional blocks of a computer

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)- 311(VT)
objectives: To develop students to gain understanding and to provide working knowledge of accounting concepts, detailed procedures and documentation involved in Accounting system.

outcomes.text: Describe the framework of accounting systems and the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
Prepare necessary financial statements for understandability and relevance of stakeholders

units.title: Conceptual basis of Accounting
units.text: Conceptual basis of Accounting Need and Importance, Definition of Accounting, Accounting Process, Accounting Cycle, Users of Accounting information, Types of Accounting, Capital & Revenue Expenditure and Income.

units.title: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
units.text: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles Accounting Concepts and Accounting Conventions.

units.title: An Introduction to Financial Statements
units.text: An Introduction to Financial Statements Use basic accounting equation, Identify assets, liabilities, and stockholders' equity, Identify financial statement components, Preparation of Income statement and Retained Earnings statement and Balance sheet, Correct an incorrectly prepared balance sheet.

units.title: A Further look at Financial Statements
units.text: A Further look at Financial Statements Classify financial statement items by balance sheet classification, Classify items as current or noncurrent, prepare assets section of balance sheet, Compute liquidity, solvency and profitability ratios.

units.title: Basis Accounting Process
units.text: Basis Accounting Process Identify accounts to be debited and credited, Analyze the effects of transactions, Record journal entries, Journalize a series of transactions.

units.title: Basis Accounting Process
units.text: Basis Accounting Process Analyze transactions and determine their effect on accounts, Post journal entries and prepare a trial balance, journalize transactions, post, and prepare a trial balance, Prepare a correct trial balance.

units.title: Accrual Accounting Concepts
units.text: Accrual Accounting Concepts Preparation of Financial Statement with adjustment entries – Closing Stock, Depreciation, Prepaid Expenses, unearned Revenue, Accruals.

units.title: Merchandising Operations and Multi-Step Income Statement
units.text: Merchandising Operations and Multi-Step Income Statement Journalizing Sales transaction, Journalizing Purchase transaction, Net Purchases and Cost of goods purchased, Journalizing Perpetual inventory entries, Prepare Cost of Goods sold using Periodic system.

units.title: Reporting and Analyzing Inventory
units.text: Reporting and Analyzing Inventory Compute ending Inventory using LIFO and FIFO, Compute ending inventory using average cost, Compute inventory turnover and days in inventory, calculate ending inventory, COGS and Gross profit.

units.title: Fraud, Internal Control and Cash
units.text: Fraud, Internal Control and Cash Bank reconciliation, analyzing outstanding checks, Deposits in transit and outstanding checks, Journalize and post petty cash transactions and preparation of Cash budget.

units.title: Reporting and Analyzing Receivables
units.text: Reporting and Analyzing Receivables Record basic accounts receivable transactions, Prepare entry using percentage of receivables method, Prepare entry for credit card sale, Prepare a balance sheet presentation of receivables, Prepare entries to record allowance for doubtful accounts, Prepare journal entries for credit card and notes receivable transactions

units.title: Reporting and Analyzing Long-Lived Assets
units.text: Reporting and Analyzing Long-Lived Assets Determine the cost of land, Compute straight-line depreciation, Journalize equipment transactions for purchase, sale, retirement, depreciation, Compute depreciation under different methods

units.title: Reporting and Analyzing Liabilities
units.text: Reporting and Analyzing Liabilities Prepare entries for an interest-bearing note payable, Prepare entries for issuance of bonds, Journalize sales and related taxes, Record accrual of payroll taxes, Prepare journal entries for redemption of bonds, Prepare instalment payments schedule, journal entries for mortgage.

units.title: Reporting and Analyzing Stockholders’ Equity
units.text: Reporting and Analyzing Stockholders’ Equity Journalize issuance of par value common stock, Prepare entries for a cash dividend, Journalize issuance of common stock, Compare issuance of stock financing to issuance of bond financing, Journalize stock dividends.

units.title: Statement of Cash Flows
units.text: Statement of Cash Flows Compute net cash provided by operating activities – indirect, Determine cash received from sale of equipment, Classify transactions by type of activity, Prepare cash flow from operating activities indirect method, Prepare a statement of cash flows - indirect method.

objectives: This course provides basic orientation towards economic (micro and macroeconomic) principles and help them understand the functions of economic system. To combine elements of basic micro and macroeconomics. To familiarize with importance of economic approach in decision making. To understand the application of economic theories in day-to-day life. To understand broader aspects of the economy and its environment.

outcomes.text: Analyze and evaluate the impact of Economic Policies and its implication on the Economic Environment
Describe basic concepts of economics -Microeconomics
Orient themselves towards higher levels of learning
Handle economic data for policy purposes

units.text: Nature and Scope of Economics Introduction to Economics, Micro and Macro Economic Analysis, Positive and Normative Economics, Types of Economic Systems, Basic Economic Problems and Uses of Economic Resources-Production Possibility Curve, Recent Developments in the Field of Economics.

units.title: Analysis of Demand and Supply
units.text: Analysis of Demand and Supply Meaning and Determinants, Demand Curve and Supply Curve, Equilibrium of Demand and Supply, Shift in Demand and Supply, Demand and Supply Function, law of Demand and law of Supply, Effects of Change in Demand and Supply, Types of Elasticity of Demand, Uses of Elasticity of Demand.

units.text: Demand Estimation and Forecasting Meaning and Importance of Demand Forecasting, Methods of Forecasting, Introduction to Regression (Simple-bivariate) Analysis, OLS Method, Estimating and interpreting the regression Coefficients and Forecasting.

units.text: Utility Analysis Types of Utility, Cardinal and Ordinal Utility Analysis, Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility (DMU), Uses of Law of DMU in Decision Making, Indifference Curve analysis and Consumer Equilibrium.

units.text: Production Analysis Meaning of Production and Productivity, Short-run and Long-run Production Function, Total-Average-Marginal Product, Law of Variable Proportions, Law of Return and Return to Scale, Classification of Isoquant Curve and Producer’s Equilibrium, Economic region of production, Production Forecasting Using Data Analysis Technique.

units.text: Market Structure and Analysis Introduction and Features of Market Structure (Perfect Competition, Monopoly, Monopolistic Competition, Oligopoly and Duopoly), Equilibrium Analysis of Firm, Price Discrimination and Degrees of Price Discrimination, Dumping.

units.text: Welfare Analysis and Game Theory Partial and General Equilibrium, Role of Government in Socio-Economic Welfare, Consumer and Producer Surplus, Price Ceiling and Price Floor, market Failure and State Intervention, Introduction to Game Theory.

objectives: The course would enable students to get a brief introduction of the Indian Constitution and its principles. The students would have knowledge of concept of ‘State’ and interdependencies of its institutions vis a vis their relation with fundamental rights.

objectives: The course aims to apply electrical circuit fundamentals to the AC and DC circuits and study electromagnetism. Describe various measuring devices and sensors

Energy Sources: Ideal and Practical Voltage and Current Sources, Concept of Dependent and Independent Sources (Definitions only for dependent or controlled sources). No Change No Change

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems
prerequisites: Knowledge of Permutation, Combination and Pre-Calculus.
objectives: This course aims to introduce basic concepts of probability theory and calculus. The course will equip the students with intermediate to advanced level concepts in probability and statistics using calculus tools that will help them to tackle relevant problems within engineering domain.

outcomes.text: explain the basic concepts of differential and integral calculus, statistical data, probability and random variables
solve problems involving conditional probability, moments and various probability distributions, differential and integral calculus
apply knowledge of various probability distributions, measures of central tendency, differential and integral calculus to evaluate real life problems
demonstrate use of differential and integral calculus in probability theory.

units.title: Descriptive Statistics
units.text: Descriptive Statistics Classification and tabulation of univariate data, graphical representation, Frequency curves. Descriptive measures - central tendency and dispersion. Bivariate data: Summarization, marginal and conditional frequency distribution.

units.title: Probability
units.text: Probability Concept of experiments, sample space, event. Definition of Combinatorial Probability, Conditional Probability, Bayes Theorem.

units.title: Expected values and moments
units.text: Expected values and moments Mathematical expectation and its properties, Moments (including variance) and their properties, interpretation, Moment generating function.

units.title: Probability distributions
units.text: Probability distributions Discrete probability distributions: Binomial, Poisson and Geometric distributions, Uniform distribution. Continuous probability distributions: Exponential, Normal distribution, Chi- square, t, F distributions.

units.title: Calculus
units.text: Calculus Basic concept of differential calculus and integral calculus, application of double and triple integral.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Business Systems
objectives: 1. Develop problem solving skills using basic Sequential Logic Structure, Decisions and Loops. 2. Enable students to implement complex problems using the knowledge of Arrays, Functions, Structures and Pointers.

outcomes.text: apply the knowledge of basic programming constructs, decision making, and iterations
develop modular programs using functions and concept of recursion
implement programs using concept of arrays, pointers and structures
understand Unix interface and perform file handling

units.text: Types Operator and Expressions with discussion of variable naming and Hungarian Notation Variable Names, Data Type and Sizes (Little Endian Big Endian), Constants, Declarations, Arithmetic Operators, Relational Operators, Logical Operators, Type Conversion, Increment Decrement Operators, Bitwise Operators, Assignment Operators and Expressions, Precedence and Order of Evaluation, proper variable naming and Hungarian Notation.

Control Flow with discussion on structured and unstructured programming Statements and Blocks, If-Else-If, Switch, Loops – while, do, for, break and continue, goto Labels, structured and un-structured programming.

Functions and Program Structure with discussion on standard library Basics of functions, parameter passing and returning type, C main return as integer, External, Auto, Local, Static, Register Variables, Scope Rules, Block structure, Initialization, Recursion, Preprocessor, Standard Library Functions and return types.

units.title: Pointers and Arrays
units.text: Pointers and Arrays Pointers and address, Pointers and Function Arguments, Pointers and Arrays, Address Arithmetic, character Pointers and Functions, Pointer Arrays, Pointer to Pointer, Multi-dimensional array and Row/column major formats, Initialization of Pointer Arrays, Command line arguments, Pointer to functions, complicated declarations and how they are evaluated.

units.title: Structures
units.text: Structures Basic Structures, Structures and Functions, Array of structures, Pointer of structures.

units.title: Input and Output

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: The course aims to apply electrical circuit fundamentals to the AC and DC circuits and study electromagnetism. The course also intends to focus on understanding the concept and working of the transformer, measuring devices, and sensors. The course concludes with a case study discussion of IoT applications.

outcomes.text: Explain DC network theorems and apply them to solve DC circuits
Understand AC fundamentals and use them to solve AC circuits
Understand the operating principle of the transformer
Describe various measuring devices and sensors
Understand the application of computer science and electrical engineering principles in real-time application

units.title: Introduction to DC Circuit Fundamentals
units.text: Introduction to DC Circuit Fundamentals: Definitions: Electrical Potential and Potential Difference, Current, Work, Power and Energy, Active and Passive Elements and Circuits, Linear and Non-linear Elements and Circuits, Unilateral and Bilateral Elements and Circuits. Network Elements: Ohm's Law, Resistance and its Properties, Concept of Series and Parallel Connection in Network, Series and Parallel Connection of Resistors, Concept of Voltage Division and Current Division, Capacitance, Dielectric Capacitor, Composite Dielectric Capacitors, Series and Parallel Connection of Capacitors, Energy Stored in Capacitors, Charging and Discharging of capacitors (Transient Analysis), Self and Mutual Inductance, Series and Parallel Connection of Inductor, Energy Stored in Inductor, Charging and Discharging of Inductor (Transient Analysis). Energy Sources: Ideal and Practical Voltage and Current Sources, Concept of Dependent and Independent Sources (Definitions only for dependent or controlled sources).

units.title: DC Network Analysis
units.text: DC Network Analysis: Kirchoff's Laws and its Application to Network Solution, Simplifications of Networks using Series-Parallel and Star-Delta Transformation, Mesh Current and Node Voltage Method for DC Network Analysis Network Theorems (Analysis using independent sources only and no dependent sources): Superposition theorem, Thevenin's theorem, Norton's Theorem, Maximum Power Transfer theorem (For DC Circuits Only)

units.title: AC Circuits Fundamentals and Analysis
units.text: AC Circuits Fundamentals and Analysis: Generation of 1-phase AC Signal AC Waveform Definitions: Cycle, Frequency, Phase, Instantaneous Amplitude, Peak Amplitude, Average Value, RMS Value, Form Factor, Peak Factor Concept of Leading and Lagging AC Quantities Analysis of R, L, C, RL, RC, RLC Series Circuit, RLC Parallel Circuit, Phasor Representation in Polar and Rectangular Form, Concept of Impedance, Admittance, Active, Reactive, Apparent and Complex Power, Power Factor 3-Phase AC Signal Generation, 3-Phase Balanced AC Circuits (Star (⅄) Connection, Delta (∆) Connection)

units.title: Transformer
units.text: Transformer: Single Phase Ideal Transformer: Definition, Construction, and the Principle of Operation, EMF equation, Voltage Ratio, Current Ratio Transformer Losses (definitions only) Loaded and Unloaded Lossy Transformer, Input Impedance of Transformer, KVA Rating, Efficiency, and Voltage Regulation

units.title: Measurements and Sensors
units.text: Measurements and Sensors: Definitions: Measurements, Sensors, Actuators, and Transducers Difference between Sensors and Transducers, Classification of Sensors and Transducers, Operating Principles of Wattmeter, Ammeter, and Voltameter, Introduction to IoT Devices and Sensors Case Study of IoT Application

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems
objectives: This course aims to provide the student with a broad understanding of the physical principles to help them develop critical thinking and quantitative reasoning skills, to empower them to think creatively about scientific problems and experiments

outcomes.text: demonstrate conceptual understanding of fundamental physics principles
relate and interpret physical information in verbal, visual, experimental and mathematical form
solve problems using qualitative and quantitative reasoning including mathematical techniques

units.title: Oscillation and fundamental of wave optics
units.text: Oscillation and fundamental of wave optics Periodic motion-simple harmonic motion-characteristics of simple harmonic motion-vibration of simple springs mass system. Resonance-definition., damped harmonic oscillator – heavy, critical and light damping, energy decay in a damped harmonic oscillator, quality factor, forced mechanical and electrical oscillators.

units.title: Interference-principle of superposition-young’s experiment
units.text: Interference-principle of superposition-young’s experiment Theory of interference fringes-types of Interference-Fresnel’s prism- Newton’s rings, Diffraction-Two kinds of diffraction-Difference between interference and diffraction-Fresnel’s half period zone and zone plate-Fraunhofer diffraction at single slit-plane diffraction grating. Temporal and Spatial Coherence.

units.title: Polarization of light
units.text: Polarization of light Polarization - Concept of production of polarized beam of light from two SHM acting at right angle; plane, elliptical and circularly polarized light, Brewster’s law, double refraction.

units.title: Basic Idea of Electromagnetisms
units.text: Basic Idea of Electromagnetisms Continuity equation for current densities, Maxwell’s equation in vacuum and non-conducting medium

units.title: Quantum Mechanics and Crystallography
units.text: Quantum Mechanics and Crystallography Introduction - Planck’s quantum theory- Matter waves, de-Broglie wavelength, Heisenberg’s Uncertainty principle, time independent and time dependent Schrödinger’s wave equation, Physical significance of wave function, Particle in a one dimensional potential box, Heisenberg Picture. Crystallography - Basic terms-types of crystal systems, Bravais lattices, miller indices, d spacing, Atomic packing factor for SC, BCC, FCC and HCP structures. Semiconductor Physics - conductor, semiconductor and Insulator; Basic concept of Band theory

units.title: Laser and Fiber optics
units.text: Laser and Fiber optics Einstein’s theory of matter radiation interaction and A and B coefficients; amplification of light by population inversion, different types of lasers: Ruby Laser, CO2 and Neodymium lasers; Properties of laser beams: mono-chromaticity, coherence, directionality and brightness, laser speckles, applications of lasers in engineering. Fiber optics and Applications, Types of optical fibers

units.title: Thermodynamics
units.text: Thermodynamics Zeroth law of thermodynamics, first law of thermodynamics, brief discussion on application of 1st law, second law of thermodynamics and concept of Engine, entropy, change in entropy in reversible and irreversible processes, third law of thermodynamics.

text_books: 1. Beiser A, Concepts of Modern Physics, 7th edition Tata McGraw Hill International, (SIE) 2015. 2. David Halliday, Robert Resnick, Jearl Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, 11th Edition Wileyplus, 2018.
reference_books: 1. Ajoy Ghatak, Optics, 6th Edition,McGraw Hill Education (India), 2017. 2. Sears & Zemansky, University Physics, 14th Edition, Pearson Education, Addison- Wesley, 2017. 3. Jenkins and White, Fundamentals of Optics, 4th Edition, McGraw-Hill, 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus. Laboratory Experiments 1. Magnetic field along the axis of current carrying coil – Stewart and Gee 2. Determination of Hall coefficient of semi-conductor 3. Determination of Plank constant 4. Determination of wave length of light by Laser diffraction method 5. Determination of wave length of light by Newton’s Ring method 6. Determination of laser and optical fiber parameters 7. Determination of Stefan’s Constant.

program: B Tech CSBS
objectives: This course aims to develop in students an ability to articulate clearly, ethically, and persuasively through creating an awareness of the fundamentals of language, morality, communication as well as through self-awareness

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the basic tenets of communication and language to be utilized while communicating
Apply relevant language usage and communication rules to listen, write, present and connect
Analyze various interpersonal scenarios towards applying appropriate communication tools and strategies in the given context
Evaluate a particular context to generate comparable and appropriate communication based solutions that are socially and ethically relevant

units.title: The Basic Tenets of Communication
units.text: The Basic Tenets of Communication Understanding Basics of communication- Communication process and Modes of Communication-Oral, written, formal-upward, downward, horizontal, vertical, Informal-grapevine, types of grapevine, advantages and disadvantages and managing grapevine; Verbal and Nonverbal communication; Interpersonal and Intrapersonal Communication barriers to communication-Socio cultural, physical, psychological; organizational etc. Intrapersonal Communication: Creating self- awareness –Multiple Intelligence Theory and application, “anubhav” or experiential activities; SWOT analyses on self and Johari Window in groups

units.title: Understanding Written Communication
units.text: Understanding Written Communication Language Usage-Articles, prepositions, sentence formation; punctuation, active passive voice, tenses, subject and verb agreement; Pronoun and antecedent agreement; vocabulary, idioms and phrases; common errors in writing; Seven Cs of communication; organizing written content- In theory and application thorough- blog writing; articles writing; bulletin boards/newsletters

units.title: Reading and Listening for communication
units.text: Reading and Listening for communication Importance of reading; setting and following reading lists, eclectic and speed reading, speed reading techniques- increasing eye span, skimming, scanning, SQ3R technique; passage based reading comprehension; Listening-Importance of listening to communicate; types of listening; barriers to listening ; Do’s and Don’ts for Active Listening

units.title: TALK MAIL WRITE CONNECT (TMWC)
units.text: TALK MAIL WRITE CONNECT (TMWC) Presentation Skills- audience analyses, Dos and Don’ts of PPT, Nonverbal elements in presentations, different modes of delivery and eliminating stage fear; Group Discussions- skills evaluated, dos and don’ts; Understanding Social media and leveraging social media platforms to connect, network and campaign, vision and mission statements, planning and running Brand campaigns; emails-format, etiquette and content; summarization; story writing and resume designing (basic version)

units.title: Team Work and Value Orientation
units.text: Team Work and Value Orientation Types of teams; effective team meetings-setting agenda; keeping minutes of meeting, Minutes formats; Belbin’s team roles. Ethical communication- slander, libel and misrepresentation of information (case studies in ethical communication) Value based mini case examples to imbibe concepts of morality, values and ethics

text_books: 1. Courtland Bovee, John Thill and Roshan Lal Raina, Business Communication Today, 14th ed. Pearson, 2013 2. Mark Lester and Larry Beason; The McGraw Hill Handbook of English Grammar and Usage,1st ed. McGraw Hill Education, 2017
reference_books: 1. M. McCarthy and Felicity O’Dell, English Vocabulary in Use, 3rd ed. Cambridge University Press, 2002 2. S Moriarty, N Mitchell, W Wells, Advertising & IMC: Principles and Practice, 2nd ed. Pearson Education India, 2016

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems
prerequisites: Knowledge of Basic Concepts in Algebra.
objectives: This course aims at providing adequate exposure to the theory and applications of Linear Algebra. It develops in students the computational competency in the subject and an ability to apply the theoritical constructs and computational techniques to solve problems within Engineering domain

outcomes.text: Demonstrate understanding of fundamental concepts of linear algebra
Make use of computational techniques of linear algebra to solve related problems
Analyse linear transformations, systems of linear equations and matrices
Demonstrate understanding of applications of linear algebra

units.title: Matrices and Determinants
units.text: Matrices and Determinants Introduction to Matrices and Determinants; Solution of Linear Equations; Cramer's rule; Inverse of a Matrix.

units.title: Rank of Matrix
units.text: Rank of Matrix Vectors and linear combinations; Rank of a matrix; Gaussian elimination; LU Decomposition; Solving Systems of Linear Equations using the tools of Matrices.

units.title: Vector Space
units.text: Vector Space Vector space; Basis; Dimension; Orthogonality; Projections; Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization and QR decomposition.

units.title: Linear transformation, Eigenvalues and vectors
units.text: Linear transformation, Eigenvalues and vectors Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors; Cayley Hamilton Theorem, Diagonalisation; Positive definite matrices; Linear transformations; Hermitian and unitary matrices.

units.title: Introduction to applications
units.text: Introduction to applications Singular value decomposition and Principal component analysis; Introduction to their applications in Image Processing and Machine Learning.

text_books: 1. David Poole, Linear Algebra: A Modern Introduction, Brooks/Cole, Cengage Learning, 4th Edition 2014. 2. B. S. Grewal, Higher Engineering Mathematics, Khanna Publication, 44th Edition 2017.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge of data structures and algorithms so that students can identify and implement appropriate data structure and determine the computational complexity of the given problem

outcomes.text: Determine the space and time complexity
Identify and implement appropriate linear data structure for the given problem
Identify and implement appropriate non-linear data structure for the given problem
Differentiate and Implement various searching, sorting algorithms and hashing

units.title: Basic
units.text: Basic Terminologies & Introduction to Algorithm and Data Organization: Algorithm specification, Recursion, Performance analysis, Asymptotic Notation - The Big-O, Omega and Theta notation, Programming Style, Refinement of Coding - Time-Space Trade Off, Testing, Data Abstraction

units.title: Linear Data Structure
units.text: Linear Data Structure: Array, Stack, Queue, Linked-list and its types, Various Representations, Operations & Applications of Linear Data Structures

units.title: Non-linear Data Structure
units.text: Non-linear Data Structure: Trees (Binary Tree, Threaded Binary Tree, Binary Search Tree, B & B+ Tree, AVL Tree, Splay Tree) and Graphs (Directed, Undirected), Various Representations, Operations (search and traversal algorithms and complexity analysis) & Applications of Non- Linear Data Structures

units.title: Searching and Sorting on Various Data Structures
units.text: Searching and Sorting on Various Data Structures: Sequential Search, Binary Search, Breadth First Search, Depth First Search, Insertion Sort, Selection Sort, Shell Sort, Divide and Conquer Sort, Merge Sort, Quick Sort, Heap Sort, Introduction to Hashing

units.title: File
units.text: File: Organisation (Sequential, Direct, Indexed Sequential, Hashed) and various types of accessing schemes.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems
prerequisites: 1. Theory of semiconductor materials, their atomic structures and properties. 2. DC circuit analysis, AC fundamentals.
objectives: The aim of the course is that the student should understand working principle, characteristics and simple applications of basic electronic devices. The course also helps students to understand the application of these devices in advanced circuits such as amplifiers. It also intends to impart hands on experience in assembling and testing simple circuits.

outcomes.text: Describe the fundamentals of semiconductors
Understand characteristics and working of diodes, BJTs and FETs and solve simple circuits
Describe operational amplifier and illustrate its applications
Describe digital electronics fundamentals

units.title: Semiconductors
units.text: Semiconductors: Crystalline material: Mechanical properties, Energy band theory, Fermi levels; Conductors, Semiconductors & Insulators: electrical properties, band diagrams. Semiconductors: intrinsic & extrinsic, energy band diagram, P&N-type semiconductors, drift & diffusion carriers.

units.title: Diodes and Diode Circuits
units.text: Diodes and Diode Circuits: Formation of P-N junction, energy band diagram, built-in-potential, forward and reverse biased P-N junction, formation of depletion zone, V-I characteristics, Zener breakdown, Avalanche breakdown and its reverse characteristics; Junction capacitance and Varactor diode. Simple diode circuits, load line, linear piecewise model; Rectifier circuits: half wave, full wave, PIV, DC voltage and current, ripple factor, efficiency, idea of regulation.

units.title: Bipolar Junction Transistors
units.text: Bipolar Junction Transistors: Formation of PNP / NPN junctions, energy band diagram; transistor mechanism and principle of transistors, CE, CB, CC configuration, transistor characteristics: cut-off active and saturation mode, transistor action, injection efficiency, base transport factor and current amplification factors for CB and CE modes. Biasing and Bias stability: calculation of stability factor

units.title: Field Effect Transistors
units.text: Field Effect Transistors: Concept of Field Effect Transistors (channel width modulation), Gate isolation types, JFET Structure and characteristics, MOSFET Structure and characteristics, depletion and enhancement type; CS, CG, CD configurations; CMOS: Basic Principles

units.title: Feed Back Amplifier, Oscillators and Operational Amplifiers
units.text: Feed Back Amplifier, Oscillators and Operational Amplifiers: Concept (Block diagram), properties, positive and negative feedback, loop gain, open loop gain, feedback factors; topologies of feedback amplifier; effect of feedback on gain, output impedance, input impedance, sensitivities (qualitative), bandwidth stability; effect of positive feedback: instability and oscillation, condition of oscillation, Barkhausen criteria. Introduction to integrated circuits, operational amplified and its terminal properties; Application of operational amplifier; inverting and non-inverting mode of operation, Adders, Subtractors, Constant-gain multiplier, Voltage follower, Comparator, Integrator, Differentiator

units.title: Digital Electronics Fundamentals
units.text: Digital Electronics Fundamentals: Difference between analog and digital signals, Logic ICs, half and full adder/subtractor, multiplexers, demultiplexers, flip-flops, shift registers, counters.

Parikh, Millman’s Integrated Electronics, McGraw Hill Education, 2nd Edition 2017. 3. M. Morris Mano, Digital Logic & Computer Design, Pearson Education India; 4th edition 2016.

Banerjee, Solid State Electronic Devices, Pearson, 7th Edition 2014. 3. A. Paul Malvino, Electronic Principles, McGraw Hill Education, 8th Edition 2016. 4. program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems
objectives: 1. Understand fundamental financial concepts of Microeconomics and Macroeconomics.

outcomes.text: Describe how microeconomic models can be used to consider fundamental economic choices of households and firms
Explain how macroeconomic models can be used to analyse the economy as a whole
Elucidate how government policy influences microeconomic choices and macroeconomic outcomes.

units.title: Microeconomics
units.text: Microeconomics: Principles of Demand and Supply — Supply Curves of Firms — Elasticity of Supply; Demand Curves of Households — Elasticity of Demand; Equilibrium and Comparative Statics (Shift of a Curve and Movement along the Curve); Welfare Analysis — Consumers’ and Producers’ Surplus — Price Ceilings and Price Floors; Consumer Behaviour — Axioms of Choice — Budget Constraints and Indifference Curves; Consumer’s Equilibrium — Effects of a Price Change, Income and Substitution Effects —Derivation of a Demand Curve; Applications — Tax and Subsidies — Intertemporal Consumption — Suppliers’ Income Effect; Theory of Production — Production Function and Iso- quants — Cost Minimization; Cost Curves — Total, Average and Marginal Costs — Long Run and Short Run Costs; Equilibrium of a Firm Under Perfect Competition; Monopoly and Monopolistic Competition

units.title: Macroeconomics
units.text: Macroeconomics: National Income and its Components — GNP, NNP, GDP, NDP; Consumption Function; Investment; Simple Keynesian Model of Income Determination and the Keynesian Multiplier; Government Sector — Taxes and Subsidies; External Sector — Exports and Imports; Money — Definitions; Demand for Money —Transactionary and Speculative Demand; Supply of Money — Bank’s Credit Creation Multiplier; Integrating Money and Commodity Markets — IS, LM Model; Business Cycles and Stabilization — Monetary and Fiscal Policy — Central Bank and the Government; The Classical Paradigm — Price and Wage Rigidities — Voluntary and Involuntary Unemployment

text_books: 1. Microeconomics, Pindyck, Robert S., and Daniel L. Rubinfeld. 2. Macroeconomics, Dornbusch, Fischer and Startz. 3. Economics, Paul Anthony Samuelson, William D. Nordhaus
reference_books: 1. Intermediate Microeconomics: A Modern Approach, Hal R, Varian. 2. Principles of Macroeconomics, N. Gregory Mankiw.

program: B Tech Computer Science and Business Systems
prerequisites: Completion of Business communication and Value Science-I
objectives: This course aims to train the students in skills like conducting research and planning for designing impactful and credible communication. Also, it aims at sensitizing them towards overcoming bias; embracing diversity and equality leading to fair, creative and productive workplace practices.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate awareness of the tools of structured written communication essential for communicating on diverse media
Apply principles of communication towards designing structured and impactful oral and written communication that can be disseminated through diverse and contemporary media
Analyze personality types, concepts of morality and diversity to create and implement bias free and impactful solutions in societal as well as professional contexts
Create well- researched and contextualized reports, presentations and other write-ups applying the essential communication tools and principles

units.title: Tools of Structured Written Communication
units.text: Tools of Structured Written Communication Principles of Lucid Writing; Vocabulary reinforcement; cloze; Language Usage- Tenses; Modification; Parallelism, Recapitulation practice- Subject verb agreement; pronoun antecedent agreement; Vision Mission Writing; Writing Taglines for Brands; Running Brand Campaigns; e-magazine Creation; Blog writing, Email writing based on organizational contexts and scenarios.

units.title: Read-Research-Report
units.text: Read-Research-Report Eclectic, and paragraph-based reading; Research- Importance of research; Ethical research, copyright, and plagiarism; -Questionnaires as data collection tools; Interviews as data collection tools etc.; Reports-Types, formats, categories, letter and memo reports; Literature review writing; Abstract Writing; Presentation of a Project Report.

units.title: Leadership Oriented Learning
units.text: Leadership Oriented Learning Designing Resumes; cover letters, and Facing Personal Interviews; telephonic and virtual Interviews; Understanding Team/group Dynamics- roles; norms, equity, diversity, pressure to conform, group cohesiveness; group size, social loafing and measures to control social loafing group think and group polarization; Decision Making-Rational Decision-Making Model; satisfice, Group decision making techniques-Brainstorming, nominal group technique, Delphi technique, electronic method, Bias in decision making; Big Five personality traits and their implications on learning, behavior and interpersonal communication.

Understanding and sharing the basic concepts of Morality and Diversity Diversity- Types of Diversity; Social context to Diversity; Organizational Diversity-Types and importance; Impact of diversity on elements like creativity, productivity, decision making etc.; Setting an organizational culture that values and encourages diversity; Moral Value based discussions and mini case examples; case-based examples on Diversity and interpersonal communication settings.

Anderson, Technical Communication-A Reader Centric Approach, 9th Edition, Cengage Publications, 2017. 3. Hory Sankar Mukherjee, ‘’Business Communication: Connecting at work’’, 2nd Edition, Oxford University Press, 2016.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems
objectives: This course will help students to develop sound knowledge and skills in theoretical, computational and application-oriented statistics. The course will equip the students with intermediate to advanced level concepts in statistics using probability theory and basic concepts in statistics that will help them to tackle relevant problems within engineering domain.

outcomes.text: explain the concepts of sampling techniques, estimation, sufficient statistic, parametric and non-parametric inference
solve problems involving correlation, linear and multiple regression, estimation techniques and time series
apply knowledge of time series, parametric and non-parametric inference to analyze statistical data
use various concepts in R programming to analyze statistical data samples.

units.title: Sampling Techniques
units.text: Sampling Techniques: Random sampling. Sampling from finite and infinite populations. Estimates and standard error (sampling with replacement and sampling without replacement), Sampling distribution of sample mean, stratified random sampling.

units.title: Linear Statistical Models
units.text: Linear Statistical Models: Scatter diagram. Linear regression and correlation. Least squares method. Rank correlation. Multiple regression & multiple correlation, Analysis of variance (one way, two way with as well as without interaction).

units.title: Estimation
units.text: Estimation: Point estimation, criteria for good estimates (un- biasedness, consistency), Methods of estimation including maximum likelihood estimation.

units.title: Sufficient Statistic
units.text: Sufficient Statistic: Concept & examples, complete sufficiency, their application in estimation.

units.title: Test of hypothesis
units.text: Test of hypothesis: Concept & formulation, Type I and Type II errors, Neyman Pearson lemma, Procedures of testing.

units.title: Non-parametric
units.text: Non-parametric Inference: Comparison with parametric inference, Use of order statistics. Sign test, Wilcoxon signed rank test, Mann-Whitney test, Run test, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. Spearman’s and Kendall’s test. Tolerance region.

units.title: Basics of Time Series Analysis & Forecasting
units.text: Basics of Time Series Analysis & Forecasting: Stationary, ARIMA Models: Identification, Estimation and Forecasting.

identify and implement appropriate linear data structure for the given problem
identify and implement appropriate non-linear data structure for the given problem
differentiate and Implement various searching, sorting algorithms and hashing.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems
prerequisites: 1. Theory of semiconductor materials, their atomic structures and properties. 2. DC circuit analysis, AC fundamentals.
objectives: The aim of the course is that the student should understand working principle, characteristics and simple applications of basic electronic devices. The course also helps students to understand the application of these devices in advanced circuits such as amplifiers. It also intends to impart hands on experience in assembling and testing simple circuits.

outcomes.text: describe the fundamentals of semiconductors
understand characteristics and working of diodes, BJTs and FETs and solve simple circuits
describe operational amplifier and illustrate its applications
describe digital electronics fundamentals.

units.title: Semiconductors
units.text: Semiconductors: Crystalline material: Mechanical properties, Energy band theory, Fermi levels; Conductors, Semiconductors & Insulators: electrical properties, band diagrams. Semiconductors: intrinsic & extrinsic, energy band diagram, P&N-type semiconductors, drift & diffusion carriers.

units.title: Diodes and Diode Circuits
units.text: Diodes and Diode Circuits: Formation of P-N junction, energy band diagram, built-in-potential, forward and reverse biased P-N junction, formation of depletion zone, V-I characteristics, Zener breakdown, Avalanche breakdown and its reverse characteristics; Junction capacitance and Varactor diode. Simple diode circuits, load line, linear piecewise model; Rectifier circuits: half wave, full wave, PIV, DC voltage and current, ripple factor, efficiency, idea of regulation.

units.title: Bipolar Junction Transistors
units.text: Bipolar Junction Transistors: Formation of PNP / NPN junctions, energy band diagram; transistor mechanism and principle of transistors, CE, CB, CC configuration, transistor characteristics: cut-off active and saturation mode, transistor action, injection efficiency, base transport factor and current amplification factors for CB and CE modes. Biasing and Bias stability: calculation of stability factor

units.title: Field Effect Transistors
units.text: Field Effect Transistors: Concept of Field Effect Transistors (channel width modulation), Gate isolation types, JFET Structure and characteristics, MOSFET Structure and characteristics, depletion and enhancement type; CS, CG, CD configurations; CMOS: Basic Principles

units.title: Feed Back Amplifier, Oscillators and Operational Amplifiers
units.text: Feed Back Amplifier, Oscillators and Operational Amplifiers: Concept (Block diagram), properties, positive and negative feedback, loop gain, open loop gain, feedback factors; topologies of feedback amplifier; effect of feedback on gain, output impedance, input impedance, sensitivities (qualitative), bandwidth stability; effect of positive feedback: instability and oscillation, condition of oscillation, Barkhausen criteria. Introduction to integrated circuits, operational amplified and its terminal properties; Application of operational amplifier; inverting and non-inverting mode of operation, Adders, Subtractors, Constant-gain multiplier, Voltage follower, Comparator, Integrator, Differentiator

units.title: Digital Electronics Fundamentals
units.text: Digital Electronics Fundamentals: Difference between analog and digital signals, Logic ICs, half and full adder/subtractor, multiplexers, demultiplexers, flip-flops, shift registers, counters.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems
objectives: 1. Understand fundamental financial concepts of Microeconomics and Macroeconomics.

outcomes.text: describe how microeconomic models can be used to consider fundamental economic choices of households and firms
explain how macroeconomic models can be used to analyse the economy as a whole
elucidate how government policy influences microeconomic choices and macroeconomic outcomes.

objectives: 1. To teach the drawbacks of classical physics in explaining several experimental facts and old quantum theory. 2. To discuss the necessity of new mechanics (i.e. quantum mechanics), the laws related to it and their applications. 3. To understand the idea of statistical mechanics and its applications.

outcomes.text: explain the basic laws related to quantum mechanics and apply them to solve related problems.
elucidate the concepts of statistical mechanics and solve problems using the same.

objectives: This course introduces the fundamental concepts and techniques underlying the construction of digital systems. It further provides insight into designing digital logic circuits using basic building blocks and necessary techniques required in computer hardware design.

outcomes.text: Translate different number systems and binary codes, including weighted and non-weighted codes.
Simplify Boolean expressions using De Morgan’s Theorem, SOP, POS, and Karnaugh maps.
Build combinational logic circuits such as adders, multiplexers, decoders, and encoders. .
Analyze sequential circuits, including flip-flops, registers, and counters.
Make use of VHDL for realizing basic digital logic circuits in different modeling styles.

units.title: Introduction to Digital Systems
units.text: Introduction to Digital Systems Number Systems - Binary, Octal, Hexadecimal, BCD, Conversion from one system to another, Binary subtraction using 1’s and 2’s complement method. Weighted codes - BCD and Binary, Non-weighted codes - Grey and Excess 3, conversion from one code to another.

objectives: This course aims to instil in prospective engineers’ knowledge of concepts and techniques in Linear Algebra and Differential Equations. It also prepares the students to deal with advanced level of Mathematics and applications that would be essential for their disciplines.

outcomes.text: Solve systems of linear equations using the matrix method and understand linear algebra concepts, including vector spaces, subspaces, basis, and dimension .
Analyze linear transformations by understanding their matrices, kernels, ranges and compute Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors of matrices and apply them to solve problems related to diagonalization .

Utilize the operator method and the method variation of parameters to find solutions of higher-order linear differential equations and the Euler-Cauchy equation .
Form partial differential equations and employ direct integration and separation of variables techniques to find solutions .
Apply concepts from linear algebra and differential equations to model and address real- world problems in engineering, physics, and applied sciences .

units.title: Experiments
units.text: Exp. No. Programming Topic 1. Concept: Implement a program using classes, objects, data members and member functions. Problem Statement: Create a class “Employee” to read and print information about an employee with the following data members: Name of the employee, ID of the employee, Department of the employee, Basic salary. Task: Perform the following functions to complete the operations: 1. Write a member function read_Employee() to initialize the object. 2. Write a member function to Calculate Gross salary and its components (declare them as data members) based on the following conditions: Dearness allowance (DA) = 50 % of basic salary HRA = 30 % basic salary TA = 10 % basic salary Gross Salary = basic salary + DA + HRA + TA. 3. Write a member function to display employee details with Gross Salary and all other components. 2. Concepts: Implement a program using Encapsulation, Abstractions and Array of Objects. Problem Statement: A school is developing Library Management system to maintain the records of the books. Where it performs basic operations such as making entry of the book, searching the book by book name and author name. It also shows availability of the books. Task: Create class to manage the books in “Library” with following data members and functions. Name of the book Author of the book Price of the book No. of copies Implement member functions to perform the following operations: Read the data of 5 books – include books in the library. Display the data of books – print the list of all the books in the library. Search the specified book in the Library by name, if it is available or not, if available then display no of copies of the book. Search the specified book in the Library by Author Name, display all the books of the same author. 3 Concept: Implement a program using the concepts of constructor to initialize the object. Problem Statement: A customer can open account in the bank with following attributes. A customer can performs basic operations with the account created using class called “Bank Account”. Customer Name Address Account Number Age Balance Amount Task: Implement following functions to perform operations with an account: 1. Use the parameterized constructor to initialize the array of objects. 2. Write a function to withdraw amount after checking account no. 3. Write a function to deposit amount after checking account no. 4. Write a function to display balance amount after checking account no. 5. Write a function to display the Customer Profile. 4. Concept: Implement a program using Inheritance, Runtime polymorphism and Modelling classes. Problem Statement: A bank want to extend two more insurance services to their customers along with basic bank operations performed using “Saving Bank Account”. These two additional services will be implemented without changing existing bank account class. So, two additional classes are created by deriving features from the “Bank Account”. These classes are name as “Life Insurance” and “Car Insurance”. Premium of both the insurance policies are linked to bank account of the customer so that it can be directly deducted from their saving account and current balance will be displayed after every deduction. Features derived from the base classes are shown in the following diagram. The “Claim” class is used to settle the claim amount and deposited in the respective saving bank account.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech (All Programs except for AI, AIML, AIDS, Civil and Mechanical)
objectives: The objective of this course is to teach the limitations of classical physics in explaining several experimental facts leading to the development of quantum physics. Also, this course will expose the students to different applications of quantum mechanics, such as quantum tunneling and quantum computation.

outcomes.text: Understand the need for Quantum mechanics
Explain the basic laws related to quantum mechanics and apply them to solve related problems.
Apply the concept of quantum mechanics to real-life instrumentation and applications.
Understand the requirement of quantum computation and its various aspects.
Gauge the theoretical principles through laboratory experimentation, enhancing problem- solving abilities and technical proficiency in modern physics applications.

units.title: Limitations of classical physics and introduction to old quantum theory
units.text: Limitations of classical physics and introduction to old quantum theory: Introduction to Quantum Physics, Black body radiation, Explanation of it using the photon concept, Photoelectric effect, Compton effect, de Broglie hypothesis, Experiments demonstrating wave properties of electron: Electron interference (double slit experiment), Electron Diffraction (Davison - Germer experiment), Uncertainty Principle, Verification of matter waves.

units.title: Schrodinger Equation and its applications
units.text: Schrodinger Equation and its applications: Basic postulates of quantum mechanics, concept of wave function, Born’s interpretation of the wave function, Superposition principle of eigenstates. Concept of collapse of wave function. Time-dependent and time- independent Schrodinger Equation. Concept of the free particle, particle in an infinite and finite potential well, box problem. Bound vs. unbound states.

units.title: Concept of Quantum Tunnelling and its applications
units.text: Concept of Quantum Tunnelling and its applications: Concept of Quantum Tunnelling. Reflection and Transmission co-efficients. Few realistic examples of tunnelling, e.g., alpha decay, Probe microscopes (Scanning Tunnelling microscope). Simple Harmonic Oscillator, explanation in 1D (no detailed derivation). Hydrogen atom.

units.title: Introduction to Quantum Computing
units.text: Introduction to Quantum Computing: Limitations of classical computation, Difference between classical and quantum computer, Qubits, Bloch Sphere, Single Qubit Operations. Quantum Gates, Bell States, Quantum Entanglement.

text_books: 1. A. Beiser, S. Mahajan and S. Choudhury, “Concept of Modern Physics”, Tata McGraw Hill, 7th Edition (SIE) 2015. 2. Arthur Beiser, Perspectives of Modern Physics, McGraw Hill, 1969. 3. Bernhardt, Chris, Quantum computing for everyone, MIT Press, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Eisberg and Resnik, “Quantum Physics of Atoms, Molecules, Solids, Nuclei and Particles” Wiley, 2nd edition 2006. 2. R. A. Serwey, C. J. Moses, C. A. Moyer, “Modern Physics”, Thomson, 3rd edition 2005. 3. David J. Griffiths, “Introduction to Quantum Mechanics”, Pearson, 2nd Edition 2015. 4. Frederick Reif, “Fundamentals of Statistical and Thermal Physics”, Waveland press 2009. 5. McMahon, David, Quantum computing explained, John Wiley & Sons, 2007.
lab_work: Minimum 8 to 10 practical exercises based on the syllabus.

outcomes.text: Understand the historic evolution of the Indian Constitution, its drafting, nature and to understand the principles mentioned in its Preamble

Inculcate fundamental rights in its true sense and also the permissible restrictions upon it so as to enjoy these rights within permissible limits while simultaneously performing their duties and to apply these principles into their professional lives
Ingrain the structure of our polity and role of Judiciary in maintaining the basic structure of the Constitution

Attain knowledge of the Emergency provisions, when and how it is imposed, to know the additional powers the bestowed upon the Government at times of Emergency and to understand the Amendment procedure.

units.text: Nature, Characteristics and Sources of Indian Constitution

Fundamental rights and Fundamental duties – Concept of State, Right to Equality under Articles 14 and 15, Right to certain freedoms under Article 19, Right to Life and liberty under Article 21, Right to religion under Article 25 and 26, Right to remedy under Article 32 and Fundamental duties
Indian Judiciary – Concept of Supreme Court and High Courts, Appointment of Judges, Independence of Judiciary, Jurisdictions of Supreme Court and High Courts
Emergency Provisions – Concept of National Emergency under Article 352, Financial Emergency under Article 360 and President rule under Article 356 of the Constitution

program: B. Tech. Artificial Intelligence
objectives: 1. To inculcate human values to grow as a responsible human being 2. To maintain ethical conduct in discharging professional duties

outcomes.text: Understand the engineering code of ethics and be able to apply them as necessary
Understand moral complexities in many engineering activities and decision-making processes
Understand some of the contemporary issues in the engineering professions
Effectively communicate their knowledge and understanding of engineering ethics.

units.text: Introduction to Ethics-  Concept of morals and ethics,  Study of engineering ethics;  Laws and ethics; Personal and professional ethics.

Human centered Technology

program: B Tech /MBA Tech Artificial Intelligence B Tech (AI and ML and AI and DS)
objectives: The primary objectives of the outlined points are to cultivate a comprehensive understanding and proficiency in statistical theory, computation, and practical application. This includes a focus on theoretical foundations as well as computational techniques within the realm of statistics. Additionally, the aim is to foster competence in grasping the intricacies of random processes and various estimation methods, emphasizing a well-rounded comprehension of statistical concepts and techniques for effective analysis and decision-making.

outcomes.text: Know the basics of random processes
Know the spectral representation of random signals and calculate power spectral density, cross- spectral density
Recognize the applications of different types of random processes
Demonstrate the ability to understand the concepts of estimation, parametric and non- parametric inference
Apply knowledge of parametric and non-parametric techniques in estimation and statistical inference

units.title: Introduction to Random Processes
units.text: Introduction to Random Processes: Basic Concepts Classification of Random Processes, Statistics– first order, Second order, Wide- Sense Stationary Processes, Strict Sense Stationary Processes, Ergodic Random Processes.

units.title: Linear Systems with Random Inputs
units.text: Linear Systems with Random Inputs Fourier Transform of Random signals, Power Spectral Density, Cross Spectral Densities, Overview of linear system with deterministic inputs, Linear system with Discrete and continuous random inputs

units.title: Special Random Processes
units.text: Special Random Processes The Bernoulli Process, Random walk process, Gaussian process, Poisson process, Markov Process

units.title: Estimation Theory
units.text: Estimation Theory Point estimation, Interval estimate and confidence Interval, criteria for good estimates (un-biasedness, consistency), Methods of estimation including maximum likelihood estimation.

units.title: Hypothesis Testing
units.text: Hypothesis Testing Large Sample estimation of the population parameters and Hypothesis testing: Basics of Estimating the populations mean and difference; estimating the proportion and difference; large sample test for population mean, difference; large sample test for proportion, difference. Estimation of a population variance: Sampling distribution of variance, estimation. Inferences from small sample: Student’s t distribution; Small sample t test for following – A population mean, A difference between two means, Confidence interval. Rejection and Non-rejection region, Type I and Type II errors, testing hypothesis about a population mean using the Z- statistic, using p-values to test Hypothesis
