program: B Tech All Program (except EXTC, Data Science, Civil, Mechatronics, Mechanical, and CSE(DS) 311 (VT)] MBA Tech All Program (except Mechanical, Data Science)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Basic concepts in Number theory and Algebra.
objectives: The principal objective of the course is to train the students in the construction and understanding of mathematical proofs and common mathematical arguments. It will instil sound knowledge of different topics of discrete mathematics which students will readily apply in the subsequent courses of their programme.

outcomes.text: Understand fundamental concepts of discrete mathematics, including set theory, relations, functions, logic, and proof techniques.
Apply mathematical logic, predicate calculus, and proof techniques, including mathematical induction, to establish the validity of statements and theorems.
Analyse problems involving combinatorics, recurrence relations, generating functions, and the pigeonhole principle to model discrete structures.
Interpret graphs and trees, including their properties, colouring, connectivity, and spanning trees, and apply algorithms like Kruskal’s and Prim’s to solve network-related problems.
Formulate concepts from abstract algebra, including groups, rings, and fields, to construct mathematical models and solve real-world problems.

units.title: Set Theory, Relations and Functions
units.text: Set Theory, Relations and Functions Revision of prerequisite concepts - ‘Sets, Venn diagrams, Operations on sets, Laws of set theory’. Power set, The principle of Inclusion-Exclusion, Partitions of sets. Relations, Properties and types of binary relations, Equivalence relation. Functions, injective, surjective and bijective functions, Composition, inverse of a function.

units.title: Logic
units.text: Logic Revision of prerequisite concepts – ‘Propositions, Truth table, Laws of logic, Equivalence’. Satisfiability, tautology, validity, disjunctive and conjunctive normal forms, Predicates and Quantifiers, Proof Techniques, Mathematical Induction.

units.title: Combinatorics
units.text: Combinatorics Pigeonhole principle, Homogeneous and non-homogeneous linear recurrence relations with constant coefficients, Generating functions.

units.title: Graphs and Trees
units.text: Graphs and Trees Graphs and their properties, Degree, Connectivity, Path, Cycle, Eulerian graph, Hamiltonian graph, Planar graphs, Graph Coloring. Trees, Rooted trees, Spanning tree and minimum spanning tree, Kruskal’s and Prim’s algorithms for minimal spanning trees.

units.title: Abstract algebra
units.text: Abstract algebra Definition and examples of groups, subgroups, cyclic groups, group homomorphism, group isomorphisms. Definitions and Examples of Rings and Fields.

program: B Tech & MBA Tech (Artificial Intelligence), B Tech Cyber Security
objectives: This theory course introduces the internal structure, functioning, and organization of computer systems. It covers data representation, instruction execution, CPU architecture, memory hierarchy, and I/O organization. The course forms the foundation for advanced topics such as operating systems, embedded systems, and computer architecture design.

outcomes.text: Identify the major functional units of a computer system and their roles.
Explain number systems, data representation formats, and basic arithmetic operations used in computer hardware.
Illustrate instruction formats, addressing modes, and the complete instruction execution cycle.
Analyze the impact of memory hierarchy, cache mapping techniques, and virtual memory performance.
Differentiate between various I/O mechanisms such as programmed I/O, interrupt- driven I/O, and DMA.
Evaluate processor performance considering pipelining, hazards, and RISC vs. CISC design principles.

units.title: Introduction to Computer Organization
units.text: Introduction to Computer Organization Basic computer organization; CPU, memory, I/O, system bus; Von Neumann architecture and Harvard Architecture; Performance metrics (MIPS, CPI, throughput)

units.title: Data Representation & Arithmetic
units.text: Data Representation & Arithmetic Number system: binary, octal, hex; Fixed-point and floating-point representation; Signed magnitude, 1’s complement, 2’s complement; IEEE 754 floating-point format; ALU operations and overflow

units.title: CPU Architecture & Instruction Execution
units.text: CPU Architecture & Instruction Execution CPU components (ALU, registers, PC); Instruction formats and addressing modes; Instruction cycle: Fetch–Decode–Execute; Control unit: hardwired vs. microprogrammed

units.title: Memory Organization
units.text: Memory Organization Memory structure; Cache memory: mapping techniques & replacement policies; Memory hierarchy; Virtual memory, paging, TLB

units.title: Input/ Output Organization
units.text: Input/ Output Organization I/O mapped vs memory-mapped I/O; Interrupts: ISR, priority, and nested interrupts; DMA and I/O channels

units.title: Bus Structures & Modern Architectures
units.text: Bus Structures & Modern Architectures System buses: data, address, control; Bus arbitration; RISC vs. CISC; Basics of pipelining and multi-core processors

program: B Tech & MBA Tech (Artificial Intelligence)
prerequisites: Programming, Computer Organization and Architecture, Data Structures and Algorithms
objectives: The objective of this course is to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of operating system principles, including process management, CPU scheduling, synchronization, deadlock handling, memory management, and I/O systems. The course aims to develop students’ ability to analyze core operating system mechanisms and to relate theoretical concepts to real-world operating systems such as UNIX, mobile platforms, and modern heterogeneous computing environments.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental concepts of operating systems, including OS evolution, system calls, and resource management.
Analyze process management and CPU scheduling techniques, including process states, context switching, threads, and scheduling algorithms such as FCFS, SJF, Priority, and Round Robin.
Apply process synchronization and concurrency control mechanisms using critical sections, semaphores, monitors, and message passing to solve classical IPC problems.

Evaluate deadlock handling strategies and memory management techniques, including deadlock prevention, avoidance (Banker’s algorithm), paging, segmentation, virtual memory, and page replacement algorithms.

Compare I/O management, disk scheduling, and file management strategies, and relate operating system concepts to real-world case studies such as UNIX, mobile operating systems, and heterogeneous architectures.

units.title: Operating System Overview
units.text: Operating System Overview OS objectives, functions, evolution, types of OS. Processes, Files, System Calls, Resource Manager view. OS architecture, Virtual Machine, RTOS, Lightweight OS

units.title: Process and Process Scheduling
units.text: Process and Process Scheduling Process definition, relationships, states, transitions. PCB, Context Switching, Types of schedulers. Scheduling objectives, Preemptive vs Non-preemptive. Scheduling Algorithms: FCFS, SJF, SRTF, Priority and Round Robin. Multilevel scheduling, Threads

units.title: Process Concurrency
units.text: Process Concurrency Concurrent processes, precedence graphs, Critical Section, Race Conditions, Mutual Exclusion, Hardware Solution, Semaphores, Peterson’s Solution, The Producer / Consumer Problem, Monitors, Message Passing, Classical IPC Problems: Reader’s & Writer Problem, Barber’s shop problem

units.title: Deadlock
units.text: Deadlock Definition, Necessary and sufficient conditions for Deadlock, Deadlock Prevention, Deadlock Avoidance: Banker’s algorithm, Deadlock detection and Recovery, Dinning Philosopher Problem

units.title: Memory Management
units.text: Memory Management Basic concepts, Memory allocation: Contiguous Memory allocation – Fixed and variable partition– Internal and External fragmentation and Compaction. Basics of Virtual Memory – Hardware and control structures – Locality of reference, Page allocation, Partitioning, Paging, Page fault, Segmentation, Demand paging, Thrashing, Page Replacement algorithms: Optimal, First in First Out (FIFO), Least Recently used (LRU).

units.title: I/O Management and Disc Scheduling
units.text: I/O Management and Disc Scheduling I/O Management and Disc Scheduling: I/O devices, Direct Memory Access, Principles of I/O, Disk structure, Disk scheduling - FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK and C-LOOK, RAID.

units.title: File Management
units.text: File Management Overview, File Organization, File Directories, File Sharing

units.title: Case Study
units.text: Case Study Operating Systems for Heterogeneous Architectures (e.g., GPUs, TPUs), Unix case study- History, General structure, Unix file system: file abstraction, directories, mount points, implementation details. Processes: memory image, lifecycle, start of day. Mobile Operating Systems: ARM and Intel architectures

program: B Tech & MBA Tech Artificial Intelligence, B Tech AI and DS
objectives: This course aims at introducing the concept of discrete time signals and systems. Taking image as a discrete time signal, some methodologies for digital image processing are explored. This course would enable the students to develop a foundation for research in the fields like computer vision, machine learning, pattern recognition, etc.

outcomes.text: Classify discrete time signals and systems
Implement Discrete Fourier Transform on discrete time signals
Apply spatial domain and frequency domain techniques for image enhancement
Demonstrate the basic morphological operation such as dilation, erosion, opening and closing on the given image
Analyze images processed by various segmentation techniques
Explain the motion estimation and compensation techniques in video processing

units.title: Discrete-Time Signal and Discrete-Time System

Classification of Discrete-Time Signals, Classification of Discrete Systems, Linear Convolution formulation (without mathematical proof), Circular Convolution (without mathematical proof), LTI system, Concept of Impulse Response and Step Response

units.title: Image Fundamentals
units.text: Image Fundamentals Representation of digital image, spatial and gray level resolution, basic relationships between pixels, image file format and color models

units.title: Image Enhancement in Spatial domain and Frequency domain

Segmentation based on discontinuities -point, line, edge, image edge detection using Robert, Sobel, Prewitt masks, Laplacian mask, segmentation based on thresholding, region based segmentation- region growing, region splitting and merging

program: B Tech & MBA Tech Artificial Intelligence
objectives: This course provides knowledge of evolutionary computation techniques such as mechanisms of natural evolution--including genetic recombination, mutation, and natural selection--to automatically produce solutions to a wide range of problems. The students will explore several evolutionary computation techniques and apply them to practical problems.

Use the concepts of variation and selection techniques for particular classes of problems
Implement various evolutionary algorithms including ant colony optimization and swarm optimization algorithms
Apply the principles of evolutionary and genetic programming for real life problems

course_name: Foundations of Information Theory for AI
program: B Tech & MBA Tech (Artificial Intelligence)
objectives: This course introduces students to the basic ideas of information, uncertainty, and entropy that are essential for understanding data and decision-making in Artificial Intelligence. Students learn how information measures like mutual information and KL divergence are used in learning, prediction, and evaluation. The course emphasizes simple statistical reasoning to understand how information flows through learning systems and how uncertainty limits performance. By the end, students will appreciate why information theory forms a fundamental mathematical basis for modern AI methods.

outcomes.text: Explain the basic concepts of information, uncertainty, and entropy.
Apply mutual information and KL divergence to compare probability distributions in learning problems.
Analyze information flow in simple learning systems using Markov assumptions and the Data Processing Inequality.
Describe how information flow and error bounds influence performance in basic classification tasks.

units.title: Information, Uncertainty & Entropy Foundations
units.text: Information, Uncertainty & Entropy Foundations Information content, uncertainty, probability and surprise, Discrete entropy: definition and properties, Joint entropy, conditional entropy, chain rules, Mutual information and its relationship with entropy, Entropy in machine learning: Cross- entropy loss and log-loss Entropy for comparing probability distributions, Entropy of Gaussian variables (with ML interpretation)

units.title: Divergence & Statistical Inference for Learning
units.text: Divergence & Statistical Inference for Learning Hypothesis testing and estimation basics, Log-likelihood ratio tests, Kullback- Leibler divergence: definition, properties, convexity, Jensen’s inequality and log-sum inequality, Connection of KL divergence to: Variational inference (e.g., VAEs), Regularization and Bayesian learning, Convexity/concavity of information functions, Information per coin toss, multiple hypothesis testing, Lower bounds related to inference (Stein’s lemma – conceptual)

units.title: Information Flow, Limits & Bounds in AI
units.text: Information Flow, Limits & Bounds in AI Markov chains and conditional independence, Information flow in learning systems, Data processing inequality: relevance to neural representations, Fano’s inequality: classification error bounds, Asymptotic Equipartition Property (AEP), Information- theoretic lower bounds: Source coding intuition and limits, Limits of inference performance

program: B Tech & MBA Tech (Artificial Intelligence)
objectives: This course aims to provide students with a thorough understanding of the importance of data visualization and its useful applications. In order to ensure that they can convert complex data into understandable, insightful visuals, students will become proficient in common data visualization tools and methodologies. Along with learning how to successfully present statistics, they will also concentrate on ethical issues and narrative. The course equips students with critical thinking and teamwork abilities, which are crucial for data science and engineering projects. By the end, students will be well-equipped to communicate insights and make data-driven decisions using data visualization as a potent tool.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate fundamental knowledge of data visualization concepts and the tools used to create them.
Apply data visualization skills to produce interactive dashboards.
Analyse intricate datasets, prepare and integrate data using visualization tools, and utilize advanced visualization techniques to generate insights.
Evaluate data visualizations for effectiveness and apply best practices in data storytelling

program: B Tech & MBA Tech (Artificial Intelligence)
objectives: The course aims to introduce students to version control using Git for collaborative software development and provide foundational knowledge of GPU architecture. It further equips learners with practical skills to program using CUDA in Python through Numba/CuPy, enabling them to build and optimize GPU- accelerated applications suitable for AI and data-intensive workloads.

outcomes.text: Apply basic Git commands to create repositories, track changes, and manage version control.
Use Git branching, merging, and collaborative workflows involving pull requests and remote repositories.
Explain GPU architecture and develop basic CUDA programs involving kernels, blocks, threads, and grids.
Implement CUDA-accelerated programs in Python using Numba or CuPy for computational tasks.
Optimize CUDA kernels and apply GPU acceleration to AI and machine-learning workloads.

units.title: Branching, Collaboration & Git Workflow

program: B Tech (All programs except Civil, Mechanical, and Mechatronics) / MBA Tech (All programs)
prerequisites: Linear Algebra and Ordinary Differential Equations
objectives: The principal objective of the course is to develop students' logical reasoning and problem-solving skills by introducing fundamental concepts of discrete mathematics essential for computer science and engineering applications. It provides a strong foundation in set theory, logic, combinatorics, graph theory, and abstract algebra, enabling students to analyze and construct mathematical arguments. Through the study of proof techniques, recurrence relations, and discrete structures, students will gain the ability to model computational problems and prove the correctness of algorithms. The course also highlights the practical applications of discrete mathematics in real- world contexts, such as data structures, cryptography, network security, and algorithm design, equipping students for advanced studies and careers in computing.

outcomes.text: Apply fundamental concepts of set theory, relations, and functions to solve mathematical and computational problems.
Construct valid mathematical arguments using propositional and predicate logic, proof techniques, and induction methods.
Analyze combinatorial structures and recurrence relations to model and solve discrete problems in engineering applications.
Implement graph and tree algorithms to solve optimization and network-related problems.
Demonstrate an understanding of abstract algebraic structures and their applications in coding theory.

Functions: injective, surjective, and bijective functions, composition, inverse of a function,’ Power set, the principle of inclusion-exclusion and applications, and partitions of sets. Relations, Properties, and types of binary relations, Equivalence relation, Computer representation of relations, Closures of relations, Warshall’s Algorithm, n-ary relations and their applications, Introduction of partial orderings, Lattice, and Boolean algebra. Functions: Functions for computer science, and permutation function.

units.title: Logic

Solve problems involving random variables, probability distributions and testing of hypothesis, correlation, and regression.

units.title: Experiments
units.text: Exp. No. Programming Topic Duration 1. Implementation of various array operations like traversal, insertion and deletion using any real life application. A school is developing a student management system to store and process student scores in various subjects. The system needs to efficiently handle tasks such as storing scores, finding top performers, and calculating statistics. Question: Write a program to store the marks of n students in an array and calculate the average score of the class. Modify the program to find the highest and lowest marks scored in the class. 02 Implement an insertion operation to add a new student’s score at a specific position in the array. How does the time complexity change when inserting at the beginning, middle, or end of the array? Implement a deletion operation to remove a student’s score from a specific position in the array. How does shifting elements affect performance? 2. Implementation of Linear search and binary search, on a scenario: 1. A software application stores a list of student IDs in an array. The system needs to quickly find whether a given student ID exists in the list. The array may be either sorted or unsorted, depending on the data storage method used. Question: Implement searching algorithm for finding a specific ID using linear and binary search? If the student IDs are stored in a sorted array, which searching algorithm would provide the most efficient search results? How does the time complexity of searching change when using a linear search versus a binary search in this case? 02 3 Revision session 02 4. Iteration and Recursion Implement a program to find the sum of all elements in an array using iteration and recursion. How can recursion be used to search for a specific element in an array? Compare its efficiency with iterative searching methods. Design a recursive function to reverse an array. How does it work, and what is its time complexity? 02 5. To study and implement concept of Stack data structure: Implement undo operation in browser using Stack. Implement operation to reverse a string using stack 02 6. Revision session 02 7. Application of stack (Expression conversion/evaluation of postfix expression /Parenthesis matching) i. Implement a program that takes input a postfix expression and evaluates it using stack to return the result. ii. Implement a program that takes input an infix expression and converts it to postfix using stack. iii. Implement a program that takes input an expression and returns True if the parentheses are balanced, otherwise False. Use a stack to match the parentheses. 02 8. Implementation of simple queues and circular queue using arrays and apply them in real life computer applications: i. Simulate bank queue by enquing and dequing customers on first come first serve basis. Input: customer id with timestamp, Output: Customer id (in FIFO order). ii. Implement a bed allocation system in hospital on first come first serve basis using linked list. 02 9 Revision session 02 10 Representation of Binary trees in memory and implementation of Binary Tree traversal algorithms Implement program to create a binary search tree and perform inorder, preorder and postorder traversal. Write a program to count number of nodes in binary search tree Write a program to print all the leaf nodes in a binary search tree 02 11 Revision session 02 12 Implementation of Binary Search Tree: Insertion, deletion and Search operation on tree data structure A university maintains a database of student records, where each student's ID is stored in a Binary Search Tree (BST) for efficient searching and retrieval. The university wants to optimize data operations such as searching, inserting, and deleting student records. Question: Implement program to insert a new student who enrolls into the BST. Implement a program for an administrator to find a student's record stored in BST. Compare it with searching in an unsorted array. Implement a program deleted student ID be from the BST, if a student withdraws from the university. If the BST becomes unbalanced due to continuous insertions and deletions, how would it affect search efficiency? What techniques can be used to maintain balance? 02 13 Implementation of Graph Traversal: Breadth first search, Depth first search A city’s transportation department is developing a navigation system to help commuters find the shortest route between different locations. The city's road network is represented as a graph, where intersections are nodes and roads between them are edges with weights representing distances or travel time. 02 Question: Implement a program to represent the city's road network using a graph? Would you use an adjacency matrix or an adjacency list? Justify your choice. Implement a program to travese all the cities stored in the graph. If a commuter wants to find the shortest route between two locations, which algorithm would be best suited? Explain why. 14 Revision session 02 15 Implementation of sorting algorithm (Insertion, Selection, Merge Sort) on a given scenario: A company maintains an employee database where employee IDs are stored in an array. The HR department needs to sort the employee IDs in ascending order to efficiently process payroll and generate reports. Question: Implement sorting algorithm to sort the employee IDs in ascending order using Insertion/ Selection/Mergesort. If the employee IDs are stored in an unsorted array, which sorting algorithm would be most efficient for a small dataset (e.g., less than 100 employees)? Why? If the dataset is very large (e.g., 100,000 employees), which sorting algorithm would be best suited for optimal performance? 02 Total 30

units.text: Data Exploration, Pre-processing and Visualization Missing Values Treatment, Handling Categorical data: Mapping ordinal features, Encoding class labels, Performing one-hot encoding on nominal features, Outlier Detection and Treatment. Feature Engineering: Variable Transformation and Variable Creation, Selecting meaningful features Library Sci-kit Learn for Pre-processing, Pandas for Exploratory Data Analysis, NumPy for Statistical Analysis, Matplotlib for Data Visualization

units.title: Regression
units.text: Regression Simple Linear Regression, Ordinary Least square, Gradient descent algorithm, Bias, Variance, Bias-variance trade off, Cross validation, Regularization- Ridge and LASSO regression, Multiple Regression, polynomial Regression.

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification Logistic Regression for binary classification, Gradient of logistic regression, Binary cross entropy function, performance evaluation of classification algorithms: confusion matrix, ROC, AUC, k-Nearest Neighbour Algorithm, Naïve Bayesian Classifier, Support Vector Machine, Kernels in SVM

units.title: Tree based algorithms
units.text: Tree based algorithms Decision tree classifier, Ensemble Learning- Bagging, Boosting, Random forest, AdaBoost, XGBoost.

units.title: Clustering
units.text: Clustering Hierarchical Methods - Agglomerate versus Divisive Hierarchical Clustering, Partitioning Methods: k-Means Clustering, Density-Based Clustering: DBSCAN. Dimensionality reduction: Principle Component Analysis.

reference_books: 1. Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jerome Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning: Data Mining, Inference, and Prediction, 2nd Edition, Springer, 2017. 2. Judith Hurwitz, Daniel Kirsch, Machine Learning for dummies, IBM Limited Edition, John Wiley & Sons, Inc., 2018.

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech Artificial Intelligence B Tech (AI and ML, AI and DS)
objectives: This course aims at introducing the concept of discrete time signals and systems. Taking image as a discrete time signal, some methodologies for digital image processing are explored. This course would enable the students to develop a foundation for research in the fields like computer vision, machine learning, pattern recognition, etc.

outcomes.text: Classify discrete time signals and systems and implement Discrete Fourier Transform on discrete time signals
Apply spatial domain and frequency domain techniques for image enhancement
Analyze images processed by various morphological and segmentation techniques
Illustrate motion estimation and compensation techniques in video processing

units.title: Discrete-Time Signal and Discrete-Time System
units.text: Discrete-Time Signal and Discrete-Time System Introduction to digital signal processing, sampling and reconstruction, standard discrete time signals, concept of digital frequency, signal manipulations -shifting, reversal, scaling, addition, multiplication), classification of discrete-time signals, classification of discrete systems, Linear convolution formulation (without mathematical proof), circular convolution (without mathematical proof), LTI system, concept of impulse response and step response.

units.title: Discrete Fourier Transform and Fast Fourier Transform
units.text: Discrete Fourier Transform and Fast Fourier Transform A brief introduction to concept of Discrete Time Fourier Series (DTFS), and Discrete Time Fourier Transform (DTFT) Introduction to DFT, IDFT, properties of DFT -scaling and linearity, periodicity, time shift and frequency shift, time reversal, convolution property and Parsevals‘ energy theorem (without mathematical proof), DFT computation using DFT properties, Linear and circular convolution using DFT, need of FFT, radix-2 DIT-FFT algorithm ,DIT-FFT Flow graph for N=2, 4 and 8, inverse DIT FFT algorithm

units.title: Image fundamentals
units.text: Image fundamentals Representation of digital image, spatial and gray level resolution, basic relationships between pixels, image file format and color models

units.title: Image Enhancement in Spatial domain and frequency domain
units.text: Image Enhancement in Spatial domain and frequency domain Intensity transformation- digital negative, contrast stretching, thresholding, gray level slicing, power law transformation, neighborhood processing- smoothing, sharpening and median filters histogram equalization- local and global, frequency domain filtering, ideal high pass and low filter, Butterworth high pass and low pass filter

units.title: Morphological Image Processing and Image Segmentation
units.text: Morphological Image Processing and Image Segmentation Morphological operations- dilation, erosion, opening and closing. Segmentation based on discontinuities -point, line, edge,image edge detection using Robert, Sobel, Prewitt masks, Laplacian mask, segmentation based on thresholding, region based segmentation- region growing, region splitting and merging

units.title: Fundamentals of digital video
units.text: Fundamentals of digital video Video representation- digital video sampling, temporal correlation, video frame classifications, I, P and B frames, digital video quality measure.

units.title: Digital video processing techniques
units.text: Digital video processing techniques Fundamentals of motion estimation and compensation, region of support and its types, motion estimation algorithms-exhaustive search block matching, 2D-log search method and 3 step search method.

text_books: 1. Tarun Kumar Rawat, Digital Signal Processing, Oxford University Press, 2014 2. R.C Gonzalez and Richard Woods, Digital Image Processing, 3rd edition, 3. Oge Marques, Practical Image and Video Processing using Matlab, 1st edition, John Wiley & Sons, 2011
reference_books: 1. John Proakis, Digital signal processing, 4th edition, Prentice Hall of India Publication, 2010. 2. Chris Solomon, Toby Breckon, Fundamentals of Digital Image Processing: A practical approach with examples in Matlab, 1st edition, Wiley, 2011. 3. Murat Tekalp, Digital Video Processing, 2nd edition, Prentice Hall, 2015.

program: B Tech (Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, CSE (Cyber), AI and ML, AI and DS, CSBS, CSE (DS), Computer Science) MBA Tech (All Programs) B Tech Integrated (Computer Engineering)
objectives: The objective of the course is to provide a comprehensive introduction to the fundamental concepts for design and development of database systems, with an emphasis on how to organize, maintain and retrieve - efficiently, and effectively - information from a database management system.

outcomes.text: Describe core concepts of database and model a database management system through ER modelling
Apply knowledge of relational algebra and structured query language to retrieve and manage data from relational database
Demonstrate the use of normalization for database design
Demonstrate the concept of transactions and use modern database techniques such as NoSQL

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Database System Applications, Purpose of Database Systems, View of Data, Database Languages, Data Models, Database Users and Administrator

units.title: Database Design and the E-R Model
units.text: Database Design and the E-R Model Overview of the Design Process, The Entity-Relationship Model, Constraints, Entity Relationship Diagrams, Reduction to Relational Schemas, Schema Diagrams , Entity-Relationship Design Issues, Extended ER features

units.title: Introduction to the Relational Model
units.text: Introduction to the Relational Model Structure of Relational Databases, Database Schema, Keys, Relational Algebra, Basic operators of Relational Algebra,

units.title: Structured Query Language
units.text: Structured Query Language Overview of the SQL Query Language, SQL Data Definition, SQL Constraints, Basic Structure of SQL Queries, Additional Basic Operations, DML operations, Set operations, Aggregate Functions, Nested Sub- queries, Joins, views

units.title: Relational Database Design
units.text: Relational Database Design Features of Good Relational Designs, Problems with bad design, Decomposition using concept of functional dependencies, Armstrong’s axioms, Closure of functional dependency, Closure of attribute, Introduction to process of Normalization and de-normalization, Normal Forms- 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF

units.title: Transactions
units.text: Transactions What is Transactions? Properties of transaction, Transaction states, Issues with concurrent executions, Schedules, Serializability- Conflict and View

units.title: Introduction to NoSQL
units.text: Introduction to NoSQL Overview of NoSQL, characteristics of NoSQL, Storage types of NoSQL, Implementing NoSQL in MongoDB - Managing Databases and Collections from the MongoDB shell, Finding Documents in MongoDB collection from the MongoDB shell.

objectives: This course aims to instill in students an understanding of Laplace transform, Fourier series Fourier Transform and Fourier Transform. It provides students with mathematics fundamentals necessary to formulate, solve and analyse complex engineering problems.

explore the various methods of Fourier series, Fourier Transform and Laplace transform to solve related problems
apply the techniques of Fourier series, Fourier Transform and Laplace transform to engineering problems

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course offers an insight into the basic understanding of biological intelligence needed to implement artificial intelligence. It also aims to enhance the knowledge of the basics of biology for bio-inspired engineering and designs while focusing on the principles of bioinspired algorithm implementation.

outcomes.text: recall basics of biological systems
summarize the intelligence at the cellular level
identify and discuss the intelligence of different biological systems
summarize and categorize different forms of intelligence in different animals.

Introduction to animal cell. Different functions of cell. Different cell components and their functions. Different functions of cell like cell biochemistry, cell metabolism, cell communication, and cell composition.

units.title: Different types of intelligent body systems like
units.text: Different types of intelligent body systems like Immune system, Hormonal system, Cardiovascular system, Muscular systems etc.
Different defence mechanisms of body, Sympathetic body systems that understand different emotions, trauma, and external attacks. Intelligence of instincts, gut intelligence.

Social and enterprising intelligence of ants, echo-locating skills of bats and such similar skills in different animals. Weather prediction, nest building skills of different species, survival tricks of

units.text: Study on implementation of biological intelligence in artificial systems. Applications of biological intelligence in field of computing like bio informatics, ANN, genetic algorithms, deep learning etc.

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The main objective of this course is to instill in students a sound knowledge of probability theory and statistical techniques with intermediate to advanced level that helps them tackle relevant problems within the engineering domain.

outcomes.text: Solve problems involving random variables, probability distributions and testing of hypothesis, correlation and regression
Identify suitable probability distribution and testing techniques to solve problems
Apply knowledge of random variables, probability distributions, measures of central tendency, correlation and regression to solve real life problems
Analyse data samples using statistical methods.

units.title: Basic Probability
units.text: Basic Probability: Probability spaces, conditional probability, independence, Bayes theorem.

units.title: Random variables and Probability Distributions
units.text: Random variables and Probability Distributions: Discrete random variables, probability mass function , cumulative distribution function, Independent random variables, Continuous random variables, distribution functions and densities, expectation, variance, raw and central moments of random variables, The multinomial distribution, Poisson approximation to the binomial distribution, Infinite sequences of Bernoulli trials, Normal distribution, exponential and gamma densities.

units.title: Basic Statistics
units.text: Basic Statistics: Measures of Central tendency; Moments, skewness, Kurtosis. Moments, skewness and Kurtosis for Binomial distribution & Poisson distribution, Moments, skewness & kurtosis for Normal distribution, Linear regression and correlation, Rank correlation.

units.title: Testing of hypothesis
units.text: Testing of hypothesis: Null and Alternate hypothesis, Test Statistic, Type I and Type II errors, One-tailed and two-tailed test, Critical region, Large sample statistical test for mean, Large sample statistical test for proportion, t-test for small samples, paired t test, Test for variance- F test, Chi-square test for Goodness of fit and independence of attributes.

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course fosters a holistic understanding of different minerals, rock types and landscape types with reference to composition and working of the Earth. It aims to apply knowledge of plate tectonic theory to differentiate structural features in rocks, decipher seismicity probabilities and predict geological hazards. It also aims to apply Earth Science theories to the Fundamentals of Geo- Economics and use geological principles in civil engineering

outcomes.text: Differentiate between various Earth materials, Earth processes and landscapes
Relate Earth movements and Earth resources with respect to basic Structural Geology and Tectonics
Identify natural disasters based on geological parameters
Utilize the geological knowledge to other core civil subjects.

units.title: Introduction to Earth Sciences
units.text: Introduction to Earth Sciences: Theories of the formation of the Earth; Compositional layering and the internal structure of the Earth Rock Cycle; Carbon Cycle; work of Geological Survey of India

units.title: Mineralogy and Physical Geology
units.text: Mineralogy and Physical Geology: Introduction to minerals, Bowen’s Reaction Series, physical properties; common rock forming mineral classes; introduction to crystallography Mineral Provinces, fundamentals of Economic Geology, India’s mineral deposits Weathering and Erosion, Types, factors and products of erosion and deposition; work of running water, sea, wind, glacier, ground water Concept of watershed, Interlinking of rivers (reference to Ministry of Water Resources Task Force) Groundwater, aquifer types, recharge

units.title: Igneous Petrology
units.text: Igneous Petrology: Depth-wise classification of igneous rocks, Volcanic eruption types and ejected materials, Concept of hot springs and geysers, Magma types, Basis of expressing Igneous texture, Types of igneous textures, Igneous intrusive and extrusive structures, common igneous rocks like Basalt, Granite, Mantle generated rocks Sedimentary Petrology: Modes of formation of sedimentary rocks, Mineralogical composition of sedimentary rocks, Basis of expressing sedimentary textures, Types of sedimentary textures, Sedimentary structures, Classification of sedimentary rocks, Sedimentary Facies and Provenance, Common sedimentary rocks like Sandstone, Limestone, Breccia, Fossiliferous rocks Metamorphic Petrology: Agents of metamorphism, Types of metamorphism, Metamorphic grades and facies, Metamorphic textures, structures, common metamorphic rocks like schists, gneisses, marble.

units.title: Structural Geology
units.text: Structural Geology: Folds, Faults, Joints, Unconformities: Types, classification Geological maps: fundamentals, symbols and basic interpretation Introduction to cartography; ArcGIS, QGIS

units.title: Plate tectonic theory
units.text: Plate tectonic theory: Evolution of the theory of plate tectonics Types of plate movements Plate Tectonic Theory Case Studies: Himalayas, Andes, New Zealand, Atlantic Ocean

units.title: Dams, Reservoirs and Tunnels
units.text: Dams, Reservoirs and Tunnels: Site selection, geological considerations and hazards; Case Studies

units.title: Geological Hazards and Exploration
units.text: Geological Hazards and Exploration: RQD, RMR, Slope Stability, Basic concept of Stress and Strain Landslides: Types, Causes, mitigation, Case Studies Earthquake: Reasons, Types of Waves, seismic zonation of India, quantification, Case Studies: Himalayan tectonics and associated earthquake events Tsunami: Causes, Warning System; Case studies: Andaman, Japan Floods: Causes; Case Studies: Ganges-Brahmaputra-Padma annual floods Direct and Indirect methods of Geophysical exploration

units.title: Historical Geology
units.text: Historical Geology: Stratigraphy: Theories, Deccan Basalt, Cuddapah, Vidhyan, Himalayas Theories of mass extinction and Ice Ages

text_books: 1. Parbin Singh, “Engineering and General Geology”, S K Kataria & Sons 2013. 2. K. C. Condie, “Plate Tectonics and Crustal Evolution”, Elsevier 4th edition 1997. (Classic Book).
reference_books: 1. N. Chenna Kesavulu, “Text Book of Engineering Geology”, Macmillan Publishers India, 3rd edition 2018. 2. J.C. Harvey, “Geology for Geotechnical Engineers”, Cambridge University Press, 1982. (Classic Book)

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course explains the various systems of forces in equilibrium, physical and mathematical principles used in mechanics. It aims to calculate the centroid and moment of inertia of a plane area and apply equations of motions to rigid bodies for resolving force system

outcomes.text: Solve the system of forces in equilibrium
Determine the centroid and moment of Inertia of a plane area
Evaluate the velocity, acceleration and displacement of a moving body
Analyze the forces developed on the bodies subjected to rigid body displacements and rotations.

units.title: System of forces
units.text: System of forces: Rectangular components of forces in space, moment of a force about a point, moment of a force about a given axis, resultant of general force system, Coplanar & non-coplanar force system, forces and their components, resultant of coplanar force system - concurrent forces, parallel forces, non-concurrent non-parallel system of forces, moment of force about a point, couple, Varignon’s theorem.

units.title: Forces and equilibrium
units.text: Forces and equilibrium: Free body diagram with examples on modelling of typical supports and joints, condition for equilibrium in three and two dimensions. Friction: Limiting and non-limiting cases, Laws of friction, angle of friction, angle of repose, cone of friction, Equilibrium of bodies on rough horizontal and inclined plane, application to problems involving wedges, ladder. Belt friction, flat belts on the flat pulleys Analysis of pin jointed plane trusses: Perfect truss, method of joints and method of section.

units.title: Centroid and moment of inertia
units.text: Centroid and moment of inertia: Centroid, moment of inertia, polar moment of inertia, and product of inertia, parallel and perpendicular axis theorem.

units.title: Kinematics of particle
units.text: Kinematics of particle: Velocity and acceleration in terms of rectangular coordinate system, rectilinear motion, motion along plane curved path, tangential and normal component of acceleration, acceleration - time, velocity- time graphs and their uses, relative velocity, projectile motion, simple harmonic motion. Kinematics of rigid bodies: Translation, pure rotation and plane motion of rigid bodies, instantaneous centre of rotation for the velocity for bodies in plane motion, link mechanisms (up to two links).

units.title: Kinetics of particles
units.text: Kinetics of particles: Newton’s laws of motion, D’Alembert’s principle, equation of dynamic equilibrium, linear motion, curvilinear motion. Kinetics of rigid bodies: D’Alembert’s principle for bodies under translational motion, rotational motion about a fixed axis and plane motion. Application to motion of bars, cylinders, spheres.

text_books: 1. Beer & Johnston et. Al., “Vector Mechanics for Engineers- Statics and Dynamics”, Tata McGraw Hill, 12th Edition 2020. 2. R. C. Hibler, ‘‘Engineering Mechanics’’, McMillan Publishers, 14th Edition 2017.
reference_books: 1. F. L. Singer, “Engineering Mechanics”, Harper & Raw Publication, 3rd Edition 1975 (Classic Book) 2. D. S. Kumar, ‘‘Engineering Mechanics’’, Tata McGraw Hill, 2013. 3. Mclean & Nelson, ‘‘Engineering Mechanics’’, Tata McGraw Hill 2010. (Schaum’s Series) 4. A. K. Tayal, ‘‘Engineering Mechanics’’, Umesh Publication 14th Edition 2019.

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course explains the internal forces, stresses in members subjected to various loads and principal stresses for the resolving force systems. It aims to evaluate material properties and deflections of members.

outcomes.text: Analyze internal forces and stresses produced in the deformable bodies
Analyze members subjected to flexure, shear and torsion
Evaluate deformations of determinate beams
Evaluate physical and mechanical properties of materials in laboratory.

units.title: Stress & strain
units.text: Stress & strain: Stress, yield stress, ultimate stress, shear stress, factor of safety, strain, modulus of elasticity (E), modulus of rigidity (G), bulk modulus (K), Poisson’s ratio, relationship between elastic constants, elongation due to self- weight, bars of varying sections, stresses in composite section, temperature stresses.

units.title: Internal Forces in Beams and Rigid Jointed Frames
units.text: Internal Forces in Beams and Rigid Jointed Frames: Axial force, shear force & bending moment diagrams for statically determinate beams and rigid jointed frames including internal hinges for different types of loading, relationship between rate of loading, shear force and bending moment.

units.title: Stresses in Beams
units.text: Stresses in Beams: Flexure formula for beam, simple problems involving the application of flexure formula, section modulus, moment of resistance of a section, concepts of flitched/ composite beams. Distribution of shear stress across plane sections used commonly for beams, shear connectors.

units.title: Simple theory of torsion
units.text: Simple theory of torsion: Torsion of circular shafts - solid and hollow, stresses and strains in shaft when transmitting power.

units.title: Bending moment combined with axial loads
units.text: Bending moment combined with axial loads: Application to members subjected to eccentric loads and chimneys, core of the section.

units.title: Principal stresses
units.text: Principal stresses: General equations for transformation of stress, principles planes and principal stresses, maximum shear stress, Mohr’s circle.

units.title: Deflections of beams
units.text: Deflections of beams: Deflection of cantilever, simply supported and overhanging beams for different types of loadings using double integration method, Macaulay’s method, Moment area theorem, deflections of beams using moment area theorems and conjugate beam method.

text_books: 1. James M. Gere, Barry J. Goodno, “Mechanics of Materials – SI Edition”, Cengage Learning, 9th Edition 2017. 2. C. S. Reddy, “Basic Structural Analysis”, Tata McGraw-Hill Education, 3rd Edition 2017.
reference_books: 1. Andrew Pytel, Jaan Kiusalaas, “Mechanics of Materials”, Cengage Learning, 2nd Edition 2010. 2. Ferdinand P. Beer, E. Russell Johnston Jr., John T. DeWolf, “Mechanics of Materials”, Tata McGraw Hill, 7th Edition 2014. 3. William Nash, Merle Potter, “Schaum's Outline of Strength of Materials”, McGraw Hill Professional, 6th Edition 2013.

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This imparts basic knowledge of construction activities and their sequence, the process of concreting from manufacturing to finishing. It aims to compare various types of flooring and their applications in different scenarios

outcomes.text: Describe various construction activities and their sequence
Explain the process of concreting from manufacturing to finishing
Discuss various types of flooring and their applications.

units.title: Excavation
units.text: Excavation: Manual and mechanical method of Excavation, disposal of excavated material, dewatering of trenches, shoring and strutting of Trenches, precaution while excavation, fencing – caution signs.

units.title: Foundation
units.text: Foundation: Necessity and Purpose of Foundation, Shallow Foundation, Spread foundation, raft foundation, deep foundation and its types, Precast concrete piles. Modern methods of pile installation

units.title: Masonry
units.text: Masonry: Terminology, load bearing and framed structures, preparation, construction procedure, post construction precautions, brick masonry stretcher bond and half brick thick masonry, hollow and solid concrete block masonry, fixing of door and window frame in masonry, block masonry. Procedure of constructing un- coursed Rubble and coursed masonry. Pointing & Plastering: Necessity and types, methods of providing pointing and plastering

units.title: Formwork and Scaffolding
units.text: Formwork and Scaffolding: Types, basic factors governing selection. Erecting and removal of formwork. Scaffolding types, precautions

units.title: Concrete
units.text: Concrete: Procedure of mixing concrete, manual and machine mixing, types of mixers, transporting, laying, compacting and curing of concrete, different types of vibrators, underwater concreting.

units.title: Floors
units.text: Floors: Solid ground floor, plinth fillings, floor finish with murum, brick-bat concrete, Indian patent stone, cement tiles, China mosaic, floorings for special purposes such as factories, warehouses, stables, garages, railway platforms, upper floors: jack arch construction, mezzanine floors and lofts, false flooring for control rooms.

text_books: 1. Rangwala S C , “Building Construction”, Charotar Publications, 33rd Edition 2016.
reference_books: 1. Mathur S., “Building Construction Handbook”, SBS Publishers, 2012. 2. McKay, “Building Construction”, Pearson India, 2013. 3. Mantri Sandeep, “The A to Z of Practical Building Construction and its Management”, Mantri Publications, 2017.

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to acquire knowledge about the principles of planning of residential buildings as well as public buildings. It also aims to preparation of different drawings for residential/public buildings as per building bye laws for planning of residential/public buildings.

outcomes.text: Apply principles of planning, architectural planning and building bye-laws while designing and preparing building drawings
Design various components of buildings as well as building as a whole, given the requirements of the building and local D.C. laws
Develop drawings of the designed components of buildings as well as buildings as a whole.

units.title: Drawing Basics
units.text: Drawing Basics: Introduction to concept of drawings, optimal layout of drawings and Scales, commonly used symbols, conventions and abbreviations used in architectural drawings, Planning drawings to show information concisely and comprehensively and Interpretation of typical drawings.

units.title: Building bye-laws
units.text: Building bye-laws: Study of building Bye-laws and documents / permissions required from commencement to completion of the building according to National Building Code (N.B.C.) of India and local Development Control (D.C.) rules, Following important bye-laws : Plot area & Built-up area, Size of rooms, Margins, Heights, Passages, Ventilation, Circulation, Open space, setback distances, carpet area and floor space index (FSI).

units.title: Principles of planning
units.text: Principles of planning: For residential/public buildings: Principles of planning such as room dimension, area, heights, privacy, ventilation, access, circulation, economy, drainage, aspect, prospect, orientation, grouping, mass composition etc.

units.title: Planning residential buildings
units.text: Planning residential buildings: Given situations & plot area; prepare detailed drawing of a single storied residential building (Load Bearing & RCC) i.e. line plan, detailed plan, elevation and section of the building, Site plan, location plan, Other plans and tables required.

units.title: Building components
units.text: Building components: Draw sketches of different types of roofs, trusses, water proofing on terrace, staircase (Dog legged and open well) and Doors and windows detailing.
Guest Lecture by Liasoning Architect

text_books: 1. Dr. N Kumara Swamy and A. Kameswara Rao, “Building Planning and Drawing”, Charotar Publishing House Pvt. Ltd., 9th Edition 2019.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The principal objective of this course is to provide a basic understanding of biological mechanisms of living organisms from the perspective of engineers. To encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools. To make them aware of the application of engineering principles in biology and engineering robust solutions inspired by biological examples.

outcomes.text: convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are diverse
identify and classify microorganisms while understanding molecular basis of DNA as a genetic material for information transfer
classify enzymes and distinguish between different mechanisms of enzyme action

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Convey that Biology is as important a scientific discipline as Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry Bring out the fundamental differences between science and engineering by drawing a comparison between eye and camera, Bird flying and aircraft. Mention the most exciting aspect of biology as an independent scientific discipline. Why we need to study biology? Discuss how biological observations of 18th Century that lead to major discoveries. Examples from -Brownian motion and the origin of thermodynamics by referring to the original observation of Robert Brown and Julius Mayor. These examples will highlight the fundamental importance of observations in any scientific inquiry.

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification Convey that classification per se is not what biology is all about. The underlying criterion, such as morphological, biochemical or ecological be highlighted. Hierarchy of life forms at phenomenological level. A common thread weaves this hierarchy Classification.Discuss classification based on (a) cellularity- Unicellular or multicellular (b) ultrastructure- prokaryotes or eucaryotes. (c) energy and Carbon utilization -Autotrophs, heterotrophs, lithotropes (d) Ammonia excretion - aminotelic, uricoteliec, ureotelic (e) Habitata- acquatic or terrestrial (e) Molecular taxonomy- three major kingdoms of life. A given organism can come under different category based on classification. Model organisms for the study of biology come from different groups. E.coli, S.cerevisiae, D. Melanogaster, C. elegance, A. Thaliana, M. musculus

units.title: Genetics
units.text: Genetics Convey that "Genetics is to biology what Newton's laws are to Physical Sciences" Mendel's laws, Concept of segregation and independent assortment. Concept of allele. Gene mapping, Gene interaction, Epistasis. Meiosis and Mitosis be taught as a part of genetics. Emphasis to be give not to the mechanics of cell division nor the phases but how genetic material passes from parent to offspring. Concepts of recessiveness and dominance. Concept of mapping of phenotype to genes. Discuss about the single gene disorders in humans. Discuss the concept of complementation using human

units.title: Biomolecules
units.text: Biomolecules Convey that all forms of life has the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are as diverse as one can imagine Molecules of life. In this context discuss monomeric units and polymeric structures. Discuss about sugars, starch and cellulose. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA. Two carbon units and lipids.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes Convey that without catalysis life would not have existed on earth Enzymology: How to monitor enzyme catalyzed reactions. How does an enzyme catalyze reactions. Enzyme classification. Mechanism of enzyme action. Discuss at least two examples. Enzyme kinetics and kinetic- parameters. Why should we know these parameters to understand biology? RNA catalysis.

units.title: Information Transfer
units.text: Information Transfer The molecular basis of coding and decoding genetic information is universal Molecular basis of information transfer. DNA as a genetic material. Hierarchy of DNA structure- from single stranded to double helix to nucleosomes. Concept of genetic code. Universality and degeneracy of genetic code. Define gene in terms of complementation and recombination.

units.title: Macromolecular analysis
units.text: Macromolecular analysis How to analyses biological processes at the reductionistic level Proteins- structure and function. Hierarch in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors and structural elements.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism The fundamental principles of energy transactions are the same in physical and biological world. Thermodynamics as applied to biological systems. Exothermic and endothermic versus endergonic and exergonic reactions. Concept of Keq and its relation to standard free energy. Spontaneity. ATP as an energy currency. This should include the breakdown of glucose to CO2 + H2O (Glycolysis and Krebs cycle) and synthesis of glucose from CO2 and H2O (Photosynthesis). Energy yielding and energy consuming reactions.

units.title: Microbiology
units.text: Microbiology Concept of single celled organisms. Concept of species and strains. Identification and classification of microorganisms. Microscopy. Ecological aspects of single celled organisms. Sterilization and media compositions. Growth kinetics.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The aim of this course is to foster a holistic understanding of the composition and working of the Earth and be able to differentiate between minerals, rock types and landscape types with reference to their genesis. Also, the course focuses on the application of plate tectonic theory to differentiate structural features in rocks, decipher seismicity probabilities and predict geological hazards, fundamentals of Geo-Economics and use geological principles in Civil Engineering.

outcomes.text: differentiate between Earth materials, Earth processes and landscapes
explain structural geology and tectonics
discuss natural disasters based on geological parameters

units.title: Introduction to Geology
units.text: Introduction to Geology Theories of the formation of the Earth; Compositional layering and the internal structure of the Earth, Rock Cycle; Carbon Cycle; work of Geological Survey of India

units.title: Mineralogy and Physical Geology
units.text: Mineralogy and Physical Geology Introduction to minerals, Bowen’s Reaction Series, physical properties; common rock forming mineral classes; introduction to crystallography, mineral Provinces, fundamentals of economic geology, India’s mineral deposits, weathering and Erosion, Types, factors and products of erosion and deposition; work of running water, sea, wind, glacier, groundwater, aquifer types, recharge

units.title: Igneous Petrology
units.text: Igneous Petrology Depth-wise classification of igneous rocks, Volcanic eruption types and ejected materials, Concept of hot springs and geysers, Magma types, Basis of expressing Igneous texture, Types of igneous textures, Igneous intrusive and extrusive structures, common igneous rocks like Basalt, Granite, Mantle generated rocks Sedimentary Petrology Modes of formation of sedimentary rocks, Mineralogical composition of sedimentary rocks, Basis of expressing sedimentary textures, Types of sedimentary textures, Sedimentary structures, Classification of sedimentary rocks, Sedimentary Facies and Provenance, Common sedimentary rocks like Sandstone, Limestone, Breccia, Fossiliferous rocks Metamorphic Petrology Agents of metamorphism, Types of metamorphism, Metamorphic grades and facies, Metamorphic textures, structures, common metamorphic rocks like schists, gneisses, marble.

units.title: Structural Geology
units.text: Structural Geology Folds, Faults, Joints, Unconformities: Types, classification Geological maps: fundamentals, symbols and basic interpretation Introduction to cartography; Introduction to ArcGIS, QGIS

units.title: Plate tectonic theory
units.text: Plate tectonic theory Evolution of the theory of plate tectonics Types of plate movements Plate Tectonic Theory Case Studies: Himalayas, Andes, New Zealand, Atlantic Ocean

units.title: Historical Geology
units.text: Historical Geology Stratigraphy: Theories, Deccan Basalt, Cuddapah, Vidhyan, Himalayas,Theories of mass extinction and Ice Ages

units.title: Geological Hazards and Exploration
units.text: Geological Hazards and Exploration Types, Causes, mitigation, Case Studies for landslides, Earthquakes, Tsunami, Floods: Direct and Indirect methods of Geophysical exploration, Site selection, geological considerations and hazards; Case Studies of dams, reservoirs and tunnels

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to acquire knowledge about the principles of planning of residential buildings as well as public buildings. It also aims to preparation of different drawings for residential/public buildings as per building bye laws for planning of residential/public buildings.

outcomes.text: Understand the principles of planning, architectural planning and building byelaws while designing and preparing building drawings
Design buildings including its various components for the given requirements of the building as per Development Control laws of local governing bodies
Plan and develop drawings for residential buildings
Draw various buildings components

units.title: Building bye-laws

units.title: Planning residential buildings

program: B Tech Civil
prerequisites: Fundamental knowledge of physics, chemistry, and mathematics.
objectives: To introduce students to modern biology with an emphasis on the evolution of biology as a multi- disciplinary field, to make them aware of the application of engineering principles in biology. This will encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools. They will also be exposed to the application of engineering principles in biology and engineering robust solutions inspired by biological examples.

outcomes.text: Identify the principles of biomimicry and explain their applications in engineering and sustainable design, demonstrating an understanding of biologically inspired solutions.
Classify the fundamental building blocks of life (carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids) and describe their structural and functional roles in cellular processes and metabolism.
Explain the molecular basis of genetic information transfer, including DNA replication, transcription, and translation, and interpret Mendel's laws and their significance in genetics.
Describe the mechanisms of enzyme action, enzyme-substrate interactions, and enzyme inhibition, and discuss their industrial and biological applications.
Explain the principles of metabolism and energy transactions, and categorize microorganisms based on their characteristics, growth kinetics, and applications in biotechnology and drug discovery.

units.title: Introduction to Biomimicry
units.text: Introduction to Biomimicry Applications of biology in engineering. Biology as an independent scientific discipline. Importance of studying biology. Various applications of biology. Biologically inspired engineering. Biomimicry in engineering uses designs, processes, and ecosystems. Sustainable engineering.

units.title: The fundamental building blocks of life
units.text: The fundamental building blocks of life Unity in diversity of life, Molecules of life. Structure and functions of carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, and lipids. Hierarchy in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors, and structural elements. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA.

units.title: Genetics and Information Transfer
units.text: Genetics and Information Transfer Genetics as the foundation of biology, Mendel's laws, Single gene disorders, Molecular basis of genetic information transfer, DNA replication, Central dogma of life: transcription and translation.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes Enzymology, Enzyme-catalyzed reactions, Enzyme-substrate complex, Mechanism of action, Enzyme classification, Enzyme inhibition, Industrial applications of enzymes.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism Metabolism: catabolism and anabolism, Principles of energy transactions, ATP as energy currency, ATP cycle, Cellular respiration, Anaerobic respiration, Aerobic respiration.

units.title: Microbiology and Drug Discovery

Solve mathematical problems using concepts of complex variables, Laplace transforms, Fourier series, and Fourier transforms.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The aim of this course is to foster a holistic understanding of the composition and working of the Earth and be able to differentiate between minerals, rock types and landscape types with reference to their genesis. Also, the course focuses on the application of plate tectonic theory to differentiate structural features in rocks, decipher seismicity probabilities and predict geological hazards, fundamentals of Geo-Economics and use geological principles in Civil Engineering.

outcomes.text: Differentiate between Earth materials, Earth processes and landscapes
Explain structural geology and tectonics
Discuss natural disasters based on geological parameters
Test and interpret Earth Materials
Test and interpret Geological Maps

units.title: Historical Geology

program: MBA Tech / B Tech
objectives: The course provide basic orientation towards microeconomic principles and help them understand the functions of management. This course also aims to understand issues dealing with small-scale economic phenomena and concepts such as prices and output of firms, industries and resource owners along with examining market impact of technological change with regards to understand broader aspects of the economy and its environment.

outcomes.text: Understand Fundamental Economic Concepts - Explain the basic concepts of economics, including scarcity of resources, economic systems, and demand-supply analysis.
Demonstrate Consumer and Producer Behavior - Apply utility analysis and production theories to understand consumer decision-making and cost structures in different market conditions

Illustrate Market Structures and Pricing Mechanisms - Differentiate between market structures such as monopoly, oligopoly, perfect and imperfect competition, and explain price and output determination.

Apply Management Principles in Decision-Making - Demonstrate an understanding of management functions such as planning, organizing, decision-making, and leadership based on classical and modern theories.

Understand the Role of Business Functions in Organizational Success - Examine the significance of key business functions such as finance, marketing, human resources, and operations, and their interdependence in achieving organizational objectives.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Definition of Economics, Problem of Scarcity of Economic Resources, Types of Economic Systems. Demand and Supply Analysis: Demand Curve and Supply Curve, Equilibrium of Demand and Supply, Shift in Demand and Supply. Application of Demand and Supply: Price Elasticity of Demand, Factors which influence Elasticity, Uses of Price Elasticity of Demand, Elasticity and Revenue.

units.title: Utility Analysis and Consumer Behaviour
units.text: Utility Analysis and Consumer Behaviour: Introduction to Cardinal and Ordinal Utility, Total Utility and Marginal Utility, Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility, Indifference Curve and Consumer’s equilibrium. New Economic Policy: Liberalization, Privatization and Globalization

units.title: Theory of Production
units.text: Theory of Production: Introduction and Meaning, Short-run and Long-run Production Function, Law of Diminishing Returns and Returns to Scale, Iso- quant Curve and Producer’s Equilibrium (Least Cost Combination). Analysis of Costs: Types of Costs and Cost Curves – Total Cost, Fixed Cost, Variable Cost, Marginal Cost, Relationship between Marginal Cost Curve and Average Cost Curve.

units.title: Market Structure /Industry Analysis Types of Competition
units.text: Market Structure /Industry Analysis Types of Competition: Monopoly, Oligopoly, Monopolistic Competition, Perfect and Imperfect Competition. Price and output determination in perfectly competitive market structure.

units.title: Introduction to Management
units.text: Introduction to Management: Management & its Nature, Management History and Management Thought-Contribution of F.W. Taylor, Henry Fayol, and Elton Mayo. Planning: Introduction and Importance, Steps in Planning, Why Plan Fails, Sound Planning. Decision Making: Managers as Decision Makers, types of Decisions, Strategic Management.

Organizing- Line and Staff Relationships, Centralization and Decentralization, Role of Delegation, Managing Human Resources, Managing Teams. Leading and Motivation: Basic Concepts and Practices –Maslow’s, Herzberg, McClelland‘s Theory of Achievement.

units.title: Controlling- Introduction to Controlling, Need and Importance, Inventory
units.text: Controlling- Introduction to Controlling, Need and Importance, Inventory Control, Quality Control. Orientation towards Finance, Marketing, Human Resources.

objectives: 1. The objective of this Course is to provide an introductory treatment of Engineering Mechanics to all the students of engineering, with a view to prepare a good foundation for taking up advanced courses in the area in the subsequent semesters 2. program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course explains the internal forces, stresses in members subjected to various loads and principal stresses for the resolving force systems. It aims to evaluate material properties and deflections of members.

outcomes.text: Identify internal forces and stresses produced in the deformable bodies
Construct axial force, shear force and bending moment diagrams for beams and rigid frames
Analyze members subjected to flexure, shear and torsion
Develop principal stresses and strains using stress transformation equations and Mohr’s Circle
Solve deflections of beams using analytical methods

units.title: Principal stresses

program: MBA Tech / B Tech
objectives: The course provide basic orientation towards microeconomic principles and help them understand the functions of management. This course also aims to understand issues dealing with small-scale economic phenomena and concepts such as prices and output of firms, industries and resource owners along with examining market impact of technological change with regards to understand broader aspects of the economy and its environment.

outcomes.text: Understand Fundamental Economic Concepts - Explain the basic concepts of economics, including scarcity of resources, economic systems, and demand-supply analysis.
Demonstrate Consumer and Producer Behavior - Apply utility analysis and production theories to understand consumer decision-making and cost structures in different market conditions

Illustrate Market Structures and Pricing Mechanisms - Differentiate between market structures such as monopoly, oligopoly, perfect and imperfect competition, and explain price and output determination.

Apply Management Principles in Decision-Making - Demonstrate an understanding of management functions such as planning, organizing, decision-making, and leadership based on classical and modern theories.

Understand the Role of Business Functions in Organizational Success - Examine the significance of key business functions such as finance, marketing, human resources, and operations, and their interdependence in achieving organizational objectives.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Definition of Economics, Problem of Scarcity of Economic Resources, Types of Economic Systems. Demand and Supply Analysis: Demand Curve and Supply Curve, Equilibrium of Demand and Supply, Shift in Demand and Supply. Application of Demand and Supply: Price Elasticity of Demand, Factors which influence Elasticity, Uses of Price Elasticity of Demand, Elasticity and Revenue.

units.title: Utility Analysis and Consumer Behaviour
units.text: Utility Analysis and Consumer Behaviour: Introduction to Cardinal and Ordinal Utility, Total Utility and Marginal Utility, Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility, Indifference Curve and Consumer’s equilibrium. New Economic Policy: Liberalization, Privatization and Globalization

units.title: Theory of Production
units.text: Theory of Production: Introduction and Meaning, Short-run and Long-run Production Function, Law of Diminishing Returns and Returns to Scale, Iso- quant Curve and Producer’s Equilibrium (Least Cost Combination). Analysis of Costs: Types of Costs and Cost Curves – Total Cost, Fixed Cost, Variable Cost, Marginal Cost, Relationship between Marginal Cost Curve and Average Cost Curve.

units.title: Market Structure /Industry Analysis Types of Competition
units.text: Market Structure /Industry Analysis Types of Competition: Monopoly, Oligopoly, Monopolistic Competition, Perfect and Imperfect Competition. Price and output determination in perfectly competitive market structure.

units.title: Introduction to Management
units.text: Introduction to Management: Management & its Nature, Management History and Management Thought-Contribution of F.W. Taylor, Henry Fayol, and Elton Mayo. Planning: Introduction and Importance, Steps in Planning, Why Plan Fails, Sound Planning. Decision Making: Managers as Decision Makers, types of Decisions, Strategic Management.

Organizing- Line and Staff Relationships, Centralization and Decentralization, Role of Delegation, Managing Human Resources, Managing Teams. Leading and Motivation: Basic Concepts and Practices –Maslow’s, Herzberg, McClelland‘s Theory of Achievement.

units.title: Controlling- Introduction to Controlling, Need and Importance, Inventory
units.text: Controlling- Introduction to Controlling, Need and Importance, Inventory Control, Quality Control. Orientation towards Finance, Marketing, Human Resources.

units.text: Stresses in Beams Flexure formula for beam, simple problems involving the application of flexure formula, section modulus, moment of resistance of a section, concepts of flitched/ composite beams. Distribution of shear stress across plane sections used commonly for beams, shear connectors.

units.title: Simple theory of torsion
units.text: Simple theory of torsion Torsion of circular shafts - solid and hollow, stresses and strains in shaft when transmitting power.

units.title: Bending moment combined with axial loads
units.text: Bending moment combined with axial loads Application to members subjected to eccentric loads and chimneys, core of the section.

units.title: Principal stresses
units.text: Principal stresses General equations for transformation of stress, principles planes and principal stresses, maximum shear stress, Mohr’s circle.

units.title: Deflections of beams
units.text: Deflections of beams Deflection of cantilever, simply supported and overhanging beams for different types of loadings using double integration method, Macaulay’s method, Moment area theorem, deflections of beams using moment area theorems and conjugate beam method.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to acquire knowledge about the principles of planning of residential buildings as well as public buildings. It also aims to preparation of different drawings for residential/public buildings as per building bye laws for planning of residential/public buildings.

outcomes.text: Apply principles of planning, architectural planning and building bye-laws while designing and preparing building drawings
Design various components of buildings as well as building as a whole, given the requirements of the building and local D.C. laws
Develop drawings of the designed components of buildings as well as buildings as a whole

units.title: Drawing Basics
units.text: Drawing Basics Introduction to concept of drawings, optimal layout of drawings and Scales, commonly used symbols, conventions and abbreviations used in architectural drawings, Planning drawings to show information concisely and comprehensively and Interpretation of typical drawings.

units.title: Building bye-laws
units.text: Building bye-laws Study of building Bye-laws and documents / permissions required from commencement to completion of the building according to National Building Code (N.B.C.) of India and local Development Control (D.C.) rules, Following important bye-laws : Plot area & Built-up area, Size of rooms, Margins, Heights, Passages, Ventilation, Circulation, Open space, setback distances, carpet area and floor space index (FSI).

units.title: Principles of planning
units.text: Principles of planning For residential/public buildings: Principles of planning such as room dimension, area, heights, privacy, ventilation, access, circulation, economy, drainage, aspect, prospect, orientation, grouping, mass composition etc.

units.title: Planning residential buildings
units.text: Planning residential buildings Given situations & plot area; prepare detailed drawing of a single storied residential building (Load Bearing & RCC) i.e. line plan, detailed plan, elevation and section of the building, Site plan, location plan, Other plans and tables required.

units.title: Building components
units.text: Building components Draw sketches of different types of roofs, trusses, water proofing on terrace, staircase (Dog legged and open well) and Doors and windows detailing.
Guest Lecture by Liasoning Architect

text_books: 1. Dr. N Kumara Swamy and A. Kameswara Rao, Building Planning and Drawing, 9th Edition, Charotar Publishing House Pvt. Ltd., 2019.

outcomes.text: Identify various instrument and their suitability used in surveying
Discuss various instruments and methods required for leveling
Explain the necessity and use and compute the geometrical properties of curves

units.text: Introduction to Surveying Principles, different scales used, Linear measurements, chaining and ranging, offsets, obstacles and errors in chaining, Compass Surveying, Bearing and corrections, traversing: plotting and corrections, Plane table surveying, instruments and methods of plane table surveying.

Theodolite Survey: Instruments, Measurement of horizontal and vertical angle, independent coordinates, errors. Modern Surveying Instruments
