program: B Tech Civil / B Tech Integrated All Program
prerequisites: Fundamental knowledge of physics, chemistry, and mathematics.
objectives: To introduce students to modem biology with an emphasis on evolution of biology as a multi- disciplinary field, to make them aware of application of engineering principles in biology. This will encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools. They will also be exposed to the application of engineering principles in biology and engineering robust solutions, inspired by biological examples.

outcomes.text: Identify key principles of biomimicry and develop engineering solutions for different fields
Classify microorganisms and their molecular properties and analyze the role of DNA as genetic material in transferring information among living organisms
Describe the fundamental building blocks of life, including carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, and lipids, and illustrate their functions in cellular processes and metabolism

units.title: Introduction to Biomimicry
units.text: Introduction to Biomimicry Applications of biology in engineering, Biology as an independent scientific discipline, Importance of studying biology, Exploring biological discoveries of the 19th century: Brownian motion and beyond. Applications of biology: Biotechnology, Bioremediation, Bioinformatics, etc., Biologically inspired engineering. Biomimicry in engineering using designs, processes, and ecosystems. Sustainable engineering. Case study: The Kingfisher's beak inspired high-speed Bullet trains.

units.title: The fundamental building blocks of life
units.text: The fundamental building blocks of life Unity in diversity of life, Molecules of life. Structure and functions of carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, and lipids. Hierarchy in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structure. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors, and structural elements. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA.

units.title: Genetics and Information Transfer
units.text: Genetics and Information Transfer Genetics as the foundation of biology, Mendel's laws, Segregation and independent assortment, Gene mapping, Single gene disorders, Molecular basis of genetic information transfer, DNA as genetic material, Genetic code, Universality of genetic code, DNA replication, Protein synthesis, Central dogma of life: transcription and translation. Case study: Breaking the storage barrier by storing massive amounts of data on DNA.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes Catalysis as a crucial element for life, Enzymology, Enzyme-catalyzed reactions, Enzyme-substrate complex, Mechanism of action, Enzyme classification, Enzyme kinetics, Enzyme inhibition, Industrial applications of enzymes.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism Metabolism: catabolism and anabolism, Principles of energy transactions, ATP as energy currency, ATP cycle, Cellular respiration, Anaerobic respiration, Aerobic respiration, Metabolic regulation, Bioenergetics.

units.title: Microbiology and Drug Discovery
units.text: Microbiology and Drug Discovery Introduction to biological classification: criteria of organization and hierarchy of life. Ecological aspects of single-celled organisms, Identification, and classification of microorganisms, Microbial growth kinetics, Microbial biotechnology. Drug discovery, Model organisms for biological studies E. coli, S. cerevisiae, D. melanogaster, C. elegance, A. thaliana, M. musculus. Vaccines, Targeted drug delivery Case study: Development of a nanoparticle-based vaccine delivery system for cancer immunotherapy.

text_books: 1. Arthur T. Johnson, Biology for Engineers, 2nd Edition, CRC Press Taylor & Francis group, 2018. 2. Prescott, L.M J.P. Harley and C.A. Klein, Microbiology, 12th edition, McGraw-Hill Higher Education, 2022.
reference_books: 1. Campbell, N. A.; Reece, J. B.; Urry, Lisa; Cain, M, L.; Wasserman, S. A.; Minorsky, P. V.; Jackson, R. B., Biology: A global approach, 12th edition, Pearson Education Ltd.,2020. 2. Nelson, D. L.; Lehninger, A. L.; and Cox, M. M., Principles of Biochemistry, 8th edition, W.H. Freeman, 2020. Laboratory/Tutorial details  Not applicable.

program: B Tech (All program except CSBS, CSDS), MBA Tech Mechanical and Computer, B Tech Integrated Mechanical and Computer
prerequisites: Calculus, Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
objectives: This course aims to instil in students an understanding of Complex Variables, Laplace Transforms, Fourier series, Fourier Transforms and their applications. It equips the students with mathematics fundamentals necessary to formulate, solve and analyse complex engineering problems.

outcomes.text: demonstrate understanding of the concepts of Complex variables, Laplace Transforms, Fourier series and Fourier Transforms
solve problems based on complex variables, Laplace Transforms, Fourier series and Fourier Transforms
apply the techniques of Complex variables, Laplace Transforms, Fourier series and Fourier Transforms to solve engineering problems

units.title: Complex Variables – Differentiation
units.text: Complex Variables – Differentiation Complex differentiation, Cauchy-Riemann equation, analytic functions, harmonic functions, harmonic conjugate, Elementary analytic functions (exponential, trigonometric, logarithmic functions), Conformal mappings: definition and problems, Mobius transformation and their properties.

units.title: Complex Variables – Integration
units.text: Complex Variables – Integration Contour Integrals: definition and problems, Cauchy-Goursat theorem, Cauchy Integral formula, Zeros and singularities of analytic functions, Taylor’s series, Laurent’s series, Residues, Cauchy Residue theorem.

units.title: Laplace Transforms
units.text: Laplace Transforms Definition of Laplace Transform, Laplace Transform of 1, eat , sin at, cos at, sinh at, cosh at, tn , Properties of Laplace Transforms: Linearity property, First and second shifting theorems of Laplace Transform, Change of scale property, Ltn f t  ,  f t   n  t  L  t  , L f t , L  f u  du , Evaluation of Inverse Laplace Transform by    0  partial fraction, Convolution theorem, Laplace Transforms of Periodic functions, Unit step functions, Dirac delta functions. Applications: Evaluation of Integrals using Laplace Transforms, Solving initial and boundary value problems involving ordinary differential equations.

units.title: Fourier Series
units.text: Fourier Series Orthogonality and Orthonormality, Periodic function, Trigonometric Series, Dirichlet’s conditions, Euler’s formulae (Derivative of Fourier coefficients a0, an ,bn is not expected), Fourier Series of Functions for the interval [,  2 ] and [,  2c] , Functions having points of discontinuity, Even and odd functions, half range sine and cosine expansions, Complex form of Fourier Series. Applications: Applications to Wave equation, Heat equation and Laplacian equation.

units.title: Fourier Transforms
units.text: Fourier Transforms Fourier integral theorem, Fourier sine and cosine integral. Fourier Transform, Fourier Sine Transform, Fourier Cosine Transform, Properties of Fourier Transforms (Linearity property, Change of scale property, Shifting property), Inverse Fourier Transform, Inverse Fourier Sine Transform, Inverse Fourier Cosine Transform, Finite Fourier Transform. Applications: Solving differential equations using Fourier Transforms.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The aim of this course is to foster a holistic understanding of the composition and working of the Earth and be able to differentiate between minerals, rock types and landscape types with reference to their genesis. Also, the course focuses on the application of plate tectonic theory to differentiate structural features in rocks, decipher seismicity probabilities and predict geological hazards, fundamentals of Geo-Economics and use geological principles in Civil Engineering.

outcomes.text: differentiate between Earth materials, Earth processes and landscapes
explain structural geology and tectonics
discuss natural disasters based on geological parameters

units.title: Introduction to Geology
units.text: Introduction to Geology Theories of the formation of the Earth; Compositional layering and the internal structure of the Earth, Rock Cycle; Carbon Cycle; work of Geological Survey of India

units.title: Mineralogy and Physical Geology
units.text: Mineralogy and Physical Geology Introduction to minerals, Bowen’s Reaction Series, physical properties; common rock forming mineral classes; introduction to crystallography, mineral Provinces, fundamentals of economic geology, India’s mineral deposits, weathering and Erosion, Types, factors and products of erosion and deposition; work of running water, sea, wind, glacier, groundwater, aquifer types, recharge

units.title: Igneous Petrology
units.text: Igneous Petrology Depth-wise classification of igneous rocks, Volcanic eruption types and ejected materials, Concept of hot springs and geysers, Magma types, Basis of expressing Igneous texture, Types of igneous textures, Igneous intrusive and extrusive structures, common igneous rocks like Basalt, Granite, Mantle generated rocks Sedimentary Petrology Modes of formation of sedimentary rocks, Mineralogical composition of sedimentary rocks, Basis of expressing sedimentary textures, Types of sedimentary textures, Sedimentary structures, Classification of sedimentary rocks, Sedimentary Facies and Provenance, Common sedimentary rocks like Sandstone, Limestone, Breccia, Fossiliferous rocks Metamorphic Petrology Agents of metamorphism, Types of metamorphism, Metamorphic grades and facies, Metamorphic textures, structures, common metamorphic rocks like schists, gneisses, marble.

units.title: Structural Geology
units.text: Structural Geology Folds, Faults, Joints, Unconformities: Types, classification Geological maps: fundamentals, symbols and basic interpretation Introduction to cartography; Introduction to ArcGIS, QGIS

units.title: Plate tectonic theory
units.text: Plate tectonic theory Evolution of the theory of plate tectonics Types of plate movements Plate Tectonic Theory Case Studies: Himalayas, Andes, New Zealand, Atlantic Ocean

units.title: Historical Geology
units.text: Historical Geology Stratigraphy: Theories, Deccan Basalt, Cuddapah, Vidhyan, Himalayas, Theories of mass extinction and Ice Ages

units.title: Geological Hazards and Exploration
units.text: Geological Hazards and Exploration Types, Causes, mitigation, Case Studies for landslides, Earthquakes, Tsunami, Floods: Direct and Indirect methods of Geophysical exploration, Site selection, geological considerations and hazards; Case Studies of dams, reservoirs and tunnels

text_books: 1. Parbin Singh, Engineering and General Geology, 8th Edition, S K Kataria & Sons, 2010. 2. K. C. Condie, Plate Tectonics and Crustal Evolution, 4th Edition, Elsevier, 1989. (Classic Book)
reference_books: 1. N. Chenna Kesavulu, Text Book of Engineering Geology, 2nd Edition, Macmillan Publishers India, 2009. 2. J.C.Harvey, Geology for Geotechnical Engineers, Cambridge University Press, 1982. (Classic Book)

program: MBA Tech/ B Tech/ BTI
objectives: The course provide basic orientation towards microeconomic principles and help them understand the functions of management. This course also aims to understand issues dealing with small-scale economic phenomena and concepts such as prices and output of firms, industries and resource owners along with examining market impact of technological change with regards to understand broader aspects of the economy and its environment.

outcomes.text: Illustrate basic concepts of economics (demand, supply, elasticity, scarcity) and explain behaviour on individual, households and firm and handle economic data and write economic report
Analyse and evaluate the impact of Economic Policies and its implication on the Business Environment

Demonstrate and determine the students towards basic management principles and act as foundation for higher levels of learning and to be able to handle basic functions of management (planning, organizing, coordination, and control).

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Definition of Economics, Problem of Scarcity of Economic Resources, Types of Economic Systems. Demand and Supply Analysis: Demand Curve and Supply Curve, Equilibrium of Demand and Supply, Shift in Demand and Supply. Application of Demand and Supply: Price Elasticity of Demand, Factors which influence Elasticity, Uses of Price Elasticity of Demand, Elasticity and Revenue.

units.title: Utility Analysis and Consumer Behaviour
units.text: Utility Analysis and Consumer Behaviour: Introduction to Cardinal and Ordinal Utility, Total Utility and Marginal Utility, Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility, Indifference Curve and Consumer’s equilibrium. New Economic Policy: Liberalization, Privatization and Globalization

units.title: Theory of Production
units.text: Theory of Production: Introduction and Meaning, Short-run and Long-run Production Function, Law of Diminishing Returns and Returns to Scale, Iso- quant Curve and Producer’s Equilibrium (Least Cost Combination). Analysis of Costs: Types of Costs and Cost Curves – Total Cost, Fixed Cost, Variable Cost, Marginal Cost, Relationship between Marginal Cost Curve and Average Cost Curve.

units.title: Market Structure /Industry Analysis Types of Competition
units.text: Market Structure /Industry Analysis Types of Competition: Monopoly, Oligopoly, Monopolistic Competition, Perfect and Imperfect Competition. Price and output determination in perfectly competitive market structure.

units.title: Introduction to Management
units.text: Introduction to Management: Management & its Nature, Management History and Management Thought-Contribution of F.W. Taylor, Henry Fayol, and Elton Mayo. Planning: Introduction and Importance, Steps in Planning, Why Plan Fails, Sound Planning. Decision Making: Managers as Decision Makers, types of Decisions, Strategic Management.

Organizing- Line and Staff Relationships, Centralization and Decentralization, Role of Delegation, Managing Human Resources, Managing Teams. Leading and Motivation: Basic Concepts and Practices –Maslow’s, Herzberg, McClelland‘s Theory of Achievement.

units.title: Controlling- Introduction to Controlling, Need and Importance, Inventory
units.text: Controlling- Introduction to Controlling, Need and Importance, Inventory Control, Quality Control. Orientation towards Finance, Marketing, Human Resources.

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics
objectives: This course aims to understand the multidisciplinary nature of environmental sciences, greenhouse effect and climate change. It also aims to discuss the basics of natural resources, biodiversity, environmental pollution.

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of natural resources, ecosystem and biodiversity
Relate the various aspects of environmental pollutions with its cause and effect
Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change.

units.title: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science
units.text: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science Definition, scope and importance of environmental sciences.

Natural Resources • Natural resources: Forest resources, Water resources, Mineral resources, Food resources. • Energy resources: Growing energy needs, renewable and non- renewable energy sources, use of alternate energy sources.

Ecosystems • Concept of an ecosystem. • Structure and function of an ecosystem. • Food chains, food webs and ecological pyramids. • Introduction, types, characteristic features of the following ecosystem:- a. Forest ecosystem b. Grassland ecosystem c. Desert ecosystem d. Aquatic ecosystems.

Biodiversity • Definition: genetic, species and ecosystem diversity. • Value of biodiversity: consumptive use, productive use. • Threats to biodiversity: habitat loss, poaching of wildlife, man-wildlife conflicts.

Environmental Pollution • Definition, Cause and effects for Air pollution, Water pollution, Soil pollution, Marine pollution, Noise pollution, Thermal pollution, Nuclear hazards and Solid waste pollution.
The Science of Climate Change • Greenhouse effect • Global warming • Global environmental changes • Acid rain • Ozone layer depletion • Carbon footprint

text_books: 1. Erach Bharucha, “Textbook of Environmental Studies”, University Press, 2nd Edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. MP Poonia & SC Sharma, “Environmental Studies”, Khanna Publishing House, 1st Edition, 2017. 2. Rajagopalan, “Environmental Studies”, Oxford University Press, Third Edition, 2015.

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to acquire the knowledge of properties of fresh, hardened and special types of concrete. It also aims to formulate the mix design of concrete.

outcomes.text: Identify the properties of different ingredients of concrete and its effect on performance of concrete
Develop mix design of concrete
Illustrate the applications of special concrete
Determine different properties of fresh and hardened concrete with the help of different tests for concrete.

units.title: Ingredients of concrete
units.text: Ingredients of concrete: Cement: Chemical composition, Bogue’s Compounds, hydration of cement and heat of hydration, types, properties and testing of cement. Aggregates: Classification, types, important properties, grading of aggregates, testing of aggregates Water: Quality of water for concreting, effect of impurities in water on properties of concrete. Admixtures: Definition, purpose, classification, types – accelerators, retarders, plasticizers, super plasticizers, air entraining agents, gas forming admixtures, grouting admixtures. Mineral admixtures : Fly ash, Silica fume, GGBFS, etc.

units.title: Properties of Fresh Concrete
units.text: Properties of Fresh Concrete: Workability and consistency, factors affecting workability, measurement of workability, segregation and bleeding, setting time of concrete and test for setting time

units.title: Properties of Hardened Concrete
units.text: Properties of Hardened Concrete: Strength of concrete – compressive, flexural and tensile, tests for determination, shrinkage and creep of concrete, stress, strain and modulus of elasticity, durability of concrete, factor affecting durability

units.title: Concrete Mix Design
units.text: Concrete Mix Design: Necessity, information required for mix design, overview of various methods – Road Note No 4, DOE, ACI, nominal mix design. Concrete mix design by IS 10262 code method, various adjustments, design using super plasticizer, fly ash. Design of pumpable concrete mix, mix design for flexure

units.title: Ready Mixed Concrete
units.text: Ready Mixed Concrete: Requirements, components of RMC plant, typical layout, advantages over site mixed concrete

units.title: Types of concrete and special concretes
units.text: Types of concrete and special concretes: High strength and high-performance concrete: Methods of production, ingredients. Concreting under extreme weather conditions – hot weather and cold weather concreting Fiber reinforced concrete, polymer concretes, high density concrete, low density concrete, no fines concrete, self-compacting concrete, ferro cement, guniting

units.title: Non-destructive Testing of Concrete
units.text: Non-destructive Testing of Concrete : Need, hammer test, ultrasonic pulse velocity test, half-cell potential test, carbonation test, Re bar locator, slab load test

text_books: 1. M.L. Gambhir, “Concrete Technology – Theory and Practice – Fifth Edition” McGraw Hill Education, 5th Edition 2017.
reference_books: 1. A.M. Neville, “Concrete Technology”, Pearson Education India, 2nd Edition 2010. 2. M.S. Shetty, “Concrete Technology – Theory and Practice – Revised Edition”, S. Chand, 2014. 3. Relevant IS Codes

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course explains the concepts of fluid mechanics, fluid statics and kinematics, buoyancy and its applications in engineering problems. It also aims to solve various hydraulic engineering problems in pipe flows

outcomes.text: Relate different properties and behavior of fluids
Examine fluid flow using different measuring devices
Analyze flow through pipes.

units.title: Properties of fluids
units.text: Properties of fluids: Distinction between a fluid and a solid, Density, Specific weight, Specific gravity, Kinematic and dynamic viscosity, Newton law of viscosity, Vapor pressure, cavitation, Surface tension, capillarity, Bulk modulus of elasticity, compressibility.

units.title: Fluid Statics
units.text: Fluid Statics: Fluid Pressure: Pressure at a point, Pascals law, pressure variation with temperature, density and altitude, Piezometer, U-Tube Manometer, Single Column Manometer, Hydrostatic pressure and force on horizontal vertical and inclined surfaces, Buoyancy and stability of floating bodies.

units.title: Fluid Kinematics
units.text: Fluid Kinematics: Continuity equation, Surface and body forces; Equations of motion - Euler’s equation, Bernoulli’s equation – derivation; Energy Principle, Practical applications of Bernoulli’s equation: venturimeter, orifice meter, Orifices: Hydraulic coefficients, small and large orifices, Mouthpieces: external, convergent, Borda’s mouthpiece, Notches and weirs: Rectangular, triangular, Cipolleti weirs.

units.title: Flow through pipes
units.text: Flow through pipes: Loss of head through pipes, Darcy Weisbach equation, Minor losses, Total energy line, hydraulic energy line, Pipes in series, pipes in parallel, Equivalent pipes, Siphons, Power transmission through pipes, Power transmission through nozzles.

text_books: 1. P M Modi and S M Seth, “Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics”, Standard Book House, 22nd Edition 2019. 2. K. Subramanya, “Theory and Applications of Fluid Mechanics”, Tata McGraw Hill, 2002. (Classic Book)

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to explain the index properties, classification soil and it’s engineering behavior. It also aims to impart knowledge of the effect of compaction, consolidation and shear characteristics of soil

outcomes.text: Determine index properties of soils and interpret their engineering behavior
Classify soils and evaluate their suitability for geotechnical applications
Analyze the soil – water characteristics and its effect on soil behavior
Compare compaction and consolidation of soils and examine shear strength characteristics.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Definitions: soils, soil mechanics, soil engineering, rock mechanics, scope of soil engineering, comparison between soil & rock, Formation of Soil: Residual Soils and their zones, Transported soil and its types

units.title: Basic Definitions & Relationship
units.text: Basic Definitions & Relationship: Soil as three phase system in terms of weight, volume, void ratio, porosity, Definitions: moisture content, densities, unit weights, degree of saturation, void ratio, porosity, specific gravity, mass specific gravity etc. Relationship between volume- weight, void ratio- moisture content, unit weight-percent air voids, saturation-moisture content, moisture content-specific gravity etc., Determination of various parameters such as moisture content by Oven Dry Method, Specific gravity by Pycnometer method, Unit weight by core cutter method and sand replacement method.

units.title: Index Properties of Soils
units.text: Index Properties of Soils: Introduction to definitions of: plasticity of soil, consistency limits- liquid limit, plastic limit, shrinkage limit, plasticity, liquidity and consistency indices, flow & toughness indices, Use of consistency limits. Sieve and sedimentation analysis by hydrometer method, particle size distribution- its use and interpretation.

units.title: Classification of Soils
units.text: Classification of Soils: Introduction of soil classification: Textural Classification, Unified Soil Classification, Indian standard soil classification system. Identification: field identification of soils.

units.title: Introduction to Effective Pressure Theory
units.text: Introduction to Effective Pressure Theory: Effective, neutral and total pressure concepts, calculation of effective pressure, capillarity and quick sand condition, critical hydraulic gradient

units.title: Permeability of Soils
units.text: Permeability of Soils: Introduction to hydraulic head, Darcy's law, Discharge velocity and seepage velocity and relation between them, factors affecting permeability of soil, Determination of coefficient of permeability, Laboratory methods: constant head method, falling head method, Field methods: pumping- in test; pumping- out test, Permeability of stratified soils.

units.title: Compaction of Soils
units.text: Compaction of Soils: Introduction, theory of compaction, laboratory determination of optimum moisture content and maximum dry density. Light weight and Heavy weight Compaction Tests as IS code, Factors affecting compaction, Compaction in the field, compaction specification and field control.

units.title: Consolidation of Soils
units.text: Consolidation of Soils: Introduction, comparison between compaction & consolidation, initial, primary & secondary consolidation, Terzaghi’s spring analogy for mechanism of consolidation, basic definitions, final settlement of soil deposits, consolidation settlement: one-dimensional consolidation. determination of Cv by Square root of time fitting and logarithmic time fitting method, secondary consolidation.

units.title: Shear Strength
units.text: Shear Strength: Principal planes and principal stresses, Mohr-Coulomb theory, types of shear tests, direct shear test, merits & demerits of direct shear test, tri-axial compression tests, drainage conditions of UU, CU and CD tests, unconfined compression test, vane shear test.

units.title: Soil Exploration
units.text: Soil Exploration: Introduction, methods of investigation, methods of boring, soil samplers and sampling, number and disposition of borings, borehole logs.

text_books: 1. VNS Murthy, “Text Book of Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering”, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd., 2018. 2. Dr. K. R. Arora, “Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering”, Standard Publishers Distributors, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Karl Terzaghi and Ralph Peck, “Soil Mechanics in Engineering Practice”, John Wiley and & Sons, 3rd edition 1996 (Classic Book) 2. Dr. Alam Singh, “Soil Engineering in Theory and Practice, Part-I”, E-Edition, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd., 2019. 3. Relevant IS Codes, BIS Publications

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course explains the concept of influence lines and plastic analysis. It also aims to acquire knowledge of analysis for determinate and indeterminate structures and deflections of structures.

outcomes.text: Construct influence lines diagrams for determinate beams
Analyse indeterminate structure by flexibility and stiffness method
Evaluate deformations in various structures
Analyze beams using plastic theory.

units.title: General theorems
units.text: General theorems: Types of structures occurring in practice and their classification. Stable and unstable structure, static and kinematic determinacy and indeterminacy of structure. Symmetric structure, symmetrical and anti- symmetrical loads, distinction between linear and non-linear behaviour of material and geometric non- linearity. Theorems relating to elastic structures, principle of virtual work. Strain energy in elastic structures, stresses due to axial load & impact load. Complementary energy, Castigliano’s theorem, Betti’s and Maxwell’s reciprocal theorems, principle of superposition.

units.title: Deflection of statically determinate structures
units.text: Deflection of statically determinate structures: Deflection of determinate pin jointed and rigid jointed frames by principle of virtual work (unit load method) and Castigliano’s theorem. Deflection due to temperature change.

units.title: Rolling loads and Influence lines for statically determinate structures
units.text: Rolling loads and Influence lines for statically determinate structures: Influence lines for cantilevers, simply supported, overhanging beams, criteria for maximum shear force and bending moment at a section, absolute maximum shear force and bending moment under moving loads (udl and series of point loads) for simply supported beams.

units.title: Analysis of indeterminate structures by flexibility method
units.text: Analysis of indeterminate structures by flexibility method: Flexibility coefficients and their use in formulation of compatibility equations. Theorem of three moments, application of above methods to propped cantilevers, fixed beams, continuous beams including effect of settlement of supports.

units.title: Analysis of indeterminate structures by stiffness method
units.text: Analysis of indeterminate structures by stiffness method: Stiffness coefficients for prismatic members and their use for formulation of equilibrium equations, direct stiffness method, slope deflection method, Moment distribution method. Application of the above methods to indeterminate beams and simple rigid jointed non-sway frames excluding the effect of settlement of supports.

units.title: Plastic Analysis
units.text: Plastic Analysis: Introduction, Definitions of plastic hinge and plastic moment capacity, Assumptions, Shape Factor for general sections. Collapse load and basic theorems for finding collapse loads. Methods of plastic analysis – static method and kinematic method, application of above method for beams.

units.title: Columns and struts
units.text: Columns and struts: Euler’s theory for long columns, columns with different end conditions, effective length and slenderness ratio of columns, Rankine’s theory for column.

text_books: 1. G. S. Pandit, S. P. Gupta, “Structural Analysis – A Matrix Approach”, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. S. S. Bhavikatti, “Structural Analysis – Volume II”, Vikas Publishing, 4th edition 2013.
reference_books: 1. R. C. Hibbeler, “Structural Analysis”, Pearson, 9th edition 2017 2. Reddy C. S., “Basic Structural Analysis ", Tata McGraw Hill, 3th edition 2017.

course_name: Open Elective - I (BSC) - Science, Technology and Society
program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The objective of the course is to highlight the role of society, media and politics in the field of science & technology, especially in a post artificial intelligence era.

outcomes.text: understand the complex relationship between science, technology and society
develop an interdisciplinary understanding of scientific knowledge and technological production
evaluate empirical evidences and theoretical claims in science, technology and society along with policy matters
analyze the policy matters and technical governance for artificial intelligence, vaccine development, stem cells and nanotechnology.

units.text: Introduction of science and technology: Definition, scope and interrelationship of science, technology and society, Inductivism versus hypothesism, structure of scientific & industrial revolution, emerging scientific community, rights and wrongs of science, cognitive, hierarchical & ethical dimensions of science.

units.title: Technology & Media
units.text: Technology & Media: Science fiction and films, philosophy of technology, role of media, technology and character of everyday life, Humans versus computers, Langdon Winner’s theory on autonomous technology, technology as a shadow constitution, net neutrality, inequalities in technology.

units.title: Social shaping of technology
units.text: Social shaping of technology: Social perspectives of modern science, open science and social media, science as a social institution, responsibilities of scientist, Kuhn and paradigm shifts, Feyerabend and problem of autonomy, Demarcation in contemporary scientific methods.

units.title: Science, Technology and Law
units.text: Science, Technology and Law: Karl Popper’s theory, controversies regarding science and technology, science, technology and the less-developed countries, technology and transformation of work; Science, technology and economic theory, stem cells, vaccines and animal experimentation.

units.title: Scientific framework and Policy matters
units.text: Scientific framework and Policy matters: Claims by scientists, verifying evidences using experimentation, machine-assisted chemical synthesis, artificial intelligence and related policy, de facto governance of nanotechnology, debating scientific knowledge and technology, STS-related policies in India and worldwide.

text_books: 1. Martin Bridgstock, “Science, Technology and Society: An Introduction,” Cambridge University Press, 1st edition, 1998. 2. Arie Rip, “Futures of Science and Technology in Society,” Springer, 1st edition, 2018.
reference_books: 1. Todd L. Pittinsky, “Science, Technology, and Society: New Perspectives and Directions,” Cambridge University Press, 1st edition, 2019. 2. Preston, P, “Reshaping Communications: Technology, Information and Social Change,” Sage Publications, 1st edition 2001. 3. Wenda K. Bauchspies, “Science, Technology and Society: A Sociological Approach,” Blackwell Publishers, 1st edition 2005.

course_name: Open Elective - I (BSC) - Fundamentals of Fuels and Lubricants
program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: To introduce basic theory of Fuels & Lubrication also familiarizing with the concepts and applications of Fuels , Combustion & Lubricants

outcomes.text: discuss theory of Fuels & Lubrication
apply principles of combustion in various real time problems
examine the different properties & testing of Fuels & Lubricants.

units.title: Introduction & Theory of Fuels
units.text: Introduction & Theory of Fuels: Definition, Classification, Characteristics, Calorific value & numerical based on calorific value, Different Types of fuels, Structure of petroleum, refining process, fuels, thermal cracking, catalytic cracking, polymerization, alkylation, isomerisation, blending, products of refining process.

units.title: Properties & Testing of Fuel
units.text: Properties & Testing of Fuel: Properties and testing of fuels, relative density, distillation, vapour pressure, flash point, spontaneous ignition temperature, viscosity, pour point, flammability, ignitability, diesel index, API gravity, aniline point etc.

units.title: Combustion & Fuel Rating
units.text: Combustion & Fuel Rating: Combustion of fuels & numerical based on combustion, Mechanism of combustion, normal combustion, knocking, octane rating, fuel requirements. CI Engine, mechanism of combustion, diesel knock, cetane rating, fuel requirements.

units.title: Theory of Lubrication
units.text: Theory of Lubrication: Introduction, Classification, Properties Mechanism of Lubrication, hydrodynamic lubrication, elasto hydrodynamic lubrication, boundary lubrication, bearing lubrication, functions of the lubrication system, introduction to design of a lubricating system. Current trends in tribology

units.title: Lubricants
units.text: Lubricants: Specific requirements for automotive lubricants, oxidation deterioration and degradation of lubricants, additives and additive mechanism, synthetic lubricants, classification of lubricating oils, properties of lubricating oils, tests on lubricants. Grease, classification, properties, test used in grease.

text_books: 1. Jain.P.C&Jain.M, Engineering Chemistry, Dhanpat Rai Publishing Co. New Delhi, 17th Edition, 2017. 2. Ganesan.V., “Internal Combustion Engineering", Tata McGraw-Hill Publishing Co., New Delhi, 2003.2nd edition 3. M.L. Mathur, R.P.Sharma “A course in internal combustion engines", Dhanpatrai publication, 2003. 4. Obert.E.F “Internal Combustion Engineering and Air Pollution", International book Co., 1988.
reference_books: 1. R.M. Mortier & S.T.Orszulik “Chemistry and Technology of Lubricants”, Springer- Science+Business Media, BV, 2nd Edition ,1998 2. Brame, J.S.S. and King, J.G. – Fuels – Solids, Liquids, Gaseous. 3. Francis, W – Fuels and Fuel Technology, Vol. I & II 4. Hobson, G.D. & Pohl.W- Modern Petroleum Technology

course_name: Open Elective - I (BSC) - Polymers in Engineering
program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The objective of this course is to introduce students to basic and advanced concepts about polymers, different techniques of polymerization used in industry, and familiarize them with the analytical tools used to evaluate polymers.

outcomes.text: Explain basic concepts and classify different polymers
Develop the relation between structure of polymers and their properties
Evaluate the polymer structure using different analytical tools
Discuss various polymerization techniques and specialty polymers used in industry.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Basic concepts & definitions: monomer & functionality, oligomer, polymer, degree of polymerization, molecular weight & molecular weight distribution, Classification of polymers, thermoplastics, thermoset, tacticity, Glass transition temperature

units.title: Thermoplastic & Thermosets
units.text: Thermoplastic & Thermosets: Structure, properties and applications of - Polyolefins, Styrenic polymers, polyamides, acrylic polymers, polyesters, epoxy resin, polyurethanes and silicones

units.title: Polymerization techniques
units.text: Polymerization techniques: Techniques of polymerization- bulk, solution, suspension, emulsion, plasma etc. Different inititators and catalysts for cationic, anionic, free radical polymerization and control over polymer structure. Condensation polymerization, Copolymerization, Metathesis polymerization. Polymer processing techniques like extrusion and molding.

units.title: Structure Property Relationship
units.text: Structure Property Relationship: Effects of type of bonds, bond energy and functional groups on properties of polymers. Molecular mass heterogeneity and structure properties, polymer chain flexibility, crystallinity of polymers. Thermal properties of polymers.

Evaluation of Polymers: Structural evaluation- IR, NMR, Mass spectrometry. Molecular weight determination- Gel Permeation Chromatography. Thermal properties- Differential Scanning Calorimetry & TGA. Rheological properties- Scanning electron and transmission electron microscopy, XRD.

units.title: Advanced Polymers
units.text: Advanced Polymers: Specialty polymers such as Conductive polymers, liquid crystal polymers, smart polymers, IPN and biodegradable polymers used in key industries including automobiles, smart devices, healthcare, energy production and storage.

text_books: 1. Gowarikar V R, “Polymer Science”, New Age International Publishers, 3rd edition, 2019. 2. Stevens. M, “Polymer Chemistry”, Oxford University Press Inc., 3rd edition, 1999.
reference_books: 1. Teraoka. I, “Polymer Solutions: An Introduction to Physical Properties’’, John Wiley and Sons Inc, 1st edition 2002. 2. Dawkins. J.V, ‘’Modern Techniques in Polymer Characterization’’, John Wiley and Sons Inc, 1st edition 1999.

course_name: Open Elective - I (BSC) - Modelling and Simulation
program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims at utilizing applied mathematics as a thought-process and a toolbox for the study and modelling of real-world phenomena along with their interpretation and comparison for further improvement if any.

outcomes.text: understand the concept of mathematical Modelling
develop models using ODE & PDE
apply optimization techniques to the designed models.

units.title: Principles of Mathematical Modeling
units.text: Principles of Mathematical Modeling: Systems, Models, Simulations, Mathematics as a Natural Modeling Language, Classification of Mathematical Models. Phenomenological Models: Linear Regression, Multiple Linear Regression, Nonlinear Regression, Neural Networks, Design of Experiments. Demonstrations Using Software.

units.title: Modeling with ODEs
units.text: Modeling with ODEs: Setting Up ODE Models, Solution of ODE’s (closed form and Numerical), Fitting ODE’s to Data, ODE Model Examples: Single- species population model, Allee effect, Predator-Prey model, Lotka- Volterra model and SIR model. Model Demonstrations Using Software.

units.title: Modeling with PDEs
units.text: Modeling with PDEs: Introduction PDEs, Closed form solution’s, Numerical Solution of PDE’s, Modeling physical phenomena in terms of PDEs. PDE Model Demonstrations. Model Demonstrations Using Software.

units.title: Simulation Modeling
units.text: Simulation Modeling: Monte Carlo algorithms, random point generation, queuing models.

units.title: Continuous optimization models
units.text: Continuous optimization models: Multivariable optimization, gradient method, Lagrange multipliers, Newton’s method.

text_books: 1. Kai Velten: Mathematical modelling and simulation. Introduction for scientists and engineers. Meccanica. Wiley, 1st edition 2015. 2. Giordano, Fox, Horton, A First Course in Mathematical Modeling, Cengage, 5th edition 2013.
reference_books: 1. Seyed M. Moghadas, Majid Jaberi-Douraki,Mathematical Modelling: A Graduate Textbook ISBN: 978-1-119-48395-3, Wiley, 1st edition 2018 2. Mathematical Modelling with Case Studies: Using Maple and MATLAB, CRC Press, 3rd edition 2016.

course_name: Open Elective - I (BSC) - Optimization for Decision Making
program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
prerequisites: Basics of calculus, statistics and probability.
objectives: The course aims at developing an understanding of linear, nonlinear, integer programming and some modern methods of optimisation. It also aims at training the students with various optimisation techniques necessary to formulate, solve and analyse decision making problems.

outcomes.text: solve problems based on linear, nonlinear and integer programming
explore various methods of solving linear and nonlinear programming using software tools
apply the techniques of linear, integer and non-linear programming in decision making.

units.title: Introduction to Optimization
units.text: Introduction to Optimization: Statement of an optimization problem, classification of optimization problems, engineering applications of optimization, necessary and sufficient conditions for constrained optimization problems (KKT conditions), Demonstration of problem-solving using software.

units.title: Linear Programming
units.text: Linear Programming: Applications of linear programming in decision making, standard form and geometry of LPP, Simplex algorithm, Two phases of the simplex method, Duality in simplex method, sensitivity analysis, Demonstration of problem-solving using software.

units.title: Non-linear Programming
units.text: Non-linear Programming: Introduction to unconstrained optimization techniques in decision making, random search methods, Grid search method, Gradient descent algorithm, Newton’s method, Interior point optimization, Sequential Quadratic programming, Demonstration of problem-solving using software.

units.title: Integer Programming
units.text: Integer Programming: Introduction to integer programming in decision making, graphical representation, Gomory’s Cutting Plane Method, Gomory’s algorithm, Mixed integer programming, Branch and bound method, Demonstration of problem-solving using software.

units.title: Modern methods of optimization
units.text: Modern methods of optimization: Genetic algorithm, simulated annealing, particle swarm optimization, ant colony optimization.

text_books: 1. A. D. Belegundu, T. R. Chanrupatla, “Optimisations concepts and applications in engineering”, Cambridge University Press, 3rd edition, 2019. 2. S. S. Rao, “Engineering optimization theory and practice”, John Wiley & Sons, 5th edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. G. Hardley “Linear Programming” Narosa Book Distributors Private Ltd, 2nd edition 2002. 2. J. Arora, “Introduction to Optimization Design”, Elsevier Academic Press, New Delhi, 2nd edition 2004. 3. R. Saravanan - ‘Manufacturing Optimization through Intelligent Techniques’ - Taylor & Francis (CRC Press), 1st edition 2006. 4. D. S. Hira, P. K. Gupta, “Operations Research”, S. Chand Publishers, 7th edition, 2017.

course_name: Workshop on Building Planning and Design
program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This aims to acquire the skill sets to prepare computer aided architectural / Civil Engineering drawings and knowledge on architectural planning aspects and building regulations. It also aims to examine a drawing critically and with understanding of CAD

outcomes.text: Construct an architectural design idea/concept graphically/ visually
Illustrate the planning and designing of buildings with the sketches
Create drawings using software.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Overview of any one of the CAD software’s prevailing in the market (AutoCAD, Revit, Google sketch up/3D Max etc.). Introduction to computer aided drawing, coordinate systems, and reference planes. Commands: Initial settings, drawing aids, drawing basic entities, Modify commands, Layers, Text and Dimensioning, Blocks. Drawing, presentation norms and standards.

units.title: Project 1
units.text: Project 1: Building for Education: schools, colleges, institutions, libraries etc.

units.title: Project 2
units.text: Project 2: Building for commercial complexes: office building, bank, health centre etc.

units.title: Project 3
units.text: Project 3: Building for Industrial shed: Details of building drawing required: Methods of making line drawing and detailed drawing, Site plan, location plan, Foundation plan, etc.

text_books: 1. Dr. N Kumara Swamy and A. Kameswara Rao, “Building Planning and Drawing”, Charotar Publishing House Pvt. Ltd., 9th edition 2019.
reference_books: 1. Shah M. G., Kale C. M., Patki S. Y., “Building Drawing”, Tata McGraw Hill, 5th edition 2017. 2. Development Control Rules of Metropolitan Cities 3. Bureau of Indian Standards, “National Building Code of India”, BIS Publications, 2016.

program: MBA Tech./B Tech.
objectives: This course provides basic orientation towards economic (micro and macroeconomics) principles and help them understand the functions of management. This course also aims to understand issues dealing with small-scale economic phenomena and concepts such as prices and output of firms, industries and resource owners along with examining market impact of technological change with regards to understand broader aspects of the economy and its environment.

outcomes.text: Illustrate basic concepts of economics (demand, supply, elasticity, scarcity) and explain behaviour on individual, households and firm and Handle economic data and write economic report
Analyse and evaluate the impact of Economic Policies and its implication on the Business Environment

Demonstrate and determine the students towards basic management principles and act as foundation for higher levels of learning and to be able to handle basic functions of management (planning, organizing, coordination, and control).

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Definition of Economics, Types of Economic Systems, Problem of Scarcity of Economic Resources. Demand and Supply: Demand Curve and Supply Curve, Equilibrium of Demand and Supply, Shift in Demand and Supply. Application of Demand and Supply: Price Elasticity of Demand, Price Elasticity of Supply, Factors which influence Elasticity, Elasticity and Revenue.

units.title: Market Structure /Industry Analysis Types of Competition
units.text: Market Structure /Industry Analysis Types of Competition: Monopoly, Oligopoly, Monopolistic Competition, Perfect and Imperfect Competition, Government Policies towards Industries. Circular Flow of Economy, Structures, Role of Government, Business Cycles. Macroeconomics: National Income – Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross National Product (GNP), Inflation – Cost Push and Demand Pull Inflation, Unemployment, Philips Curve.

units.title: Functions of Central Bank, Money supply, RBI & Monetary Policy
units.text: Functions of Central Bank, Money supply, RBI & Monetary Policy. (Current Credit Policy to be critiqued) Stabilization Policy: Role of Fiscal Policy. Demand and Consumer Behavior: Utility and Marginal Utility. New Economic Policy: Liberalization, Privatization and Globalization

units.title: Theory of Production
units.text: Theory of Production: Law of Diminishing Returns, Returns to Scale, Productivity. Analysis of Costs: Types of Costs – Total Cost, Fixed Cost, Variable Cost, Marginal Cost, Impact of Marginal Cost on Average Cost.

units.title: Introduction to Management
units.text: Introduction to Management: Management & Organizations, Management History. Understanding Management Thought, Contribution of F.W. Taylor, Henry Fayol, Elton –Mayo Contexts- Constraints & Challenges. Planning: Managers as Decision Makers, Foundations of Planning, Strategic Management.

units.title: Organizing
units.text: Organizing: Line and Staff Relationships, Centralization and Decentralization, Role of Delegation, Managing Human Resources, Managing Teams. Leading and Motivation: Basic Concepts and Practices –Maslow’s, Herzberg, McClelland ‘s Theory of Achievement.

units.title: Controlling
units.text: Controlling: Introduction to Controlling Inventory, Quality Control. Orientation towards Finance, Marketing, Human Resources and Operation Departments.

text_books: 1. Samuelson and Nordhaus, (2020), Economics - 20th edition- Special Indian Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Publication. 2. Mishra and Puri, (2018), Indian Economy-36th Revised Updated Edition, Himalaya Publishing House. 3. Koontz. H. and Weihrich H. (2018). Essentials of Management: An International, Innovation and Leadership Perspective. 10th reprint Edition, McGraw Hill Education (India). 4. Deviga V. and Karunagaran M., (2013), Principles of Economics, Oxford University Press, 3rd Edition.
reference_books: 1. Mankiw Gregory, (2011), Economics: Principles and applications, Cengage Learning 2. Robbins et al. (2019), Management, Pearson India, 14th Edition. Details of Internal Continuous Assessment (ICA) Test Marks:

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course focusses on the properties of fluid, fluid statics and kinematics, buoyancy and its applications in engineering problems. It also gives understanding of flow through pipes.

outcomes.text: Assess types of fluids based on their properties
Calculate fluid flow using various flow measuring devices
Determine losses in pipe flow

units.title: Properties of fluids
units.text: Properties of fluids Distinction between a fluid and a solid, Density, Specific weight, Specific gravity, Kinematic and dynamic viscosity, Newton law of viscosity, Vapor pressure, cavitation, Surface tension, capillarity, Bulk modulus of elasticity, compressibility.

units.title: Fluid Statics-I
units.text: Fluid Statics-I Fluid Pressure: Pressure at a point, Pascals law, pressure variation with temperature, density and altitude, Piezometer, U-Tube Manometer, Single Column Manometer

units.title: Fluid Statics-II
units.text: Fluid Statics-II Hydrostatic pressure and force on horizontal vertical and inclined surfaces, Buoyancy and stability of floating bodies.

units.title: Fluid Kinematics
units.text: Fluid Kinematics Continuity equation, Surface and body forces; Equations of motion - Euler’s equation, Bernoulli’s equation – derivation; Energy Principle, Practical applications of Bernoulli’s equation

units.title: Flow Measuring Devices
units.text: Flow Measuring Devices Venturimeter, orifice meter, Orifices: Hydraulic coefficients, small and large orifices, Mouthpieces: external, convergent, Borda’s mouthpiece, Notches and weirs: Rectangular, triangular, Cipolleti weirs.

units.title: Flow through pipes
units.text: Flow through pipes Loss of head through pipes, Darcy Weisbach equation, Minor losses, Total energy line, hydraulic energy line, Pipes in series, pipes in parallel, Equivalent pipes, Siphons, Power transmission through pipes, Power transmission through nozzles.

text_books: 1. P M Modi and S M Seth, Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics, 22nd Edition, Standard Book House, 2019. 2. K. Subramanya, Theory and Applications of Fluid Mechanics, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2018.
reference_books: 1. R.L. Daugherty, J.B. Franzini and E. J. Finnemore, Fluid Mechanics with Engineering Applications, International Student Edition, Mc Graw Hill, 2017. 2. Victor L. Streeter, E. Benjamin Wylie, Fluid mechanics, 9th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments /Tutorial exercises based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course focusses on the principles of planning and design of highways, their geometric design and principles of traffic engineering. It also focuses on planning of airports.

outcomes.text: Classify the type of roads based on the loading conditions
Plan and design the highways
Illustrate various signaling processes system for highways and air traffic control

units.title: Introduction to Transportation
units.text: Introduction to Transportation Need and importance of transportation, types of transportation. Highway Planning: Classification of roads. Highway alignment: Basic requirement of ideal alignment, factors governing highway alignment. Highway location survey: Map study, reconnaissance, topographic surveys, highway alignment in hilly area, drawing and report preparation. Highway materials: Aggregate, bitumen and subgrade materials and their testing for quality control.

units.title: Geometric Design of Highways
units.text: Geometric Design of Highways Terrain classification, vehicular characteristics, highway cross section elements, salient dimensions, clearances, width of carriage way, shoulders, medians, width of road way, right of way, camber and its profile. Design speed, sight distance, perception time, break reaction time, analysis of safe sight distance, analysis of overtaking sight distance, intersection sight distance. Horizontal curves: design of super elevation and its provisions, minimum radius of horizontal curves, widening of pavement, transition curves. Gradients: different types, maximum, minimum, ruling and exceptional, grade compensation in curves, vertical curves: design factors, comfort sight distance, Summit curve, valley curve.

units.title: Traffic Engineering
units.text: Traffic Engineering Traffic characteristics, theory of traffic flow, intersection of design, traffic signs and signal design, highway capacity.

units.title: Introduction to Railway and Airport Engineering
units.text: Introduction to Railway and Airport Engineering Railway Engineering: Introduction-Advantages, classification, gauges. Railway track- components & their functions, cross section, conning of wheels, wear and creep of rails, failure, joints, fittings and fixtures, sleepers and drainage. Points and crossing, Station and yards, Signaling and Interlocking, Traction and track resistance, Construction and maintenance. Airport Engineering: Introduction- Terminology, Airport Classification ICAO, components of an aircraft, aircraft characteristics. Runway- orientation, wind rose, basic runway length, geometric design, airport capacity, runway patterns.

text_books: 1. Khanna S.K. and C.E.G. Justo, Highway Engineering, 10th Edition, Nem Chand & Bros, Roorkee, 2014. 2. Rangwala, Airport Engineering, 17th edition, Charotar Publishing House Pvt. Ltd., 2018.
reference_books: 1. Horonjeff Robert, The Planning and Design of Airports, 5th Edition, Tata Mcgraw hill, 2010. (Classic Book) 2. Dr. L. R. Kadiyali and Dr. N. B. Lal, Principles and Practices of Highway Engineering (Including Expressways And Airport Engineering), Khanna Publication, New Delhi, 2019.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to acquire the knowledge of properties of fresh, hardened and special types of concrete. It also aims to formulate the mix design of concrete.

outcomes.text: Identify the properties of different ingredients of concrete and its effect on performance of concrete
Develop mix design of concrete
Illustrate the applications of special concrete
Determine different properties of fresh and hardened concrete with the help of different tests for concrete

units.title: Ingredients of concrete
units.text: Ingredients of concrete Cement: Chemical composition, Bogue’s Compounds, hydration of cement and heat of hydration, types, properties and testing of cement. Aggregates: Classification, types, important properties, grading of aggregates, testing of aggregates Water: Quality of water for concreting, effect of impurities in water on properties of concrete. Admixtures: Definition, purpose, classification, types – accelerators, retarders, plasticizers, super plasticizers, air entraining agents, gas forming admixtures, grouting admixtures. Mineral admixtures : Fly ash, Silica fume, GGBFS, etc.

units.title: Properties of Fresh Concrete
units.text: Properties of Fresh Concrete Workability and consistency, factors affecting workability, measurement of workability, segregation and bleeding, setting time of concrete and test for setting time

units.title: Properties of Hardened Concrete
units.text: Properties of Hardened Concrete Strength of concrete – compressive, flexural and tensile, tests for determination, shrinkage and creep of concrete, stress, strain and modulus of elasticity, durability of concrete, factor affecting durability

units.title: Concrete Mix Design
units.text: Concrete Mix Design Necessity, information required for mix design, overview of various methods – Road Note No 4, DOE, ACI, nominal mix design. Concrete mix design by IS 10262 code method, various adjustments, design using super plasticizer, fly ash. Design of pumpable concrete mix, mix design for flexure

units.title: Ready Mixed Concrete
units.text: Ready Mixed Concrete Requirements, components of RMC plant, typical layout, advantages over site mixed concrete

units.title: Types of concrete and special concretes
units.text: Types of concrete and special concretes High strength and high-performance concrete: Methods of production, ingredients. Concreting under extreme weather conditions – hot weather and cold weather concreting Fiber reinforced concrete, polymer concretes, high density concrete, low density concrete, no fines concrete, self-compacting concrete, ferro cement, guniting

units.title: Non-destructive Testing of Concrete
units.text: Non-destructive Testing of Concrete Need, hammer test, ultrasonic pulse velocity test, half-cell potential test, carbonation test, Re bar locator, slab load test

text_books: 1. M.L. Gambhir, Concrete Technology – Theory and Practice, 5th Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017.
reference_books: 1. A.M. Neville, Concrete Technology, 2nd Edition, Pearson Education India, 2010. 2. M.S. Shetty, Concrete Technology – Theory and Practice – Revised Edition, S. Chand, 2014. 3. Relevant IS Codes

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to explain the index properties, classification soil and it’s engineering behavior. It also aims to impart knowledge of the effect of compaction, consolidation and shear characteristics of soil.

outcomes.text: Determine index properties of soils and interpret their engineering behavior
Classify soils and evaluate their suitability for geotechnical applications
Analyze the soil – water characteristics and its effect on soil behavior
Compare compaction and consolidation of soils and examine shear strength characteristics

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Definitions: soils, soil mechanics, soil engineering, rock mechanics, scope of soil engineering, comparison between soil & rock, Formation of Soil: Residual Soils and their zones, Transported soil and its types

units.title: Basic Definitions & Relationship
units.text: Basic Definitions & Relationship Soil as three phase system in terms of weight, volume, void ratio, porosity, Definitions: moisture content, densities, unit weights, degree of saturation, void ratio, porosity, specific gravity, mass specific gravity etc. Relationship between volume- weight, void ratio-moisture content, unit weight-percent air voids, saturation-moisture content, moisture content- specific gravity etc., Determination of various parameters such as moisture content by Oven Dry Method, Specific gravity by Pycnometer method, Unit weight by core cutter method and sand replacement method.

units.title: Index Properties of Soils
units.text: Index Properties of Soils Introduction to definitions of: plasticity of soil, consistency limits- liquid limit, plastic limit, shrinkage limit, plasticity, liquidity and consistency indices, flow & toughness indices, Use of consistency limits. Sieve and sedimentation analysis by hydrometer method, particle size distribution- its use and interpretation.

units.title: Classification of Soils
units.text: Classification of Soils Introduction of soil classification: Textural Classification, Unified Soil Classification, Indian standard soil classification system. Identification: field identification of soils.

units.title: Introduction to Effective Pressure Theory
units.text: Introduction to Effective Pressure Theory Effective, neutral and total pressure concepts, calculation of effective pressure, capillarity and quick sand condition, critical hydraulic gradient

units.title: Permeability of Soils
units.text: Permeability of Soils Introduction to hydraulic head, Darcy's law, Discharge velocity and seepage velocity and relation between them, factors affecting permeability of soil, Determination of coefficient of permeability, Laboratory methods: constant head method, falling head method, Field methods: pumping-in test; pumping- out test, Permeability of stratified soils.

units.title: Compaction of Soils
units.text: Compaction of Soils Introduction, theory of compaction, laboratory determination of optimum moisture content and maximum dry density. Light weight and Heavy weight Compaction Tests as IS code, Factors affecting compaction, Compaction in the field, compaction specification and field control.

units.title: Consolidation of Soils
units.text: Consolidation of Soils Introduction, comparison between compaction & consolidation, initial, primary & secondary consolidation, Terzaghi’s spring analogy for mechanism of consolidation, basic definitions, final settlement of soil deposits, consolidation settlement: one-dimensional consolidation. determination of Cv by Square root of time fitting and logarithmic time fitting method, secondary consolidation.

units.title: Shear Strength
units.text: Shear Strength Principal planes and principal stresses, Mohr-Coulomb theory, types of shear tests, direct shear test, merits & demerits of direct shear test, tri-axial compression tests, drainage conditions of UU, CU and CD tests, unconfined compression test, vane shear test.

units.title: Soil Exploration
units.text: Soil Exploration Introduction, methods of investigation, methods of boring, soil samplers and sampling, number and disposition of borings, borehole logs.

text_books: 1. VNS Murthy, Text Book of Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd., 2018. 2. Dr. K. R. Arora, Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering, Standard Publishers Distributors, 2020.

Dr. Alam Singh, Soil Engineering in Theory and Practice, Part-I, E-Edition, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd., 2019. 3. Relevant IS Codes, BIS Publications

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course explains the concept of influence lines and plastic analysis. It also aims to acquire knowledge of analysis for determinate and indeterminate structures and deflections of structures.

outcomes.text: Construct influence lines diagrams for determinate beams
Analyse indeterminate structure by flexibility and stiffness method
Evaluate deformations in various structures
Analyze beams using plastic theory

units.title: General theorems
units.text: General theorems Types of structures occurring in practice and their classification. Stable and unstable structure, static and kinematic determinacy and indeterminacy of structure. Symmetric structure, symmetrical and anti-symmetrical loads, distinction between linear and non-linear behaviour of material and geometric non- linearity. Theorems relating to elastic structures, principle of virtual work. Strain energy in elastic structures, stresses due to axial load & impact load. Complementary energy, Castigliano’s theorem, Betti’s and Maxwell’s reciprocal theorems, principle of superposition.

units.title: Deflection of statically determinate structures
units.text: Deflection of statically determinate structures Deflection of determinate pin jointed and rigid jointed frames by principle of virtual work (unit load method) and Castigliano’s theorem. Deflection due to temperature change.

units.title: Rolling loads and Influence lines for statically determinate structures
units.text: Rolling loads and Influence lines for statically determinate structures Influence lines for cantilevers, simply supported, overhanging beams, criteria for maximum shear force and bending moment at a section, absolute maximum shear force and bending moment under moving loads (udl and series of point loads) for simply supported beams.

units.title: Analysis of indeterminate structures by flexibility method
units.text: Analysis of indeterminate structures by flexibility method Flexibility coefficients and their use in formulation of compatibility equations. Theorem of three moments, application of above methods to propped cantilevers, fixed beams, continuous beams including effect of settlement of supports.

units.title: Analysis of indeterminate structures by stiffness method
units.text: Analysis of indeterminate structures by stiffness method Stiffness coefficients for prismatic members and their use for formulation of equilibrium equations, direct stiffness method, slope deflection method, Moment distribution method. Application of the above methods to indeterminate beams and simple rigid jointed non-sway frames excluding the effect of settlement of supports.

units.title: Plastic Analysis
units.text: Plastic Analysis Introduction, Definitions of plastic hinge and plastic moment capacity, Assumptions, Shape Factor for general sections. Collapse load and basic theorems for finding collapse loads. Methods of plastic analysis – static method and kinematic method, application of above method for beams.

units.title: Columns and struts
units.text: Columns and struts Euler’s theory for long columns, columns with different end conditions, effective length and slenderness ratio of columns, Rankine’s theory for column.

text_books: 1. G. S. Pandit, S. P. Gupta, Structural Analysis – A Matrix Approach, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. S. S. Bhavikatti, Structural Analysis – Volume II, 4th Edition, Vikas Publishing, 2013.
reference_books: 1. R. C. Hibbeler, Structural Analysis, 9th Edition, Pearson, 2017 2. Reddy C. S., Basic Structural Analysis, 3th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2017.

units.title: Bivariate Distributions

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course focusses on the properties of fluid, fluid statics and kinematics, buoyancy and its applications in engineering problems. It also gives understanding of flow through pipes.

outcomes.text: Assess types of fluids based on their properties
Calculate fluid flow using various flow measuring devices
Determine losses in pipe flow

units.title: Properties of fluids
units.text: Properties of fluids Distinction between a fluid and a solid, Density, Specific weight, Specific gravity, Kinematic and dynamic viscosity, Newton law of viscosity, Vapor pressure, cavitation, Surface tension, capillarity, Bulk modulus of elasticity, compressibility.

units.title: Fluid Statics-I
units.text: Fluid Statics-I Fluid Pressure: Pressure at a point, Pascals law, pressure variation with temperature, density and altitude, Piezometer, U-Tube Manometer, Single Column Manometer

units.title: Fluid Statics-II
units.text: Fluid Statics-II Hydrostatic pressure and force on horizontal vertical and inclined surfaces, Buoyancy and stability of floating bodies.

units.title: Fluid Kinematics
units.text: Fluid Kinematics Continuity equation, Surface and body forces; Equations of motion - Euler’s equation, Bernoulli’s equation – derivation; Energy Principle, Practical applications of Bernoulli’s equation

units.title: Flow Measuring Devices
units.text: Flow Measuring Devices Venturimeter, orifice meter, Orifices: Hydraulic coefficients, small and large orifices, Mouthpieces: external, convergent, Borda’s mouthpiece, Notches and weirs: Rectangular, triangular, Cipolleti weirs.

units.title: Flow through pipes
units.text: Flow through pipes Loss of head through pipes, Darcy Weisbach equation, Minor losses, Total energy line, hydraulic energy line, Pipes in series, pipes in parallel, Equivalent pipes, Siphons, Power transmission through pipes, Power transmission through nozzles.

text_books: 1. P M Modi and S M Seth, Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics, 22nd Edition, Standard Book House, 2019. 2. K. Subramanya, Theory and Applications of Fluid Mechanics, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2018.
reference_books: 1. R.L. Daugherty, J.B. Franzini and E. J. Finnemore, Fluid Mechanics with Engineering Applications, International Student Edition, Mc Graw Hill, 2017. 2. Victor L. Streeter, E. Benjamin Wylie, Fluid mechanics, 9th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments /Tutorial exercises based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course focusses on the principles of planning and design of highways, their geometric design and principles of traffic engineering. It also focuses on planning of airports.

outcomes.text: Classify the type of roads based on the loading conditions
Plan and design the highways
Illustrate various signaling processes system for highways and air traffic control

units.title: Introduction to Transportation
units.text: Introduction to Transportation Need and importance of transportation, types of transportation. Highway Planning: Classification of roads. Highway alignment: Basic requirement of ideal alignment, factors governing highway alignment. Highway location survey: Map study, reconnaissance, topographic surveys, highway alignment in hilly area, drawing and report preparation. Highway materials: Aggregate, bitumen and subgrade materials and their testing for quality control.

units.title: Geometric Design of Highways
units.text: Geometric Design of Highways Terrain classification, vehicular characteristics, highway cross section elements, salient dimensions, clearances, width of carriage way, shoulders, medians, width of road way, right of way, camber and its profile. Design speed, sight distance, perception time, break reaction time, analysis of safe sight distance, analysis of overtaking sight distance, intersection sight distance. Horizontal curves: design of super elevation and its provisions, minimum radius of horizontal curves, widening of pavement, transition curves. Gradients: different types, maximum, minimum, ruling and exceptional, grade compensation in curves, vertical curves: design factors, comfort sight distance, Summit curve, valley curve.

units.title: Traffic Engineering
units.text: Traffic Engineering Traffic characteristics, theory of traffic flow, intersection of design, traffic signs and signal design, highway capacity.

units.title: Introduction to Railway and Airport Engineering
units.text: Introduction to Railway and Airport Engineering Railway Engineering: Introduction-Advantages, classification, gauges. Railway track- components & their functions, cross section, conning of wheels, wear and creep of rails, failure, joints, fittings and fixtures, sleepers and drainage. Points and crossing, Station and yards, Signaling and Interlocking, Traction and track resistance, Construction and maintenance. Airport Engineering: Introduction- Terminology, Airport Classification ICAO, components of an aircraft, aircraft characteristics. Runway- orientation, wind rose, basic runway length, geometric design, airport capacity, runway patterns.

text_books: 1. Khanna S.K. and C.E.G. Justo, Highway Engineering, 10th Edition, Nem Chand & Bros, Roorkee, 2014. 2. Rangwala, Airport Engineering, 17th edition, Charotar Publishing House Pvt. Ltd., 2018.
reference_books: 1. Horonjeff Robert, The Planning and Design of Airports, 5th Edition, Tata Mcgraw hill, 2010. (Classic Book) 2. Dr. L. R. Kadiyali and Dr. N. B. Lal, Principles and Practices of Highway Engineering (Including Expressways And Airport Engineering), Khanna Publication, New Delhi, 2019.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to acquire the knowledge of properties of fresh, hardened and special types of concrete. It also aims to formulate the mix design of concrete.

outcomes.text: Identify the properties of different ingredients of concrete and its effect on performance of concrete
Develop mix design of concrete
Illustrate the applications of special concrete
Determine different properties of fresh and hardened concrete with the help of different tests for concrete

units.title: Ingredients of concrete
units.text: Ingredients of concrete Cement: Chemical composition, Bogue’s Compounds, hydration of cement and heat of hydration, types, properties and testing of cement. Aggregates: Classification, types, important properties, grading of aggregates, testing of aggregates Water: Quality of water for concreting, effect of impurities in water on properties of concrete. Admixtures: Definition, purpose, classification, types – accelerators, retarders, plasticizers, super plasticizers, air entraining agents, gas forming admixtures, grouting admixtures. Mineral admixtures : Fly ash, Silica fume, GGBFS, etc.

units.title: Properties of Fresh Concrete
units.text: Properties of Fresh Concrete Workability and consistency, factors affecting workability, measurement of workability, segregation and bleeding, setting time of concrete and test for setting time

units.title: Properties of Hardened Concrete
units.text: Properties of Hardened Concrete Strength of concrete – compressive, flexural and tensile, tests for determination, shrinkage and creep of concrete, stress, strain and modulus of elasticity, durability of concrete, factor affecting durability

units.title: Concrete Mix Design
units.text: Concrete Mix Design Necessity, information required for mix design, overview of various methods – Road Note No 4, DOE, ACI, nominal mix design. Concrete mix design by IS 10262 code method, various adjustments, design using super plasticizer, fly ash. Design of pumpable concrete mix, mix design for flexure

units.title: Ready Mixed Concrete
units.text: Ready Mixed Concrete Requirements, components of RMC plant, typical layout, advantages over site mixed concrete

units.title: Types of concrete and special concretes
units.text: Types of concrete and special concretes High strength and high-performance concrete: Methods of production, ingredients. Concreting under extreme weather conditions – hot weather and cold weather concreting Fiber reinforced concrete, polymer concretes, high density concrete, low density concrete, no fines concrete, self-compacting concrete, ferro cement, guniting

units.title: Non-destructive Testing of Concrete
units.text: Non-destructive Testing of Concrete Need, hammer test, ultrasonic pulse velocity test, half-cell potential test, carbonation test, Re bar locator, slab load test

text_books: 1. M.L. Gambhir, Concrete Technology – Theory and Practice, 5th Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017.
reference_books: 1. A.M. Neville, Concrete Technology, 2nd Edition, Pearson Education India, 2010. 2. M.S. Shetty, Concrete Technology – Theory and Practice – Revised Edition, S. Chand, 2014. 3. Relevant IS Codes
