program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to explain the index properties, classification soil and it’s engineering behavior. It also aims to impart knowledge of the effect of compaction, consolidation and shear characteristics of soil.

outcomes.text: Determine index properties of soils and interpret their engineering behavior
Classify soils and evaluate their suitability for geotechnical applications
Analyze the soil – water characteristics and its effect on soil behavior
Compare compaction and consolidation of soils and examine shear strength characteristics

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Definitions: soils, soil mechanics, soil engineering, rock mechanics, scope of soil engineering, comparison between soil & rock, Formation of Soil: Residual Soils and their zones, Transported soil and its types

units.title: Basic Definitions & Relationship
units.text: Basic Definitions & Relationship Soil as three phase system in terms of weight, volume, void ratio, porosity, Definitions: moisture content, densities, unit weights, degree of saturation, void ratio, porosity, specific gravity, mass specific gravity etc. Relationship between volume- weight, void ratio-moisture content, unit weight-percent air voids, saturation-moisture content, moisture content- specific gravity etc., Determination of various parameters such as moisture content by Oven Dry Method, Specific gravity by Pycnometer method, Unit weight by core cutter method and sand replacement method.

units.title: Index Properties of Soils
units.text: Index Properties of Soils Introduction to definitions of: plasticity of soil, consistency limits- liquid limit, plastic limit, shrinkage limit, plasticity, liquidity and consistency indices, flow & toughness indices, Use of consistency limits. Sieve and sedimentation analysis by hydrometer method, particle size distribution- its use and interpretation.

units.title: Classification of Soils
units.text: Classification of Soils Introduction of soil classification: Textural Classification, Unified Soil Classification, Indian standard soil classification system. Identification: field identification of soils.

units.title: Introduction to Effective Pressure Theory
units.text: Introduction to Effective Pressure Theory Effective, neutral and total pressure concepts, calculation of effective pressure, capillarity and quick sand condition, critical hydraulic gradient

units.title: Permeability of Soils
units.text: Permeability of Soils Introduction to hydraulic head, Darcy's law, Discharge velocity and seepage velocity and relation between them, factors affecting permeability of soil, Determination of coefficient of permeability, Laboratory methods: constant head method, falling head method, Field methods: pumping-in test; pumping- out test, Permeability of stratified soils.

units.title: Compaction of Soils
units.text: Compaction of Soils Introduction, theory of compaction, laboratory determination of optimum moisture content and maximum dry density. Light weight and Heavy weight Compaction Tests as IS code, Factors affecting compaction, Compaction in the field, compaction specification and field control.

units.title: Consolidation of Soils
units.text: Consolidation of Soils Introduction, comparison between compaction & consolidation, initial, primary & secondary consolidation, Terzaghi’s spring analogy for mechanism of consolidation, basic definitions, final settlement of soil deposits, consolidation settlement: one-dimensional consolidation. determination of Cv by Square root of time fitting and logarithmic time fitting method, secondary consolidation.

units.title: Shear Strength
units.text: Shear Strength Principal planes and principal stresses, Mohr-Coulomb theory, types of shear tests, direct shear test, merits & demerits of direct shear test, tri-axial compression tests, drainage conditions of UU, CU and CD tests, unconfined compression test, vane shear test.

units.title: Soil Exploration
units.text: Soil Exploration Introduction, methods of investigation, methods of boring, soil samplers and sampling, number and disposition of borings, borehole logs.

text_books: 1. VNS Murthy, Text Book of Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd., 2018. 2. Dr. K. R. Arora, Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering, Standard Publishers Distributors, 2020.

Dr. Alam Singh, Soil Engineering in Theory and Practice, Part-I, E-Edition, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd., 2019. 3. Relevant IS Codes, BIS Publications

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course explains the concept of influence lines and plastic analysis. It also aims to acquire knowledge of analysis for determinate and indeterminate structures and deflections of structures.

outcomes.text: Construct influence lines diagrams for determinate beams
Analyse indeterminate structure by flexibility and stiffness method
Evaluate deformations in various structures
Analyze beams using plastic theory

units.title: General theorems
units.text: General theorems Types of structures occurring in practice and their classification. Stable and unstable structure, static and kinematic determinacy and indeterminacy of structure. Symmetric structure, symmetrical and anti-symmetrical loads, distinction between linear and non-linear behaviour of material and geometric non- linearity. Theorems relating to elastic structures, principle of virtual work. Strain energy in elastic structures, stresses due to axial load & impact load. Complementary energy, Castigliano’s theorem, Betti’s and Maxwell’s reciprocal theorems, principle of superposition.

units.title: Deflection of statically determinate structures
units.text: Deflection of statically determinate structures Deflection of determinate pin jointed and rigid jointed frames by principle of virtual work (unit load method) and Castigliano’s theorem. Deflection due to temperature change.

units.title: Rolling loads and Influence lines for statically determinate structures
units.text: Rolling loads and Influence lines for statically determinate structures Influence lines for cantilevers, simply supported, overhanging beams, criteria for maximum shear force and bending moment at a section, absolute maximum shear force and bending moment under moving loads (udl and series of point loads) for simply supported beams.

units.title: Analysis of indeterminate structures by flexibility method
units.text: Analysis of indeterminate structures by flexibility method Flexibility coefficients and their use in formulation of compatibility equations. Theorem of three moments, application of above methods to propped cantilevers, fixed beams, continuous beams including effect of settlement of supports.

units.title: Analysis of indeterminate structures by stiffness method
units.text: Analysis of indeterminate structures by stiffness method Stiffness coefficients for prismatic members and their use for formulation of equilibrium equations, direct stiffness method, slope deflection method, Moment distribution method. Application of the above methods to indeterminate beams and simple rigid jointed non-sway frames excluding the effect of settlement of supports.

units.title: Plastic Analysis
units.text: Plastic Analysis Introduction, Definitions of plastic hinge and plastic moment capacity, Assumptions, Shape Factor for general sections. Collapse load and basic theorems for finding collapse loads. Methods of plastic analysis – static method and kinematic method, application of above method for beams.

units.title: Columns and struts
units.text: Columns and struts Euler’s theory for long columns, columns with different end conditions, effective length and slenderness ratio of columns, Rankine’s theory for column.

text_books: 1. G. S. Pandit, S. P. Gupta, Structural Analysis – A Matrix Approach, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. S. S. Bhavikatti, Structural Analysis – Volume II, 4th Edition, Vikas Publishing, 2013.
reference_books: 1. R. C. Hibbeler, Structural Analysis, 9th Edition, Pearson, 2017 2. Reddy C. S., Basic Structural Analysis, 3th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2017.

units.text: Compaction of Soils Introduction, theory of compaction, laboratory determination of optimum moisture content and maximum dry density. Light weight and Heavy weight Compaction Tests as IS code, Factors affecting compaction, Compaction in the field, compaction specification and field control.

units.title: Consolidation of Soils
units.text: Consolidation of Soils Introduction, comparison between compaction & consolidation, initial, primary & secondary consolidation, Terzaghi’s spring analogy for mechanism of consolidation, basic definitions, final settlement of soil deposits, consolidation settlement: one-dimensional consolidation. determination of Cv by Square root of time fitting and logarithmic time fitting method, secondary consolidation.

units.title: Shear Strength
units.text: Shear Strength Principal planes and principal stresses, Mohr-Coulomb theory, types of shear tests, direct shear test, merits & demerits of direct shear test, tri-axial compression tests, drainage conditions of UU, CU and CD tests, unconfined compression test, vane shear test.

units.title: Soil Exploration
units.text: Soil Exploration Introduction, methods of investigation, methods of boring, soil samplers and sampling, number and disposition of borings, borehole logs.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course explains the concept of influence lines and plastic analysis. It also aims to acquire knowledge of analysis for determinate and indeterminate structures and deflections of structures.

outcomes.text: Apply knowledge of general theorems related to elastic structures
Examine the deflections of statically determinate structures
Construct influence lines diagrams for determinate beams
Analyze indeterminate structures by flexibility and stiffness method
Analyze column for various end conditions
Analyze beams using plastic theory

units.title: General theorems
units.text: General theorems Types of structures occurring in practice and their classification. Stable and unstable structure, static and kinematic determinacy and indeterminacy of structure. Symmetric structure, symmetrical and anti-symmetrical loads, distinction between linear and non-linear behaviour of material and geometric non- linearity. Theorems relating to elastic structures, principle of virtual work. Strain energy in elastic structures, stresses due to axial load & impact load. Complementary energy, Castigliano’s theorem, Betti’s and Maxwell’s reciprocal theorems, principle of superposition.

units.title: Deflection of statically determinate structures
units.text: Deflection of statically determinate structures Deflection of determinate pin jointed and rigid jointed frames by principle of virtual work (unit load method) and Castigliano’s theorem. Deflection due to temperature change.

units.title: Rolling loads and Influence lines for statically determinate structures
units.text: Rolling loads and Influence lines for statically determinate structures Influence lines for cantilevers, simply supported, overhanging beams, criteria for maximum shear force and bending moment at a section, absolute maximum shear force and bending moment under moving loads (udl and series of point loads) for simply supported beams.

units.title: Analysis of indeterminate structures by flexibility method
units.text: Analysis of indeterminate structures by flexibility method Flexibility coefficients and their use in formulation of compatibility equations. Theorem of three moments, application of above methods to propped cantilevers, fixed beams, continuous beams including effect of settlement of supports.

units.title: Analysis of indeterminate structures by stiffness method
units.text: Analysis of indeterminate structures by stiffness method Stiffness coefficients for prismatic members and their use for formulation of equilibrium equations, direct stiffness method, slope deflection method, Moment distribution method. Application of the above methods to indeterminate beams and simple rigid jointed non-sway frames excluding the effect of settlement of supports.

units.title: Plastic Analysis
units.text: Plastic Analysis Introduction, Definitions of plastic hinge and plastic moment capacity, Assumptions, Shape Factor for general sections. Collapse load and basic theorems for finding collapse loads. Methods of plastic analysis – static method and kinematic method, application of above method for beams.

units.title: Columns and struts
units.text: Columns and struts Euler’s theory for long columns, columns with different end conditions, effective length and slenderness ratio of columns, Rankine’s theory for column.

text_books: 1. G. S. Pandit, S. P. Gupta, Structural Analysis – A Matrix Approach, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. S. S. Bhavikatti, Structural Analysis – Volume II, 4th Edition, Vikas Publishing, 2013.
reference_books: 1. R. C. Hibbeler, Structural Analysis, 9th Edition, Pearson, 2017 2. Reddy C. S., Basic Structural Analysis, 3th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2017.

program: B Tech and MBA Tech (All branches)
objectives: The course aims to introduce and explore a chosen problem, providing students with the opportunity to engage with a variety of real-world challenges presented by different agencies. Students come onboard at different stages of project completion. The course seeks to guide students in selecting a project that aligns with their interests, expertise, and career goals. Through this approach, the course integrates elements of Design Thinking and Research, to enhance practical learning and problem-solving skills.

outcomes.text: Identify and explain real-world challenges in their context, relevance, and impact.
Collaborate effectively within diverse teams to solve complex design problems
Utilize Design Thinking principles to develop and iteratively refine practical solutions for the selected problem.
Design and prototype innovative solutions that integrate research insights and feasibility analysis.
Demonstrate effective oral and written communication skills relevant to the problem.

units.title: Introduction and Team Formation
units.text: Introduction and Team Formation: Familiarize with real-world problems and project options and team formation based on interests and skills. Problem Analysis: Understand the problem context and requirements and conduct literature review relevant to the problem objectives. Design Thinking and Concept Development: Develop innovative solutions. Apply Design Thinking phases and refine concepts based on feedback. Project Management and Documentation: Ensure organized execution. Assign roles, manage tasks, and maintain design documents. Communication and Review: Present and refine project outcomes. Prepare presentations, conduct reviews, and incorporate feedback. Reflection and Improvement: Enhance skills and identify next steps. Reflect on lessons learned and document final outcomes.

lab_work: The Laboratory work comprises various activities performed by the project teams for formulation, solution implementation and modification. Each team needs to submit the following documents: • Problem Statement Document • Project Development Report • Mid Semester Project Report • Final Report

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Except Data Science)
prerequisites: Basic understanding of algebra, calculus, and fundamental statistical concepts.
objectives: This course aims to instill in students a sound knowledge of probability theory and statistical techniques. It equips the students with intermediate to advanced level concepts and tools in probability and statistics that help them tackle relevant problems within the engineering domain.

outcomes.text: Understand the basic concepts of probability theory and statistics.
Solve problems involving random variables, probability distributions and testing of hypothesis, correlation, and regression.
Identify suitable probability distribution and testing techniques to solve problems.
Apply knowledge of random variables, probability distributions, measures of central tendency, correlation and regression to solve real life problems.
Analyse data samples using statistical methods.

units.title: Basic Probability
units.text: Basic Probability Probability spaces, conditional probability, independence; Bayes theorem.

units.title: Random variables and Probability Distributions
units.text: Random variables and Probability Distributions Discrete random variables, probability mass function, cumulative distribution function, Independent random variables, Continuous random variables, distribution functions and densities, expectation, variance, raw and central moments of random variables, Binomial distribution, Poisson distribution, Normal distribution.

Large sample statistical test for mean, Large sample statistical test for proportion, t-test for small samples, Test for variance- F test, Chi-square test for Goodness of fit and independence of attributes, Analysis of variance.

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics
objectives: This course aims to understand the multidisciplinary nature of environmental sciences, greenhouse effect and climate change. It also aims to discuss the basics of natural resources, biodiversity, environmental pollution.

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of natural resources, ecosystem and biodiversity
Relate the various aspects of environmental pollutions with its cause and effect
Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change.

units.title: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science
units.text: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science Definition, scope and importance of environmental sciences.

Natural Resources • Natural resources: Forest resources, Water resources, Mineral resources, Food resources. • Energy resources: Growing energy needs, renewable and non- renewable energy sources, use of alternate energy sources.

Ecosystems • Concept of an ecosystem. • Structure and function of an ecosystem. • Food chains, food webs and ecological pyramids. • Introduction, types, characteristic features of the following ecosystem:- a. Forest ecosystem b. Grassland ecosystem c. Desert ecosystem d. Aquatic ecosystems.

Biodiversity • Definition: genetic, species and ecosystem diversity. • Value of biodiversity: consumptive use, productive use. • Threats to biodiversity: habitat loss, poaching of wildlife, man-wildlife conflicts.

Environmental Pollution • Definition, Cause and effects for Air pollution, Water pollution, Soil pollution, Marine pollution, Noise pollution, Thermal pollution, Nuclear hazards and Solid waste pollution.
The Science of Climate Change • Greenhouse effect • Global warming • Global environmental changes • Acid rain • Ozone layer depletion • Carbon footprint

reference_books: 1. MP Poonia & SC Sharma, “Environmental Studies”, Khanna Publishing House, 1st Edition, 2017. 2. Rajagopalan, “Environmental Studies”, Oxford University Press, Third Edition, 2015.

understand some of the contemporary issues in the engineering professions

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To make students familiar with behaviour of steel structure and their components under the action of loads. 2. To train the students for effective use of IS codes, design tables and aids in analysing and designing the steel structures by limit state method. 3. To equip students with aspects required for designing tension members, compression members and column bases. 4. To equip students with aspects required for designing beams. 5. To help students design connections in steel members. 6. To aid students in designing steel trusses.

outcomes.text: Explain the Limit State Design philosophy as applied to steel structures
Demonstrate ability to follow IS codes, design tables and aids in analysis and design of steel structures
Design columns and their bases

units.title: Introduction to Steel structures
units.text: Introduction to Steel structures: Introduction to types of steel, mechanical properties of steel, advantages of steel as structural material, design philosophies of Working Stress Method (WSM) and Limit State Method (LSM)

units.title: Introduction to Limit State Method
units.text: Introduction to Limit State Method: Limit state method, limit state of strength and serviceability (deflection, vibration, durability, fatigue, fire), characteristics and design loads, Classification of cross section- plastic, compact, semi-compact and slender, limiting width to thickness ratio.

units.title: Axially loaded and Eccentrically loaded connections

units.title: Design of Tension members
units.text: Design of Tension members: Design of tension members with welded / bolted end connections using single and double angle sections by LSM, design strength due to- yielding of gross section, rupture of critical section and block shear.

units.title: Design of Compression members
units.text: Design of Compression members: Design of compression members with welded / bolted end connections using single and double angle by LSM, design strength, effective length of compression members. Design of columns with single and built-up sections, design of lacing and batten plates with bolted and welded connections using LSM, column buckling curves, effective length, slenderness ratio, limiting values of effective slenderness ratio, buckling class of various cross sections.

units.title: Design of Column bases
units.text: Design of Column bases: Design of slab base and gusseted base using bolted and welded connection by LSM subjected to axial load, Effective area of a base plate.

units.title: Design of Beams and Beam End Connections
units.text: Design of Beams and Beam End Connections: Design of members subjected to bending by LSM, design strength in bending, effective length, laterally supported and unsupported beams, single and built-up rolled steel sections using bolted and welded connections, shear lag effect, design for shear, web buckling and web crippling, beam to beam and beam to column connections, design of framed, un- stiffened and stiffened seat connections.

program: B.Tech. (Civil Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics.
objectives: 1. To provide a basic understanding of biological mechanisms of living organisms from the perspective of engineers. 2. To encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools.

outcomes.text: Convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are diverse.
Identify DNA as a genetic material in the molecular basis of information transfer.
Classify enzymes and distinguish between different mechanisms of enzyme action.
Apply thermodynamic principles to biological systems.
Identify and classify microorganisms.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Convey that Biology is as important a scientific discipline as Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry Bring out the fundamental differences between science and engineering by drawing a comparison between eye and camera, Bird flying and aircraft. Mention the most exciting aspect of biology as an independent scientific discipline. Why we need to study biology? Discuss how biological observations of 18th Century that lead to major discoveries. Examples from Brownian motion and the origin of thermodynamics by referring to the original observation of Robert Brown and Julius Mayor. These examples will highlight the fundamental importance of observations in any scientific inquiry.

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification: Convey that classification per se is not what biology is all about. The underlying criterion, such as morphological, biochemical or ecological be highlighted. Hierarchy of life forms at phenomenological level. A common thread weaves this hierarchy Classification. Discuss classification based on (a) cellularity- Unicellular or multicellular (b) ultrastructure- prokaryotes or eucaryotes. (c) energy and Carbon utilization -Autotrophs, heterotrophs, lithotropes (d) Ammonia excretion – aminotelic, uricoteliec, ureotelic (e) Habitata- acquatic or terrestrial (e) Molecular taxonomy- three major kingdoms of life. A given organism can come under different category based on classification. Model organisms for the study of biology come from different groups. E.coli, S.cerevisiae, D. Melanogaster, C. elegance, A. Thaliana, M. musculus

units.title: Genetics
units.text: Genetics: Convey that “Genetics is to biology what Newton’s laws are to Physical Sciences” Mendel’s laws, Concept of segregation and independent assortment. Concept of allele. Gene mapping, Gene interaction, Epistasis. Meiosis and Mitosis be taught as a part of genetics. Emphasis to be give not to the mechanics of cell division nor the phases but how genetic material passes from parent to offspring. Concepts of recessiveness and dominance. Concept of mapping of phenotype to genes. Discuss about the single gene disorders in humans. Discuss the concept of complementation using human genetics.

units.title: Biomolecules
units.text: Biomolecules: Convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are as diverse as one can imagine Molecules of life. In this context discuss monomeric units and polymeric structures. Discuss about sugars, starch and cellulose. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA. Two carbon units and lipids.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes: Convey that without catalysis life would not have existed on earth Enzymology: How to monitor enzyme catalyzed reactions. How does an enzyme catalyze reactions. Enzyme classification. Mechanism of enzyme action. Discuss at least two examples. Enzyme kinetics and kinetic parameters. Why should we know these parameters to understand biology? RNA catalysis.

units.title: Information Transfer
units.text: Information Transfer: The molecular basis of coding and decoding genetic information is universal Molecular basis of information transfer. DNA as a genetic material. Hierarchy of DNA structure- from single stranded to double helix to nucleosomes. Concept of genetic code. Universality and degeneracy of genetic code. Define gene in terms of complementation and recombination.

units.title: Macromolecular analysis
units.text: Macromolecular analysis: How to analyses biological processes at the reductionistic level Proteins- structure and function. Hierarch in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors and structural elements.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism: The fundamental principles of energy transactions are the same in physical and biological world. Thermodynamics as applied to biological systems. Exothermic and endothermic versus endergonic and exergonic reactions. Concept of Keq and its relation to standard free energy. Spontaneity. ATP as an energy currency. This should include the breakdown of glucose to CO2 + H2O (Glycolysis and Krebs cycle) and synthesis of glucose from CO2 and H2O (Photosynthesis). Energy yielding and energy consuming reactions. Concept of Energy Charge.

units.title: Microbiology
units.text: Microbiology: Concept of single celled organisms. Concept of species and strains. Identification and classification of microorganisms. Microscopy. Ecological aspects of single celled organisms. Sterilization and media compositions. Growth kinetics.

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge of Characteristics of water on basis of its occurrence 2. To knowledge of Suitable method of Water Modelling for improvement of Water Quality 3. To study Water Quality Management and its legal aspects

outcomes.text: Understand characteristics of water on basis of its occurrence
Recommend suitable method of Water Modelling for improvement of Water Quality
Elaborate Water Quality Management and its legal aspects

units.title: Occurrence of Water
units.text: Occurrence of Water: Land Processes Subsurface and Channel Processes- Precipitation – Rain gauge network, Abstractions, Infiltration, Evaporation, Transpiration, Process and models Unit Hydrograph & S curve hydrograph, Dimensionless unit hydrograph, GUIH, Watershed Model and Conceptual Models.

Occurrence and Movement of Ground water, Properties of aquifer, Groundwater flow equations, Dupuit For chheimer assumptions, Well hydraulics, Partial penetration of wells, Interference of wells, Collector wells and Infiltration galleries. Pumping tests, Analysis for unconfined and non leaky and leaky confined aquifer and water table aquifer, Locating hydro geologic boundaries, Well design criteria. Natural and Artificial Recharge of Ground water- Salt water intrusion, Application of Finite Difference in ground water.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Water Quality, Water quality characteristics, sampling and analysis, Analytical methods, Automated analysis and remote monitoring. Water quality monitoring: Water Pollution, Sources of Pollution, Nature of pollutants, Existing Approaches for Control/ - Abatement of Water Quality Degradation, Water Quality Monitoring in River Basins

units.title: Water quality modelling
units.text: Water quality modelling: Modelling and Monitoring, Evolution of Water Quality Models, Types of Water Quality Models, DO and BOD in streams, Transformation and transport processes, Oxygen transfer, Turbulent mixing, Non-Point Source Pollution, Modelling Approaches For Modelling Non-point Sources.

units.title: Water Quality Management
units.text: Water Quality Management: Water quality objectives and standards, Water quality control models, Flow augmentation, River and Lake water quality Models, Groundwater quality Models, Wastewater Transport Systems. River Quality modelling, Streeter Phelps model, Fate and transport of pollutants in rivers and streams, Pulse and step inputs, transport in estuaries, Fate and transport of pollutants in lakes, step and pulse input models, Fate and transport of pollutants in subsurface systems, Step and pulse input models. Legal Aspects of Water quality: Water pollution control acts and Legislation.

text_books: 1. Steven C. Chapra (2008), “Surface Water-Quality Modelling”, Waveland Press 2. Boyd C E (2015), Water Quality An Introduction 2nd Edition, SPRINGER 3. Claude E.(2014), “Boyd Water Quality: An Introduction Springer Science & Business Media”
reference_books: 1. Howard S. Peavy, Donald R. Rowe, George Tchobanoglous Environmental Engineering (Indian Edition) McGraw-Hill, 2017 2. Tebutt, T.H.Y., (1998), “Principles of Water Quality Control”, Pergamon Press, Oxford (Classic Book) 3. Gerard Kiely, (1998), “Environmental Engineering”, McGraw Hill Publications (Classic Book) 4. Viessman, W. Jr and M.J. Hammer (1985), “Water Supply and Pollution Control”, Harper and Row Publishers, New York. (Classic Book) 5. Jerald L. Schnoor, (1996), “Environmental Modeling – Fate and Transport of Pollutants in Water, Air and Soil”, John Wiley & Sons Inc., New York. (Classic Book)

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge of structural and functional components of Ecosystem 2. To provide ability to apply knowledge of Eco technology and its relevance 3. To provide understanding to classify various Ecological Processes and its significance

outcomes.text: Understand structural and functional components of Ecosystem
Elaborate application of Eco technology and its relevance
Discuss the various Ecological Processes

units.title: Introduction to Ecology and Ecological Engineering
units.text: Introduction to Ecology and Ecological Engineering: Aim – scope and applications of Ecology, Ecological Engineering and Ecotechnology and their relevance to human civilization Ecosystem – Concept of an ecosystem, structure and function of an ecosystem, Producers, Consumers, and decomposers, Energy Flow in the ecosystem, ecological Succession, Food Chains, Food Webs and ecological pyramids, Material Cycling, Productivity, Balance of natureand ecosystem, Energy Flow in Ecosystem -Lotic and Lentic Systems, Eutrophication of Lakes. Population Growth Forms, Carrying Capacity, quantitative Ecology, Concept of Ecosystem Types of Ecosystems Development and evolution of ecosystems – Principles and concepts pertaining to communities in ecosystem – Energy flow and material cycling in ecosystems – Productivity in ecosystems.

units.title: Systems Approach in Ecological Engineering
units.text: Systems Approach in Ecological Engineering: Classification of ecotechnology – Principles and components of Systems and Modeling – Structural and functional interactions in environmental systems – Human modifications of environmental systems. Ecotechnology for Waste Treatment: Principles and operation of soil infiltration systems – wetlands and ponds – source separation systems – aquacultural systems – detritus based treatment for solid wastes – Applications of ecological engineering marine systems.

units.title: Ecological Engineering Processes
units.text: Ecological Engineering Processes: Self-organizing processes – Multiple seeded microcosms – Interface coupling in ecological systems. Concepts of energy – Adapting ecological engineering systems to potentially catastrophic events – Agro ecosystems – Determination of sustainable loading of ecosystems.

units.title: Hydroponics
units.text: Hydroponics: Definition, History of Hydroponics, Advantages and Disadvantages, Growing substrates, Types of syatems, Nutrients Solutions, Additional Improvements Aquaponics - Definition, History of Aquaponics, Aquaponics Cycle, Types of Aquaponics, Aquaponics Stages, Sustainability approach, Advantages and Disadvantages

units.title: Case Studies
units.text: Case Studies: Case studies of integrated ecological engineering systems.

text_books: 1. DR. ing.Hein van Bohemen (2005), “Ecological Engineering” Boxtel : Aeneas Technical Publishers. 2. Eugene P Odum (2005), "Fundamentals of Ecology", Cenage Learning India Private Limited
reference_books: 1. Kangas, P.C and Kangas, P.,(2003), "Ecological Engineering: Principles and Practice", Lewis Publishers, New York. 2. Etnier, C. and Guterstam, B., (1996), "Ecological Engineering for Wastewater Treatment",Lewis Publishers, New York. (Classic Book)

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To identify the different properties and functions of subgrade 2. To evaluate the grading requirements, soil survey procedure and ground improvement techniques 3. To analyse stresses in soil

outcomes.text: Identify the different properties and functions of subgrade
Evaluate the grading requirements, soil survey procedure and ground improvement techniques
Analyse stresses in soil

units.title: Subgrade
units.text: Subgrade: Functions, Importance of subgrade soil properties on pavement performance, subgrade soil classification for highway engineering purpose soils as per PRA system, revised PRA system, Burmister system, Compaction system.

units.title: Grading requirements for aggregate, selection of bases and subbase material
units.text: Grading requirements for aggregate, selection of bases and subbase material (including stabilized materials), selection of different grade of bitumen, types of bituminous surfaces, skid qualities, bituminous mix design, Marshall stability test, design aspect of paving concrete. Experimental characteristics of road aggregate.

units.title: Soil Survey
units.text: Soil Survey: Soil Survey Procedure for Highway and Ground Water Investigation. Identification and Significance of soil Characteristics, effect of water in soil Swelling/shrinkage, cohesion, plasticity in soil. Soil Moisture movement- ground water, gravitational water, held water, soil suction.

units.title: Storm water Drainage
units.text: Storm water Drainage: General principles, subsoil Drainage. Frost action soil: Frost susceptible soils, depth of frost penetration, loss of strength during frost melting. Compaction of soils, field and laboratory method of soil compaction, equipments used in field compaction. Design of surface and subsurface drainage system, pumping system, water body, holding ponds.

units.title: Stress in soil
units.text: Stress in soil: Theories of elastic and plastic behaviour of soils, Methods of reducing settlement, estimation of rate of settlement due to consolidation in foundation of road embankment., static and cyclic triaxial test on subgrade soils, resilient deformation, resilient strain, resilient modulus. CBR test, effect of lateral confinement on CBR and E – value of Subgrade soil. Static and cyclic plate load test, estimation of modulus of subgrade reaction, correction for plate size, correction for worst moisture content.

units.title: Ground Improvement Technique
units.text: Ground Improvement Technique: Different method of soil stabilization, use of geo-textile, geogrid and fibres in highway subgrade. Vertical sand drain: design criteria, construction and uses

text_books: 1. L. R. Kadiyali and Dr. N. B. Lal (2011), “Principles and Practices of Highway Engineering”, Khanna Publication, New Delhi
reference_books: 1. Khanna & Justo, (2011), “Highway Engineering”, New Chand & Brothers, Roorkee 2. Yoder, E. J., (1975), “Principles of Pavement Design, Second edition”, John Wiley & Sons, Inc., New York (Classic Book)

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
prerequisites: Soil Mechanics, Mechanics of Materials, Geology
objectives: 1. To give an overview of latest ground improvement techniques 2. To understand the problems related to soil and select the best method

outcomes.text: identify the problems in soft soils
Implement the modification methods such as compaction, stone column, vibro-flotation etc.
Apply vertical drain and grouting techniques
Application of design principles of geosynthetics, anchors and soil nailing

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Needs, different types of problematic soil distribution in India, role of ground improvement in foundation engineering. Methods of ground improvement - selection of ground improvement techniques

units.title: Mechanical modifications
units.text: Mechanical modifications: Introduction - terminology – compaction, stabilisation, consolidation. Method of compaction - Shallow surface compaction, Deep compaction Techniques – Pre compression, explosion, heavy temping, vibration, vibro-compaction, Vibro- replacement, compaction grouting. Calculation MDD, OMC and percentage compaction in the field Stone Columns - design criteria, failure mechanism, principles of soil compactions, properties of compacted soil, Compaction control tests, Dynamic Compaction, Liquefaction of compaction and its remedial measures, Numerical problems.

units.title: Preloading and the use of vertical drains
units.text: Preloading and the use of vertical drains: Preloading without vertical drains - needs for preloading, numerical problems. Preloading with vertical drains - numerical problems, assessment of ground conditions, introduction to Prefabricated vertical drains (PVD) with vacuum consolidation Instrumentation – Piezometers, settlement plates, gauges and levelling point, use of inclinometers

units.title: Modification by grouting
units.text: Modification by grouting: Introduction - categories of grouting, grout materials. Grout with cement - Portland cement, Micro-fine cement. Jet grouting – procedure, Compaction grouting, Chemical grouts –properties. Grouting Theory - basic consideration, stability of interface, flow through soil voids, effect of pumping rate on grout flow, effect of pumping pressure on grout flow, fracturing. Grouting technology, field equipment, application of grouting - Case study

units.title: Geosynthetics
units.text: Geosynthetics: Introductions- types of geosynthetics, function of geosynthetics. Application areas - Retaining walls, Embankments, Shallow foundations, Roads, Railways, Slopes, Dams, Tunnels. Design of geotextiles – properties, frictional behaviour Design of geotextile walls, Design of geotextile stabilized embankments; Geotextile stabilized Foundation soil design, Design of geotextile filtration, numerical problems.

units.title: In-situ ground reinforcement
units.text: In-situ ground reinforcement: Introduction - ground anchors, components of anchors, transfer of load in anchors, mechanism of bond between grout and borehole wall. Rock Anchors - case study, anchor in granular soils, anchor in cohesive soils. Soil nailing - case study.

text_books: 1. Nihar Rajan Patra, (2013), “Ground Improvement Techniques”, Vikas Publishing House Pvt Ltd.
reference_books: 1. R. M. Koerner (2012), “Designing with Geosynthetics”, Volume -I & II, Sixth Edition, Pearson Prentice Hall 2. P. Purushothama Raj (2005) “Ground Improvement Techniques”, Laxmi Publications Pvt. Ltd. 3. M. P. Mose ley (1998) “Ground Improvement Blockie Academic and Professional”, Chapman and Hall, Glasgow (Classic Book) 4. M.R. Hausmann (1990) “Engineering Principles of Ground Modification”, McGraw-Hill Inc., US (Classic Book)

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
prerequisites: Soil Mechanics, Foundation Engineering, Advanced Geotechnical Engineering
objectives: 1. To introduce the concepts of planning of for geotechnical investigations 2. To identify the situation-based selection of sampling technique 3. To get acquainted with the different instrumentation techniques and equipment 4. To analyse the data obtained from geotechnical investigation for interpretations

outcomes.text: Apply the principles pf planning of geotechnical investigations
Evaluate the geotechnical situation for proper selection of sampling techniques and method of field testing
Analyse the proper use of appropriate instrumentation for geotechnical investigations and monitoring
Interpret the geotechnical data and prepare the geotechnical investigation reports

units.title: Geotechnical investigation
units.text: Geotechnical investigation: Planning of Exploration and experimental programme, investigations, exploration for preliminary design, exploration for detailed design geo-physical explorations (soundings, probing, boring, boring methods), excavation methods for explorations, ground water investigations, rock boring, miscellaneous exploratory techniques, use of hydraulic rig for boring

units.title: Sampling and in-situ field tests
units.text: Sampling and in-situ field tests: Types of samples, samplers, preservation, shipment and storage of samples, bore log, pore pressure measurements, core recovery, rock strength, rock quality designation In-situ field testing and laboratory investigation of soils and rock (including advanced equipment), instrumentation, data acquisition and measurement techniques: SPT, SCPT, DCPT, pressure-meter, dilatometer, permeability, plate load test, determination of subgrade modulus. Numerical problems

units.title: Instrumentation
units.text: Instrumentation: Pore pressure measurement, types of piezometers, factors affecting pore pressure measurement, measurement of displacements, establishment of permanent bench mark in loose soil, types of settlement gauges, measurement of heave, measurement of horizontal displacements

units.title: Data interpretation
units.text: Data interpretation: Data interpretation for determination of engineering properties of soils and their application to geotechnical design, reading and preparation of soil investigation report from the data obtained from site

text_books: 1. Dr. N. V Nayak (2018), “Foundation Design Manual”, Dhanpat Rai Publications 2. John Dunnicliff (1982) “Geotechnical Instrumentation for Monitoring Field Performance”, Transportation Research Board (Classic book) Reference Book and Material: 1. “Earth Manual - Part 1” (1990), U.S. Department of the interior bureau of reclamation (Classic Book) 2. C. R. I. Clayton, M. C. Matthews and N. E. Simons (1982), “Site Investigation” Second Edition, Halsted Press (Classic Book)

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)

objectives: 1. To introduce financial statements and their analysis 2. To develop capability of using various methods of analysis for investment proposals 3. To introduce various aspects of project financing and fund management for projects

outcomes.text: Understand and analyze financial statements
Analyze investment alternatives
Understand management of funds for projects

units.title: Overview of Finance Management
units.text: Overview of Finance Management: Overview, finance functions, relevance of finance management in construction industry

units.title: Financial Statements and Analysis
units.text: Financial Statements and Analysis: Necessity of preparing financial statements, Income statement and Balance Sheet structure, terminologies associated, concept of depreciation, financial ratios and analysis, construction accounting

units.title: Time Value of Money
units.text: Time Value of Money:Principle of equivalence, Cash Flow diagram – Nominal and effective interest- continuous interest. Compounding and discounting concepts, future value, present value, annuity, perpetuity

units.title: Comparing Alternative Proposals
units.text: Comparing Alternative Proposals: Capital budgeting principles and process, discounting and non discounting techniques for evaluation and comparison of proposals, payback period, ARR, NPV, IRR, Replacement analysis, IROR, benefit/cost analysis, break even analysis

units.title: Working capital management
units.text: Working capital management : Concept of working capital, factors affecting working capital, working capital cycle and calculating working capital cycle,, calculation of working capital, Sources of working capital

units.title: Fund Management
units.text: Fund Management: Project Financing principles, balance sheet and off balance sheet finance, project cash flows, sources of long term finance, project appraisal

text_books: 1. Prasanna Chandra (2011), “Fundamentals of financial Management”, Mc- Graw Hill Book Co. 2. Patel, B M (2016), “Project management- Strategic Financial Planning, Evaluation and Control”, Vikas Publishing House Pvt. Ltd. New Delhi.
reference_books: 1. Collier C. and GlaGola C. (1998), “Engineering Economics & Cost Analysis”, 3rd Edn. Addison Wesley Education Publishers. (Classic Book) 2. program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
prerequisites: Objectives: 1. To understand safety measures and safety issues in construction 2. To understand various safety regulations and methods of fire prevention
objectives: 1. To understand safety measures and safety issues in construction 2. To understand various safety regulations and methods of fire prevention

outcomes.text: Discuss various safety measures and safety issues in construction
Discuss various safety regulations and fire prevention

units.title: Construction Safety Management
units.text: Construction Safety Management: Role of various parties, duties and responsibilities of top management, site managers, supervisors etc. role of safety officers, responsibilities of general employees, safety committee, safety training, incentives and monitoring. Writing safety manuals, preparing safety checklists and inspection reports, PPE and it’s uses.

units.title: Reporting, Recording and Investigation
units.text: Reporting, Recording and Investigation: Investigation of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences, Principles of Accident Prevention , Accident definitions ,Incidents ‘Hazard’, ‘Danger’ and ‘Risk’ , Accident prevention strategies , Safe systems of work Safety monitoring systems ,Accident and ill- health rates , Risk assessment , The role of the health and safety practitioner

units.title: Human Factors
units.text: Human Factors: Behavioural safety, Human error, Planned motivation schemes. The application of ergonomics in working situations, Principles of ergonomic design, Controls and displays , Display screen equipment , Manual handling injuries and conditions , Management action Stress at Work, Post- traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)

units.title: Occupational Health
units.text: Occupational Health: Occupational Diseases and Conditions, Occupational health, Occupational diseases, Provisions for Occupational health in BOCW Act, Occupational health schemes, Benefits of occupational health services, Sickness absence control, Sickness absence procedure, Sickness absence monitoring

units.title: Selection of work equipment
units.text: Selection of work equipment: Principles of machinery safety, Other hazards associated with machinery operation, Machinery guards, Machinery safety devices, Planned maintenance, Lifting operations and lifting equipment, Machinery safety assessment etc., safety of scaffolding and working platforms.

units.title: Fire Prevention
units.text: Fire Prevention: The fire triangle, Causes of fire spread, Safety while using electrical appliances, Explosives, Fire extinction, Fire appliances, Colour coding of fire appliances, Fire protection systems, Legal requirements

units.title: Safety Regulations
units.text: Safety Regulations: Labour laws, legal requirement and cost aspects of accidents on site. Study of safety policies, methods, equipment, and training provided on any ISO approved construction company

text_books: 1. Phil & Ferrett, Ed (2011), “Introduction to Health and Safety in Construction :The Handbook for the NEBOSH National Certificate in Construction”, Health and Safety / Hughes 2. R. K. Mishra (2013),”Construction Safety”, AITBS Publication
reference_books: 1. Stranks, Jeremy (2010), “Health and Safety at Work: An Essential Guide for Managers 9th Edition” 2. Girimaldi and Simonds (1986),” Safety Management”, AITBS Publication (Classic Book)

program: B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To understand various processes in manpower planning, organizational and welfare measures in construction.

outcomes.text: After completion of this course, students would be able to understand various processes in manpower planning, organizational and welfare measures in construction

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Human Resources Management in context of construction, relationship between human resources management and the external environment, human resources management arising from organization culture and traditions.

units.title: Organization
units.text: Organization: Requirement of Organisation – Organisation structure – Organisation Hierarchical charts – Staffing Plan - Development and Operation of human resources – Manpower Planning, Managerial Staffing – Recruitment – Selection strategies – Placement and Training.

units.title: External Issues affecting human resources management in construction
units.text: External Issues affecting human resources management in construction: Technological change, new work pattern, social values.

units.title: Human Relations and Organizational Behavior
units.text: Human Relations and Organizational Behavior: Basic individual psychology – Approaches to job design and job redesign – Self managing work teams – Intergroup – Conflict in organizations – Leadership-Engineer as Manager – al aspects of decision making – Significance of human relation and organizational – Individual in organization – Motivation – Personality and creativity – Group dynamics, Team working – Communication and negotiation skills.

units.title: Industrial relations in construction
units.text: Industrial relations in construction: Labour force, employers, industrial relations systems, future of industrial relations

units.title: Management and Development Methods
units.text: Management and Development Methods: Wages and Salary, Employee benefits, Employee appraisal and assessment – Employee services – Safety and Health Management – Special Human resource problems – Productivity in human resources – Innovative approach to designing and managing organization – Managing New Technologies – Total Quality Management – Concept of quality of work life – Levels of change in the organizational Development – Requirements of organizational Development – System design and methods for automation and management of operations – Developing policies, practices and establishing process pattern – Competency upgradation and their assessment – New methods of training and development – Performance Management.

text_books: 1. Langford D, Hancock M.R. (2014) “Human resources management in construction”, Routledge Publishing, UK. 2. Dwivedi R.S (2005), "Human Relations and Organisational Behaviour", Macmillian India Ltd.
reference_books: 1. Charles D Pringle, Justin Gooderi Longenecter(1981), “Management”, CE Merril Publishing Co. 2. Familaro (1987), "Handbook of Human Resources Administration", McGraw-Hill International Edition. (Classic Book) 3. Memoria,C.B.(1997), "Personnel Management", Himalaya Publishing Co. (Classic Book)

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To make students familiar with behaviour of steel structure and their components under the action of loads. 2. To train the students for effective use of IS codes, design tables and aids in analysing and designing the steel structures by limit state method. 3. To equip students with aspects required for designing tension members, compression members and column bases. 4. To equip students with aspects required for designing beams. 5. To help students design connections in steel members. 6. To aid students in designing steel trusses.

outcomes.text: Explain the Limit State Design philosophy as applied to steel structures
Demonstrate ability to follow IS codes, design tables and aids in analysis and design of steel structures
Design columns and their bases
Design the various end connections for beams and trusses
Design steel trusses subjected to live load and wind load

units.title: Introduction to Steel structures
units.text: Introduction to Steel structures: Introduction to types of steel, mechanical properties of steel, advantages of steel as structural material, design philosophies of Working Stress Method (WSM) and Limit State Method (LSM)

units.title: Introduction to Limit State Method
units.text: Introduction to Limit State Method: Limit state method, limit state of strength and serviceability (deflection, vibration, durability, fatigue, fire), characteristics and design loads, Classification of cross section- plastic, compact, semi-compact and slender, limiting width to thickness ratio.

units.title: Axially loaded and Eccentrically loaded connections
units.text: Axially loaded and Eccentrically loaded connections: Introduction to bolted and welded axially and eccentrically loaded connections by LSM.

units.title: Design of Tension members
units.text: Design of Tension members: Design of tension members with welded / bolted end connections using single and double angle sections by LSM, design strength due to- yielding of gross section, rupture of critical section and block shear.

units.title: Design of Compression members
units.text: Design of Compression members: Design of compression members with welded / bolted end connections using single and double angle by LSM, design strength, effective length of compression members. Design of columns with single and built-up sections, design of lacing and batten plates with bolted and welded connections using LSM, column buckling curves, effective length, slenderness ratio, limiting values of effective slenderness ratio, buckling class of various cross sections.

units.title: Design of Column bases
units.text: Design of Column bases: Design of slab base and gusseted base using bolted and welded connection by LSM subjected to axial load, Effective area of a base plate.

units.title: Design of Beams and Beam End Connections
units.text: Design of Beams and Beam End Connections: Design of members subjected to bending by LSM, design strength in bending, effective length, laterally supported and unsupported beams, single and built-up rolled steel sections using bolted and welded connections, shear lag effect, design for shear, web buckling and web crippling, beam to beam and beam to column connections, design of framed, un- stiffened and stiffened seat connections.

text_books: 1. S. K. Duggal (2009), “Design of Steel Structure - 3rd Edition”, Tata McGraw- Hill Education 2. S. S. Bhavikatti (2014), “Design of Steel Structures (By Limit State Method as Per IS: 800 2007)”, I. K. International Pvt Ltd
reference_books: 1. N. Subramanian (2011), “Design of Steel Structures”, Oxford 2. P. Dayaratnam (2008), “Design of Steel Structures”, S Chand Limited 3. IS:800, “General Construction in Steel – Code of Practice Third Revision”, BIS Publication 4. Relevant IS codes and handbooks

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge on design concepts of RCC structures 2. To understand and design beams of rectangular and flanged sections using LSM 3. To understand and design slabs and staircases using limit state method of design 4. To understand and design columns and simple footings subjected to axial loads and moments

outcomes.text: Analyse and design reinforced concrete members using WSM and ULM
Analyse and design beams of rectangular and flanged sections using LSM
Analyse and design slabs and staircases using limit state method of design
Analyse and design columns and simple footings subjected to axial loads and moments

units.title: Introduction to Reinforced Concrete
units.text: Introduction to Reinforced Concrete: Concept of reinforced concrete, various methods of design for reinforced concrete, permissible stresses as per IS 456, stress strain curve of concrete and steel, characteristics of concrete and steel reinforcement.

units.title: Working stress method and Ultimate load method
units.text: Working stress method and Ultimate load method: Analysis and design of singly reinforced and doubly reinforced rectangular beams by WSM. Brief introduction to fundamentals of ultimate strength theory: curved stress distribution, compressive stress block, simplified rectangular stress block as per Whitney's approach, ultimate moment of resistance of singly reinforced section and doubly reinforced sections.

units.title: Limit state method
units.text: Limit state method: Introduction to limit state method of design as per IS 456 (latest edition): concepts of probability and reliability, characteristic loads, characteristic strength, partial safety factors for loads and materials, introduction to various limit states.

units.title: Limit state of collapse - Flexure
units.text: Limit state of collapse - Flexure: Limit state of collapse in flexure, shear and Limit state of serviceability in deflection and cracking, design of singly and doubly reinforced rectangular and T sections for flexure, design of members in shear and bond, design of beam.

units.title: Design of slabs
units.text: Design of slabs: Design of simply supported one-way, two-way cantilever slabs and flooring systems.

units.title: Limit state of collapse - Compression
units.text: Limit state of collapse - Compression: Compression: Limit state of collapse compression for short and slender column.

units.title: Design of staircases
units.text: Design of staircases: Design of Dog legged staircase

units.title: Design of Foundations
units.text: Design of Foundations: Isolated square and rectangular footings subjected to axial load and moments.

text_books: 1. S. N. Sinha (2007), “Reinforced Concrete Design”, Tata McGraw Hill. 2. H. J. Shah (2008), “Reinforced Concrete I & II”, Charotar Publishing House Pvt. Ltd. 3. Shah & Karve (2010), “Illustrated Reinforced Concrete Design”, Structure Publication, Pune.
reference_books: 1. IS 456, "Code of Practice for Plain and Reinforced Concrete ", BIS Publication 2. Shah & Karve (2010), “Limit State Design - Reinforced Concrete”, Structure Publication, Pune. 3. Dayaratnam P (2008), “Limit State Design of Reinforced Concrete Structures”, Oxford & IBH. 4. Jain A K (2007), “Limit State design - Reinforced Concrete”, New Chand.

units.text: Review of recent geotechnical research: Present a State of the Art report on the recent research topics in geotechnical engineering
