program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. The aim of this course is to introduce students to the application of scientific procedures to the conduction of research.

outcomes.text: Comprehend the basics of research process
Recognise the importance of literature review
Write a technical report/paper.
Relate ethical guidelines to conducting research, data collection and report writing

units.title: Introduction to research
units.text: Introduction to research: The importance of research, research process overview, types of research, research terminology

units.title: Literature search and review
units.text: Literature search and review: Searching for existing literature on a selected topic, reviewing the papers in selected area, use of abstract and citation databases for literature search

units.title: Formulating and solving a research problem
units.text: Formulating and solving a research problem: Identifying a research problem, formulation of hypothesis, research objectives and questions, different types of research designs, experimental setup, data sampling and collection, data analysis

units.title: Technical writing
units.text: Technical writing: Research paper writing, referencing in proper format, tools for technical writing,

units.title: Ethics in research
units.text: Ethics in research: Research integrity, plagiarism basics and checks

text_books: -- 1. Research Methodology: Methods and techniques, C R Kothari, New Age International (P) Limited Publishers. 2. Research Methodology a step by step guide for beginners, Ranjit Kumar, Pearson Publications
reference_books: -- 1. Smart Melville, Wayne Goddard, Research Methodology: An introduction or Science and Engineering Students, Juta &Co. Ltd.

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge of analysis for determinate and indeterminate arches 2. To impart knowledge of analysis of components of cable and suspension bridges 3. Apply the concepts of analysis for indeterminate structures 4. Apply the concept of plastic analysis for frames

outcomes.text: Analyse the arches and determine the internal forces developed
Analyse the components of the cable and suspension bridge
Analyse indeterminate structure by flexibility method
Analyse indeterminate structure by stiffness method
Analyse frames using concepts of plastic analysis

units.title: Analysis of two and three hinged arches
units.text: Analysis of two and three hinged arches: Three hinged symmetrical and unsymmetrical circular and parabolic arches- determination of support reactions, normal thrust, radial shear and bending moment at any section, influence lines for symmetrical arches. Analysis of two hinged parabolic arches

units.title: Analysis of cable and suspension bridges
units.text: Analysis of cable and suspension bridges: Simple suspension cable & symmetrical, unsymmetrical, minimum and maximum tension in the cable, anchor cable, cable supports, suspension cable with three hinged stiffening girder, shear force and bending moment at any section of the stiffening girder, influence lines for the girder and the cable

units.title: Application of flexibility method
units.text: Application of flexibility method: Flexibility coefficients and their use in formulation of compatibility equations. Theorem of three moments, Castigliano’s theorem of least work, application of above methods to indeterminate beams, frames and trusses including effect of settlement of supports, lack of fit, spring supports.

units.title: Application of stiffness method
units.text: Application of stiffness method: Stiffness coefficients for prismatic members and their use for formulation of equilibrium equations, direct stiffness method, slope deflection method, Moment distribution method. Application of above methods to indeterminate beams, frames and including effect of settlement of supports.

units.title: Plastic Analysis of Frames
units.text: Plastic Analysis of Frames: Analysis of single-bay-single-storey, single-bay- multiple-storey, multiple-bay-single-storey frames. Concept of loss of plastic hinge

text_books: 1. G. S. Pandit, S. P. Gupta (2007), “Structural Analysis – A Matrix Approach”, Tata McGraw Hill 2. S. S. Bhavikatti (2013), “Structural Analysis – Volume II”, Vikas Publishing
reference_books: 1. R. C. Hibbeler (2016), “Structural Analysis in SI Units”, Pearson 2. Reddy C. S. (2011), “Basic Structural Analysis – Third Edition”, Tata McGraw Hill

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
prerequisites: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics; Hydraulics and Fluid Machinery
objectives: 1. To introduce various hydraulic problems related to open channel flow 2. To understand GVF,RVF and surges and relate the theory and practice of problems in hydraulic engineering

outcomes.text: Apply their knowledge of fluid mechanics in addressing problems in open channels.
Possess the skills to solve problems in uniform, gradually and rapidly varied flows in steady state conditions.
Possess the skills to solve problems in surges

units.title: Gradually Varied Flow
units.text: Gradually Varied Flow: Dynamic Equation of Gradually Varied Flow, Classification of channel bottom slopes, Classification of surface profile, characteristics of surface profile.

units.title: Water surface profile
units.text: Water surface profile: Computation of water surface profile by graphical, numerical and analytical approaches. Direct Step method, Graphical Integration method and Direct integration method.

units.title: Non-Uniform Flow
units.text: Non-Uniform Flow : Specific energy, Specific energy curve, critical flow, discharge curve Specific force Specific depth, and Critical depth. Channel transitions. Measurement of Discharge and Velocity – Venturi Flume, Standing Wave Flume, Parshall Flume, Broad Crested Weir. Measurement of Velocity- Current meter, Floats, Hot-wire anemometer.

units.title: Hydraulic Jump
units.text: Hydraulic Jump: Theory of Hydraulic jump, Elements of characteristics of hydraulic jump in a rectangular channel, Length and height of jump, location of jump, Types, applications and location of hydraulic jump. Energy dissipation and other uses.

units.title: Waves and Surges
units.text: Waves and Surges: Unsteady flow, Types of Surges, Positive surge, Negative surge, Celerity

text_books: 1. P.M. Modi and S.M. Seth (2017), “Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics”, Standard Book House 2. K. Subramanya (2018), “Theory and Applications of Fluid Mechanics”, Tata McGraw Hill. 3. K. Subramanya (2009), “Open channel Flow”, Tata McGraw Hill.
reference_books: 1. Ven Te Chow (2009), “Open Channel Hydraulics”, Tata McGraw Hill.

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To estimate stresses in soil 2. To analyse stability of earth slopes 3. To analyse earth retaining structures 4. To estimate bearing capacity of shallow and group of pile foundation

outcomes.text: Estimate stresses in soil using appropriate theories
Distinguish between types of slope failures, and analyze the stability of earth slopes
Analyse earth retaining structures like gravity and cantilever retaining walls
Analyse and estimate bearing capacity and settlement of shallow and pile foundations

units.title: Stress distribution in soils
units.text: Stress distribution in soils: Introduction, Boussinesq’s theory, vertical stress distribution diagrams, construction of isobars, Pressure bulbs, Influence coefficients, vertical stresses beneath loaded areas - point load, line load, uniformly loaded rectangular and circular areas, Newmark’s influence chart, Westergaard’s analysis

units.title: Consolidation of soils
units.text: Consolidation of soils: Introduction to consolidation, basic definitions, spring analogy, computation of total settlement, Terzaghi’s one-dimensional theory of consolidation, secondary consolidation, degree of consolidation, time rate of consolidation, computation of rate of settlements, determination of cv from consolidation test results, square root of time and logarithm of time methods

units.title: Stress and strain behaviour of soils
units.text: Stress and strain behaviour of soils: Shear strength of sands and clays, triaxial test - drained and undrained behaviour of sands and clays, Skempton’s pore pressure Strain softening and strain hardening, Octahedral plane, Mohr - Coulomb’s criterion, ideal, plastic, and real soil behaviour

units.title: Stability of slopes
units.text: Stability of slopes: Introduction, types of slope failure, different factors of safety, analysis of infinite slopes, Stability of finite slopes- plane failure, Swedish circle method, friction circle method, stability numbers and charts

units.title: Design of shallow foundations
units.text: Design of shallow foundations: Types of shear failure - general, local and punching; ultimate bearing capacity in case of general and local shear failure, Vesic method, IS code method. Plate load test in detail with reference to IS: 1888 and its applications and estimation of settlements, bearing capacity based on standard penetration tests

units.title: Analysis of pile foundations
units.text: Analysis of pile foundations: Pile load test as per IS: 2911 specifications, negative skin friction, capacity of single piles, pile groups, ultimate capacity of groups, settlement of pile groups in sand and in clays as per IS 2911 and critical depth method, Introduction to piled raft foundation, NDT for piles

units.title: Earth pressure on retaining structures
units.text: Earth pressure on retaining structures: Analysis of gravity retaining wall

units.title: Braced cuts
units.text: Braced cuts: Lateral earth pressure distribution, apparent pressure diagrams, estimation of strut forces and loads in deep cuts in stiff clay, sand, saturated clay. Bjerrum and Eide method of analysis, use of touch piles, secant piles, anchors for shoring system

text_books: 1. Dr. Alam Singh (2014), “Soil Engineering in Theory and Practice”, Vol-I, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd. 2. VNS Murthy (2011), “Text Book of Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering”, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd.
reference_books: 1. Hans Winterkorn and Hsai-Yang Fang (1986), “Foundation Engineering Handbook”, Publisher in India- Galgotia Booksource (Classic Book) 2. B. M. Das (2011), “Principles of Foundation Engineering”, Cengage Learning 3. Relevant IS Codes, BIS Publications

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To introduce substructure construction using advanced techniques 2. To impart knowledge of superstructure construction 3. To impart knowledge of construction of special structures 4. To understand concepts of demolition, repairs and rehabilitation

outcomes.text: Understand modern construction techniques for substructure, superstructure and special structures
Understand demolition techniques and rehabilitation techniques

units.title: Substructure Construction
units.text: Substructure Construction: Box jacking, pipe jacking, under water construction of diaphragm walls and basement, tunnelling techniques, piling techniques, driving well and caisson, sinking cofferdam, cable anchoring and grouting, driving diaphragm walls, sheet piles, laying operations for built up offshore system, shoring for deep cutting, large reservoir construction, well points, dewatering for underground open excavation.

units.title: Superstructure Construction
units.text: Superstructure Construction: Vacuum dewatering of concrete flooring, concrete paving technology, techniques of construction for continuous concreting operation in tall buildings of various shapes and varying sections, erection techniques of tall structures, concrete chimneys and cooling towers, large span structures, launching techniques for heavy decks, in-situ pre-stressing in high rise structures, post tensioning of slab, handling and erecting lightweight components on tall structures.

units.title: Construction of Special Structures
units.text: Construction of Special Structures: Erection of lattice towers, rigging of transmission line structures, construction sequence in cooling towers, silos, chimney, sky scrapers, bow string bridges, cable stayed bridges, launching and pushing of box decks, construction of jetties and break water structures, construction sequence and methods in domes, support structure for heavy equipment and machinery in heavy industries, erection of articulated structures and space decks.

units.title: Demolition
units.text: Demolition: Demolition techniques, demolition by machines, demolition by explosives, advanced techniques using robotic machines, demolition sequence, dismantling techniques, safety precaution in demolition and dismantling.

units.title: Repairs and Rehabilitation
units.text: Repairs and Rehabilitation: Repairs and Rehabilitation techniques for Column, Beam, Footing, Basics of seismic retrofitting, Use of chemicals and polymers for repairs and rehabilitation. Use of FRP.

text_books: 1. Sarkar, S.K. and Saraswati, S (2008), “Construction Technology”, Oxford University Press, New Delhi. 2. Gahlot P.S., Sharma S.(2014), “Building Repairs and Maintanance Management”, CBS Publishers and Distributors.
reference_books: 1. Robert wade Brown (2005), "Practical Foundation Engineering Hand Book", Mcgraw Hill Publications 2. Patrick Powers. J. (2015), “Construction Dewatering and Groundwater Control”, John Wiley & Sons. 3. CPWD Handbook on “Repair and Rehabilitation of RCC buildings”, Govt of India Press, New Delhi

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To introduce rehabilitation of structures 2. To study non-destructive and destructive testing methods 3. To evaluate structural damage 4. To study materials for repair: 5. To develop capability to investigate appropriate rehabilitation technique 6. To understand guidelines for repair and rehabilitation works

outcomes.text: Estimate causes for distress and deterioration of structures
Understand NDT techniques for condition assessment of structures for identifying damages in structures.
Select repair material and retrofitting strategy suitable for distress
Formulate guidelines for repair management of deteriorated structures

units.title: Introduction to Rehabilitation
units.text: Introduction to Rehabilitation: An overview of present repair practices, distress identification and repair management, Causes of distress in concrete structures- Holistic Models for deterioration of concrete, Permeability of concrete, aggressive chemical agents, durability aspects, Condition Survey- Definition, objectives, different stages-Preliminary inspection, planning stage, visual inspection, field laboratory testing stage, consideration for repair strategy.

units.title: Non-Destructive and Destructive Testing Methods
units.text: Non-Destructive and Destructive Testing Methods: Non-Destructive evaluation tests, Concrete strength assessment , Rebound hammer test , Ultrasonic pulse velocity tests, penetration resistance, pull out tests, core sampling and testing, Chemical tests - Carbonation tests and chloride content, Corrosion potential assessment, cover meter survey, half-cell potentiometer test, resistivity measurement, Discussion of case studies of RCC buildings subjected to distress, Identification and estimation of damage.

units.title: Evaluation of Structural properties
units.text: Evaluation of Structural properties: Fire damage assessment, structural integrity and soundness assessment, interpretation and evaluation of results, Evaluation of reserve strength of existing structures, analysis necessary to identify critical sections, active and passive repairs, modelling of repaired composite structures.

units.title: Repair materials and case studies
units.text: Repair materials and case studies: Selection of repair materials for concrete, Essential parameters for repair materials, Strength and durability aspects, cost and suitability aspects, Materials for repair, Premixed cement concrete and mortars, polymer modified mortars and concrete, epoxy and epoxy systems including epoxy mortars and concrete, polyester resins, coatings, Discussion of case studies- RCC buildings, water tanks, industrial structures, Identifying a suitable repair option for certain damage in a structure.

units.title: Repair/ Rehabilitation methods and strategies
units.text: Repair/ Rehabilitation methods and strategies: Rehabilitation and retrofitting methods, repair options, performance requirements of repair systems, important factors to be considered for selection of repair methods, Repair stages, Guniting, shotcreting, polymer concrete system, reinforcement replacement, strengthening concrete by surface impregnation, polymer and epoxy overlays, Resin/polymer modified slurry injection, plate bonding technique, ferrocement jacketing, RCC jacketing, propping and supporting, fiber wrap technique, foundation rehabilitation methods, chemical and electrochemical method of repair, Repair/Rehabilitation strategies, Stress reduction technique, repair and strengthening of columns and beams, Compressive strength of concrete, cracks/joints, masonry, foundation, base isolation.

units.title: Guidelines for repair and rehabilitation works
units.text: Guidelines for repair and rehabilitation works: Guidelines for framing terms and conditions for repair and rehabilitation works contracts, engagement of consultants, contractors, execution of work, post repair inspection.

text_books: 1. CPWD Handbook on “Repair and Rehabilitation of RCC buildings”, Govt of India Press, New Delhi
reference_books: 1. Raikar, R.N.(1987), “Learning from failures - Deficiencies in Design, Construction and Service” R&D Centre (SDCPL), Raikar Bhavan, Bombay,(Classic Book)

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge of unsymmetrical bending and shear centre 2. To impart knowledge of analysis of curved beams 3. Apply the concepts of analysis for deep beams and beams on elastic foundation 4. Understand the concept of theories of failure

outcomes.text: Determine the internal forces developed in various structures subjected to various loads
Calculate the stresses at failure applying the concepts of theories of failure
Analyse deep beams and beams on elastic foundation

units.title: Unsymmetrical Bending and Shear Centre
units.text: Unsymmetrical Bending and Shear Centre: Bending of symmetrical and non- symmetrical (about both axis) sections, shear centre for thin walled open sections
Bending of beams with large initial curvature loaded in their plane of curvature: Application to analysis of hooks, circular closed rings, chain links with straight length and semi-circular ends.

units.title: Beams on elastic foundation
units.text: Beams on elastic foundation: Analysis of beams of infinite length subjected to concentrated force/moment and semi-infinite length subjected to concentrated load/moment at one end. Semi-infinite beam hinged at one end (origin) & subjected to UDL throughout.

units.title: Beams curved in plan
units.text: Beams curved in plan: Analysis of beams loaded perpendicular to their own plane, simply supported, fixed and continuous beams.

units.title: Theories of Failure
units.text: Theories of Failure: Maximum principal stress theory, Maximum principal strain theory, Maximum shear stress theory, maximum total strain energy theory.

units.title: Analysis of deep beams
units.text: Analysis of deep beams: Determination of deflection. Determination of shear correction factor for various sections rectangular solid and hollow section and circular solid and hollow section and I-section

units.title: Torsion in non-circular sections
units.text: Torsion in non-circular sections: Torsion of solid section rectangle, triangular and hexagon section

text_books: 1. James M. Gere, Barry J. Goodno (2012), “Mechanics of Materials – SI Edition”, Cengage Learning 2. Subramanian (2010), “Strength of Materials”, Oxford University Press
reference_books: 1. Andrew Pytel, Jaan Kiusalaas (2011), “Mechanics of Materials – Second Edition”, Cengage Learning 2. Ferdinand P. Beer, E. Russell Johnston Jr., John T. DeWolf (2008), “Mechanics of Materials – Third Edition”, Tata McGraw Hill 3. William Nash, Merle Potter (2010), “Schaum's Outline of Strength of Materials, Fifth Edition”, McGraw Hill Professional 4. Arthur P. Boresi and Richard J. Schmidt (2009), “Advanced Mechanics of Materials”, Wiley India Pvt. Ltd.

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge of the basic concept and applications of FEM 2. To impart knowledge of analysis of one- and two-dimensional problems 3. Apply the concepts of FEM to analysis for structures

outcomes.text: Describe the basic concept and applications of FEM
Analyse one- and two-dimensional problems by FEM
Analyse the beam, frame and truss elements by FEM

units.title: Overview of Finite element analysis
units.text: Overview of Finite element analysis: Basic concepts, Types of governing equations, numerical modelling, General applications of FEM, General description and comparison with other analysis methods, brief history of FEM, Merits and demerits of FEM

units.title: Different approaches in FEM
units.text: Different approaches in FEM: Direct approach, variational, energy and Weighted Residual approach, Iso-parametric elements, Eigen values

units.title: One dimensional finite element analysis
units.text: One dimensional finite element analysis: One dimensional finite element analysis: 1D torsion of a circular shaft, 1D steady state heat conduction, 1D flow through porous media, 1D ideal flow through pipes, Linear spring, Flow network analysis, Electrical network analysis

units.title: Application to solid mechanics problems
units.text: Application to solid mechanics problems: Analysis of beam element, frames and trusses (based on minimum potential energy approach)

units.title: Two-dimensional analysis
units.text: Two-dimensional analysis: Galerkin’s method for time dependent and time independent approach for two dimensional equations (Laplace, parabolic equations)

text_books: 1. Desai Y.M., Eldho T.I., Shah A.H. (2011), “Finite Element Method with Applications in Engineering”, Pearson. 2. Tirupathi R. Chandrupatla, Ashok D. Belegundu (2014), “Introduction to Finite Elements in Engineering”, Pearson Education Ltd.
reference_books: 1. Reddy J.N. (2005), “An introduction to the Finite Element Method”, Tata McGraw Hill. 2. Rao S.S. (2010), “The Finite Element Method in Engineering”, Elsevier. 3. O.C. Zienkiewicz & R. L. Taylor (2003), “The Finite Element Method: Its Basis and Fundamentals”, Elsevier Butterworth- heinemann (Classic Book)

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge of various characteristics of industrial wastewater on basis of type of industry 2. To provide ability to analyse Quality and calculate Quantity of Industrial Wastewater 3. To understand and apply knowledge of wastewater treatment process for specific characteristics of industrial Wastewater

outcomes.text: Differentiate various characteristics of industrial wastewater on basis of type of industry
Evaluate Quality and Quantity of Industrial Wastewater
Recommend wastewater treatment process for specific characteristics of industrial Wastewater

units.title: Necessity for Industrial Waste Treatment
units.text: Necessity for Industrial Waste Treatment: Introduction to Industrial Standards for disposal of treated industrial wastewaters into water bodies, municipal sewer and land, Standards for Disposal of industrial solid wastes and gaseous emission from various industries and treatment systems such as Incinerator etc.

units.title: Characteristics of Industrial Waste
units.text: Characteristics of Industrial Waste: Industrial waste generation (solid & liquid waste and gaseous emission) and their characteristics, variation in its Quality and quantity, Estimation of capacity of equalisation tank. Industry specific physico-chemical and biological treatment requirements, alternatives and their evaluation in respect of treatment.

units.title: Industrial Waste Treatment Typical Case Studies
units.text: Industrial Waste Treatment Typical Case Studies: Waste streams (solid, liquid and gaseous), their characteristics and manufacturing processes of integrated steel plant, sponge iron unit, alumina/aluminum manufacturing unit, copper smelter, fertilizer plant, thermal power plant, distillery/brewery, paper/pulp industry, tannery, textile unit and oil refinery

units.title: Industrial Waste Treatment Methods
units.text: Industrial Waste Treatment Methods: Methods of waste reduction such as process modification, volume and strength reduction, segregation, reuse, recycle, material conservation, good housekeeping. Neutralization, equalization, Engineering precipitation and solidification. Economic feasibility of joint treatment of raw industrial effluent with municipal sewage. Need assessment and design of common effluent treatment plant for industrial estates. Planning and management of industrial wastes (solid, liquid and gaseous) from small scale industries.

units.title: Industrial Waste Treatment for various Industries
units.text: Industrial Waste Treatment for various Industries: Selection of unit operations and their design for treatment and management of wastes (solid, liquid and gaseous) from integrated steel plant, sponge iron unit, alumina/aluminum manufacturing unit, copper smelter, fertilizer plant, thermal power plant, distillery/brewery, paper/pulp industry, tannery, textile unit and oil refinery.

text_books: 1. Patwardhan A. D.(2008), “Industrial Waste Water Treatment”, Prentice Hall of India
reference_books: 1. Soli J. Arceivala, Shyam R. Asolekar (2007), “Waste Water Treatment for Pollution Control and Reuse” Tata McGraw Hill Professional 2. Vivek V. Ranade, Vinay M Bhandari (2014) Industrial Treatment Recycling and Reuse, B&H Publishing 3. Nelson Leonard Nemerow (2006), Industrial Waste Treatment: Contemporary Practice and Vision for the Future, B&H Publishing 4. Mukesh Doble, Anil Kumar (2005), Biotreatment of Industrial Effluents, B&H Publishing

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge of Characteristics of water on basis of its occurrence 2. To knowledge of Suitable method of Water Modelling for improvement of Water Quality 3. To study Water Quality Management and its legal aspects

outcomes.text: Understand characteristics of water on basis of its occurrence
Recommend suitable method of Water Modelling for improvement of Water Quality
Elaborate Water Quality Management and its legal aspects

units.title: Occurrence of Water
units.text: Occurrence of Water: Land Processes Subsurface and Channel Processes- Precipitation – Rain gauge network, Abstractions, Infiltration, Evaporation, Transpiration, Process and models Unit Hydrograph & S curve hydrograph, Dimensionless unit hydrograph, GUIH, Watershed Model and Conceptual Models.

Occurrence and Movement of Ground water, Properties of aquifer, Groundwater flow equations, Dupuit For chheimer assumptions, Well hydraulics, Partial penetration of wells, Interference of wells, Collector wells and Infiltration galleries. Pumping tests, Analysis for unconfined and non leaky and leaky confined aquifer and water table aquifer, Locating hydro geologic boundaries, Well design criteria. Natural and Artificial Recharge of Ground water- Salt water intrusion, Application of Finite Difference in ground water.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Water Quality, Water quality characteristics, sampling and analysis, Analytical methods, Automated analysis and remote monitoring. Water quality monitoring: Water Pollution, Sources of Pollution, Nature of pollutants, Existing Approaches for Control/ - Abatement of Water Quality Degradation, Water Quality Monitoring in River Basins

units.title: Water quality modelling
units.text: Water quality modelling: Modelling and Monitoring, Evolution of Water Quality Models, Types of Water Quality Models, DO and BOD in streams, Transformation and transport processes, Oxygen transfer, Turbulent mixing, Non-Point Source Pollution, Modelling Approaches For Modelling Non-point Sources.

units.title: Water Quality Management
units.text: Water Quality Management: Water quality objectives and standards, Water quality control models, Flow augmentation, River and Lake water quality Models, Groundwater quality Models, Wastewater Transport Systems. River Quality modelling, Streeter Phelps model, Fate and transport of pollutants in rivers and streams, Pulse and step inputs, transport in estuaries, Fate and transport of pollutants in lakes, step and pulse input models, Fate and transport of pollutants in subsurface systems, Step and pulse input models. Legal Aspects of Water quality: Water pollution control acts and Legislation.

text_books: 1. Steven C. Chapra (2008), “Surface Water-Quality Modelling”, Waveland Press 2. Boyd C E (2015), Water Quality An Introduction 2nd Edition, SPRINGER 3. Claude E.(2014), “Boyd Water Quality: An Introduction Springer Science & Business Media”
reference_books: 1. Howard S. Peavy, Donald R. Rowe, George Tchobanoglous Environmental Engineering (Indian Edition) McGraw-Hill, 2017 2. Tebutt, T.H.Y., (1998), “Principles of Water Quality Control”, Pergamon Press, Oxford (Classic Book) 3. Gerard Kiely, (1998), “Environmental Engineering”, McGraw Hill Publications (Classic Book) 4. Viessman, W. Jr and M.J. Hammer (1985), “Water Supply and Pollution Control”, Harper and Row Publishers, New York. (Classic Book) 5. Jerald L. Schnoor, (1996), “Environmental Modeling – Fate and Transport of Pollutants in Water, Air and Soil”, John Wiley & Sons Inc., New York. (Classic Book)

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge of structural and functional components of Ecosystem 2. To provide ability to apply knowledge of Eco technology and its relevance 3. To provide understanding to classify various Ecological Processes and its significance

outcomes.text: Understand structural and functional components of Ecosystem
Elaborate application of Eco technology and its relevance
Discuss the various Ecological Processes

units.title: Introduction to Ecology and Ecological Engineering
units.text: Introduction to Ecology and Ecological Engineering: Aim – scope and applications of Ecology, Ecological Engineering and Ecotechnology and their relevance to human civilization Ecosystem – Concept of an ecosystem, structure and function of an ecosystem, Producers, Consumers, and decomposers, Energy Flow in the ecosystem, ecological Succession, Food Chains, Food Webs and ecological pyramids, Material Cycling, Productivity, Balance of natureand ecosystem, Energy Flow in Ecosystem -Lotic and Lentic Systems, Eutrophication of Lakes. Population Growth Forms, Carrying Capacity, quantitative Ecology, Concept of Ecosystem Types of Ecosystems Development and evolution of ecosystems – Principles and concepts pertaining to communities in ecosystem – Energy flow and material cycling in ecosystems – Productivity in ecosystems.

units.title: Systems Approach in Ecological Engineering
units.text: Systems Approach in Ecological Engineering: Classification of ecotechnology – Principles and components of Systems and Modeling – Structural and functional interactions in environmental systems – Human modifications of environmental systems. Ecotechnology for Waste Treatment: Principles and operation of soil infiltration systems – wetlands and ponds – source separation systems – aquacultural systems – detritus based treatment for solid wastes – Applications of ecological engineering marine systems.

units.title: Ecological Engineering Processes
units.text: Ecological Engineering Processes: Self-organizing processes – Multiple seeded microcosms – Interface coupling in ecological systems. Concepts of energy – Adapting ecological engineering systems to potentially catastrophic events – Agro ecosystems – Determination of sustainable loading of ecosystems.

units.title: Hydroponics
units.text: Hydroponics: Definition, History of Hydroponics, Advantages and Disadvantages, Growing substrates, Types of syatems, Nutrients Solutions, Additional Improvements Aquaponics - Definition, History of Aquaponics, Aquaponics Cycle, Types of Aquaponics, Aquaponics Stages, Sustainability approach, Advantages and Disadvantages

units.title: Case Studies
units.text: Case Studies: Case studies of integrated ecological engineering systems.

text_books: 1. DR. ing.Hein van Bohemen (2005), “Ecological Engineering” Boxtel : Aeneas Technical Publishers. 2. Eugene P Odum (2005), "Fundamentals of Ecology", Cenage Learning India Private Limited
reference_books: 1. Kangas, P.C and Kangas, P.,(2003), "Ecological Engineering: Principles and Practice", Lewis Publishers, New York. 2. Etnier, C. and Guterstam, B., (1996), "Ecological Engineering for Wastewater Treatment",Lewis Publishers, New York. (Classic Book)

program: MBA Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: 1. To identify the different properties and functions of subgrade 2. To evaluate the grading requirements, soil survey procedure and ground improvement techniques 3. To analyse stresses in soil

outcomes.text: Identify the different properties and functions of subgrade
Evaluate the grading requirements, soil survey procedure and ground improvement techniques
Analyse stresses in soil

units.title: Subgrade
units.text: Subgrade: Functions, Importance of subgrade soil properties on pavement performance, subgrade soil classification for highway engineering purpose soils as per PRA system, revised PRA system, Burmister system, Compaction system.

units.title: Grading requirements for aggregate, selection of bases and subbase material
units.text: Grading requirements for aggregate, selection of bases and subbase material (including stabilized materials), selection of different grade of bitumen, types of bituminous surfaces, skid qualities, bituminous mix design, Marshall stability test, design aspect of paving concrete. Experimental characteristics of road aggregate.

units.title: Soil Survey
units.text: Soil Survey: Soil Survey Procedure for Highway and Ground Water Investigation. Identification and Significance of soil Characteristics, effect of water in soil Swelling/shrinkage, cohesion, plasticity in soil. Soil Moisture movement- ground water, gravitational water, held water, soil suction.

units.title: Storm water Drainage
units.text: Storm water Drainage: General principles, subsoil Drainage. Frost action soil: Frost susceptible soils, depth of frost penetration, loss of strength during frost melting. Compaction of soils, field and laboratory method of soil compaction, equipments used in field compaction. Design of surface and subsurface drainage system, pumping system, water body, holding ponds.

units.title: Stress in soil
units.text: Stress in soil: Theories of elastic and plastic behaviour of soils, Methods of reducing settlement, estimation of rate of settlement due to consolidation in foundation of road embankment., static and cyclic triaxial test on subgrade soils, resilient deformation, resilient strain, resilient modulus. CBR test, effect of lateral confinement on CBR and E – value of Subgrade soil. Static and cyclic plate load test, estimation of modulus of subgrade reaction, correction for plate size, correction for worst moisture content.

units.title: Ground Improvement Technique
units.text: Ground Improvement Technique: Different method of soil stabilization, use of geo-textile, geogrid and fibres in highway subgrade. Vertical sand drain: design criteria, construction and uses

outcomes.text: identify the problems in soft soils
Implement the modification methods such as compaction, stone column, vibro-flotation etc.
Apply vertical drain and grouting techniques
Application of design principles of geosynthetics, anchors and soil nailing

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Needs, different types of problematic soil distribution in India, role of ground improvement in foundation engineering. Methods of ground improvement - selection of ground improvement techniques

units.title: Mechanical modifications
units.text: Mechanical modifications: Introduction - terminology – compaction, stabilisation, consolidation. Method of compaction - Shallow surface compaction, Deep compaction Techniques – Pre compression, explosion, heavy temping, vibration, vibro-compaction, Vibro- replacement, compaction grouting. Calculation MDD, OMC and percentage compaction in the field Stone Columns - design criteria, failure mechanism, principles of soil compactions, properties of compacted soil, Compaction control tests, Dynamic Compaction, Liquefaction of compaction and its remedial measures, Numerical problems.

units.title: Preloading and the use of vertical drains
units.text: Preloading and the use of vertical drains: Preloading without vertical drains - needs for preloading, numerical problems. Preloading with vertical drains - numerical problems, assessment of ground conditions, introduction to Prefabricated vertical drains (PVD) with vacuum consolidation. Instrumentation – Piezometers, settlement plates, gauges and levelling point, use of inclinometers.

units.title: Modification by grouting
units.text: Modification by grouting: Introduction - categories of grouting, grout materials. Grout with cement - Portland cement, Micro-fine cement. Jet grouting – procedure, Compaction grouting, Chemical grouts –properties. Grouting Theory - basic consideration, stability of interface, flow through soil voids, effect of pumping rate on grout flow, effect of pumping pressure on grout flow, fracturing. Grouting technology, field equipment, application of grouting - Case study

units.title: Geosynthetics
units.text: Geosynthetics: Introductions- types of geosynthetics, function of geosynthetics. Application areas - Retaining walls, Embankments, Shallow foundations, Roads, Railways, Slopes, Dams, Tunnels. Design of geotextiles – properties, frictional behaviour Design of geotextile walls, Design of geotextile stabilized embankments; Geotextile stabilized Foundation soil design, Design of geotextile filtration, numerical problems.

units.title: In-situ ground reinforcement
units.text: In-situ ground reinforcement: Introduction - ground anchors, components of anchors, transfer of load in anchors, mechanism of bond between grout and borehole wall. Rock Anchors - case study, anchor in granular soils, anchor in cohesive soils. Soil nailing - case study.

program: B Tech/MBA Tech/BTI Information Technology

Identify how microprocessor, memory, peripheral components and buses interact in an embedded system design
Develop solutions for various real time applications using Embedded programming

outcomes.text: Demonstrate a working knowledge of data visualization
Create visualization charts appropriate for the underlying data
Apply modern statistical learning techniques on data visualizations
Design and implement interactive links between various objects in a data visualization report

program: B Tech/MBA Tech Information Technology, B Tech (AI and ML)
objectives: This course gives an introduction to Management Information Systems. It aims at explaining how Information Technology / Information Systems help organizations to achieve competitive advantage in the market.

outcomes.text: Explain the role of Information System in business environment
Analyze existing business applications in use and design a business application for a given scenario
Describe the implications of social media on organizations
Identify the challenges in the management of global information systems and assess the security and ethical concerns

units.title: Foundations of Information systems and Management
units.text: Foundations of Information systems and Management Why Information systems? Fundamental behavioural, technical, business and managerial concepts about the components and roles of information systems, Types of information systems: Operations support systems and Management support systems, Definition, role and impact of MIS, MIS as a support to the management and a tool for management process.

units.title: Strategic Use of Information Systems
units.text: Strategic Use of Information Systems Fundamentals of strategic advantage –What is strategic advantage, brief overview of business strategy, organizational strategy and information systems strategy. Porter’s five forces model.

units.title: Using Information Technology for strategic advantage
units.text: Using Information Technology for strategic advantage Major concepts, developments, and management issues in information technology (hardware, software, networks, data resource management, and other information processing technologies such as the Internet).

units.title: Business Applications-I
units.text: Business Applications-I Major uses of information systems for the operations, management, and competitive advantage of an e-business enterprise. Electronic Business Systems – Enterprise business systems, Functional business systems Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems – What is ERP? Benefits, challenges and trends in ERP Customer relationship Management (CRM) systems - What is CRM? Three phases of CRM, Benefits, challenges and trends in CRM Supply Chain Management (SCM) systems - What is SCM? Role of SCM, Benefits, challenges and trends in SCM.

units.title: Business Applications-II
units.text: Business Applications-II Decision support systems (DSS) – Introduction, DSS components, Decision and management, information quality, Reporting, Online analytical processing, Using DSS – what-if analysis, sensitivity analysis, Goal-seeking analysis, Optimization analysis, Data mining for decision support. Knowledge Management and Business Analytics - Data, information and Knowledge, What is knowledge Management, Managing Knowledge to Business Intelligence, Why manage knowledge, Knowledge management processes, Components of business analytics.

units.title: Social Media and Organizations

Explore semantic web to create ontologies and to query RDFs

program: B Tech/MBA Tech / BTI Information Technology
objectives: The objective of this course is to familiarize students with the working of internetworks. This course focus on top-down approach, the Internet and a modern treatment of computer networking, its attention to both principles and practice, and its accessible style and approach toward learning about computer networking.

outcomes.text: Describe medium access layer protocols
Design IP addressing scheme, analyze packet forwarding, and compare different routing protocols
Compare and analyze transport protocols and other key protocols essential for networking
Explain various multimedia protocols, internet security concepts and future networks

units.title: Internet protocol

units.title: Network Layer

units.title: Transport layer
units.text: Transport layer Transmission Control Protocol - Reno, SCTP, I-TCP, Snoop TCP and Mobile TCP.

units.title: Multimedia in the internet
units.text: Multimedia in the internet SIP, QoS (flow classes, flow control to improve QoS - FIFO, Priority and WFQ).

units.title: Network security
units.text: Network security Introduction to Internet security - application layer security, transport layer security (SSL and TLS), IPSec, VPN, Firewall, WPA2, WPA3.
Introduction to Internet of Things and applications, software defined networks and 5G.

To provide an understanding of measurement of cost and tracing the costs to products and customers. 4. To explain the role of relevant costs in decision making and developing better strategies. 5. To discuss contemporary issues in Cost and Management Accounting and their practical applications.

outcomes.text: Apply concepts of accounting
Applying techniques for analysis.
Use budgetary control techniques for managerial decision making
Apply Activity Based Costing to generate reliable and accurate product cost data.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)
objectives: This course provides basic orientation towards macroeconomic principles and help them understand the functions of economy at Macro level:  To combine elements of basic variables of macroeconomics.  To familiarize with importance of macroeconomic approach in managing economy.  To understand the application of macroeconomic theories at aggregate level.  To emphasize the role of macroeconomic policies and analyze their implication for economy along with international linkages.

outcomes.text: Learn various macroeconomic variables, circular flow of income and their linkages to macro economy.
Analyze aggregates of macroeconomics and understand goods market and money market, Indian Financial System, Business fluctuations and Stabilization Policies.
Orient oneself towards higher levels of learning related to economic planning, international trade, foreign exchange market and international organizations at macro level.

units.title: Introduction to Macroeconomics
units.text: Introduction to Macroeconomics: Meaning, Nature & Scope and importance of Macroeconomics, Interdependence between Microeconomics & Macroeconomics, macroeconomics goals, major issues and concerns of macroeconomics.

units.title: Structure of Macroeconomics
units.text: Structure of Macroeconomics: Subject matter of Macroeconomics, Structure of Macro Economy, Different sectors of the economy, Circular Flow of Income & Product, Leakages & Injections in the Circular Flow.

units.title: Keynes’s Theory of Employment
units.text: Keynes’s Theory of Employment: Principles of effective demand, aggregate demand function, aggregate supply function, determination of equilibrium level of employment-Effective demand.

units.title: Macroeconomic Aggregates
units.text: Macroeconomic Aggregates: Aggregate Consumption- component of consumption, determinant of consumption, consumption function, Saving function, Capital formation- component of investment, determinant of investment, investment function and investment multiplier.

units.title: Goods Market and Money Market (IS-LM Curves Model)
units.text: Goods Market and Money Market (IS-LM Curves Model): Introduction to Goods Market and Money Market and links between them, Goods Market equilibrium- derivation of IS Curve, Money market equilibrium- derivation of LM Curve, Equilibrium of goods Market and Money Market, critique of IS-LM Curves model.

units.title: Inflation – Unemployment Trade-off (Philips Curve)
units.text: Inflation – Unemployment Trade-off (Philips Curve): Types and causes of unemployment, Unemployment situation in India, policy measures to solve unemployment problem in India, Inflation- meaning and types, effects of Inflation on distribution of income & wealth and on output & growth, methods to control Inflation, Unemployment and Inflation- The Philips Curve, causes of shift in Philips Curve, relation between short-run Philips Curve and long-run Philips Curve.

units.title: Indian Financial System
units.text: Indian Financial System: Credit and Commercial Banking- meaning and functions, purposes, roles of commercial banks in economic development, credit creation and limitations on the credit creating power of the banks, Central Banking- principles and functions of commercial banking, methods of credit control by central bank for economic prosperity.

units.title: Analysis of Business Cycle
units.text: Analysis of Business Cycle: Phases of Business Cycle, Features of Business Cycle, Theories of Business Cycle, Business Cycle and Indian Economy in post-liberalization era.

units.title: Economic Stabilization Policy- Monetary Policy
units.text: Economic Stabilization Policy- Monetary Policy: Tools of Monetary policy, expansionary monetary policy to cure recession, monetary policy to control inflation, liquidity trap and effectiveness of monetary policy, tight monetary policy, RBI’s Monetary policy in India and its critical evaluation.

units.title: Economic Stabilization Policy- Fiscal policy I
units.text: Economic Stabilization Policy- Fiscal policy I: Tools of Fiscal policy- Public Finance, Public Expenditure, Taxation.

units.title: Economic Stabilization Policy- Fiscal policy II
units.text: Economic Stabilization Policy- Fiscal policy II: Introduction and importance of Budget in Economy, Indian Budgeting System, Budget Deficit and Government Borrowing, Crowding-out effect and effectiveness of Fiscal Policy.

units.title: Economic Planning and Policy
units.text: Economic Planning and Policy: Rational, Features and Objectives of Economic Planning, Strategies of India’s Developmental Plans, Assessment of India’s planning, Export-Import Policy, Evaluation of latest Foreign Trade Policy of India.

units.title: International Trade, Comparative Advantage, and Protectionism
units.text: International Trade, Comparative Advantage, and Protectionism: International Trade, Reasons for International Trade, Absolute Cost Theory, Comparative Cost Theory, Free Trade versus Protection, Cases for Protection, Foreign Capital and Foreign Aid.

units.title: Foreign Exchange and Foreign Exchange Market
units.text: Foreign Exchange and Foreign Exchange Market: India’s Exchange Rate Policy, Foreign Exchange Reserve, Exchange Rate Regimes, Exchange Rate Management in India, Capital Account Convertibility.

units.title: International Organizations
units.text: International Organizations: World Bank, International Monetary Fund and World Trade Organization- History, Importance and Functions, International Organizations and Indian Economy.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
objectives: To provide conceptual understanding of Cost and Management Accounting principles and practices relevant for business analysis and decision making. To develop the ability to understand, analyze and use cost information in day-to-day business functioning. To provide an understanding of measurement of cost and tracing the costs to products and customers. To explain the role of relevant costs in decision making and developing better strategies. To discuss contemporary issues in Cost and Management Accounting and their practical applications.

outcomes.text: Apply concepts of accounting
Applying techniques for analysis
Use budgetary control techniques for managerial decision making
Apply Activity Based Costing to generate reliable and accurate product cost data

Variance analysis  Direct labour variances  Cost Variance  Rate Variance  Efficiency Variance
Budgetary Control  Flexible Budget  Cash Budget

Activity Based Costing, Lean Operations, and the Costs of Quality  Under costing and Over costing-  Traditional vs Activity-based costing-  Evaluation of costs and benefits of implementing ABC systems  Application of Activity based costing in decision making
Time Value of Money  Concept of Time Value of Money  Present Value (PV) and Future Value (FV)  PV and FV of Annuity  Difference between Annuity and Annuity Due

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
objectives: This course provides basic orientation towards macroeconomic principles and help them understand the functions of economy at Macro level. To combine elements of basic variables of macroeconomics. To familiarize with importance of macroeconomic approach in managing economy. To understand the application of macroeconomic theories at aggregate level. To emphasize the role of macroeconomic policies and analyse their implication for economy along with international linkages.

outcomes.text: Learn various macroeconomic variables, circular flow of income and their linkages to macro economy
Analyze aggregates of macroeconomics and understand goods market and money market, Indian Financial System, Business fluctuations and Stabilization Policies
Orient oneself towards higher levels of learning related to economic planning, international trade, foreign exchange market and international organizations at macro level

units.title: Introduction to Macroeconomics
units.text: Introduction to Macroeconomics Meaning, Nature & Scope and importance of Macroeconomics, Interdependence between Microeconomics & Macroeconomics, macroeconomics goals, major issues and concerns of macroeconomics.

units.title: Structure of Macroeconomics
units.text: Structure of Macroeconomics Subject matter of Macroeconomics, Structure of Macro Economy, Different sectors of the economy, Circular Flow of Income & Product, Leakages & Injections in the Circular Flow.

units.title: Keynes’s Theory of Employment
units.text: Keynes’s Theory of Employment Principles of effective demand, aggregate demand function, aggregate supply function, determination of equilibrium level of employment- Effective demand.

units.title: Macroeconomic Aggregates
units.text: Macroeconomic Aggregates Aggregate Consumption- component of consumption, determinant of consumption, consumption function, Saving function, Capital formation- component of investment, determinant of investment, investment function and investment multiplier.

units.title: Goods Market and Money Market (IS-LM Curves Model)
units.text: Goods Market and Money Market (IS-LM Curves Model) Introduction to Goods Market and Money Market and links between them, Goods Market equilibrium- derivation of IS Curve, Money market equilibrium- derivation of LM Curve, Equilibrium of goods Market and Money Market, critique of IS-LM Curves model.

units.title: Inflation – Unemployment Trade-off (Philips Curve)
units.text: Inflation – Unemployment Trade-off (Philips Curve) Types and causes of unemployment, Unemployment situation in India, policy measures to solve unemployment problem in India, Inflation- meaning and types, effects of Inflation on distribution of income & wealth and on output & growth, methods to control Inflation, Unemployment and Inflation- The Philips Curve, causes of shift in Philips Curve, relation between short-run Philips Curve and long-run Philips Curve.

units.title: Indian Financial System
units.text: Indian Financial System Credit and Commercial Banking- meaning and functions, purposes, roles of commercial banks in economic development, credit creation and limitations on the credit creating power of the banks, Central Banking- principles and functions of commercial banking, methods of credit control by central bank for economic prosperity.

units.title: Analysis of Business Cycle
units.text: Analysis of Business Cycle Phases of Business Cycle, Features of Business Cycle, Theories of Business Cycle, Business Cycle and Indian Economy in post- liberalization era.

units.title: Economic Stabilization Policy- Monetary Policy
units.text: Economic Stabilization Policy- Monetary Policy Tools of Monetary policy, expansionary monetary policy to cure recession, monetary policy to control inflation, liquidity trap and effectiveness of monetary policy, tight monetary policy, RBI’s Monetary policy in India and its critical evaluation.

units.title: Economic Stabilization Policy- Fiscal policy I
units.text: Economic Stabilization Policy- Fiscal policy I Tools of Fiscal policy- Public Finance, Public Expenditure, Taxation.

units.text: Economic Stabilization Policy- Fiscal policy II Introduction and importance of Budget in Economy, Indian Budgeting System, Budget Deficit and Government Borrowing, Crowding-out effect and effectiveness of Fiscal Policy.

units.title: Economic Planning and Policy
units.text: Economic Planning and Policy Rational, Features and Objectives of Economic Planning, Strategies of India’s Developmental Plans, Assessment of India’s planning, Export- Import Policy, Evaluation of latest Foreign Trade Policy of India.

units.text: International Trade, Comparative Advantage, and Protectionism International Trade, Reasons for International Trade, Absolute Cost Theory, Comparative Cost Theory, Free Trade versus Protection, Cases for Protection, Foreign Capital and Foreign Aid.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
objectives: This course provides basic orientation towards macroeconomic principles and help them understand the functions of economy at Macro level. To combine elements of basic variables of macroeconomics. To familiarize with importance of macroeconomic approach in managing economy. To understand the application of macroeconomic theories at aggregate level. To emphasize the role of macroeconomic policies and analyse their implication for economy along with international linkages.

outcomes.text: Learn various macroeconomic variables, circular flow of income and their linkages to macro economy
Analyze aggregates of macroeconomics and understand goods market and money market, Indian Financial System, Business fluctuations and Stabilization Policies
Orient oneself towards higher levels of learning related to economic planning, international trade, foreign exchange market and international organizations at macro level

objectives: The objectives of offering this course are to provide a brief overview of Boolean Algebra, Combinational Logic, and Sequential Logic; to understanding the fundamental structure and functions of a computer, including the arithmetic and logic units, as well as the implementation of fixed-point and floating-point arithmetic and finally to learn the different ways of communication with I/O devices.

program: B Tech (Computer Engineering, CSBS, CSEDS- 311(VT)) MBA Tech (Computer Engineering)
objectives: The course aims to introduce and explore a chosen problem, providing students with the opportunity to engage with a variety of real-world challenges presented by different agencies. Students come onboard at different stages of project completion. The course seeks to guide students in selecting a project that aligns with their interests, expertise, and career goals. Through this approach, the course integrates elements of Design Thinking and Research, to enhance practical learning and problem-solving skills.

outcomes.text: Identify and explain real-world challenges in their context, relevance, and impact.
Collaborate effectively within diverse teams to solve complex design problems
Utilize Design Thinking principles to develop and iteratively refine practical solutions for the selected problem.
Design and prototype innovative solutions that integrate research insights and feasibility analysis.
Demonstrate effective oral and written communication skills relevant to the problem.

units.title: Introduction and Team Formation
units.text: Introduction and Team Formation: Familiarize with real-world problems and project options and team formation based on interests and skills. Problem Analysis: Understand the problem context and requirements and conduct literature review relevant to the problem objectives. Design Thinking and Concept Development: Develop innovative solutions. Apply Design Thinking phases and refine concepts based on feedback. Project Management and Documentation: Ensure organized execution. Assign roles, manage tasks, and maintain design documents. Communication and Review: Present and refine project outcomes. Prepare presentations, conduct reviews, and incorporate feedback. Reflection and Improvement: Enhance skills and identify next steps. Reflect on lessons learned and document final outcomes.

lab_work: The Laboratory work comprises various activities performed by the project teams for formulation, solution implementation and modification. Each team needs to submit the following documents: • Problem Statement Document • Project Development Report • Mid Semester Project Report • Final Report

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)
objectives: This course seeks to equip students from all backgrounds with a basic understanding of the international business environment and the fundamentals of international business strategy. In addition, this course aims to develop the following skills in students:  Critical thinking  Collaboration and teamwork  Research and writing skills

outcomes.text: Explain how differences between countries create additional challenges for firms doing business internationally
Explain how firms can create value by doing business internationally
Identify key decisions related to foreign market selection, market entry modes, and international strategy that firms need to make when going international
Apply theoretical frameworks to make informed recommendations for such firms
Describe how foreign exchange markets work; derive business/economic implications
Evaluate arguments for and against government restrictions on trade and investment; derive business/economic implications
Identify ethical challenges related to international business
Explain long-run trends and development in the international business environment; derive business/economic implications.

units.title: The environment of international business
units.text: The environment of international business: Examine how countries differ in terms of their economic, political, and social characteristics – and how this matters for international business. The basics of foreign exchange markets and how they affect international business.

The globalization of business, Economic development and emerging markets, Emerging markets: Business implications, Foreign market analysis: The PEST framework, Political risk and corruption, Culture and cultural differences, Foreign exchange rates

units.title: International business strategy
units.text: International business strategy: why companies do business internationally and how this can create value. Exploring the different options available to firms for entering foreign markets and discuss the main challenges and decisions firms face when going international. How these general principles apply to companies with ‘digital’ business models, such as Netflix, Facebook, OLA, UBER, FLIPKART etc.

units.title: Why do firms expand internationally?, Foreign direct investment
units.text: Why do firms expand internationally?, Foreign direct investment (FDI), Local adaptation vs global integration, International business in the digital age, The globalization of research & development (R&D)

Current issues in international business including the role of international trade policy (e.g. the “trade war” between the US and China), the role of technology, as well as ethical challenges associated with international business.

units.title: Theories of international trade, Trade barriers and “trade wars”
units.text: Theories of international trade, Trade barriers and “trade wars”: Impact on IB, Trade agreements and international institutions, The “dark side” of globalization? Social, environmental and other concerns, Ethics in IB, The future of IB

outcomes.text: Explain the foundational knowledge of the subject using chemistry principles
Identify newer chemical materials for better product designing
Analyze the impact of science and its progress on society and provide solution for cleaner environment
Evaluate the various aspects of chemistry to convert into useful applications.

units.title: Atomic structure and Periodic properties of elements
units.text: Atomic structure and Periodic properties of elements: Study of atom structure with reference to Bohr’s model, wave particle duality, Schrodinger wave equation. Concept of valency and electronic configuration. Explanation of Aufbau principle, Hund’s rule and Pauli’s Exclusion Principle that helps in writing electronic configuration. Introduction to Modern periodic table, Nomenclature of s, p, d, f group elements. Trends in physical properties: effective nuclear charge, atomic radii, ionization energy, electron affinity, electronegativity. Concept of semiconductors and metalloids. Concept of acids and bases.

units.title: Chemical bonding
units.text: Chemical bonding: Intermolecular forces: Ionic, covalent, co-ordinate bonds and types of intramolecular interactions (with one example for each type). Introduction to co-ordination chemistry and Co-ordination number, magnetism of the co-ordinate complexes.

units.title: Electrochemistry
units.text: Electrochemistry: Concept of electrochemical cell & electrolytic cell. Cell potential, EMF of Cell, Relation of free energy with EMF of cell, Faraday’s law, Derivation of Nernst equation, Applicability of Nernst equation

units.title: Important Engineering Materials
units.text: Important Engineering Materials: Nanomaterials: Structure, properties, applications of CNTs, Fullerenes, Graphite. Liquid Crystals: Definition, classification, properties with applications. Polymers: Introduction to polymers and polymerization mechanisms, Types of polymers, Specialty polymers like Conducting polymers, Self- healing polymers with applications.

units.title: Spectroscopic techniques and Applications
units.text: Spectroscopic techniques and Applications: General idea on Electromagnetic radiation, Basic Principle of Spectroscopy, UV-Visible Spectroscopy & applications, IR Spectroscopy & applications, Nuclear magnetic resonance & applications. MRI applications in medicine.

units.title: Environmental Chemistry
units.text: Environmental Chemistry: E-waste management: Definition, classification and management of e- waste in India with reference to Environment (Protection) Act. Solutions and Stoichiometry: Types of solutions and its characteristics, properties of aqueous solutions, different units for expressing concentration of solutions (ppm, ppb, normality, molarity, molality, mole fraction of solute, mass fraction of solute and solvent), empirical and molecular formula from elemental composition, numerical based on empirical formula, normality, molarity, molality molarity. Organic Reactions: Basic organic reactions like- addition reactions, elimination reactions, substitution reactions, pericyclic reactions, rearrangement reactions, photochemical reactions and redox reactions. Specific Reactions of functional groups containing oxygen (-COOH, - OH, -CHO, -C=O); Nucleophilic substitution reaction, Elimination reaction. Organic Name Reactions E.g. Aldol & related reactions.

program: MBA Tech/ B Tech
objectives: The course provide basic orientation towards microeconomic principles and help them understand the functions of management. This course also aims to understand issues dealing with small-scale economic phenomena and concepts such as prices and output of firms, industries and resource owners along with examining market impact of technological change with regards to understand broader aspects of the economy and its environment.

outcomes.text: Illustrate basic concepts of economics (demand, supply, elasticity, scarcity) and explain behaviour on individual, households and firm and handle economic data and write economic report
Analyse and evaluate the impact of Economic Policies and its implication on the Business Environment

Demonstrate and determine the students towards basic management principles and act as foundation for higher levels of learning and to be able to handle basic functions of management (planning, organizing, coordination, and control).

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Definition of Economics, Problem of Scarcity of Economic Resources, Types of Economic Systems. Demand and Supply Analysis: Demand Curve and Supply Curve, Equilibrium of Demand and Supply, Shift in Demand and Supply. Application of Demand and Supply: Price Elasticity of Demand, Factors which influence Elasticity, Uses of Price Elasticity of Demand, Elasticity and Revenue.

units.title: Utility Analysis and Consumer Behaviour
units.text: Utility Analysis and Consumer Behaviour: Introduction to Cardinal and Ordinal Utility, Total Utility and Marginal Utility, Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility, Indifference Curve and Consumer’s equilibrium. New Economic Policy: Liberalization, Privatization and Globalization

units.title: Theory of Production
units.text: Theory of Production: Introduction and Meaning, Short-run and Long-run Production Function, Law of Diminishing Returns and Returns to Scale, Iso- quant Curve and Producer’s Equilibrium (Least Cost Combination). Analysis of Costs: Types of Costs and Cost Curves – Total Cost, Fixed Cost, Variable Cost, Marginal Cost, Relationship between Marginal Cost Curve and Average Cost Curve.

units.title: Market Structure /Industry Analysis Types of Competition
units.text: Market Structure /Industry Analysis Types of Competition: Monopoly, Oligopoly, Monopolistic Competition, Perfect and Imperfect Competition. Price and output determination in perfectly competitive market structure.

units.title: Introduction to Management
units.text: Introduction to Management: Management & its Nature, Management History and Management Thought-Contribution of F.W. Taylor, Henry Fayol, and Elton Mayo. Planning: Introduction and Importance, Steps in Planning, Why Plan Fails, Sound Planning. Decision Making: Managers as Decision Makers, types of Decisions, Strategic Management.

Organizing- Line and Staff Relationships, Centralization and Decentralization, Role of Delegation, Managing Human Resources, Managing Teams. Leading and Motivation: Basic Concepts and Practices –Maslow’s, Herzberg, McClelland‘s Theory of Achievement.

units.title: Controlling- Introduction to Controlling, Need and Importance, Inventory
units.text: Controlling- Introduction to Controlling, Need and Importance, Inventory Control, Quality Control. Orientation towards Finance, Marketing, Human Resources.

prerequisites: Digital Logic Design, Computer Organization and Architecture
objectives: The principal objective of this course is to provide a basic understanding of biological mechanisms of living organisms from the perspective of engineers. To encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools. To make them aware of the application of engineering principles in biology and engineering robust solutions inspired by biological examples.

outcomes.text: convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are diverse
identify and classify microorganisms while understanding molecular basis of DNA as a genetic material for information transfer
classify enzymes and distinguish between different mechanisms of enzyme action.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Convey that Biology is as important a scientific discipline as Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry Bring out the fundamental differences between science and engineering by drawing a comparison between eye and camera, Bird flying and aircraft. Mention the most exciting aspect of biology as an independent scientific discipline. Why we need to study biology? Discuss how biological observations of 18th Century that lead to major discoveries. Examples from -Brownian motion and the origin of thermodynamics by referring to the original observation of Robert Brown and Julius Mayor. These examples will highlight the fundamental importance of observations in any scientific inquiry.

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification Convey that classification per se is not what biology is all about. The underlying criterion, such as morphological, biochemical or ecological be highlighted. Hierarchy of life forms at phenomenological level. A common thread weaves this hierarchy Classification.Discuss classification based on (a) cellularity- Unicellular or multicellular (b) ultrastructure- prokaryotes or eucaryotes. (c) energy and Carbon utilization -Autotrophs, heterotrophs, lithotropes (d) Ammonia excretion - aminotelic, uricoteliec, ureotelic (e) Habitata- acquatic or terrestrial (e) Molecular taxonomy- three major kingdoms of life. A given organism can come under different category based on classification. Model organisms for the study of biology come from different groups. E.coli, S.cerevisiae, D. Melanogaster, C. elegance, A. Thaliana, M. musculus

units.title: Genetics
units.text: Genetics Convey that "Genetics is to biology what Newton's laws are to Physical Sciences" Mendel's laws, Concept of segregation and independent assortment. Concept of allele. Gene mapping, Gene interaction, Epistasis. Meiosis and Mitosis be taught as a part of genetics. Emphasis to be give not to the mechanics of cell division nor the phases but how genetic material passes from parent to offspring. Concepts of recessiveness and dominance. Concept of mapping of phenotype to genes. Discuss about the single gene disorders in humans. Discuss the concept of complementation using human genetics.

units.title: Biomolecules
units.text: Biomolecules Convey that all forms of life has the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are as diverse as one can imagine Molecules of life. In this context discuss monomeric units and polymeric structures. Discuss about sugars, starch and cellulose. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA. Two carbon units and lipids.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes Convey that without catalysis life would not have existed on earth Enzymology: How to monitor enzyme catalyzed reactions. How does an enzyme catalyze reactions. Enzyme classification. Mechanism of enzyme action. Discuss at least two examples. Enzyme kinetics and kinetic- parameters. Why should we know these parameters to understand biology? RNA catalysis.

units.title: Information Transfer
units.text: Information Transfer The molecular basis of coding and decoding genetic information is universal Molecular basis of information transfer. DNA as a genetic material. Hierarchy of DNA structure- from single stranded to double helix to nucleosomes. Concept of genetic code. Universality and degeneracy of genetic code. Define gene in terms of complementation and recombination.

units.title: Macromolecular analysis
units.text: Macromolecular analysis How to analyses biological processes at the reductionistic level Proteins- structure and function. Hierarch in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors and structural elements.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism The fundamental principles of energy transactions are the same in physical and biological world. Thermodynamics as applied to biological systems. Exothermic and endothermic versus endergonic and exergonic reactions. Concept of Keq and its relation to standard free energy. Spontaneity. ATP as an energy currency. This should include the breakdown of glucose to CO2 + H2O (Glycolysis and Krebs cycle) and synthesis of glucose from CO2 and H2O (Photosynthesis). Energy yielding and energy consuming reactions. Concept of Energy Charge.

units.title: Microbiology
units.text: Microbiology Concept of single celled organisms. Concept of species and strains. Identification and classification of microorganisms. Microscopy. Ecological aspects of single celled organisms. Sterilization and media compositions. Growth kinetics.

objectives: The course aims to introduce and explore a chosen problem, providing students with the opportunity to engage with a variety of real-world challenges presented by different agencies. Students come onboard at different stages of project completion. The course seeks to guide students in selecting a project that aligns with their interests, expertise, and career goals. Through this approach, the course integrates elements of Design Thinking and Research, to enhance practical learning and problem-solving skills.

outcomes.text: Identify and explain real-world challenges in their context, relevance, and impact.
Collaborate effectively within diverse teams to solve complex design problems
Utilize Design Thinking principles to develop and iteratively refine practical solutions for the selected problem.
Design and prototype innovative solutions that integrate research insights and feasibility analysis.
Demonstrate effective oral and written communication skills relevant to the problem.

units.title: Introduction and Team Formation
units.text: Introduction and Team Formation: Familiarize with real-world problems and project options and team formation based on interests and skills. Problem Analysis: Understand the problem context and requirements and conduct literature review relevant to the problem objectives. Design Thinking and Concept Development: Develop innovative solutions. Apply Design Thinking phases and refine concepts based on feedback. Project Management and Documentation: Ensure organized execution. Assign roles, manage tasks, and maintain design documents. Communication and Review: Present and refine project outcomes. Prepare presentations, conduct reviews, and incorporate feedback. Reflection and Improvement: Enhance skills and identify next steps. Reflect on lessons learned and document final outcomes.

lab_work: The Laboratory work comprises various activities performed by the project teams for formulation, solution implementation and modification. Each team needs to submit the following documents:  Problem Statement Document  Project Development Report  Mid Semester Project Report  Final Report
