program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To impart the knowledge of Engineering approach to software development and project management. To impart knowledge of Software Building Techniques. Make students understand the Importance of Software quality and reliability. To make students understand the importance of Analysis, design and construction (both structured and object oriented). To impart the knowledge of Software Testing.

outcomes.text: Understand the concepts of software engineering
Apply project management skills to manage the project
Design and Analyze the software to be built
Implement and test the software project.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Programming in the small vs. programming in the large; software project failures and importance of software quality and timely availability; engineering approach to software development; role of software engineering towards successful execution of large software projects; emergence of software engineering as a discipline.

units.title: Software Project Management
units.text: Software Project Management: Basic concepts of life cycle models, different models and milestones; software project planning – identification of activities and resources; concepts of feasibility study; techniques for estimation of schedule and effort; software cost estimation models and concepts of software engineering economics; techniques of software project control and reporting; introduction to measurement of software size; introduction to the concepts of risk and its mitigation; configuration management.

units.title: Software Quality and Reliability
units.text: Software Quality and Reliability: Internal and external qualities; process and product quality; principles to achieve software quality; introduction to different software quality models like McCall, Boehm, FURPS / FURPS+, Dromey, ISO – 9126; introduction to Capability Maturity Models (CMM and CMMI); introduction to software reliability, reliability models and estimation.

units.title: Software Requirements Analysis, Design and Construction
units.text: Software Requirements Analysis, Design and Construction: Introduction to Software Requirements Specifications (SRS) and requirement elicitation techniques; techniques for requirement modeling – decision tables, event tables, state transition tables, Petri nets; requirements documentation through use cases; introduction to UML, introduction to software metrics and metrics based control methods; measures of code and design quality.

units.title: Object Oriented Analysis, Design and Construction
units.text: Object Oriented Analysis, Design and Construction: Concepts -- the principles of abstraction, modularity, specification, encapsulation and information hiding; concepts of abstract data type; Class Responsibility Collaborator (CRC) model; quality of design; design measurements; concepts of design patterns; Refactoring; object oriented construction principles; object oriented metrics.

units.title: Software Testing
units.text: Software Testing: Introduction to faults and failures; basic testing concepts; concepts of verification and validation; black box and white box tests; white box test coverage – code coverage, condition coverage, branch coverage; basic concepts of black-box tests – equivalence classes, boundary value tests, usage of state tables; testing use cases; transaction based testing; testing for non-functional requirements – volume, performance and efficiency; concepts of inspection.

text_books: 1. Ian Sommerville, “Software Engineering”, 9th edition, Pearson, 2011.
reference_books: 1. Carlo Ghezzi, Jazayeri Mehdi, Mandrioli Dino, “Fundamentals of Software Engineering”, 2nd edition, Pearson, 2002 2. program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To impart the knowledge of Engineering approach to software development and project management. To impart knowledge of Software Building Techniques. Make students understand the Importance of Software quality and reliability. To make students understand the importance of Analysis, design and construction (both structured and object oriented). To impart the knowledge of Software Testing.

outcomes.text: Understand the concepts of software engineering
Apply project management skills to manage the project
Design and Analyze the software to be built
Implement and test the software project.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Programming in the small vs. programming in the large; software project failures and importance of software quality and timely availability; engineering approach to software development; role of software engineering towards successful execution of large software projects; emergence of software engineering as a discipline.

units.title: Software Project Management
units.text: Software Project Management: Basic concepts of life cycle models, different models and milestones; software project planning – identification of activities and resources; concepts of feasibility study; techniques for estimation of schedule and effort; software cost estimation models and concepts of software engineering economics; techniques of software project control and reporting; introduction to measurement of software size; introduction to the concepts of risk and its mitigation; configuration management.

units.title: Software Quality and Reliability
units.text: Software Quality and Reliability: Internal and external qualities; process and product quality; principles to achieve software quality; introduction to different software quality models like McCall, Boehm, FURPS / FURPS+, Dromey, ISO – 9126; introduction to Capability Maturity Models (CMM and CMMI); introduction to software reliability, reliability models and estimation.

units.title: Software Requirements Analysis, Design and Construction
units.text: Software Requirements Analysis, Design and Construction: Introduction to Software Requirements Specifications (SRS) and requirement elicitation techniques; techniques for requirement modeling – decision tables, event tables, state transition tables, Petri nets; requirements documentation through use cases; introduction to UML, introduction to software metrics and metrics based control methods; measures of code and design quality.

units.title: Object Oriented Analysis, Design and Construction
units.text: Object Oriented Analysis, Design and Construction: Concepts -- the principles of abstraction, modularity, specification, encapsulation and information hiding; concepts of abstract data type; Class Responsibility Collaborator (CRC) model; quality of design; design measurements; concepts of design patterns; Refactoring; object oriented construction principles; object oriented metrics.

units.title: Software Testing
units.text: Software Testing: Introduction to faults and failures; basic testing concepts; concepts of verification and validation; black box and white box tests; white box test coverage – code coverage, condition coverage, branch coverage; basic concepts of black-box tests – equivalence classes, boundary value tests, usage of state tables; testing use cases; transaction based testing; testing for non-functional requirements – volume, performance and efficiency; concepts of inspection.

program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: Introduction to subject as a logical, Quantitative approach in decision-making. To introduce and exercise a range of analytical modeling techniques useful in decision- making in the system design environment.

outcomes.text: Implement concepts of Linear Programming
Solve assignment and transportation problems
Implement Network analysis and Queuing theory
Demonstrate use of Inventory control and Simulation Methodology.

units.title: Introduction to OR
units.text: Introduction to OR: Origin of OR and its definition. Concept of optimizing performance measure, Types of OR problems, Deterministic vs. Stochastic optimization, Phases of OR problem approach – problem formulation, building mathematical model, deriving solutions, validating model, controlling and implementing solution.

units.title: Linear Programming
units.text: Linear Programming: Linear programming – Examples from industrial cases, formulation & definitions, Matrix form. Implicit assumptions of LPP. Some basic concepts and results of linear algebra – Vectors, Matrices, Linear Independence / Dependence of vectors, Rank, Basis, System of linear eqns., Hyperplane, Convex set, Convex polyhedron, Extreme points, Basic feasible solutions. Geometric method: 2-variable case, Special cases – infeasibility, unboundedness, redundancy & degeneracy, Sensitivity analysis. Simplex Algorithm – slack, surplus & artificial variables, computational details, big-M method, identification and resolution of special cases through simplex iterations. Duality – formulation, results, fundamental theorem of duality, dual-simplex and primal-dual algorithms.

units.title: Transportation and Assignment problems
units.text: Transportation and Assignment problems: TP - Examples, Definitions – decision variables, supply & demand constraints, formulation, Balanced & unbalanced situations, Solution methods – NWCR, minimum cost and VAM, test for optimality (MODI method), degeneracy and its resolution. AP - Examples, Definitions – decision variables, constraints, formulation, Balanced & unbalanced situations, Solution method – Hungarian, test for optimality (MODI method), degeneracy & its resolution.

units.title: PERT – CPM
units.text: PERT – CPM: Project definition, Project scheduling techniques – Gantt chart, PERT & CPM, Determination of critical paths, Estimation of Project time and its variance in PERT using statistical principles, Concept of project crashing/time-cost trade-off.

units.title: Inventory Control
units.text: Inventory Control: Functions of inventory and its disadvantages, ABC analysis, Concept of inventory costs, Basics of inventory policy (order, lead time, types), Fixed order-quantity models – EOQ, POQ & Quantity discount models. EOQ models for discrete units, sensitivity analysis and Robustness, Special cases of EOQ models for safety stock with known / unknown stock out situations, models under prescribed policy, Probabilistic situations.

units.title: Queuing Theory
units.text: Queuing Theory: Definitions – queue (waiting line), waiting costs, characteristics (arrival, queue, service discipline) of queuing system, queue types (channel vs. phase). Kendall’s notation, Little’s law, steady state behaviour, Poisson’s Process & queue, Models with examples - M/M/1 and its performance measures; M/M/m and its performance measures; brief description about some special models.

units.title: Simulation Methodology
units.text: Simulation Methodology: Definition and steps of simulation, random number, random number generator, Discrete Event System Simulation – clock, event list, Application in Scheduling, Queuing systems and Inventory systems.

Wagner, “Principles of OR with Application to Managerial Decisions” 1st Edition, Prentice Hall India Learning Pvt., 1980. 4. F.S. Hiller and G.J. Lieberman, “Introduction to Operations Research”, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017. 5. Thomas L. Saaty, “Elements of Queuing Theory”, 1st Edition, McGraw-Hill Inc., Us, 1961. 6. A. Prichard and R.H. Eagle, “Modern Inventory Management”, 1st Edition, Wiley, New York, 1965.

program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Objectives - To enable students to understand the basic concepts of an Operating system. To strengthen the understanding of various algorithms related to the process, memory, I/O and file management through implementation.
objectives: To enable students to understand the basic concepts of an Operating system. To strengthen the understanding of various algorithms related to the process, memory, I/O and file management through implementation.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental concepts of Operating system
Simulate process management strategies
Simulate memory, I/O and file management strategies.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Concept of Operating Systems (OS), Generations of OS, Types of OS, OS Services, Interrupt handling and System Calls, Basic architectural concepts of an OS, Concept of Virtual Machine, Resource Manager view, process view and hierarchical view of an OS.

units.title: Processes
units.text: Processes: Definition, Process Relationship, Different states of a Process, Process State transitions, Process Control Block (PCB), Context switching. Thread: Definition, Various states, Benefits of threads, Types of threads, Concept of multithreads.

units.title: Process Scheduling
units.text: Process Scheduling: Foundation and Scheduling objectives, Types of Schedulers, Scheduling criteria: CPU utilization, Throughput, Turnaround Time, Waiting Time, Response Time. Scheduling algorithms: Pre-emptive and non-pre-emptive, FCFS, SJF, RR; Multiprocessor scheduling: Real Time scheduling: RM and EDF.

units.title: Inter-process Communication
units.text: Inter-process Communication: Concurrent processes, precedence graphs, Critical Section, Race Conditions, Mutual Exclusion, Hardware Solution, Semaphores, Strict Alternation, Peterson’s Solution, The Producer / Consumer Problem, Event Counters, Monitors, Message Passing, Classical IPC Problems: Reader’s & Writer Problem, Dinning Philosopher Problem, Barber’s shop problem Deadlocks: Definition, Necessary and sufficient conditions for Deadlock, Deadlock Prevention, Deadlock Avoidance: Banker’s algorithm, Deadlock detection and Recovery.

units.title: Concurrent Programming
units.text: Concurrent Programming: Critical region, conditional critical region, monitors, concurrent languages, communicating sequential process (CSP); Deadlocks - prevention, avoidance, detection and recovery.

units.title: Memory Management
units.text: Memory Management: Basic concept, Logical and Physical address maps, Memory allocation: Contiguous Memory allocation – Fixed and variable partition– Internal and External fragmentation and Compaction. Virtual Memory: Basics of Virtual Memory – Hardware and control structures – Locality of reference, Page allocation, Partitioning, Paging, Page fault, Working Set, Segmentation, Demand paging, Page Replacement algorithms: Optimal, First in First Out (FIFO), Second Chance (SC), Not recently used (NRU) and Least Recently used (LRU).

units.title: I/O Hardware
units.text: I/O Hardware: I/O devices, Device controllers, Direct Memory Access, Principles of I/O. File Management: Concept of File, Access methods, File types, File operation, Directory structure, File System structure, Allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed), Free-space management (bit vector, linked list, grouping), directory implementation (linear list, hash table), efficiency and performance.

units.title: Disk Management
units.text: Disk Management: Disk structure, Disk scheduling - FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, Disk reliability, Disk formatting, Boot-block, Bad blocks.

units.title: Case study
units.text: Case study: Comparison of Windows and UNIX, UNIX OS file system, shell, filters, shell programming, programming with the standard I/O, UNIX system calls.

text_books: 1. Abraham Silberschatz, Peter Baer Galvin and Greg Gagne, “Operating System Concepts Essentials”, 2nd Edition, John Wiley & Sons, 2014.
reference_books: 1. William Stallings, “Operating Systems: Internals and Design Principles”, William Stallings, 9th Edition, Pearson, 2018. 2. Charles Patrick Crowley, “Operating System: A Design-oriented Approach”, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017. 3. Gary J. Nutt., “Operating Systems: A Modern Perspective”, 3rd Edition, Pearson, 2014. 4. Maurice J. Bach, “Design of the Unix Operating Systems”, 3rd Edition, Pearson Education India, 2015. 5. Daniel Pierre Bovet, Marco Cesati, “Understanding the Linux Kernel”, 3rd Edition, O'Reilly Media, 2002.

program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To understand the different issues involved in the design and implementation of a database system. To model, design and build a simple database system. To understand and use database query languages to access and manage a database. To understand query processing and optimization. To develop an understanding of essential DBMS concepts: Normalization, Transactions, concurrency Control, Storage strategies, database security and advance topics.

outcomes.text: Understand the terminology, features, types, advantages and characteristics embodied in database systems
Design database system architecture and data models
Formulate and solve problems using structure query languages with optimization
Understand indexing techniques, concurrency control techniques, database security advanced concepts.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Introduction to Database. Hierarchical, Network and Relational Models.

units.title: Database system architecture
units.text: Database system architecture: Data Abstraction, Data Independence, Data Definition Language (DDL), Data Manipulation Language (DML).

units.title: Data models
units.text: Data models: Entity-relationship model, network model, relational and object oriented data models, integrity constraints, data manipulation operations.

units.title: Relational query languages
units.text: Relational query languages: Relational algebra, Tuple and domain relational calculus, SQL3, DDL and DML constructs, Open source and Commercial DBMS - MYSQL, ORACLE, DB2, SQL server.

units.title: Relational database design
units.text: Relational database design: Domain and data dependency, Armstrong's axioms, Functional Dependencies, Normal forms, Dependency preservation, Lossless design.

units.title: Query processing and optimization
units.text: Query processing and optimization: Evaluation of relational algebra expressions, Query equivalence, Join strategies, Query optimization algorithms.

units.title: Storage strategies
units.text: Storage strategies: Indices, B-trees, Hashing.

units.title: Transaction processing
units.text: Transaction processing: Concurrency control, ACID property, Serializability of scheduling, Locking and timestamp based schedulers, Multi-version and optimistic Concurrency Control schemes, Database recovery.

units.title: Database Security
units.text: Database Security: Authentication, Authorization and access control, DAC, MAC and RBAC models, Intrusion detection, SQL injection.

units.title: Introduction to Advanced topics
units.text: Introduction to Advanced topics: Object oriented and object relational databases, Logical databases, Web databases, Distributed databases, Data warehousing and data mining, Unstructured database, Dataswarm

text_books: 1. Abraham Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth and S. Sudarshan, “Database System Concepts”, 6th Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2013
reference_books: 1. J. D. Ullman, “Principles of Database and Knowledge – Base Systems”, 1st Edition, Computer Science Press, 2016 2. R. Elmasri and S. Navathe, “Fundamentals of Database Systems.”, 7th Edition, Pearson Education, 2017 3. Abiteboul, Richard Hull, Victor Vianu, “Foundations of Databases”, 1st Edition, Pearson Publication, 1994

program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: Introduction to subject as a logical, Quantitative approach in decision- making. To introduce and exercise a range of analytical modeling techniques useful in decision-making in the system design environment.

outcomes.text: Implement concepts of Linear Programming
Solve assignment and transportation problems
Implement Network analysis and Queuing theory
Demonstrate use of Inventory control and Simulation Methodology.

units.title: Introduction to OR
units.text: Introduction to OR: Origin of OR and its definition. Concept of optimizing performance measure, Types of OR problems, Deterministic vs. Stochastic optimization, Phases of OR problem approach – problem formulation, building mathematical model, deriving solutions, validating model, controlling and implementing solution.

units.title: Linear Programming
units.text: Linear Programming: Linear programming – Examples from industrial cases, formulation & definitions, Matrix form. Implicit assumptions of LPP. Some basic concepts and results of linear algebra – Vectors, Matrices, Linear Independence / Dependence of vectors, Rank, Basis, System of linear eqns., Hyperplane, Convex set, Convex polyhedron, Extreme points, Basic feasible solutions. Geometric method: 2-variable case, Special cases – infeasibility, unboundedness, redundancy & degeneracy, Sensitivity analysis. Simplex Algorithm – slack, surplus & artificial variables, computational details, big-M method, identification and resolution of special cases through simplex iterations. Duality – formulation, results, fundamental theorem of duality, dual- simplex and primal-dual algorithms.

units.title: Transportation and Assignment problems
units.text: Transportation and Assignment problems: TP - Examples, Definitions – decision variables, supply & demand constraints, formulation, Balanced & unbalanced situations, Solution methods – NWCR, minimum cost and VAM, test for optimality (MODI method), degeneracy and its resolution. AP - Examples, Definitions – decision variables, constraints, formulation, Balanced & unbalanced situations, Solution method – Hungarian, test for optimality (MODI method), degeneracy & its resolution.

units.title: PERT – CPM
units.text: PERT – CPM: Project definition, Project scheduling techniques – Gantt chart, PERT & CPM, Determination of critical paths, Estimation of Project time and its variance in PERT using statistical principles, Concept of project crashing/time-cost trade-off.

units.title: Inventory Control
units.text: Inventory Control: Functions of inventory and its disadvantages, ABC analysis, Concept of inventory costs, Basics of inventory policy (order, lead time, types), Fixed order-quantity models – EOQ, POQ & Quantity discount models. EOQ models for discrete units, sensitivity analysis and Robustness, Special cases of EOQ models for safety stock with known / unknown stock out situations, models under prescribed policy, Probabilistic situations.

units.title: Queuing Theory
units.text: Queuing Theory: Definitions – queue (waiting line), waiting costs, characteristics (arrival, queue, service discipline) of queuing system, queue types (channel vs. phase). Kendall’s notation, Little’s law, steady state behaviour, Poisson’s Process & queue, Models with examples - M/M/1 and its performance measures; M/M/m and its performance measures; brief description about some special models.

units.title: Simulation Methodology
units.text: Simulation Methodology: Definition and steps of simulation, random number, random number generator, Discrete Event System Simulation – clock, event list, Application in Scheduling, Queuing systems and Inventory systems.

text_books: 1. H.A. Taha, “Operations Research: An Introduction”, 10th edition, Pearson Education, 2019.
reference_books: 1. K.G. Murthy, “Linear Programming”, 1st Edition, John Wiley & Sons, 1983. 2. G. Hadley, “Linear Programming”, 3rd Edition, Narosa, 2002. 3. H.M. Wagner, “Principles of OR with Application to Managerial Decisions” 1st Edition, Prentice Hall India Learning Pvt., 1980. 4. F.S. Hiller and G.J. Lieberman, “Introduction to Operations Research”, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017. 5. Thomas L. Saaty, “Elements of Queuing Theory”, 1st Edition, McGraw-Hill Inc., Us, 1961. 6. A. Ravi Ravindran, “Operations Research and Management Science, Hand Book”, 1st Edition, CRC Press, 2011. 7. Wiest & Levy, “Management Guide to PERT/CPM”, 1st Edition, Prentice Hall, 1970 8. J.W. Prichard and R.H. Eagle, “Modern Inventory Management”, 1st Edition, Wiley, New York, 1965.

program: B Tech CSBS
prerequisites: Completion of Business communication and Value Science-I & Business Communication and Value Science-II
objectives: This course aims of developing an ability to engage in persuasive, technical and domain specific communication in a clear and format driven manner. Also, the course aims at developing in the stakeholders’ critical leadership skills and an ability to effectively engage in crises as well as cross cultural communication.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to utilize critical leadership skills with understanding and empathy to communicate and to solve problems
Apply the conceptual insights derived through this course to efficiently engage in workplace as well as cross cultural communications
Analyze a crisis situation to communicate promptly and in an impactful manner towards effectively managing and resolving crisis
Create technical and scientific papers and writings to disseminate evidence based field specific knowledge

units.title: Technical Writing and Persuasive Communication
units.text: Technical Writing and Persuasive Communication Persuasive Communication tools for writing-AIDA; Rhetorical Triangle; organizing principles of writing; ethical use of AI Tools for writing and Paraphrasing. Journal Paper writing-Format and Publication Process; Literature Review and Review Articles. Technical instructions writing – Definition, process, and object description. Case Essay writing: Position Statement; critique of evaluation; evaluative, problem and decision case essays. Conducting business analyses using SWOT, TOWS and PESTELLE as tools; Presenting Business analyses based Feasibility Reports using persuasive communication strategies.

units.title: Cross Cultural Communication
units.text: Cross Cultural Communication Meaning and Importance of Cross Cultural Communication; Geert Hofstede’s six dimensions of cross cultural Communication; etiquette governing verbal and nonverbal cross cultural communication; Pitfalls to avoid while engaging in cross cultural Communication.

units.title: Crisis Communication
units.text: Crisis Communication Crisis Communication Strategy; Significance of creating a crisis communication plan; Importance of prompt and well defined timelines for crisis communication; Social media and crisis communication; drafting media statements for crises.

units.title: Leadership Skills
units.text: Leadership Skills Individual Leadership styles- demonstrated through conducting leader profile analyses; Impact of Personality Traits on Leadership Styles.

units.title: Intersection between Leadership and communication
units.text: Intersection between Leadership and communication: The context an environment facing leaders; building skills for one to one; one to many and e form of communication for leaders. Critical and soft skills for leaders: Leaders as listeners; Leaders as writers; Delegation and empowerment through motivational communication.; Leadership in groups and teams; leadership in crises.

text_books: 1. Mike Markel and Stuart Selber, Technical Communication, Bedford/St. Martins publication, 13th Edition, 2021. 2. Craig E. Johnson. & Michael E. Hackman, Leadership-A communication Perspective, 7th Edition, Waveland Press Inc., 2018.
reference_books: 1. Bovee, C., Thill, J., & Roshan Lal Raina, Business Communication Today, 14th Edition, Pearson, 2013. 2. Richard Dool, 12 Months of Leadership Insights, self - Published, 2019. 3. Ellet William, The Case Study Handbook, Harvard Business Publishing, 3rd Edition, 2007.
lab_work: 8 to 10 activities based on the syllabus.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: To provide knowledge about various component and functional blocks of digital computer architecture. Learning of Computer arithmetic, Memory organization, I/O interface, Instruction set and Multi-processor architecture.

outcomes.text: Explain various functional blocks and their interactions in computer architecture
Explain Memory operations and their types
Describe Computer Arithmetic and characteristics of Instruction Set with respect to internal architecture
Describe operations of I/O interfacing and Multiprocessor architecture.

units.title: Computer architectural Evolution and History
units.text: Computer architectural Evolution and History: Generations of computer and evolutions in terms of various technical aspects, major landmarks in history, future view of architecture.

units.title: Basic blocks and processes in computer
units.text: Basic blocks and processes in computer: Block level description of the functional units inside CPU and their interactions to execute program fetch, decode and execution cycle, performance evaluation of computer architecture.

units.title: Memory architecture
units.text: Memory architecture: Various types of memory technology, static and dynamic RAM comparison, cache memory and memory hierarchy, different types of address mapping, virtual memory concepts and operations.

units.title: Processor Architecture
units.text: Processor Architecture: Details understanding of internal functional units inside general processor, registers, buses, IO interface, ALU.

units.title: Computer Arithmetic
units.text: Computer Arithmetic: Floating-point arithmetic format and arithmetic operations.

units.title: Instruction set Characteristics and Architecture
units.text: Instruction set Characteristics and Architecture: Instruction sets, assembly language, instruction cycles, addressing modes, internal storage and data handling, interrupts handling, various types of instructions for various operations, RISC versus CISC architectures.

units.title: Input / Output systems
units.text: Input / Output systems: Interfacing with various IO interface, Programmed IO, concept of handshaking, interrupt driven and polled IO, DMA operations, types of bus and its operations, timing diagram for IO interface. Storage systems Principles of working for hard disk, RAID, cloud storage.

units.title: Multiprocessor organization
units.text: Multiprocessor organization: Pipeline processing, instruction and arithmetic pipeline concept, parallel processing.

text_books: 1. William Stallings, “Computer Organization and Architecture Designing for Performance”, Pearson Education, 11th Edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. John P. Hayes, “Computer Architecture and Organization”, Tata Mc-Graw Hill, 3rd Edition, 2012. 2. David A. Patterson and John L. Hennessy, “Computer Organization and Design The Hardware/Software interface”, Elsevier, 6th Edition, 2017.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: Enable students to understand linear data structures, implement them to utilize computer memory efficiently. Also to understand searching and sorting algorithms to solve real-life problems.

outcomes.text: Comprehend data structures and implement stacks and queues
Use linked list to solve real life problem statements
Solve real life problem statements using searching and sorting algorithms.

units.title: Introduction to Data Structures
units.text: Introduction to Data Structures: Basic data types, data structure definition, need for data structures, elementary data structure organization, classification of data structures, operations on data structures, abstract data type.

units.title: Linear Data Structure I Arrays and Stacks
units.text: Linear Data Structure I Arrays and Stacks: Introduction, declaration of arrays, operations on arrays. introduction to stacks, array representation of stacks, operations of a stack, push, pop, peek, stack overflow and stack underflow, applications of a stack reversing a list, decimal to binary conversion using stack, conversion and evaluation of arithmetic expression, recursion, tower of Hanoi.

units.title: Linear Data Structure II Queues
units.text: Linear Data Structure II Queues: Introduction to queues, array representation of queues, queue operations insertion, deletion, queue overflow, queue underflow, circular queues, priority queues, applications of queues.

units.title: Linear Data Structure III Linked List
units.text: Linear Data Structure III Linked List: Introduction, basic terminologies, linked list versus arrays, dynamic memory allocation and deallocation for a linked list, types of linked lists singly linked list, doubly linked list, operations of linked list, traversing a linked list, applications of linked lists.

units.title: Searching and Sorting
units.text: Searching and Sorting: Basic searching techniques sequential search, binary search, sorting definitions, selection sort, insertion sort, radix sort, hashing and collision resolution techniques.

text_books: 1. Y. Langsam, M.J. Augenstein, A.M. Tenenbaum, “Data Structures using C and C++”, PHI publication, 2nd Edition, 2015. 2. Seymour Lipschutz, “Data structures with C”, Schaum’s Outlines, 1st Edition, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Mark Allen Weiss, “Data Structures and Algorithm analysis in C++”, PHI publication, 4th Edition, 2013. 2. Reema Thareja, “Data Structures using C”, Oxford University Press, Tata McGraw Hill, 2nd Edition, 2014.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: The objective of the course is to present an introduction to database management systems, with an emphasis on how to organize, maintain and retrieve - efficiently, and effectively - information from a DBMS.

outcomes.text: Describe core concepts of database and model a database management system through ER modelling
Apply knowledge of relational algebra and structural query language to retrieve and manage data from relational database
Design database by applying principles of normalization and including integrity constraints
Discover importance of indexing, transaction management, concurrency and recovery in database management system.

units.title: Introduction to Database concepts
units.text: Introduction to Database concepts: Introduction to data processing overview of files systems, drawback of file systems, purpose of database system, concept of a database, database system vs file system, view of data, data models, database users and administrator.

units.title: Entity Relationship Model
units.text: Entity Relationship Model: Overview of design process, the entity- relationship model, constraints, ER diagram, and reduction to relational schemas, entity-relationship design issues, extended ER features.

units.title: Relational Model
units.text: Relational Model: Concept of relation, notion of primary and secondary keys, foreign keys, structure of relational database, relational algebra and extended relational algebra operations, formation of queries, modification of the database views.

units.title: Structured Query Language (SQL)
units.text: Structured Query Language (SQL): Background, basic structure, set operations, aggregate functions, NULL values, nested queries, views, complex queries, database modification, DDL, embedded SQL, stored procedures and functions, dynamic SQL featured.

units.title: Integrity and Security
units.text: Integrity and Security: Domain constrains, referential integrity, assertions, triggers and assertions in SQL, security and authorization in SQL.

units.title: Relational Database Design
units.text: Relational Database Design: Features of good relational database design, atomic domains and first normal form, decomposition using functional dependencies, functional dependency theory, normalization, decomposition, first normal to fifth normal forms, BCNF, pitfall in relational-database design, indexing and hashing, basic concepts, ordered indices – dense, sparse index, multilevel indices, static hashing, dynamic hashing.

units.title: Transactions
units.text: Transactions: Basic concept of transaction, state of a transaction, implementation of atomicity and durability, concurrent executions, serializability, recoverability, implementation of isolation, transaction in SQL.

units.title: Concurrency
units.text: Concurrency Control and Recovery: Lock based protocols, timestamp-based protocols, validation-based protocols, deadlock handling, recovery and atomicity, log-based recovery.

text_books: 1. Hennery Korth and Abraham Silberschatz, “Database System Concepts”, McGraw Hill, 7th Edition, 2019
reference_books: 1. Elmarsi and Navathe, “Fundamentals of Database Design”, Addison Wesley 7th Edition, 2019. 2. Bob Bryla, Kevin Loney “Oracle Database 12C The Complete Reference”, Tata McGraw Hill, 2017.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: To enable the students understand the advantage of using Object Oriented programming over procedural programming to tackle complex real word programming problems. The course focuses on the understanding and developing a practical mastery on object- oriented concepts.

outcomes.text: Describe and implement the Classes and relevant methods to solve a given problem
Design solutions for a given problem using the concepts of Abstraction, Polymorphism, Encapsulation & Inheritance in OOP paradigm
Solve a real-world problem by designing and implementing Class diagrams.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Review of object orientation, class and objects, primitive object types.

units.title: Strings and Arrays
units.text: Strings and Arrays: Strings, string buffer, arrays, vectors, operators, loop control, decision making.

units.title: Object Oriented Systems
units.text: Object Oriented Systems: Encapsulation, constructors, inheritance, polymorphism (overloading, over riding).

units.title: Exception Handling
units.text: Exception Handling: Pre defined exceptions, try-catch-finally, throws, throw, and user-defined exception.

units.title: IO Streams
units.text: IO Streams: Byte-oriented streams, character – oriented streams, file handling.

units.title: Abstract Class, Interfaces
units.text: Abstract Class, Interfaces: Abstract classes, interface, inner classes, wrapper classes.

units.title: Modelling Classes
units.text: Modelling Classes: UML class diagram, associations and multiplicity, generalization, process of developing class diagrams, implementing class diagrams in object oriented programming language.

text_books: 1. Y. Daniel Liang, “Introduction to Java Programming”, Comprehensive Version, Global Edition, Pearson Education, 11th Edition 2019. 2. Herbert Schildt, “Java 2 The Complete Reference”, McGraw-Hill Education, 11th Edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. Herbert Schildt, “Java A Beginner’s Guide”, McGraw-Hill Education, 8th Edition, 2020. 2. Cay S. Horstmann, “Core Java Volume I—Fundamentals”, Pearson, 11th Edition, 2018.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
prerequisites: knowledge of Discrete Mathematics, Modular Arithmetic and Linear Algebra.
objectives: 1. To introduce Algebraic structures as a foundation for coding theory and cryptography. 2. To give exposure to information theory and coding techniques for data compression and correcting and detecting errors.

outcomes.text: Understand Algebraic structures, concept of information, entropy, Shannon’s theorem and Channel capacity.
Solve problems related to groups, rings and field theory.
Understand applications of algebraic structures and implement various coding techniques.

units.title: Groups
units.text: Groups: Definitions and examples, elementary properties of groups, abelian group, finite group, subgroup, cyclic groups, permutation groups, dihedral groups, group homomorphism, isomorphism and auto morphism, cosets, normal subgroup, quotient group.

units.title: Rings and Integrals Domains
units.text: Rings and Integrals Domains: Definition and examples, subring, integral domain, ideal, ring homomorphism, polynomial rings, irreducibility of polynomials.

units.title: Field Theory
units.text: Field Theory: Definition and examples, extension fields, degree of extension, splitting field, finite fields, classification of finite fields, subfield of finite field, Galois field.

units.title: Introduction to information theory
units.text: Introduction to information theory: Information, average information, entropy, properties of entropy, information rate, discrete memory less channel- BSC, joint and conditional entropies, mutual information, information sources, zero memory information source, markov information source, Shannon’s theorem, channel capacity, Shannon limit.

units.title: Source coding algorithms (Lossless compression)
units.text: Source coding algorithms (Lossless compression): Classification of codes- uniquely decodable codes, prefix codes, Kraft- McMillan inequality Shannon Fano code, Huffman code, minimum variance Huffman code.

units.title: Channel Coding (Linear Block Codes)
units.text: Channel Coding (Linear Block Codes): Generator matrix, parity check matrix, error detecting and correcting capability, syndrome testing, decoding, Cyclic codes: properties, encoder and decoder, Hamming codes.

text_books: 1. Joseph A. Gallian, Contemporary Abstract Algebra, 10th Edition, CRC press, 2021. 2. Ranjan Bose, Information Theory and Coding, 3rd Edition McGraw Hill Publication, July 2016.
reference_books: 1. John B. Fraleigh, A First Course in Abstract Algebra, 8th Edition, Pearson Education, 2020. 2. M. Kulkarni and K. Shivaprakash, Information Theory and Coding, Wiley India, 2015.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics
objectives: This course aims to understand the multidisciplinary nature of environmental sciences, greenhouse effect and climate change. It also aims to discuss the basics of natural resources, biodiversity, environmental pollution.

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of natural resources, ecosystem and biodiversity
Relate the various aspects of environmental pollutions with its cause and effect
Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change.

units.title: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science
units.text: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science Definition, scope and importance of environmental sciences.

Natural Resources • Natural resources: Forest resources, Water resources, Mineral resources, Food resources. • Energy resources: Growing energy needs, renewable and non- renewable energy sources, use of alternate energy sources.

Ecosystems • Concept of an ecosystem. • Structure and function of an ecosystem. • Food chains, food webs and ecological pyramids. • Introduction, types, characteristic features of the following ecosystem:- a. Forest ecosystem b. Grassland ecosystem c. Desert ecosystem d. Aquatic ecosystems.

Biodiversity • Definition: genetic, species and ecosystem diversity. • Value of biodiversity: consumptive use, productive use. • Threats to biodiversity: habitat loss, poaching of wildlife, man-wildlife conflicts.

Environmental Pollution • Definition, Cause and effects for Air pollution, Water pollution, Soil pollution, Marine pollution, Noise pollution, Thermal pollution, Nuclear hazards and Solid waste pollution.
The Science of Climate Change • Greenhouse effect • Global warming • Global environmental changes • Acid rain • Ozone layer depletion • Carbon footprint

text_books: 1. Erach Bharucha, “Textbook of Environmental Studies”, University Press, 2nd Edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. MP Poonia & SC Sharma, “Environmental Studies”, Khanna Publishing House, 1st Edition, 2017. 2. Rajagopalan, “Environmental Studies”, Oxford University Press, Third Edition, 2015.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: 1. To inculcate human values to grow as a responsible human being 2. To maintain ethical conduct in discharging professional duties

outcomes.text: understand the engineering code of ethics and be able to apply them as necessary
understand moral complexities in many engineering activities and decision-making processes
understand some of the contemporary issues in the engineering professions
effectively communicate their knowledge and understanding of engineering ethics.

units.text: Introduction to Ethics-  Concept of morals and ethics,  Study of engineering ethics;  Laws and ethics;  Personal and professional ethics.
Professional Practice in Engineering-  Common morality ASME code of ethics,  Technical codes and standards,  Accepted standards of Engineering practice and the standard of care.

Ethics as design-doing justice to moral Problem-  Discuss about ethics as a design to solve moral problems  Comparison between moral problems and engineering design problems;  Moral lessons from design problems;  Implications of the dynamic character of problem situations.

Rights and Responsibilities of Engineers-  Moral responsibilities;  Conflicts of interests;  Confidentiality,  Engineers, organizations and ethics,  Engineer-manager relationships;  loyalty;  The concept of whistleblowing.

Responsibility for the Environment-  Rapid Technological growth and depletion of resources,  Reports of the Club of Rome.  Limits of growth: sustainable development  Energy Crisis: Renewable Energy Resources  Environmental degradation and pollution.  Eco-friendly Technologies.  Environmental Regulations,  Environmental Ethics  Appropriate Technology,  Movement of Schumacher; later developments of Technology and developing notions.  Problems of Technology transfer,  Technology assessment impact analysis.  Problems of man, machine, interaction,  Impact of assembly line and automation.  Human centered Technology

text_books: 1. M.W. Martin and R. Schinzinger, “Ethics in Engineering”, McGraw-Hill, Second Edition, 2005. 2. Charles B. Fleddermann, “Engineering Ethics”, Pearson, Third Edition, 2007. 3. P.A. Vesilind and A. S Gunn, “Engineering Ethics and Environment”, Cambridge University Press, First Edition, 1998.
reference_books: 1. Caroline Whitbeck, “Ethics in Engineering – Practice and Research”, Cambridge University Press, Second Edition, 2011.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: 1. To enable the students to understand the principles mentioned in our Constitution and apply them in regular course of activities, personal or professional. 2. To enable them to know the structure of Indian polity, legal framework and inter-relations of institutions of ‘State’ in India

outcomes.text: understand the historic evolution of the Indian Constitution, its drafting, nature and to understand the principles mentioned in its Preamble.

inculcate fundamental rights in its true sense and also the permissible restrictions upon it so as to enjoy these rights within permissible limits while simultaneously performing their duties and to apply these principles into their professional lives.
ingrain the structure of our polity and role of Judiciary in maintaining the basic structure of the Constitution.

attain knowledge of the Emergency provisions, when and how it is imposed, to know the additional powers the bestowed upon the Government at times of Emergency and to understand the Amendment procedure.

units.text: Nature, Characteristics and Sources of Indian Constitution

Fundamental rights and Fundamental duties – Concept of State, Right to Equality under Articles 14 and 15, Right to certain freedoms under Article 19, Right to Life and liberty under Article 21, Right to religion under Article 25 and 26, Right to remedy under Article 32 and Fundamental duties
Indian Judiciary – Concept of Supreme Court and High Courts, Appointment of Judges, Independence of Judiciary, Jurisdictions of Supreme Court and High Courts
Emergency Provisions – Concept of National Emergency under Article 352, Financial Emergency under Article 360 and President rule under Article 356 of the Constitution

text_books: 1. Dr. Durga Das Basu, “Introduction to the Constitution of India” Lexis Nexis, 24th Edition 2019.
reference_books: 1. P. M. Bakshi, “The Constitution of India” Universal Law Publishing, 14th Edition 2017. 2. J. N. Pandey, “Constitutional Law of India” Central Law Agency, 54th Edition 2017. 3. N. A. Palkhivala, “We the people” UBS Publishers Distributors, 1999.

units.text: Logic Gates and Boolean Algebra Logic gates, Concept of universal logic and implementation of digital logic using universal gates, Review of Boolean algebra and De maps up to 4 variables.

units.text: Combinational logic circuit and its implementation Combinational circuits - Adders, Subtractors (half and full), Multiplexers, DE-multiplexers, Decoders, Encoders, Design of digital logic using multiplexers.

objectives: This course provides the fundamental knowledge of computer networks through understanding each layer of computer network architecture, and transmission systems to network applications. It also focuses on congestion control techniques, protocols, and application layer functions.

outcomes.text: Explain the concepts of computer networks, topologies and data communication.
Analyze the various error detection and correction and medium access techniques.
Apply network layer addressing and routing techniques to different network topologies.
Analyze the different protocols of the layered architecture of computer networks.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Computer Network, Peer-to-peer and client-server communication, Classifications of computer networks, Network Topologies.

units.title: Physical Layer
units.text: Physical Layer Introduction to OSI and TCP/IP model, Transmission Media.

units.title: Data Link Layer and Medium Access Sub Layer
units.text: Data Link Layer and Medium Access Sub Layer Fundamentals of Error Detection and Error Correction, Block coding, Hamming Distance, Flow Control and Error control; error control mechanism - CRC; flow control protocols - Stop and Wait ARQ, Go-back– N ARQ, Selective Repeat ARQ, Multiple access protocols - Random Access - Pure ALOHA, Slotted ALOHA, CSMA/CD, CDMA/CA.

units.title: Network Layer

units.title: Transport Layer

units.title: Application Layer
units.text: Application Layer HTTP, DNS, FTP, SMTP.

units.title: Experiments
units.text: Exp. No. Programming Topic 1. Concept: Implement a program using classes, objects, data members and member functions. Problem Statement: Create a class “Employee” to read and print information about an employee with the following data members: Name of the employee, ID of the employee, Department of the employee, Basic salary. Task: Perform the following functions to complete the operations: 1. Write a member function read_Employee() to initialize the object. 2. Write a member function to Calculate Gross salary and its components (declare them as data members) based on the following conditions: Dearness allowance (DA) = 50 % of basic salary HRA = 30 % basic salary TA = 10 % basic salary Gross Salary = basic salary + DA + HRA + TA. 3. Write a member function to display employee details with Gross Salary and all other components. 2. Concepts: Implement a program using Encapsulation, Abstractions and Array of Objects. Problem Statement: A school is developing Library Management system to maintain the records of the books. Where it performs basic operations such as making entry of the book, searching the book by book name and author name. It also shows availability of the books. Task: Create class to manage the books in “Library” with following data members and functions. Name of the book Author of the book Price of the book No. of copies Implement member functions to perform the following operations: Read the data of 5 books – include books in the library. Display the data of books – print the list of all the books in the library. Search the specified book in the Library by name, if it is available or not, if available then display no of copies of the book. Search the specified book in the Library by Author Name, display all the books of the same author. 3 Concept: Implement a program using the concepts of constructor to initialize the object. Problem Statement: A customer can open account in the bank with following attributes. A customer can performs basic operations with the account created using class called “Bank Account”. Customer Name Address Account Number Age Balance Amount Task: Implement following functions to perform operations with an account: 1. Use the parameterized constructor to initialize the array of objects. 2. Write a function to withdraw amount after checking account no. 3. Write a function to deposit amount after checking account no. 4. Write a function to display balance amount after checking account no. 5. Write a function to display the Customer Profile. 4. Concept: Implement a program using Inheritance, Runtime polymorphism and Modelling classes. Problem Statement: A bank want to extend two more insurance services to their customers along with basic bank operations performed using “Saving Bank Account”. These two additional services will be implemented without changing existing bank account class. So, two additional classes are created by deriving features from the “Bank Account”. These classes are name as “Life Insurance” and “Car Insurance”. Premium of both the insurance policies are linked to bank account of the customer so that it can be directly deducted from their saving account and current balance will be displayed after every deduction. Features derived from the base classes are shown in the following diagram. The “Claim” class is used to settle the claim amount and deposited in the respective saving bank account.

program: B Tech and MBA Tech (Information Technology), B Tech CSE (Cybersecurity)
objectives: The course aims to introduce and explore a chosen problem, providing students with the opportunity to engage with a variety of real-world challenges presented by different agencies. Students come onboard at different stages of project completion. The course seeks to guide students in selecting a project that aligns with their interests, expertise, and career goals. Through this approach, the course integrates elements of Design Thinking and Research, to enhance practical learning and problem-solving skills.

outcomes.text: Identify and explain real-world challenges in their context, relevance, and impact.
Collaborate effectively within diverse teams to solve complex design problems
Utilize Design Thinking principles to develop and iteratively refine practical solutions for the selected problem.
Design and prototype innovative solutions that integrate research insights and feasibility analysis.
Demonstrate effective oral and written communication skills relevant to the problem.

units.title: Introduction and Team Formation
units.text: Introduction and Team Formation: Familiarize with real-world problems and project options and team formation based on interests and skills. Problem Analysis: Understand the problem context and requirements and conduct literature review relevant to the problem objectives. Design Thinking and Concept Development: Develop innovative solutions. Apply Design Thinking phases and refine concepts based on feedback. Project Management and Documentation: Ensure organized execution. Assign roles, manage tasks, and maintain design documents. Communication and Review: Present and refine project outcomes. Prepare presentations, conduct reviews, and incorporate feedback. Reflection and Improvement: Enhance skills and identify next steps. Reflect on lessons learned and document final outcomes.

lab_work: The Laboratory work comprises various activities performed by the project teams for formulation, solution implementation and modification. Each team needs to submit the following documents: • Problem Statement Document • Project Development Report • Mid Semester Project Report • Final Report

program: B Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: This course aims to instill in students a sound knowledge of probability theory and statistical techniques. It equips the students with intermediate to advanced level concepts and tools in probability and statistics that help them tackle relevant problems within engineering domain.

outcomes.text: solve problems involving random variables, probability distributions and testing of hypothesis, correlation and regression
identify suitable probability distribution and testing techniques to solve related problems
apply knowledge of random variables, probability distributions, measures of central tendency, correlation and regression to solve real life problems
analyse data samples using statistical methods.

units.title: Basic Probability
units.text: Basic Probability Probability spaces, conditional probability, independence; Bayes theorem.

units.title: Random variables and Probability Distributions
units.text: Random variables and Probability Distributions Discrete random variables, probability mass function, cumulative distribution function, Independent random variables, Continuous random variables, distribution functions and densities, expectation, variance, raw and central moments of random variables, Binomial distribution, Poisson approximation to the binomial distribution, Normal distribution.

units.title: Bivariate Distributions
units.text: Bivariate Distributions Definition of Bivariate Distribution and their properties, Conditional densities.

units.title: Basic Statistics
units.text: Basic Statistics Measures of Central tendency; Moments, Moment generating function, skewness, kurtosis. Mean and variance of Binomial distribution & Poisson distribution, Moments, skewness & kurtosis for Normal distribution.

units.title: Testing of hypothesis
units.text: Testing of hypothesis: Point estimation, Interval estimate and Confidence interval, Criteria for good estimates, Null and Alternate hypothesis, Test Statistic, Type I and Type II errors, One-tailed and two-tailed test, Critical region, Large sample statistical test for mean, Large sample statistical test for proportion, t-test for small samples, Test for variance- F test, Chi-square test for Goodness of fit and independence of attributes, Analysis of variance.

units.title: Linear Statistical Models
units.text: Linear Statistical Models: Scatter diagram, Linear regression and correlation, Least squares method, Rank correlation, Multiple regression.

program: B Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: The aim of this course is to provide an understanding of the fundamental characteristics of signals and systems from the perspective of both the time and transform domains. The course will help the student to develop the mathematical skills needed to analyze continuous and discrete time signals and systems in both the domains.

outcomes.text: Classify continuous time and discrete time signals and systems
Apply various mathematical operations to analyze signals and systems
Analyze continuous time signals and systems using various transforms
Determine the frequency spectrum of continuous and discrete time signals and systems.

units.title: Introduction to Signals and Systems
units.text: Introduction to Signals and Systems: Signals- definitions, classification, operations and elementary signals. System and its classification - discrete and continuous time signals and systems.

units.title: LTI System and Classification
units.text: LTI System and Classification Time domain representations for linear time-invariant systems, convolution integral and convolution sum, impulse response representation for LTI systems, interconnection of systems, series, parallel and mixed, differential and difference equation representations for LTI systems.

units.title: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Signals
units.text: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Signals: Different types of Fourier series representation and interconnection between exponential and trigonometric Fourier series, Fourier series representation of continuous time periodic signal, magnitude and phase spectrum, Fourier series representation of discrete time periodic signal and its spectrum.

units.title: Fourier Transform
units.text: Fourier Transform Development of Fourier transform from Fourier series, frequency spectrum using Fourier transform, properties of Fourier transform - linearity property, change of scale property, shifting property, inverse Fourier transform.

units.title: Laplace Transform
units.text: Laplace Transform Limitations of Fourier transform, introduction to Laplace transform, ROC and its properties, Laplace transform of elementary signals, unilateral Laplace transform, inverse Laplace transform.

units.title: Z Transform
units.text: Z Transform Introduction to Z transform, Z transform of elementary signals, ROC, properties of Z transform, inverse of Z transform using partial fraction and long division rule, solution of difference equation.

text_books: 1. Tarun Kumar Rawat, “Signals and Systems”, Oxford University Press, 1st edition 2010. 2. Nagoor Kani, “Signals and Systems”, McGraw-Hill, 1st edition, 2010.
reference_books: 1. Oppenheim and Willsky,” Signals and Systems”, Prentice Hall of India, 2nd edition, 2016. 2. Simon Haykin and Barry Van Veen, “Signals and Systems”, John Wiley, 2nd edition, 2008.

program: B Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
prerequisites: Computer Organization & Architecture, Programming for Problem Solving.
objectives: To present an introduction to Operating Systems, with an emphasis on the policies for scheduling, deadlocks, memory management, synchronization, system calls, and file systems.

outcomes.text: Comprehend the objectives, services and different architectures of the Operating System and their types
Conduct simulation experiments on process scheduling, inter-process communication, deadlock avoidance of system by using different algorithms
Implement and evaluate the various memory management techniques provided by the OS to improve the overall system performance
Comprehend the techniques to manage files & methods to access different storage devices.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Concept of operating systems, generations of operating systems, types of operating Systems, OS Services, system calls, structure of an OS.

units.title: Processes
units.text: Processes: Definition, process relationship, different states of a process, process state transitions, process control block (PCB), context switching Thread definition, various states, benefits of threads, types of threads, concept of multithreads. Process Scheduling: Foundation and scheduling objectives, types of schedulers, scheduling criteria CPU utilization, throughput, turnaround time, waiting time, response time, scheduling algorithms- pre-emptive and non-pre-emptive, FCFS, SJF and RR.

units.title: Inter-process Communication
units.text: Inter-process Communication: Critical section, race conditions, mutual exclusion, Peterson’s solution, semaphores, monitors. Classical IPC Problems: Reader’s & writer problem.

units.title: Deadlocks
units.text: Deadlocks: Definition, necessary and sufficient conditions for deadlock, deadlock prevention, deadlock avoidance, banker’s algorithm, deadlock detection and recovery.

units.title: Memory Management
units.text: Memory Management: Basic concept, logical and physical address map, memory allocation- contiguous memory allocation – fixed and variable partition– internal and external fragmentation and compaction. Paging: Principle of operation – page allocation – hardware support for paging, protection and sharing, disadvantages of paging.

units.title: I/O Hardware
units.text: I/O Hardware: I/O devices, device controllers, direct memory access principles of I/O software- goals of interrupt handlers, device drivers, device independent I/O software. File Management: Overview, file organization, file directories, file sharing and record blocking.

text_books: 1. Achyut S. Godbole and Atul Kahate, “Operating Systems”, McGraw-Hill, 3rd Edition, 2017. 2. William Stallings, “Operating Systems Internals and Design Principles”, Pearson Education, 9th Edition, 2018.
reference_books: 1. Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin and Greg Gagne, “Operating System Concepts”, Wiley, 9th Edition, 2018. 2. Ann McHoes and Ida M. Flynn, “Understanding Operating Systems”, Course Technology, 5th Edition, 2013.

program: B Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: This is an introductory course in computer networks. The course is designed to enable students to understand and analyze the protocols, and applications of computer networks. The objective is to learn how computer networks work today and the basics of its architecture. Course Outcomes After completion of this course, students will be able to- 1. Describe the function of different network models, associated protocols and standards, 2. Compare different transmission media, and understand error detection and correction techniques, 3. Analyze medium access control algorithms, and network layer error control, flow control, and routing algorithms, 4. Describe transport layer congestion control techniques, application layer protocols and basic security concepts.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Introduction to computer networks, classification of computer networks, topology, layering and protocol, OSI reference model, TCP/IP model, networking devices, performance issues (bandwidth, latency, delay etc.).

units.title: Application Layer
units.text: Application Layer: DNS, E-mail (working of email transfer and delivery), WWW (Architectural overview), WWW (Architectural overview).

units.title: Transport Layer
units.text: Transport Layer: Transport layer services, elements of transport layer, UDP and TCP (Tahoe, Reno).

units.title: Network layer
units.text: Network layer: Forwarding and routing, virtual circuit and datagram networks, router internals, routing algorithms - (optimality principle, shortest path routing, flooding, distance vector routing, link state routing, IPv4 and IPv6 overview).

units.title: Medium access control sublayer
units.text: Medium access control sublayer: Channel allocation problem, random access protocol (ALOHA, Carrier Sense Multiple Access (CSMA), Carrier Sense Multiple Access Collision Detection – (CSMA/CD), controlled access (reservation, polling, token passing), channelization (FDMA, TDMA, CDMA), Ethernet overview and binary exponential back off.

units.title: Data Link Layer
units.text: Data Link Layer: Data link layer design issues (services provided to network layer, framing, error control and flow control), error detection and correction techniques (parity checks, check-summing methods, CRC, Hamming code), reliable transmission (stop and wait, sliding window protocol with its variants).

units.title: Physical Layer and media
units.text: Physical Layer and media: Analog and digital signals, transmission impairment, data rate limits, guided media and unguided media.

units.title: Network Security
units.text: Network Security: Cryptography- introduction, substitution ciphers, transposition ciphers, one time pads, symmetric key algorithm, and public key algorithm.

text_books: 1. James F. Kurose, Keith W. Ross, “Computer Networking A Top Down Approach”, Pearson Education, 7th Edition, 2017. 2. Behrouz A Forouzan, Firouz Mosharraf, “Computer Networks A Top Down Approach”, TMH, 6th Edition, 2012.
reference_books: 1. Behrouz A. Forouzan, “Data Communications and Networking”, McGraw-Hill, 5th Edition, 2013. 2. Larry L. Peterson, Bruce S. Davie, “Computer Networks A systems approach”, Morgan Kaufmann Publishers, 5th Edition, 2011. 3. Andrew S. Tanenbaum, David Wetherall, “Computer Networks”, Pearson Education, 5th Edition, 2012. 4. objectives: This course provides basic orientation towards economic (micro and macroeconomics) principles and help them understand the functions of management. (2) Sampling distributions of the difference between sample means/ proportion – Mean and Standard Deviation, Conditions for estimation. Hypothesis Testing: (1) Large Sample estimation of the population parameters and Hypothesis testing: Basics of Estimating the populations mean and difference; estimating the proportion and difference; large sample test for population mean, difference; large sample test for proportion, difference. objectives: Students will be familiar with basic rules of probability and will be able to use them in modelling uncertainty in obtaining and recording data. course_name: Introduction to Data and Signal Analysis
program: B Tech & MBA Tech Data Science
objectives: This course aims to introduce students to the fundamental concepts of data and signal analysis. It provides a strong mathematical foundation for signal representation, processing, and transformation techniques. The course will help students understand signal characterization, and frequency-domain analysis using various transforms. Additionally, students will learn the importance of sampling and its role in digital signal processing, along with Fourier and Laplace transformations for analysing signals in different domains.

outcomes.text: Describe the fundamental concepts of data communication and perform mathematical operations on signals
Explain convolution techniques & Z-transforms and apply them in analysing discrete-time signals
Apply the Nyquist Sampling Theorem to determine the optimal sampling rate
Analyse signals using series and transforms to interpret and solve signal processing problems

Need and Importance of Sampling, Nyquist Sampling Theorem (without proof), problems to determine ideal sampling rate when an analog signal is given, obtaining a discrete signal from continuous signal
Trigonometric Fourier Series (for periodic cts), Fourier Transform of signals (for non-periodic cts)
Laplace transform; its properties, problems based on properties

program: B Tech & MBA Tech Data Science
prerequisites: Data Wrangling/Data Wrangling Fundamentals and Practices
objectives: The objective of this course is to introduce students to the fundamental concepts of data engineering. The course provides a conceptual understanding of data systems, data architecture, data movement, data preparation, and basic data pipeline concepts using structured datasets. Emphasis is placed on understanding how data flows through different stages in a data system, ensuring data quality and consistency.

outcomes.text: Explain the structure and components of data systems and basic architectural concepts used in data-driven applications
Describe different data sources and ingestion mechanisms involved in moving data into a data system
Apply data structuring and preparation techniques to organize datasets for processing across multiple stages
Analyze datasets to ensure data quality, consistency, and reliability during data preparation and integration

program: B Tech (EXTC)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Electronic Devices and circuits
objectives: This course aims to acquaint students with the fundamentals of the ac small signal models of BJT and JFET amplifier and the designing of BJT, JFET, power supplies and oscillator circuits. This course also helps to understand and analyze negative feedback amplifiers, Power Amplifier and various Op-amp applications.

outcomes.text: Illustrate the small-signal and large-signal models of BJTs and JFETs, including their high- frequency behavior and hybrid-π model.
Design of single-stage and multistage amplifiers using BJT and FET transistor considering temperature drift, midpoint biasing.
Design Power Supply Circuit Analysis and Design.
Analyze the effects of negative feedback on amplifier circuits and oscillator circuits.
Demonstrate the design and working of linear and non-linear op-amp circuits, including inverting, non-inverting, summing, differentiator, integrator, Schmitt trigger, and waveform generators.
Explain the principles, classifications, and performance parameters of power amplifiers (Class A, B, AB, and C) along with their circuit topologies.

units.title: Amplifiers Analysis and Design

units.title: Oscillator Circuits and Design

units.title: Rectifiers and design

units.title: Power Amplifiers
units.text: Power Amplifiers Class A, B, AB, C amplifiers, efficiency analysis, Push-pull configurations, transformer-coupled stages

units.title: Operational Amplifier Applications

program: B Tech (EXTC)
objectives: This subject is designed to make students competent in AC and DC circuit analysis techniques and several methods of simplifying networks. Steady state and transient analysis will make them understand deeper aspects of circuit behaviour. They would also be acquainted with the fundamental principles of circuit theory and network synthesis.

outcomes.text: Identify the methods of mesh and node analysis for circuits with independent and dependent AC and DC sources.
Explain the use of network theorems, including Thevenin’s, Norton’s, and superposition theorems, in analyzing electrical circuits.
Apply graph theory principles, including trees, cut sets, and tie sets, to model and analyze electrical networks.
Solve first- and second-order differential equations to evaluate transient and steady-state responses in electrical circuits.
Determine the parameters and functions of two-port networks, including Z, Y, ABCD, and hybrid parameters, for analyzing circuit behavior.

units.title: Mesh and Node Analysis
units.text: Mesh and Node Analysis Mesh and node analysis of circuits with independent and dependent ac and dc sources.

units.title: Network Theorems
units.text: Network Theorems Linearity, current and voltage source transformation, superposition theorem, Thevenin’s theorem, Norton’s theorem, maximum power transfer theorem, compensation theorem and Tellegen’s theorem as applied with independent and dependent ac and dc sources.

units.title: Circuit Analysis
units.text: Circuit Analysis Introduction to graph theory, tree, link currents, branch voltages, cut set and tie set, duality.

units.title: Transient and Steady State Analysis of Circuits using Classical Technique

units.title: Transient and Steady State Response of Circuits using Laplace Transform
units.text: Transient and Steady State Response of Circuits using Laplace Transform Circuit analysis using Laplace transform, transfer function, concept of poles and zeros of emittance functions and their properties, sinusoidal response from pole-zero locations.

units.title: Network functions and Two - port Networks
units.text: Network functions and Two - port Networks Concept of two- port network, driving point and transfer functions, open circuit impedance (Z) parameters, short circuit admittance (Y) parameters, transmission (ABCD) parameters, inverse transmission (A’B’C’D’) parameters, hybrid (h) parameters, inter relationships of different parameters, t and pi representation, terminated two - port networks.

outcomes.text: Illustrate the fundamental concepts of signals and systems, including classification and operations on signals.
Explain the properties of Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems and apply convolution techniques.
Illustrate the Fourier series representation of periodic signals, analyze their magnitude, and phase spectra.
Utilize Fourier and Laplace transforms, their properties for system analysis applications.

demonstrate the ability to understand concepts in abstract algebra , complex variables and conformal mapping.
solve problems based on combinatorics, graph theory, group theory differentiation and integration of functions of complex variables.

Design and analyze combinational circuits.
Design and analyze sequential circuits.
Implement HDL & appropriate EDA tools for basic digital logic.

outcomes.text: Describe the principles and concepts of different analog & digital modulation techniques.
Implement different base band shaping techniques for data transmission and detection.
Analyze different algorithms for source and error control coding.
Describe the concepts and applications of spread spectrum modulation.

program: B Tech (EXTC)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Engineering Mathematics, Circuits and Network Technology, Signals and Systems.
objectives: This course aims to acquaint students with the fundamentals of the Basics theory of process and control systems and System stability. It also helps to analyse and design the system for fulfilling the performance and stability criterion.

outcomes.text: Describe the modelling of linear-time-invariant systems using transfer function and state space representations

Design simple feedback controllers
Analyse the state space variable and models

units.title: Introduction to control problem

program: B Tech (EXTC)
prerequisites: Signals and Systems, Probability and Stochastic Processes
objectives: The aim of this course is to provide knowledge of the basic elements of various types of Analog & digital modulation and demodulation techniques. This course also makes student acquainted with different types of coding, decoding and spread spectrum techniques.

outcomes.text: Describe the principles and concepts of different analog & digital modulation techniques.
Implement different base band shaping techniques for data transmission and detection.
Analyze different algorithms for source and error control coding.
Describe the concepts and applications of spread spectrum modulation.

Multiplexing: Principles of Time Division Multiplexing (TDM), Frequency Division Multiplexing (FDM).

units.title: Waveform coding techniques

units.title: Digital Modulation Techniques
