program: B Tech (EXTC)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Electronic Devices and circuits
objectives: This course aims to acquaint students with the fundamentals of the ac small signal models of BJT and JFET amplifier and the designing of BJT, JFET, power supplies and oscillator circuits. This course also helps to understand and analyze negative feedback amplifiers, Power Amplifier and various Op-amp applications.

outcomes.text: Design and model different types of BJT and FET circuits
Analyze the designing process of power supply and oscillator circuits
Examine the performance of different types of feedback amplifiers, Power Amplifier and Op- amp linear and non-linear application
Apply various circuit design tools for designing of amplifiers circuits

units.title: Modeling and designing of BJT Amplifier
units.text: Modeling and designing of BJT Amplifier Different types of BJTs, Small signal and large signal models, Behavior of transistor at high frequencies, High frequency hybrid π CE amplifier model, Rating and specifications of BJT from datasheet. Design of single stage transistor amplifier, Design of multistage amplifier, Use of tools in design of amplifiers.

units.title: Modeling and designing of FET Amplifier
units.text: Modeling and designing of FET Amplifier Small signal JFET models for CS, CD and CG amplifiers, Rating and specifications of JFET from datasheet. Design of single stage and multistage JFET amplifier – designing with zero temperature drift, designing with midpoint biasing and designing with variation in parameters.

units.title: Power Supply Circuit Analysis and Design
units.text: Power Supply Circuit Analysis and Design Design of Rectifier Circuits and Filters (all types). Study of Linear regulators, Transistorized series regulator, Regulator with error amplifier.

units.title: Negative Feedback Amplifier
units.text: Negative Feedback Amplifier Introduction to Feed Back, Basic Feedback Concepts, Ideal Close–Loop Gain, Gain Sensitivity Bandwidth Extension, Noise Sensitivity, Reduction of Nonlinear Distortion, Ideal Feedback Topologies, Voltage Series, Voltage Shunt, No Change Current Series and Current Shunt Feedback Amplifiers, Effect of Negative Feedback on Various Performance Parameters of an Amplifier, Analysis of each Topology.

units.title: Oscillator Circuit Analysis and Design
units.text: Oscillator Circuit Analysis and Design Design of Phase-Shift Oscillator, Wien-bridge Oscillator, Colpitts Oscillator, Hartley Oscillator, Crystal Oscillator.

units.title: Introduction to Op-amp (Linear and Non-linear applications of Op-amp)
units.text: Introduction to Op-amp (Linear and Non-linear applications of Op-amp). Ideal characteristics of Op-amp, Inverting, Non Inverting, Summing, Subtractor, Instrumentation amplifier, Integrator and differentiator, Precision Rectifier, Square Waveform Generation, Zero crossing detector, Schmitt trigger, Active filters, sample and hold circuit and Peak Detector circuits

units.title: Classification of Power Amplifiers
units.text: Classification of Power Amplifiers Class A, Class B, Class AB and Class C operation, and performance parameter comparisons. Single-ended Transformer Coupled Stage, Class A Amplifier, Class B Push-pull, Complementary Symmetry Output Stage, Class AB Push-pull stage and Power Transistors.

text_books: 1. Donald A. Neamen, Electronic Circuit Analysis and Design, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill International, 2006. 2. B. P. Singh, Rekha Singh, Electronic Devices & Integrated Circuits, 1st Edition, Pearson Education, 2009.
reference_books: 1. David A. Bell, Electronic Devices & Circuits, 5th Edition, Oxford Publication, 2008. 2. Donald Schilling & Charles Belove, Electronic Circuits Discrete and Integrated, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill International, 1989. 3. Martin Roden, Gordon Carpenter, William Wieserman, Electronic Design, 4th Edition, Shroff Publishers, 2002.

program: B Tech (EXTC)
objectives: The course stresses on the programming and interfacing aspects of microprocessor and microcontroller and covers the integrated approach of 8-bit microcontrollers and its interfacing with different devices. It further provides an insight on advanced microcontroller’s architecture.

outcomes.text: Understand the architectural design of 8086 along with its feature
Create assembly language programs using 8086 microprocessor
Understand the microcontroller architecture (8/32 bit) and its programming
Design microcontroller based system for real time applications

units.title: Introduction and Hardware of 8051 Microcontrollers
units.text: Introduction and Hardware of 8051 Microcontrollers Comparison of microprocessor and microcontroller, architecture and pin functions of 8051 chip controller, CPU timing and machine cycles, internal memory organization, program counter and stack, input/output ports, counters and timers, serial data input and output interrupts.

units.title: 8051 Assemble language programming
units.text: 8051 Assemble language programming Introduction to 8051 Assembly programming, Data Types and directives, 8051 flag bits and PSW register. Register banks and stack. Jump loop and call instructions, I/O Port programming: Addressing modes and accessing memory using various addressing modes. Arithmetic instructions and programs, Logic instructions and programs, memory and Timer/counters of 8051.

units.title: Microcontroller Design and Interfacing
units.text: Microcontroller Design and Interfacing Serial communication, 8051 connection to RS 232 and its programming, Interfacing of microcontroller to LCD, ADC and DAC, 4*4Keyboard, and stepper motor. No Change

units.title: Intel 8086/8088 microprocessor family
units.text: Intel 8086/8088 microprocessor family:- Introduction Feature of 8086Architecture and programming model of 8086, Min and Max Mode Timing diagram of 8086, 8288 bus controller. Hardware software and program generated interrupts in 8086, Response to interrupt, Interrupt vector Table, Block diagram of 8259 Priority Interrupt Controller.

units.title: Programming of 8086
units.text: Programming of 8086 Introduction, Addressing Modes, Instruction sets of 8086, Assembly language programming, Assembler Directive, Passing parameter to Procedure and Macro. Introduction 8255A Programmable peripheral interface and its programming, Study of architecture of 8087 and its data types.

units.title: Introduction to advanced Microcontroller
units.text: Introduction to advanced Microcontroller Introduction of 32-bit microcontrollers (ARM7), its architecture, Registers model, Current Program and Status program Register, ARM Pipeline and its stages.

units.title: Programming of ARM 7
units.text: Programming of ARM 7 Interfacing and programming using LPC 21XX/22XX series (2148/2294) with IO peripherals such as LED, LCD, ADC, DAC, RTC and Keyboard interface with the help of timers and serial communication ports such as SPI, I2C, UART etc.

text_books: 1. Muhammad Ali Mazidi, Microcontroller & Embedded system, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall, 2011. 2. Douglas Hall, Microprocessors Interfacing and Programming, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2006. 3. Andrew Sloss, Dominic Symes, and Chris Wright, ARM System Developer’s Guide, 1st Edition, Morgan Kaufmann Publishers, 2004. 4. LPC 2148 and LPC 2294 data sheet form Philips semiconductor.
reference_books: 1. Kenneth Ayala(2012),The 8051 Microcontroller, 3rd Edition, CENGAGE Learning. 2. MykePredko, “Programming and customizing the 8051 Microcontroller”, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2008. 3. Badri Ram, “Advanced Microprocessors and Interfacing”, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2011.

program: B Tech (Computer Engineering, CSBS)
prerequisites: Knowledge of all core and elective courses completed till semester VII.
objectives: This course provides a culminating design experience to the final-year students’ learning with essentially required hands-on experience to ensure that they graduate with the required practical and soft skills. It aims to expose the students to the entire product development life cycle starting from literature review, feasibility study, analysis, design, development and validation so as to enhance the technical skill sets in the chosen field. The course also provides an opportunity to the students for the development of their academic skills and logical thinking, oral communication skills, teamwork and planning.

outcomes.text: Analyze existing literature and industry trends to identify research gaps or practical issues and formulate a well-defined problem statement that addresses both academic and industry needs.
Apply theoretical knowledge and engineering principles to develop feasible design models ensuring both innovation and real word applicability.
Create prototype/ proof-of-concept to test and validate the solutions through real-word data analysis.
Demonstrate the ability to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams, showing leadership, communication, and project management skills.
Compile finding into detail technical report and present result effectively to both academic and industry stakeholders, showcasing the impact and practical applicability of the project.

units.title: Programming of ARM 7
units.text: Programming of ARM 7 Interfacing and programming using LPC 21XX/22XX series (2148/2294) with IO peripherals such as LED, LCD, ADC, DAC, RTC and Keyboard interface with the help of timers and serial communication ports such as SPI, I2C, UART etc.

text_books: 1. Muhammad Ali Mazidi, Microcontroller & Embedded system, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall, 2011. 2. Douglas Hall, Microprocessors Interfacing and Programming, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2006. 3. Andrew Sloss, Dominic Symes, and Chris Wright, ARM System Developer’s Guide, 1st Edition, Morgan Kaufmann Publishers, 2004. 4. LPC 2148 and LPC 2294 data sheet form Philips semiconductor.
reference_books: 1. Kenneth Ayala(2012),The 8051 Microcontroller, 3rd Edition, CENGAGE Learning. 2. MykePredko, “Programming and customizing the 8051 Microcontroller”, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2008. 3. Badri Ram, “Advanced Microprocessors and Interfacing”, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2011.

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)
objectives: To provide knowledge about various component and functional blocks of digital computer architecture. Learning of Computer arithmetic, Memory organization, I/O interface, Instruction set and Multi-processor architecture.

outcomes.text: Explain various functional blocks and their interactions in computer architecture
Explain Memory operations and their types
Describe Computer Arithmetic and characteristics of Instruction Set with respect to internal architecture
Describe operations of I/O interfacing and Multiprocessor architecture.

units.title: Computer architectural Evolution and History
units.text: Computer architectural Evolution and History: Generations of computer and evolutions in terms of various technical aspects, major landmarks in history, future view of architecture.

units.title: Basic blocks and processes in computer
units.text: Basic blocks and processes in computer: Block level description of the functional units inside CPU and their interactions to execute program fetch, decode and execution cycle, performance evaluation of computer architecture.

units.title: Memory architecture
units.text: Memory architecture: Various types of memory technology, static and dynamic RAM comparison, cache memory and memory hierarchy, different types of address mapping, virtual memory concepts and operations.

units.title: Processor Architecture
units.text: Processor Architecture: Details understanding of internal functional units inside general processor, registers, buses, IO interface, ALU.

units.title: Computer Arithmetic
units.text: Computer Arithmetic: Floating-point arithmetic format and arithmetic operations.

units.title: Instruction set Characteristics and Architecture
units.text: Instruction set Characteristics and Architecture: Instruction sets, assembly language, instruction cycles, addressing modes, internal storage and data handling, interrupts handling, various types of instructions for various operations, RISC versus CISC architectures.

units.title: Input / Output systems
units.text: Input / Output systems: Interfacing with various IO interface, Programmed IO, concept of handshaking, interrupt driven and polled IO, DMA operations, types of bus and its operations, timing diagram for IO interface. Storage systems Principles of working for hard disk, RAID, cloud storage.

units.title: Multiprocessor organization
units.text: Multiprocessor organization: Pipeline processing, instruction and arithmetic pipeline concept, parallel processing.

text_books: 1. William Stallings, “Computer Organization and Architecture Designing for Performance”, Pearson Education, 11th Edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. John P. Hayes, “Computer Architecture and Organization”, Tata Mc-Graw Hill, 3rd Edition, 2012. 2. David A. Patterson and John L. Hennessy, “Computer Organization and Design The Hardware/Software interface”, Elsevier, 6th Edition, 2017.

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)
objectives: Enable students to understand linear data structures, implement them to utilize computer memory efficiently. Also to understand searching and sorting algorithms to solve real-life problems.

outcomes.text: Comprehend data structures and implement stacks and queues
Use linked list to solve real life problem statements
Solve real life problem statements using searching and sorting algorithms.

units.title: Introduction to Data Structures
units.text: Introduction to Data Structures: Basic data types, data structure definition, need for data structures, elementary data structure organization, classification of data structures, operations on data structures, abstract data type.

units.title: Linear Data Structure I Arrays and Stacks
units.text: Linear Data Structure I Arrays and Stacks: Introduction, declaration of arrays, operations on arrays. introduction to stacks, array representation of stacks, operations of a stack, push, pop, peek, stack overflow and stack underflow, applications of a stack reversing a list, decimal to binary conversion using stack, conversion and evaluation of arithmetic expression, recursion, tower of Hanoi.

units.title: Linear Data Structure II Queues
units.text: Linear Data Structure II Queues: Introduction to queues, array representation of queues, queue operations insertion, deletion, queue overflow, queue underflow, circular queues, priority queues, applications of queues.

units.title: Linear Data Structure III Linked List
units.text: Linear Data Structure III Linked List: Introduction, basic terminologies, linked list versus arrays, dynamic memory allocation and deallocation for a linked list, types of linked lists singly linked list, doubly linked list, operations of linked list, traversing a linked list, applications of linked lists.

units.title: Searching and Sorting
units.text: Searching and Sorting: Basic searching techniques sequential search, binary search, sorting definitions, selection sort, insertion sort, radix sort, hashing and collision resolution techniques.

text_books: 1. Y. Langsam, M.J. Augenstein, A.M. Tenenbaum, “Data Structures using C and C++”, PHI publication, 2nd Edition, 2015. 2. Seymour Lipschutz, “Data structures with C”, Schaum’s Outlines, 1st Edition, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Mark Allen Weiss, “Data Structures and Algorithm analysis in C++”, PHI publication, 4th Edition, 2013. 2. Reema Thareja, “Data Structures using C”, Oxford University Press, Tata McGraw Hill, 2nd Edition, 2014.

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)
objectives: The objective of the course is to present an introduction to database management systems, with an emphasis on how to organize, maintain and retrieve - efficiently, and effectively - information from a DBMS.

outcomes.text: Describe core concepts of database and model a database management system through ER modelling
Apply knowledge of relational algebra and structural query language to retrieve and manage data from relational database
Design database by applying principles of normalization and including integrity constraints
Discover importance of indexing, transaction management, concurrency and recovery in database management system.

units.title: Introduction to Database concepts
units.text: Introduction to Database concepts: Introduction to data processing overview of files systems, drawback of file systems, purpose of database system, concept of a database, database system vs file system, view of data, data models, database users and administrator.

units.title: Entity Relationship Model
units.text: Entity Relationship Model: Overview of design process, the entity- relationship model, constraints, ER diagram, and reduction to relational schemas, entity-relationship design issues, extended ER features.

units.title: Relational Model
units.text: Relational Model: Concept of relation, notion of primary and secondary keys, foreign keys, structure of relational database, relational algebra and extended relational algebra operations, formation of queries, modification of the database views.

units.title: Structured Query Language (SQL)
units.text: Structured Query Language (SQL): Background, basic structure, set operations, aggregate functions, NULL values, nested queries, views, complex queries, database modification, DDL, embedded SQL, stored procedures and functions, dynamic SQL featured.

units.title: Integrity and Security
units.text: Integrity and Security: Domain constrains, referential integrity, assertions, triggers and assertions in SQL, security and authorization in SQL.

units.title: Relational Database Design
units.text: Relational Database Design: Features of good relational database design, atomic domains and first normal form, decomposition using functional dependencies, functional dependency theory, normalization, decomposition, first normal to fifth normal forms, BCNF, pitfall in relational-database design, indexing and hashing, basic concepts, ordered indices – dense, sparse index, multilevel indices, static hashing, dynamic hashing.

units.title: Transactions
units.text: Transactions: Basic concept of transaction, state of a transaction, implementation of atomicity and durability, concurrent executions, serializability, recoverability, implementation of isolation, transaction in SQL.

units.title: Concurrency
units.text: Concurrency Control and Recovery: Lock based protocols, timestamp-based protocols, validation-based protocols, deadlock handling, recovery and atomicity, log-based recovery.

text_books: 1. Hennery Korth and Abraham Silberschatz, “Database System Concepts”, McGraw Hill, 7th Edition, 2019
reference_books: 1. Elmarsi and Navathe, “Fundamentals of Database Design”, Addison Wesley 7th Edition, 2019. 2. Bob Bryla, Kevin Loney “Oracle Database 12C The Complete Reference”, Tata McGraw Hill, 2017.

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)
objectives: To enable the students understand the advantage of using Object Oriented programming over procedural programming to tackle complex real word programming problems. The course focuses on the understanding and developing a practical mastery on object- oriented concepts.

outcomes.text: Describe and implement the Classes and relevant methods to solve a given problem
Design solutions for a given problem using the concepts of Abstraction, Polymorphism, Encapsulation & Inheritance in OOP paradigm
Solve a real-world problem by designing and implementing Class diagrams.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Review of object orientation, class and objects, primitive object types.

units.title: Strings and Arrays
units.text: Strings and Arrays: Strings, string buffer, arrays, vectors, operators, loop control, decision making.

units.title: Object Oriented Systems
units.text: Object Oriented Systems: Encapsulation, constructors, inheritance, polymorphism (overloading, over riding).

units.title: Exception Handling
units.text: Exception Handling: Pre defined exceptions, try-catch-finally, throws, throw, and user-defined exception.

units.title: IO Streams
units.text: IO Streams: Byte-oriented streams, character – oriented streams, file handling.

units.title: Abstract Class, Interfaces
units.text: Abstract Class, Interfaces: Abstract classes, interface, inner classes, wrapper classes.

units.title: Modelling Classes
units.text: Modelling Classes: UML class diagram, associations and multiplicity, generalization, process of developing class diagrams, implementing class diagrams in object oriented programming language.

text_books: 1. Y. Daniel Liang, “Introduction to Java Programming”, Comprehensive Version, Global Edition, Pearson Education, 11th Edition 2019. 2. Herbert Schildt, “Java 2 The Complete Reference”, McGraw-Hill Education, 11th Edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. Herbert Schildt, “Java A Beginner’s Guide”, McGraw-Hill Education, 8th Edition, 2020. 2. Cay S. Horstmann, “Core Java Volume I—Fundamentals”, Pearson, 11th Edition, 2018.

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)
objectives: To provide basic knowledge of logic circuits theory, elementary analysis and its implementation in practical applications. Study of Boolean algebra and K-map techniques to design combinational and sequential logic circuits for solving digital logic design problems.

outcomes.text: Explain different number systems and their conversions
Use Boolean algebra and K-map to simplify logic functions
Design and implement combinational logic circuits
Design and implement sequential logic circuits.

units.title: Number Systems
units.text: Number Systems: Decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal number system and conversion, binary codes, 1's and 2's complement codes, binary arithmetic.

units.title: Boolean Algebra
units.text: Boolean Algebra: Binary logic functions, Boolean laws, truth tables, associative and distributive properties, De Morgan’s theorems, universal gates, realization of switching functions using logic gates.

units.title: Simplification of Boolean Functions
units.text: Simplification of Boolean Functions: Canonical and standard forms, sum of product & product of sum, minimization of functions using karnaugh maps - two, three and four variable, don’t care conditions.

units.title: Analysis and Design of Combinational Circuits
units.text: Analysis and Design of Combinational Circuits: Analyzing a combinational circuit, code conversion, decoder, encoder, priority encoder, multiplexers, de-multiplexers, binary adder, subtractor, magnitude comparator.

units.title: Combinational Circuits using Programmable Logic Devices (PLDs)
units.text: Combinational Circuits using Programmable Logic Devices (PLDs): Programmable logic devices, programmable logic arrays and programmable array logic.

units.title: Analysis and Design of Sequential Circuits
units.text: Analysis and Design of Sequential Circuits: Flip-flops-RS, JK, T and D, clocked and edge triggered flip-flops, characteristic table, characteristic equation, excitation table, state table, and state transition diagram.

units.title: Sequential Circuits
units.text: Sequential Circuits: Registers, shift registers (SISO, SIPO, PISO, PIPO), counters, ripple and synchronous counters, modulo counters, ring and Johnson counters, timing specifications and counter design.

text_books: 1. M. Morris Mano, "Digital Design", Pearson Education India, 6th Edition, 2018. 2. R. P. Jain, "Modern Digital Electronics", McGraw Hill Education, 4th Edition, 2016.
reference_books: 1. Thomas L. Floyd “Digital Fundamentals”, Pearson Education India, 11th Edition, 2018. 2. A. B. Marcovitz, “Introduction to Logic Design”, Tata McGraw Hill Education, 3rd Edition, 2010.

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)
prerequisites: Linear Algebra and Ordinary Differential Equations
objectives: The principal objective of the course is to train the students in the construction and understanding of mathematical proofs and common mathematical arguments. It will instil sound knowledge of different topics of discrete mathematics which students will readily apply in the subsequent courses of their programme.

outcomes.text: define and relate basic notions of discrete mathematics.
demonstrate the ability to understand mathematical logic, concepts in abstract algebra and mathematical proof techniques.
solve problems based on combinatorics, graph theory and abstract algebra.
demonstrate understanding of the applications of algebra, combinatorics and graph theory.

units.title: Set Theory, Relations and Functions
units.text: Set Theory, Relations and Functions Revision of prerequisite concepts - ‘ Sets, Venn diagrams, Operations on sets, Laws of set theory’. Power set, The principle of Inclusion-Exclusion, Partitions of sets. Relations, Properties and types of binary relations, Equivalence relation. Functions, injective, surjective and bijective functions, Composition, inverse of a function.

units.title: Logic
units.text: Logic Revision of prerequisite concepts – ‘Propositions, Truth table, Laws of logic, Equivalence’. Satisfiability, tautology, validity, disjunctive and conjunctive normal forms, Predicates and Quantifiers, Proof Techniques, Mathematical Induction.

units.title: Combinatorics
units.text: Combinatorics Pigeonhole principle, Homogeneous and non-homogeneous linear recurrence relations with constant coefficients, Generating functions.

units.title: Graphs and Trees
units.text: Graphs and Trees Graphs and their properties, Degree, Connectivity, Path, Cycle, Eulerian graph, Hamiltonian graph, Planar graphs, Graph Coloring. Trees, Rooted trees, Spanning tree and minimum spanning tree, Kruskal’s and Prim’s algorithms for minimal spanning trees.

units.title: Abstract algebra
units.text: Abstract algebra Definition and examples of groups, subgroups, cyclic groups, group homomorphism, group isomorphisms. Definitions and Examples of Rings and Fields.

text_books: 1. Kenneth H. Rosen , “Discrete Mathematics and its Applications”, Tata McGraw Hill, 8th edition 2018. 2. Kolman, Busby and Ross, “Discrete Mathematical Structures”, Prentice Hall India, 6th edition 2015.
reference_books: 1. C. L. Liu, “Elements of Discrete Mathematics” McGraw Hill, New Delhi, 4th edition 2017. 2. Seymour Lipschutz and Mark Lipson, “Discrete Mathematics”, McGraw Hill education, Schaum’s Outline Series, Revised 3rd edition 2017. 3. I. N. Herstein , “Topics in Algebra”, John Wiley and Sons, 2nd edition 1975. 4. Narsingh Deo, Graph theory with Applications to Engineering and computer science, Prentice Hall India, 1st edition 2016.

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)
objectives: 1. To inculcate human values to grow as a responsible human being 2. To maintain ethical conduct in discharging professional duties

outcomes.text: understand the engineering code of ethics and be able to apply them as necessary
understand moral complexities in many engineering activities and decision-making processes
understand some of the contemporary issues in the engineering professions
effectively communicate their knowledge and understanding of engineering ethics.

units.text: Introduction to Ethics-  Concept of morals and ethics,  Study of engineering ethics;  Laws and ethics;  Personal and professional ethics.
Professional Practice in Engineering-  Common morality ASME code of ethics,  Technical codes and standards,  Accepted standards of Engineering practice and the standard of care.

Ethics as design-doing justice to moral Problem-  Discuss about ethics as a design to solve moral problems  Comparison between moral problems and engineering design problems;  Moral lessons from design problems;  Implications of the dynamic character of problem situations.

Rights and Responsibilities of Engineers-  Moral responsibilities;  Conflicts of interests;  Confidentiality,  Engineers, organizations and ethics,  Engineer-manager relationships;  loyalty;  The concept of whistleblowing.

Responsibility for the Environment-  Rapid Technological growth and depletion of resources,  Reports of the Club of Rome.  Limits of growth: sustainable development  Energy Crisis: Renewable Energy Resources  Environmental degradation and pollution.  Eco-friendly Technologies.  Environmental Regulations,  Environmental Ethics  Appropriate Technology,  Movement of Schumacher; later developments of Technology and developing notions.  Problems of Technology transfer,  Technology assessment impact analysis.  Problems of man, machine, interaction,  Impact of assembly line and automation.  Human centered Technology

text_books: 1. M.W. Martin and R. Schinzinger, “Ethics in Engineering”, McGraw-Hill, Second Edition, 2005. 2. Charles B. Fleddermann, “Engineering Ethics”, Pearson, Third Edition, 2007. 3. P.A. Vesilind and A. S Gunn, “Engineering Ethics and Environment”, Cambridge University Press, First Edition, 1998.
reference_books: 1. Caroline Whitbeck, “Ethics in Engineering – Practice and Research”, Cambridge University Press, Second Edition, 2011.

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics
objectives: This course aims to understand the multidisciplinary nature of environmental sciences, greenhouse effect and climate change. It also aims to discuss the basics of natural resources, biodiversity, environmental pollution.

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of natural resources, ecosystem and biodiversity
Relate the various aspects of environmental pollutions with its cause and effect
Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change.

units.title: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science
units.text: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science Definition, scope and importance of environmental sciences.

Natural Resources • Natural resources: Forest resources, Water resources, Mineral resources, Food resources. • Energy resources: Growing energy needs, renewable and non- renewable energy sources, use of alternate energy sources.

Ecosystems • Concept of an ecosystem. • Structure and function of an ecosystem. • Food chains, food webs and ecological pyramids. • Introduction, types, characteristic features of the following ecosystem:- a. Forest ecosystem b. Grassland ecosystem c. Desert ecosystem d. Aquatic ecosystems.

Biodiversity • Definition: genetic, species and ecosystem diversity. • Value of biodiversity: consumptive use, productive use. • Threats to biodiversity: habitat loss, poaching of wildlife, man- wildlife conflicts.

Environmental Pollution • Definition, Cause and effects for Air pollution, Water pollution, Soil pollution, Marine pollution, Noise pollution, Thermal pollution, Nuclear hazards and Solid waste pollution.
The Science of Climate Change • Greenhouse effect • Global warming • Global environmental changes • Acid rain • Ozone layer depletion • Carbon footprint

text_books: 1. Erach Bharucha, “Textbook of Environmental Studies”, University Press, 2nd Edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. MP Poonia & SC Sharma, “Environmental Studies”, Khanna Publishing House, 1st Edition, 2017. 2. Rajagopalan, “Environmental Studies”, Oxford University Press, Third Edition, 2015.

program: B. Tech Information Technology
objectives: This course aims to instill in students a sound knowledge of probability theory and statistical techniques. It equips the students with intermediate to advanced level concepts and tools in probability and statistics that help them tackle relevant problems within engineering domain.

outcomes.text: solve problems involving random variables, probability distributions and testing of hypothesis, correlation and regression
identify suitable probability distribution and testing techniques to solve related problems
apply knowledge of random variables, probability distributions, measures of central tendency, correlation and regression to solve real life problems
analyse data samples using statistical methods.

units.title: Basic Probability
units.text: Basic Probability Probability spaces, conditional probability, independence; Bayes theorem.

units.title: Random variables and Probability Distributions
units.text: Random variables and Probability Distributions Discrete random variables, probability mass function, cumulative distribution function, Independent random variables, Continuous random variables, distribution functions and densities, expectation, variance, raw and central moments of random variables, Binomial distribution, Poisson approximation to the binomial distribution, Normal distribution.

units.title: Bivariate Distributions
units.text: Bivariate Distributions Definition of Bivariate Distribution and their properties, Conditional densities.

units.title: Basic Statistics
units.text: Basic Statistics Measures of Central tendency; Moments, Moment generating function, skewness, kurtosis. Mean and variance of Binomial distribution & Poisson distribution, Moments, skewness & kurtosis for Normal distribution.

units.title: Testing of hypothesis
units.text: Testing of hypothesis: Point estimation, Interval estimate and Confidence interval, Criteria for good estimates, Null and Alternate hypothesis, Test Statistic, Type I and Type II errors, One-tailed and two-tailed test, Critical region, Large sample statistical test for mean, Large sample statistical test for proportion, t-test for small samples, Test for variance- F test, Chi-square test for Goodness of fit and independence of attributes, Analysis of variance.

units.title: Linear Statistical Models
units.text: Linear Statistical Models: Scatter diagram, Linear regression and correlation, Least squares method, Rank correlation, Multiple regression.

text_books: 1. Veerarajan T, “Probability, Statistics and Random Processes”, McGraw hill Education, 4th Edition, 2017. 2. S. Ross , “A First Course in Probability”, Pearson Education India, 9th Edition, 2013.
reference_books: 1. W. Feller , “An Introduction to Probability Theory and its Applications”,Vol.1, John Wiley & Sons, 3rd Edition, 2017. 2. Devore, “Probability and Statistics for Engineering and Sciences”, Cengage Learning, 2nd Indian Edition, 2009. 3. Irwin Miller, John E. Freund and R.A. Johnson, “Probability & Statistics for Enginees”, Pearson Education India, 8th Edition, 2015. 4. S.C. Gupta, V. K. Kapoor, “Fundamentals of Mathematical Statistics”, Sultan Chand & Sons, 12th Edition, 2014. 5. Murray R. Spiegel, John J. Schiller, R. Alu Srinivasn, “Probability and Statistics, McGraw Hill Education, 4th edition, 2013. Details of Internal Continuous Assessment (ICA)

program: B. Tech Information Technology
objectives: The aim of this course is to provide an understanding of the fundamental characteristics of signals and systems from the perspective of both the time and transform domains. The course will help the student to develop the mathematical skills needed to analyze continuous and discrete time signals and systems in both the domains.

outcomes.text: Classify continuous time and discrete time signals and systems
Apply various mathematical operations to analyze signals and systems
Analyze continuous time signals and systems using various transforms
Determine the frequency spectrum of continuous and discrete time signals and systems.

units.title: Introduction to Signals and Systems
units.text: Introduction to Signals and Systems: Signals- definitions, classification, operations and elementary signals. System and its classification - discrete and continuous time signals and systems.

units.title: LTI System and Classification
units.text: LTI System and Classification Time domain representations for linear time-invariant systems, convolution integral and convolution sum, impulse response representation for LTI systems, interconnection of systems, series, parallel and mixed, differential and difference equation representations for LTI systems.

units.title: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Signals
units.text: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Signals: Different types of Fourier series representation and interconnection between exponential and trigonometric Fourier series, Fourier series representation of continuous time periodic signal, magnitude and phase spectrum, Fourier series representation of discrete time periodic signal and its spectrum.

units.title: Fourier Transform
units.text: Fourier Transform Development of Fourier transform from Fourier series, frequency spectrum using Fourier transform, properties of Fourier transform - linearity property, change of scale property, shifting property, inverse Fourier transform.

units.title: Laplace Transform
units.text: Laplace Transform Limitations of Fourier transform, introduction to Laplace transform, ROC and its properties, Laplace transform of elementary signals, unilateral Laplace transform, inverse Laplace transform.

units.title: Z Transform
units.text: Z Transform Introduction to Z transform, Z transform of elementary signals, ROC, properties of Z transform, inverse of Z transform using partial fraction and long division rule, solution of difference equation.

text_books: 1. Tarun Kumar Rawat, “Signals and Systems”, Oxford University Press, 1st edition 2010. 2. Nagoor Kani, “Signals and Systems”, McGraw-Hill, 1st edition, 2010.
reference_books: 1. Oppenheim and Willsky,” Signals and Systems”, Prentice Hall of India, 2nd edition, 2016. 2. Simon Haykin and Barry Van Veen, “Signals and Systems”, John Wiley, 2nd edition, 2008.

program: B. Tech Information Technology
prerequisites: Computer Organization & Architecture, Programming for Problem Solving.
objectives: To present an introduction to Operating Systems, with an emphasis on the policies for scheduling, deadlocks, memory management, synchronization, system calls, and file systems.

outcomes.text: Comprehend the objectives, services and different architectures of the Operating System and their types
Conduct simulation experiments on process scheduling, inter-process communication, deadlock avoidance of system by using different algorithms
Implement and evaluate the various memory management techniques provided by the OS to improve the overall system performance
Comprehend the techniques to manage files & methods to access different storage devices.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Concept of operating systems, generations of operating systems, types of operating Systems, OS Services, system calls, structure of an OS.

units.title: Processes
units.text: Processes: Definition, process relationship, different states of a process, process state transitions, process control block (PCB), context switching Thread definition, various states, benefits of threads, types of threads, concept of multithreads. Process Scheduling: Foundation and scheduling objectives, types of schedulers, scheduling criteria CPU utilization, throughput, turnaround time, waiting time, response time, scheduling algorithms- pre-emptive and non-pre-emptive, FCFS, SJF and RR.

units.title: Inter-process Communication
units.text: Inter-process Communication: Critical section, race conditions, mutual exclusion, Peterson’s solution, semaphores, monitors. Classical IPC Problems: Reader’s & writer problem.

units.title: Deadlocks
units.text: Deadlocks: Definition, necessary and sufficient conditions for deadlock, deadlock prevention, deadlock avoidance, banker’s algorithm, deadlock detection and recovery.

units.title: Memory Management
units.text: Memory Management: Basic concept, logical and physical address map, memory allocation- contiguous memory allocation – fixed and variable partition– internal and external fragmentation and compaction. Paging: Principle of operation – page allocation – hardware support for paging, protection and sharing, disadvantages of paging.

units.title: I/O Hardware
units.text: I/O Hardware: I/O devices, device controllers, direct memory access principles of I/O software- goals of interrupt handlers, device drivers, device independent I/O software. File Management: Overview, file organization, file directories, file sharing and record blocking.

text_books: 1. Achyut S. Godbole and Atul Kahate, “Operating Systems”, McGraw-Hill, 3rd Edition, 2017. 2. William Stallings, “Operating Systems Internals and Design Principles”, Pearson Education, 9th Edition, 2018.
reference_books: 1. Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin and Greg Gagne, “Operating System Concepts”, Wiley, 9th Edition, 2018. 2. Ann McHoes and Ida M. Flynn, “Understanding Operating Systems”, Course Technology, 5th Edition, 2013.

program: B. Tech Information Technology
objectives: This is an introductory course in computer networks. The course is designed to enable students to understand and analyze the protocols, and applications of computer networks. The objective is to learn how computer networks work today and the basics of its architecture. Course Outcomes After completion of this course, students will be able to- 1. Describe the function of different network models, associated protocols and standards, 2. Compare different transmission media, and understand error detection and correction techniques, 3. Analyze medium access control algorithms, and network layer error control, flow control, and routing algorithms, 4. Describe transport layer congestion control techniques, application layer protocols and basic security concepts.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Introduction to computer networks, classification of computer networks, topology, layering and protocol, OSI reference model, TCP/IP model, networking devices, performance issues (bandwidth, latency, delay etc.).

units.title: Application Layer
units.text: Application Layer: DNS, E-mail (working of email transfer and delivery), WWW (Architectural overview), WWW (Architectural overview).

units.title: Transport Layer
units.text: Transport Layer: Transport layer services, elements of transport layer, UDP and TCP (Tahoe, Reno).

units.title: Network layer
units.text: Network layer: Forwarding and routing, virtual circuit and datagram networks, router internals, routing algorithms - (optimality principle, shortest path routing, flooding, distance vector routing, link state routing, IPv4 and IPv6 overview).

units.title: Medium access control sublayer
units.text: Medium access control sublayer: Channel allocation problem, random access protocol (ALOHA, Carrier Sense Multiple Access (CSMA), Carrier Sense Multiple Access Collision Detection – (CSMA/CD), controlled access (reservation, polling, token passing), channelization (FDMA, TDMA, CDMA), Ethernet overview and binary exponential back off.

units.title: Data Link Layer
units.text: Data Link Layer: Data link layer design issues (services provided to network layer, framing, error control and flow control), error detection and correction techniques (parity checks, check-summing methods, CRC, Hamming code), reliable transmission (stop and wait, sliding window protocol with its variants).

units.title: Physical Layer and media
units.text: Physical Layer and media: Analog and digital signals, transmission impairment, data rate limits, guided media and unguided media.

units.title: Network Security
units.text: Network Security: Cryptography- introduction, substitution ciphers, transposition ciphers, one time pads, symmetric key algorithm, and public key algorithm.

text_books: 1. James F. Kurose, Keith W. Ross, “Computer Networking A Top Down Approach”, Pearson Education, 7th Edition, 2017. 2. Behrouz A Forouzan, Firouz Mosharraf, “Computer Networks A Top Down Approach”, TMH, 6th Edition, 2012.
reference_books: 1. Behrouz A. Forouzan, “Data Communications and Networking”, McGraw-Hill, 5th Edition, 2013. 2. Larry L. Peterson, Bruce S. Davie, “Computer Networks A systems approach”, Morgan Kaufmann Publishers, 5th Edition, 2011. 3. Andrew S. Tanenbaum, David Wetherall, “Computer Networks”, Pearson Education, 5th Edition, 2012. 4. Nader F Mir, “Computer and Communication Networks”, Pearson Education, 2nd Edition, 2014. 5. Bhushan Trivedi, “Computer Networks”, Oxford University Press, 1st Edition, 2012.

program: B. Tech Information Technology
objectives: The course objective is to familiarize with client server architecture and develop web applications using HTML5, DOM, AJAX for dynamic pages and interactivity through JavaScript, PHP scripting languages. Build database applications using open source server environment i.e. Node JS with NoSQL database i.e. MongoDB.

outcomes.text: Describe different architectural components used in web development
Apply JavaScript, HTML and CSS effectively to create interactive and dynamic websites
Employ server side scripting using PHP with MySQL for Database Connectivity
Apply Node JS to create applications.

units.title: Web Designing
units.text: Web Designing: HTML5 – form elements, input types and media elements, CSS3 - selectors, box model, backgrounds and borders, text effects, animations, multiple column layout, user interface.

units.title: Client-Side Processing
units.text: Client-Side Processing: JavaScript introduction, functions, arrays, DOM, built-in objects, regular expression, exceptions, event handling, validation- AJAX - JQuery.

units.title: Server Side Processing
units.text: Server Side Processing: PHP - operators, conditionals, looping, functions, arrays.

units.title: Database Connectivity

Analyzing data sets and creating summary reports using various data mining techniques.

units.title: Data Transformations
units.text: Data Transformations Manipulating character variables, manipulating numeric variables, manipulating numeric variables based on dates, converting variable type and using various Debugging Techniques

program: B Tech and MBA Tech IT
objectives: To provide a strong foundation of fundamental concepts in Artificial Intelligence and to enable the student to apply these techniques in applications, which involve perception, reasoning and learning.

outcomes.text: Explain the history & basic principles of AI in solutions that require problem solving
Discuss knowledge representation and apply learning techniques like Neural networks, Bayesian networks etc. in various AI problems
Analyze and design a real-world problem for implementation of NLP methods

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Overview and historical perspective, Turing test, physical symbol systems and the scope of symbolic AI, agents & its types

units.title: Problem Solving
units.text: Problem Solving Problem spaces (states, goals and operators), problem solving by search, uninformed search (breadth-first, depth-first, depth-first with iterative deepening), heuristics and informed search (hill-climbing, generic best first, A*, AO*), minimax search, alpha-beta pruning, two-player games (introduction to minimax search), constraint satisfaction (backtracking and local search methods).

units.title: Knowledge and Reasoning
units.text: Knowledge and Reasoning Building a knowledge base, propositional logic, first order logic, resolution and theorem proving.

units.title: Learning
units.text: Learning Overview of different forms of learning, learning decision trees, probabilistic learning Bayesian networks, neural networks and SVMs.

units.title: Introduction to Natural Language Processing
units.text: Introduction to Natural Language Processing Language models, n-grams, vector space models, bag of words, text classification, information retrieval, PageRank, information extraction, question answering.

text_books: 1. Dan W. Patterson, Introduction to Artificial Intelligence and Expert Systems, 1st Edition, Pearson 2. Stuart Russel and Peter Norvig, Artificial Intelligence A Modern Approach, 4th Edition, Pearson
reference_books: 1. Elaine Rich, Kevin Knigh and Shivashankar B Nair , Artificial Intelligence, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2017.

course_name: Partial Differential Equations and Laplace Transforms
program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Calculus, Linear Algebra and Ordinary Differential Equations.
objectives: This course teaches the students techniques in solving problems based on Laplace transform and Partial Differential Equations and further directs them to think mathematically and apply these techniques to solve engineering problems.

outcomes.text: use effective mathematical methods to solve partial differential equations
solve problems based on Laplace transform
apply the techniques of partial differential equations and Laplace transforms to solve real life problems.

units.title: Partial Differential Equations
units.text: Partial Differential Equations Pre-requisite: Fourier series in (c, c+2l), half range sine and cosine series. Separation of variables method to simple problems in Cartesian coordinates. Second-order linear equations and their classification, Initial & boundary value problems and solutions by separation of variables.

units.title: Applications of Partial Differential Equations
units.text: Applications of Partial Differential Equations Solution of the wave equation; Solution of one dimensional and two dimensional heat flow equation, Laplacian equation in Cartesian and polar coordinates.

units.title: Laplace transformation
units.text: Laplace transformation Definition of Laplace transform, Laplace transform of 1, , , Properties of Laplace transform: Linearity property, First and second shifting theorems of Laplace transform, Change of scale property,   ( ) n L t f t , ( ) f t L t       ,   ( ) n L f t , ( ) t L f u du        , Application: Evaluation of Integrals using Laplace Transforms. Evaluation of Inverse Laplace transform by partial fraction, Convolution theorem, by derivative, Laplace transforms of Periodic functions, Unit step functions, Dirac delta functions. Application: to solve initial and boundary value problems involving ordinary differential equations.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at developing thorough understanding of physical and mathematical principles used in mechanics. This course will help students get acquainted with the various systems of forces and the importance of center of gravity. It is designed for the students to master the concept of static equilibrium and its applications along with the development of equations of motion for rigid bodies. The topics covered are tailored to suit the requirements of an intermediate undergraduate level in engineering.

outcomes.text: Determine the resultant / equilibrant of various systems of forces
Analyse the system of forces in equilibrium
Determine the centroid and moment of inertia of a plane area
Evaluate the velocity, acceleration and displacement of a moving body along with forces developed on rigid bodies subjected to displacements and rotations.

units.title: System of forces
units.text: System of forces: Rectangular components of forces in space, moment of a force about a point, moment of a force about a given axis, resultant of general force system, Coplanar and non-coplanar force system, forces and their components, resultant of coplanar force system - concurrent forces, parallel forces, non-concurrent non-parallel system of forces, moment of force about a point, couple, Varignon’s theorem. Concept of virtual work, Principle of virtual work.

units.title: Application of system of forces and equilibrium
units.text: Application of system of forces and equilibrium Free body diagram with examples on modelling of typical supports and joints, condition for equilibrium in three and two dimensions. Friction: Limiting and non-limiting cases, Laws of friction, angle of friction, angle of repose, cone of friction, Equilibrium of bodies on rough horizontal and inclined plane, application to problems involving wedges, ladder. Belt friction, flat belts on the flat pulleys. Analysis of pin jointed plane trusses: Perfect truss, method of joints and method of section.

units.title: Centroid and moment of inertia
units.text: Centroid and moment of inertia: Centroid, moment of inertia, polar moment of inertia, and product of inertia, parallel and perpendicular axis theorem.

units.title: Kinematics of particle
units.text: Kinematics of particle: Velocity and acceleration in terms of rectangular coordinate system, rectilinear motion, motion along plane curved path, tangential and normal component of acceleration, acceleration - time, velocity- time graphs and their uses, relative velocity, projectile motion, simple harmonic motion. Kinematics of rigid bodies: Translation, pure rotation and plane motion of rigid bodies, instantaneous centre of rotation for the velocity for bodies in plane motion, link mechanisms (up to two links).

units.title: Kinetics of particles
units.text: Kinetics of particles: Newton’s laws of motion, D’Alembert’s principle, equation of dynamic equilibrium, linear motion, curvilinear motion. Kinetics of rigid bodies: D’Alembert’s principle for bodies under translational motion, rotational motion about a fixed axis and plane motion. Application to motion of bars, cylinders, spheres.

text_books: 1. Beer & Johnston, “Engineering Mechanics”, Tata McGraw Hill, 12th Edition, 2020. 2. R. C. Hibler, ‘‘Engineering Mechanics’’, Pearson Education, 14th Edition, 2017.
reference_books: 1. F. L. Singer, “Engineering Mechanics”, Harper & Raw Publication. (Classic Book), 1954. 2. D. S. Kumar, ‘‘Engineering Mechanics’’, Tata McGraw Hill, 12th Edition, 2013.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course describes the fundamentals of Thermodynamics including thermodynamic systems and properties, work and heat interactions, relationships among the thermo-physical properties, the laws of thermodynamics and applications of these basic laws in thermodynamic systems such as various thermodynamic cycles. This course will provide the essential tools required to study thermodynamic systems in Applied Thermodynamics.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental concepts of engineering thermodynamics
Analyze various flow systems, laws of thermodynamics, concept of exergy and various power cycles
Understand the properties of pure substances using steam tables and charts.

units.title: Definitions and Concepts
units.text: Definitions and Concepts: System, Property, Energy, Thermodynamic Equilibrium, Work interaction & various modes of work, Heat, State Postulate; Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics, Temperature Scale, Heat and Work Interactions

units.title: Properties of Pure substances
units.text: Properties of Pure substances: Pure substance, Phase of substances, Molecular models of matter, Phase change processes in pure substance, Graphical representation of phase change processes, Steam Table. Equation of State, van der Walls Equation of State; Law of corresponding states, Compressibility chart, Pressure-volume; Temperature-volume and Phase diagrams; Mollier diagram and Steam tables.

units.title: First Law of Thermodynamics for Non flow process
units.text: First Law of Thermodynamics for Non flow process: Application of First Law for elementary processes; First Law analysis of Non-flow processes. First Law of Thermodynamics for flow process: Application of First Law of Thermodynamics for Flow Process-Steady state, steady flow processes, throttling process; Transient Flow Processes, Charging & discharging of tanks.

units.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics
units.text: Second Law of Thermodynamics: Limitations of the First Law of Thermodynamics, Heat Engine, Heat Pump/Refrigerator. Second Law of Thermodynamics– Kelvin Planck and Clausius statements & their equivalence. Reversible & irreversible processes, Criterion of reversibility, Carnot cycle & Carnot principles.

units.title: Applications of Second Law of Thermodynamics
units.text: Applications of Second Law of Thermodynamics: Thermodynamic Temperature scale, Clausius inequality, Entropy, Calculations of entropy change, Principle of entropy increase, T-S diagram, II Law analysis of Control volume. Available energy, Availability; Second law efficiency. Thermodynamic relations.

units.title: Power Cycles
units.text: Power Cycles: Vapour Power Cycles: Rankine cycle – Ideal, Reheat and Regenerative Rankine cycles. Gas Power Cycles: Otto cycle, Diesel cycle, Dual cycle and Brayton cycle.

text_books: 1. P. K. Nag, “Engineering Thermodynamics”, Tata McGraw Hill, 6th Edition, 2008. 2. Vanwvylen & Sonntag, “Classical Thermodynamics”, Wiley Eastern, 5th Edition, 1994.
reference_books: 1. Y. Cengel and M. Boles, “Thermodynamics -An Engineering Approach”, Tata McGraw Hill, 6th Edition, 2008. 2. M. J. Moran, H. N. Shapiro, D. D. Boettner, M. B. Bailey, “Fundamentals of Engineering Thermodynamics”, John Wiley and Sons, 7th Edition, (2011).

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is aimed at detailed introduction of various key manufacturing processes such as casting, welding, forging, rolling, extrusion, drawing and machining. The course has been structured to impart the in-depth understanding of industrial applications of various processes and equipment used in manufacturing.

outcomes.text: Recognize different metal casting processes, forming processes and joining processes along with defects associated with them
Apply the knowledge, techniques, skills and tools of the manufacturing processes to broadly defined engineering technology activities
Demonstrate the knowledge of construction of a lathe machine and its various operations.

units.title: Metal Casting
units.text: Metal Casting: Pattern Making: Types of patterns, allowances, colour coding. Moulding sands: types, properties, preparation and testing of sand. Core boxes, core making, types of cores and their manufacturing; Gating system – runner and risers. Moulding processes: Shell moulding, CO2 moulding, investment casting, die casting, centrifugal casting and continuous casting; Study of various defects in castings.

units.title: Forming processes
units.text: Forming processes: Cold and hot working. Rolling: Principle and mechanism, types of rolling mills, various rolling processes and their applications, defects in rolling. Forging: Classification of forging processes, basic categories and methods of forging. Extrusion: Hot and cold extrusion, Extrusion equipment, defects in extruded parts. Wire and tube Drawing: Metal stamping and embossing, blanking, piercing, bending, deep drawing. Press tools: Different type of presses and their working, progressive die, compound and combination dies.

units.title: Joining processes
units.text: Joining processes: Surface preparation for joining and various types of joints; classification of welding processes, Arc welding - Types, submerged arc welding, gas metal arc welding, shielded metal arc welding, tungsten arc welding – theory and their applications; electron beam welding, laser beam welding, Solid state welding processes - ultrasonic welding, friction welding, resistance welding and its types - spot, seam and projection welding processes, welding of various metals, characteristics of good weld, weld defects and weldability of metals; soldering, brazing and their applications; adhesives for joining.

units.title: Lathe
units.text: Lathe: Introduction, construction, working and operations performed on lathe, attachments and accessories, cutting parameters such as spindle speed, feed and depth of cut, Capstan and Turret lathe, automatic lathes and their construction.

text_books: 1. Rao P. N., “Manufacturing Technology-Vol I”, Tata McGraw Hill, 4th Edition, 2013. 2. Kalpakjian S. and Schmid S. R., “Manufacturing Engineering and Technology”, Pearson, 8th Edition, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Chapman, W., Workshop Technology Part 1, CRC Press,5th edition, 2019. 2. Kou, Sindo., Welding Metallurgy, Wiley publishers, 3rd edition, 2020.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at exposing the students to the concepts of symbolic representations, limits-fits-tolerances and assembly-part detail drawings for machine components. This course is designed for students to master the assembly and part detail drawings of machine components using symbols and tolerances. The course uses a CAD software for rendering the assembly part details. The students are also exposed to the concepts of auxiliary views and interpenetration of solids.

outcomes.text: Understand the conventions and prepare drawings of auxiliary views and intersection of solids
Apply the tolerances, limits, fits and surface finish on the existing and new drawings, as per standards
Analyze the field of application of given machine and the functional requirement of individual parts
Create 2D assembly and part detail drawings using CAD software packages.

units.title: Conventional Representation
units.text: Conventional Representation: Materials: Cast Iron, Mild Steel, Brass, Bronze, Aluminium, Wood, Glass, Concrete and Rubber Pipes, Rods and Shafts: Long and Short Break in Pipe, Rod and Shaft Bearings, Joints and Valves: Ball and Roller Bearing, Pipe Joints and Valves Various Sections: Half, Removed, Offset, Partial, and Aligned Sections Threaded Parts: Conventional Representation of Threaded Parts Welding Representations: General Welding Symbols, Sectional Representation and Symbol used in Engineering Practices.

units.title: Limits, Fits and Tolerances
units.text: Limits, Fits and Tolerances: Characteristics of Surface Roughness: Indication of Machining Symbols Showing Direction of Lay, Roughness Grades, Machining Allowances and Manufacturing Methods. Limits, Fits and Tolerances: ISO Systems of Tolerances, Dimensional Tolerances, Elements of Interchangeable System, Hole and Shaft Based System, Limits, Fits and Allowances, Selection of Fits. Geometrical Tolerances: Geometrical Tolerances, Tolerances of Form and Position, Geometrical Representation of Tolerances of Form and Position,

units.title: Part Details and Assembly
units.text: Part Details and Assembly: Couplings: Muff Coupling, Flange Coupling, Bush-pin type Flexible Coupling, Universal Coupling and Oldham’s Coupling. Bearings: Foot-step Bearing and Plummer Block. Lathe: Lathe Tool Post and Lathe Tail Stock. Valves: V Gate Valve, Globe Valve and Non-return Valve. Joints: Knuckle Joint and Cotter Joint (Sleeve Joint, Socket and Spigot Joint). Vice: Pipe Vice and Machine Vice. Miscellaneous: Screw Jack, Drill Jig and Fixture and Piston and Connecting Rod.

units.title: Intersection of Surfaces of Solids
units.text: Intersection of Surfaces of Solids: Combinations: Two Prisms, Two Cylinders, Prism and Cylinder, Prism and Pyramid, Cone and Cylinder Conditions: When Axes are at 90o and Intersecting and when Axes are at 90o and Offset and when axis of cylinder is parallel to both reference planes and cone is resting on H.P. and with axis intersecting and at an offset from axis of cylinder.

units.title: Auxiliary Views
units.text: Auxiliary Views: Study of Auxiliary Planes, Projection of Objects on Auxiliary Planes, Completing the Regular Views with the Help of Given Auxiliary Views.

text_books: 1. Bhatt N. D. and Panchal V. M., “Machine Drawing”, Charotar Publishing House, 46th Edition, 2012.
reference_books: 1. Sideshvar and Shashtri, “Machine Drawing”, Tata McGraw Hill (Classic), 30th Edition, 2006. 2. K. L. Narayana, P. Kannaiah and K. V. Reddy, “Production Drawing”, New Age International, 3rd Edition, 2010. 3. General Principles of Presentation of Technical Drawing IS: 10714-2006. 4. Guide for Selection of Fits IS: 2709-1982.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at imparting basic knowledge of science of materials and physical metallurgy. This course introduces and cements the concept of structure property correlations. It is designed to lay the foundation for the detailed understanding of mechanical behavior of materials, phase diagrams, heat treatment and failure of materials. The students are also introduced to certain applications of ferrous, non-ferrous and new age materials.

outcomes.text: Relate mechanical properties with the mechanical processing of materials
Analyze the root cause of failure in different types of materials
Recommend heat treatment processes with the help of phase diagrams
Select appropriate materials for various applications depending on the structural requirements.

units.title: Mechanical Behavior of Metals
units.text: Mechanical Behavior of Metals: Deformation: Crystal structures and imperfections, elastic and plastic deformation. Deformation in single crystal and polycrystalline materials. Cold and Hot working of materials and Strain hardening of metals. Recrystallization annealing, recovery and grain growth.

units.title: Testing of Materials
units.text: Testing of Materials: Destructive Testing: Basic mechanical properties, tensile testing, hardness testing, Impact testing. Non-Destructive Testing: Dye Penetrant, magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing.

units.title: Failure of Metals
units.text: Failure of Metals: Fracture: Definition and types of fracture. Difference between ductile and brittle fracture. Fatigue: Definition and significance of cyclic stress, mechanism of fatigue failure. S-N curve and its interpretation, Notch effect, surface effect, Corrosion and thermal fatigue. Creep: Definition and significance of creep, analysis of classical creep curve, creep resistant materials.

units.title: Phase Diagrams
units.text: Phase Diagrams: Concept of solidification of metals, Solidification of pure metals, solid solutions. Hume Rothery rules, Phase rule, Cooling curves, Important binary phase diagrams, isomorphous system, Eutectic system, Eutectoid system, Peritectic system, Gibb’s phase rule, Lever rule.

units.title: Fe-Fe3C Equilibrium Diagram
units.text: Fe-Fe3C Equilibrium Diagram: Importance of iron as engineering material, Allotropic forms of irons. Fe-Fe3C diagram: phases, reactions, and critical temperatures. Solidification and microstructure of different steels. Effect of Alloying Elements in Steels: Limitation of plain carbon steels. Significance of alloying elements.

units.title: Heat Treatment of Steel
units.text: Heat Treatment of Steel: Definition and significance of heat treatment, Time temperature transformation diagrams (TTT), Continuous cooling Transformation (CCT). Annealing: Process, properties and applications of full annealing, diffusion annealing, process Annealing and cyclic annealing. Normalizing: Process, properties and applications of normalizing. Hardening and Tempering: Process, properties and applications of hardening.

units.title: Engineering Alloys
units.text: Engineering Alloys Ferrous Alloys: Classification, Alloy cast iron stainless steels, Tool Steels. Non-ferrous alloys: Copper alloys: Brass, bronzes (Tin, Beryllium and Silicon), Aluminium and its alloys. Cast irons: White, gray and malleable cast iron, Nodular and mottled cast iron. New age Materials: Introduction to composite materials and smart materials.

text_books: 1. Willam D. Callister, Jr., Adopted by R. Balsubramanium, “Materials science and Engineering”, Wiley India (P) Ltd, 2nd Edition, 2014. 2. S. H. Avner, “Introduction to Physical Metallurgy”, Tata McGraw Hill, 2nd Edition, 2012.
reference_books: 1. Kodgire V. D., Kodgire S. V., “Material science and Metallurgy”, Everest Publishing House, Pune., 2003. 2. V Raghavan, “Material Science and Engineering: A first Course, PHI Publication, 6th Edition, 2015. 3. K.G. Budinksi & M.K. Budinksi, “Engineering materials: Properties and Selection”, Pearson India Education Service Pvt. Ltd., 9th Edition, 2009.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course offers an insight into the basic understanding of biological intelligence needed to implement artificial intelligence. It also aims to enhance the knowledge of the basics of biology for bio-inspired engineering and designs while focusing on the principles of bioinspired algorithm implementation. To understand principles of bioinspired algorithm implementation.

outcomes.text: recall basics of biological systems
summarize the intelligence at the cellular level
identify and discuss the intelligence of different biological systems
summarize and categorize different forms of intelligence in different animals.

units.text: Introduction to intelligence in plants and animals. Need for intelligence for survival. Difference in animal intelligence and plant intelligence.

Introduction to animal cell. Different functions of cell. Different cell components and their functions. Different functions of cell like cell biochemistry, cell metabolism, cell communication, and cell composition.
Different types of intelligent body systems like- Immune system, Hormonal system, Cardiovascular system, Muscular systems etc.
Different defence mechanisms of body, Sympathetic body systems that understand different emotions, trauma, and external attacks. Intelligence of instincts, gut intelligence.

Different types of intelligence in different animals as case study. Survival intelligence, leadership intelligence, social intelligence, body language decoding, cognitive intelligence. Social and enterprising intelligence of ants, echo-locating skills of bats and such similar skills in different animals. Weather prediction, nest building skills of different species, survival tricks of different animals.

units.title: Study on implementation of biological intelligence in artificial systems
units.text: Study on implementation of biological intelligence in artificial systems. Applications of biological intelligence in field of computing like bio informatics, ANN, genetic algorithms, deep learning etc.

text_books: 1. T. Devasana, ‘’Cell Biology’’, Oxford university press, 2012. 2. Peter Parhan, “Immune System”, Garland Series, Taylor and Francis, 4th Edition, 2015. 3. Bernhard Kleine, Winfried G. Rossmanith, “Hormones and Endocrine system”, Springer, 1st Edition, 2016. 4. “Bio-Inspired Computational Algorithms and Their Applications”, Edited by Shangce Gao, Tongji University, China. IntechOpen, 1st Edition, 2012.
reference_books: 1. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology (Guyton Physiology), John E. Hall, 13th edition, 2015, EEE series.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical)
prerequisites: Fundamental knowledge of Derivatives, Partial Derivatives, Integration and Probability.
objectives: 1. To instill in prospective engineers knowledge of techniques in Laplace Transformation and Fourier series. 2. To introduce probability distributions and the solution methodologies for second order partial differential equations with applications in engineering.

outcomes.text: Solve problems based on Laplace transform and random variables.
Demonstrate understanding of orthogonality, expansion of functions as a Fourier series and Parseval‟s identity.
Solve problems in engineering involving partial differential equations.
Use suitable probability distribution to solve real life problems; apply Laplace Transform to solve differential equations.

units.title: Laplace transform
units.text: Laplace transform: Definition and Examples, Laplace transform of standard functions- ,sin ,cos , at e at at sinh ,cosh , n at at t , linearity property, change of scale property, first shifting property, second shifting property,   ( ) n L t f t , ( ) f t L t       , ( ) t L f t dt        ,   ( ) n L f t . Inverse Laplace transform using formulae and properties, partial fraction, Convolution Theorem. Laplace transform of Special Functions: periodic functions, Unit step function, Dirac delta function. Solutions of ordinary differential equations using Laplace Transform.

units.title: Fourier Series
units.text: Fourier Series: Dirichlet‟s conditions, orthogonal and orthonormal set of functions, Euler‟s formulae, Fourier Series of continuous; discontinuous functions in the interval [ , 2 ]    and [ , 2 ]c  , Parseval‟s identity, Fourier series of even and odd functions, half range sine and cosine series.

units.title: Partial Differential Equations and Applications
units.text: Partial Differential Equations and Applications: Separation of variables method to simple problems in Cartesian coordinates. Second-order linear equations and their classification. Initial & boundary value problems and solutions by separation of variables. Solution of the wave equation; Solution of one dimensional and two dimensional heat flow equation. Laplacian equation in Cartesian and polar coordinates.

units.title: Probability Distributions
units.text: Probability Distributions: Random variables, probability density function, cumulative distribution function, mean, variance, moments. Discrete probability distributions: Binomial, Poisson distribution. Fitting of Binomial and Poisson distribution. Continuous probability distribution: Normal distribution, additive property of Normal distribution, Central limit theorem.

program: B. Tech. ( Mechanical Engineering )
objectives: 1. The objective of this Course is to provide an introductory treatment of Engineering Mechanics to all the students of engineering, with a view to prepare a good foundation for taking up advanced courses in the area in the subsequent semesters 2. A working knowledge of statics with emphasis on force equilibrium and free body diagrams provides an understanding of the kinds of stress and deformation and how to determine them in a wide range of simple, practical structural problems, and an understanding of the mechanical behaviour of materials under various load conditions.

outcomes.text: Determine resultant forces and equilibrium of various force systems.
Determine centroid and moment of inertia of plane areas.
Determine the displacement, velocity, acceleration & their components for a moving particle and rigid body.
Determine forces produced due to motion of particles and rigid body.

units.title: System of Forces
units.text: System of Forces: Resultant of coplanar concurrent and non-concurrent forces, Resultant of concurrent and non-concurrent forces in space Equilibrium: Equilibrium of system of concurrent and non-concurrent forces in plane and space, Free body diagrams.

units.title: Application of Coplanar Forces and Equilibrium
units.text: Application of Coplanar Forces and Equilibrium: Trusses: Evaluation of member forces using method of sections and method of joints. Beams: Evaluation of reactions using equilibrium and principle of virtual work Simple frames: Evaluation of reactions using equilibrium

units.title: Friction
units.text: Friction: Types of friction, Limiting friction, Laws of Friction, Static and Dynamic Friction; wedge friction, screw jack

units.title: Centroid and Centre of Gravity
units.text: Centroid and Centre of Gravity: Centroid of simple figures from first principle, centroid of composite sections; Centre of Gravity and its implications; Area moment of inertia- Definition, Moment of inertia of plane sections from first principles, Moment of inertia of standard sections and composite sections; Mass moment inertia of circular plate, Cylinder, Sphere.

units.title: Kinematics of Particles
units.text: Kinematics of Particles: Rectilinear motion; Plane curvilinear motion (rectangular, path and polar coordinates), velocity-time graph and their usage, relative motion; Newton‟s 2nd law (rectangular, path, and polar coordinates). Kinematics of Rigid Bodies: Translation, pure rotation and plane motion of rigid bodies, ICR, link mechanisms

units.title: Kinetics of Particles and Rigid Bodies
units.text: Kinetics of Particles and Rigid Bodies: Newton‟s Law of motion, D‟Alembert‟s principle, equation of dynamic equilibrium, Work energy principle and its application in plane motion of connected bodies; Kinetics of rigid body in translation, rotation and plane motion.

text_books: 1. Irving H. Shames (2008), “Engineering Mechanics”, Prentice Hall, 4th Edition. 2. R. C. Hibbler (2017), “Engineering Mechanics: Principles of Statics and Dynamics”, Pearson Press.
reference_books: 1. F. P. Beer and E. R. Johnston (2017), “Vector Mechanics for Engineers”, Vol I & II, Tata McGraw Hill, 9th Edition. 2. Shanes and Rao (2006), “Engineering Mechanics”, Pearson Education. 3. Hibler and Gupta (2010), “Engineering Mechanics (Statics, Dynamics)” by Pearson Education 4. Tayal A.K. (2010), “Engineering Mechanics”, Umesh Publications

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives:  To learn the fundamental science and engineering relevant to materials  To introduce the concept of mechanical deformation in metals  To impart the knowledge of various failure mechanisms in materials and the theories and design modifications to avoid them.

outcomes.text: Design a process, microstructure and components to satisfy the system requirements.
Analyze the root cause of failure in different types of materials.
Understand formation of alloys and their applications.
Select appropriate materials for various applications depending on the structural requirements.

units.title: Mechanical Behavior of Metals
units.text: Mechanical Behavior of Metals: Deformation: Definition, elastic and plastic deformation and significance in design and shaping deformation in single crystal and polycrystalline materials, critical stress for deformation. Material Testing: Destructive Testing: Basic mechanical properties, tensile testing, hardness testing, Impact testing. Non Destructive Testing: Dye Penetrant, magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing Strain Hardening: Definition and importance, dislocation theory, effect of strain hardening on engineering behavior of material. Recrystallization annealing, recovery, recrystallization and grain growth.

units.title: Failure of Metals
units.text: Failure of Metals: Fracture: Definition and types, Griffth‟s theory of fracture, Orowan‟s Modification. Fatigue: Definition and significance of cyclic stress, mechanism of fatigue and theories of fatigue failure, S-N curve and its interpretation, Notch effect, surface effect, Corrosion and thermal fatigue. Creep: Definition and significance of creep, analysis of classical creep curve, creep resistant materials

units.title: Phase Diagrams
units.text: Phase Diagrams: Concept of solidification of metals, Solidification of pure metals, solid solutions, nucleation, growth of the new phase, solidification of alloys, progressive and directional solidification. Objectives and classification of phase diagram, System, phases and structural constituent of phase diagram, Gibb‟s phase rule, Lever rule. Coring and dendritic segregation, Eutectic, Peritectic and eutectoid system.

units.text: Fe-Fe3C Equilibrium Diagram: Importance of iron as engineering material, Allotropic forms of irons, Fe-Fe3C diagram: phases, reactions, and critical temperatures Solidification and microstructure of different steels Effect of Alloying Elements in Steels: Limitation of plain carbon steels. program: B. Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives:  To introduce the concepts of detail drawing of mechanical components, assemblies, intersection of solids and auxiliary views.  To understand limits, fits and tolerances in mechanical components and assemblies.  To learn symbolic representation of materials and different type of sections.

outcomes.text: Understand the conventions and prepare drawings of Auxiliary views and Intersection of solids.
Apply the tolerances, limits, fits and surface finish and surface finish on the existing and new drawings, as per standards.
Analyze the field of application of given machine and also the functional requirement of individual parts.
Create assembly and detail drawings (2D) using CAD software packages.

General welding symbols, sectional representation and symbol used in engineering practices
