program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Differential and integral calculus (BTME01001 and BTME02008)
objectives:  Introduce basics of thermodynamics and concepts of work and heat transfer.  Impart knowledge of laws of thermodynamics and their applications  To provide understanding of properties and behavior of pure substances and gas mixtures.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental concepts of engineering thermodynamics.
Analyze closed systems, steady and unsteady flow systems and laws of thermodynamics and available energy.
Understand the properties of gases, mixtures of gases and pure substances using steam tables and charts.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Definition, and basic concepts of engineering thermodynamics; description of matter – macroscopic description and microscopic description; thermodynamic system, surroundings and the system boundary; thermodynamic properties, processes and cycles; homogeneous and heterogeneous systems; thermodynamic equilibrium; quasi-static process; pure-substance; concepts of continuum. Pressure, Volume and Temperature: definition of pressure, volume and temperature and their measurements; Thermal equilibrium; Zeroth law of thermodynamics; – thermometric property, scale of temperature, reference points,. Work and Heat Transfer: thermodynamics definition of work; classification of work; general expression for mechanical displacement work; expressions for various forms of work; definition of heat transfer; characteristics of heat transfer.

units.title: First Law of Thermodynamics
units.text: First Law of Thermodynamics: Definition of the first law; Application of first law for a closed system undergoing a cyclic and non-cyclic process; different forms of stored energy; specific heats, Application of first law for an isolated system; first law equation for steady and unsteady flow open systems.

units.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics
units.text: Second Law of Thermodynamics: Limitations of first law; Kelvin- Planck statement of second law; Clausius statement of second law; equivalence between the two statements; reversibility and irreversibility- definition of a reversible heat engine; corollaries of second law of thermodynamics; reversibility and irreversibility as applied to a non-cyclic process; Statement of Third Law of Thermodynamics and its importance

units.title: Entropy
units.text: Entropy: Introduction; Clausius inequality (or Clausius theorem); Entropy as a property of a system; Temperature – entropy plot and its usefulness in analyzing thermodynamic processes; entropy change for an irreversible process; principle of increase of entropy ; Tds relations and their significance(first and second law combined), Isentropic process. Introduction of Available energy, Availability and Irreversibility: Classification of energy- high grade energy and low grade energy; concept of available energy, unavailable energy and availability.

units.title: Properties of Pure Substances
units.text: Properties of Pure Substances: p-v and p-T diagrams for a pure substance; T-s and h-s diagrams for a pure substance; quality/dryness fraction; steam tables and Mollier chart, calculation of thermodynamic properties such as specific volume, internal energy, enthalpy, entropy and steam quality for various processes using steam tables and Mollier chart.

units.title: Properties of Gases and Gas Mixtures
units.text: Properties of Gases and Gas Mixtures: Avogadro‟s law; equation of state for a gas; ideal gas; equations of state; properties of mixtures of gases- Dalton‟s law and Gibb‟s law, internal energy, enthalpy , specific heats and entropy of a mixture of gases

text_books: 1. P. K. Nag (2008), “Engineering Thermodynamics”, Tata McGraw Hill. 2. M. J. Moran, H. N. Shapiro, D. D. Boettner, M. B. Bailey (2011), “Fundamentals of Engineering Thermodynamics”, 7th Edition, John Wiley and Sons.
reference_books: 1. Y. Cengel and M. Boles (2008), “Thermodynamics -An Engineering Approach”, Tata McGraw Hill. 2. R. E. Sonntag, C. Borgnakke and G. J. V. Wylen (2005), “Fundamentals of Thermodynamics”, 6th Edition, Wiley India.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart an understanding of basic tenets of business communication that helps students to effectively engage in organizational communication. 2. To develop in students an understanding of interpersonal communication challenges and the ability to effectively overcome these challenges in an organizational context. 3. To develop leadership, team building and decision making skills which could be later applied in a professional set up. 4. To impart technical writing skills towards designing and structuring persuasive technical communication. 5. To build and strengthen presentation skills towards making impressive and persuasive presentations. 6. To train the students for participating in group discussions, building Resume and facing personal interviews.

outcomes.text: Understand and apply the postulates of technical writing in a formal set up
Apply fundamentals of business correspondence to create well-structured Resumes, application letters, Minutes of Meetings and similar business related documents
Understand and analyse group dynamics and apply leadership skills for effective team building in professional set ups.
Analyze the context and select appropriate communication techniques for effective interpersonal communication in professional context.

units.title: Understanding the foundations of Business Communication
units.text: Understanding the foundations of Business Communication: Professional Communication in a Digital, Social, Mobile World

units.title: Collaboration, Interpersonal Communication and Business Etiquette
units.text: Collaboration, Interpersonal Communication and Business Etiquette: Communicating effectively, collaborating, conducting productive meetings, using meeting technologies, improving listening skills and non-verbal communication, business etiquettes.

units.title: Development of Interpersonal and Group Communication Skills
units.text: Development of Interpersonal and Group Communication Skills Theatre techniques: Use of drama (in workshop format) to promote meaningful, active and reflective thinking processes as well as enhancing communication skills development. Group Communication  Forms of Group Communication; Use of body language in Group communication  Group Discussion etiquette: Introducing oneself and others; Expressing Opinions and Ideas; expressing disagreement etc. Group Discussion Strategies: Speaking, taking turns, Creating a Cordial and cooperative atmosphere etc.

Building Problem-solving teams  Orientation to Personality Values – Importance of Values  Understanding of Teams- Types of Teams, stages of Team development; Team building leadership skills and leaderless scenarios  Decision Making-Group and Individual Decision Making Techniques  Stress Management-Sources of Stress; consequences; Managing Stress

Employment Communication  Personal Interviews-Objectives, Types, Stages of Interview  Interview Preparation-types of Interview Questions; Interview Follow ups  Resume- Types and Format; Cover letters  Mock Interviews ( simulation )

Organizational networks and communication Structures  Process and Functions of Communication; Formal Networks in Organizational Communication  Informal networks of organizational communications ;choice of communication channels

Meetings  Meetings- Purposes, Importance and Meeting Procedures including Chairperson‟s and participants‟ roles Meeting Documentation (Minutes of resolution; Minutes of Narration; Meeting Notice and Agenda)
Technical Report Writing  Importance, objectives and Characteristic of Reports; Types of Reports  Report formats and Structure -Memo Reports; Letter Reports; Office Orders and Manuscript Reports

Presentation Skills  Planning and structuring Presentations; Visual Aids in Presentations  Applications of MS Power Point Audience analyses; Nuances of Delivery; Modes of delivery; Controlling Nervousness and stage fright

text_books: 1. Bovee, C., Thill, J., & Roshan Lal Raina (2013). Business Communication Today (14th ed.). Pearson. 2. Meenakshi Raman and Sangeeta Sharma (2015), Technical Communication Oxford University Press,3rd Edition
reference_books: 1. Fred Luthans ( 2013), „Organizational Behavior‟, McGraw Hill, 12th Edition

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: 1. Introduce – Environment, Environmental Pollution, 2. Acquaint with Social Issues and methods to manage them 3. Improving Planning of activities

outcomes.text: Discuss Types of Environmental Pollution, Natural resources and its misuse, Importance of Environmental management for Construction Projects
Prepare plan for water management, promotion of recycle and reuse, generation of less waste, avoiding electricity waste
Prepare Slogan, Poster and plan activities for environmental protection and social issues

units.title: Introduction to Environment and its components
units.text: Introduction to Environment and its components: Natural Resources and it Misuse leading to Environmental degradation. Role of Ecology in Environmental Degradation and Protection. Major industrial and other environmental disasters Environmental pollution- Types, Causes, Effects, Reduction methodology.

units.title: Introduction to waste generation, Methods to Reduce, Reuse and
units.text: Introduction to waste generation, Methods to Reduce, Reuse and Recycle of Waste Importance of 3R‟s, Promotion of 3R‟s - Methods Solid wastes, Industrial Waste, Bio-Medical Waste and Hazardous waste management – Types, Storage, Transportation, Treatment Disposal. C&D and E-waste – Concept, methods for reduction, management Campaigning for waste reduction and management.
Concept of EIA and SIA, significance, methodology, report drafting. Environmental Management System, ISO 14000 EMS certification

units.title: Environmental Protection, Social Issues, Disaster Management
units.text: Environmental Protection, Social Issues, Disaster Management Social Issues and Environment International Conventions, Summits and Protocols Generation of less waste and avoiding electricity waste. Environmental management for construction Projects

Role of the Government in managing the environmental activities in all sectors. Organisational set up at the Central and state level to manage the environment. Role of judiciary in managing the environment. Role of Citizens, Role of NGOs/ Environmental Activists. Major Laws Air (P&C.P.) Act, Water (P & C.P) Act. Environment Protection Act EPA 1986. Wild life Protection Act etc., PIL

reference_books: 1. P. Aarne Vesilind, Susan M. Morgan (2004), “Introduction to Environmental Engineering”, Thomas/Brook/Cole. 2. Mackenzie Davis, David Cornwell (2017), “Introduction to Environmental Engineering”, McGraw-Hill Companies.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering) B Tech (Civil Engineering and Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: In this course students will get acquainted with the various systems of forces. It is designed for the students to understand the concept of static equilibrium and apply the equations of motion to rigid bodies.

outcomes.text: Determine the resultant of various systems of forces
Analyse the system of forces in equilibrium
Evaluate the displacement, velocity and acceleration of a moving bodies
Determine the forces developed on rigid bodies subjected to displacements and rotations

units.title: System of Forces
units.text: System of Forces Rectangular components of forces in space, moment, couple, Varignon’s theorem, resolution of forces, resultant of force system (coplanar, non-coplanar), concept of virtual work, principle of virtual work.

units.title: Application of System of Forces and Equilibrium
units.text: Application of System of Forces and Equilibrium Conditions of equilibrium, types of support, loads and beams, free body diagrams, support reactions. Friction Laws of friction, angle of friction, angle of repose, cone of friction, equilibrium of bodies on rough horizontal and inclined plane, application to inclined planes, wedges, ladder & screw jack. Analysis of Pin Jointed Plane Trusses Perfect truss, analysis using method of joints and method of sections.

units.title: Centroid and Moment of Inertia
units.text: Centroid and Moment of Inertia Centroid, moment of inertia, polar moment of inertia, and product of inertia, parallel and perpendicular axis theorem.

units.title: Kinematics of Particle
units.text: Kinematics of Particle Velocity and acceleration in terms of rectangular coordinate system, rectilinear motion, curvilinear motion, projectile motion, tangential and normal component of acceleration, acceleration - time, velocity- time graphs and their uses, relative velocity Kinematics of Rigid Bodies Translation, pure rotation and plane motion of rigid bodies, instantaneous centre of rotation for the velocity for bodies in plane motion, link mechanisms (up to two links).

units.title: Kinetics of Particles
units.text: Kinetics of Particles Newton’s laws of motion, D’Alembert’s principle, equation of dynamic equilibrium, linear motion, curvilinear motion. Kinetics of Rigid Bodies D’Alembert’s principle for bodies under translational motion, rotational motion about a fixed axis and plane motion.

text_books: 1. Beer & Johnston, Engineering Mechanics, 12th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2020. 2. R. C. Hibler, Engineering Mechanics’, 14th Edition, Pearson Education, 2017.
reference_books: 1. F. L. Singer, Engineering Mechanics, Harper & Raw Publication, 1954. (Classic Book) 2. D. S. Kumar, Engineering Mechanics, 12th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2013.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course describes the fundamentals of Thermodynamics including thermodynamic systems and properties, work and heat interactions, relationships among the thermo-physical properties, the laws of thermodynamics and applications of these basic laws in thermodynamic systems such as various thermodynamic cycles. This course will provide the essential tools required to study thermodynamic systems in Applied Thermodynamics.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental concepts of engineering thermodynamics
Analyze various flow systems, laws of thermodynamics, concept of exergy and various power cycles
Understand the properties of pure substances using steam tables and charts

units.title: Definitions and Concepts
units.text: Definitions and Concepts System, Property, Energy, Thermodynamic Equilibrium, Work interaction & various modes of work, Heat, State Postulate; Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics, Temperature Scale, Heat and Work Interactions

units.title: Properties of Pure substances
units.text: Properties of Pure substances Pure substance, Phase of substances, Molecular models of matter, Phase change processes in pure substance, Graphical representation of phase change processes, Steam Table. Equation of State, van der Walls Equation of State; Law of corresponding states, Compressibility chart, Pressure-volume; Temperature-volume and Phase diagrams; Mollier diagram and Steam tables.

units.title: First Law of Thermodynamics for Non flow process
units.text: First Law of Thermodynamics for Non flow process Application of First Law for elementary processes; First Law analysis of Non-flow processes. First Law of Thermodynamics for flow process Application of First Law of Thermodynamics for Flow Process-Steady state, steady flow processes, throttling process; Transient Flow Processes, Charging & discharging of tanks.

units.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics
units.text: Second Law of Thermodynamics Limitations of the First Law of Thermodynamics, Heat Engine, Heat Pump/Refrigerator. Second Law of Thermodynamics Kelvin Planck and Clausius statements & their equivalence. Reversible & irreversible processes, Criterion of reversibility, Carnot cycle & Carnot principles.

units.title: Applications of Second Law of Thermodynamics
units.text: Applications of Second Law of Thermodynamics Thermodynamic Temperature scale, Clausius inequality, Entropy, Calculations of entropy change, Principle of entropy increase, T-S diagram, II Law analysis of Control volume. Available energy, Availability; Second law efficiency. Thermodynamic relations.

units.title: Power Cycles
units.text: Power Cycles Vapour Power Cycles: Rankine cycle – Ideal, Reheat and Regenerative Rankine cycles. Gas Power Cycles Otto cycle, Diesel cycle, Dual cycle and Brayton cycle.

text_books: 1. P. K. Nag, Engineering Thermodynamics, 6th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. Vanwvylen & Sonntag, Classical Thermodynamics, 5th Edition, Wiley Eastern, 1994.
reference_books: 1. Y. Cengel and M. Boles, Thermodynamics -An Engineering Approach, 6th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. M. J. Moran, H. N. Shapiro, D. D. Boettner, M. B. Bailey, Fundamentals of Engineering Thermodynamics, 7th Edition, John Wiley and Sons, 2011.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is aimed at detailed introduction of various key manufacturing processes such as casting, welding, forging, rolling, extrusion, drawing and machining. The course has been structured to impart the in-depth understanding of industrial applications of various processes and equipment used in manufacturing.

outcomes.text: Recognize different metal casting processes, forming processes and joining processes along with defects associated with them
Apply the knowledge, techniques, skills and tools of the manufacturing processes to broadly defined engineering technology activities
Demonstrate the knowledge of construction of a lathe machine and its various operations

units.title: Metal Casting
units.text: Metal Casting Pattern Making Types of patterns, allowances, colour coding. Moulding sands Types, properties, preparation and testing of sand. Core boxes, core making, types of cores and their manufacturing; Gating system – runner and risers. Moulding processes Shell moulding, CO2 moulding, investment casting, die casting, centrifugal casting and continuous casting; Study of various defects in castings.

units.title: Forming processes
units.text: Forming processes Cold and hot working. Rolling Principle and mechanism, types of rolling mills, various rolling processes and their applications, defects in rolling. Forging Classification of forging processes, basic categories and methods of forging. Extrusion Hot and cold extrusion, Extrusion equipment, defects in extruded parts. Wire and tube Drawing Metal stamping and embossing, blanking, piercing, bending, deep drawing. Press tools Different type of presses and their working, progressive die, compound and combination dies.

units.title: Joining processes
units.text: Joining processes Surface preparation for joining and various types of joints; classification of welding processes, Arc welding - Types, submerged arc welding, gas metal arc welding, shielded metal arc welding, tungsten arc welding – theory and their applications; electron beam welding, laser beam welding, Solid state welding processes - ultrasonic welding, friction welding, resistance welding and its types - spot, seam and projection welding processes, welding of various metals, characteristics of good weld, weld defects and weldability of metals; soldering, brazing and their applications; adhesives for joining.

units.title: Lathe
units.text: Lathe Introduction, construction, working and operations performed on lathe, attachments and accessories, cutting parameters such as spindle speed, feed and depth of cut, Capstan and Turret lathe, automatic lathes and their construction.

text_books: 1. Rao P. N., Manufacturing Technology-Vol I, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2013. 2. Kalpakjian S. and Schmid S. R., Manufacturing Engineering and Technology, 8th Edition, Pearson, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Chapman, W., Workshop Technology Part 1, 5th Edition, CRC Press, 2019. 2. Kou, Sindo., Welding Metallurgy, 3rd Edition, Wiley publishers, 2020.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at exposing the students to the concepts of symbolic representations, limits-fits- tolerances and assembly-part detail drawings for machine components. This course is designed for students to master the assembly and part detail drawings of machine components using symbols and tolerances. The course uses a CAD software for rendering the assembly part details. The students are also exposed to the concepts of auxiliary views and interpenetration of solids.

outcomes.text: Understand the conventions and prepare drawings of auxiliary views and intersection of solids
Apply the tolerances, limits, fits and surface finish on the existing and new drawings, as per standards
Analyze the field of application of given machine and the functional requirement of individual parts
Create 2D assembly and part detail drawings using CAD software packages

Geometrical Tolerances Geometrical Tolerances, Tolerances of Form and Position, Geometrical Representation of Tolerances of Form and Position,

units.title: Part Details and Assembly
units.text: Part Details and Assembly Couplings Muff Coupling, Flange Coupling, Bush-pin type Flexible Coupling, Universal Coupling and Oldham’s Coupling. Joints Knuckle Joint and Cotter Joint (Sleeve Joint, Socket and Spigot Joint). Vice Pipe Vice and Machine Vice. Miscellaneous Screw Jack, Drill Jig and Fixture and Piston and Connecting Rod.

units.text: Intersection of Surfaces of Solids Combinations Two Prisms, Two Cylinders, Prism and Cylinder, Prism and Pyramid, Cone and Cylinder Conditions When Axes are at 90o and Intersecting and when Axes are at 90o and Offset and when axis of cylinder is parallel to both reference planes and cone is resting on H.P. and with axis intersecting and at an offset from axis of cylinder.

units.text: Auxiliary Views Study of Auxiliary Planes, Projection of Objects on Auxiliary Planes, Completing the Regular Views with the Help of Given Auxiliary Views.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at imparting basic knowledge of science of materials and physical metallurgy. This course introduces and cements the concept of structure property correlations. It is designed to lay the foundation for the detailed understanding of mechanical behavior of materials, phase diagrams, heat treatment and failure of materials. The students are also introduced to certain applications of ferrous, non-ferrous and new age materials.

outcomes.text: Relate mechanical properties with the mechanical processing of materials
Analyze the root cause of failure in different types of materials
Recommend heat treatment processes with the help of phase diagrams
Select appropriate materials for various applications depending on the structural requirements

units.title: Mechanical Behavior of Metals
units.text: Mechanical Behavior of Metals Deformation Crystal structures and imperfections, elastic and plastic deformation. Deformation in single crystal and polycrystalline materials. Cold and Hot working of materials and Strain hardening of metals. Recrystallization annealing, recovery and grain growth.

units.title: Testing of Materials
units.text: Testing of Materials Destructive Testing Basic mechanical properties, tensile testing, hardness testing, Impact testing. Non-Destructive Testing Dye Penetrant, magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing.

units.title: Failure of Metals
units.text: Failure of Metals Fracture Definition and types of fracture. Difference between ductile and brittle fracture. Fatigue Definition and significance of cyclic stress, mechanism of fatigue failure. S-N curve and its interpretation, Notch effect, surface effect, Corrosion and thermal fatigue. Creep Definition and significance of creep, analysis of classical creep curve, creep resistant materials.

units.title: Phase Diagrams
units.text: Phase Diagrams Concept of solidification of metals, Solidification of pure metals, solid solutions. Hume Rothery rules, Phase rule, Cooling curves, Important binary phase diagrams, isomorphous system, Eutectic system, Eutectoid system, Peritectic system, Gibb’s phase rule, Lever rule.

units.title: Fe-Fe3C Equilibrium Diagram
units.text: Fe-Fe3C Equilibrium Diagram Importance of iron as engineering material, Allotropic forms of irons. Fe-Fe3C diagram phases, reactions, and critical temperatures. Solidification and microstructure of different steels. Effect of Alloying Elements in Steels Limitation of plain carbon steels. Significance of alloying elements.

units.title: Heat Treatment of Steel
units.text: Heat Treatment of Steel Definition and significance of heat treatment, Time temperature transformation diagrams (TTT), Continuous cooling Transformation (CCT). Annealing Process, properties and applications of full annealing, diffusion annealing, process Annealing and cyclic annealing. Normalizing Process, properties and applications of normalizing. Hardening and Tempering Process, properties and applications of hardening.

units.title: Engineering Alloys
units.text: Engineering Alloys Ferrous Alloys Classification, Cast iron, Stainless steels, Tool Steels. Non-ferrous alloys Copper alloys: Brass, bronzes (Tin, Beryllium and Silicon), Aluminium and its alloys. Cast irons White, gray and malleable cast iron, Nodular and mottled cast iron. New age Materials Introduction to composite materials and smart materials.

Analysis of Pin Jointed Plane Trusses Perfect truss, analysis using method of joints and method of sections.

units.title: Centroid and Moment of Inertia
units.text: Centroid and Moment of Inertia Centroid, moment of inertia, polar moment of inertia, and product of inertia, parallel and perpendicular axis theorem.

units.title: Kinematics of Particle
units.text: Kinematics of Particle Velocity and acceleration in terms of rectangular coordinate system, rectilinear motion, curvilinear motion, projectile motion, tangential and normal component of acceleration, acceleration - time, velocity- time graphs and their uses, relative velocity Kinematics of Rigid Bodies Translation, pure rotation and plane motion of rigid bodies, instantaneous centre of rotation for the velocity for bodies in plane motion, link mechanisms (up to two links).

units.title: Kinetics of Particles
units.text: Kinetics of Particles Newton’s laws of motion, D’Alembert’s principle, equation of dynamic equilibrium, linear motion, curvilinear motion. Kinetics of Rigid Bodies D’Alembert’s principle for bodies under translational motion, rotational motion about a fixed axis and plane motion.

text_books: 1. Beer & Johnston, Engineering Mechanics, 12th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2020. 2. R. C. Hibler, Engineering Mechanics’, 14th Edition, Pearson Education, 2017.
reference_books: 1. F. L. Singer, Engineering Mechanics, Harper & Raw Publication, 1954. (Classic Book) 2. D. S. Kumar, Engineering Mechanics, 12th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2013.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is aimed at detailed introduction of various key manufacturing processes such as casting, welding, forging, rolling, extrusion, drawing and machining. The course has been structured to impart the in-depth understanding of industrial applications of various processes and equipment used in manufacturing.

outcomes.text: Identify different types of patterns, moulding sands, and casting techniques
Explain the principles and applications of rolling, forging, and extrusion processes
Classify various welding techniques and their applications in manufacturing
Apply suitable metal forming and joining techniques based on material and process requirements
Analyze the working principles and machining operations of a lathe machine

units.title: Metal Casting
units.text: Metal Casting Pattern Making Types of patterns, allowances, colour coding. Moulding sands Types, properties, preparation and testing of sand. Core boxes, core making, types of cores and their manufacturing; Gating system – runner and risers. Moulding processes Shell moulding, CO2 moulding, investment casting, die casting, centrifugal casting and continuous casting; Study of various defects in castings.

units.title: Forming processes
units.text: Forming processes Cold and hot working. Rolling Principle and mechanism, types of rolling mills, various rolling processes and their applications, defects in rolling. Forging Classification of forging processes, basic categories and methods of forging. Extrusion Hot and cold extrusion, Extrusion equipment, defects in extruded parts. Wire and tube Drawing Metal stamping and embossing, blanking, piercing, bending, deep drawing. Press tools Different type of presses and their working, progressive die, compound and combination dies.

units.title: Joining processes
units.text: Joining processes Surface preparation for joining and various types of joints; classification of welding processes, Arc welding - Types, submerged arc welding, gas metal arc welding, shielded metal arc welding, tungsten arc welding – theory and their applications; electron beam welding, laser beam welding, Solid state welding processes - ultrasonic welding, friction welding, resistance welding and its types - spot, seam and projection welding processes, welding of various metals, characteristics of good weld, weld defects and weldability of metals; soldering, brazing and their applications; adhesives for joining.

units.title: Lathe
units.text: Lathe Introduction, construction, working and operations performed on lathe, attachments and accessories, cutting parameters such as spindle speed, feed and depth of cut, Capstan and Turret lathe, automatic lathes and their construction.

text_books: 1. Rao P. N., Manufacturing Technology-Vol I, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2013. 2. Kalpakjian S. and Schmid S. R., Manufacturing Engineering and Technology, 8th Edition, Pearson, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Chapman, W., Workshop Technology Part 1, 5th Edition, CRC Press, 2019. 2. Kou, Sindo., Welding Metallurgy, 3rd Edition, Wiley publishers, 2020.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at imparting basic knowledge of science of materials and physical metallurgy. This course introduces and cements the concept of structure property correlations. It is designed to lay the foundation for the detailed understanding of mechanical behavior of materials, phase diagrams, heat treatment and failure of materials. The students are also introduced to certain applications of ferrous, non-ferrous and new age materials.

outcomes.text: Relate mechanical properties with the mechanical processing of materials
Demonstrate the mechanical behaviour of metals using destructive and non-destructive testing
Analyze the root cause of failure in different types of materials
Interpret Phase Transformations in Iron-Iron Carbon Alloys
Recommend suitable heat treatment processes with the help of phase diagrams.

units.title: Mechanical Behavior of Metals
units.text: Mechanical Behavior of Metals Deformation Crystal structures and imperfections, elastic and plastic deformation. Deformation in single crystal and polycrystalline materials. Cold and Hot working of materials and Strain hardening of metals. Recrystallization annealing, recovery and grain growth.

units.title: Testing of Materials
units.text: Testing of Materials Destructive Testing Basic mechanical properties, tensile testing, hardness testing, Impact testing. Non-Destructive Testing Dye Penetrant, Magnetic Particle and Ultrasonic testing.

units.title: Failure of Metals
units.text: Failure of Metals Fracture: Definition and types of fracture. Fatigue: Definition and significance of cyclic stress, mechanism of fatigue failure. S-N curve and its interpretation, Notch effect, surface effect, Corrosion and thermal fatigue. Creep: Definition and significance of creep, analysis of classical creep curve, creep resistant materials.

units.title: Phase Diagrams
units.text: Phase Diagrams Concept of solidification of metals, Solidification of pure metals, solid solutions. Hume Rothery rules, Phase rule, Cooling curves, Important binary phase diagrams, isomorphous system, Eutectic system, Eutectoid system, Peritectic system, Gibb’s phase rule, Lever rule.

units.title: Fe-Fe3C Equilibrium Diagram
units.text: Fe-Fe3C Equilibrium Diagram Importance of iron as engineering material, Allotropic forms of irons. Fe-Fe3C Diagram Phases, reactions, microstructures and critical temperatures. Effect of Alloying Elements in Steels Engineering Alloys, Significance of alloying elements.

units.title: Heat Treatment of Steel
units.text: Heat Treatment of Steel Definition and significance of heat treatment, Time temperature transformation diagrams (TTT), Continuous cooling Transformation (CCT). Heat treatment processes: Annealing, Normalizing, Hardening and Tempering.

text_books: 1. Willam F. Smith, Foundations of Materials science and Engineering, 5th Edition, McGraw Hill Science Engineering, 2022. 2. Kodgire V. D., Kodgire S. V., Material science and Metallurgy for Engineers, Everest Publishing House, Pune., 2024.
reference_books: 1. Beer. F.P, Johnston R., DeWolf. J, Mechanics of Materials, 8th Edition, McGraw Hill ,2020.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is aimed at training the students on lathe machine with different turning operations like such as plain, taper turning along with operations like facing, thread cutting, grooving, knurling and wire drawing die on metals.

outcomes.text: Apply different operations on lathe like plain, taper turning, facing, grooving and knurling
Operate different operations like screw cutting and threading
Perform different operation on lathe like drilling, boring, counter boring, internal taper turning

units.text: Job on lathe performing plain and taper turning.
Job on precision turning and screw cutting.
Assembly of Two pieces using operations like drilling, boring, counter boring, internal taper turning and broaching operations.

lab_work: Performing 15 week practical to complete jobs as per the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at exposing the students to the concepts of symbolic representations, limits-fits- tolerances and assembly-part detail drawings for machine components. This course is designed for students to master the assembly and part detail drawings of machine components using symbols and tolerances. The course uses a CAD software for rendering the assembly part details. The students are also exposed to the concepts of auxiliary views and interpenetration of solids.

outcomes.text: Understand the conventions and prepare drawings of auxiliary views and intersection of solids
Apply the tolerances, limits, fits and surface finish on the existing and new drawings, as per standards
Analyze the field of application of given machine and the functional requirement of individual parts
Create 2D assembly drawings using CAD software packages
Create 2D part detail drawings using CAD software packages

units.title: Conventional Representation
units.text: Conventional Representation Materials Cast Iron, Mild Steel, Brass, Bronze, Aluminium, Wood, Glass, Concrete and Rubber Pipes, Rods and Shafts Long and Short Break in Pipe, Rod and Shaft Bearings, Joints and Valves Ball and Roller Bearing, Pipe Joints and Valves Various Sections Half, Removed, Offset, Partial, and Aligned Sections Threaded Parts Conventional Representation of Threaded Parts Welding Representations General Welding Symbols, Sectional Representation and Symbol used in Engineering Practices.

units.title: Limits, Fits and Tolerances
units.text: Limits, Fits and Tolerances Characteristics of Surface Roughness Indication of Machining Symbols Showing Direction of Lay, Roughness Grades, Machining Allowances and Manufacturing Methods. Limits, Fits and Tolerances ISO Systems of Tolerances, Dimensional Tolerances, Elements of Interchangeable System, Hole and Shaft Based System, Limits, Fits and Allowances, Selection of Fits. Geometrical Tolerances Geometrical Tolerances, Tolerances of Form and Position, Geometrical Representation of Tolerances of Form and Position,

units.title: Part Details and Assembly
units.text: Part Details and Assembly Couplings Muff Coupling, Flange Coupling, Bush-pin type Flexible Coupling, Universal Coupling and Oldham’s Coupling. Bearings Foot-step Bearing and Plummer Block. Lathe Lathe Tool Post and Lathe Tail Stock. Valves V Gate Valve, Globe Valve and Non-return Valve. Joints Knuckle Joint and Cotter Joint (Sleeve Joint, Socket and Spigot Joint). Vice Pipe Vice and Machine Vice. Miscellaneous Screw Jack, Drill Jig and Fixture and Piston and Connecting Rod.

units.title: Intersection of Surfaces of Solids
units.text: Intersection of Surfaces of Solids Combinations Two Prisms, Two Cylinders, Prism and Cylinder, Prism and Pyramid, Cone and Cylinder Conditions When Axes are at 90o and Intersecting and when Axes are at 90o and Offset and when axis of cylinder is parallel to both reference planes and cone is resting on H.P. and with axis intersecting and at an offset from axis of cylinder.

units.title: Auxiliary Views
units.text: Auxiliary Views Study of Auxiliary Planes, Projection of Objects on Auxiliary Planes, Completing the Regular Views with the Help of Given Auxiliary Views.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The CAD Advanced Processes course aims to enhance students' proficiency in the NX platform by introducing advanced commands and modeling techniques. It focuses on transitioning from sketches to 3D models, including raster image development. Students will gain expertise in face and edge operations, along with fundamental freeform modeling. Additionally, the course covers assembly modeling and the effective use of reference sets for complex designs.

outcomes.text: Gain the experience about the NX platform on advance commands.
Sketch to model and raster image development.
Understand face and edge operations and basics of freeform.
Learn assembly in models and using reference set.

units.title: Advanced Curve and Freeform Modeling Techniques in NX
units.text: Advanced Curve and Freeform Modeling Techniques in NX: Documenting design intent (feature groups, product interfaces), editing parametric models (replace features, suppression by expression, model updates), associative curve operations (project, join, intersect, wrap/unwrap, text), create curves and derived curves used in creating freeform features, analyze curves and faces, create freeform shapes through curves, create freeform shapes by sweeping sections along curves.

units.title: Advanced Embossing and Blending Techniques in NX
units.text: Advanced Embossing and Blending Techniques in NX: Emboss geometry (emboss body, emboss, offset emboss), blending techniques (advanced edge blend options, face blends), interpart references (interpart expressions, overriding expressions), capturing part shape variations (deformable parts), design optimization (optimization study, local and global algorithms), create thicken and draft faces.

units.title: Modifying Detail Features Using Synchronous Modeling
units.text: Modifying Detail Features Using Synchronous Modeling: Introduction to synchronous modeling (move, pull, replace, delete face), modifying detail features using synchronous (resize blend, chamfer, replace blend), create transition and blend shapes, reusing and relating faces using synchronous (pattern face, copy/paste face, dimensions), optional: history-free synchronous (optimize face, adaptive, extend and offset faces.

text_books: 1. Sham Tickoo, Siemens NX 12.0 for Designers, 11th Edition, CADCIM Technologies, 2018.
reference_books: 1. Stephen Samuel, Basic to Advanced computer aided design using NX, Design Visionaries Inc & Applied ACX, 2022
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course introduces students to the systems-level engineering of modern vehicles, with emphasis on Electric Vehicles (EVs). It covers vehicle architecture, powertrain systems, energy storage, dynamics, control, safety, and emerging technologies. Students also gain basic knowledge of the integration of individual subsystems to achieve an efficient, safe, and sustainable vehicle.

outcomes.text: Understand vehicle systems architecture and subsystem integration
Describe Electric vehicle architecture
Differentiate between types of motors and power electronic systems
Apply fundamentals of vehicle dynamics and control
Explain battery systems, charging, safety, and emerging technologies.

units.title: Introduction to Vehicle Systems
units.text: Introduction to Vehicle Systems Classification of vehicles: Passenger, commercial, off-road, electric, hybrid. Vehicle layout and architecture, Vehicle as a system: System engineering approach, Overview of ICE, Hybrid, and Electric Vehicles, Global trends in electrification and sustainability.

units.title: Electric Vehicle Architectures
units.text: Electric Vehicle Architectures Classification of electric vehicles (BEV, HEV, PHEV, FCEV), EV layouts and component placement, drivetrain architectures (FWD, RWD, AWD), comparison of ICE and EV systems. EV Performance Metrics Range, efficiency, power, and acceleration, battery fundamentals and characteristics.

units.title: Electric Motors and Power Electronics Systems for Evs
units.text: Electric Motors and Power Electronics Systems for Evs Electric motors for EV applications: DC motors, Brushless DC motors (BLDC), Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM), Induction motors, Motor operating characteristics, Power electronics for electric vehicles: Transmission systems for electric vehicles; Principles and operation of regenerative braking systems.

units.title: Vehicle Dynamics and Control
units.text: Vehicle Dynamics and Control Longitudinal vehicle dynamics, Traction and braking systems, Regenerative braking control, Steering systems and stability; Basics of ABS (Anti-lock Braking System), ESC (Electronic Stability Control), and torque vectoring.

units.title: Safety Standards and Emerging Technologies
units.text: Safety Standards and Emerging Technologies Functional safety (ISO26262-Overview), Electrical safety in Evs, Crash safety consideration, Solid state batteries, Autonomous and connected vehicles, AI in vehicle systems, Sustainability and lifecycle assessment.

text_books: 1. Mehrdad Ehsani, Yimin Gao, Stefano Longo, Kambiz Ebrahimi, Modern Electric, Hybrid Electric, and Fuel Cell Vehicles, 3rd Edition, CRC Press, 2018. 2. G.K. Awari, V.S. Kumbhar, R.B. Tirpude, Automotive Systems Principles and Practice, CRC Press, 2021
reference_books: 1. J.D. Halderman, C. Ward, Electric and Hybrid Electric Vehicles, 1st Edition, Pearson, 2021 2. Alexander Kossiakoff, Steven M. Biemer, Samuel J. Seymour, David A. Flanigan, Systems Engineering Principles and Practice, 3rd Edition, Wiley, 2020
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed to introduce the fundamentals of automation and its importance in mechanical engineering industries. This course helps the students to understand the basic concepts of automated systems, including sensors, actuators, mechanisms, and fluid power elements used in manufacturing and material handling. Students also develop an understanding of the integration of mechanical systems with automation components and the role of experimentation and simulation in realizing automated processes.

outcomes.text: Explain fundamentals, applications, and types of automation drives in manufacturing
Identify sensors and actuators used in automated mechanical systems.
Analyze mechanisms and motion transfer used in mechanical automation systems.
Illustrate fluid power components and their role in automation systems.
Demonstrate automation concepts through experimentation and simulations.

units.title: Introduction to Automation
units.text: Introduction to Automation Definition of automation, need for automation in industries, evolution of automation, manual, semi-automatic and automatic systems, levels of automation, advantages and limitations of automation. Types and Applications Applications of automation in manufacturing, types of automation drives – mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, comparison of automation drives.

units.title: Basic Elements of an Automated System
units.text: Basic Elements of an Automated System Basic structure of automated system, input–process–output concept, sensors and their role in automation, classification of sensors – contact and non-contact, proximity sensors – inductive, capacitive, photoelectric, magnetic. Principles and working Basic principles of sensing, actuators used in mechanical automation, linear and rotary actuators, comparison between sensors and actuators.

units.title: Mechanical Automation and Mechanisms
units.text: Mechanical Automation and Mechanisms Role of mechanisms in automation, motion transfer and motion conversion, mechanisms used in automated machines, slider–crank mechanism, cam and follower mechanism, Geneva mechanism, four-bar linkage. Use Cases Applications of mechanisms in assembly, packaging and indexing systems, sequencing of mechanical operations using mechanisms.

units.title: Fluid Power and Automation System Integration
units.text: Fluid Power and Automation System Integration Role of fluid power in automation, overview and comparison of hydraulic and pneumatic systems, basic components of hydraulic systems, hydraulic power pack and its components, basic components of pneumatic systems, air preparation system, Filter–Regulator–Lubricator (FRL) unit. System Amalgamation Interaction of mechanical systems with sensors and actuators, overview of automated assembly and material handling systems, introduction to automation system simulation.

text_books: 1. Mikell P. Groover, Automation, Production Systems, and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing, 6th Edition, Pearson Education, 2020. 2. W. Bolton, Mechatronics: Electronic Control Systems in Mechanical Engineering, 7th Edition, Pearson Education, 2021.
reference_books: 1. Anthony Esposito, Fluid Power with Applications, 8th Edition, Pearson Education, 2020. 2. Clarence W. de Silva, Mechatronics: Fundamentals and Applications, 3rd Edition, CRC Press, 2023.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course gives comprehensive introduction to nanotechnology including Nano materials and the knowledge of various measurement techniques at the nanoscale, and different engineering applications

outcomes.text: Understand fundamentals of nanoscience and nanotechnology
Apply Experimental Characterization Techniques
Analyze synthesis methods and concepts in nano systems
Evaluate carbon nanostructures and their functional Properties
Develop engineering solutions using nanotechnology.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Definition and concept of Nanotechnology, History of Nanotechnology, Nanotechnology as Emerging Technology. Fundamental Scientific Concepts Nano-Bio-Physics-Chemistry Convergence, Concepts from Solid State Physics: Crystal structures, size dependence of properties, semiconductors, energy bands, excitations.

units.title: Experimental Methods of Investigation
units.text: Experimental Methods of Investigation Introduction to experimental investigation methods in Nanotechnology, Sample Preparation Methods for Nanoparticle Study. Measurement of Properties and Characterization Technique Structural & Morphological Characterization of nanomaterials using Electron Microscopy, Scanning Probe Microscopy, X-Ray techniques, Use of Optical & Spectroscopic Characterization Techniques, Evaluation of Mechanical, Thermal and Electric properties of nanomaterials.

units.title: Synthesis Methods in Nano Systems
units.text: Synthesis Methods in Nano Systems Synthesis methods-Common Issues, Size Control, Magnetic nanomaterials, Anisotropic nanomaterials. Theoretical Concepts in Nano Systems Magic Number and its uses, Bulk semiconductors and their optical properties, Quantum wells, wires and dots, Band gap engineering.

units.title: Carbon Nanostructures
units.text: Carbon Nanostructures Carbon clusters; Fullerenes Cluster stability and properties, Carbon Nanotubes- Fabrication; Arc discharge method, Laser ablation, Chemical Vapour Deposition (CVD), Single-walled vs. multi-walled CNTs Properties and Applications of Carbon Nanotubes Mechanical & Electrical properties, Applications (Computers, Fuel Cells, Chemical Sensors, Mechanical Reinforcement, Field Emission & Shielding).

units.title: Nano-Devices and Nano-Fabrication Technologies
units.text: Nano-Devices and Nano-Fabrication Technologies MEMS (Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems) & NEMS (Nano-Electro-Mechanical Systems) - Fabrication and applications, Nanocoatings, Nanolithography Applied Nanomaterials and Functional Applications Nanomaterials for Environmental Remediation, Nanofluids for enhancement in cooling and heating, Nano lubricants, Nano sensors, Energy storage devices.

text_books: 1. T. Pradeep, A Textbook of Nanoscience and Nanotechnology, 1st Edition, Mc Graw Hill Education, 2017. (classic) 2. C. Binns, Introduction to Nanoscience and Nanotechnology, 2nd Edition, Wiley, 2021.

program: B Tech (Civil, Mechanical, and Mechatronics, EXTC, Computer) / MBA Tech (Computer)
prerequisites: Calculus, Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
objectives: This course aims to instill in students an understanding of Complex Variables, Laplace Transforms, Fourier series, Fourier Transforms, and their applications. It equips the students with the mathematics fundamentals necessary to formulate, solve, and analyze complex engineering problems.

outcomes.text: Explain the concepts of differentiation of complex variables.
Evaluate complex integrals using contour integration techniques.
Execute Laplace transforms on mathematical functions.
Apply Fourier series to represent periodic functions and identify orthogonal sets.
Determine Fourier Transforms for standard functions.
Utilize the techniques of Complex variables and transforms to solve engineering problems.

units.title: Complex Variables Differentiation
units.text: Complex Variables Differentiation Complex differentiation, Cauchy-Riemann equation, analytic functions, harmonic functions, harmonic conjugate, Elementary analytic functions (exponential, trigonometric, logarithmic functions), Conformal mappings: definition and problems, Mobius transformation and their properties.

units.title: Complex Variables Integration
units.text: Complex Variables Integration Contour Integrals: definition and problems, Cauchy-Goursat theorem, Cauchy Integral formula, Zeros and singularities of analytic functions.

units.title: Laplace Transforms
units.text: Laplace Transforms Definition of Laplace Transform, Laplace Transform of 1, eat , sin at, cos at, sinh at, cosh at, tn , Properties of Laplace Transforms: Linearity property, First and second shifting theorems of Laplace Transform, Change of scale property, , , , . Evaluation of Inverse Laplace Transform by partial fraction, Convolution theorem, Laplace Transforms of Periodic functions, Unit step functions, Dirac delta functions. Applications to solve ordinary differential equations.

units.title: Fourier Series
units.text: Fourier Series Orthogonality and Orthonormality, Periodic function, Trigonometric conditions, formulae (Derivative of Fourier coefficients a0, an ,bn is not expected), Fourier Series of Functions for the interval and . Functions having points of discontinuity, Even and odd functions, half range sine and cosine expansions, Complex form of Fourier Series. Applications to solve Wave equation, Heat equation and Laplace equation.

units.title: Fourier Transforms
units.text: Fourier Transforms Fourier integral theorem, Fourier sine and cosine integral. Fourier Transform, Fourier Sine Transform, Fourier Cosine Transform, Properties of Fourier Transforms (Linearity property, Change of scale property, Shifting property), Inverse Fourier Transform, Inverse Fourier Sine Transform, Inverse Fourier Cosine Transform, Finite Fourier Transform. Applications to solve ordinary differential equations.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech All Programs
objectives: The objective of the course is to develop proficiency in written technical communication so that they are able to produce documents of the kind required in the workplace, such as reports and letters, that are sound, effective, coherent and error-free

outcomes.text: Apply the fundamentals of written communication to create written documents that are coherent, error-free and well organized
Develop the ability to create effective and persuasive business correspondence, such as letters and emails, that follow etiquette and are able to achieve the desired outcomes
Create basic reports such as memo, letter and survey-based report, using their understanding of report writing

units.text: Principles of Effective Writing Salient features of sentence construction, Paragraph writing, 7 Cs of communication, Making outlines, Writing for the Web

units.title: Writing Skills

units.title: Business Correspondence
units.text: Business Correspondence Business letter writing principles and types, Business email writing subject line, recipient design, language, structuring content, framing, etiquette, cultural sensitivity

units.title: Report Writing

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to instill in students a sound knowledge of probability theory and statistical techniques. It equips the students with intermediate to advanced level concepts and tools in probability and statistics that help them tackle relevant problems within engineering domain.

outcomes.text: solve problems involving random variables, probability distributions and testing of hypothesis, correlation and regression
identify suitable probability distribution and testing techniques to solve related problems
apply knowledge of random variables, probability distributions, measures of central tendency, correlation and regression to solve real life problems
analyse data samples using statistical methods.

units.title: Basic Probability
units.text: Basic Probability Probability spaces, conditional probability, independence; Bayes theorem.

units.title: Random variables and Probability Distributions
units.text: Random variables and Probability Distributions Discrete random variables, probability mass function, cumulative distribution function, Independent random variables, Continuous random variables, distribution functions and densities, expectation, variance, raw and central moments of random variables, Binomial distribution, Poisson approximation to the binomial distribution, Normal distribution.

units.title: Bivariate Distributions
units.text: Bivariate Distributions Definition of Bivariate Distribution and their properties, Conditional densities.

units.title: Basic Statistics
units.text: Basic Statistics Measures of Central tendency; Moments, Moment generating function, skewness, kurtosis. Mean and variance of Binomial distribution & Poisson distribution, Moments, skewness & kurtosis for Normal distribution.

units.title: Testing of hypothesis
units.text: Testing of hypothesis: Point estimation, Interval estimate and Confidence interval, Criteria for good estimates, Null and Alternate hypothesis, Test Statistic, Type I and Type II errors, One-tailed and two-tailed test, Critical region, Large sample statistical test for mean, Large sample statistical test for proportion, t-test for small samples, Test for variance- F test, Chi-square test for Goodness of fit and independence of attributes, Analysis of variance.

units.title: Linear Statistical Models
units.text: Linear Statistical Models: Scatter diagram, Linear regression and correlation, Least squares method, Rank correlation, Multiple regression.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at providing adequate understanding of the fundamentals of stresses and strains in deformable bodies subjected to various types of static loads. It is designed to impart the knowledge of basic concepts of deformation & deflection, identifying the relevant tests to be performed on beams and power transmitting shafts. It develops the ability to assess the strength of engineering materials and subsequently examine the failure criteria of structural members using relevant analysis.

outcomes.text: Understand the resultant stresses induced in beams and other structural members
Evaluate the deformations of various determinate beams
Analyse stress on thin shells due to internal pressure
Calculate the stresses in circular torsion members.

units.title: Stress and Strain
units.text: Stress and Strain: Strain, modulus of elasticity, modulus of rigidity, bulk modulus, yield stress, ultimate stress, factor of safety, shear stress, Poisson’s ratio, analysis of members made of composite materials.

units.title: Stresses in Beams due to transverse loading
units.text: Stresses in Beams due to transverse loading: Shear Force and Bending Moment: Axial force, shear force and bending moment diagrams for statically determinate beams for different types of loading. Simple Theory of Bending: Flexure formula for straight beams, simple problems involving application of flexure formula, section modulus, moment of resistance of a section. Shear Stress in Beams: Distribution of shear stress across plane sections used commonly for structural purposes.

units.title: Simple Theory of Torsion
units.text: Simple Theory of Torsion: Torsion of circular shafts – solid and hollow, stresses in power transmission shafts (including shafts in series and parallel).

units.title: Bending Moment Combined with Axial Loads
units.text: Bending Moment Combined with Axial Loads: Application to members subjected to eccentric loads, core of a section, problems on chimneys involving lateral loads.

units.title: Principal Stresses
units.text: Principal Stresses: Stresses in a tensile member, stresses due to pure shearing, stresses due to two mutually perpendicular direct stresses, stress on an oblique plane of a member subjected to two dimensional stress systems (General). Principal planes and principal stresses, maximum shear stress, Mohr’s circle concept.

units.title: Deflection of Beams
units.text: Deflection of Beams: Deflection of cantilevers, simply supported and overhanging beams using methods like Moment-Area, double integration and Macaulay’s method for different types of loading.

units.title: Thin Shells
units.text: Thin Shells: Stresses in thin cylindrical and spherical shells subjected to internal pressure. Efficiency of Rivetted Joints.

text_books: 1. James M. Gere, Barry J. Goodno, “Mechanics of Materials” – SI Edition, Cengage Learning, 8th Edition, 2012. 2. Ferdinand P. Beer, E Russell Johnson Jr. John T. De Wolf, David Mazurek, “Mechanics of Materials”, McGraw Hill Education, 7th Edition, 2015.
reference_books: 1. Andrew Pytel, Jaan Kiusalaas, “Mechanics of Materials”- SI Edition, Cengage Learning, 2nd Edition, 2012. 2. William Nash, Merle Potter, “Schaum's Outline of Strength of Materials”, McGraw Hill Professional, 7th Edition, 2020

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at developing the detailed understanding of various mechanism used in devices or machines. This course focuses on analysis of the motion of mechanisms and to design mechanisms that yield the desired motion. The course is designed for the students to understand and master the concepts of displacement, velocity and acceleration of simple mechanisms and machine components. These include cam profile and its analysis, gear kinematics with gear train calculations, belt drives and chain drives, and friction clutches and brakes.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of links, mechanisms, machines, brakes, clutches and gyroscope
Analyse planar mechanism for displacement, velocity and acceleration graphically and analytically
Construct various type of Cam profiles and analyze the standard motion of the follower
Compare different type of gears, gear-trains and its applications.

units.title: Introduction of Mechanisms and Machines
units.text: Introduction of Mechanisms and Machines: Concepts of Kinematics and Dynamics, Mechanisms and Machines, Planar and Spatial Mechanisms, Kinematic Pairs, Kinematic Chains, Kinematic Diagrams, Kinematic Inversion, four bar chain, single and double Slider Crank Mechanisms and their Inversions, Degrees of Freedom, Mobility and range of movement - Kutzbach and Grubler’s criterion, Number Synthesis, Grashof’s criterion, straight line mechanisms.

units.title: Velocity and Acceleration Analysis
units.text: Velocity and Acceleration Analysis: Velocity and Acceleration analysis: (Graphical approach) Velocity analysis: instantaneous centre of rotation method, relative velocity method for four bar pin jointed linkages and four bar slider crank linkages. Velocity and Acceleration analysis - relative method four bar pin jointed linkages and four bar slider crank linkages.

units.title: CAM
units.text: CAM: Types of cams, Types of followers, Follower displacement programming, Derivatives of follower Motion, Motions of follower, Layout of cam profiles.

units.title: Belt, Ropes and Chains
units.text: Belt, Ropes and Chains: Types of belt drive, Velocity ratio, Slip, Pulley arrangement, Length of belt, Law of belting, Ratio of friction tension, Power transmitted, Centrifugal effects on belts, Maximum power transmitted, Creep, Chains, Chain length, Angular speed ratio, Classification of chains.

units.title: Friction Clutches and Brakes
units.text: Friction Clutches and Brakes: Introduction to friction clutches, Rolling Friction, Types of Clutches, Types of brakes, Block and Shoe brakes, Differential band brake, Internal expanding shoe brake.

units.title: Gears and Gear Trains
units.text: Gears and Gear Trains: Terminology, Law of Gearing, Characteristics of involute and cycloidal action, Interference and undercutting, centre distance variation, minimum number of teeth, contact ratio, spur, helical, spiral bevel and worm gears, problems. Gear Trains: Synthesis of Simple, compound & reverted gear trains, Analysis of epicyclic gear trains

text_books: 1. Thomas Beven, “Theory of Machines”, Pearson, 3rd Edition, 2009. 2. S. S. Rattan, “Theory of Machines”, Tata McGraw Hill, New Delhi, 3rd Edition, 2009.
reference_books: 1. John Uicker, G R Pennock J. E. Shigley, “Theory of Mechanisms and Machines”, University Press, 3rd Edition, 2010. 2. P. L. Ballaney, “Theory of Machines and Mechanisms”, Khanna Publishing, New Delhi, 24th Edition, 2005.

program: B. Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course describes the application of Engineering Thermodynamics to model the energy conversion phenomenon. With this course one can impart knowledge of air compressors and components of steam power system. This course provides basics of I.C engines, refrigeration systems and air conditioning systems and also build a bridge for these courses.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental concepts of applied thermodynamics
Analyze the components of steam power systems
Investigate the concept of I.C. Engines, air compressors and refrigeration and air conditioning system.

units.title: Reciprocating air compressors
units.text: Reciprocating air compressors: Working principle, work done, Effect of clearance volume, Single and multistage compressors, Volumetric efficiency, Intercooling in multistage compressors, calculation of power requirement, Rotary compressors. Review of Thermodynamics, Vapour Power cycles, Binary Vapour Cycle, Combined Cycle and Co-generation.

units.title: Steam Generators
units.text: Steam Generators: Fire Tube Boilers, Water Tube Boilers, Boiler Mountings and Accessories, High Pressure Boilers. Draught, Performance of Boilers, Combustion of Fuel.

units.title: Nozzles and Diffusers
units.text: Nozzles and Diffusers: Theory and Design, Efficiency and Critical Pressure, General Relationship and supersaturated Flow. Steam Turbines: Impulse and Reaction turbine Principles - Compounding – Types - Velocity diagrams for simple and multistage turbines - Speed regulations – Governors.

units.title: Condensers and cooling towers
units.text: Condensers and cooling towers: Classification of condenser, air leakage, condenser performance parameters. Cooling tower design.

units.title: Refrigeration
units.text: Refrigeration: Refrigeration cycles, Reversed Carnot cycle, Vapour compression system, Vapour absorption refrigeration system. Refrigerants: Their classification and desirable properties. Air-Conditioning: Principles of air-conditioning, Types of Air- conditioning Systems, Summer and Winter air -conditioning. Cryogenics: Introduction and applications.

units.title: IC Engines
units.text: IC Engines: Classification, Working of SI & CI engine, Port timing and Valve timing diagram, Performance testing of I.C Engines, Heat balance calculations.

text_books: 1. P. K. Nag, “Basics and Applied Thermodynamics”, Tata McGraw Hill, 2nd Edition, 2008. 2. P. K. Nag, “Power Plant Engineering”, Tata McGraw Hill, 4th Edition, 2016. 3. Vanwvylen & Sonntag, “Classical Thermodynamics”, Wiley Eastern, 5th Edition, 1994.
reference_books: 1. Y. Cengel and M. Boles, “Thermodynamics -An Engineering Approach”, Tata McGraw Hill, 6th Edition, 2008. 2. M. J. Moran, H. N. Shapiro, D. D. Boettner, M. B. Bailey, “Fundamentals of Engineering Thermodynamics”, John Wiley and Sons, 7th Edition, 2011.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is aimed at training the students on lathe machine with different turning operations like such as plain, taper turning along with operations like facing, thread cutting, grooving, knurling and wire drawing die on metals.

outcomes.text: Apply different operations on lathe like plain, taper turning, facing, grooving and knurling
Operate different operations like screw cutting and threading
Perform different operation on lathe like drilling, boring, counter boring, internal taper turning.

units.text: Job on lathe performing plain and taper turning.
Job on precision turning and screw cutting.
Assembly of Two pieces using operations like drilling, boring, counter boring, internal taper turning and broaching operations.

program: B. Tech. Mechanical Engineering
objectives: This course aims to introduce students to the concepts of dynamical motion of rigid body and to develop their skill in applying these concepts to understand and analyze real life phenomena.

outcomes.text: explain the motion of rigid bodies
apply the concepts of rigid body motion to interpret real world phenomena and their applications
solve advanced problems involving the dynamic motion of rigid bodies including celestial objects.

units.text: Motion and Coordinate frames, Cartesian polar and spherical coordinate frames, Displacement; Velocity; Acceleration in this frames, Particles and rigid bodies, Newton’s Law of motion, Coulomb friction damping, Viscous friction damping, Relative Motion, Motion of rigid bodies
Linear and angular Momentum, Impulse-momentum and Work- Energy principles, 3D rigid body motion, 3D rotation, Euler angles

Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion, Satellite orbits, Weather Satellites and Sensing Systems, Operational polar orbiting and geostationary satellites, weather sensors, Satellite data archives , Ground based sensors

text_books: 1. N.C. Rana and P S Joag, “Classical Mechanics”, McGraw Hill Education, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Herbert Goldstein, Charles P Poole, John Safko, “Classical Mechanics”, 3rd edition. 2011.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics
objectives: This course aims to understand the multidisciplinary nature of environmental sciences, greenhouse effect and climate change. It also aims to discuss the basics of natural resources, biodiversity, environmental pollution.

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of natural resources, ecosystem and biodiversity
Relate the various aspects of environmental pollutions with its cause and effect
Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change.

units.title: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science
units.text: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science Definition, scope and importance of environmental sciences.

Natural Resources • Natural resources: Forest resources, Water resources, Mineral resources, Food resources. • Energy resources: Growing energy needs, renewable and non- renewable energy sources, use of alternate energy sources.

Ecosystems • Concept of an ecosystem. • Structure and function of an ecosystem. • Food chains, food webs and ecological pyramids. • Introduction, types, characteristic features of the following ecosystem:- a. Forest ecosystem b. Grassland ecosystem c. Desert ecosystem d. Aquatic ecosystems.

Biodiversity • Definition: genetic, species and ecosystem diversity. • Value of biodiversity: consumptive use, productive use. • Threats to biodiversity: habitat loss, poaching of wildlife, man- wildlife conflicts.

Environmental Pollution • Definition, Cause and effects for Air pollution, Water pollution, Soil pollution, Marine pollution, Noise pollution, Thermal pollution, Nuclear hazards and Solid waste pollution.
The Science of Climate Change • Greenhouse effect • Global warming • Global environmental changes • Acid rain • Ozone layer depletion • Carbon footprint

text_books: 1. Erach Bharucha, “Textbook of Environmental Studies”, University Press, 2nd Edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. MP Poonia & SC Sharma, “Environmental Studies”, Khanna Publishing House, 1st Edition, 2017. 2. Rajagopalan, “Environmental Studies”, Oxford University Press, Third Edition, 2015.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: 1. To inculcate human values to grow as a responsible human being 2. To maintain ethical conduct in discharging professional duties

outcomes.text: understand the engineering code of ethics and be able to apply them as necessary
understand moral complexities in many engineering activities and decision-making processes
understand some of the contemporary issues in the engineering professions
effectively communicate their knowledge and understanding of engineering ethics.

units.text: Introduction to Ethics-  Concept of morals and ethics,  Study of engineering ethics;  Laws and ethics;  Personal and professional ethics.
Professional Practice in Engineering-  Common morality ASME code of ethics,  Technical codes and standards,  Accepted standards of Engineering practice and the standard of care.

Ethics as design-doing justice to moral Problem-  Discuss about ethics as a design to solve moral problems  Comparison between moral problems and engineering design problems;  Moral lessons from design problems;  Implications of the dynamic character of problem situations.

Rights and Responsibilities of Engineers-  Moral responsibilities;  Conflicts of interests;  Confidentiality,  Engineers, organizations and ethics,  Engineer-manager relationships;  loyalty;  The concept of whistleblowing.

Responsibility for the Environment-  Rapid Technological growth and depletion of resources,  Reports of the Club of Rome.  Limits of growth: sustainable development  Energy Crisis: Renewable Energy Resources  Environmental degradation and pollution.  Eco-friendly Technologies.  Environmental Regulations,  Environmental Ethics  Appropriate Technology,  Movement of Schumacher; later developments of Technology and developing notions.  Problems of Technology transfer,  Technology assessment impact analysis.  Problems of man, machine, interaction,  Impact of assembly line and automation.  Human centered Technology

text_books: 1. M.W. Martin and R. Schinzinger, “Ethics in Engineering”, McGraw-Hill, Second Edition, 2005. 2. Charles B. Fleddermann, “Engineering Ethics”, Pearson, Third Edition, 2007. 3. P.A. Vesilind and A. S Gunn, “Engineering Ethics and Environment”, Cambridge University Press, First Edition, 1998.
reference_books: 1. Caroline Whitbeck, “Ethics in Engineering – Practice and Research”, Cambridge University Press, Second Edition, 2011.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to introduce the students to the fundamentals of material removal processes including non-conventional machining processes. The students will be able to identify/control the appropriate process parameters and possible defects of manufacturing processes.

outcomes.text: Classify the metal cutting processes with tool geometry and forces of cutting
Choose appropriate method of machining, to produce required geometrical features in components
Analyze various process parameters that affect machining processes

units.title: Metal cutting
units.text: Metal cutting Tool Geometry, forces in single point cutting, tool wear and tool life, formation of chips and types of chips, mechanics of orthogonal and oblique cutting, chip thickness ratio, velocity relationship in orthogonal cutting, Merchant’s circle diagram, analysis of stresses and strains and work done during metal cutting, friction and thermal aspects of metal cutting, cutting fluids, types of cutting fluids

units.title: Shaper and Planer
units.text: Shaper and Planer Introduction, construction, working and operations performed on Shapers, Planers and slotters. Milling Machines Types of milling machines, tools and their geometry, various operations on milling machine.

units.title: Drilling Machines
units.text: Drilling Machines Types of machines, operations such as drilling, boring, reaming, spot facing, counter boring and sinking, tapping, drill speed and feeds. Boring and Broaching Machine Classification-horizontal and vertical boring machine, types of broaching machines, advantages, limitations and applications of broaching.

units.title: Non-conventional Machining Processes
units.text: Non-conventional Machining Processes Introduction, classification and overview of non-conventional machining processes, abrasive jet machining (AJM), abrasive water jet machining (AWJM), electric discharge machining (EDM), electro-chemical machining (ECM), laser beam machining and allied processes

units.title: Processing of Plastics
units.text: Processing of Plastics General aspects, methods of processing of plastics, compression moulding, transfer moulding, injection moulding, thermoforming, Joining of thermoplastic.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Calculus, Engineering Mechanics, Classical Physics
objectives: The objective of this course is to familiarize the learner with the electric and hybrid vehicle architecture, technologies and fundamentals. The use of tools to design and simulate electric and hybrid vehicles is also covered.

outcomes.text: Explain electric and hybrid vehicle technology and its dynamics
Compare motors, batteries and controllers used in electric and hybrid vehicles
Evaluate incentives and barriers encountered in the use of EV technology
Simulate electric hybrid vehicle systems

units.title: Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Introduction
units.text: Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Introduction EVs and hybrids, correlation of cost and emissions, some myth busting facts, EV layouts and architecture, hybrid vehicle layouts.

units.title: Vehicle Dynamics
units.text: Vehicle Dynamics Introduction, Forces acting on a Rolling vehicle, Power required for rolling motion, Modeling Real-World conditions.

units.title: Motors
units.text: Motors Introduction, the Lorentz Force law, Coulomb’s, Biot-Savarts law, brush and brushless motors, reluctance Motors, Faraday’s law, AC induction motors, motor efficiency, maximum acceleration.

units.title: Batteries
units.text: Batteries Introduction, battery fundamentals, lithium-ion batteries, battery characteristics, electric vehicle charging.

units.title: Controllers
units.text: Controllers Introduction, circuit elements, step-down DC controllers, step-up/down DC controllers, AC controllers.

units.title: Incentives and Barriers
units.text: Incentives and Barriers Introduction, national incentives, state incentives, FAME-I, FAME-II, e-AMRIT. Barriers to development of EV infrastructure in India.

units.title: Modeling and Simulation of Electric and Hybrid Vehicles
units.text: Modeling and Simulation of Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Fundamentals of vehicle system modeling, HEV Modeling using simulation software.

text_books: 1. Per Enge, Nick Enge, Stephen Zoepf, Electric Vehicle Engineering, 1st Edition, McGraw Hill, 2021. 2. Tom Denton, Electric and Hybrid Vehicles, Roultedge, 2nd Edition, Taylor & Francis Group, 2020.
