Chitra A., S. Padamanaban, Jens Bo Holm-Nielsenm S. Himavathi, Artificial Intelligent Techniques for Electric and Hybrid Electric Vehicles, 1st Edition, Scrivener Publishing - Wiley, 2020.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to appraise the students with different types of wastes and defects during manufacturing and the remedial steps to eliminate them. It imparts knowledge associated with aligning production processes with customer expectations and benchmark with efficient business processes.

outcomes.text: Summarize the relationship between Work in Progress and cycle time
Articulate the integration of batch size, setup, manufacturing processes and waste
Apply lean manufacturing techniques to manufacturing, projects and service industries

units.title: Introduction to Lean Manufacturing
units.text: Introduction to Lean Manufacturing History of lean, fundamental purpose of lean manufacturing, comparison to other methods. The seven Wastes, their causes and the effects, Implication of lean manufacturing – traditional vs lean manufacturing.

Tools of Lean Manufacturing 5S Principles, workplace organization, Process mapping / Value stream mapping, pull Systems (Kanban and WIP systems), error proofing and set-up reduction, total quality management (TQM), total productive maintenance (TPM), Toyota production systems, Ford production systems.

units.title: Value Stream Mapping (VSM)
units.text: Value Stream Mapping (VSM) Preparation for building a current state VSM, building a current state map (principles, concepts, loops, and methodology). Application to the factory simulation scenario. Line balancing, Poka Yoke, kanban, overall equipment effectiveness.

units.title: Just - In - time Manufacturing (JIT)
units.text: Just - In - time Manufacturing (JIT) Introduction, elements of JIT, uniform production rate, pull vs push method, kanban system, small lot size, quick and inexpensive set-up, continuous Improvement, optimized production technology.

units.title: Designing for Quality
units.text: Designing for Quality Introduction to concurrent engineering, quality function deployment (QFD) and failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA), concept, methodology and application (with case studies). Quality in service sectors: Characteristics of service sectors, quality dimensions in service sectors, measuring quality in different service sectors.

units.title: Six Sigma
units.text: Six Sigma Meaning of six sigma, why six sigma? six sigma improvement model, DMAIC and DMADV principle, building six sigma organization and culture, six sigma application, case studies.

units.title: Quality Circle
units.text: Quality Circle Quality circle structure, it’s operation, characteristics of quality circle, developing quality circle in organization, basic problem-solving techniques.

text_books: 1. M.K. Khanduja, Lean Manufacturing Implementation made easy, Inversio Solutions LLP, 2021. 2. Pascal Dennis, Lean Production Simplified, 3rd Edition, CRC Press, 2015.
reference_books: 1. James Edge, “Lean Six Sigma”, Bravex Publications, 2020. 2. Jeffrey K. Liker, “The Toyota way”, 2nd Edition, McGraw Hill Publications, 2021.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course covers alternative fuels and the analysis of their properties. The course also provides a comprehensive overview of the recent advances in the production and utilization aspects of different types of liquid and gaseous alternative fuels.

outcomes.text: Classify different alternate fuels used for spark ignition and compression ignition engines
Compare different alternate fuels and energy system in terms of their characteristics
Analyze environmental, social, and technological issues related to the future widespread use of alternative fuels

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Estimation of petroleum reserve, need for alternate fuels, availability and properties of alternate fuels, American Society for Testing of Materials (ASTM) standards.

units.title: Liquid Fuels
units.text: Liquid Fuels Petroleum based liquid fuels and refining. Liquid Alternative Fuels Alcohols, general use of alcohols, properties as engine fuel, gasoline and alcohol blends, performance in spark ignition engine, methanol and gasoline blend, combustion characteristics in engine, emission characteristics. algae as a source for fuels. Vegetable Oils Soybean oil, jatropha, pongamia, rice bran, mahua etc. as alternate fuel and their properties, esterification of oils, biodiesel and emulsified fuels, lubricating oils composition and effect of alternate fuels.

units.title: Gaseous Alternative Fuels
units.text: Gaseous Alternative Fuels Hydrogen production, hydrogen as an alternative fuel, fuel cell, availability of compressed natural gas, properties and modification required to use in engines, performance and emission characteristics of compressed natural and liquefied natural gas in spark ignition and compression ignition engines, dimethyl ether, and hythane as an alternative fuel.

units.title: Analysis of Gaseous Bio-fuel
units.text: Analysis of Gaseous Bio-fuel Determination of methane, carbon dioxide , carbon monoxide, hydrogen sulphide, hydrogen in biogas , volatile fatty acid (VFA) and its constituents, alkalinity (total and partial), biological oxygen demand (BOD), Chemical oxygen demand (COD) and conversion efficiency.

units.title: Analysis of Fuel Qualities/Properties
units.text: Analysis of Fuel Qualities/Properties Bomb calorimeter, Junker’s calorimeter, flash point, pour point, viscosity, kinematic viscosity, acid value, saponification, fatty acid composition, iodine value, cetane index, octane value, oxidative stability and shelf life determination.

text_books: 1. Sergio Capareda, “Introduction to Biomass Energy Conversions”, CRC Press, 2013. 2. Colin R. Ferguson, Allan T. Kirkpatrick ·, “Internal Combustion Engines: Applied Thermosciences”, Wiley, 2015.)
reference_books: 1. Sunggyu Lee, James G. Speight, Sudarshan K. Loyalka “Handbook of Alternative Fuel Technologies” CRC Press, 2018. 2. Akhilendra Pratap Singh, Avinash Kumar Agarwal, Nirendra N. Mustafi, Yogesh C. Sharma “Alternative Fuels and Their Utilization Strategies in Internal Combustion Engines” Springer Singapore, 2019. 3. Kurt Marcel, “Alternative Fuels and Petroleum Technology”, Syrawood Publishing House 2016.
lab_work: 8 to 10 Tutorial exercises based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to acquaint students with control of mechanical operations, sensors and their interfacing with microcontrollers. The course offers learning of pneumatic/hydraulic systems, electrical controls and programmable logic controllers.

outcomes.text: Identify the suitable sensors and actuators for a mechatronics systems using pneumatic and hydraulic systems and electro-pneumatic circuits
Apply suitable logic controls and develop ladder logic programming
Design an appropriate robot for given industrial applications and carryout kinematic analysis for a robot

units.title: Introduction to Automation
units.text: Introduction to Automation Definition and fundamentals of automation, reasons for automating, basic elements of an automated system, power, program and control system. Introduction of mechatronics and its block diagram representation, key elements of mechatronics, applications of mechatronics, domestic, industrial etc. Representation of mechatronic system in block diagram and concept of transfer function for each element of mechatronic system, reduction methods and its numerical treatment for represented block diagram.

units.title: Selection of Sensors and Actuators
units.text: Selection of Sensors and Actuators Criteria for selection of sensors based on requirements, principle of measurement, sensing method, performance chart etc. Displacement, temperature, acceleration, force, pressure based on static and dynamic characteristics. Actuators, selection of actuators based on principle of operation, performance characteristics, maximum loading conditions, safety etc. Principle and selection of mechano- electrical actuators, DC motors, stepper motors, solenoid actuators, servo motors, BLDC.

units.title: Pneumatics and Hydraulics
units.text: Pneumatics and Hydraulics Hydraulic and pneumatic devices, different types of valves, actuators and auxiliary elements in pneumatics and hydraulics, their applications and use of their ISO symbols, synthesis and design of circuits (up to 2 cylinders) pneumatic, electro- pneumatics and hydraulics, electrohydraulic. Discrete control system, Programming Logic Control (PLC). Introduction to PLC, architecture, ladder logic programming for different types of logic gates, latching, timers, counter, practical examples of ladder programming.

units.title: Introduction to Robotics
units.text: Introduction to Robotics Definition of robot, evolution of robots, laws of robots, international robotic standards, types of robots, selection of robots, robot classifications, degrees of freedom, robot configuration, accuracy and repeatability, specification of a robot. Robot feedback controls, point to point control and continuous path control, control system for robot joint, adaptive control, actuators and sensors, drives and transmission systems, end effectors, applications of robots.

units.title: Analysis of Robots
units.text: Analysis of Robots Grubler - kutzbach criterion, denavit - hartneberg classic algorithm for reference frames, homogeneous coordinate transformation, the homogeneous coordinate transformation matrix, the arm matrix. Kinematics of robots, forward kinematics, inverse kinematics, simple robots, 2D cartesian robot, 2D polar robot, differential robot, geared wrists and grippers.

units.title: Modeling and Simulation
units.text: Modeling and Simulation SCARA robot, deriving equations of motion, simulation of equations of motion for relevant robots. Humanoids wheeled and legged, legged locomotion and balance, arm movement and control, performance, interaction, safety and robustness, applications, case studies.

text_books: 1. W. Bolton, Mechatronics: Electronic Control Systems in Mechanical Engineering, 6th edition, Pearson education, 2015. 2. Robert J. Schilling, Fundamentals of Robotics: Analysis and Control, 1st edition, Pearson education, 2015.
reference_books: 1. Clarence W. De Silva, Farbod Khoshnoud, Saman K. Halgamuge, Maoqing Li, Mechatronics: Fundamentals and Applications, CRC press London, 2015. 2. Rany Rizk, Mariette Awad, Mechanism, Machine, Robotics and Mechatronics Sciences, Springer international publishing, 2018.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course deals with the design of marine structures subjected to different types of environmental loads and also discusses the detailed design of major and sub components of offshore structures.

outcomes.text: Identify the function of marine and multipurpose offshore structures and systems
Relate the physical problem of the fluid–structure interaction in marine structures
Design different structural components in offshore applications

units.title: Introduction to Marine Structures
units.text: Introduction to Marine Structures History of offshore structures, overview of field development, types of offshore platforms, types of ships, design codes, offshore wind turbines, wave energy converters, tidal energy converters, combined offshore energy systems, multipurpose offshore structures and systems, submerged floating tunnels, floating bridges, aquaculture and fish Farms.

units.title: Offshore Environmental Conditions
units.text: Offshore Environmental Conditions Gravity load, impact load, wind load, wave load, current load, earthquake load, ice loads, marine growth, scour.

units.title: Offshore Structures Design
units.text: Offshore Structures Design Guide for preliminary design, structure analysis, cylinder member strength, tubular joint design, fatigue analysis, topside design.

units.title: Helidecks and Boat Landing Design
units.text: Helidecks and Boat Landing Design Helideck design, design load conditions, boat landing design, riser guard design.

units.title: Construction and Installation
units.text: Construction and Installation Engineering the execution, construction process, installation process, lifting analysis.

text_books: 1. Madjid Karimirad, Constantine Michailides and Ali Nematbakhsh, Offshore mechanics: structural and fluid dynamics for recent applications, 1st Edition, John Wiley & Sons, 2018. 2. Yong Bai and Wei-Liang Jin, Marine Structural Design, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2016.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The main objective of this course is to provide basic understanding of composite materials used in various engineering applications. The course also explains mechanical properties, micromechanics and manufacturing methods of composite materials.

outcomes.text: Relate processing, characterization and applications of various composite materials
Apply failure criteria and evaluate the results of composite materials
Evaluate the relative merits of using alternatives (corresponding to various simple and composite materials) for important engineering and other applications

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Definition, history, characteristics, concept of composite materials, comparison with metals, composite materials in engineering, industrial scenario, advantages and limitations of composites

units.title: Types of Matrix Materials and Reinforcements
units.text: Types of Matrix Materials and Reinforcements Functions of a matrix, desired properties of a matrix, polymer matrix (thermosets and thermoplastics), metal matrix, ceramic matrix, carbon matrix, glass matrix etc., role and selection of reinforcement materials, types of fibers - glass fibers, boron fibers, carbon fibers, organic fibers - aramid fibers, ceramic fibers - oxide fibers and nonoxide fibers, alumina fibers, silicon carbide fibers, tungsten carbide fibers, multiphase fibers, whiskers, flakes etc.

units.title: Types of Composites
units.text: Types of Composites Based on matrix materials, polymer matrix composites (PMC), metal matrix composites (MMC), ceramic matrix composites (CMC), carbon fiber composites; based on reinforcements, fiber reinforced composites, fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) composites, laminated composites, particulate composites, polymer matrix composites (PMC) – processing, structure and properties, applications, metal matrix composites (MMC) – types, processing, properties, applications, ceramic matrix composites (CMC) - processing, properties, applications, carbon fiber composites - processing, properties, applications.

units.title: Micromechanics and Macromechanics of Composites
units.text: Micromechanics and Macromechanics of Composites Density, mechanical properties - prediction of elastic constants, elastic constants of an isotropic material, elastic constants of a lamina.

units.title: Monotonic Strength and Fracture
units.text: Monotonic Strength and Fracture Tensile strength of unidirectional fiber composites, compressive strength of unidirectional fiber composites, fracture modes in composites - single and multiple fractures, deboning and delamination fracture.

units.title: Advanced Composites
units.text: Advanced Composites Nanocomposites, hybrid composites, self-healing composites, self- reinforced composites, in-situ composites, smart composites, industrial applications of composite materials - aerospace industries, automobile and other surface transport industries, packaging industries, house hold and sports components etc., recycling of composites

text_books: 1. Krishan K. Chawla, Composite Materials: Science and Engineering, 4th edition, Springer, 2019. 2. M. Balasubramanian, Composite Materials and Processing, 1st edition (Reprint), CRC press, 2017.
reference_books: 1. S. Mazumdar, Composites manufacturing: materials, product, and process engineering, 1st edition, CRC press, 2002. 2. F.C. Campbell Jr, Manufacturing processes for advanced composites, 1st edition, Elsevier, 2004.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course focusses on the application of classical mechanics to various biological problems by combining the fields of biology and physiology. This course is concerned with the application of principles of mechanics to the conceptualization, design, development and analysis of equipment and systems as applied to human body.

outcomes.text: Correlate mechanics, biomechanics and kinesiology and differentiate between their uses in the analysis of human movement
Relate the reference positions, planes, and axes associated with the human body
Evaluate the skeletal considerations for movement and the different mechanics involved in bones

units.title: Basic Terminology
units.text: Basic Terminology Biomechanics, kinesiology, anatomy, functional anatomy linear motion, angular motion, kinematics, kinetics, statics and dynamics.

units.title: Kinematic Concepts for Analyzing Human Motion
units.text: Kinematic Concepts for Analyzing Human Motion Linear, angular and general motion, anatomical reference position, planes and axes, joint movement terminology, spatial reference systems, analyzing human movement and tools for measuring kinematic quantities.

units.title: Applications of Statics to Biomechanics
units.text: Applications of Statics to Biomechanics Skeletal joints, skeletal muscles, mechanics of the elbow, mechanics of the shoulder, mechanics of the spinal column, mechanics of the hip, mechanics of the knee and mechanics of the ankle.

units.title: Skeletal Considerations for Movement
units.text: Skeletal Considerations for Movement Bone tissue function, composition of bone tissue, macroscopic structure of bone, bone formation, strength and stiffness of bone, loads applied to bone, stress fractures, articular cartilage, fibrocartilage and ligaments.

text_books: 1. Joseph Hamill, Kathleen M. Knutzen, Timothy R. Derrick, Biomechanical Basis of Human Movement, 4th Edition, Wolters Kluwer, 2015. 2. Hall, S.J. Basic Biomechanics, 7th Edition, McGraw-Hill Education, 2012.
reference_books: 1. Nihat Özkaya, David Goldsheyder, Margareta Nordin, Fundamentals of Biomechanics Equilibrium, Motion, and Deformation, 4th Edition, Springer, 2017. 2. Peterson, D.R. and Bronzino, J.D, Biomechanics: principles and practices, CRC Press, 2015.
lab_work: 8 to 10 Tutorial exercises based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Manufacturing Processes I and II, Machine Drawing
objectives: The objective of the course is to impart introductory knowledge of Additive Manufacturing (AM) and its capabilities in the modern digital manufacturing industries. The course is structured to acquaint the students with the operating principles and applications of most prominent technologies in the field of additive manufacturing.

outcomes.text: Compare the fundamental principles of various additive manufacturing technologies in terms of material requirements, manufacturing technologies and applications
Identify critical areas where AM can be applied to create value for the product
Apply the necessary skills in selecting the right AM process for a given application

units.title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
units.text: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing Introduction to AM, history of AM, definition, distinction between AM, CNC & other digital manufacturing techniques, reasons to use AM, classifications of AM processes, design for additive manufacturing (DfAM), AM industry: present and future, AM process chain, AM file formats (STL, 3MF, AMF, PLY, VRML, and LEO), part orientation, support generation, model slicing, contour generation, machine set-up, build file preparation.

units.title: Classification of Additive Manufacturing Techniques
units.text: Classification of Additive Manufacturing Techniques Material Extrusion: Process mechanism, process parameters, extrusion of: ceramics, metals, biomaterials, composites, contour crafting, concrete printing Vat Polymerization: Process mechanism, process parameters, advantages, disadvantages, applications, Digital Light Processing (DLP), recent advances, Large-Scale Rapid Liquid Printing. Binder & material jetting processes: Binder jettng process workflow, material requirements, binder-powder interaction, binder properties. Material Jetting process workflow, thermal and piezoelectric inkjet, material jetting fluid mechanics, drop-on-demand and continuous methods of MJ. Powder bed fusion AM process: Selective laser sintering (SLS), process mechanism, process parameters, selective laser melting (SLM), process workflow and material requirements, powder melting mechanisms, electron beam melting (EBM) process. Sheet Lamination AM Processes: Process mechanism, process parameters, ultrasonic additive manufacturing (UAM), ultrasonic welding fundamentals, UAM process parameters Directed Energy Deposition (DED) Processes: Process workflow, materials feeding for DED: powder (Laser Engineered Net Shaping) and wire, process parameters, cold spray.

units.title: Post- Processing
units.text: Post- Processing Product quality evaluation, need for post-processing, support material removal, surface finish improvement, aesthetic improvement, property enhancements using non-thermal and thermal techniques.

units.title: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM)
units.text: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM) Design guidelines: part orientation, support, geometry considerations, layer thickness, part size, material consideration, residual stress, topology optimization, case studies on design for AM.

units.title: Applications of AM & Industry 4.0
units.text: Applications of AM & Industry 4.0 Aerospace, biomedical, defence, automobile, rapid tooling, reverse engineering, economic consideration, Industry 4.0 for AM, case studies on application of AM in various industries.

text_books: 1. Gibson I, Rosen D W, Stucker B, Additive Manufacturing Technologies: Rapid Prototyping to Direct Digital Manufacturing, 2nd Edition, Springer, 2015. 2. Filemon Schöffer, Ben Redwood, Brian Garret, The 3D Printing Handbook: Technologies, design and applications, 3D Hubs, 2017. References Books 1. Yang, L., Hsu, K., Baughman, B., Godfrey, D., Medina, F., Menon, M., & Wiener, S., Additive manufacturing of metals: the technology, materials, design and production, Springer, Edition 2017. 2. Gebhardt, Andreas, Understanding additive manufacturing, 2nd Edition, Hanser Publication, 2018.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech and MBA Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: The main purpose of this course is to introduce students with renewable energy resources availability, potential and suitability as a substitute for conventional energy resources in future energy demands.

outcomes.text: Identify sustainable energy solutions for sustainable development
Analyze renewable energy resources availability and utilization
Demonstrate competency in renewable systems analysis independently

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Renewable and non-renewable energy sources, global and Indian scenario. Energy Alternatives The solar option, nuclear option, tar sands and oil shale, tidal energy, geothermal energy.

units.title: Solar Energy
units.text: Solar Energy Solar radiation, availability, measurement and estimation, solar thermal conversion devices such as flat plate collector, tubular collector, solar air collector, solar concentrator and storage. Applications Crop drying, distillation, water heating, electric power generation. Solar Photovoltaic Photovoltaic cell technologies, generations of solar cell, electrical characteristics, photovoltaic module and array, photovoltaic module system components and design.

units.title: Biomass Energy Conversion
units.text: Biomass Energy Conversion Biomass characteristics and their availability, biofuel production processes, bio-methane, bio-hydrogen, alcoholic fermentation, biodiesel, microbial fuel cell, biomass based steam power plant, combined cycle power plant, cogeneration plant, Energy from Waste.

units.title: Wind Energy
units.text: Wind Energy Wind turbines, aerodynamics, types of turbines wind energy conversion system, wind turbine generator types, advantages and disadvantages. Hydro Power Water turbines, hydroelectric system theory, measurement and components, advantages and disadvantages of hydroelectric system.

units.title: Geothermal Energy
units.text: Geothermal Energy Structure of earth, geothermal resources, exploration of geothermal energy. OTEC Principle, applications. Tidal principle, power calculation, tidal modes of operation. Wave wave motion, energy conversion and devices applications.

units.title: Economic Analysis
units.text: Economic Analysis Initial and annual costs, present worth calculation, annual savings, payback period.

K Khan, Non-Conventional Energy Resources, TMH New Delhi, 2013. 3. J. A. Duffie and W. A. Beckman, Solar Engineering of Thermal Processes, John Wiley, New York, 2013.

program: B Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: The objective of this course is to help the students understand the principles and applications relevant to the planning, design, and operations of manufacturing or service firms. This course also develops an understanding about quality management practices in organizations that facilitate organizational effectiveness.

outcomes.text: Develop an understanding of manufacturing and service operations management as a subject and outline the strategic concerns involved in operations decisions
Apply the principles, philosophy underpinning inventory management techniques, just- in-time and MRP systems along with their limitations
Analyze the economic aspects related to production management

units.title: Concept of Production Management
units.text: Concept of Production Management Meaning of production, production process system, scope of production management, objectives of production management, functions and scopes of production management, scope of production management, brief history of production management, responsibilities of production manager.

units.title: Productivity
units.text: Productivity Introduction, meaning of productivity, factors affecting on productivity, productivity improvement, measurement of productivity.

units.title: Economic Analysis
units.text: Economic Analysis Factors to be considered in product design. production cost concepts; fixed cost, variable cost, break even analysis, P-V chart, and make-buy decision.

units.title: Plant Location and Plant Layout
units.text: Plant Location and Plant Layout Meaning of plant layout, objective of a good plant layout, factors to be considered in plant location, types of plant layout, process layout. techniques of plant layout, concept of group technology, group layout.

units.title: Production Planning and Control (PPC)
units.text: Production Planning and Control (PPC) Objective of PPC, functions of PPC, capacity planning, manufacturing resource planning and scheduling, JIT system, Kanban pull system of scheduling, line balancing.

units.title: Materials Management
units.text: Materials Management Bill of materials, quantity planning, inventory control, economic order quantity (EOQ), lead time, consumption rate, different ordering systems, Q system, P system, the store’s function and ABC analysis.

units.title: Quality
units.text: Quality Introduction to quality control, quality management, function of quality, quality control stages, function of inspection, statistical quality control, statistical quality control, control charts, acceptance sampling.

text_books: 1. S. N. Chary, Production and Operations Management, 6th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2019. 2. Bedi Kanishka, Production and Operations Management, 3rd Edition, Oxford University Press, 2016.
reference_books: 1. S. Gupta and M. Starr, Introduction to Production and Operations Management, RC Press, 1st Edition, 2014. 2. R. Panneerselvam, Production and Operations Management, 3rd Edition, PHI Learning, 2012.

program: B Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: This course introduces aspects of project management such as formulation, budgeting, planning, scheduling and control of projects from initiation to completion.

outcomes.text: Interpret the project feasibility and identify the role of project manager
Relate the resources and durations using scheduling tools and techniques
Plan the costs and risks of projects
Apply the tools for monitoring the progress of projects

units.title: Introduction to Project Management
units.text: Introduction to Project Management Definition, classification of project management in different environments, scope, systems approach, project feasibility, project life cycle, systems development cycle phases.

units.title: Project Organization
units.text: Project Organization Project organization, types of structures, roles of project managers and team, integration in large scale projects.

units.title: Project Planning and Scheduling
units.text: Project Planning and Scheduling Planning fundamentals, project master plan, work breakdown structure and other tools of project planning, work packages, project organization structure and responsibilities, responsibility matrix, use of Gantt charts, critical path method (CPM) and project evaluation and review technique (PERT) for scheduling and resource allocation, introduction to software tools for documentation, scheduling, analysis etc.

units.title: Cost Estimating and Budgeting
units.text: Cost Estimating and Budgeting Cost estimating process, elements of budgeting, project cost accounting and management information systems, cost schedules and forecasts.

units.title: Project Risk Management
units.text: Project Risk Management Risk concepts and identification, risk response planning, risk management methods, information monitoring, control process, cost accounting systems for project control, performance analysis.

units.title: Evaluation and Termination
units.text: Evaluation and Termination Project evaluation and reporting, closing the contract.

text_books: 1. Jack R Meredith, Samuel J Mantel, Shafer Project Management –A Managerial Approach, 8th Edition, Wiley Publications, 2017. 2. Erik W Larson, Clifford F Gray, Rohit Joshi, Project Management the Managerial Process, 8th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Dennis Lock, The Essentials of Project and Programme Management, 4th Edition, Routledge Publications, 2017. 2. Prasanna Chandra, Projects: Planning, Analysis, Selection, Financing Implementation and Review, 8th Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017.

program: B Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: This course focusses on a critical understanding and strategic importance of operations management. The students can get familiar with interactions between firms based on parameters such as information sharing, contracting and coordination in supply chain management.

outcomes.text: Evaluate the application of operations management policies and techniques to the service sector as well as manufacturing firms
Analyze and organize Global Network Logistics for trade and transport systems, sourcing and procurement
Apply the latest developments in information technology to supply chain management in order to generate greater benefit

units.title: Production Concepts
units.text: Production Concepts Introduction, meaning, nature and scope of production and operations management. Difference between production and operations management. Productivity, factors affecting productivity and productivity measurement. Work study— Method study and work measurement. Production Technology – Types of manufacturing processes. Plant location and types of plant layout.

units.title: Material and Inventory Management
units.text: Material and Inventory Management Types of production planning, process of production planning and control (PPC) – routing, scheduling and loading. Master production schedule, aggregate production planning. Types of inventories, inventory control techniques- EOQ, ABC, VED, FSN, HML and SDE (Simple numerical problems on Inventory control techniques).

units.title: Building a Strategic Framework to Analyze Supply Chain
units.text: Building a Strategic Framework to Analyze Supply Chain Supply chain stages and decision phases, Process View of Supply Chain: Supply Chain Flows, Examples of Supply Chain, Competitive and Supply Chain Strategies, achieving strategic fit: Expanding strategic scope, Drivers of supply chain performance, Framework for structuring drivers: inventory, transportation facilities, information obstacles to achieving fit.

units.title: Designing the Supply Chain Network
units.text: Designing the Supply Chain Network Distribution networking: Role, Design, Supply Chain Network (SCN): Role, Factors, framework for design decisions.

units.title: Warehouse and Transportation Management
units.text: Warehouse and Transportation Management Concept of strategic storage, Warehouse functionality, Warehouse operating principles, Developing warehouse resources, Material handling and packaging in warehouse, Transportation management, Transport functionality and principles, Transport infrastructure, Transport economics and pricing, Transport decision making

units.title: IT in Supply Chain
units.text: IT in Supply Chain IT framework, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Internal supply chain management, supplier Relationship Management (SRM) and transaction management. Coordination in supply chain: Lack of supply chain coordination and the Bullwhip effect, Obstacle to coordination, Managerial levers, Building partnership and trust, Emerging trends and issues. Vendor managed inventory 3PL-4PL, Reverse logistics: Reasons, Role, Activities; RFID systems: Components, Applications, Implementation; Lean supply chain, Implementation of Six Sigma in supply chain, Green supply chain.

text_books: 1. Sunil Chopra, Peter Meindl, Supply Chain Management Strategy, Planning and Operations, 6th Edition, Pearson, 2016. 2. Chase, R.B., Shankar, R. & Jacobs, F.R., Operations & Supply Chain Management, 14th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Robert B. Handfield, Ernest L. Nichols, Introduction to Supply Chain Management, Prentice Hall PTR, 2007. (Classic Book) 2. Bedi, Kanishka, Production & Operations Management, 3rd Edition, Oxford University Press, 2013.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at developing the detailed understanding of various mechanism used in devices or machines. This course focuses on analysis of the motion of mechanisms and to design mechanisms that yield the desired motion. The course is designed for the students to understand and master the concepts of displacement, velocity and acceleration of simple mechanisms and machine components. These include cam profile and its analysis, gear kinematics with gear train calculations, belt drives and chain drives, and friction clutches and brakes.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of links, mechanisms, machines, brakes, clutches and gyroscope
Analyse planar mechanism for displacement, velocity and acceleration graphically and analytically
Construct various type of Cam profiles and analyze the standard motion of the follower
Compare different type of gears, gear-trains and its applications

units.title: Introduction of Mechanisms and Machines
units.text: Introduction of Mechanisms and Machines Concepts of Kinematics and Dynamics, Mechanisms and Machines, Planar and Spatial Mechanisms, Kinematic Pairs, Kinematic Chains, Kinematic Diagrams, Kinematic Inversion, four bar chain, single and double Slider Crank Mechanisms and their Inversions, Degrees of Freedom, Mobility and range of movement - Kutzbach and Grubler’s criterion, Number Synthesis, Grashof’s criterion, straight line mechanisms.

units.title: Velocity and Acceleration Analysis
units.text: Velocity and Acceleration Analysis Velocity and Acceleration analysis: (Graphical approach) Velocity analysis: instantaneous centre of rotation method, relative velocity method for four bar pin jointed linkages and four bar slider crank linkages. Velocity and Acceleration analysis - relative method four bar pin jointed linkages and four bar slider crank linkages.

units.title: CAM
units.text: CAM Types of cams, Types of followers, Follower displacement programming, Derivatives of follower Motion, Motions of follower, Layout of cam profiles.

units.title: Belt, Ropes and Chains
units.text: Belt, Ropes and Chains Types of belt drive, Velocity ratio, Slip, Pulley arrangement, Length of belt, Law of belting, Ratio of friction tension, Power transmitted, Centrifugal effects on belts, Maximum power transmitted, Creep, Chains, Chain length, Angular speed ratio, Classification of chains.

units.title: Friction Clutches and Brakes
units.text: Friction Clutches and Brakes Introduction to friction clutches, Rolling Friction, Types of Clutches, Types of brakes, Block and Shoe brakes, Differential band brake, Internal expanding shoe brake.

units.title: Gears and Gear Trains
units.text: Gears and Gear Trains Terminology, Law of Gearing, Characteristics of involute and cycloidal action, Interference and undercutting, centre distance variation, minimum number of teeth, contact ratio, spur, helical, spiral bevel and worm gears, problems. Gear Trains: Synthesis of Simple, compound & reverted gear trains, Analysis of epicyclic gear trains

text_books: 1. Thomas Beven, Theory of Machines, 3rd Edition, Pearson, 2009. 2. S. S. Rattan, Theory of Machines, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, New Delhi, 2009.
reference_books: 1. John Uicker, G R Pennock J. E. Shigley, Theory of Mechanisms and Machines, 3rd Edition, University Press, 2010. 2. P. L. Ballaney, Theory of Machines and Mechanisms, 24th Edition, Khanna Publishing, New Delhi, 2005.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech /B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course describes the application of Engineering Thermodynamics to model the energy conversion phenomenon. With this course one can impart knowledge of air compressors and components of steam power system. This course provides basics of I.C engines, refrigeration systems and air conditioning systems and also build a bridge for these courses.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental concepts of applied thermodynamics
Analyze the components of steam power systems
Investigate the concept of I.C. Engines, air compressors and refrigeration and air conditioning systems

units.title: Reciprocating Air Compressors
units.text: Reciprocating Air Compressors Working principle, work done, Effect of clearance volume, Single and multistage compressors, Volumetric efficiency, Intercooling in multistage compressors, calculation of power requirement, Rotary compressors. Review of Thermodynamics, Vapour Power cycles, Binary Vapour Cycle, Combined Cycle and Co-generation.

units.title: Steam Generators
units.text: Steam Generators Fire Tube Boilers, Water Tube Boilers, Boiler Mountings and Accessories, High Pressure Boilers. Draught, Performance of Boilers, Combustion of Fuel.

units.title: Nozzles and Diffusers
units.text: Nozzles and Diffusers Theory and Design, Efficiency and Critical Pressure, General Relationship and supersaturated Flow. Steam Turbines Impulse and Reaction turbine Principles - Compounding – Types - Velocity diagrams for simple and multistage turbines - Speed regulations – Governors.

units.title: Condensers and Cooling Towers
units.text: Condensers and Cooling Towers Classification of condenser, air leakage, condenser performance parameters. Cooling tower design.

units.title: Refrigeration
units.text: Refrigeration Refrigeration cycles, Reversed Carnot cycle, Vapour compression system, Vapour absorption refrigeration system. Refrigerants Their classification and desirable properties. Air-Conditioning Principles of air-conditioning, Types of Air- conditioning Systems, Summer and Winter air -conditioning. Cryogenics Introduction and applications.

units.title: IC Engines
units.text: IC Engines Classification, Working of SI & CI engine, Port timing and Valve timing diagram, Performance testing of I.C Engines, Heat balance calculations.

text_books: 1. P. K. Nag, Basics and Applied Thermodynamics, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. P. K. Nag, Power Plant Engineering, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2016. 3. Vanwvylen & Sonntag, Classical Thermodynamics, 5th Edition, Wiley Eastern, 1994.
reference_books: 1. Y. Cengel and M. Boles, Thermodynamics -An Engineering Approach, 6th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. M. J. Moran, H. N. Shapiro, D. D. Boettner, M. B. Bailey, Fundamentals of Engineering Thermodynamics, 7th Edition, John Wiley and Sons, 2011.

Operate different operations like screw cutting and threading

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at providing adequate understanding of the fundamentals of stresses and strains in deformable bodies subjected to various types of static loads. It is designed to impart the knowledge of basic concepts of deformation & deflection, identifying the relevant tests to be performed on beams and power transmitting shafts. It develops the ability to assess the strength of engineering materials and subsequently examine the failure criteria of structural members using relevant analysis.

outcomes.text: Explain fundamental concepts of stress, strain and material properties in structural analysis
Construct shear force and bending moment diagrams for statically determinate beams under various loading conditions
Analyze beam bending stresses, shear stresses, and deflections using beam theory
Analyze torsional stresses in solid and hollow circular shafts used in power transmission
Determine principal stresses, maximum shear stress, and stress transformation using Mohr’s circle
Determine mechanical properties and access failure characteristics by material testing using UTM or similar equipment.

Shear Stress in Beams Distribution of shear stress across plane sections used commonly for structural purposes.

units.title: Bending Moment Combined with Axial Loads
units.text: Bending Moment Combined with Axial Loads Application to members subjected to eccentric loads, core of a section, problems on chimneys involving lateral loads.

units.title: Principal Stresses
units.text: Principal Stresses Stresses in a tensile member, stresses due to pure shearing, stresses due to two mutually perpendicular direct stresses, stress on an oblique plane of a member subjected to two dimensional stress systems (General). Principal planes and principal stresses, maximum shear stress, Mohr’s circle concept.

units.title: Deflection of Beams
units.text: Deflection of Beams Deflection of cantilevers, simply supported and overhanging beams using methods like Moment-Area, double integration and Macaulay’s method for different types of loading.

units.title: Thin Shells
units.text: Thin Shells Stresses in thin cylindrical and spherical shells subjected to internal pressure. Efficiency of Rivetted Joints.

objectives: The course is aimed at developing the detailed understanding of various mechanism used in devices or machines. This course focuses on analysis of the motion of mechanisms and to design mechanisms that yield the desired motion. The course is designed for the students to understand and master the concepts of displacement, velocity and acceleration of simple mechanisms and machine components. objectives: The basic objective is to provide fundamental concepts of digital logic families & digital systems as well as their applications. The course helps the students to design and analyse the combinational and sequential logic circuits.

outcomes.text: choose simplification techniques for optimized implementation of Boolean expressions using logic gates
build combinational logic circuits
construct sequential logic circuits which can be applied for real time applications of complex digital circuits and systems.

Weighted, reflective, sequential, gray, error detecting codes, hamming codes, alphanumeric, ASCII, EBCDIC codes, converting binary to gray and gray to binary and XS3.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: Enable students to understand linear data structures, implement them to utilize computer memory efficiently. Also to understand searching and sorting algorithms to solve real-life problems.

outcomes.text: Comprehend data structures and implement stacks and queues
Use linked list to solve real life problem statements
Solve real life problem statements using searching and sorting algorithms.

units.title: Introduction to Data Structures
units.text: Introduction to Data Structures Basic data types, Data structure definition, Need for data structures, Elementary Data Structure organization, Classification of Data Structures, Operations on Data Structures, Abstract data type.

units.title: Linear Data Structure I
units.text: Linear Data Structure I: Arrays and Stacks Introduction, Declaration of Arrays, operations on Arrays. Introduction to Stacks, Array representation of Stacks, Operations of a Stack: Push, Pop, Peek, Stack overflow and Stack underflow, Applications of a Stack: Reversing a list, Decimal to Binary conversion using Stack, Conversion and evaluation of Arithmetic Expression, Recursion, Tower of Hanoi

units.title: Linear Data Structure II
units.text: Linear Data Structure II: Queues Introduction to Queues, Array representation of Queues, Queue operations: Insertion, Deletion, Queue overflow, Queue underflow, Circular Queues, Priority Queues, Applications of Queues

units.title: Linear Data Structure III
units.text: Linear Data Structure III: Linked List Introduction, Basic terminologies, Linked List versus Arrays, Dynamic Memory Allocation and Deallocation for a Linked List, Types of Linked Lists: Singly Linked List, Doubly Linked List, Operations of Linked List, Traversing a Linked List, Applications of Linked Lists.

units.title: Searching and Sorting
units.text: Searching and Sorting Basic searching techniques: Sequential search, Binary search, Sorting definitions, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, Radix Sort, Hashing and collision resolution techniques

text_books: 1. Y. Langsam, M.J. Augenstein, A.M. Tenenbaum, “Data Structures using C and C++”, PHI 2nd Edition, 2015. 2. Seymour Lipschutz, “Data structures with C”, Schaum’s Outlines, 1st Edition, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Mark Allen Weiss, PHI publication, “Data Structures and Algorithm analysis in C, PHI publication, ++”, 4th Edition 2013. 2. Reema Thareja, “Data Structures using C”, 2nd Edition, Oxford University Press, Tata McGraw Hill, 2014.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To inculcate human values to grow as a responsible human being 2. To maintain ethical conduct in discharging professional duties

outcomes.text: understand the engineering code of ethics and be able to apply them as necessary
understand moral complexities in many engineering activities and decision- making processes
understand some of the contemporary issues in the engineering professions
effectively communicate their knowledge and understanding of engineering ethics.

units.text: Introduction to Ethics-  Concept of morals and ethics,  Study of engineering ethics;  Laws and ethics;  Personal and professional ethics.
Professional Practice in Engineering-  Common morality ASME code of ethics,  Technical codes and standards,  Accepted standards of Engineering practice and the standard of care.

Ethics as design-doing justice to moral Problem-  Discuss about ethics as a design to solve moral problems  Comparison between moral problems and engineering design problems;  Moral lessons from design problems;  Implications of the dynamic character of problem situations.

Rights and Responsibilities of Engineers-  Moral responsibilities;  Conflicts of interests;  Confidentiality,  Engineers, organizations and ethics,  Engineer-manager relationships;  loyalty;  The concept of whistleblowing.

Responsibility for the Environment-  Rapid Technological growth and depletion of resources,  Reports of the Club of Rome.  Limits of growth: sustainable development  Energy Crisis: Renewable Energy Resources  Environmental degradation and pollution.  Eco-friendly Technologies.  Environmental Regulations,  Environmental Ethics  Appropriate Technology,  Movement of Schumacher; later developments of Technology and developing notions.  Problems of Technology transfer,  Technology assessment impact analysis.  Problems of man, machine, interaction,  Impact of assembly line and automation.  Human centered Technology

text_books: 1. M.W. Martin and R. Schinzinger, “Ethics in Engineering”, McGraw-Hill, Second Edition, 2005. 2. Charles B. Fleddermann, “Engineering Ethics”, Pearson, Third Edition, 2007. 3. P.A. Vesilind and A. S Gunn, “Engineering Ethics and Environment”, Cambridge University Press, First Edition, 1998.
reference_books: 1. Caroline Whitbeck, “Ethics in Engineering – Practice and Research”, Cambridge University Press, Second Edition, 2011.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering) B Tech (Civil Engineering and Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: In this course students will get acquainted with the various systems of forces. It is designed for the students to understand the concept of static equilibrium and apply the equations of motion to rigid bodies.

outcomes.text: Determine the resultant of various systems of forces
Analyse the system of forces in equilibrium
Evaluate the displacement, velocity and acceleration of a moving bodies
Determine the forces developed on rigid bodies subjected to displacements and rotations

units.title: System of Forces
units.text: System of Forces Rectangular components of forces in space, moment, couple, Varignon’s theorem, resolution of forces, resultant of force system (coplanar, non- coplanar), concept of virtual work, principle of virtual work.

units.title: Application of System of Forces and Equilibrium
units.text: Application of System of Forces and Equilibrium Conditions of equilibrium, types of support, loads and beams, free body diagrams, support reactions. Friction Laws of friction, angle of friction, angle of repose, cone of friction, equilibrium of bodies on rough horizontal and inclined plane, application to inclined planes, wedges, ladder & screw jack. Analysis of Pin Jointed Plane Trusses Perfect truss, analysis using method of joints and method of sections.

units.title: Centroid and Moment of Inertia
units.text: Centroid and Moment of Inertia Centroid, moment of inertia, polar moment of inertia, and product of inertia, parallel and perpendicular axis theorem.

units.title: Kinematics of Particle
units.text: Kinematics of Particle Velocity and acceleration in terms of rectangular coordinate system, rectilinear motion, curvilinear motion, projectile motion, tangential and normal component of acceleration, acceleration - time, velocity- time graphs and their uses, relative velocity Kinematics of Rigid Bodies Translation, pure rotation and plane motion of rigid bodies, instantaneous centre of rotation for the velocity for bodies in plane motion, link mechanisms (up to two links).

units.title: Kinetics of Particles
units.text: Kinetics of Particles Newton’s laws of motion, D’Alembert’s principle, equation of dynamic equilibrium, linear motion, curvilinear motion. Kinetics of Rigid Bodies D’Alembert’s principle for bodies under translational motion, rotational motion about a fixed axis and plane motion.

text_books: 1. Beer & Johnston, Engineering Mechanics, 12th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2020. 2. R. C. Hibler, Engineering Mechanics’, 14th Edition, Pearson Education, 2017.
reference_books: 1. F. L. Singer, Engineering Mechanics, Harper & Raw Publication, 1954. (Classic Book) 2. D. S. Kumar, Engineering Mechanics, 12th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2013.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The basic objective is to provide fundamental concepts of digital logic families & digital systems as well as their applications. The course helps the students to design and analyse the combinational and sequential logic circuits.

outcomes.text: Choose simplification techniques for optimized implementation of Boolean expressions using logic gates
Build combinational logic circuits
Construct sequential logic circuits which can be applied for real time applications of complex digital circuits and systems

units.title: Introduction to Digital Systems and Binary Codes
units.text: Introduction to Digital Systems and Binary Codes Number Systems- binary, octal, hexadecimal, BCD and others, conversion from one system to another, binary arithmetic including 1’s and 2’s complement. Weighted, reflective, sequential, gray, error detecting codes, hamming codes, alphanumeric, ASCII, EBCDIC codes, converting binary to gray and gray to binary and XS3.

units.title: Logic Gates and Simplification of Boolean Expressions
units.text: Logic Gates and Simplification of Boolean Expressions Logic gates and implementation of digital logic using universal gates, review of boolean algebra and De Morgan’s theorem, multi-level circuits. SOP & POS forms, canonical forms, Karnaugh maps up to 4 variables.

units.title: Introduction to VHDL
units.text: Introduction to VHDL VLSI design flow - design entry, schematic, different modelling styles in VHDL- dataflow, behavioural and structural modelling, data types and objects, synthesis and simulation of any digital logic.

units.title: Combinational Logic Circuits
units.text: Combinational Logic Circuits Design of code converter circuits - binary to gray, BCD to 7 segments, priority encoder, binary comparator, binary arithmetic circuits – adders, subtractors (half and full), BCD adder, subtractor, multiplexers, De-multiplexers, decoders, encoders, hazards in combinational circuits. VHDL codes for combinational digital circuits, applications- washing machine control, vending machine

units.title: Sequential Logic Circuits
units.text: Sequential Logic Circuits Comparison of combinational and sequential circuits, flip-flops, SR, T, D, JK, master slave JK, converting one flip-flop to another, synchronous and asynchronous counters, modulus of a counter, up / down counter, counter designing by drawing state transition diagram and state transition table using all kinds of Flip –Flops, ring counter, Johnson counter, twisted ring counter, registers, Finite State Machines- Mealy and Moore machines, design of synchronous FSM.

units.title: Memories
units.text: Memories RAM, ROM, PAL, PLA, FPGA

text_books: 1. Morris Mano, Digital Design, 6th Edition PHI, 2018. 2. Malvino & Brown, Digital Computer Electronics, Reprint 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008.
reference_books: 1. R.P Jain, Digital Electronics and Microprocessors, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw-Hill, 2009. 2. Roth and John, Principles of Digital Systems Design, 6th Indian Reprint, Cengage Learning, 2011. 3. John M. Yarbrough, Digital Logic Applications and Design, 1st Edition, Cengage Learning, , 2006.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (EXTC/IT/MTRX/ CSE -Cyber Security) and MBA Tech (IT)
objectives: This course helps to develop and analyse continuous and discrete time signals and systems. It also forms the foundation for further studies in the areas such as speech/audio processing, image processing, and communication systems.

outcomes.text: Classify the continuous time and discrete time signals and systems
Apply various mathematical operations to analyze signals and systems
Analyze the continuous time signals and systems using various transforms
Determine the frequency spectrum of discrete time signals and systems response

units.title: Introduction to Signals and Systems
units.text: Introduction to Signals and Systems Signals - definitions, classification, elementary continuous and discrete time signals, operations on continuous and discrete time signals, system and its classification.

units.title: Linear Time Invariant System
units.text: Linear Time Invariant System Continuous and discrete time LTI systems, convolution integral and convolution sum, interconnection of systems, series, parallel and mixed.

units.title: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Signals
units.text: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Signals Introduction to different types of Fourier series representation, Exponential Fourier Series representation of continuous time periodic signal, magnitude and phase spectrum.

units.title: Fourier Transform
units.text: Fourier Transform Fourier transform of elementary signals and its frequency spectrum, properties of Fourier transform, inverse Fourier transform, analysis of LTI continuous time system in frequency domain.

units.title: Laplace Transform
units.text: Laplace Transform Limitations of Fourier transform, introduction to Laplace transform, ROC and its properties, Laplace transform of elementary signals, properties of Laplace transform, inverse Laplace transform, solution of differential equation.

units.title: Z-transforms
units.text: Z-transforms Introduction to Z transform, Z transform of elementary signals, ROC, properties of Z transform, inverse Z transform, solution of difference equation.

text_books: 1. Tarun Kumar Rawat, Signals and Systems, 1st Edition, Oxford University Press, 2010. 2. Nagoor Kani, Signals and Systems, 1st Edition, McGraw-Hill publication, 2010.
reference_books: 1. Oppenheim & Willsky, Signal and Systems, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall of India publication, 2008. (Classic Book) 2. Simon Haykin & Barry Van Veen, Signal and Systems, 2nd Edition, John Wiley publication, 2008.
lab_work: 8 to 10 practical exercises (and a practicum) based on the syllabus.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Physics
objectives: The basic objective is to provide the students with fundamental concepts of solid-state devices and their applications. This course helps the students to understand the construction, working principle, characteristics and applications of electronic devices such as diodes, transistors and Op- amps. Students will also be able to design different types of filters and timer circuits for the given specifications.

outcomes.text: Choose the solid-state semiconductor devices for various applications
Explain the applications of simple op-amp, diode and transistor circuits
Construct filter and timer Circuits for various applications

units.title: Semiconductor Diodes and Applications
units.text: Semiconductor Diodes and Applications PN Diode- construction, working and characteristics of PN junction diode. Other SC diodes - zener, LED, Schottky, photodiode.

units.title: Bipolar Junction Transistor
units.text: Bipolar Junction Transistor BJT- PNP and NPN transistors, currents in BJT, characteristics of BJT, BJT configurations (CE, CB and CC) Biasing of BJT- concept of biasing of BJT, Q-point and load line, voltage divider biasing of BJT in CE configuration

units.title: Field Effect Transistors
units.text: Field Effect Transistors CMOS- construction of CMOS, static and dynamic characteristics of CMOS, and its small signal analysis

units.title: Application od Diodes and Transistors
units.text: Application od Diodes and Transistors Diode Applications- rectifiers, capacitive filter, clipper and clamper, SMPS, Linear Regulated Power Supply, mobile charger. BJT Applications- BJT as switch, BJT as amplifier CMOS Application- CMOS as amplifier, transmission gates, tri-state inverters, and buffers

Foundation of Operational Amplifiers ideal and practical op-amps, inverting and non-inverting amplifier, op-amp parameters, fundamentals of IC-741. Linear Applications of Operational Amplifiers Amplifiers- adder, differentiator, integrator, instrumentation amplifiers with three op-amps Converters- V to I, I to V converters Oscillators- Wien Bridge Oscillator using op-amp.

units.title: Non-Linear Applications of Operational Amplifiers
units.text: Non-Linear Applications of Operational Amplifiers Inverting Schmitt trigger Comparators- inverting and non-inverting comparator, zero crossing detector Precision Rectifiers- half wave and full wave precision rectifiers Sample and Hold Circuits and Logarithmic Amplifiers

units.title: Timer and Filter Circuits
units.text: Timer and Filter Circuits Timers-IC555 timer, working of astable and monostable multivibrator circuits. Filters-first order filters - low pass, high pass, band pass filter, band reject filters

text_books: 1. Donald A. Neamen, Electronic Circuit Analysis and Design, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill International, 2006. 2. David A. Bell, Electronic Devices & Circuits, 5th Edition, Prentice Hall India Pvt. Ltd, 2008. 3. R. A. Gayakwad, Op-Amps and Linear Integrated Circuits, 4th Edition, Prentice Hall of India Pvt. Ltd, 2009. 4. Sergio Franco, Design with operational amplifiers and analog circuits, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill, 2002.
reference_books: 1. Adel S. Sedra, Kenneth Carlers Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, Volume 1, Oxford University Press, 2004. 2. Robert Boylestad & Louis Nashelsky, Electronic Devices & Circuit Theory, 9th Edition, Pearson Education India, 2007. 3. Jacob Millman, Christos Halkias, Chetan Parikh, Integrated Electronics, 2nd Edition, McGraw hill Publication, 2009. 4. Robert Coughlin and F. Driscoll, Operational Amplifiers and Linear Integrated Circuits, 6th Edition, Prentice Hall of India Pvt. Ltd, 2009.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course starts out with elaborate illustrations of the first and second laws of thermodynamics. The course emphasizes the relationship between work and energy by examples. It teaches the students to use thermodynamic properties of materials and the analytical tools necessary to solve engineering problems.

outcomes.text: Identify various forms of energy
Describe the laws of thermodynamic principles related to various thermal systems
Apply the laws of thermodynamics to determine the performance parameters of thermal systems

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Fundamentals: System, control volume, property, state, process, cycle, equilibrium, Zeroth law, Principles of Thermometry, forms of energy, heat, work, various forms of work

units.title: First Law of Thermodynamics
units.text: First Law of Thermodynamics First law Analysis of closed system for cyclic & non-cyclic process, internal energy, enthalpy, free expansion process, application of First law to flow processes, limitations of first law

units.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics
units.text: Second Law of Thermodynamics Qualitative difference between the heat and work, heat engines, refrigerators, heat pumps, Kelvin-Planck & Clausius statements, PMM-II, Carnot Cycle, reversible & irreversible cycles, statement of third law of thermodynamics and its importance Entropy Clausius inequality, definition of entropy, demonstration that entropy is a property, T-s diagram, isentropic efficiency, available and unavailable energy, concept of irreversibility and lost work, T-ds equations

units.title: Pure Substances and Gases
units.text: Pure Substances and Gases Properties of pure substances, water and steam - constant temperature and constant pressure heating, use of steam tables: saturation tables, superheated tables, Mollier chart, ideal gas and their mixtures, real gases

units.title: Thermodynamic Cycles and Steam Generators
units.text: Thermodynamic Cycles and Steam Generators Analysis of air standard cycles and vapor power cycles, steams generators, fire tube and water tube boilers, boiler mountings and accessories

text_books: 1. P. K. Nag, Engineering Thermodynamics, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. Y. A. Cengel, and M. A. Boles, Thermodynamics: An Engineering Approach, 8th Edition, McGraw-Hill, 2011.
reference_books: 1. C. Borgnakke and R. E. Sonntag, Fundamentals of Thermodynamics, 7th Edition, Wiley, 2009. 2. Boettner and Bailey, Principles of Engineering Thermodynamics, 8th Edition, Wiley, 2015.
lab_work: 8 to 10 Tutorial exercises based on the syllabus.
