reference_books: 1. F. L. Singer, Engineering Mechanics, Harper & Raw Publication, 1954. (Classic Book) 2. D. S. Kumar, Engineering Mechanics, 12th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2013.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (EXTC/ Mechatronics/Computer/ Information Technology /CSE -Cyber Security) MBA Tech (Information Technology / Computer) B Tech Integrated (Computer / Information Technology)
objectives: This course introduces the fundamental concepts and techniques underlying the construction of digital systems. It further provides insight into designing digital logic circuits using basic building blocks and necessary techniques required in computer hardware design.

outcomes.text: Translate different number systems and binary codes, including weighted and non-weighted codes.
Simplify Boolean expressions using De Morgan’s Theorem, SOP, POS, and Karnaugh maps.
Build combinational logic circuits such as adders, multiplexers, decoders, and encoders. .
Analyze sequential circuits, including flip-flops, registers, and counters.
Make use of VHDL for realizing basic digital logic circuits in different modeling styles.

units.title: Introduction to Digital Systems
units.text: Introduction to Digital Systems Number Systems - Binary, Octal, Hexadecimal, BCD, Conversion from one system to another, Binary subtraction using 1’s and 2’s complement method. Weighted codes - BCD and Binary, Non-weighted codes - Grey and Excess 3, conversion from one code to another.

units.title: Logic Gates and Boolean Algebra
units.text: Logic Gates and Boolean Algebra Logic gates, Concept of universal logic and implementation of digital logic using universal gates, Review of Boolean algebra and De Morgan’s Theorem, SOP & POS forms, Canonical forms, Karnaugh maps up to 4 variables.

units.title: Combinational logic circuit and its implementation
units.text: Combinational logic circuit and its implementation Combinational circuits - Adders, Subtractors (half and full), Multiplexers, DE-multiplexers, Decoders, Encoders, Design of digital logic using multiplexers.

units.title: Sequential Logic Circuits
units.text: Sequential Logic Circuits Flip flops - SR, T, D, JK, master slave JK, converting one flip-flop to another, Registers - Serial input, serial output; serial input-parallel output; Parallel In- Parallel Out, Serial In -Serial Out, Bi-Directional Shift Registers, Counters -Synchronous Counters, Asynchronous (Ripple) Counters and asynchronous counter designing.

units.title: Introduction to VHDL
units.text: Introduction to VHDL VLSI Design flow - Design entry, Schematic, Different modelling styles in VHDL - Dataflow, Behavioural and Structural Modelling, Data types and objects, Synthesis and Simulation of any basic digital logic circuits.

text_books: 1. Morris Mano, Digital Design - With an Introduction to the Verilog HDL, VHDL, and System Verilog, 6th Edition, Pearson Education, 2018. 2. R.P Jain, Modern Digital Electronics, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw-Hill, 2013.
reference_books: 1. Kumar A. Anand, Fundamental of digital circuits, 4th Edition, 2016. 2. D.P. Kothari and J.S. Dhillon, Digital Circuits and Design, Pearson Education, 2015. 3. Roth and John, Principles of Digital Systems Design, 6th Edition, Ceneage Learning, 2011.
lab_work: 8 to 10 practical exercises (and a practicum) based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (EXTC/ Mechatronics/ Information Technology /CSE -Cyber Security) and MBA Tech (Information Technology) B Tech Integrated (Information Technology)
objectives: This course helps to develop and analyse continuous and discrete time signals and systems. It also forms the foundation for further studies in the areas such as speech/audio processing, image processing, and communication systems.

outcomes.text: Illustrate the fundamental concepts of signals and systems, including classification and operations on signals.
Explain the properties of Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems and apply convolution techniques.
Illustrate the Fourier series representation of periodic signals, analyze their magnitude, and phase spectra.
Utilize Fourier and Laplace transforms, their properties for system analysis applications.
Apply Z-transform in solving difference equations for discrete-time systems.

units.title: Introduction to Signals and Systems
units.text: Introduction to Signals and Systems Signals - definitions, classification, elementary continuous and discrete time signals, operations on continuous and discrete time signals, system and its classification.

units.title: Linear Time Invariant System
units.text: Linear Time Invariant System Continuous and discrete time LTI systems, convolution integral and convolution sum, interconnection of systems, series, parallel and mixed.

units.title: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Signals
units.text: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Signals Introduction to different types of Fourier series representation, Exponential Fourier Series representation of continuous time periodic signal, magnitude and phase spectrum.

units.title: Fourier Transform
units.text: Fourier Transform Fourier transform of elementary signals and its frequency spectrum, properties of Fourier transform, inverse Fourier transform, analysis of LTI continuous time system in frequency domain.

units.title: Laplace Transform
units.text: Laplace Transform Limitations of Fourier transform, introduction to Laplace transform, ROC and its properties, Laplace transform of elementary signals, properties of Laplace transform, inverse Laplace transform, solution of differential equation.

units.title: Z-transforms
units.text: Z-transforms Introduction to Z transform, Z transform of elementary signals, ROC, properties of Z transform, inverse Z transform, solution of difference equation.

text_books: 1. Tarun Kumar Rawat, Signals and Systems, 1st Edition, Oxford University Press, 2010. 2. Nagoor Kani, Signals and Systems, 1st Edition, McGraw-Hill publication, 2010.
reference_books: 1. (Classic) Oppenheim & Willsky, Signal and Systems, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall of India publication, 2008. 2. Simon Haykin & Barry Van Veen, Signal and Systems, 2nd Edition, John Wiley publication, 2008.
lab_work: 8 to 10 practical exercises (and a practicum) based on the syllabus.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To provide an understanding of Laplace transform and its applications, Fourier series, Fourier Transform, Z-transform 2. To provide students with mathematics fundamentals necessary to formulate, solve and analyses complex engineering problems

outcomes.text: Solve problems using Laplace transform, Fourier series, Fourier Transform, Z - transform.
Analyze the concept of Laplace transform, Fourier series, Fourier Transform, Z - transform.
Apply the techniques of Laplace transform, Fourier series, Fourier Transform and Z - transform to engineering problems.

units.title: Laplace transformation
units.text: Laplace transformation: Definition of Laplace transform, Laplace transform of 1, at e , sin , at cos , at sinh , at cosh , at nt , Properties of Laplace transform: Linearity property, First and second shifting theorems of Laplace transform, Change of scale property,    n L t f t ,  f t L t       ,    n L f t ,  t L f u du        , Evaluation of Inverse Laplace transform by partial fraction, Convolution theorem, Laplace transforms of Periodic functions, Unit step functions, Dirac delta functions. Applications: to solve initial and boundary value problems involving ordinary differential equations.

units.title: Fourier series
units.text: Fourier series: Orthogonality and Orthonormality, Periodic function, Trigonometric Series, Dirichlet’s conditions, Euler’s formulae (Derivative of Fourier coefficients 0, , n n a a b is not expected), Fourier Series of Functions for the interval [ , 2 ]    and [ , 2 ] c  , Functions having points of discontinuity, Even and odd functions, half range sine and cosine expansions, Parseval’s identities. Complex form of Fourier series, Fourier integral theorem, Fourier sine and cosine integral.

units.title: Fourier Transform
units.text: Fourier Transform: Fourier Transform, Fourier Sine Transform, Fourier Cosine Transform, Properties of Fourier Transform (Linearity property, Change of scale property, Shifting property), Inverse Fourier Transform, Inverse Fourier Sine Transform, Inverse Fourier Cosine Transform, Finite Fourier Transform. Application: Fourier transform to solve differential equations.

units.title: Z-transforms
units.text: Z-transforms: Introduction, Sequences, Representation of sequences, Basic operators on Sequences, Z-transforms, Properties of Z-Transforms, Change of scale, Shifting Properties, Inverse Z-transform, Solution of Difference equations, Multiplication by K, Division by K, Initial value, Final value, Partial sum, Convolution, Convolution Property of Casual Sequence, Transform of important sequences, Inverse of Z-transform by division, binomial expansion and partial fraction, Inverse by residue Method, Solution of Difference equation.

text_books: 1. B. V. Ramana (2017), “Higher Engineering Mathematics”, McGraw Hill Education, 1st Edition.
reference_books: 1. G. B. Thomas (2014), “Calculus”, Pearson, 13th Edition. 2. Erwin Kreyszig (2017), “Advanced Engineering Mathematics”, Wiley India, 10th Edition. 3. B. S. Grewal (2017), Higher Engineering Mathematics, Khanna Publishers, 44th Edition.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart an understanding of basic tenets of business communication that helps students to effectively engage in organizational communication. 2. To develop in students an understanding of interpersonal communication challenges and the ability to effectively overcome these challenges in an organizational context. 3. To develop leadership, team building and decision making skills which could be later applied in a professional set up. 4. To impart technical writing skills towards designing and structuring persuasive technical communication. 5. To build and strengthen presentation skills towards making impressive and persuasive presentations. 6. To train the students for participating in group discussions, building Resume and facing personal interviews.

outcomes.text: Understand and apply the postulates of technical writing in a formal set up
Apply fundamentals of business correspondence to create well-structured Resumes, application letters, Minutes of Meetings and similar business related documents
Understand and analyse group dynamics and apply leadership skills for effective team building in professional set ups.
Analyze the context and select appropriate communication techniques for effective interpersonal communication in professional context.

units.title: Understanding the foundations of Business Communication
units.text: Understanding the foundations of Business Communication: Professional Communication in a Digital, Social, Mobile World

units.title: Collaboration, Interpersonal Communication and Business Etiquette
units.text: Collaboration, Interpersonal Communication and Business Etiquette: Communicating effectively, collaborating, conducting productive meetings, using meeting technologies, improving listening skills and non-verbal communication, business etiquettes.

units.title: Development of Interpersonal and Group Communication Skills
units.text: Development of Interpersonal and Group Communication Skills Theatre techniques: Use of drama (in workshop format) to promote meaningful, active and reflective thinking processes as well as enhancing communication skills development. Group Communication  Forms of Group Communication; Use of body language in Group communication  Group Discussion etiquette: Introducing oneself and others; Expressing Opinions and Ideas; expressing disagreement etc.  Group Discussion Strategies: Speaking, taking turns, Creating a Cordial and cooperative atmosphere etc.

Building Problem-solving teams  Orientation to Personality Values – Importance of Values  Understanding of Teams- Types of Teams, stages of Team development; Team building leadership skills and leaderless scenarios  Decision Making-Group and Individual Decision Making Techniques  Stress Management-Sources of Stress; consequences; Managing Stress

Employment Communication  Personal Interviews-Objectives, Types, Stages of Interview  Interview Preparation-types of Interview Questions ; Interview Follow ups  Resume- Types and Format; Cover letters  Mock Interviews ( simulation )

Organizational networks and communication Structures  Process and Functions of Communication ;Formal Networks in Organizational Communication  Informal networks of organizational communications ;choice of communication channels

Meetings  Meetings- Purposes ,Importance and Meeting Procedures including Chairperson’s and participants’ roles  Meeting Documentation (Minutes of resolution; Minutes of Narration; Meeting Notice and Agenda)
Technical Report Writing  Importance , objectives and Characteristic of Reports ; Types of Reports  Report formats and Structure -Memo Reports; Letter Reports; Office Orders and Manuscript Reports

Presentation Skills  Planning and structuring Presentations; Visual Aids in Presentations  Applications of MS Power Point  Audience analyses; Nuances of Delivery; Modes of delivery; Controlling Nervousness and stage fright

text_books: 1. Bovee, C., Thill, J., & Roshan Lal Raina (2013), “Business Communication Today”, Pearson. 14th edition. 2. Meenakshi Raman and Sangeeta Sharma (2015), “Technical Communication”, Oxford University Press, 3rd Edition.
reference_books: 1. Fred Luthans ( 2013), ‘Organizational Behavior’, McGraw Hill, 12th Edition.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To provide knowledge of digital logic & digital system as well as their applications in technical field. 2. To provide knowledge of designing the digital logic circuit using basic building blocks and necessary techniques which is required in computer hardware design.

outcomes.text: Apply the knowledge of fundamental number systems and the various codes.
Design Combinational Logic Circuits.
Implement Sequential Logic Circuits which can be applied for real time applications for complex digital circuits and systems.

units.title: Introduction to Digital Systems & Binary Codes
units.text: Introduction to Digital Systems & Binary Codes: Comparison of Analog and Digital Systems, Number Systems: binary, octal, hexadecimal, BCD and others. Conversion from one system to another, Binary Arithmetic including 1’s and Two Complement Arithmetic, Importance of Binary and Hexadecimal Numbers. Weighted, reflective, sequential, gray, error detecting codes, even parity, Hamming codes, alphanumeric, Morse, teletypewriter ASCII, EBCDIC codes, converting binary to gray and gray to binary and XS3.

units.title: Logic Gates and Boolean Algebra
units.text: Logic Gates and Boolean Algebra: AND, OR, NOT, XOR, XNOR, operation NAND, NOR use of universal gates for performing different operations. Laws Boolean algebra, DeMorgan’s theorems. Relating truth table to a Boolean expression. Multi-level circuits.

units.title: Combinational Logic Circuits
units.text: Combinational Logic Circuits: Canonical Logic Form, minterm, maxterm SOP and POS implementation. Implementing a logic function using universal gates. K-maps and their use in simplifying Boolean expressions, Variable entered maps for five and six variables functions. Design of Code converter circuits-Binary to Gray, BCD to 7 segments, priority encoder, Binary comparator, binary arithmetic circuits – adders, subtractors (half and full), BCD adder, subtractor, ALU, Parity generator. Multiplexers (ULM), De-multiplexers, Decoders, Encoders, Tree structures. Hazards in combinational circuits.

units.title: Sequential Logic Circuits
units.text: Sequential Logic Circuits: Comparison of combinational and sequential circuits, flip-flops, SR, T, D, JK, master slave JK, converting one flip-flop to another, use of debounce switch. Synchronous and Asynchronous Counters, modulus of a counter, up / down counter, Counter designing by drawing state transition diagram and state transition table using all kinds of Flip –Flops. Ring counter, Johnson counter, twisted ring counter, Finite and Mixed state Machines- Mealy and Moore Design, Logic state diagram analysis.

units.title: Registers & Memories
units.text: Registers & Memories: Serial input -serial output; serial input-parallel output; Parallel In -Parallel Out, Serial In -Serial Out, Bi Directional Shift Registers, Universal Shift Registers. RAM, ROM, basic bipolar cell, CMOS, dynamic RAM cell. Magnetic core NVRAM, bubble memory, CCD, PAL, PLA, FPGA. Introduction to VHDL

text_books: 1. Morris Mano (2008), “Digital Design”, PHI, 4th edition. 2. Malvino & Brown (2008), “Digital Computer Electronics”, Tata McGraw Hill, Reprint 3rd Edition.
reference_books: 1. R.P Jain (2007), “Digital Electronics and Microprocessors”, Tata McGraw-Hill, 25th reprint 2. Roth and John (2011), “Principles of Digital Systems Design”, Cengage Learning, Sixth Indian Reprint.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. The objective of this Course is to provide an introductory treatment of Engineering Mechanics to all the students of engineering, with a view to prepare a good foundation for taking up advanced courses in the area in the subsequent semesters 2. A working knowledge of statics with emphasis on force equilibrium and free body diagrams provides an understanding of the kinds of stress and deformation and how to determine them in a wide range of simple, practical structural problems, and an understanding of the mechanical behaviour of materials under various load conditions.

outcomes.text: Determine resultant forces and equilibrium of various force systems.
Determine centroid and moment of inertia of plane areas.
Determine the displacement, velocity, acceleration & their components for a moving particle and rigid body.
Determine forces produced due to motion of particles and rigid body.

units.title: System of Forces
units.text: System of Forces: Resultant of coplanar concurrent and non-concurrent forces, Resultant of concurrent and non-concurrent forces in space Equilibrium: Equilibrium of system of concurrent and non-concurrent forces in plane and space, Free body diagrams.

units.title: Application of Coplanar Forces and Equilibrium
units.text: Application of Coplanar Forces and Equilibrium: Trusses: Evaluation of member forces using method of sections and method of joints. Beams: Evaluation of reactions using equilibrium and principle of virtual work Simple frames: Evaluation of reactions using equilibrium

units.title: Friction
units.text: Friction: Types of friction, Limiting friction, Laws of Friction, Static and Dynamic Friction; wedge friction, screw jack

units.title: Centroid and Centre of Gravity
units.text: Centroid and Centre of Gravity: Centroid of simple figures from first principle, centroid of composite sections; Centre of Gravity and its implications; Area moment of inertia- Definition, Moment of inertia of plane sections from first principles, Moment of inertia of standard sections and composite sections; Mass moment inertia of circular plate, Cylinder, Sphere

units.title: Kinematics of Particles
units.text: Kinematics of Particles: Rectilinear motion; Plane curvilinear motion (rectangular, path and polar coordinates), velocity-time graph and their usage, relative motion; Newton’s 2nd law (rectangular, path, and polar coordinates). Kinematics of Rigid Bodies: Translation, pure rotation and plane motion of rigid bodies, ICR, link mechanisms

units.title: Kinetics of Particles and Rigid Bodies
units.text: Kinetics of Particles and Rigid Bodies: Newton’s Law of motion, D’Alembert’s principle, equation of dynamic equilibrium, Work energy principle and its application in plane motion of connected bodies; Kinetics of rigid body in translation, rotation and plane motion.

text_books: 1. Irving H. Shames (2008), “Engineering Mechanics”, Prentice Hall, 4th Edition. 2. R. C. Hibbler (2017), “Engineering Mechanics: Principles of Statics and Dynamics”, Pearson Press.
reference_books: 1. F. P. Beer and E. R. Johnston (2017), “Vector Mechanics for Engineers”, Vol I & II, Tata McGraw Hill, 9th Edition. 2. Shanes and Rao (2006), “Engineering Mechanics”, Pearson Education. 3. Hibler and Gupta (2010), “Engineering Mechanics (Statics, Dynamics)”, Pearson Education 4. Tayal A.K. (2010), “Engineering Mechanics”, Umesh Publications

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To introduce different manufacturing processes like casting, forging, machining, rolling etc. 2. To impart knowledge of various process equipment used in manufacturing processes.

outcomes.text: Understand and differentiate the different types of metal casting and forming process.
Explain the different types of equipment used in casting, and metal forming process.
Understand the operations of lathe, milling and drilling machines
Know the abrasive machining processes

units.title: Metal Casting
units.text: Metal Casting: Pattern Making: Types of patterns, allowances, color coding; Foundry practices Moulding sands: types, properties, preparation and testing of sand. Core boxes, core making, types of cores and their manufacturing; Gating system – runner and risers; Moulding processes: shell moulding, CO2 moulding, investment casting, die casting, centrifugal casting and continuous casting; Study of various defects in castings.

units.title: Forming processes
units.text: Forming processes: Cold and hot working Rolling: Principle and mechanism, types of rolling and their applications, defects in rolling. Forging: Classification of forging processes, basic categories and methods of forging, heat treatment of forged parts. Extrusion: Hot and cold Extrusion, Equipment, Estimation of extrusion force, defects in extruded parts; wire and tube. Drawing: Metal Stamping and Forming, blanking, piercing, bending, deep drawing, roll forming, shear forming and flow Forming. Press tools: Different type of presses and their working, strip layout, Progressive die, Compound and combination dies.

units.title: Abrasive Machining Processes
units.text: Abrasive Machining Processes: Mechanics of grinding, types and operations of grinding machines, Centerless grinding, Grinding wheel specifications and its selection, Truing and dressing of wheels, super finishing processes such as lapping and honing. Abrasive jet machining (AJM) and Abrasive water jet machining (AWJM).

units.title: Machining Operations
units.text: Machining Operations: Lathe: Construction and working and operations performed on lathe, attachments and accessories, types of cutting tools, cutting parameters such as spindle speed, feed and depth of cut, Capstan and Turret lather, automatic lathes and their construction. Milling Machines: Types of milling machines, tools and their geometry, various operations on milling machine, different attachments (including dividing heads) and work holding devices. Drilling Machines: Types of machines, drilling operations such as drilling, boring, reaming, spot facing, counter boring and sinking, tapping, drill speed and feeds. Boring and Broaching Machine: Classification – horizontal and vertical boring machine, types of broaching machines, advantages, limitations and applications of broaching.

text_books: 1. P. N. Rao (2008), “Manufacturing Technology-Vol I”, Tata McGraw Hill. 2. S. Kalpakjian and S. R. Schmid (2002), “Manufacturing Engineering and Technology”, 4th Edition, Pearson.
reference_books: 1. G. K. Lal (2010), “Fundamentals of Manufacturing Processes”, Alfa Science International. 2. W. A. J. Chapman (2011), “Work Shop Technology- Vol I, II, III”, ELBS Publishers. 3. Kou Sindo (2003), “Welding Metallurgy”, Wiley Inter science.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To understand the construction, working principle, characteristics and simple applications of basic electronic devices. 2. To know the ac small signal models of BJT and JFET. 3. To provide knowledge of the circuit building block of Op-Amp, its dc and ac equivalent circuit and its applications. 4. To understand and provide knowledge of various Analog Integrated circuits such as IC 741, 555 timer, IC 337 and IC 723 voltage regulator. 5. To understand the different types of filters and design them for the given specifications.

outcomes.text: Identify various semi-conductor devices and analyze small and large signal models.
Know various configurations and specifications of ideal and practical Op-Amp.
Analyze the working of power controller, PLL, VCO ICs and their applications.
Design various filter circuits.

units.title: Semiconductor Diodes and Applications
units.text: Semiconductor Diodes and Applications: Construction, Working and Characteristics of PN junction diode. Diode equation and temperature effects. Types of diodes – Zener, LED, Schottky, Photodiode. Diode Applications: Half wave, Full Wave (Center-tap and Bridge) rectifier circuits and working. Capacitive Filter – theory and limitations. Clipper and Clamper Circuits: Basic Series and Shunt Clipper Circuits, Clamper Circuits.

units.title: Bipolar Junction Transistor
units.text: Bipolar Junction Transistor: Construction, working, and input-output characteristics of npn transistor. Modes of operation – cutoff, active, and saturation. Transistor configurations – CB, CE and CC. BJT Biasing: Working, limitations and advantages of Fixed Bias, Collector Feedback, Voltage Divider Bias. BJT Applications: BJT as an AC amplifier. BJT as a switch.

units.title: Field Effect Transistor
units.text: Field Effect Transistor: Construction and working of p-channel JFET. Construction, Working and input – output characteristics of n-channel JFET. JFET Biasing: Working, limitations and advantages of Fixed Bias, Self Bias, Voltage Divider Bias. JFET Applications: JFET as an AC amplifier

units.title: BJT and FET Small Signal Amplifier
units.text: BJT and FET Small Signal Amplifier: Working of DC – RC Transformer BJT amplifier (CB, CE, CC). Working of DC – RC JFET amplifier (CS, CD). Positive and Negative Feedback circuits – advantages and limitations. Feedback Applications: Negative Feedback –Current and Power Amplifiers (Class A, B and AB). Positive Feedback – Barkhausen Criteria.

units.title: Operational Amplifiers
units.text: Operational Amplifiers: Parameters, working (open loop) and characteristics of IC 741C. Applications of Closed loop with negative feedback (Ideal): Inverting, Non- inverting, Buffer, Adder, Scalar, Subtractor, Differentiator, Integrator, V to I, I to V converters, Instrumentation Amplifiers with 3 Op-amp

units.title: Non-linear Op-Amps
units.text: Non-linear Op-Amps: Comparator, Schmitt Trigger, Precision HW Rectifier, Peak Detector, Sample and Hold Circuit, Basic Log Amplifier.

units.title: Oscillators and Timer Circuits
units.text: Oscillators and Timer Circuits: Working of RC and Wien Bridge Oscillator using op-amp. IC555 Timer Circuits: Working of Astable and Monostable multivibrator circuits. VCO Circuits: IC 566 block diagram and working. PLL circuits: Working of IC 4046 CMOS PLL. Series Regulator and 3 Terminal Regulators: IC 337 and IC 723.

units.title: Filter Circuits
units.text: Filter Circuits: First Order Filters - Low Pass, High Pass, Band Pass and Band Reject filters. Notch Filter. All Pass filter.

Bell (2008), Electronic Devices & Circuits, Prentice Hall India Pvt. Ltd, 5th Edition. 3. R. A. Gayakwad (2009), Op-Amps and Linear Integrated Circuits, Prentice Hall of India Pvt. Ltd, 4th edition. 4. Sergio Franco(2002), Design with operational amplifiers and analog circuits, McGraw Hill, 3rd edition.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics
objectives: This course aims to understand the multidisciplinary nature of environmental sciences, greenhouse effect and climate change. It also aims to discuss the basics of natural resources, biodiversity, environmental pollution.

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of natural resources, ecosystem and biodiversity
Relate the various aspects of environmental pollutions with its cause and effect
Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change.

units.title: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science
units.text: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science Definition, scope and importance of environmental sciences.

Natural Resources • Natural resources: Forest resources, Water resources, Mineral resources, Food resources. • Energy resources: Growing energy needs, renewable and non- renewable energy sources, use of alternate energy sources.

Ecosystems • Concept of an ecosystem. • Structure and function of an ecosystem. • Food chains, food webs and ecological pyramids. • Introduction, types, characteristic features of the following ecosystem:- a. Forest ecosystem b. Grassland ecosystem c. Desert ecosystem d. Aquatic ecosystems.

Biodiversity • Definition: genetic, species and ecosystem diversity. • Value of biodiversity: consumptive use, productive use. • Threats to biodiversity: habitat loss, poaching of wildlife, man-wildlife conflicts.

Environmental Pollution • Definition, Cause and effects for Air pollution, Water pollution, Soil pollution, Marine pollution, Noise pollution, Thermal pollution, Nuclear hazards and Solid waste pollution.
The Science of Climate Change • Greenhouse effect • Global warming • Global environmental changes • Acid rain • Ozone layer depletion • Carbon footprint

text_books: 1. Erach Bharucha, “Textbook of Environmental Studies”, University Press, 2nd Edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. MP Poonia & SC Sharma, “Environmental Studies”, Khanna Publishing House, 1st Edition, 2017. 2. Rajagopalan, “Environmental Studies”, Oxford University Press, Third Edition, 2015.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to instill in students a sound knowledge of probability theory and statistical techniques. It equips the students with intermediate to advanced level concepts and tools in probability and statistics that help them tackle relevant problems within engineering domain.

outcomes.text: solve problems involving random variables, probability distributions and testing of hypothesis, correlation and regression
identify suitable probability distribution and testing techniques to solve related problems
apply knowledge of random variables, probability distributions, measures of central tendency, correlation and regression to solve real life problems
analyse data samples using statistical methods.

units.title: Basic Probability
units.text: Basic Probability Probability spaces, conditional probability, independence; Bayes theorem.

units.title: Random variables and Probability Distributions
units.text: Random variables and Probability Distributions Discrete random variables, probability mass function, cumulative distribution function, Independent random variables, Continuous random variables, distribution functions and densities, expectation, variance, raw and central moments of random variables, Binomial distribution, Poisson approximation to the binomial distribution, Normal distribution.

units.title: Bivariate Distributions
units.text: Bivariate Distributions Definition of Bivariate Distribution and their properties, Conditional densities.

units.title: Basic Statistics
units.text: Basic Statistics Measures of Central tendency; Moments, Moment generating function, skewness, kurtosis. Mean and variance of Binomial distribution & Poisson distribution, Moments, skewness & kurtosis for Normal distribution.

units.title: Testing of hypothesis
units.text: Testing of hypothesis: Point estimation, Interval estimate and Confidence interval, Criteria for good estimates, Null and Alternate hypothesis, Test Statistic, Type I and Type II errors, One-tailed and two-tailed test, Critical region, Large sample statistical test for mean, Large sample statistical test for proportion, t-test for small samples, Test for variance- F test, Chi-square test for Goodness of fit and independence of attributes, Analysis of variance.

units.title: Linear Statistical Models
units.text: Linear Statistical Models: Scatter diagram, Linear regression and correlation, Least squares method, Rank correlation, Multiple regression.

Alu Srinivasn, “Probability and Statistics, McGraw Hill Education, 4th edition, 2013.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course will help students to understand the fundamental concepts of control systems and system stability. The course also helps to analyze and evaluate the system design pertaining to the system performance, stability criterion, controllability and observability.

outcomes.text: explain the basic functioning and components of feedback control systems

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The principal objective of this course is to provide a basic understanding of biological mechanisms of living organisms from the perspective of engineers. To encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools. To make them aware of the application of engineering principles in biology and engineering robust solutions inspired by biological examples.

outcomes.text: convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are diverse
identify and classify microorganisms while understanding molecular basis of DNA as a genetic material for information transfer
classify enzymes and distinguish between different mechanisms of enzyme action.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Convey that Biology is as important a scientific discipline as Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry Bring out the fundamental differences between science and engineering by drawing a comparison between eye and camera, Bird flying and aircraft. Mention the most exciting aspect of biology as an independent scientific discipline. Why we need to study biology? Discuss how biological observations of 18th Century that lead to major discoveries. Examples from -Brownian motion and the origin of thermodynamics by referring to the original observation of Robert Brown and Julius Mayor. These examples will highlight the fundamental importance of observations in any scientific inquiry.

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification Convey that classification per se is not what biology is all about. The underlying criterion, such as morphological, biochemical or ecological be highlighted. Hierarchy of life forms at phenomenological level. A common thread weaves this hierarchy Classification.Discuss classification based on (a) cellularity-Unicellular or multicellular (b) ultrastructure- prokaryotes or eucaryotes. (c) energy and Carbon utilization -Autotrophs, heterotrophs, lithotropes (d) Ammonia excretion - aminotelic, uricoteliec, ureotelic (e) Habitata- acquatic or terrestrial (e) Molecular taxonomy- three major kingdoms of life. A given organism can come under different category based on classification. Model organisms for the study of biology come from different groups. E.coli, S.cerevisiae, D. Melanogaster, C. elegance, A. Thaliana, M. musculus

units.title: Genetics
units.text: Genetics Convey that "Genetics is to biology what Newton's laws are to Physical Sciences" Mendel's laws, Concept of segregation and independent assortment. Concept of allele. Gene mapping, Gene interaction, Epistasis. Meiosis and Mitosis be taught as a part of genetics. Emphasis to be give not to the mechanics of cell division nor the phases but how genetic material passes from parent to offspring. Concepts of recessiveness and dominance. Concept of mapping of phenotype to genes. Discuss about the single gene disorders in humans. Discuss the concept of complementation using human genetics.

units.title: Biomolecules
units.text: Biomolecules Convey that all forms of life has the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are as diverse as one can imagine Molecules of life. In this context discuss monomeric units and polymeric structures. Discuss about sugars, starch and cellulose. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA. Two carbon units and lipids.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes Convey that without catalysis life would not have existed on earth Enzymology: How to monitor enzyme catalyzed reactions. How does an enzyme catalyze reactions. Enzyme classification. Mechanism of enzyme action. Discuss at least two examples. Enzyme kinetics and kinetic- parameters. Why should we know these parameters to understand biology? RNA catalysis.

units.title: Information Transfer
units.text: Information Transfer The molecular basis of coding and decoding genetic information is universal Molecular basis of information transfer. DNA as a genetic material. Hierarchy of DNA structure- from single stranded to double helix to nucleosomes. Concept of genetic code. Universality and degeneracy of genetic code. Define gene in terms of complementation and recombination.

units.title: Macromolecular analysis
units.text: Macromolecular analysis How to analyses biological processes at the reductionistic level Proteins- structure and function. Hierarch in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors and structural elements.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism The fundamental principles of energy transactions are the same in physical and biological world. Thermodynamics as applied to biological systems. Exothermic and endothermic versus endergonic and exergonic reactions. Concept of Keq and its relation to standard free energy. Spontaneity. ATP as an energy currency. This should include the breakdown of glucose to CO2 + H2O (Glycolysis and Krebs cycle) and synthesis of glucose from CO2 and H2O (Photosynthesis). Energy yielding and energy consuming reactions. Concept of Energy Charge.

units.title: Microbiology
units.text: Microbiology Concept of single celled organisms. Concept of species and strains. Identification and classification of microorganisms. Microscopy. Ecological aspects of single celled organisms. Sterilization and media compositions. Growth kinetics.

program: B. Tech Civil , Mechanical / Mechatronics Engineering
objectives: The aim is to acquaint students with engineering materials like lubricants, polymers, nanomaterials and composites. Also to familiarize them with the industrial importance of water chemistry, application of fuels and concept of metal corrosion.

outcomes.text: Explain the basic concepts of polymers, their types, and applications
Apply knowledge of lubrication properties and numerical problem-solving
Evaluate combustion processes and the characteristics of different types of fuels by solving related numerical problems
Assess the chemistry of water hardness, and softening methods, and solve related numerical problems
Investigate the properties and applications of engineering materials, composites, and nanomaterials

units.title: Polymers
units.text: Polymers Introduction, basic concepts of degree of polymerization, tacticity, melting and glass transition temperature and its importance. Types of polymerizations (Addition, condensation and co-polymerization). Smart polymer materials, conducting polymers, liquid crystals, applications of polymers.

units.title: Lubricants
units.text: Lubricants Definition, Mechanism of lubrication, Properties- viscosity, viscosity index, flash & fire, cloud & pour points, oiliness, saponification & acid value (numericals based on saponification and acid value)

units.title: Fuels & Combustion
units.text: Fuels & Combustion Discuss the definition, classification and characteristics. Calculation of Calorific Value-Theoretical & Experimental method (Bomb calorimeter). Solid Fuels: Coal, proximate and ultimate analysis, Numerical based on analysis of coal. (Dulong’s formula) and bomb calorimetry. Combustion: calculation on air and oxygen requirement. Liquid fuels: Mining of Petroleum, Cracking, Reforming, Knocking in IC engines, Octane number, Cetane number & anti-knocking agents (TEL and MTBE) Gaseous fuel: (LPG, CNG) Composition, properties and application.

units.title: Water Chemistry
units.text: Water Chemistry Concept of hardness of water, types of hardness and its determination by EDTA methods, numerical based on water hardness. Water softening processes by: Lime-soda method, ion-exchange process and reverse osmosis process. Role of water as a universal solvent.

units.title: Chemistry of Corrosion and protection
units.text: Chemistry of Corrosion and protection Introduction, types of corrosion, chemical and electrochemical theories of Corrosion and their sub-types (corrosion by oxygen and other gases and liquids), factors affecting corrosion, preventive measures for corrosion- Cathodic and anodic protection methods, use of protective coatings (galvanization, tinning, metal cladding, electroplating, organic coatings like paints and varnishes).

units.title: Chemistry of Important Engineering Materials and Nanomaterials
units.text: Chemistry of Important Engineering Materials and Nanomaterials Introduction to alloys (steels, special steels, Carbon steel, brass, bronze and applications). Introduction to composites; Classification (Polymer, Metal & Ceramic composites, Cement), applications of composites. Introduction to nanomaterials, Structural features and properties of Nanomaterials, recent advances in nanomaterials, application of nano materials in catalysis, medicine, construction chemicals, paints and pigments and heat transfer fluids.

text_books: 1. Palanna. O.G., Engineering Chemistry, 1st Edition Tata McGraw Hill Education. Pvt. Ltd, 2009.
reference_books: 1. Advance Organic Chemistry, 7th edition, Jerry March,2013 2. P. W. Atkins, Physical Chemistry, 9th Edition, ELBS/Oxford, 2010. 3. Textbook of Nanoscience and Nanotechnology, B.S. Murty, P. Shankar, Baldev Raj, B B Rath, James Murday, Springer Science, 2013
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics
objectives: This course aims to understand the multidisciplinary nature of environmental sciences, greenhouse effect and climate change. It also aims to discuss the basics of natural resources, biodiversity, environmental pollution.

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of natural resources, ecosystem and biodiversity
Relate the various aspects of environmental pollutions with its cause and effect
Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change.

units.title: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science
units.text: Multidisciplinary nature of environmental science Definition, scope and importance of environmental sciences.

Natural Resources • Natural resources: Forest resources, Water resources, Mineral resources, Food resources. • Energy resources: Growing energy needs, renewable and non- renewable energy sources, use of alternate energy sources.

Ecosystems • Concept of an ecosystem. • Structure and function of an ecosystem. • Food chains, food webs and ecological pyramids. • Introduction, types, characteristic features of the following ecosystem:- a. Forest ecosystem b. Grassland ecosystem c. Desert ecosystem d. Aquatic ecosystems.

Biodiversity • Definition: genetic, species and ecosystem diversity. • Value of biodiversity: consumptive use, productive use. • Threats to biodiversity: habitat loss, poaching of wildlife, man-wildlife conflicts.

Environmental Pollution • Definition, Cause and effects for Air pollution, Water pollution, Soil pollution, Marine pollution, Noise pollution, Thermal pollution, Nuclear hazards and Solid waste pollution.
The Science of Climate Change • Greenhouse effect • Global warming • Global environmental changes • Acid rain • Ozone layer depletion • Carbon footprint

text_books: 1. Erach Bharucha, “Textbook of Environmental Studies”, University Press, 2nd Edition, 2019.
reference_books: 1. MP Poonia & SC Sharma, “Environmental Studies”, Khanna Publishing House, 1st Edition, 2017. 2. Rajagopalan, “Environmental Studies”, Oxford University Press, Third Edition, 2015.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The main objective of this course is to instill in students a sound knowledge of probability theory and statistical techniques with intermediate to advanced level that helps them tackle relevant problems within the engineering domain.

outcomes.text: Solve problems involving random variables, probability distributions and testing of hypothesis, correlation and regression
Identify suitable probability distribution and testing techniques to solve problems
Apply knowledge of random variables, probability distributions, measures of central tendency, correlation and regression to solve real life problems
Analyse data samples using statistical methods.

units.title: Basic Probability
units.text: Basic Probability Probability spaces, conditional probability, independence, Bayes theorem.

units.title: Random variables and Probability Distributions
units.text: Random variables and Probability Distributions Discrete random variables, probability mass function , cumulative distribution function, Independent random variables, Continuous random variables, distribution functions and densities, expectation, variance, raw and central moments of random variables, The multinomial distribution, Poisson approximation to the binomial distribution, Infinite sequences of Bernoulli trials, Normal distribution, exponential and gamma densities.

units.title: Basic Statistics
units.text: Basic Statistics Measures of Central tendency; Moments, skewness, Kurtosis. Moments, skewness and Kurtosis for Binomial distribution & Poisson distribution, Moments, skewness & kurtosis for Normal distribution, Linear regression and correlation, Rank correlation.

units.title: Testing of hypothesis
units.text: Testing of hypothesis Null and Alternate hypothesis, Test Statistic, Type I and Type II errors, One-tailed and two-tailed test, Critical region, Large sample statistical test for mean, Large sample statistical test for proportion, t-test for small samples, paired t test, Test for variance- F test, Chi-square test for Goodness of fit and independence of attributes.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: This course offers an insight into the basic understanding of biological intelligence needed to implement artificial intelligence. It also aims to enhance the knowledge of the basics of biology for bio-inspired engineering and designs while focusing on the principles of bioinspired algorithm implementation.

outcomes.text: recall basics of biological systems
summarize the intelligence at the cellular level
identify and discuss the intelligence of different biological systems
summarize and categorize different forms of intelligence in different animals.

units.text: Introduction to intelligence in plants and animals. Need for intelligence for survival. Difference in animal intelligence and plant intelligence.

Introduction to animal cell. Different functions of cell. Different cell components and their functions. Different functions of cell like cell biochemistry, cell metabolism, cell communication, and cell composition.
Different types of intelligent body systems like- Immune system, Hormonal system, Cardiovascular system, Muscular systems etc.
Different defence mechanisms of body, Sympathetic body systems that understand different emotions, trauma, and external attacks. Intelligence of instincts, gut intelligence.

Different types of intelligence in different animals as case study. Survival intelligence, leadership intelligence, social intelligence, body language decoding, cognitive intelligence. Social and enterprising intelligence of ants, echo-locating skills of bats and such similar skills in different animals. Weather prediction, nest building skills of different species, survival tricks of

units.title: Study on implementation of biological intelligence in artificial systems
units.text: Study on implementation of biological intelligence in artificial systems. Applications of biological intelligence in field of computing like bio informatics, ANN, genetic algorithms, deep learning etc.

objectives: The course develops student understanding of mathematical aspects of motion. It emphasizes the analysis of moving rigid body systems using constitutive laws based on force and energy. It also introduces students to synthesize solutions using scripting on a computational platform.

outcomes.text: Describe the theoretical concepts in mathematical modelling
Analyze the given system using constitutive laws

objectives: The course introduces microprocessor architecture and enables students to learn programming and interfacing of microprocessor. This course will also help the students to understand the concepts of advanced processors, programming and interfacing of microcontrollers.

outcomes.text: explain the architectural design of basic and advanced microprocessors
build interfacing circuits using microprocessors and develop programs for various applications
construct interfacing circuits using microcontroller and develop programs for various applications

units.text: Microcontroller Programming and Hardware Interfacing Addressing modes, assembler directives and instruction set, programming timer and counters, interfacing of matrix keyboard, LCD, DAC and stepper motor.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course presents an elaborate treatment of stresses and strains induced in solid bodies under load conditions. The course emphasizes the system parameters critical to calculate deformation in solids. The course teaches the students the use of analytical tools to solve problems of elementary engineering design.

outcomes.text: Apply stress-strain relationships in beams to solve problems under varying load conditions
Determine the stresses and strains in members subjected to combined loading and select the theory of failure for static loading
Solve problems of practical importance using principles in solid mechanics

units.title: Simple Stress & Strain
units.text: Simple Stress & Strain Definitions of stress, axial, tensile and compressive stresses, shear stress. Hooke’s law, elastic limit, modulus of elasticity, yield stress, ultimate stress, modulus of rigidity, bulk modulus, Poisson’s ratio, factor of safety Testing of Materials Tensile test, compression test, shear test & hardness test, stress- strain diagram permissible stress: FOS, stress concentration factor

units.title: Internal Forces & Stresses in Beams
units.text: Internal Forces & Stresses in Beams Shear force & bending moment diagrams for statically determinate beams for different types of loading, relationship between rate of loading, shear force and bending moment Theory of bending, classical flexural formula for straight beams & Bending stress distribution for different sections. Distribution of shear stress across commonly used plane sections

units.title: Simple Theory of Torsion
units.text: Simple Theory of Torsion Torsion of circular shafts - solid and hollow, stresses and strains in shaft when transmitting power

units.title: Direct & Bending Stress/ Bending moment combined with axial loads
units.text: Direct & Bending Stress/ Bending moment combined with axial loads Application to members subjected to eccentric loads and chimneys, core of the section

units.title: Principal Stresses
units.text: Principal Stresses General equations for transformation of stress, principles planes and principal stresses, Mohr’s circle

units.title: Thin cylindrical and spherical shells
units.text: Thin cylindrical and spherical shells Deformations in thin cylinders and spheres due to internal pressure, Hoop’s stress, longitudinal stress, compressibility, internal pressure analysis

text_books: 1. E. P. Popov, Mechanics of Materials, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall, 2015. 2. J. M. Gere and B. J. Goodno, Mechanics of Materials – SI Edition, 9th Edition, Cengage Learning, 2018.
reference_books: 1. W. Nash and M. Potter, Schaum's Outlines: Strength of Materials, 5th Edition, McGraw Hill Professional, 2010. 2. F. P. Beer, E. R. Johnston Jr. and J. T. DeWolf, Mechanics of Materials, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course elaborately explains the fluid properties and the static-dynamic nature of incompressible fluids. It emphasizes analytical techniques necessary for understanding the fundamental behavior of incompressible fluids. It teaches the students to use principles of laminar flow, turbulent flow and boundary layer theory to solve important practical problems.

outcomes.text: Summarize various fluid properties and understand static-dynamic nature of fluids
Analyze various practical problems using fundamental concepts of fluid kinematics and dynamics
Solve problems of practical importance using the fundamental physics of laminar and turbulent flow and boundary layer theory

units.title: Introduction to Fluid mechanics
units.text: Introduction to Fluid mechanics Concept of continuum, fluid properties, classification of fluid, Newton’s law of viscosity, stress-strain relationship, applications of fluid mechanics

units.title: Fluid Statics
units.text: Fluid Statics Pressure variation in static fluid, forces on submerged surfaces, stability of floating bodies

units.title: Fluid Kinematics & Dynamics
units.text: Fluid Kinematics & Dynamics Classification of flow, continuity equation, Euler equation of fluid flow, Bernoulli’s equation and its applications, conservation of mass, linear and angular momentum, Navier-Stokes equation and its applications

units.title: Internal flows
units.text: Internal flows Pipe flow, friction factor, Moody’s Diagram, minor and major losses, pipe networks, concept of laminar and turbulent flows

units.title: External Flows
units.text: External Flows Concept of boundary layer approximation, boundary layer over flat plate, Boundary Layer thickness, Von-Karman momentum integral equation, concept of flow separation, control and concept of drag

text_books: 1. S. K. Som, G. Biswas, Introduction to Fluid Mechanics and Fluid Machines, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017. 2. Y.A. Cengel and J. M. Cimbala, Fluid Mechanics: Fundamentals and Applications, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017.
reference_books: 1. P.N. Modi, S.M. Seth, Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics including Hydraulic Machines, 22nd Edition, Standard Book House, 2019. 2. F. M. White, Fluid Mechanics in SI Units, 8th Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Physics
objectives: The basic objective is to provide the students with fundamental concepts of solid-state devices and their applications. This course helps the students to understand the construction, working principle, characteristics and applications of electronic devices such as diodes, transistors and Op- amps. Students will also be able to design different types of filters and timer circuits for the given specifications.

outcomes.text: Choose the solid-state semiconductor devices for various applications
Explain the applications of simple op-amp, diode and transistor circuits
Construct filter and timer Circuits for various applications

units.title: Semiconductor Diodes and Applications
units.text: Semiconductor Diodes and Applications PN Diode- construction, working and characteristics of PN junction diode. Other SC diodes - zener, LED, Schottky, photodiode.

units.title: Bipolar Junction Transistor
units.text: Bipolar Junction Transistor BJT- PNP and NPN transistors, currents in BJT, characteristics of BJT, BJT configurations (CE, CB and CC) Biasing of BJT- concept of biasing of BJT, Q-point and load line, voltage divider biasing of BJT in CE configuration

units.title: Field Effect Transistors
units.text: Field Effect Transistors CMOS- construction of CMOS, static and dynamic characteristics of CMOS, and its small signal analysis

units.title: Application od Diodes and Transistors
units.text: Application od Diodes and Transistors Diode Applications- rectifiers, capacitive filter, clipper and clamper, SMPS, Linear Regulated Power Supply, mobile charger. BJT Applications- BJT as switch, BJT as amplifier CMOS Application- CMOS as amplifier, transmission gates, tri-state inverters, and buffers
Foundation of Operational Amplifiers ideal and practical op-amps, inverting and non-inverting amplifier, op-amp parameters, fundamentals of IC-741.

units.title: Linear Applications of Operational Amplifiers
units.text: Linear Applications of Operational Amplifiers Amplifiers- adder, differentiator, integrator, instrumentation amplifiers with three op-amps Converters- V to I, I to V converters Oscillators- Wien Bridge Oscillator using op-amp.

units.title: Non-Linear Applications of Operational Amplifiers
units.text: Non-Linear Applications of Operational Amplifiers Inverting Schmitt trigger Comparators- inverting and non-inverting comparator, zero crossing detector Precision Rectifiers- half wave and full wave precision rectifiers Sample and Hold Circuits and Logarithmic Amplifiers

units.title: Timer and Filter Circuits
units.text: Timer and Filter Circuits Timers-IC555 timer, working of astable and monostable multivibrator circuits. Filters-first order filters - low pass, high pass, band pass filter, band reject filters

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course elaborately explains the fluid properties and the static-dynamic nature of incompressible fluids. It emphasizes analytical techniques necessary for understanding the fundamental behavior of incompressible fluids. It teaches the students to use principles of laminar flow, turbulent flow and boundary layer theory to solve important practical problems.

outcomes.text: Summarize various fluid properties and understand static-dynamic nature of fluids
Analyze various practical problems using fundamental concepts of fluid kinematics and dynamics
Solve problems of practical importance using the fundamental physics of laminar and turbulent flow and boundary layer theory

units.title: Internal flows

objectives: The basic objective is to provide the students with fundamental concepts of solid-state devices and their applications. Explain the applications of simple op-amp, diode and transistor circuits
Construct filter and timer Circuits for various applications

program: B Tech Artificial Intelligence B Tech/MBA Tech. Computer Engineering
objectives: This course is an introduction to the field of Cyber Security. This course presents a balance of the managerial and technical aspects of the discipline. It will prepare students with the technical knowledge and skills needed to protect and defend computer systems and networks.

outcomes.text: Explain the basics of cyber security.
Implement mechanisms of cryptography, authentication and access controls.
Differentiate security mechanisms in programs and networks.
Describe risk management related to computer security.

program: B Tech Integrated Computer Engineering / B Tech / MBA Tech (Computer , EXTC)

objectives: This course provides a concise introduction to the fundamental concepts in machine learning from a practical perspective. Also it covers the different learning algorithms, paradigms and frameworks used in Machine Learning.

Apply regression model to solve problems in machine learning domain.

objectives: The course aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) by covering its foundational concepts and advanced applications. Students will gain insight into the historical development and evolution of RPA, along with a deep appreciation for the benefits and challenges of its implementation. By delving into RPA tools and their features, students will learn to harness workflow automation, create apps, grasp the distinctions between attended and unattended bots, and comprehend the symbiotic relationship between RPA and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

outcomes.text: Demonstrate understanding of fundamental RPA concepts, historical evolution, benefits and process analysis and selection
Analyze RPA tools, design bot workflows, and apply decision-making strategies, constructing optimized automation processes
Create user-centric app interfaces, develop integrated app functionalities aligned with RPA workflows, and deploy applications within operational frameworks
Evaluate ethical considerations, including data security and privacy, ensuring compliant RPA implementations, and making informed decisions regarding automation practices.

units.text: Building RPA Bots Basics of bot creation and configuration, Designing bot workflows using flowcharts, Implementing decision-making and branching in bots, Using variables and data types in RPA, Version control and change management for bots.

units.title: Advanced RPA Concepts
units.text: Advanced RPA Concepts Integrating with APIs and web services, Automating email communication and document processing, Handling unstructured data using OCR (Optical Character Recognition), Advanced error handling and recovery strategies, Using triggers and event-based automation.

units.title: App Creation, Deployment and Maintenance Using RPA

program: B Tech and MBA Tech Artificial Intelligence
objectives: This course develops students' skills in human-centered design, interdisciplinary teamwork, and problem-solving through structured project work. Students will engage in stakeholder analysis, prototyping, testing, and iterative refinement while integrating engineering principles, creativity, and sustainability. Emphasizing collaboration and ethical responsibility, the course prepares students for industry and community-driven challenges by enhancing their project management, communication, and critical thinking abilities.

outcomes.text: Critically evaluate complex, real-world challenges using systematic problem-solving approaches.
Lead and collaborate in interdisciplinary teams to develop scalable and impactful solutions.
Apply advanced design methodologies and emerging technologies to prototype and refine innovative solutions in research.
Integrate sustainability, ethics, and feasibility analysis into the design and implementation process.
Demonstrate professional communication through technical reports, presentations, and stakeholder engagement.

units.text: The course covers Problem Analysis, where students assess the problem context, constraints, stakeholders, and solution stage while conducting literature reviews and benchmarking existing solutions. In Design Thinking & Concept Development, they apply the phases of Design Thinking— Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test—to develop and refine innovative solutions. Prototyping & Testing involves transforming ideas into practical prototypes, conducting experiments, usability testing, and iterative refinements. Through Project Management & Documentation, students assign roles, track progress, and maintain structured records. Communication & Review focuses on preparing presentations, conducting design reviews, and incorporating feedback. Finally, Reflection & Improvement allows students to analyze challenges, enhance their skills, and document key learnings.

lab_work: The Laboratory work comprises various activities performed by the project teams for formulation, solution implementation and modification. Each team needs to submit the following documents:  Problem Statement Document  Project Development Report  Mid Semester Project Report  Research Paper / Conference Paper  Final Report / Page

objectives: The course aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) by covering its foundational concepts and advanced applications. Students will gain insight into the historical development and evolution of RPA, along with a deep appreciation for the benefits and challenges of its implementation. By delving into RPA tools and their features, students will learn to harness workflow automation, create apps, grasp the distinctions between attended and unattended bots, and comprehend the symbiotic relationship between RPA and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

outcomes.text: Demonstrate understanding of fundamental RPA concepts, historical evolution, benefits and process analysis and selection
Analyze RPA tools, design bot workflows, and apply decision-making strategies, constructing optimized automation processes
Create user-centric app interfaces, develop integrated app functionalities aligned with RPA workflows, and deploy applications within operational frameworks
Evaluate ethical considerations, including data security and privacy, ensuring compliant RPA implementations, and making informed decisions regarding automation practices.

objectives: This course aims to acquaint students with the fundamentals of the Internet of Things (IoT) and its building blocks. It helps to understand the IoT hardware and various protocols used in IoT applications for everyday life. It also provides information on associated technologies like cloud computing and hands-on expertise in building IoT applications.

outcomes.text: Describe the fundamentals of IoT
Demonstrate appropriate use of protocols and cloud services for a given application
Distinguish the IoT data using various data analytics methods
Construct IoT based projects using suitable hardware boards.

units.title: Introduction to IoT
units.text: Introduction to IoT Introduction and definition of IoT, IoT growth A statistical View, Application areas of IoT, Characteristics of IoT, IoT stack, Enabling Technologies Sensors, Cloud Computing, Big data Analytics, Embedded Computing Board, Communication protocols and user interface. Internet of Things challenges, IoT levels.

units.title: IoT hardware interface
units.text: IoT hardware interface Introduction to sensor interfacing, Types of sensors (LDR, Ultrasonic, Obstacle, Heartbeat, Gyro sensor, Gas sensor etc.), overview of Microcontrollers and ARM, Overview of Arduino boards, Node MCU and Raspberry PI board.

units.title: Protocols for IoT
units.text: Protocols for IoT Networking Architectures: Star, Mesh, Tree, Short distance protocols: IEEE 802.15.4, 6LowPan, Zigbee, Wi-Fi, Messaging protocols: MQTT, CoAP and REST. Addressing and Identification Protocols: IPv4, IPV6 and Uniform Resource Identifier.

units.title: Cloud for IoT
units.text: Cloud for IoT Introduction, IoT with Cloud, Selection of Cloud services, Introduction of Fog Computing, Cloud Computing: Security aspects, Case study: Adafruit Cloud

units.title: Data Analytics in IoT
units.text: Data Analytics in IoT Machine Learning models: Classification, Regression, Clustering, Model building process: Training the model, Testing the model, Validation of Model, Electronics & Telecommunication (2023 2024) Modelling Algorithms: Decision tree, Liner Regression, Logistic Regression, and K means, Model Performance, Introduction to Big Data Platform, Big data pipeline. Case studies on data analytics

units.title: Application building with IoT
units.text: Application building with IoT Getting familiarized with Raspberry Pi: Architecture, Compatible Peripherals, Add-Ons, and Accessories, operating system for Raspberry Pi, setting up and initial configuration of Raspberry Pi, Application development with Raspberry Pi Web Lamp etc. Case Studies: Smart Cities, Smart Home Industrial Control, Smart Social Networks, Smart warehouse monitoring etc.

text_books: 1. Shriram K Vasudevan, Abishek S Nagarajan and RMD Sundaram, Internet of Things, 2nd Edition, Wiley, 2020. 2. Andrew Minteer, Analytics for the Internet of Things (IoT), 1st Edition, Packt Publishing Ltd, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Rajkumar Buyya and Amir Vahid Dastjerdi, Internet of Things: Principles and Paradigms, 2nd Edition, Morgan Kaufmann, 2016. 2. Harry G. Perros, An Introduction to IoT Analytics, 1st Edition, CRC Press, 2021.
lab_work: 8 to 10 practical exercises (and a practicum) based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech (Data Science and Artificial Intelligence)
prerequisites: Statistical Structures in Data and Inference
objectives: This course provides an introduction to time series analysis. It will educate students on how to choose an appropriate forecasting method in a particular environment and then apply it using necessary computations. It aims to equip students with various forecasting techniques and knowledge on modern statistical methods for analyzing time series data. It will also provide directions to Improve forecasting using better statistical models based on statistical analysis.

outcomes.text: Describe time series models and list their applications in various fields
Predict real life problems using time series models
Use statistical software to estimate the models from real data to draw conclusions and develop solutions from the estimated models
Compare different statistical models to integrate larger data points

units.title: Examples of time series
units.text: Examples of time series The basic steps in a forecasting task Time series graph Seasonal plots, Seasonal subseries plots, Lag plots, Autocorrelation and time series decomposition, Stationary models and autocorrelation function Estimation and elimination of trend and seasonal components
Time series regression models and Exponential smoothing

units.title: Modeling and Forecasting with ARMA Processes
units.text: Modeling and Forecasting with ARMA Processes Preliminary estimation, Maximum likelihood estimation, Diagnostics ,Forecasting Order selection

units.title: Nonstationary and Seasonal Time Series Models
units.text: Nonstationary and Seasonal Time Series Models ARIMA models, Identification techniques, Unit roots in time series, Forecasting ARIMA models, Seasonal ARIMA models, Regression with ARMA errors
SARIMA - Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average

units.title: Forecasting hierarchical and grouped time series
units.text: Forecasting hierarchical and grouped time series Hierarchical and grouped time series, Single level approaches, Forecast reconciliation

units.title: Advanced forecasting methods
units.text: Advanced forecasting methods Complex seasonality, Prophet model, Vector auto regressions, Bootstrapping and bagging

program: B Tech /MBA Tech Artificial Intelligence B Tech (AI and ML and AI and DS)
prerequisites: Basics of machine learning and deep learning
objectives: The course on Advanced Topics in Machine Learning aims to provide students with a deep understanding of contemporary techniques and methodologies. This course focuses on the recent advances in machine learning like few-shot learning, autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), transformer models. Finally, by delving into graph neural networks, students will learn to handle and analyze graph-structured data effectively. Overall, the course integrates theory with hands-on practice to prepare students for advanced challenges in machine learning.

outcomes.text: Explain and use meta-learning techniques for different applications
Apply concepts of Generative Adversarial Networks to real-world applications
Describe and use transformer architecture for sequence to sequence applications
Identify and analyze the use of graph neural networks for machine learning models

units.title: Meta- Learning
units.text: Meta- Learning Introduction to Meta-learning, Traditional machine learning vs. meta learning, Challenges in traditional machine learning and deep learning models with small datasets, need of few-shot, one shot and zero shot learning Siamese Network Architecture: Concept of Siamese Networks, Shared weights and parameters, Training Siamese Networks for Few-Shot Learning, Contrastive loss function, Triplet loss function, Real-world applications.

units.title: Autoencoders
units.text: Autoencoders Introduction to Autoencoders, Comparison of PCA with Autoencoders, Applications of Autoencoders, Types of Autoencoders: under complete autoencoders, Denoising Autoencoders, Sparse autoencoders, Variational Autoencoders, outlier detection using Autoencoders.

units.title: Deep Generative Models
units.text: Deep Generative Models Generative vs Discriminative Models, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN),Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks,Applications of GAN.

units.title: Transformer Architecture
units.text: Transformer Architecture Encoder decoder Architecture, Attention Cues, Attention Pooling, Attention Scoring Functions, Bahdanau Attention, Self-Attention and Positional Encoding, Multiheaded attention, Transformer Architecture.

units.title: Graph Neural Networks
units.text: Graph Neural Networks Introduction to Graph Neural Networks, Applications, graph construction, graph representation learning.

units.title: Graph Neural Networks for Node Classification
units.text: Graph Neural Networks for Node Classification Supervised Graph Neural Networks: General Framework of Graph Neural Networks, Graph Convolutional Networks, Graph Attention Networks, Neural Message Passing Networks, Continuous Graph Neural Networks Unsupervised Graph Neural Networks: Variational Graph Auto-Encoders, Deep Graph Infomax. Introduction to the concepts: Over-smoothing Problem, Expressive Power of Graph Neural Networks, scalability, interpretability, adversarial robustness.

objectives: This course provides knowledge of evolutionary computation techniques such as mechanisms of natural evolution--including genetic recombination, mutation, and natural selection--to automatically produce solutions to a wide range of problems. The students will explore several evolutionary computation techniques and apply them to practical problems.

outcomes.text: Explain the concepts Evolutionary computations and algorithms
Use the concepts of variation and selection techniques for particular classes of problems
Implement various evolutionary algorithms including ant colony optimization and swarm optimization algorithms
Apply the principles of evolutionary and genetic programming for real life problems

objectives: We live in a technology enabled world where data is collected and process as we interact with any technology product or service. outcomes.text: Analyze various cybersecurity threats and countermeasures
Explain various security technologies and mechanisms
Describe various professional, ethical and legal issues related to cybersecurity

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Basic Components of Cybersecurity, Characteristics of Information, vulnerabilities, threats , Attacks and controls ,goals of security, Mitre ATT&CK framework, Cyber Kill Chain, Security System development life cycle, cybercrimes and criminals, professional, legal and ethical issues.

units.title: Design Principles
units.text: Design Principles Various Security threats and attacks, method of defence, Design Principles, Security policies, types of security policies, Case Study

units.title: Program Security
units.text: Program Security Secure programs, Non malicious Program Errors, Viruses and other malicious code, countermeasures.

units.title: OS Security
units.text: OS Security Security Features of OS, security in the design of OS, Rootkit

units.title: Database Security
units.text: Database Security Security requirements for databases, reliability and integrity, database disclosure

units.title: Identity and access management(IAM)
units.text: Identity and access management(IAM) Authentication basics, Passwords, authentication tokens, certificate based and biometric authentication, Kerberos, SSO approaches, Multi- Factor Authentication, attacks on authentication schemes, Access control principles, DAC, MAC, and Role based Access Control, Access control models, identity and access provisioning lifecycle

units.title: Security Technologies
units.text: Security Technologies Firewalls, Kinds of Firewalls, Filtering Services, DMZ, Implementing policies (Default allow, Default Deny) on proxy, NAT, Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems, types of IDPS, Virtual Private Network, SSH

text_books: 1. C. Pfleeger, S. L. Pfleeger and J. Margulies, Security in Computing, 5th Edition, Pearson Education, 2018. 2. M. Whitman and H. Mattford, Principles of Information Security with MindTap, 7th Edition, Cengage, 2023.
reference_books: 1. B. Forouzan, D. Mukhopadhya, Cryptography and Network Security, 4th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2019. 2. W. Stallings, Cryptography and Network Security: Principles and Practice, 8th Edition, Pearson Education, 2023.
lab_work: 8 to 10 exercises based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech CSE-Cybersecurity
objectives: This course provides an introduction to the network security. The course discusses about various network attacks and their countermeasures. It also discusses about various security protocols like TLS, IPSec, DNSSEC and other.

outcomes.text: Discuss various network (wired and wireless) attacks and suggest their countermeasures
Describe security protocols used at different layers of the OSI model
Discuss about cloud security and network monitoring

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction The OSI Security architecture, security attacks, services and mechanisms, attack surfaces and attack trees, network security model.

units.title: Network Access Control
units.text: Network Access Control Network Access Control, Extensible Authentication Protocol, IEEE 802.1X Port-Based Network Access Control.

units.title: Cloud and virtualization security
units.text: Cloud and virtualization security Introduction to cloud computing, cloud security risks and countermeasures, data protection in the cloud, Cloud security as the service, types of hypervisors, virtualization security, infrastructure as a code, security concerns for virtual environment.

units.title: Transport-Level Security
units.text: Transport-Level Security Web Security Considerations, Secure Sockets Layer, Transport Layer Security, HTTPS standard, Secure Shell (SSH) application.

units.title: Wireless Network Security

units.title: Electronic Mail Security
units.text: Electronic Mail Security Pretty Good Privacy, S/MIME, DNSSEC, Sender Policy Framework, Domain Keys Identified Mail, Domain-Based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC).

units.title: IP Security
units.text: IP Security IP Security Overview, IP Security Policy, Encapsulating Security Payload, Combining Security Associations, Internet Key Exchange (IKE).

units.title: Network Traffic Monitoring and SIEM
units.text: Network Traffic Monitoring and SIEM Introduction, network monitoring techniques, SIEM.

Demonstrate an understanding of various Analysis and Design models that provide a basis for the software development

program: B Tech/MBA Tech Information Technology, B Tech CSE-Cybersecurity

objectives: The objective of the course is to familiarize the students with tools and processes to analyze datasets using visual representations of the data. Create visualization charts appropriate for the underlying data
Apply modern statistical learning techniques on data visualizations
Design and implement interactive links between various objects in a data visualization report
