program: B Tech CSE-Cybersecurity
objectives: This course teaches the fundamentals of secure programming in C. Students will learn how a C program runs “under-the-hood” by analysing at the machine-level representation. The coding standards and design principles of secure programming are explored so that security can be built- in the design time to avoid security vulnerabilities.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamentals of secure programming
Analyse C programs for security vulnerabilities
Implement security attacks

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Philosophy of Secure Programming, Security Policies and Procedures, Motivation behind Software Security, Examples of Vulnerabilities, A Tour of Computer Systems, Secure Programming Design Principles.

units.title: Representing Information
units.text: Representing Information Bits and Bytes, Hexadecimal Notation, Addressing and Byte Ordering, Integer Security, Integer Arithmetic, Integer Overflow and Security Vulnerabilities.

units.title: Machine-Level Representation of C Programs and Optimizing Program
units.text: Machine-Level Representation of C Programs and Optimizing Program Performance Conditional Statements, Switch-Case Statements, Loops, Procedures, Array Allocation and Access, Eliminating Loop Inefficiencies, reducing Procedure Calls, Eliminating Unneeded Memory References, Loop Unrolling, Enhancing Parallelism, Memory Performance, Stack-based Buffer Overflow.

units.title: Data Pointer and Function Pointer Vulnerabilities
units.text: Data Pointer and Function Pointer Vulnerabilities Smashing the stack by exploiting pointers, Dynamic Memory Allocation and security.

units.title: Linking
units.text: Linking Load-time exploitation, Basics of static and dynamic linking.

units.title: Format String Vulnerabilities
units.text: Format String Vulnerabilities Stack layout of variadic functions, Exploit the formatted output string and buffer overflow vulnerabilities.

units.title: Concurrency and File I/O Security
units.text: Concurrency and File I/O Security Path Traversal Vulnerabilities, File I/O deadlock and Race Condition, time of check and time of use (TOCTOU) vulnerabilities.

program: B Tech CSE-Cybersecurity
objectives: This course is an in-depth study of Cloud security. It aims at providing adequate exposure to the security measures adopted in Cloud. Students will learn various security issues along with techniques and ways to protect cloud.

outcomes.text: Classify the cloud reference model and its usage
Examine Cloud Security w.r.t data, Platform, Infrastructure, application and operations
Evaluate the legal, ethical and compliance aspects of cloud

units.text: Cloud Concepts and Reference Architecture Cloud Computing Definitions, Cloud Computing Characteristics, Cloud Service Categories, Cloud Deployment Models, Cloud Shared Considerations.

units.title: Cloud Data Security

program: B Tech CSE-Cybersecurity
objectives: We live in a technology enabled world where data is collected and process as we interact with any technology product or service. This data is used by the companies to predict our tastes, our habits, or future possible health problems. This use of data has created a big privacy threat. Various governments have developed stringent privacy laws like GDPR to protect the privacy of their citizens. Effective information privacy is very difficult. Globally organizations are approaching privacy problem based on two concepts: Privacy by design and privacy engineering. In this course students will be exposed to both the concepts.

outcomes.text: Identify data privacy threats and suggest their countermeasures
Implement various privacy models
Design privacy program for an organization

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Data privacy need and concepts, privacy by design principles, information privacy requirements and guidelines, information privacy threats and vulnerabilities, privacy risk assessment, privacy and security control selection, privacy integration, testing and evaluation, trade-offs between privacy and security, usable privacy.

units.title: Data Privacy Attacks and Models
units.text: Data Privacy Attacks and Models The evolving threat environment, privacy threat taxonomy, NIST threat model, privacy attacks (Linkage Attack, re-identification Attack, Statistical Attack), De-identification of direct identifiers, Basic Privacy Models K- Anonymity, L-Diversity, t-closeness, Differential Privacy, Generalisation, Suppression, Perturbation, Randomization.

units.title: Online Privacy
units.text: Online Privacy The online eco-system for personal data, online privacy threats, online privacy requirements, privacy notices and tracking, Privacy Preserving Data Sharing and Publications, Privacy Preserving Access Control Models.

units.title: Information Privacy Management
units.text: Information Privacy Management Information privacy governance, privacy roles, privacy program plan, key areas of privacy management, privacy policy, NIST privacy framework, OASIS privacy management model, privacy awareness training and education.

units.title: Legal and Regulatory Requirements
units.text: Legal and Regulatory Requirements The EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), US Privacy laws (COPPA, HIPPA and others), The China Personal Information Protection Law, Draft Indian Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019.

text_books: 1. William Stallings, Information Privacy Engineering and Privacy by Design, Addison-Wesley, 2020.
reference_books: 1. N. Venkataramanan and A. Shriram, Data privacy: principles and practice, CRC Press, 2017. 2. Joanna Lyn Grama, Legal and privacy issues in information security, 3rd Edition, JB Learning, 2022. 3. Nishant Bhajaria, Data Privacy A Run Book for Engineers, Manning Publications, 2022.

objectives: To provide knowledge of the basic techniques and tools of Operations Research and apply these techniques constructively to make effective business decisions.

Solve problems based on Transportation Models and Assignment Models

units.title: Introduction to OR
units.text: Introduction to OR Origin of OR and its definition. Concept of optimizing performance measure, Types of OR problems, Deterministic vs. Stochastic optimization, Phases of OR problem approach.

units.title: Linear Programming Problem
units.text: Linear Programming Problem Linear programming – Examples from industrial cases, formulation & definitions, Matrix form. Implicit assumptions of LPP. Hyperplane, Convex set, Convex polyhedron, Extreme points, Basic feasible solutions. Graphical method: Special cases – infeasibility, unboundedness, redundancy & degeneracy. Simplex Algorithm –computational details, Big-M method, identification and resolution of special cases through simplex iterations. Sensitivity analysis. Duality – formulation, results, dual-simplex and primal-dual algorithms.

units.title: Integer Programming Problem
units.text: Integer Programming Problem Gomory cutting plane method, branch and bound algorithm, applications.

units.title: Transportation and Assignment problems
units.text: Transportation and Assignment problems Transportation Problems -Formulation, minimization and maximization models, Solution methods – NWCR, Least cost and VAM, test for optimality (MODI method), variations in Transportation problem (Unbalanced, Degeneracy, Alternate solution, Prohibited routes) Assignment Problem - Formulation, Balanced & unbalanced situations, Hungarian method, variations in Assignment problem (Multiple solution, Maximization case, Restrictions on assignment).

units.title: Network Analysis
units.text: Network Analysis CPM Project definition, Project scheduling techniques –PERT & CPM, Determination of critical paths, Estimation of Project time and its variance in PERT using statistical principles, Concept of project crashing/time-cost trade-off.

units.title: Game Theory
units.text: Game Theory Introduction - Characteristics of Game Theory, two-person zero-sum games with and without saddle-points, pure and mixed strategies.

units.title: Simulation Methodology
units.text: Simulation Methodology Definition and steps of simulation, random number, random number generator, Discrete Event System Simulation– clock, event list, Application in Scheduling, Queuing systems and Inventory systems. Introduction, Processing n jobs through two machines, Processing n jobs through 3 machines, Processing n jobs through m machines.

program: B. Tech (Computer Engineering)
objectives: The primary objective of this course is to study and practice fundamental techniques in developing secure web based applications, including vulnerability of web based applications and how to protect those applications from attacks. In addition, advanced topics related to Web, such as E-commerce security, advance internet security protocols and certificate management etc., will also be studied. Students are encouraged to read a published research paper on the related topics.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of web security such as SSL & HTTP security protocols.
Understand the proxy server and various firewalls and internet security protocols.
Understand the Certificates Management & analyse Electronic Payment Systems.
Classify different web based malwares and evaluate a web-based system with respect to its security requirements.

objectives: This course provides a concise introduction to the fundamental concepts in machine learning from a practical perspective. Also, it covers the different learning algorithms and paradigms used in Machine Learning.

outcomes.text: Identify machine learning techniques suitable for a given problem
Solve the problems using various machine learning techniques
Develop an application using machine learning techniques
Evaluate and interpret the results of the algorithms.

units.text: Exploratory data Analysis Missing Value Treatment, Handling Categorical data: Mapping ordinal features, Encoding class labels, Performing one-hot encoding on nominal features, Outlier Detection and Treatment. Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes Classifier, Support Vector Machines, Neural Networks: Perceptron, Multi-layer Perceptron, Training using Back-propagation, Applications

prerequisites: Programming concepts and Image Processing fundamentals
objectives: The objective of this course is to provide concepts of Computer Vision, key algorithms for image descriptors, image segmentation, and motion estimation. This course also provides the emerging object detection techniques using deep learning.

outcomes.text: Explain fundamental image processing techniques required for computer vision.
Apply feature extraction and image segmentation techniques.
Understand the concept of image classification and image recognition.
Analyze applications of computer vision techniques in real-time scenarios.
Implement computer vision techniques using appropriate tools and frameworks.

units.title: Introduction to Computer Vision and Image Descriptors
units.text: Introduction to Computer Vision and Image Descriptors Introduction to Computer Vision, Low-level, Mid-level, High-level, Overview of Diverse Computer Vision Applications Edge Detectors- Laplacian Of Gaussian (LOG), Difference Of Gaussians (DOG), Histogram of Oriented Gaussian

units.title: Interest Point Descriptors
units.text: Interest Point Descriptors Harris, Hessian, Local invariant feature detectors and descriptors, SIFT, SURF, FAST, BRIEF, ORB

units.title: Feature Matching
units.text: Feature Matching Matching key points, weighted distance function, normalized cross correlation, cosine similarity, matching criteria, matching histograms, Geometric transformation, correspondence and least square, RANSAC, From points to images, nearest neighbor matching, bag of words, Vector of Locally Aggregated Descriptors (VLAD) representation and matching, pyramid matching- Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD)

units.title: Image segmentation and Object Tracking
units.text: Image segmentation and Object Tracking K-Means, Mean-shift, blob detection, Background subtraction, Optical flow, Lucas-Kanade method, change detection, Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), object tracking using template matching, tracking by feature detection

units.title: Stereo Vision and Camera Calibration
units.text: Stereo Vision and Camera Calibration Overview, Linear camera model, intrinsic and extrinsic matrices, simple stereo, Image transformations, 2D Transformation, Geometric Operators, Affine Transformations, Computing Homography, dealing with outliers, warping and blending images, Epipolar geometry, Stereo Vision for depth estimation

objectives: This course provides a concise introduction to the fundamental concepts in machine learning from a practical perspective. Also, it covers the different learning algorithms and paradigms used in Machine Learning.

outcomes.text: Identify machine learning techniques suitable for a given problem
Solve the problems using various machine learning techniques
Develop an application using machine learning techniques
Evaluate and interpret the results of the algorithms.

units.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
units.text: Machine Learning Fundamentals Terminology, Supervised and Unsupervised Learning with examples, Underfitting / Overfitting, Bias-Variance Trade-off, Model Selection, Applications

units.title: Exploratory data Analysis
units.text: Exploratory data Analysis Missing Value Treatment, Handling Categorical data: Mapping ordinal features, Encoding class labels, Performing one-hot encoding on nominal features, Outlier Detection and Treatment. Feature Engineering: Variable Transformation and Variable Creation, Selecting meaningful features.

units.title: Regression
units.text: Regression Linear regression using Least Squares (analytical approach), Linear regression using Gradient Descent (iterative approach), Multiple linear regression, Polynomial regression

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification Performance Evaluation, Confusion Matrix, Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, ROC Curves, AUC, k-fold Cross-Validation. Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes Classifier, Support Vector Machines, Neural Networks: Perceptron, Multi-layer Perceptron, Training using Back-propagation, Applications

units.title: Tree-Based Methods
units.text: Tree-Based Methods Basics of Decision Trees, Regression Trees, Classification Trees, Trees v/s Linear Models, Advantages and Disadvantages of Trees, Ensemble techniques- Bagging, Boosting, Random forest

units.title: Unsupervised Learning
units.text: Unsupervised Learning Challenges of Unsupervised Learning, Partitioning Methods: K-Means clustering, Dimension Reduction Methods, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Hierarchical Clustering, Introduction to Recommender systems (Non-personalized and Content-based)

text_books: 1. Judith Hurwitz, Daniel Kirsch, “Machine Learning for dummies”, IBM Limited Edition, John Wiley & Sons, Inc., 2018. 2. Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jerome Friedman, “The Elements of Statistical Learning: Data Mining, Inference, and Prediction”, 2nd Edition, Springer, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Aurelien Geron, “Hands-on Machine Learning with Scikit Learn, Keras and Tensorflow”, 2nd Edition, Oreilly Publication, 2019. 2. James, Witten, Hastie, Tibshirani,” Introduction to Statistical Learning”, 7th Edition, Springer, 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments (and a practicum where applicable) based on the syllabus

program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Business Communication & value Science-I (BTCS01006), Business Communication & value Science-II (BTCS02006)
objectives: Recognize the importance of DT, Explain the phases in the DT process, List the steps required to complete each phase in DT process, Apply each phase in the DT process, Use doodling and story telling in presenting ideas and prototypes, Create value proposition statements as part of their presentations, Recognize how DT can help in functional work, Recognize how Agile and DT complement each other to deliver customer satisfaction.

outcomes.text: Identify the steps in the DT process
Recognize the steps in the empathize phase of DT and create Empathy Map
Identify the steps required to conduct an immersion activity
Create a prototype.

units.title: Why is Design Thinking important for business?
units.text: Why is Design Thinking important for business? Stories and examples will be used to introduce Design Thinking to the participants. We will use relevant stories and the following videos. 1. YouTube video: The Design Thinking Process – Sprouts (3.57 mins) Leverage TCS-provided DT content to show the evolution of DT and why is important in present 2. Business environment. Can be a video. (2 mins) Lecturer to encourage the students to maintain their Satori slam book and capture their learning points in it.

units.title: Why is Design Thinking important for you?
units.text: Why is Design Thinking important for you? Experiential activity, Products that you loved and hated: In this activity, learners will have to share about a product they like of disliked based on their experience. What would they need in a bad product to make it good?

units.title: What is DT?
units.text: What is DT? Introduce the 5-Step Stanford Model using YouTube videos: The video will give a brief idea about the five steps:  Empathize (search for rich stories and find some love)  Define (user need and insights – their POV)  Ideate (ideas, ideas, ideas)  Prototype (build to learn)  Test (show, don’t tell) Start all over and iterate the flow as much as possible

units.title: What is empathy?
units.text: What is empathy? Touch the target activity (Recap from Sem 2 Unit 4), Discussions in class

text_books: 1. Idris Mootee, “Design Thinking for Strategic Innovation, CEO Idea Couture”, 1st Edition, Wiley, 2014 Reference Books: 1. Nir Eyal,” how to build habit forming products”, 1st Edition, Portfolio/penguin,2014 2. Rod Judkins, “The Art of Creative Thinking”, 1st Edition, Perigee Books, 2016 3. Dan Senor and Saul singer, “Start Up nation”, 1st Edition, Grand central publishing, 2011 4. Simon Sinek, “Start with Why”, 1st Edition, Portfolio/penguin,2011
reference_books: FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | EMPATHY (2:29 mins) 01 5 How to empathize? Moccasin Walk activity for 1 hour to allow learners experience stepping into the shoes of another person. This is an individual activity. Sharing observations with the group. Suggest that students try this even in their free time away from studies. 01 6 Intro to Immersion Activity Introduction to immersion activity through flowcharts and handouts and examples (to be provided by TCS DT Team) (steps and the question template: 1. We met; 2. We were amazed to realize that; 3. We wonder if this means It would change the world if) 01 7 Immersion activity Participants will be divided into four groups. Each group will need to visit any one of the following places to conduct an immersion activity. They need to interview people and fill up the DT question template 02 (explained in the last class) 1. College cafeteria 2. College library 3. College sports facility 4. Transport facility near college 8 Creating personas Start with YouTube videos explaining the process of persona creation: 1. Personas – What is a persona and how do I create one? (2019) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GNvLpfXCge8 Each group will create at least one persona based on the immersion study they conducted in the empathize stage (refer to the four question templates). The group can use A4 pages, colours and other props to create and display their respective persona. Reference: https://www.interaction- design.org/literature/article/personas-why-and-how-you-should- use-them Lecturer to guide participants on getting the personas right (based on guidelines provided by TCS DT Team). 03 9 Problem statements Session will begin with YouTube videos on how to define problem statements in the Define phase. 1. FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | REFRAME (1:55 mins) Lecturer will provide examples of problem statements in class (based on handouts provided by TCS DT Team) 01 10 Defining problem statements Group activity, in which each group will define the key problem statements (max three) for their lead personas. Each group will present while the remaining groups will do a peer 02 review. Finally, lecturer will moderate/validate the problem statements (based on handouts provided by TCS DT Team) 11 How to Ideate? The session will start with YouTube videos: 1. FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | IDEATE (1:54 secs) 2. What Is Six Thinking Hats? (Litmos Heroes) (1:58 secs) Lecturer to briefly tell them about the guidelines of ideating (to be provided by TCS DT Team) 01 12 Ideation games Game 1: Six Thinking Hats Game 2: Million-dollar idea 01 13 Ideate to find solutions Participants will work in their assigned groups to ideate solutions for the problem statements they identified (as continuation of immersion activity) applying ideation methods discussed in the previous session. They will get scores based on how well they can apply the ideation methods. Lecturers will observe the groups separately and assign them scores based on specific rubric (provided by the TCS DT Team). 01 14 Let’s doodle! Participants will first watch a video on doodling: Doodling – how it can help in presenting ideas during ideate and protype phases After that, participants will complete an activity on doodling. 01 15 What is Storytelling in DT? Activity- Research to find out about people who have used DT in providing solutions. Present their findings in forms of stories. (Recap 02 from Unit- Sem-) Suggested topics to be provided by the TCS DT team. 16 Why is a Prototype important in Design Thinking? The session will start with an activity to drive home the importance of creating a prototype in the design thinking process. As part of debrief of the activity, lecturer will share relevant examples and prototyping guidelines (provided by the TCS DT Team). Finally, the participants will watch two YouTube videos: 1. FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | PROTOTYPE 2. Prototyping Phase - Design Thinking | Coursera https://www.coursera.org/lecture/patient-safety-project- planning/prototyping-phase-jVuQn 01 17 Prototype your idea This is a group activity in which the participants will work in groups (created at the beginning of the course, in which they did immersion, persona creation, defining problem statement and ideating) to create prototypes based on the solutions they had identified. Lecturer to share feedback based on guidelines provided by the TCs DT team. 02 18 Value Proposition Statement You Tube: What is Value Proposition (by Venture Well) (3:51 mins)? Lecturer to discuss the guidelines for creating a value proposition statement (to be provided by the TCS DT Team Each group now needs to create value proposition statement for the solution they have suggested. 01 19 Testing in Design Thinking Participants will first watch a YouTube video: FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | TESTING 01 After that lecturers will explain them the importance of Testing the prototype through stories (provided by the TCS DT Team). They will also explain how the loop works in DT between the Empathize and Testing phases. 20 Test the Prototype Each group needs to test their prototype created earlier and: 1. Document user feedback 2. Write down their inference from the feedback 01 21 Role of DT in your work Lecturer conducts a group/open house discussion on: “How DT can help me to become a better coder?”, Lecturer needs to capture the key learning points in these discussions. 01 22 Suggested session on: How Agile and DT complement each other to deliver customer satisfaction 01 23 Share your Satori Participants will be asked to share their Satori moments from the DT sessions 01 Total

units.title: What is DT?
units.text: What is DT? Introduce the 5-Step Stanford Model using YouTube videos: The video will give a brief idea about the five steps:  Empathize (search for rich stories and find some love)  Define (user need and insights – their POV)  Ideate (ideas, ideas, ideas)  Prototype (build to learn)  Test (show, don’t tell) Start all over and iterate the flow as much as possible

objectives: The course intends to introduce students to the fundamentals of developing application on Cloud, specifically public clouds such as AWS, AZURE and Google.

outcomes.text: Understand fundamentals and know how to design applications for Cloud
Develop applications using various services
Deploy applications on Cloud by using cloud native services
Analyse recent developments in Cloud computing.

units.title: Virtualization

units.title: Cloud
units.text: Cloud Service Components and Providers: Cloud Service Components, Cloud components Guiding Principle with respect to utilization/Security/Pricing. And the applications of Cloud. Public Cloud Platforms overview and their usage: AWS, Azure and Google

Cloud Security and Monitoring Tools
Recent trends in Cloud Computing

program: B Tech/MBA Tech (Computer Engineering) / B Tech Computer Science/ B Tech Computer Science and Business Systems
prerequisites: Programming for Problem Solving, Data Structures, Discrete Mathematics
objectives: Objective of this course is to demonstrate a familiarity with major algorithm design paradigm. Analyze the asymptotic performance of algorithms and Devise efficient algorithms in common engineering design situations.

outcomes.text: Understand the space-time complexity of an algorithm
Evaluate divide and conquer approach of algorithm design
Apply greedy technique of algorithm design
Analyze dynamic programming and Backtracking algorithm design paradigm.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: What is Algorithms, types of Algorithms: greedy, divide & conquer, backtracking, etc. Analysis of Algorithms complexity. Introduction of P, NP, NP Complete and NP hard problems.

units.title: Analysing the Algorithms
units.text: Analysing the Algorithms: Time and Space Complexity of Algorithms, Asymptotic notations, Asymptotic order, Properties of big oh, big omega, and big theta, Classifying functions by their asymptotic growth rates, Best case, average Case and worst case analysis. Master’s Theorem and Substitution Method, Recursion Tree Method.

units.title: Divide and Conquer Technique
units.text: Divide and Conquer Technique: The general method, control abstraction for divide and conquer, Finding the maximum and minimum: straightforward and recursive algorithm, Merge sort, Quick sort.

units.title: Greedy Technique
units.text: Greedy Technique: The general method, control abstraction, Optimal storage on tapes, Knapsack problem, Job sequencing with deadlines, Optimal merge patterns, Huffman code.

units.title: Dynamic Programming
units.text: Dynamic Programming: The general method, principle of optimality, Multistage graphs, Single source shortest path - Bellman Ford algorithm, 0/1-knapsack, Matrix Chain multiplication, Longest Common Subsequence problem.

units.title: Backtracking
units.text: Backtracking: The general method, The n–queens problem, Sum of subsets, Graph coloring.

text_books: 1. Ellis Horowitz, and Sartaj Sahani, Fundamentals of Computer Algorithms, 2nd Edition, University Press, 2008. 2. Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E., Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Introduction to Algorithms, 2nd Edition, PHI Learning, 2010.
reference_books: 1. Sara Baase and Alan Van Gelder, Computer Algorithms Introduction to Design and Analysis, 3rd Edition, Addison-Wesley, 2000. 2. Aho, Hopcroft and Ullman, Data Structures and Algorithms, Addison-Wesley, 2000.

program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To Provide the foundation for understanding the theory and practice of compilers, learn programming language translation and compiler design concepts, understand language recognition, symbol table management, semantic analysis and code generation.

outcomes.text: Comprehend the working of lexical analysis, parsing
Understand the significance of code generation and code optimization
Implement working module of compiler.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Phases of compilation and overview. Lexical Analysis (scanner): Regular languages, finite automata, regular expressions, regular expression to finite automata, scanner generator (lex, flex).

units.title: Syntax Analysis (Parser)
units.text: Syntax Analysis (Parser): Context-free languages and grammars, push-down automata, LL(1) grammars and top-down parsing, operator grammars, LR(O), SLR(1), LR(1), LALR(1) grammars and bottom-up parsing, ambiguity and LR parsing, LALR(1) parser generator (yacc, bison)

units.title: Semantic Analysis
units.text: Semantic Analysis: Attribute grammars, syntax directed definition, evaluation and flow of attribute in a syntax tree.

units.title: Symbol Table
units.text: Symbol Table: Basic structure, symbol attributes and management. Run-time environment: Procedure activation, parameter passing, value return, memory allocation, scope.

units.title: Intermediate Code Generation
units.text: Intermediate Code Generation: Translation of different language features, different types of intermediate forms.

units.title: Code Improvement (optimization)
units.text: Code Improvement (optimization): control-flow, data-flow dependence, local optimization, global optimization, loop optimization, peep-hole optimization.

units.title: Architecture dependent code improvement
units.text: Architecture dependent code improvement: instruction scheduling (for pipeline), loop optimization (for cache memory), Register allocation and target code generation.

units.title: Advanced topics
units.text: Advanced topics: Type systems, data abstraction, compilation of Object Oriented features and non-imperative programming languages

text_books: 1. V. Aho, R. Sethi and J. Ullman, “Compilers: Principles, Techniques and Tools”, 2nd Edition, Addison-Wesley, 2006. 2. Levine R. John, Tony Mason and Doug Brown, “Lex & Yacc”, 2nd Edition, O’Reilly media, 2007.
reference_books: 1. Bjarne Stroustrup, “The Design and Evolution of C++” 2nd Edition, Addison-Wesley, 2007.

program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To acquaint students with various facets of management, sensitize students on social issues impacting society in general and business in particular.

outcomes.text: Comprehend concepts of management to Analyze and evaluate the influence of historical forces on the current practice of management
Develop the process of management's four functions: planning, organizing, leading, and controlling
Recognize the ethical issues in corporate governance and to adhere to the ethical codes.

units.title: Management Theories
units.text: Management Theories: Concept and Foundations of Management, Evolution of Management Thoughts [Pre-Scientific Management Era (before 1880), Classical management Era (1880-1930), Neo-classical Management Era (1930- 1950), Modern Management era (1950-on word). Contribution of Management Thinkers: Taylor, Fayol, Elton Mayo etc. Functions of Management- Planning, Organizing, Staffing, Directing, Controlling.

Planning & Strategy- Concept of planning, Significance of planning, Classification of planning: Strategic plan, Tactical plan and Operational plan, Process of planning, Barriers to effective planning. MBO, Management by Exception. Business Environment- Macro & Micro Environment, Understanding Management Contexts- Constraints & Challenges.Vision & Mission.

units.title: Decision Making
units.text: Decision Making: Managers as Decision makers. Types of decision- Programmed and Un-programmed decisions, concept of Rationality and bounded rationality in decision making, role of intuition in decision making. Steps in an effective decision-making process.

units.title: Organizing
units.text: Organizing: Formal and Informal Organization, Organization structures- mechanistic Vs Organic Structures, Types of structures (Simple, functional, Divisional & Matrix) Line and staff authority. Specialization, Centralization Vs Decentralization, Formalization. Structures with Narrow and wide spans.

units.title: Individual Differences
units.text: Individual Differences: Personality & Individual characteristics, differences and significance, Diversity.

units.title: Work Related Attitudes, Values and Perception
units.text: Work Related Attitudes, Values and Perception: Attitude and Behaviour, Major Job Attitudes, Values- Rockeach, Hofstede, Meaning and concept of Perception, Factors influencing perception. , Frequently used shortcuts in judging others

units.title: Leading and Managing Teams
units.text: Leading and Managing Teams: Leader Vs Manager, Leadership Styles Leadership theories- Trait, Behavioural and Leadership. Groups Vs. teams, skills necessary to manage teams. Five stages of group/team development
Motivation - Types of Motivation; Relationship between Motivation, Performance and Engagement, Content Motivational Theories - Needs Hierarchy Theory, Two Factor Theory, Theory X and Theory Y.

units.title: Introduction to Major Areas of HRM
units.text: Introduction to Major Areas of HRM: Orientation to talent management – onboarding, recruitment, selection, appraisal, training, exit.

units.title: Controlling
units.text: Controlling: Control, Types and Strategies for Control, Steps in Control Process, Budgetary and Non- Budgetary Controls. Characteristics of Effective Controls, Establishing control systems, Control frequency, and Methods.

units.title: Managerial Ethics
units.text: Managerial Ethics: Ethics and Business, Ethics of Marketing & advertising, Ethics of Finance & Accounting, Decision – making frameworks, Business and Social Responsibility, International Standards, Corporate Governance, Corporate Citizenship, Corporate Social Responsibility

units.title: Organizational Culture
units.text: Organizational Culture: Meaning and dimensions, Role of founders’ values and vision in creating and sustaining culture,Types of organizational cultures,Impact of culture on image and performance of the organization. , Managing Cultural Diversity

units.title: Organizational Outcomes
units.text: Organizational Outcomes : Power & Influence- Sources of Power, Power tactics, Stress :Sources of stress at workplace, Stress Management, Impact of stress on performance.

units.title: Organization Change
units.text: Organization Change: Need for change, Resistance to change, how to overcome resistance to change, Kurt Lewin’s process of change.
Project presentations

text_books: 1. Daft RL, “Understanding the theory and design of organizations.”,11th Edition, IGI Global, 2016.
reference_books: 1. Stephen P. Robbins, Timothy A. Judge, Neharika Vohra, “Organizational Behavior”, 16th Edition, Pearson, 2018

program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To familiarize the participants with the basic concepts of business strategy, facilitate the participants to apply the concepts to live corporate situations, and to explain contemporary concepts of strategy.

outcomes.text: Comprehend fundamental concepts of strategic management to analyze business situations and apply these concepts to solve business problems
Understand the fundamental principles of and interrelationships among business functions such as: R&D, production, marketing, finance, HR and information technology
Understand the inter-relationships of business to individuals, other organizations, government and society
Analyze complex, unstructured qualitative and quantitative problems, using appropriate tools.

units.title: Introduction to Strategic Management
units.text: Introduction to Strategic Management: Importance of Strategic Management, Vision and Objectives, Schools of thought in Strategic Management, Strategy Content, Process, and Practice, Fit Concept and Configuration Perspective in Strategic Management.

units.title: Internal Environment of Firm- Recognizing a Firm’s Intellectual Assets
units.text: Internal Environment of Firm- Recognizing a Firm’s Intellectual Assets: Core Competence as the Root of Competitive Advantage, Sources of Sustained Competitive Advantage, Business Processes and Capabilities-based Approach to Strategy.

units.title: External Environments of Firm- Competitive Strategy
units.text: External Environments of Firm- Competitive Strategy: Five Forces of Industry Attractiveness that Shape Strategy, The concept of Strategic Groups, and Industry Life Cycle, Generic Strategies, Generic Strategies and the Value Chain.

units.title: Corporate Strategy, and Growth Strategies
units.text: Corporate Strategy, and Growth Strategies: The Motive for Diversification, Related and Unrelated Diversification, Business Portfolio Analysis, Expansion, Integration and Diversification, Strategic Alliances, Joint Ventures, and Mergers & Acquisitions.

units.title: Strategy Implementation
units.text: Strategy Implementation: Structure and Systems: The 7S Framework, Strategic Control and Corporate Governance.

units.title: Home Assignment
units.text: Home Assignment: Latest business events would be discussed in class and students should be ready to discuss these events (in groups). The topic will be mentioned beforehand. Students are required to meet in groups before coming to class and prepare on the topic. There will be periodic homework assignments relating to the course concepts or mini-cases. Specific instructions will be given separately.

prerequisites: Business Communication & value Science-I (BTCS01006), Business Communication & value Science-II (BTCS02006)
objectives: Recognize the importance of DT, Explain the phases in the DT process, List the steps required to complete each phase in DT process, Apply each phase in the DT process, Use doodling and story telling in presenting ideas and prototypes, Create value proposition statements as part of their presentations, Recognize how DT can help in functional work, Recognize how Agile and DT complement each other to deliver customer satisfaction.

outcomes.text: Identify the steps in the DT process
Recognize the steps in the empathize phase of DT and create Empathy Map
Identify the steps required to conduct an immersion activity
Create a prototype.

units.title: Why is Design Thinking important for business?
units.text: Why is Design Thinking important for business? Stories and examples will be used to introduce Design Thinking to the participants. We will use relevant stories and the following videos. 1. YouTube video: The Design Thinking Process – Sprouts (3.57 mins) Leverage TCS-provided DT content to show the evolution of DT and why is important in present 2. Business environment. Can be a video. (2 mins) Lecturer to encourage the students to maintain their Satori slam book and capture their learning points in it.

units.title: Why is Design Thinking important for you?
units.text: Why is Design Thinking important for you? Experiential activity, Products that you loved and hated: In this activity, learners will have to share about a product they like of disliked based on their experience. What would they need in a bad product to make it good?

units.title: What is DT?
units.text: What is DT? Introduce the 5-Step Stanford Model using YouTube videos: The video will give a brief idea about the five steps:  Empathize (search for rich stories and find some love)  Define (user need and insights – their POV)  Ideate (ideas, ideas, ideas)  Prototype (build to learn)  Test (show, don’t tell) Start all over and iterate the flow as much as possible

units.title: What is empathy?
units.text: What is empathy? Touch the target activity (Recap from Sem 2 Unit 4), Discussions in class

text_books: 1. Idris Mootee, “Design Thinking for Strategic Innovation, CEO Idea Couture”, 1st Edition, Wiley, 2014 Reference Books: 1. Nir Eyal,” how to build habit forming products”, 1st Edition, Portfolio/penguin,2014 2. Rod Judkins, “The Art of Creative Thinking”, 1st Edition, Perigee Books, 2016 3. Dan Senor and Saul singer, “Start Up nation”, 1st Edition, Grand central publishing, 2011 4. Simon Sinek, “Start with Why”, 1st Edition, Portfolio/penguin,2011
reference_books: FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | EMPATHY (2:29 mins) 01 5 How to empathize? Moccasin Walk activity for 1 hour to allow learners experience stepping into the shoes of another person. This is an individual activity. Sharing observations with the group. Suggest that students try this even in their free time away from studies. 01 6 Intro to Immersion Activity Introduction to immersion activity through flowcharts and handouts and examples (to be provided by TCS DT Team) (steps and the question template: 1. We met; 2. We were amazed to realize that; 3. We wonder if this means It would change the world if) 01 7 Immersion activity Participants will be divided into four groups. Each group will need to visit any one of the following places to conduct an immersion activity. They need to interview people and fill up the DT question template (explained in the last 02 class) 1. College cafeteria 2. College library 3. College sports facility 4. Transport facility near college 8 Creating personas Start with YouTube videos explaining the process of persona creation: 1. Personas – What is a persona and how do I create one? (2019) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GNvLpfXCge8 Each group will create at least one persona based on the immersion study they conducted in the empathize stage (refer to the four question templates). The group can use A4 pages, colours and other props to create and display their respective persona. Reference: https://www.interaction-design.org/literature/article/personas- why-and-how-you-should-use-them Lecturer to guide participants on getting the personas right (based on guidelines provided by TCS DT Team). 03 9 Problem statements Session will begin with YouTube videos on how to define problem statements in the Define phase. 1. FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | REFRAME (1:55 mins) Lecturer will provide examples of problem statements in class (based on handouts provided by TCS DT Team) 01 10 Defining problem statements Group activity, in which each group will define the key problem statements 02 (max three) for their lead personas. Each group will present while the remaining groups will do a peer review. Finally, lecturer will moderate/validate the problem statements (based on handouts provided by TCS DT Team) 11 How to Ideate? The session will start with YouTube videos: 1. FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | IDEATE (1:54 secs) 2. What Is Six Thinking Hats? (Litmos Heroes) (1:58 secs) Lecturer to briefly tell them about the guidelines of ideating (to be provided by TCS DT Team) 01 12 Ideation games Game 1: Six Thinking Hats Game 2: Million-dollar idea 01 13 Ideate to find solutions Participants will work in their assigned groups to ideate solutions for the problem statements they identified (as continuation of immersion activity) applying ideation methods discussed in the previous session. They will get scores based on how well they can apply the ideation methods. Lecturers will observe the groups separately and assign them scores based on specific rubric (provided by the TCS DT Team). 01 14 Let’s doodle! Participants will first watch a video on doodling: Doodling – how it can help in presenting ideas during ideate and protype phases After that, participants will complete an activity on doodling. 01 15 What is Storytelling in DT? Activity- Research to find out about people who have used DT in providing solutions. Present their findings in forms of stories. (Recap from Unit- Sem-) Suggested topics to be provided by the TCS DT team. 02 16 Why is a Prototype important in Design Thinking? The session will start with an activity to drive home the importance of creating a prototype in the design thinking process. As part of debrief of the activity, lecturer will share relevant examples and prototyping guidelines (provided by the TCS DT Team). Finally, the participants will watch two YouTube videos: 1. FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | PROTOTYPE 2. Prototyping Phase - Design Thinking | Coursera https://www.coursera.org/lecture/patient-safety-project- planning/prototyping-phase-jVuQn 01 17 Prototype your idea This is a group activity in which the participants will work in groups (created at the beginning of the course, in which they did immersion, persona creation, defining problem statement and ideating) to create prototypes based on the solutions they had identified. Lecturer to share feedback based on guidelines provided by the TCs DT team. 02 18 Value Proposition Statement You Tube: What is Value Proposition (by Venture Well) (3:51 mins)? Lecturer to discuss the guidelines for creating a value proposition statement (to be provided by the TCS DT Team 01 Each group now needs to create value proposition statement for the solution they have suggested. 19 Testing in Design Thinking Participants will first watch a YouTube video: FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | TESTING After that lecturers will explain them the importance of Testing the prototype through stories (provided by the TCS DT Team). They will also explain how the loop works in DT between the Empathize and Testing phases. 01 20 Test the Prototype Each group needs to test their prototype created earlier and: 1. Document user feedback 2. Write down their inference from the feedback 01 21 Role of DT in your work Lecturer conducts a group/open house discussion on: “How DT can help me to become a better coder?”, Lecturer needs to capture the key learning points in these discussions. 01 22 Suggested session on: How Agile and DT complement each other to deliver customer satisfaction 01 23 Share your Satori Participants will be asked to share their Satori moments from the DT sessions 01 Total

units.title: Home Assignment
units.text: Home Assignment: Latest business events would be discussed in class and students should be ready to discuss these events (in groups). The topic will be mentioned beforehand. Students are required to meet in groups before coming to class and prepare on the topic. There will be periodic homework assignments relating to the course concepts or mini-cases. program: B Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Business Communication & value Science-I (BTCS01006), Business Communication & value Science-II (BTCS02006)
objectives: Recognize the importance of DT, Explain the phases in the DT process, List the steps required to complete each phase in DT process, Apply each phase in the DT process, Use doodling and story telling in presenting ideas and prototypes, Create value proposition statements as part of their presentations, Recognize how DT can help in functional work, Recognize how Agile and DT complement each other to deliver customer satisfaction.

outcomes.text: Identify the steps in the DT process
Recognize the steps in the empathize phase of DT and create Empathy Map
Identify the steps required to conduct an immersion activity
Create a prototype.

units.title: Why is Design Thinking important for business?
units.text: Why is Design Thinking important for business? Stories and examples will be used to introduce Design Thinking to the participants. We will use relevant stories and the following videos. 1. YouTube video: The Design Thinking Process – Sprouts (3.57 mins) Leverage TCS-provided DT content to show the evolution of DT and why is important in present 2. Business environment. Can be a video. (2 mins) Lecturer to encourage the students to maintain their Satori slam book and capture their learning points in it.

units.title: Why is Design Thinking important for you?
units.text: Why is Design Thinking important for you? Experiential activity, Products that you loved and hated: In this activity, learners will have to share about a product they like of disliked based on their experience. What would they need in a bad product to make it good?

units.title: What is DT?
units.text: What is DT? Introduce the 5-Step Stanford Model using YouTube videos: The video will give a brief idea about the five steps:  Empathize (search for rich stories and find some love)  Define (user need and insights – their POV)  Ideate (ideas, ideas, ideas)  Prototype (build to learn)  Test (show, don’t tell) Start all over and iterate the flow as much as possible

units.title: What is empathy?
units.text: What is empathy? Touch the target activity (Recap from Sem 2 Unit 4), Discussions in class

Moccasin Walk activity for 1 hour to allow learners experience stepping into the shoes of another person. This is an individual activity. Sharing observations with the group. Suggest that students try this even in their free time away from studies. 01 6 Intro to Immersion Activity Introduction to immersion activity through flowcharts and handouts and examples (to be provided by TCS DT Team) (steps and the question template: 1. Each group will need to visit any one of the following places to conduct an immersion activity. They need to interview people and fill up the DT question template (explained in the last 02 class) 1. Personas – What is a persona and how do I create one? Reference: https://www.interaction-design.org/literature/article/personas- why-and-how-you-should-use-them Lecturer to guide participants on getting the personas right (based on guidelines provided by TCS DT Team). 03 9 Problem statements Session will begin with YouTube videos on how to define problem statements in the Define phase. 1. FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | REFRAME (1:55 mins) Lecturer will provide examples of problem statements in class (based on handouts provided by TCS DT Team) 01 10 Defining problem statements Group activity, in which each group will define the key problem statements 02 (max three) for their lead personas. Each group will present while the remaining groups will do a peer review. Finally, lecturer will moderate/validate the problem statements (based on handouts provided by TCS DT Team) 11 How to Ideate? The session will start with YouTube videos: 1. FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | IDEATE (1:54 secs) 2. What Is Six Thinking Hats? (Litmos Heroes) (1:58 secs) Lecturer to briefly tell them about the guidelines of ideating (to be provided by TCS DT Team) 01 12 Ideation games Game 1: Six Thinking Hats Game 2: Million-dollar idea 01 13 Ideate to find solutions Participants will work in their assigned groups to ideate solutions for the problem statements they identified (as continuation of immersion activity) applying ideation methods discussed in the previous session. They will get scores based on how well they can apply the ideation methods. Lecturers will observe the groups separately and assign them scores based on specific rubric (provided by the TCS DT Team). 01 14 Let’s doodle! Participants will first watch a video on doodling: Doodling – how it can help in presenting ideas during ideate and protype phases After that, participants will complete an activity on doodling. 01 15 What is Storytelling in DT? Activity- Research to find out about people who have used DT in providing solutions. Present their findings in forms of stories. (Recap from Unit- Sem-) Suggested topics to be provided by the TCS DT team. 02 16 Why is a Prototype important in Design Thinking? The session will start with an activity to drive home the importance of creating a prototype in the design thinking process. As part of debrief of the activity, lecturer will share relevant examples and prototyping guidelines (provided by the TCS DT Team). Finally, the participants will watch two YouTube videos: 1. FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | PROTOTYPE 2. Prototyping Phase - Design Thinking | Coursera https://www.coursera.org/lecture/patient-safety-project- planning/prototyping-phase-jVuQn 01 17 Prototype your idea This is a group activity in which the participants will work in groups (created at the beginning of the course, in which they did immersion, persona creation, defining problem statement and ideating) to create prototypes based on the solutions they had identified. Lecturer to share feedback based on guidelines provided by the TCs DT team. 02 18 Value Proposition Statement You Tube: What is Value Proposition (by Venture Well) (3:51 mins)? Lecturer to discuss the guidelines for creating a value proposition statement (to be provided by the TCS DT Team 01 Each group now needs to create value proposition statement for the solution they have suggested. 19 Testing in Design Thinking Participants will first watch a YouTube video: FHIL | Stages of Design Thinking | TESTING After that lecturers will explain them the importance of Testing the prototype through stories (provided by the TCS DT Team). They will also explain how the loop works in DT between the Empathize and Testing phases. 01 20 Test the Prototype Each group needs to test their prototype created earlier and: 1. Document user feedback 2. program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: The objective of the course is to understand the growing significance and impact of services on the growth and economy and the scientific ways to run the operations so as to optimize the business and brand returns.

outcomes.text: Understand concepts about Services and distinguish it from Goods
Able to identify characteristics and nature of Services
Comprehend ways to design Services and evaluate them using Service qualities
Understand how various methods can be used to operate and manage Service businesses
Understand how innovation can be approached from Services point of view

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Introduction to the course, Introduction to service operations, Role of service in economy and society, Introduction to Indian service sector. Nature of Services and Service Encounters: Differences between services and operations, Service package, characteristics, various frameworks to design service operation system, Kind of service encounter, importance of encounters. Service-Dominant Logic: From Goods-Dominant logic to Service-Dominant logic, Value Co-creation.

units.title: Service Strategy and Competitiveness
units.text: Service Strategy and Competitiveness: Development of Strategic Service Vision (SSV), Data Envelopment Analysis. New Service Development: NSD cycle, Service Blueprinting, Elements of service delivery system. Service Design: Customer Journey and Service Design, Design Thinking methods to aid Service Design. Locating facilities and designing their layout: models of facility locations (Huff's retail model), Role of service-scape in layout design. Service Quality: SERVQUAL, Walk through Audit, Dimensions of Service quality & other quality tools.

units.title: Service Guarantee & Service Recovery
units.text: Service Guarantee & Service Recovery: How to provide Service guarantee? How to recover from Service failure?

units.title: Forecasting Demand for Services
units.text: Forecasting Demand for Services: A review of different types of forecasting methods for demand forecasting. Managing Capacity and Demand: Strategies for matching capacity and demand, Psychology of waiting, Application of various tools used in managing waiting line in services. Managing Facilitating Goods: Review of inventory models, Role of inventory in services. Managing service supply relationship: Understanding the supply chain/hub of service, Strategies for managing suppliers of service. Vehicle Routing Problem: Managing after sales service, Understanding services that involve transportation of people and vehicle, Techniques for optimizing vehicle routes.

units.title: Service Innovation
units.text: Service Innovation: Services Productivity, Need for Services Innovation. Student Project: Option 1: Choose any service organization around and present it from the perspective of: nature of service, classification of service, blueprint or service design analysis, service quality, and any additional perspective you would like to add. Option 2: Choose any latest research paper in services and explain your understanding and feedback on the same.

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To provide a brief introduction to data mining techniques from a practical perspective. To introduce several data pre-processing and data mining techniques for accurate model building based on real domain data.

outcomes.text: Understand basic concepts and techniques of Data Mining
Develop skills of using data mining software for solving practical problems
Understand and apply several statistical analysis techniques: regression, ANOVA and data reduction.

units.title: Introduction to Data Mining
units.text: Introduction to Data Mining: What is data mining? Related technologies - Machine Learning, DBMS, OLAP, Statistics, Stages of the Data Mining Process, Data Mining Techniques, Knowledge Representation Methods, Applications

units.title: Data preprocessing
units.text: Data preprocessing: Data cleaning, Data transformation, Data reduction, Discretization and generating concept hierarchies, Installing Weka 3 Data Mining System, Experiments with Weka - filters, discretization Data mining knowledge representation: Task relevant data, Background knowledge, Representing input data and output knowledge, Visualization techniques Attribute-oriented analysis: Attribute generalization, Attribute relevance, Class comparison, Statistical measures

units.title: Data mining algorithms - Association rules
units.text: Data mining algorithms - Association rules: Motivation and / terminology, Example: mining weather data, Basic idea: item sets, Generating item sets and rules efficiently, Correlation analysis Data mining algorithms - Classification: Basic learning/mining tasks, Inferring rudimentary rules: 1R, algorithm, Decision trees, covering rules Data mining algorithms – Prediction: The prediction task, Statistical (Bayesian) classification, Bayesian networks, Instance- based methods (nearest neighbor), linear models

units.title: Descriptive analytics
units.text: Descriptive analytics: Data Modeling, Trend Analysis, Simple Linear Regression Analysis

units.title: Forecasting models
units.text: Forecasting models: Heuristic methods, predictive modeling and pattern discovery, Logistic Regression: Logit transform, ML estimation, Tests of hypotheses, Wald test, LR test, score test, test for overall regression, multiple logistic regression, forward, backward method, interpretation of parameters, and relation with categorical data analysis. Interpreting Regression Models, Implementing Predictive Models Generalized Linear model: link functions such as Poisson, binomial, inverse binomial, inverse Gaussian, Gamma. Non-Linear Regression (NLS): Linearization transforms their uses & limitations, examination of non-linearity, initial estimates, and iterative procedures for NLS, grid search, Newton-Raphson, steepest descent, Marquardt’s methods. Introduction to semiparametric regression models, additive regression models. Introduction to nonparametric regression methods

units.title: Time Series Analysis
units.text: Time Series Analysis: Auto - Covariance, Auto-correlation and their properties. Exploratory time series analysis, Test for trend and seasonality, Exponential and moving average smoothing, Holt – Winter smoothing, forecasting based on smoothing Linear time series models: Autoregressive, Moving Average, / Autoregressive Moving Average and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average models; Estimation of ARMA models such as Yule-Walker estimation for AR Processes, Maximum likelihood and least squares estimation for ARMA Processes, Forecasting using ARIMA models Prescriptive Analytics: Mathematical optimization, Networks modeling-Multi-objective optimization-Stochastic modeling, Decision and Risk analysis, Decision trees.

Box, G.E.P and Jenkins G.M. “Time Series Analysis, Forecasting and Control”, 1st Edition, Holden-Day, 1970.
reference_books: 1. Draper, N. R. and Smith. H, Hosmer, D. W. and Lemeshow, S., “Applied Logistic Regression”, 3rd Edition, Wiley Publication, 1998.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of web programming
Design front end of the web application using HTML5, CSS3, Javascript.
Implement client-side technologies – Jquery, Ajax, Bootstrap, AngularJS
Implement back end technology and databases for restful services

objectives: The capstone project is designed to provide a culminating design experience to the final-year students’ learning with essentially required hands-on experience to ensure that they graduate with the required practical and soft skills. The course aims to encourage students to think critically, solve challenging problems, do a feasibility study and develop written and oral communication skills, teamwork and planning. The students may also work in interdisciplinary areas which will help broaden their scope and learning in different domains.

outcomes.text: Select an appropriate problem statement after reviewing the literature and identifying the research gaps.
Formulate the different use cases/feasible design model.
Implement the prototype/proof of concept, test and validate the results.
Manage a team project.
Summarize the topic into a technical report.

prerequisites: Business Strategy, Financial & Cost Accounting, Financial Management
objectives: This course will help the students to get an overview of the traditional financial theories of portfolio management, calculus models, and optimization techniques.

outcomes.text: Understand existing financial models in a quantitative and mathematical way.
Apply these quantitative tools to solve complex problems in the areas of portfolio management, risk management and financial engineering.
Explain the approaches required to calculate the price of options.
Identify the methods required to analyse information from financial data and trading systems.

units.text: Numerical methods relevant to integration, differentiation and solving the partial differential equations of mathematical finance: examples of exact solutions including Black Scholes and its relatives, finite difference methods including algorithms and question of stability and convergence, treatment of near and far boundary conditions, the connection with binomial models, interest rate models, early exercise, and the corresponding free boundary problems, and a brief introduction to numerical methods for solving multi-factor models.

units.title: Black-Scholes framework
units.text: Black-Scholes framework: Black-Scholes PDE: simple European calls and puts; put-call parity. The PDE for pricing commodity and currency options. Discontinuous payoffs - Binary and Digital options. The Greeks: theta, delta, gamma, vega & rho and their role in hedging. The mathematics of early exercise - American options: perpetual calls and puts; optimal exercise strategy and the smooth pasting condition. Volatility considerations - actual, historical, and implied volatility; local vol and volatility surfaces. Simulation including random variable generation, variance reduction methods and statistical analysis of simulation output. Pseudo random numbers, Linear congruential generator, Mersenne twister RNG. The use of Monte Carlo simulation in solving applied problems on derivative pricing discussed in the current finance literature. The technical topics addressed include importance sampling, Monte Carlo integration, Simulation of Random walk and approximations to diffusion processes, martingale control variables, stratification, and the estimation of the “Greeks.”

units.title: Financial Products and Markets
units.text: Financial Products and Markets: Introduction to the financial markets and the products which are traded in them: Equities, indices, foreign exchange, and commodities. Options contracts and strategies for speculation and hedging.

Application areas include the pricing of American options, pricing interest rate dependent claims, and credit risk. The use of importance sampling for Monte Carlo simulation of VaR for portfolios of options.

units.title: Statistical Analysis of Financial Returns
units.text: Statistical Analysis of Financial Returns: Fat-tailed and skewed distributions, outliers, stylized facts of volatility, implied volatility surface, and volatility estimation using high frequency data.

Copulas, Hedging in incomplete markets, American Options, Exotic options, Electronic trading, Jump Diffusion Processes, High-dimensional covariance matrices, Extreme value theory, Statistical Arbitrage.

program: B Tech CSBS
objectives: This course introduces concepts, methodologies and performance metrics for still image and motion picture processing. It also helps to develop a foundation for further study and research in the signal processing domain.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamentals of digital images, including pixel relationships, resolution, distance measures, and file formats.
Apply image enhancement techniques such as point processing, spatial filtering, and histogram equalization for image improvement.
Analyze morphological image processing techniques and edge detection methods for feature extraction.
Compare different image segmentation methods, including thresholding, region-based segmentation, and the Otsu method.
Explain video representation concepts and motion estimation techniques used in digital video compression.

units.title: Image fundamentals
units.text: Image fundamentals Representation of digital image, image as a matrix, image as a function, basics of colour image, spatial and gray level resolution, distance measures-Euclidean distance and m path, image file formats (TIFF, PNG, JPEG).

units.title: Image enhancement
units.text: Image enhancement Point processing techniques Linear- digital negative, Piecewise linear-contrast stretching, thresholding, intensity level slicing, Nonlinear- log transformation, power law transformation, Neighborhood processing techniques-smoothing spatial filters, sharpening spatial filters, median filters, Gaussian filtering. Histogram processing-histogram equalization. Image in Frequency domain: Fourier spectrum, Fourier analysis, filtering in frequency domain

units.title: Image transforms
units.text: Image transforms Discrete Fourier Transform, Hadamard transform, Discrete cosine transform and its applications for image compression

units.title: Morphological image processing
units.text: Morphological image processing Dilation, erosion, opening, closing, Hit–or-Miss transformation, basic morphological algorithms- boundary extraction on binary images, thinning, thickening, gray scale morphology

units.title: Edge Detection
units.text: Edge Detection Gradient based edge detection- First order and second order derivative, Edge detection operators- Prewitt, Sobel, Laplacian, Laplacian of Gaussian, canny edge detector.

units.title: Image segmentation
units.text: Image segmentation Basic relationships between pixels, Component labeling (4, 8 and m connectivity) Segmentation using thresholding, Bayesian classification of foreground and background pixels, expectation- maximization theorem for binarization, Otsu method, region-based segmentation- region growing, region splitting and merging.

units.title: Colour Image Processing
units.text: Colour Image Processing Colour fundamentals and colour models (RGB, CMY, CMYK, HSI, YUV, HSV), model transformation, colour slicing, histogram processing of colour images.

units.title: Fundamentals of digital video and its compression
units.text: Fundamentals of digital video and its compression Video representation- temporal correlation, video frame classifications, I, P and B frames, Fundamentals of motion estimation, motion estimation algorithms- exhaustive search block matching, 2D-log search method and 3 step search method.

text_books: 1. R.C Gonzalez and Richard Woods, Digital Image Processing, Pearson publication, 4th Edition, 2018. 2. Wilhelm Burger and Mark J. Burge, Digital Image Processing: An Algorithmic Introduction, Springer publications, 2nd Edition, 2022.
reference_books: 1. Alasdair McAndrew, A Computational Introduction to Digital Image Processing, CRC Press, 2nd Edition, 2021 2. Syed Jahangir Badashah, Digital Image Processing, Lambert Academic Publishing, 2020

program: B Tech.(Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: This course focusses on the models, tools, and techniques for enforcement of security with some emphasis on the use of cryptography. Students will learn security from multiple perspectives. After the completion of the course, the students will be able to develop basic understanding of Information security, system attacks and defenses against them.

outcomes.text: Understand the basic goals of Information Security and Authentication Mechanism and Access control models in Information domain
Understand and Simulate Program Security tools and Understand Types of Virus and Threats
Understand and Compare various system and system designs
Compare and contrast between security of various operating systems and Database System.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Confidentiality, integrity and availability; Security violation and threats; Security policy and procedure; Assumptions and Trust; Security Assurance, Implementation and Operational Issues; Security Life Cycle.

units.title: Authentication
units.text: Authentication: Authentication basics, Password, Challenge response, SSO, Biometrics

units.title: Access Control Models
units.text: Access Control Models: Discretionary, mandatory, roll-based and task-based models, unified models, access control algebra, temporal and spatio-temporal models.

units.title: Program Security
units.text: Program Security: Secure programs, Non malicious Program Errors, Viruses and other malicious code, types of viruses, / attack mechanism of viruses, Targeted Malicious Code, Controls Against Program Threats.

units.title: Systems Design
units.text: Systems Design: Design principles, representing identity, control of access and information flow, confinement problem. Assurance: Building systems with assurance, formal methods, evaluating systems.

units.title: Logic-based System
units.text: Logic-based System: Malicious logic, vulnerability analysis, auditing, intrusion detection. Applications: Network security, operating system security, user security, program security. Special Topics: Data privacy, introduction to digital forensics, enterprise security specification.

units.title: Operating Systems Security
units.text: Operating Systems Security: Security Architecture, Analysis of Security in Linux/Windows.

units.title: Database Security
units.text: Database Security: Security requirements, Reliability and integrity, Sensitive data, Inference, Multilevel database, Proposals for multilevel security

units.title: Security Policies
units.text: Security Policies: Confidentiality policies, integrity policies, hybrid policies, non-interference and policy composition, international standards.

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To provide a brief introduction to data mining techniques from a practical perspective. To introduce several data pre-processing and data mining techniques for accurate model building based on real domain data.

outcomes.text: Understand basic concepts and techniques of Data Mining
Develop skills of using data mining software for solving practical problems
Understand and apply several statistical analysis techniques: regression, ANOVA and data reduction.

units.title: Introduction to Data Mining
units.text: Introduction to Data Mining: What is data mining? Related technologies - Machine Learning, DBMS, OLAP, Statistics, Stages of the Data Mining Process, Data Mining Techniques, Knowledge Representation Methods, Applications

units.title: Data preprocessing
units.text: Data preprocessing: Data cleaning, Data transformation, Data reduction, Discretization and generating concept hierarchies, Installing Weka 3 Data Mining System, Experiments with Weka - filters, discretization Data mining knowledge representation: Task relevant data, Background knowledge, Representing input data and output knowledge, Visualization techniques Attribute-oriented analysis: Attribute generalization, Attribute relevance, Class comparison, Statistical measures

units.title: Data mining algorithms - Association rules
units.text: Data mining algorithms - Association rules: Motivation and terminology, Example: mining weather data, Basic idea: item / sets, Generating item sets and rules efficiently, Correlation analysis Data mining algorithms - Classification: Basic learning/mining tasks, Inferring rudimentary rules: 1R, algorithm, Decision trees, covering rules Data mining algorithms – Prediction: The prediction task, Statistical (Bayesian) classification, Bayesian networks, Instance- based methods (nearest neighbor), linear models

units.title: Descriptive analytics
units.text: Descriptive analytics: Data Modeling, Trend Analysis, Simple Linear Regression Analysis

units.title: Forecasting models
units.text: Forecasting models: Heuristic methods, predictive modeling and pattern discovery, Logistic Regression: Logit transform, ML estimation, Tests of hypotheses, Wald test, LR test, score test, test for overall regression, multiple logistic regression, forward, backward method, interpretation of parameters, and relation with categorical data analysis. Interpreting Regression Models, Implementing Predictive Models Generalized Linear model: link functions such as Poisson, binomial, inverse binomial, inverse Gaussian, Gamma. Non-Linear Regression (NLS): Linearization transforms their uses & limitations, examination of non-linearity, initial estimates, and iterative procedures for NLS, grid search, Newton-Raphson, steepest descent, Marquardt’s methods. Introduction to semiparametric regression models, additive regression models. Introduction to nonparametric regression methods

units.title: Time Series Analysis
units.text: Time Series Analysis: Auto - Covariance, Auto-correlation and their properties. Exploratory time series analysis, Test for trend and seasonality, Exponential and moving average smoothing, Holt – Winter smoothing, forecasting based on smoothing Linear time series models: Autoregressive, Moving Average, Autoregressive Moving Average and Autoregressive Integrated / Moving Average models; Estimation of ARMA models such as Yule-Walker estimation for AR Processes, Maximum likelihood and least squares estimation for ARMA Processes, Forecasting using ARIMA models Prescriptive Analytics: Mathematical optimization, Networks modeling-Multi-objective optimization-Stochastic modeling, Decision and Risk analysis, Decision trees.

text_books: 1. Jiawei Han and Micheline Kamber, “Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques”, 3rd Edition, Morgan Kaufmann Publishers, 2010. 2. Lior Rokach and Oded Maimon, “Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery Handbook”, 2nd Edition, Springer, 2010. 3. Box, G.E.P and Jenkins G.M. “Time Series Analysis, Forecasting and Control”, 1st Edition, Holden-Day, 1970.
reference_books: 1. Draper, N. R. and Smith. H, Hosmer, D. W. and Lemeshow, S., “Applied Logistic Regression”, 3rd Edition, Wiley Publication, 1998.

program: B. Tech /MBA Tech (Computer Engineering, EXTC) B Tech CSBS
prerequisites: Data Structure and Algorithms, Programming for Problem Solving.
objectives: To impart knowledge of the fundamental theories, methods and techniques in the field of Artificial Intelligence and to design and develop AI systems.

outcomes.text: Explain agents and environment in AI
Apply various heuristic and searching strategies to solve problems in the AI domain
Design knowledge base using expert systems and game playing
Implement supervised and unsupervised learning approaches to solve problems in the AI domain

units.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
units.text: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Definitions of AI, Applications of Artificial Intelligence, Concept of Modeling, Inference and Learning. Introduction to Machine learning and Deep learning as a subset of AI. Intelligent agents, concept of rationality, structure of agents, Environment, Properties of task environment. Real world Examples of agents and environments.

units.title: Solving problems by Searching
units.text: Solving problems by Searching Problem solving agents, searching for solutions. Uninformed Search: Breadth first search, Depth first search, Uniform cost search Informed Search: Informed search strategies, Greedy Best First Search, A* search, Hill climbing, problems with hill climbing such as Local Maxima, Plateau, Ridge, Genetic Algorithm. Adversarial Search: Introduction to the Domain of a game, optimal decisions in games, minimax algorithm, Alpha-beta pruning.

units.title: Knowledge Representation

units.title: Constraint satisfaction Problem (CSP)
units.text: Constraint satisfaction Problem (CSP) Constraint satisfaction problems, Backtracking search for CSPs, variables and value ordering, propagating information through constraints, Intelligent backtracking, Local search for CSP. Case study on CSP.

units.title: Learning
units.text: Learning Inductive learning, Types of learning, supervised - decision trees classification, unsupervised learning – K- means clustering.

units.title: Expert system

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To provide a brief introduction to data mining techniques from a practical perspective. To introduce several data pre-processing and data mining techniques for accurate model building based on real domain data.

outcomes.text: Understand basic concepts and techniques of Data Mining
Develop skills of using data mining software for solving practical problems
Understand and apply several statistical analysis techniques: regression, ANOVA and data reduction.

units.text: Data preprocessing: Data cleaning, Data transformation, Data reduction, Discretization and generating concept hierarchies, Installing Weka 3 Data Mining System, Experiments with Weka - filters, discretization Data mining knowledge representation: Task relevant data, Background knowledge, Representing input data and output knowledge, Visualization techniques Attribute-oriented analysis: Attribute generalization, Attribute relevance, Class comparison, Statistical measures

units.title: Descriptive analytics
units.text: Descriptive analytics: Data Modeling, Trend Analysis, Simple Linear Regression Analysis

units.title: Forecasting models

Interpreting Regression Models, Implementing Predictive Models Generalized Linear model: link functions such as Poisson, binomial, inverse binomial, inverse Gaussian, Gamma. Introduction to semiparametric regression models, additive regression models. Introduction to nonparametric regression methods

outcomes.text: Understand Unified process
Elicit the Requirements using use case diagram for the given problem
Design interaction, structural, and dynamic model for a given problem
Design package, component and deployment model for the given problem.

Description of the Object Oriented Analysis process vs. the Structure Analysis Model.
