program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Introduction to Business Analytics and Business Intelligence, Machine Learning.
objectives: Students will be familiar with basic concepts of cognitive and analytical learning and will be able to use them in problem solving. The purpose of this course is to give students a broad understanding of the field of cognitive science. The course discusses models of cognition that are based on empirical studies of human behaviour and computer models of artificial intelligence. They will gain an in-depth understanding of the computational properties of natural languages and the commonly used algorithms for processing linguistic information.

outcomes.text: Understand the concepts of analytics and areas of cognitive learning
Analyse the various data and cognitive analytical techniques
Apply various artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning approaches and methodologies in real life work

units.title: Foundational Areas of Analytics
units.text: Foundational Areas of Analytics Introduction to Analytics: Definition, Description & Evolution of Analytics, History of Analytics, and Applicability of Analytics with development of Technology and Computer, How Analytics entered mainstream Concepts of Analytics: Various overlapping concepts and fields of Analytics such as Data Mining, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence and Simulation Introduction of Emerging Areas in Analytics: Understanding of emerging research areas of Analytics: Mathematical programming, Evolutionary computation, Simulation, Machine learning/data mining, Logic-based models, and, Combinations of categories Introduction of Value Chain of Analytics: Descriptive Analytics Covering Exploratory Data Analysis & Basic of Statistics, / VI Diagnostics Analytics: BI/Analysis, Trend, Pattern, Simultaneous Relationship, Predictive Analytics: Cause-Effect Relationship and Futuristic prediction in terms of probabilities, Continuous & Categorical Predictions, Simulation, Optimization, Multi-faceted Intelligent Technology driven Analytics combining Machine Intelligence with Human Brain Processing Abilities

units.title: Foundational Areas of Cognitive Science
units.text: Foundational Areas of Cognitive Science Introduction & Evolution of Cognitive Science: Introduction to the study of cognitive sciences, Brief history of cognitive science development and Methodological concerns in philosophy Understand Brain and Sensory Motor Information: Fundamentals of Neuro Science, Processing of sensory information in the brain, and Brain Imaging Elements Language & Linguistic Knowledge: Background and details of Syntax & Semantics, Understanding of Generative Linguistic Memory & Processing: Theory of Information Processing, Fundamentals of Short term Memory

units.title: Data Theory & Taxonomy Of Data
units.text: Data Theory & Taxonomy Of Data Data as a whole: Understanding of Data as a whole for distinguishing and relating various types of data and Categorization of Data: Structured, Unstructured Data, Quantitative & Qualitative Data Views of Data: Understanding Data as an interdisciplinary framework for learning methodologies: covering statistics, neural networks, and fuzzy logic, Various types of Scales: Nominal, Ordinal, Interval & Ratio Scales

units.title: Multivariate Data Analytics & Cognitive Analytics
units.text: Multivariate Data Analytics & Cognitive Analytics Overview: High level overview of Categorization of Techniques: Inter-dependence Relationship Techniques and Dependence Relationship Techniques Analytics Value Chain & Application of Analytics across Value Chain: Basic statistical concepts such as Descriptive & Diagnostics statistics, concept of random variables, discrete and continuous random variables, confidence interval, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance and correlation. Introduction of Prescriptive analytics Concepts: linear programming, integer programming, stochastic models. Cognitive analytics Concepts: Text Analytics, Learning Analytics, Data Mining, Cognitive Systems

units.title: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
units.text: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence: Various areas of AI: Knowledge: Text Analytics, Topic Modelling, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Natural Language Generation (NLG), Natural Language Understanding (NLU), Named-entity recognition (NER) Perception: Image Analytics, Video Analytics & Audio Analytics Memory: Cognitive Engagement: BOTs, Virtual & Digital Assistants, Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, Mixed Reality Learning: Intelligent Automation, Spectrum of AI Reactive Machine: Low memory, works on Known rules, such as Object Detection/Games/Recommendations specific to known Rules Limited Memory: Memory used to learn and improve continuously such as Most ML Models, Automated VehiclesTheory of Mind: Machine Understands and responds such as BoTs/Virtual/Digital Assistants Self-Aware: Human like intelligence such as Super Robots in Space etc

units.title: Approach & Methodology
units.text: Approach & Methodology: World Standard Methodology: CRISP-DM Methodology, SEMMA Methodology Real Life Work around Multi-Variate Analytics: A few Selected Real Life Work around Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Deep Learning: A few Selected Commonly used Techniques & Algorithms: ANN (Artificial Neural Network), CNN (Convolutional Neural Network), RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) RN Architecture: LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM, Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), CTRNN (Continuous Time RNN) Object Detection models: Faster R-CNN, cascade R-CNN. Mask RCNN, Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) ,You Only Look Once (YOLO), Retina-Net Autoencoders: Denoising Autoencoder, GAN Transformers: Attention based Encoder and Decoder: Eg- BERT(Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), Generative Pretrained Transformers GPT-3, GPT-2

objectives: This course introduces concepts in cryptography and computer security and discusses both their theoretical foundations and practical applications. It also provides fundamental knowledge on various aspects of network and system Security

outcomes.text: Explain and analyze symmetric key encryption and decryption
Use asymmetric key cryptography for data encryption
Describe various techniques of network security
Discuss various system security mechanisms

units.title: Introduction of Data Encryption
units.text: Introduction of Data Encryption Need for Data encryption, Goal of Security: confidentiality, integrity, authentication, Security attacks: Active, Passive attacks, Cryptanalytic and non- cryptanalytic. Classical techniques: Substitution ciphers, Transposition ciphers, Symmetric and asymmetric encryption.

units.title: Symmetric Key Encryption
units.text: Symmetric Key Encryption Data Encryption Standard (DES) Structure, Key generation, Encryption and Decryption, 2-DES, triple DES, confusion and Diffusion, Avalanche attack. Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) Algebraic structures, GF(28) fields, AES structure, round functions, key expansion, Encryption and Decryption, AES Security: Avalanche attack, confusion and Diffusion Key management: Kerberos

units.title: Asymmetric Key Encryption

units.title: Message Integrity and message Authentication
units.text: Message Integrity and message Authentication Message authentication codes (MAC), Hash functions, SHA-512, digital signatures

units.title: Network Security
units.text: Network Security Need for Security of Computer Networks, Transport layer security: Secure Socket Layer (SSL), IP Security: transport and tunnel modes, E-mail Security: PGP and S/MIME.

units.title: System Security
units.text: System Security Users, Trust and Trusted systems, Buffer overflow and malicious software, worms, viruses, denial of service attacks, Firewalls: construction and working principals, Intrusion detection systems, Introduction to SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) technology.

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: This course provides an introduction to the theory and practice of quantum computation. Topics covered include: physics of information processing, quantum logic, quantum algorithms including Shor's factoring algorithm and Grover's search algorithm, quantum error correction, quantum communication, and cryptography.

outcomes.text: Describe States, Operators, Measurements in Quantum computing.
Implement and apply Quantum Algorithms in real world problems.
Apply Quantum True Random Number Generators and Quantum key distribution (QKD) in real world problem.
Review the topics from Post-Quantum Cryptography.

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Operating Systems, Object Oriented Programming and Computer Networks
objectives: To educate students with wide knowledge in Mobile Computing

outcomes.text: Describe the mobile computing architecture and applications.
Compare location and handoff techniques.
Analyse wireless transmission networks and assess mobile ad-hoc, WSNs and cognitive radio networks.
Identify issues related to recent communication technologies for cellular network i.e. 5G network.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Overview of wireless and mobile infrastructure; Preliminary concepts on cellular architecture; Design objectives and performance issues; Radio resource management and interface; Propagation and path loss models; Channel interference and frequency reuse; Cell splitting; Channel assignment strategies; Overview of generations:- 1G to 5G.

units.title: Location and handoff management
units.text: Location and handoff management: Introduction to location management (HLR and VLR); Mobility models characterizing individual node movement (Random walk, Fluid flow, Markovian, Activity based); Mobility models characterizing the movement of groups of nodes (Reference point based group mobility model, Community based group mobility model); Static (Always vs. Never update, Reporting Cells, Location Areas) and Dynamic location management schemes (Time, Movement, Distance, Profile Based); Terminal Paging (Simultaneous paging, Sequential paging); Location management and Mobile IP; Overview of handoff process; Factors affecting handoffs and performance evaluation metrics; Handoff strategies; Different types of handoffs (soft, hard, horizontal, vertical)

units.title: Wireless transmission fundamentals
units.text: Wireless transmission fundamentals: Introduction to narrow and wideband systems; Spread spectrum; Frequency hopping; Introduction to MIMO; MIMO Channel Capacity and diversity gain; Introduction to OFDM; MIMO-OFDM system; Multiple access control (FDMA, TDMA, CDMA, SDMA); Wireless local area network; Wireless personal area network (Bluetooth and ZigBee)

units.title: Mobile Ad-hoc networks
units.text: Mobile Ad-hoc networks: Characteristics and applications; Coverage and connectivity problems; Routing in MANETs. Wireless sensor networks: Concepts, basic architecture, design objectives and applications; Sensing and communication range; Coverage and connectivity; Sensor placement; Data relaying and aggregation; Energy consumption; Clustering of sensors; Energy efficient Routing (LEACH). Cognitive radio networks: Fixed and dynamic spectrum access; Direct and indirect spectrum sensing; Spectrum sharing; Interoperability and co-existence issues; Applications of cognitive radio networks.

units.title: D2D communications in 5G cellular networks

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
objectives: This course will help students learn to evaluate and apply design principles and human factors to apparel, housing and residential technologies and other consumer products. Exploring the use and design of products through history, in different cultures, and by diverse users adds to the knowledge base for all consumers. This course is to sensitize the students about the Design domain and help them collaborate with designers in their professional practice.

outcomes.text: Identify and discuss design principles and elements and their application to consumer products for diverse users, such as apparel, housing and residential technologies
Explain the historical and cultural context of design and consumer products through pre- industrial and industrial periods and modern era
Apply interpretive strategies or methodologies in design
Discuss the design process and the importance of diverse user needs in the creation of consumer products

units.title: Introduction to Design
units.text: Introduction to Design Idea of Design, Understanding its landscape, Design VS Art , Design VS Engineering, Definitions, Design and its relevance to the Data Sciences, Brief History of Design, Cultural Contexts of Design, Users & User Centric Design, Position of Design across Knowledge Domains

units.title: Design Process
units.text: Design Process Introduction, iterative nature of Design, Design Methodology, Emergence of Design Thinking, Design as a Creative Process, Prototyping as a testing and validation process.

units.title: Elements of Design
units.text: Elements of Design Line, Shape, Pattern and Texture, illusion of space, illusion of motion, Value, Colour Consumer Products

units.title: Principles of Design
units.text: Principles of Design Emphasis, Balance, Contrast, Repetition, Proportion, Movement, White space, Unity

units.title: Ergonomics & Human Factors
units.text: Ergonomics & Human Factors Introduction, Idea of Fit, Anthropometry, Affordances, Gestalt, usability, Introduction to Visual Semiotics.

units.title: Design of Consumer Products
units.text: Design of Consumer Products Introduction, Art of Making things - History of Products, Product Basics –Aesthetics, Ergonomics and Function (Form, Fit and Function), Types of Products, Typical and Atypical Products, Effect of Digitization on Products, Design of Interfaces, Product Architecture.

units.title: Design Management
units.text: Design Management Design as a Multidisciplinary collaborative Activity, Digital Tools, Design Brief, Design Scope, Design protection, Design Ethics, Good Principles of Design, Design Maturity Models

Waldemar Karwowski, Marcelo M. Soares, Neville A. Stanton, Human Factors and Ergonomics in Consumer Product Design: Uses and Applications, CRC Press, 2011.
reference_books: 1. Product Design and Development, 7th Edition Paperback – Illustrated, by Karl T. Ulrich, Steven D. Eppinger, Maria C. Yang, McGraw Hill. 2. Donna Lynne Fullmer, Design Basics, Fairchild Books New York, 2010.
lab_work: 8 to 10 exercises comprising of observation/ demo / experiments / discussions (and a practicum where applicable) based on the syllabus.

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
objectives: To understand the amount of data needed today for business decision is increasing, which is Big Data. Mostly 60-75 percentage of time is spent on data gathering, cleaning and making these data process worthy for business decision. Hence, it is important for students to understand ETL (Extract, Transform, and Load) process. To give information about fundamental concepts of Data Warehousing like slowly changing dimensions, data granularity, data velocity, metadata etc.

outcomes.text: Obtain data from a variety of sources. Know the principles of tidy data and data sharing.
Understand and be able to apply the basic tools for data cleaning and manipulation.
Learn the basic concepts of data warehousing like metadata, SCD, ETL etc.

Dimensional Modelling, Fact tables, dimension tables, ER model, slowly changing dimensions, Cyclicity of data, Schemas

program: B Tech and MBA Tech (All branches)
objectives: This course develops students' skills in human-centered design, interdisciplinary teamwork, and problem-solving through structured project work. Students will engage in stakeholder analysis, prototyping, testing, and iterative refinement while integrating engineering principles, creativity, and sustainability. Emphasizing collaboration and ethical responsibility, the course prepares students for industry and community-driven challenges by enhancing their project management, communication, and critical thinking abilities.

outcomes.text: Critically evaluate complex, real-world challenges using systematic problem- solving approaches.
Lead and collaborate in interdisciplinary teams to develop scalable and impactful solutions.
Apply advanced design methodologies and emerging technologies to prototype and refine innovative solutions in research.
Integrate sustainability, ethics, and feasibility analysis into the design and implementation process.
Demonstrate professional communication through technical reports, presentations, and stakeholder engagement.

units.text: The course covers Problem Analysis, where students assess the problem context, constraints, stakeholders, and solution stage while conducting literature reviews and benchmarking existing solutions. In Design Thinking & Concept Development, they apply the phases of Design Thinking—Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test—to develop and refine innovative solutions. Prototyping & Testing involves transforming ideas into practical prototypes, conducting experiments, usability testing, and iterative refinements. Through Project Management & Documentation, students assign roles, track progress, and maintain structured records. Communication & Review focuses on preparing presentations, conducting design reviews, and incorporating feedback. Finally, Reflection & Improvement allows students to analyze challenges, enhance their skills, and document key learnings.

lab_work: The Laboratory work comprises various activities performed by the project teams for formulation, solution implementation and modification. Each team needs to submit the following documents: • Problem Statement Document • Project Development Report • Mid Semester Project Report • Research Paper / Conference Paper • Final Report

program: B Tech / MBA Tech [EXTC/ Information Technology/ Computer Engineering/ CSBS/ CSE(DS) 311 (VT)] BTI (EXTC / Computer Engineering / Information Technology)
objectives: This course introduces concepts, methodologies and performance metrics for still image and motion picture processing. It also helps to develop a foundation for further study and research in the signal processing domain.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamentals of digital images, including distance measures, and file formats.
Apply image enhancement techniques such as point processing, spatial filtering, and histogram equalization for image improvement and image transforms for analyzing and compressing images.
Analyze morphological image processing techniques and edge detection methods for feature extraction.
Compare different image segmentation methods, including thresholding, region-based segmentation, and the Otsu method.
Explain video representation concepts and motion estimation techniques used in digital video compression.

units.title: Image fundamentals
units.text: Image fundamentals Representation of digital image, image as a matrix, image as a function, basics of colour image, spatial and gray level resolution, distance measures-Euclidean distance and m path, image file formats (TIFF, PNG, JPEG).

units.title: Image enhancement
units.text: Image enhancement Point processing techniques Linear- digital negative, Piecewise linear-contrast stretching, thresholding, intensity level slicing, Nonlinear- log transformation, power law transformation, Neighborhood processing techniques-smoothing spatial filters, sharpening spatial filters, median filters, Gaussian filtering. Histogram processing-histogram equalization. Image in Frequency domain: Fourier spectrum, Fourier analysis, filtering in frequency domain

units.title: Image transforms

units.title: Morphological image processing

units.title: Edge Detection

units.title: Image segmentation
units.text: Image segmentation Basic relationships between pixels, Component labeling (4, 8 and m connectivity) Segmentation using thresholding, Bayesian classification of foreground and background pixels, expectation- maximization theorem for binarization, Otsu method, region-based segmentation- region growing, region splitting and merging.

units.title: Colour Image Processing
units.text: Colour Image Processing Colour fundamentals and colour models (RGB, CMY, CMYK, HSI, YUV, HSV), model transformation, colour slicing, histogram processing of colour images.

units.title: Fundamentals of digital video and its compression
units.text: Fundamentals of digital video and its compression Video representation- temporal correlation, video frame classifications, I, P and B frames, Fundamentals of motion estimation, motion estimation algorithms- exhaustive search block matching, 2D-log search method and 3 step search method.

objectives: To develop an understanding of essential database concepts. To understand different issues involved in the design and implementation of a database systems. To understand and use database query languages to access and manage a database. To design and build a simple database system with modeling, designing and implementation To understand the need of data analytics and advanced database systems like data warehouse and data mining

outcomes.text: Describe the terminology, features and basic concepts of database systems
Formulate queries using structured query language and relational algebra
Design a model expressed in the form of an entity relationship diagram and transform it into a relational model
Demonstrate an understanding of normalization theory, transactions and need for data analytics and advanced database models

units.text: Introduction to Database Management Systems Role and advantages of the DBMS, Types of Databases, Importance of database design, Evolution of file system, Problems with file system, Database System environment, DBMS functions, Data models, importance of data models, types of data models, Data abstraction (Book : “Database System Design, Implementation, and Management”, Carlos Coronel, Steven Morris, Peter Bob)

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
prerequisites: Software Engineering (MCNB02003), Object Oriented Software Engineering (MCNB03004)
objectives: The objective of this course is to provide an understanding of the management issues and processes during the software development project. It provides a holistic view of the different aspects of the development process. Students will become conversant with various tools & techniques used in project management in modern industrial environment.

outcomes.text: Explain basic concepts of project planning, management and evaluation.
Demonstrate the use of software effort estimation and activity plan in a given project.
Discuss resource allocation and risk management in software projects.
Describe project tracking, project management and software quality processes.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Software development as a project, Stakeholders in software project, process, resources, quality and cost. Objective issues and problems relating to software projects.

units.title: Project Planning and Project Evaluation
units.text: Project Planning and Project Evaluation Steps in project planning, Defining scope and objective, project Phases and Project Lifecycle, work breakdown structure, GANTT Chart, Developing Project Charter, Project Management plan, Execute plans, Social-Economic Environmental influences. Evaluation: Strategic assessment, Technical assessment, Cost-benefit analysis, Cash flow forecasting, Breakeven analysis, Risk Evaluation.

units.title: Project Management Process
units.text: Project Management Process Project processes, Process groups, Process Interaction, Customising process interaction, Mapping of project Management processes

units.title: Selection of Appropriate Project Approach
units.text: Selection of Appropriate Project Approach Choosing development technology and methodology, Various Process models.

units.title: Software Effort Estimation
units.text: Software Effort Estimation Problems in software estimation, effort estimation techniques, expert judgment, Estimation by analogy, top-down and bottom-up estimation, function point analysis, object points, COCOMO model.

units.title: Activity planning
units.text: Activity planning Network planning model, Activity-on-arrow network, PERT, precedence network, forward pass and backward pass, critical path, slack and float, Product Data Management (PDM)

units.title: Risk Management and Resource Allocation
units.text: Risk Management and Resource Allocation The nature of risk, Types of risk, Managing risk, Hazard identification, Hazard analysis, Quantitative and Qualitative Risk Analysis, Risk planning and control, Evaluating risks to the schedule. The nature of resources, Identifying resource requirements, Scheduling resources, Creating critical paths, Resource Loading and Resource Levelling, Counting the cost, Being specific, publishing the resource, Cost schedules, The scheduling sequence.

units.title: Project Tracking and Control
units.text: Project Tracking and Control Measurement of physical and financial progress, earned value analysis, Status reports, Milestone reports and change control.

units.title: Managing contracts, Managing people and organizing teams
units.text: Managing contracts, Managing people and organizing teams Types of contract, Stages in contract placement, Typical terms of a contract, Contract management, Acceptance, Contract closeout. Organizational behavior, Recruitment and placement, motivation. Group behavior, individual and group decision making, Staff acquisition and Team Development, Leadership and forms of organizational structures.

units.title: Software quality
units.text: Software quality Planning for quality, product verses process quality management, procedural and quantitative approaches, Quality Assurance, Quality Control, defect analysis and prevention, quality standards: ISO 9000, Capability Maturity model, quality audit.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
prerequisites: Discrete Mathematics (BTCS01001), Data Structures and Algorithms (BTCS02003)
objectives: To introduce fundamentals of automata theory, regular sets and grammars, To design automata for different types of languages.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamentals of Automata theory and regular sets
Design regular language modelling in Finite Automata and non-deterministic finite automata
Describe context free and context sensitive languages and design automata for these languages
Explain undecidability and complexity of problems.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Alphabet, languages and grammars, productions and derivation, Chomsky hierarchy of languages

units.title: Regular languages and finite automata
units.text: Regular languages and finite automata Regular expressions and languages, deterministic finite automata (DFA) and equivalence with regular expressions, nondeterministic finite automata (NFA) and equivalence with DFA, regular grammars and equivalence with finite automata, properties of regular languages, Kleene’s theorem, pumping lemma for regular languages, Myhill-Nerode theorem and its uses, minimization of finite automata.

units.title: Context-free languages and pushdown automata
units.text: Context-free languages and pushdown automata Context-free grammars (CFG) and languages (CFL), Chomsky and Greibach normal forms, nondeterministic pushdown automata (PDA) and equivalence with CFG, parse trees, ambiguity in CFG, pumping lemma for context-free languages, deterministic pushdown automata, closure properties of CFLs.

units.title: Context-sensitive languages
units.text: Context-sensitive languages Context-sensitive grammars (CSG) and languages, linear bounded automata and equivalence with CSG.

units.title: Turing machines
units.text: Turing machines The basic model for Turing machines (TM), Turing recognizable (recursively enumerable) and Turing-decidable (recursive) languages and their closure properties, variants of Turing machines, nondeterministic TMs and equivalence with deterministic TMs, unrestricted grammars and equivalence with Turing machines, TMs as enumerators.

units.title: Undecidability
units.text: Undecidability Church-Turing thesis, universal Turing machine, the universal and diagonalization languages, reduction between languages and Rice s theorem, undecidable problems about languages.

units.title: Basic Introduction to Complexity
units.text: Basic Introduction to Complexity Introductory ideas on Time complexity of deterministic and nondeterministic Turing machines, P and NP, NP- completeness, Cook’s Theorem, other NP -Complete problems.

objectives: To impart knowledge of the current theories, methods and techniques in the field of Artificial Intelligence. To create ability to analyze, design and develop Al-systems.

outcomes.text: Formulate Artificial Intelligent problem and identify agents and environments.
Apply informed and uninformed searching strategies.
Apply knowledge representation schemes for expert systems and game playing.
Implement supervised and unsupervised learning approaches to solve problems in AI domain

units.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
units.text: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Definitions of AI, Broad overview of application areas of AI (like vision, Natural language processing, Robotics etc.) Concept of Modelling, Inference and Learning. Introduction to Machine learning and Deep learning as a subset of AI. Intelligent agents, concept of rationality, structure of agents, Environment, Properties of task environment. Real world Examples of agents and environments.

units.title: Solving problems by Searching
units.text: Solving problems by Searching Problem solving agents, well define problems and solutions, formulating problems. What is searching? problem as a state space search, Informed search and uninformed search. Uninformed Search Breadth first search, Depth first search, Uniform cost search Informed Search Informed search strategies, Greedy Best first Search, A* search, Hill climbing, problem with hill climbing such as Local Maxima, Plateau, Ridge, Genetic Algorithm. Adversarial Search Introduction to Domain of a game, optimal decisions in games, minimax algorithm, Alpha-beta pruning.

units.title: Knowledge Representation
units.text: Knowledge Representation Prepositional Logic Syntax, Semantics Knowledge base and inference. Predicate logic Facts, Representation of fact, mapping between facts and representation, properties and issues of knowledge representation system, Instance relationship, Isa, gt & Lt predicate. Unification algorithm, resolution in predicate and prepositional logic.

units.title: Rules
units.text: Rules Procedural versus Declarative knowledge, forward versus backward reasoning, forward & backward chaining rule system. Constraint satisfaction Problem (CSP) Constraint satisfaction problems, Backtracking search for CSPs, variables and value ordering, propagating information through constraints, Intelligent backtracking, Local search for CSP. Case study: Complete example on CSP.

units.title: Learning
units.text: Learning Forms of learning, Super-vised learning- decision tree classification, Unsupervised learning- K means clustering. Reinforcement learning- passive and active reinforcement learning

units.title: Expert system
units.text: Expert system Expert system: Definition, model, characteristic, architecture, development process, limitations, and knowledge representation schemes, Case study: JESS’s rule based engine with RETE algorithm.

units.title: Case study
units.text: Case study Complete application of AI as Natural language understanding and generation, Robotic Vision and Self driving car.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
objectives: 1. To provide the fundamental knowledge of Image processing and related algorithms involved in it.

outcomes.text: Outline the fundamentals of image processing
Compute and analyse effects of various image transformation techniques in spatial and frequency domains
Analyse images using image segmentation and morphological operations
Compress the images using basic transforms, wavelets

units.title: Digital Image Processing Systems
units.text: Digital Image Processing Systems Introduction, Fundamental steps of image processing, Display Image Sampling and quantization, Basic relationships between pixels. Types of images: Monochrome, grey, colour.

units.title: Image Enhancement in the Spatial domain
units.text: Image Enhancement in the Spatial domain Grey level transformations, Histogram processing, Arithmetic and logic operations, Spatial filtering: Introduction, Smoothing and sharpening filters.

units.title: Image Segmentation, Representation and Description
units.text: Image Segmentation, Representation and Description Detection of discontinuities, Edge linking and Boundary detection, Thresholding, Region based segmentation, Representation – Chain Codes, polynomial approximations, Signatures, Boundary Descriptors, Regional Descriptors

units.title: Morphological Image Processing
units.text: Morphological Image Processing Introduction, Dilation, Erosion, Opening, closing, Hit –or-Miss transformation, Morphological algorithm operations on binary images and Morphological algorithm operations on gray-scale images.

units.title: Image Transforms
units.text: Image Transforms Introduction to Fourier transform, Walsh transform, Hadamard transform, Discrete Sine transform, Discrete cosine transform,. Frequency domain filters: Smoothing and Sharpening filters,

units.title: Wavelets and Multiresolution Processing
units.text: Wavelets and Multiresolution Processing STFT, need of wavelets, Image pyramids, Filter Banks, Haar transform, Application of wavelets.

units.title: Image Data Compression
units.text: Image Data Compression Fundamentals, Redundancies: Coding, Interpixel, Pysycho-visual, fidelity criteria, Image compression models, Error free compression, Lossy compression methods.

text_books: 1. R.C Gonzalez and Richard Woods, Digital Image Processing, 7th Indian reprint, Pearson publication, 2012. 2. Anil K. Jain, Fundamental of Digital Image processing, PHI, 2015.
reference_books: 1. B. Chanda & D. Dutta Majumder, Digital Image Processing and Analysis, 2nd Edition, PHI, 2009

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
objectives: To provide the knowledge of computer networking and applications. To understand the data communication techniques and switching techniques. To understand various networking technologies. To understand the concept of inter-networking and other networking concepts (VoIP) and its trends.

outcomes.text: Understand the significance of networking and telecommunications
Understand the basics of data communication techniques and switching techniques
Distinguish the various networking technologies
Analyze the inter-networking concepts and multimedia communication and its trends

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Growth of computer networking, Five key aspects of networking, Public and Private network, Network Interoperability and standards, Protocol suites and layering model, Resource sharing, resource sharing to communication

units.title: Internet Applications
units.text: Internet Applications Introduction, Connection-oriented Communication, The Client-Server Model- Interaction, Characteristics, Server Programs and Server-Class Computers, Requests, Responses, And Direction Of Data Flow, Multiple Clients and Multiple Servers, Server Identification and Demultiplexing, Concurrent Servers, Circular Dependencies among Servers, Peer-To-Peer Interactions, Application-Layer Protocols, Representation And Transfer, Web Protocols, Document Representation With HTML, Uniform Resource Locators And Hyperlinks, Web Document Transfer With HTTP, Caching In Browsers, Browser Architecture

units.title: Data Communication Basics
units.text: Data Communication Basics Overview of Data Communications, Information Sources and Signals, Transmission Media - Guided and Unguided Transmission, Measuring Transmission Media, effect of noise, Reliability and Channel Coding The Three Main Sources of Transmission Errors, Effect of Transmission Errors on Data, Two Strategies for Handling Channel Errors, Block And convolutional Error Code, tradeoff, error correction, CRC Transmission Modes Taxonomy, timing, Simplex, full duplex and half duplex transmission, Modems, Multiplexing and Demultiplexing (Channelization) types and comparison, Access and Interconnection Technologies- Upstream and Downstream, Narrow band, broad band, cable modem, DSL, ADSL

units.title: Packet Switching and Network Technologies
units.text: Packet Switching and Network Technologies Local Area Networks: Packets, Frames, And Topologies – circuit and packet switching, standard for packet format, topologies, address types, frame, byte and bit stuffing, The IEEE MAC Sub-Layer- multiple access, controlled access protocols, Wired LAN Technology (Ethernet and 802.3)- ethernet frame format, 802.3 frame format, wiring, variants

units.title: Wireless Networking Technologies
units.text: Wireless Networking Technologies PAN, LAN, Wi-Fi, LAN architecture, format, Wireless Man and WiMaX, WAN, LAN Extensions - Fiber Modems, Repeaters, Bridges, and Switches, WAN Technologies

units.title: Internetworking
units.text: Internetworking Concepts, Architecture, and Protocols- Concepts, Internetworking, Internet architecture, virtual network, IP: Internet Addressing- Class of IP address, addressing, subnet and classless addressing, address mask, CIDR, Special IP address, Routers and IP addressing principle, Datagram Forwarding- connectionless, IP datagram, Header format, forwarding, Network prefix, IP encapsulation, MTU and datagram fragmentation, Reassembly, UDP: Datagram Transport Service – UDP, Message oriented interface, communication semantics, mode of interaction, delivery, datagram format, encapsulation

units.title: Other Networking Concepts
units.text: Other Networking Concepts Multimedia and IP telephony (VoIP)- Real time data transmission, data delivery, Jitter buffer, real time transport protocol, RTP encapsulation, IP telephony, Components of an IP telephone system, H.323, SIP, Telephone number mapping and routing, Trends in networking technologies and usage - Content Caching (Akamai), Web Load Balancers, Server Virtualization, Distributed Data Centers And Replication, Universal representation (XML), Social Networking, Mobility And Wireless Networking, Use Of Networking In Business, Sensors At Large And In The Home, Ad Hoc Networks

text_books: 1. Douglas E. Comer, Computer Networks and Internets with Applications, 5th Edition, Prentice Hall, 2015.
reference_books: 1. Comer, Douglas E, The Internet Book: Everything You Need to Know about Computer Networking and How the Internet Works, 5th Edition, United Kingdom: CRC Press, 2018.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
prerequisites: Basic Knowledge of Computer Network, Operating Systems and programming
objectives: To impart knowledge to Critically assess organisation's security and be able to apply managerial, technical, operational security controls to improve organisation's security.

outcomes.text: Identify and apply key elements of managerial and operational security practice
Analyse and evaluate a company of your choosing and compile a formal risk assessment of your analysis, findings, and suggest actions for the company to take through interpretation of your findings
Identify key elements of technical security and be able to explain how they function and how and where they may be usefully applied
Use technical security software and identify how and where it may be usefully applied

units.title: Introduction to Information Security
units.text: Introduction to Information Security Overview, definition, information security concepts, threats, vulnerabilities and security controls, attack (active and passive attacks) with examples, security design principles, methods of defenses, security policies and its types, legal and ethical aspect

units.title: Cryptography
units.text: Cryptography Cryptography basics, transposition and substitution ciphers, symmetric and asymmetric cryptographic algorithms (AES, Diffie Hellman, and RSA), stream and block ciphers, key management, digital signature, hash functions, Attacks on cryptosystems.

units.title: Program Security
units.text: Program Security Secure programs, Non malicious Program Errors, malicious software, database security, countermeasures.

units.title: User Authentication
units.text: User Authentication Authentication basics, factors of authentication, password based authentication, token based authentication, biometric authentication, remote user authentication, security issues

units.title: Access control
units.text: Access control Access control principles, discretionary access control, mandatory access control, role based access control, identity, credential, and access management, trust frameworks

units.title: Security Technologies
units.text: Security Technologies Firewalls, types of Firewalls, Filtering Services, DMZ, Implementing policies (Default allow, Default Deny) on proxy, NAT, Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems, types of IDPS, Security information and event management (SIEM)

units.title: Risk Management
units.text: Risk Management Overview of risk management, risk identification and assessment, risk control strategies, selecting risk control strategy, continuity strategies (Business continuity planning, Incident response planning, Disaster Recovery planning)

text_books: Primary TextBook 1. William Stallings and Lawrie Brown, Computer Security Principles and Practice, 4th Edition, Pearson Education, 2018.
reference_books: 1. C. Pfleeger, S. L. Pfleeger and J. Margulies, Security in Computing, 5th Edition, Pearson Education, 2018. 2. M. Whitman and H. Mattford, Principles of Information Security with MindTap, 6th Edition, Cengage, 2018. 3. Daniel Lachance and Glen E. Clarke, CompTIA Security+ Certification Practice Exams, 4th Edition (Exam SY0-601), McGraw-Hill, 2021.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
prerequisites: Programming for Problem Solving, Data structures
objectives: To develop an understanding of essential database concepts. To understand different issues involved in the design and implementation of a database systems. To understand and use database query languages to access and manage a database. To design and build a simple database system with modeling, designing and implementation To understand the need of data analytics and advanced database systems like data warehouse and data mining

outcomes.text: Describe the terminology, features and basic concepts of database systems
Formulate queries using structured query language and relational algebra
Design a model expressed in the form of an entity relationship diagram and transform it into a relational model
Demonstrate an understanding of normalization theory, transactions and need for data analytics and advanced database models

units.title: Introduction to Database Management Systems
units.text: Introduction to Database Management Systems Role and advantages of the DBMS, Types of Databases, Importance of database design, Evolution of file system, Problems with file system, Database System environment, DBMS functions, Data models, importance of data models, types of data models, Data abstraction (Book : “Database System Design, Implementation, and Management”, Carlos Coronel, Steven Morris, Peter Bob)

units.title: Introduction to Relational Model
units.text: Introduction to Relational Model Structure of relational databases- relation, attribute, tuple, domain, Codd’s rules, Database schema, Keys, schema diagrams, Database integrity constraints : Domain integrity, Entity integrity, Referential integrity, Relational query languages, Introduction to Relational Algebra, Basic Relational Algebra Operations, Cartesian Product, Joins, Aggregate functions, Modification of the databases

units.title: Introduction to SQL
units.text: Introduction to SQL Data Definition Commands, Data Definition Commands, Data Manipulation Commands, Select Queries, Additional Data Definition Commands, Additional Select Query Keywords (Book : “Database System Design, Implementation, and Management”, Carlos Coronel, Steven Morris, Peter Bob)

units.title: Advanced SQL
units.text: Advanced SQL Set operators, Join operators, Views, Sub-queries (Book : “Database System Design, Implementation, and Management”, Carlos Coronel, Steven Morris, Peter Bob)

units.title: Database Design Using the ER Model
units.text: Database Design Using the ER Model Overview of the design process, Components of the ER Model, Concepts of ER model : Mapping Cardinalities, Primary Key, Participation constraints, Weak entity sets, Generalization, specialization, Converting ER model to Relational Model, ER model Design issues

units.title: Relational Database Design
units.text: Relational Database Design Features of Good Relational Designs, Problems with bad design, Decomposition using concept of functional dependencies, Introduction to process of normalization and de-normalization. Normal forms – 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, De- normalization

units.title: Indexing
units.text: Indexing Introduction to indexes, Need of index in database systems, Types of indexes, SQL implementation of index

units.title: Transactions
units.text: Transactions What is transactions? Properties of transaction, Transaction states, Issues with concurrent executions, Schedules, Serializability –Conflict and View

units.title: Data Warehousing and Data Mining
units.text: Data Warehousing and Data Mining The need for data analysis, Decision support data, Introduction to Data Warehouse and Data Mining, Introduction to Online Analytical Processing, SQL extensions for OLAP- Rollup and Cube Operators (Book : “Database System Design, Implementation, and Management”, Carlos Coronel, Steven Morris, Peter Bob)

text_books: 1. Carlos Coronel and Steven Morris, Database Systems: Design, Implementation and Management, 13th Edition, Cengage Learning 2019 2. Avi Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth, S. Sudarshan, Database System Concepts, 7th Edition, Mc-Graw Hill, March 2019.
reference_books: 1. Elmasri, Ramez, and Shamakant B. Navathe, Fundamentals of Database System, 7th Edition, Pearson Education Limited, 2017 2. Gehrke, Johannes and Raghu Ramakrishnan, Database Management Systems, 3rd Edition, Mc- Graw Hill, 2014 3. S. K. Singh, Database Systems Concepts, Design and Applications, , 2nd Edition, Pearson Publication2009 4. Coronel, Carlos, Steven Morris, and Peter Rob, Database Systems: design, implementation and Management, 9th Edition, Cengage Learning, 2009.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
prerequisites: Software Engineering (MCNB02003), Object Oriented Software Engineering (MCNB03004)
objectives: The objective of this course is to provide an understanding of the management issues and processes during the software development project. It provides a holistic view of the different aspects of the development process. Students will become conversant with various tools & techniques used in project management in modern industrial environment.

outcomes.text: Explain basic concepts of project planning, management and evaluation.
Demonstrate the use of software effort estimation and activity plan in a given project.
Discuss resource allocation and risk management in software projects.
Describe project tracking, project management and software quality processes.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Software development as a project, Stakeholders in software project, process, resources, quality and cost. Objective issues and problems relating to software projects.

units.title: Project Planning and Project Evaluation
units.text: Project Planning and Project Evaluation Steps in project planning, Defining scope and objective, project Phases and Project Lifecycle, work breakdown structure, GANTT Chart, Developing Project Charter, Project Management plan, Execute plans, Social-Economic Environmental influences. Evaluation: Strategic assessment, Technical assessment, Cost-benefit analysis, Cash flow forecasting, Breakeven analysis, Risk Evaluation.

units.title: Project Management Process
units.text: Project Management Process Project processes, Process groups, Process Interaction, Customising process interaction, Mapping of project Management processes

units.title: Selection of Appropriate Project Approach
units.text: Selection of Appropriate Project Approach Choosing development technology and methodology, Various Process models.

units.title: Software Effort Estimation
units.text: Software Effort Estimation Problems in software estimation, effort estimation techniques, expert judgment, Estimation by analogy, top-down and bottom-up estimation, function point analysis, object points, COCOMO model.

units.title: Activity planning
units.text: Activity planning Network planning model, Activity-on-arrow network, PERT, precedence network, forward pass and backward pass, critical path, slack and float, Product Data Management (PDM)

units.title: Risk Management and Resource Allocation
units.text: Risk Management and Resource Allocation The nature of risk, Types of risk, Managing risk, Hazard identification, Hazard analysis, Quantitative and Qualitative Risk Analysis, Risk planning and control, Evaluating risks to the schedule. The nature of resources, Identifying resource requirements, Scheduling resources, Creating critical paths, Resource Loading and Resource Levelling, Counting the cost, Being specific, publishing the resource, Cost schedules, The scheduling sequence.

units.title: Project Tracking and Control
units.text: Project Tracking and Control Measurement of physical and financial progress, earned value analysis, Status reports, Milestone reports and change control.

units.title: Managing contracts, Managing people and organizing teams
units.text: Managing contracts, Managing people and organizing teams Types of contract, Stages in contract placement, Typical terms of a contract, Contract management, Acceptance, Contract closeout. Organizational behavior, Recruitment and placement, motivation. Group behavior, individual and group decision making, Staff acquisition and Team Development, Leadership and forms of organizational structures.

units.title: Software quality
units.text: Software quality Planning for quality, product verses process quality management, procedural and quantitative approaches, Quality Assurance, Quality Control, defect analysis and prevention, quality standards: ISO 9000, Capability Maturity model, quality audit.

text_books: 1. Bob Hughes and Mike Cotterell, Software Project Management, 5th edition, McGraw-Hall, 2011. 2. Milton D. Rosenau, Jr. & Gregory D. Githers, Successful Project Management, 4th Edition, Wiley India, 2006 3. A Guide to Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK®) Guide, 6th Edition,2017.
reference_books: 1. Pankaj Jalote, Software Project Management in Practice, 1st Edition, Pearson Education, 2005. 2. Robert K. Wysocki, Effective Software Project Management, 7th Edition , Frommer’s, 2014. 3. Walker Royce, Software Project Management- A Unified, Framework, Addison-Wesley, 1998. 4. Kathy Schwalbe, Project Management in IT, 7th Edition, Cengage Learning, 2012 5. Clements, Gido, Effective Project Management, 5th Edition, Cengage Learning, 2011 6. Jack R. Meredith, Samuel J Mantel Jr., Project Management, 7th Edition, Wiley, 2009.

program: B. Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 311 (VT)
prerequisites: Discrete Mathematics (BTCS01001), Data Structures and Algorithms (BTCS02003)
objectives: To introduce fundamentals of automata theory, regular sets and grammars, To design automata for different types of languages.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamentals of Automata theory and regular sets
Design regular language modelling in Finite Automata and non-deterministic finite automata
Describe context free and context sensitive languages and design automata for these languages
Explain undecidability and complexity of problems.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Alphabet, languages and grammars, productions and derivation, Chomsky hierarchy of languages

units.title: Regular languages and finite automata
units.text: Regular languages and finite automata Regular expressions and languages, deterministic finite automata (DFA) and equivalence with regular expressions, nondeterministic finite automata (NFA) and equivalence with DFA, regular grammars and equivalence with finite automata, properties of regular languages, Kleene’s theorem, pumping lemma for regular languages, Myhill-Nerode theorem and its uses, minimization of finite automata.

units.title: Context-free languages and pushdown automata
units.text: Context-free languages and pushdown automata Context-free grammars (CFG) and languages (CFL), Chomsky and Greibach normal forms, nondeterministic pushdown automata (PDA) and equivalence with CFG, parse trees, ambiguity in CFG, pumping lemma for context-free languages, deterministic pushdown automata, closure properties of CFLs.

units.title: Context-sensitive languages
units.text: Context-sensitive languages Context-sensitive grammars (CSG) and languages, linear bounded automata and equivalence with CSG.

units.title: Turing machines
units.text: Turing machines The basic model for Turing machines (TM), Turing recognizable (recursively enumerable) and Turing-decidable (recursive) languages and their closure properties, variants of Turing machines, nondeterministic TMs and equivalence with deterministic TMs, unrestricted grammars and equivalence with Turing machines, TMs as enumerators.

units.title: Undecidability
units.text: Undecidability Church-Turing thesis, universal Turing machine, the universal and diagonalization languages, reduction between languages and Rice s theorem, undecidable problems about languages.

units.title: Basic Introduction to Complexity
units.text: Basic Introduction to Complexity Introductory ideas on Time complexity of deterministic and nondeterministic Turing machines, P and NP, NP- completeness, Cook’s Theorem, other NP -Complete problems.

text_books: 1. John E. Hopcroft, Rajeev Motwani and Jeffrey D. Ullman., Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation, 3rd Edition , Pearson Education2008.
reference_books: 1. Harry R. Lewis and Christos H. Papadimitriou, Elements of the Theory of Computation, 2nd Edition, Pearson Education, 2015 2. Dexter C. Kozen , Automata and Computability, 3rd Edition , Springer Verlag , 1999 3. Michael Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd Edition, Cengage Learning 2012 4. John Martin, Introduction to Languages and the Theory of Computation, 3rd Edition, ,Tata Mac Graw Hill, 2007. 5. M. R. Garey and D. S. Johnson, Computers and Intractability: A Guide to the Theory of NP Completeness, W.H. freeman and Company, 1st Edition, 1979

program: B. Tech CSE- Cybersecurity
prerequisites: Basic Knowledge of Computer Network, Operating Systems and programming
objectives: This course is an introduction to the field of Cybersecurity. This course introduces various aspects of cybersecurity to the students. Students will learn about various security threats and countermeasures.

outcomes.text: Analyze various cybersecurity threats and countermeasures
Explain various security technologies and mechanisms
Describe various professional, ethical and legal issues related to cybersecurity

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Basic Components of Cybersecurity, Characteristics of Information, vulnerabilities, threats , Attacks and controls ,goals of security, Mitre ATT&CK framework, Cyber Kill Chain, Security System development life cycle, cybercrimes and criminals, professional, legal and ethical issues.

units.title: Design Principles
units.text: Design Principles Various Security threats and attacks, method of defence, Design Principles, Security policies, types of security policies, Case Study

units.title: Program Security
units.text: Program Security Secure programs, Non malicious Program Errors, Viruses and other malicious code, countermeasures.

units.title: OS Security
units.text: OS Security Security Features of OS, security in the design of OS, Rootkit

units.title: Database Security
units.text: Database Security Security requirements for databases, reliability and integrity, database disclosure

units.title: Identity and access management(IAM)
units.text: Identity and access management(IAM) Authentication basics, Passwords, authentication tokens, certificate based and biometric authentication, Kerberos, SSO approaches, Multi- Factor Authentication, attacks on authentication schemes, Access 702IT0C013 702IT0C013 control principles, DAC, MAC, and Role based Access Control, Access control models, identity and access provisioning lifecycle

units.title: Security Technologies
units.text: Security Technologies Firewalls, Kinds of Firewalls, Filtering Services, DMZ, Implementing policies (Default allow, Default Deny) on proxy, NAT, Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems, types of IDPS, Virtual Private Network, SSH

program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: We live in a technology enabled world where data is collected and process as we interact with any technology product or service. This data is used by the companies to predict our tastes, our habits, or future possible health problems. This use of data has created a big privacy threat. Various governments have developed stringent privacy laws like GDPR to protect the privacy of their citizens. Effective information privacy is very difficult. Globally organizations are approaching privacy problem based on two concepts: Privacy by design and privacy engineering. In this course students will be exposed to both the concepts.

outcomes.text: Identify data privacy threats and suggest their countermeasures
Implement various privacy models
Design privacy program for an organization

program: B. Tech Data Science (Business Analytics)
objectives: • Learn about the most effective machine learning techniques, and gain practice implementing them and getting them to work. • Understand the theoretical underpinnings of learning and gaining the practical know-how needed to quickly and powerfully apply these techniques to new problems. • Develop a broad vision to machine learning, datamining, and statistical pattern recognition. • Implement (i) Supervised learning (parametric/non-parametric algorithms, support vector machines, kernels, neural networks). (iii) Best practices in machine learning (bias/variance theory; innovation process in machine learning and AI). • Analyze numerous case studies and applications and know how to apply learning algorithms to building smart robots (perception, control), text understanding (web search, anti-spam), computer vision, medical informatics, audio, database mining, and other areas.

program: B. Tech Data Science (Business Analytics)
objectives:  Data is rich and abundant. However, every data wrangler has come across most of the time this data, which is very noisy in nature. Processing noisy signals and removing unwanted part from an image has been a huge concern over the last few decades. Signal and image processing techniques developed today are very robust and effective models. The objective is to port some processing techniques from the audio and signal field and use them to process sensor data.  To provide a few filter processing techniques and algorithms that can help eliminate the data signal noise and help user get the desired image.  To provide insights on fundamentals of image processing.

outcomes.text: Identify and perform operations on discrete and continuous data
Apply algorithm and remove the unwanted noise in the data signals using filtering and would be able to design efficiently working filter bands for defined intervals
Apply the concepts of Convolution and Sampling for real time applications
Learn various processes that an image goes through during its mechanism like segmentation and enhancement

units.text: Data Communication Fundamentals, Data and signals, A simplified model of a data communication system, Defining Data and its types, Electrical representation of data, its characteristics, domain and spectrum concept, Distinguish between data and signal, basic parameters that are required for characterizing the signal, Various operations on Data and its graphical representation, folding, scaling, shifting operations on discrete data points and continuous data signals.

Data structure classification, Disjunct data, Continual data, plotting of various types convolution on different data types, energy of a given signal, periodic and non-periodic signals, Identifying the types of Input - output correlation and identifying the systems, convolution integral, circular convolution, single and double side representations.

units.title: Discrete Fourier Transform of signal, Fast Fourier Transform, Butterfly
units.text: Discrete Fourier Transform of signal, Fast Fourier Transform, Butterfly Diagram, Fourier series for continuous data, Fourier Transforms and its properties, graphical exponential data points, one and two sided, time domain and frequency domain representations, increasing amplitude value of function by multiplying it with a constant.

Image Fundamentals, Vector Space Image Representation, Image probability Density Models, initial and final values from given equations, designing frequency response as flat as possible in the pass band for a maximally flat, Butterworth filter, various windowing methods, overlap add, overlap save method.

Sampling, Standardization of data, manipulation of discrete data sequences, discrete models solved with difference equations, state transition matrix for data science problems, noisy data and impulse response estimation, step response, transfer function calculations, constructing State variable equations from the given order difference equation of a system, difference equations with zero input, state and total response

Elements of Digital Image processing system, Basic relationship between pixels, spatial and tonal resolution, Image Enhancement, Performing Zooming on Image by replication and interpolation, Image segmentation, Point detection, Line detection, Edge detection, Find input image using inverse Hadamard, Global descriptor attributes based image retrieval

program: B. Tech Data Science (Business Analytics)
objectives:  To provide an understanding of various Mathematical Concepts such as Vector Integration, Matrices, Analytic functions and Mapping which forms basics for data science to solve engineering problems.  Impart knowledge of Laplace Transform and generalization for the fundamental theorem of calculus like Greens, Stokes and Gauss Diversion.

outcomes.text: Solve problems using Matrices, Laplace and apply it to engineering problems.

Solve and Apply applications of Greens Theorems to find relationship between a line integral around a simple closed curve C and a double integral over the plane region D bounded by C in real life engineering problems.

units.text: Analytic Function, Analytic Function Equations, Harmonic functions, Relation between Analytic and Harmonic functions, Milne Thompson method, function u given with another function v not given and derive function of w, Either addition or subtraction of two variables u and v given and derive function of w, Cauchy Reiman equations in Cartesian and polar coordinates, Mapping – Determining the image in the plane, bilinear transformation and fixed points of Bilinear transformations, cross ratio formula.

Integration solution for Equation along the path of unit circle, parabola, Cauchy Integral Theorem, Cauchy Integral Formula, Simple pole, Multiple Pole, Repeated Poles, Function of Single random variable, Taylors and Laurentz Series, Residues, Contour integration.

Vector Integration – Line Integral, Boundary over square, over straight line segments joining points, moving particle along circle, ellipse, conservative and irrational field, Scalar Potentials, Multivariable calculus Greens Theorem, Stokes Theorem, Gauss Diversion Theorem.

Matrices – Eigen values, Eigen vectors, Quadratic form over real field, Reduction of Quadratic form to a diagonal canonical form, Rank, Index and non-Derogatory Matrices, Cayley-Hamilton theorem (without proof), similar Matrices, Linear dependence and Independence using matrix equations, orthogonally similar Matrices, Single Vector Decomposition.

Laplace Transform – Introduction, Derivatives and Integrals, Definition, Linearity property, Laplace transform of standard functions, first shifting theorem, second shifting theorem, Effect of multiplication by t, Effect of division by t, Laplace Transform of Derivatives and Integrals, Inverse Laplace Transforms, Laplace Transform of special functions, Application of Laplace.

Solve and Apply applications of Greens Theorems to find relationship between a line integral around a simple closed curve C and a double integral over the plane region D bounded by C in real life engineering problems.

units.text: Analytic Function, Analytic Function Equations, Harmonic functions, Relation between Analytic and Harmonic functions, Milne Thompson method, function u given with another function v not given and derive function of w, Either addition or subtraction of two variables u and v given and derive function of w, Cauchy Reiman equations in Cartesian and polar coordinates, Mapping – Determining the image in the plane, bilinear transformation and fixed points of Bilinear transformations, cross ratio formula.

Integration solution for Equation along the path of unit circle, parabola, Cauchy Integral Theorem, Cauchy Integral Formula, Simple pole, Multiple Pole, Repeated Poles, Function of Single random variable, Taylors and Laurentz Series, Residues, Contour integration.

Vector Integration – Line Integral, Boundary over square, over straight line segments joining points, moving particle along circle, ellipse, conservative and irrational field, Scalar Potentials, Multivariable calculus Greens Theorem, Stokes Theorem, Gauss Diversion Theorem.

Matrices – Eigen values, Eigen vectors, Quadratic form over real field, Reduction of Quadratic form to a diagonal canonical form, Rank, Index and Signature of quadratic form, Functions of square matrix, Derogatory and non-Derogatory Matrices, Cayley-Hamilton theorem (without proof), similar Matrices, Linear dependence and Independence using matrix equations, orthogonally similar Matrices, Single Vector Decomposition.

Laplace Transform – Introduction, Derivatives and Integrals, Definition, Linearity property, Laplace transform of standard functions, first shifting theorem, second shifting theorem, Effect of multiplication by t, Effect of division by t, Laplace Transform of Derivatives and Integrals, Inverse Laplace Transforms, Laplace Transform of special functions, Application of Laplace.

objectives: The aim of the course is to focus on the basic principles of machine learning and use the concepts for developing models. The course will emphasize on topics from matrix algebra, calculus, optimization, and probability theory those are having strong linkage with machine learning

outcomes.text: Recall and define key concepts of machine learning, including types of learning, model evaluation metrics, and essential terminology.
Explain the fundamental differences between supervised vs. unsupervised learning, classification vs. regression, and concepts like bias-variance.
Apply foundational machine learning techniques to both supervised and unsupervised learning problems, including regression, classification, and dimensionality reduction.
Assess and interpret model performance using key evaluation metrics, understand the bias-variance trade-off, and distinguish quality of fit in various settings.

Understand and apply fundamental concepts of optimization, including gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, gradient descent, and constrained optimization, with applications to training neural networks and building feedforward architectures. (L2-Understanding and L3- Applying)

Perform and interpret dimensionality reduction techniques, such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Fisher Discriminant Analysis, and apply support vector machines for classification with kernel methods and geometric interpretations.

objectives: This course provides an introduction to time series analysis. It will educate students on how to choose an appropriate forecasting method in a particular environment and then apply it using necessary computations. It aims to equip students with various forecasting techniques and knowledge on modern statistical methods for analyzing time series data. It will also provide directions to Improve forecasting using better statistical models based on statistical analysis

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental components of time series data, such as trend, seasonality, and autocorrelation, and visualize them using various plotting techniques.
Apply time series regression models, exponential smoothing, ARMA, ARIMA, and SARIMA models to forecast univariate and seasonal data.
Analyze stationary and non-stationary time series processes using ACF, PACF, unit root tests, and diagnostics to identify appropriate forecasting models.
Evaluate forecasting performance of hierarchical and grouped time series models using reconciliation methods and compare with alternative approaches.
Design advanced forecasting solutions using complex seasonality, the Prophet model, VARs, bootstrapping, and bagging on real-world datasets using statistical software.

objectives: To educate students on building cloud infrastructure based on a cloud computing reference model. outcomes.text: Describe the foundational concepts of computer networks and cloud computing, including network architectures, models, protocols, and cloud service/deployment models.

prerequisites: Statistical Structures in Data and Inference
objectives: The aim of the course is to focus on the basic principles of machine learning and use the concepts for developing models. The course will emphasize on topics from matrix algebra, calculus, optimization, and probability theory those are having strong linkage with machine learning

outcomes.text: Recall and define key concepts of machine learning, including types of learning, model evaluation metrics, and essential terminology.
Explain the fundamental differences between supervised vs. unsupervised learning, classification vs. regression, and concepts like bias-variance.
Apply foundational machine learning techniques to both supervised and unsupervised learning problems, including regression, classification, and dimensionality reduction.
Assess and interpret model performance using key evaluation metrics, understand the bias-variance trade-off, and distinguish quality of fit in various settings.

Understand and apply fundamental concepts of optimization, including gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, gradient descent, and constrained optimization, with applications to training neural networks and building feedforward architectures. (L2-Understanding and L3- Applying)

Perform and interpret dimensionality reduction techniques, such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Fisher Discriminant Analysis, and apply support vector machines for classification with kernel methods and geometric interpretations.

objectives: To acquaint the students with various modeling and simulation techniques for discrete, dynamic and stochastic systems. It will focus on the important aspects of simulation study, including modelling, simulation languages, validation, and output data analysis.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of system modeling and simulation techniques, including deterministic/stochastic systems, discrete event simulation, continuous simulation, and Monte Carlo methods.
Apply discrete event simulation techniques using time-advance mechanisms and event-driven approaches to model systems such as single-server queues.

analyze random numbers and variates using statistical tests (chi-square, runs test), and select appropriate probability distributions for simulation input modeling.
Evaluate simulation results using statistical techniques such as confidence intervals, variance reduction methods, and experimental design to compare system alternatives.

Describe the key concepts, processes, and advantages of data mining and its applications in real- world business scenarios. 2. objectives: This course provides an introduction to time series analysis. program: B Tech and MBA Tech Data Science
objectives: This course develops students' skills in human-centered design, interdisciplinary teamwork, and problem-solving through structured project work. Students will engage in stakeholder analysis, prototyping, testing, and iterative refinement while integrating engineering principles, creativity, and sustainability. Emphasizing collaboration and ethical responsibility, the course prepares students for industry and community-driven challenges by enhancing their project management, communication, and critical thinking abilities.

outcomes.text: Critically evaluate complex, real-world challenges using systematic problem-solving approaches.
Lead and collaborate in interdisciplinary teams to develop scalable and impactful solutions.
Apply advanced design methodologies and emerging technologies to prototype and refine innovative solutions in research.
Integrate sustainability, ethics, and feasibility analysis into the design and implementation process.
Demonstrate professional communication through technical reports, presentations, and stakeholder engagement.

units.text: The course covers Problem Analysis, where students assess the problem context, constraints, stakeholders, and solution stage while conducting literature reviews and benchmarking existing solutions. In Design Thinking & Concept Development, they apply the phases of Design Thinking— Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test—to develop and refine innovative solutions. Prototyping & Testing involves transforming ideas into practical prototypes, conducting experiments, usability testing, and iterative refinements. Through Project Management & Documentation, students assign roles, track progress, and maintain structured records. Communication & Review focuses on preparing presentations, conducting design reviews, and incorporating feedback. Finally, Reflection & Improvement allows students to analyze challenges, enhance their skills, and document key learnings.

lab_work: The Laboratory work comprises various activities performed by the project teams for formulation, solution implementation and modification. Each team needs to submit the following documents:  Problem Statement Document  Project Development Report  Mid Semester Project Report  Research Paper / Conference Paper  Final Report

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech Data Science
prerequisites: Python for Data Analytics, Introduction to Data, Signal and Image analysis, Foundation of Machine Learning
objectives: This aim of the course is to familiarize the students with the fundamental concepts of Computer Vision. It will provide information on the techniques and algorithms that are currently used in real-world computer vision systems and their applications. It will encourage students to develop new systems based on integrating machine vision and deep learning.

outcomes.text: Describe the theoretical features and apply the practical aspects of computing with images
Determine the foundation of image formation and image analysis. Explain the basics of 2D and 3D Computer Vision
Estimate fundamental perceptions tasks such as image segmentation, object tracking, and object recognition
Summarize the key application areas of computer vision
