program: B Tech/ MBA Tech Data Science
objectives: The aim of the course is to provide progressive understanding of pattern classification and algorithms in order to classify multivariate data. It will also give information on the interpretation and implementation of the various genetic algorithms. Further, it will help students acquire knowledge of Q-Learning methods which will aid them in developing new machine learning techniques.

outcomes.text: Apply various classification and regression algorithms to categorize multivariate data and find relationship between data variables
Analyze reinforcement learning algorithms to test various complex systems
Evaluate different computational learning methods and results using scientific reports

units.title: Definition of Learning Systems
units.text: Definition of Learning Systems Goals and applications of machine learning. Aspects of developing a learning system training data, concept representation, function approximation Streamlining Workflows with Pipelines Loading the Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset, Combining transformers and estimators in a pipeline

units.title: Decision Tree Learning
units.text: Decision Tree Learning Representing concepts as decision trees. Recursive induction of decision trees. Picking the best splitting attribute: entropy and information gain. Searching for simple trees and computational complexity. Occam's razor. Overfitting, noisy data, and pruning.

units.title: Ensemble Learning
units.text: Ensemble Learning Bagging & boosting and its impact on bias and variance, boosting, Random forest, Gradient Boosting Machines and XGBoost Applying bagging to classify samples in the Wine dataset

units.title: Experimental Evaluation of Learning Algorithms
units.text: Experimental Evaluation of Learning Algorithms Measuring the accuracy of learned hypotheses. Comparing learning algorithms: cross-validation, learning curves, and statistical hypothesis testing.

units.title: Computational Learning Theory
units.text: Computational Learning Theory Models of learnability: learning in the limit; probably approximately correct (PAC) learning. Sample complexity: quantifying the number of examples needed to PAC learn. Computational complexity of training. Sample complexity for finite hypothesis spaces. PAC results for learning conjunctions, kDNF, and kCNF. Sample complexity for infinite hypothesis spaces, Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension. Implementing a kernel principal component analysis: separating half-moon shapes, separating concentric circles

units.title: Support Vector Machines
units.text: Support Vector Machines Maximum margin linear separators. Quadratic programming solution to finding maximum margin separators. Kernels for learning non-linear functions.

units.title: Bayesian Learning
units.text: Bayesian Learning Bayes Theorem Concept Learning Maximum Likelihood Minimum Description Length Principle Bayes Optimal Classifier Gibbs Algorithm Naïve Bayes Classifier Bayesian Belief Network EM Algorithm Probability Learning Sample Complexity Finite and Infinite Hypothesis Spaces – Mistake Bound Model

units.title: Text Classification
units.text: Text Classification Bag of words representation. Vector space model and cosine similarity. Relevance feedback and Rocchio algorithm. Versions of nearest neighbor and Naive Bayes for text

units.title: Clustering and Unsupervised Learning
units.text: Clustering and Unsupervised Learning Learning from unclassified data. Clustering. Hierarchical Aglomerative Clustering. k-means partitional clustering. Expectation maximization (EM) for soft clustering. Semi-supervised learning with EM using labeled and unlabeled data.

text_books: 1. Peter Wlodarczak, Machine Learning and its Applications, 1st Edition, CRC Press, 2021 2. Ethem Alpaydın, Machine Learning, 1st Edition, MIT Press, 2021. 3. Mettu Srinivas, G. Sucharitha, Anjanna, Machine Learning Algorithms and Applications, 1st Edition, Wiley-Scrivener, 2021.
reference_books: 1. Chip Huyen, Designing Machine Learning Systems, 1st Edition, O'Reilly Publications, May 2022. 2. Petry, Genetic Algorithms for Pattern Recognition, 1st Edition, CRC Press, 2021.

program: B Tech, MBA Tech & B Tech Integrated Data Science
prerequisites: Python for Data Analytics, Introduction to Data, Signal and Image analysis, Foundation of Machine Learning
objectives: This aim of the course is to familiarize the students with the fundamental concepts of Computer Vision. It will provide information on the techniques and algorithms that are currently used in real-world computer vision systems and their applications. It will encourage students to develop new systems based on integrating machine vision and deep learning.

outcomes.text: Describe computer‑vision basics and set up OpenCV for simple image tasks.
Analyze image formation and perform pixel‑level operations such as masking and geometric transforms.
Apply filtering, color‑space conversion, and smoothing to enhance images.
Detect and match features for edge extraction, template matching, and object tracking.
Deploy ML/DL models (SVM, CNN) for face recognition, pedestrian and lane detection, and motion analysis.

units.title: Image Processing

units.title: Feature Detection and Matching

program: B Tech, MBA Tech & B Tech Integrated Data Science
objectives: The aim of the course is to provide progressive understanding of pattern classification and algorithms in order to classify multivariate data. It will also give information on the interpretation and implementation of the various genetic algorithms. Further, it will help students acquire knowledge of Q-Learning methods which will aid them in developing new machine learning techniques.

outcomes.text: Apply various classification and regression algorithms to categorize multivariate data and find relationships between variables.
Analyze reinforcement-learning algorithms to evaluate the performance of complex systems.
Evaluate different computational learning methods and interpret results using scientific reporting techniques.
Construct machine-learning workflows using pipelines and ensemble techniques for optimization of performance.
Distinguish between supervised and unsupervised learning approaches to appropriately model real-world datasets.

units.title: Definition of Learning Systems
units.text: Definition of Learning Systems Goals and applications of machine learning. Aspects of developing a learning system training data, concept representation, function approximation Streamlining Workflows with Pipelines Loading the Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset, Combining transformers and estimators in a pipeline

units.title: Decision Tree Learning
units.text: Decision Tree Learning Representing concepts as decision trees. Recursive induction of decision trees. Picking the best splitting attribute: entropy and information gain. Searching for simple trees and computational complexity. Occam's razor. Overfitting, noisy data, and pruning.

units.title: Ensemble Learning
units.text: Ensemble Learning Bagging & boosting and its impact on bias and variance, boosting, Random forest, Gradient Boosting Machines and XGBoost, Applying bagging to classify samples in the Wine dataset

units.title: Experimental Evaluation of Learning Algorithms
units.text: Experimental Evaluation of Learning Algorithms Measuring the accuracy of learned hypotheses. Comparing learning algorithms: cross-validation, learning curves, and statistical hypothesis testing.

units.title: Computational Learning Theory
units.text: Computational Learning Theory Models of learnability: learning in the limit; probably approximately correct (PAC) learning. Sample complexity: quantifying the number of examples needed to PAC learn. Computational complexity of training. Sample complexity for finite hypothesis spaces. PAC results for learning conjunctions, kDNF, and kCNF. Sample complexity for infinite hypothesis spaces, Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension. Implementing a kernel principal component analysis: separating half-moon shapes, separating concentric circles

units.title: Support Vector Machines
units.text: Support Vector Machines Maximum margin linear separators. Quadratic programming solution to finding maximum margin separators. Kernels for learning non-linear functions.

units.title: Bayesian Learning
units.text: Bayesian Learning Bayes Theorem Concept Learning Maximum Likelihood Minimum Description Length Principle Bayes Optimal Classifier Gibbs Algorithm Naïve Bayes Classifier Bayesian Belief Network EM Algorithm Probability Learning Sample Complexity Finite and Infinite Hypothesis Spaces – Mistake Bound Model

units.title: Text Classification
units.text: Text Classification Bag of words representation. Vector space model and cosine similarity. Relevance feedback and Rocchio algorithm. Versions of nearest neighbor and Naive Bayes for text

units.title: Clustering and Unsupervised Learning
units.text: Clustering and Unsupervised Learning Learning from unclassified data. Clustering. Hierarchical Aglomerative Clustering. k-means partitional clustering. Expectation maximization (EM) for soft clustering. Semi-supervised learning with EM using labeled and unlabeled data.

outcomes.text: Describe the concept of data structures and their computational complexity in terms of time and space.
Design and implement appropriate data structures for the given problem.
Analyze and differentiate various searching algorithms.
Analyze and differentiate various sorting algorithms.
Implement and analyze advanced data structures like Union-Find, balanced trees, and hash tables.

program: B Tech, MBA Tech & B Tech Integrated Data Science
prerequisites: Managing Uncertainty, Stochastic Processes and Applications
objectives: The aim of the course is to introduce the concepts of statistical treatment of risk-neutral valuation, arbitrage, options and derivatives. It will provide hands-on implementation of various risk and pricing models that are used in the industry. The purpose of this course is to give the students exposure to the practical applications of quantitative finance in the real world. It will teach the students how to put their theoretical understanding into practice

outcomes.text: Describe the structure and characteristics of financial markets and instruments including equities, bonds, derivatives, and their relevance in time value of money and portfolio theory.
Apply models such as Markowitz Portfolio Theory, CAPM, Fama-French models, and the Black-Scholes-Merton (BSM) model to evaluate portfolio performance and price derivatives.
Analyze various risk types (market, credit, operational) and model them using techniques such as Value at Risk (VaR), credit scoring (Z-score), and operational risk frameworks.

Evaluate financial instruments using the no-arbitrage principle, risk-neutral pricing, and mathematical constructs such as martingales, Markov chains, and Brownian motion in discrete and continuous time frameworks.
Construct and test quantitative finance models by identifying assumptions, verifying model outputs, and generating counter-examples for incorrect financial statements or invalid pricing strategies.

units.text: Introduction to financial markets Financial instruments, bonds, stocks and financial derivatives.

units.text: Time Value of Money Concept Time value of money, simple and compound interest rate, net present value, internal rate of return and annuities

units.title: Risk Learning
units.text: Risk Learning No arbitrage principle, pricing of forwards and futures, properties of options

units.title: Quantitative Modelling
units.text: Quantitative Modelling Derivative pricing by replication in binomial model. Discrete probability spaces, filtration, conditional expectation Discrete time martingales, Markov chain, risk-neutral pricing in binomial model for European and American derivatives.
General probability spaces, conditional expectation, Brownian motion.

units.title: Modern Financial Theory
units.text: Modern Financial Theory Black-Scholes-Merton (BSM) model, pricing of European derivatives in BSM framework. Valuation of options in BSM model, BSM formula, BSM partial differential equation, hedging, model completeness, fundamental theorems of asset pricing

units.title: Corporate Finance

units.title: Market risk modelling

program: B Tech, MBA Tech & B Tech Integrated Data Science
objectives: The aim of the course is to give a holistic orientation of the marketing strategy concepts and marketing analytics fundamentals with the practical skills to analyze consumer data to make successful marketing decisions. It will also provide understanding of the techniques used to identify, collect, manage, and understand marketing data for profitable use

outcomes.text: Understand and explain the role of marketing analytics, qualitative investigations, and consumer behavior studies in marketing decision-making.
Apply marketing concepts, segmenting, targeting techniques, and cluster analysis to identify high-potential market segments.
Analyze product positioning strategies using experimental analytics, conjoint analysis, and factor analysis for product development and pricing decisions.
Create and implement marketing strategies for new market entries, competitive growth, and managing mature and declining markets.
Apply advanced marketing analytics techniques such as logit modeling, demand models, and predictive modeling to understand consumer behavior and value customers.

program: B Tech, MBA Tech & B Tech Integrated Data Science
prerequisites: Statistical Structures in Data and Inference, Foundations of Machine Learning
objectives: The aim of the course is to emphasize on the importance of nonparametric methods and equip students with the conceptual and technical skills necessary to select and apply the appropriate procedures in the absence of the underlying distribution to make statistical inferences. This course will also provide information on the basic theory and computing tools required to perform nonparametric tests

outcomes.text: Understand the foundational concepts of non-parametric inference, such as empirical quantile functions, order statistics, and their asymptotic distributions.
Apply goodness-of-fit and independence tests, including Chi-squared and Fisher’s exact tests, to categorical data.
Analyze and interpret results using linear rank statistics for problems involving scale differences.
Perform and interpret non-parametric hypothesis tests like the sign test, Wilcoxon tests, Kruskal-Wallis, and runs test to compare populations. (L3 – Apply, L4 – Analyze)
Evaluate bivariate associations using Kendall’s Tau and Spearman’s Rank and analyze count data using McNemar’s and Fisher’s tests.

units.title: Introduction to Non-parametric Inference
units.text: Introduction to Non-parametric Inference Estimation of Location and Dispersion, Empirical quantile function, Probability Integral transformation, Asymptotic distribution of order statistics

units.title: Test of Goodness-of-fit
units.text: Test of Goodness-of-fit Categorical association and independence, Chi-squared test, Interpreting the Chi-squared test, Chi-squared as goodness-of-fit and, Fisher's exact test

units.title: Introduction to Linear Rank Statistics
units.text: Introduction to Linear Rank Statistics Linear ranks tests for Scale Problem, Some results on Linear Rank Statistics

units.title: Test of Equality
units.text: Test of Equality The sign test, One sample - Wilcoxon signed rank test, Two samples - Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney, Several samples - Kruskal-Wallis test, The runs test

units.title: Measures of Association of Bivariate Samples
units.text: Measures of Association of Bivariate Samples Kendall’s Tau Coefficient, Spearman’s Rank Coefficient, Equality of k independent samples

units.title: Analysis of Count Data
units.text: Analysis of Count Data Fishers exact test, Mc Nemars test, Analysis of multinomial data

objectives: The aim of the course is to familiarize students with current supply chain management trends and apply them in practice using latest analytical tools and demonstrate the problem solving ability to provide solutions. It will also educate students on improving operational efficiency and effectiveness by enabling data-driven decisions at strategic, operational and tactical levels

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental concepts of supply chain management including forecasting, network design, inventory types, and supply chain integration.
Apply prescriptive analytics techniques such as optimization models, facility location, and scheduling to improve supply chain decision-making.
Analyze the use of supervised machine learning techniques such as regression, decision trees, random forests, and neural networks in solving supply chain problems.
Evaluate unsupervised learning algorithms such as clustering and association rule mining for applications like customer segmentation and recommendation systems in supply chains.
Design AI-enabled solutions by integrating modern advancements in artificial intelligence to address real-world supply chain analytics problems.

objectives: The aim of the course is to provide Students with basic consortium related to market trading. It also provides information on development of real-time strategies. It focuses on creating trading engines that will be supported by advance data analytics

outcomes.text: Describe the fundamental concepts of algorithmic trading including market structure, order types, brokers, dealers, and various market participants.
Analyze different chart patterns and technical indicators (e.g., SMA, EMA, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands) to interpret market trends and price movements.
Apply suitable trading strategies such as scalping, arbitrage, mean-reverting, and sentiment-based strategies in different trading environments (e.g., equities, derivatives, forex).

objectives: The aim of the course is to provide progressive understanding of pattern classification and algorithms in order to classify multivariate data. It will also give information on the interpretation and implementation of the various genetic algorithms. Further, it will help students acquire knowledge of Q-Learning methods which will aid them in developing new machine learning techniques.

outcomes.text: Apply various classification and regression algorithms to categorize multivariate data and find relationship between data variables
Analyze reinforcement learning algorithms to test various complex systems
Evaluate different computational learning methods and results using scientific reports

units.title: Definition of learning systems
units.text: Definition of learning systems Goals and applications of machine learning. Aspects of developing a learning system training data, concept representation, function approximation Streamlining workflows with pipelines Loading the Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset, Combining transformers and estimators in a pipeline

units.title: Decision Tree Learning
units.text: Decision Tree Learning Representing concepts as decision trees. Recursive induction of decision trees. Picking the best splitting attribute: entropy and information gain. Searching for simple trees and computational complexity. Occam's razor. Overfitting, noisy data, and pruning.

units.title: Ensemble Learning

units.title: Computational Learning Theory
units.text: Computational Learning Theory Models of learnability: learning in the limit; probably approximately correct (PAC) learning. Sample complexity: quantifying the number of examples needed to PAC learn. Computational complexity of training. Sample complexity for finite hypothesis spaces. PAC results for learning conjunctions, kDNF, and kCNF. Sample complexity for infinite hypothesis spaces, Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension. Implementing a kernel principal component analysis: separating half- moon shapes, separating concentric circles

units.title: Support Vector Machines

units.title: Bayesian Learning

units.title: Text
units.text: Text Classification Bag of words representation. Vector space model and cosine similarity. Relevance feedback and Rocchio algorithm. Versions of nearest neighbor and Naive Bayes for text.

units.title: Clustering and Unsupervised Learning
units.text: Clustering and Unsupervised Learning Learning from unclassified data. Clustering. Hierarchical Aglomerative Clustering. k-means partitional clustering. Expectation maximization (EM) for soft clustering. Semi-supervised learning with EM using labeled and unlabeled data.

objectives: This course introduces concepts and techniques to design discrete time systems for processing of discrete time signals. It will help to develop applications based on image, speech and biomedical signals.

outcomes.text: Analyze the frequency response, pole-zero plots, and phase distortion of LTI systems to determine system characteristics.
Apply Discrete Fourier and Fast Fourier Transform their properties for system analysis applications.
Design FIR and IIR filters using appropriate techniques such as windowing, bilinear transformation, and frequency transformation for various applications.
Evaluate the computational complexity of DFT and FFT algorithms, comparing their efficiency in signal processing applications.
Implement FIR and IIR digital filters using different structures (Direct Form, Cascade, and Parallel) to achieve desired frequency response.

program: B Tech EXTC and B Tech Integrated IT and Computer
prerequisites: Knowledge of Basic concepts in Number theory and Algebra.
objectives: The principal objective of the course is to train the students in the construction and understanding of mathematical proofs and common mathematical arguments. It will instil sound knowledge of different topics of discrete mathematics which students will readily apply in the subsequent courses of their programme.

outcomes.text: Understand fundamental concepts of discrete mathematics, including set theory, relations, functions, logic, and proof techniques.
Apply mathematical logic, predicate calculus, and proof techniques, including mathematical induction, to establish the validity of statements and theorems.
Analyse problems involving combinatorics, recurrence relations, generating functions, and the pigeonhole principle to model discrete structures.
Interpret graphs and trees, including their properties, colouring, connectivity, and spanning trees, and apply algorithms like Kruskal’s and Prim’s to solve network-related problems.
Formulate concepts from abstract algebra, including groups, rings, and fields, to construct mathematical models and solve real-world problems.

units.title: Set Theory, Relations and Functions

Power set, The principle of Inclusion-Exclusion, Partitions of sets.Relations, Properties and types of binary relations, Equivalence relation. Functions, injective, surjective and bijective functions, Composition, inverse of a function.

units.title: Logic
units.text: Logic Revision of prerequisite concepts – ‘Propositions, Truth table, Laws of logic, Equivalence’. Satisfiability, tautology, validity, disjunctive and conjunctive normal forms, Predicates and Quantifiers, Proof Techniques, Mathematical Induction.

units.title: Combinatorics
units.text: Combinatorics Pigeonhole principle, Homogeneous and non-homogeneous linear recurrence relations with constant coefficients, Generating functions.

units.title: Graphs and Trees
units.text: Graphs and Trees Graphs and their properties, Degree, Connectivity, Path, Cycle, Eulerian graph, Hamiltonian graph, Planar graphs, Graph Coloring. Trees, Rooted trees, Spanning tree and minimum spanning tree, Kruskal’s and Prim’s algorithms for minimal spanning trees.

units.title: Abstract algebra

Explain the properties of Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems and apply convolution techniques.
Illustrate the Fourier series representation of periodic signals, analyze their magnitude, and phase spectra.
Utilize Fourier and Laplace transforms, their properties for system analysis applications.
Apply Z-transform in solving difference equations for discrete-time systems.

program: BTI Integrated (Computer / Information Technology)
objectives: This course introduces the fundamental concepts and techniques underlying the construction of digital systems. It further provides insight into designing digital logic circuits using basic building blocks and necessary techniques required in computer hardware design.

outcomes.text: Translate different number systems and binary codes, including weighted and non-weighted codes.
Simplify Boolean expressions using De Morgan’s Theorem, SOP, POS, and Karnaugh maps.
Build combinational logic circuits such as adders, multiplexers, decoders, and encoders. .
Analyze sequential circuits, including flip-flops, registers, and counters.
Make use of VHDL for realizing basic digital logic circuits in different modeling styles.

units.title: Introduction to Digital Systems
units.text: Introduction to Digital Systems Number Systems - Binary, Octal, Hexadecimal, BCD, Conversion from one system to another, Binary subtraction using 1’s and 2’s complement method. Weighted codes - BCD and Binary, Non-weighted codes - Grey and Excess 3, conversion from one code to another.

units.title: Logic Gates and Boolean Algebra
units.text: Logic Gates and Boolean Algebra Logic gates, Concept of universal logic and implementation of digital logic using universal gates, Review of Boolean algebra and De Morgan’s Theorem, SOP & POS forms, Canonical forms, Karnaugh maps up to 4 variables.

units.title: Combinational logic circuit and its implementation
units.text: Combinational logic circuit and its implementation Combinational circuits - Adders, Subtractors (half and full), Multiplexers, DE-multiplexers, Decoders, Encoders, Design of digital logic using multiplexers.

units.title: Sequential Logic Circuits
units.text: Sequential Logic Circuits Flip flops - SR, T, D, JK, master slave JK, converting one flip-flop to another, Registers - Serial input, serial output; serial input-parallel output; Parallel In- Parallel Out, Serial In -Serial Out, Bi-Directional Shift Registers, Counters -Synchronous Counters, Asynchronous (Ripple) Counters and asynchronous counter designing.

units.title: Introduction to VHDL
units.text: Introduction to VHDL VLSI Design flow - Design entry, Schematic, Different modelling styles in VHDL - Dataflow, Behavioural and Structural Modelling, Data types and objects, Synthesis and Simulation of any basic digital logic circuits.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Signals and Systems, Probability and Stochastic Processes
objectives: 1. To teach various types of Analog & digital modulation and demodulation techniques. 2. To recognise concept of baseband shaping for data transmission and detection. 3. Understand various coding and decoding techniques. 4. To learn basic concepts spread spectrum techniques and their applications.

outcomes.text: Evaluate the principles and concepts of different analog & digital modulation techniques.
Apply different base band shaping techniques for data transmission and detection.
Analyze different algorithms for source and error control coding.
Understand the concepts and applications of spread spectrum modulation.

units.title: Introduction to Electronic communications
units.text: Introduction to Electronic communications: Elements of a communication system, modulation and demodulation, Electromagnetic frequency spectrum, Principles of Amplitude Modulation systems- DSB, SSB and VSB modulations. Angle modulation: Frequency modulation (FM), Phase modulation (PM), FM noise triangle, pre-emphasis and de- emphasis.

units.title: Analog Pulse modulation and Multiplexing Techniques
units.text: Analog Pulse modulation and Multiplexing Techniques: Sampling theorem for low- pass and band–pass signals- proof with spectrum, aliasing, Sampling techniques. Pulse modulation: Classification of Pulse modulation, Generation and detection of: Pulse amplitude modulation (PAM), Pulse width modulation (PWM), and Pulse position modulation (PPM). Multiplexing: Principles of Time division multiplexing (TDM), Frequency division multiplexing (FDM).

units.title: Waveform coding techniques
units.text: Waveform coding techniques: Model of digital communication system, Quantization and Encoding, Pulse Code Modulation (PCM) transmitter and receiver, Differential PCM (DPCM) transmitter and receiver, Delta Modulation (DM) transmitter and receiver, quantization noise and slope overload distortion, Adaptive delta modulation (ADM) transmitter and receiver, Discrete PAM signals: Line coding techniques: Unipolar, Polar and bipolar.

units.title: Base Band Shaping for data Transmission and detection
units.text: Base Band Shaping for data Transmission and detection: GRAM-SCHMIDT orthogonalization procedure, Geometric Interpretation of signal, Power Spectra of discrete PAM, Inter symbol Interference (ISI), Eye pattern. Baseband Detection: Detection of binary signals, Maximum likely hood detector, Probability of error, Correlation receiver, Matched filter receiver.

units.title: Digital Modulation Techniques
units.text: Digital Modulation Techniques: Digital Modulation formats, Coherent Binary modulation techniques: FSK and PSK , Coherent Quadrature modulation techniques: Quadriphase-shift Keying, Minimum Shift Keying.

units.title: Source coding and Error Control Coding
units.text: Source coding and Error Control Coding: Uncertainty, Information and Entropy, Properties of Entropy, Source coding Theorem, Huffman coding. Channel Coding Theorem, Linear Block codes, Encoder and Decoder using Shift Register Method for Cyclic codes.

units.title: Spread Spectrum Modulation
units.text: Spread Spectrum Modulation: Pseudo noise sequences, A Notion of Spread spectrum, Direct sequence spread coherent binary phase shift keying, Frequency hop spread spectrum: Slow Frequency hopping and fast frequency hopping, applications.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Engineering Mathematics, Circuits and Network Technology, Signals and Systems.
objectives: 1. To understand the Basics theory of process and control systems and System stability. 2. To analyze and Design the system for fulfilling the performance and stability criterion. 3. To evaluate different stability criterion.

outcomes.text: Understand the modelling of linear-time-invariant systems using transfer function and state space representations.
Understand the concept of stability and its assessment for linear-time invariant systems.
Design simple feedback controllers.

units.title: Introduction to control problem
units.text: Introduction to control problem Industrial Control examples. Mathematical models of physical systems. Control hardware and their models. Transfer function models of linear time-invariant systems. Feedback Control: Open-Loop and Closed-loop systems. Benefits of Feedback. Block diagram algebra.

units.title: Time Response Analysis
units.text: Time Response Analysis Standard test signals. Time response of first and second order systems for standard test inputs. Application of initial and final value theorem. Design specifications for second-order systems based on the time- response. Concept of Stability. Routh-Hurwitz Criteria. Relative Stability analysis. Root-Locus technique. Construction of Root-loci.

units.title: Frequency-response analysis
units.text: Frequency-response analysis Relationship between time and frequency response, Polar plots, Bode plots. Nyquist stability criterion. Relative stability using Nyquist criterion – gain and phase margin. Closed-loop frequency response.

units.title: Introduction to Controller Design
units.text: Introduction to Controller Design Stability, steady-state accuracy, transient accuracy, disturbance rejection, insensitivity and robustness of control systems. Root-loci method of feedback controller design. Design specifications in frequency-domain. Frequency-domain methods of design. Application of Proportional, Integral and Derivative Controllers, Lead and Lag compensation in designs. Analog and Digital implementation of controllers.

units.title: State variable Analysis
units.text: State variable Analysis Concepts of state variables. State space model. Diagonalization of State Matrix. Solution of state equations. Eigenvalues and Stability Analysis. Concept of Controllability and Observability. Pole-placement by state feedback. Discrete-time systems. Difference Equations. State-space models of linear discrete-time systems. Stability of linear discrete-time systems.

units.title: Introduction to Optimal Control and Nonlinear Control
units.text: Introduction to Optimal Control and Nonlinear Control Performance Indices. Regulator problem, Tracking Problem. Nonlinear system–Basic concepts.

text_books: 1. M. Gopal, “Control Systems: Principles and Design”, McGraw Hill Education, 4th Edition 2012. 2. B. C. Kuo, F. Golnaraghi “Automatic Control System”, John Wiley & Sons,9th Edition 2010.
reference_books: 1. K. Ogata, “Modern Control Engineering”, Prentice Hall, 5th Edition 2010. 2. I. J. Nagrath and M. Gopal, “Control Systems Engineering”, New Age International, 6th Edition 2017. 3. Norman S. Nise, “Control Systems Engineering” Wiley Student Publication, 7th Edition 2014.

Apply various transforms on Discrete Time signals.
Design Finite Impulse Response and Infinite Impulse response filters.

units.text: Design of IIR filters: Butterworth filter, Introduction to Chebyshev filters. Design IIR filter using Bilinear transformation Frequency transformation low pass to high pass, band pass, band reject filters

Understand various modes of propagation in WG, active and passive microwave components and their properties.
Understand basics of antenna parameters and its types.
Measurement of different microwave and antenna parameters.

units.title: Mathematical Model of Microwave Transmission

units.text: Real-Time Operating System (RTOS) Basics: Operating System Basics, Types of OS, Tasks, Process and Threads, Multiprocessing and Multitasking, Task Scheduling, Threads and Processes Scheduling: Putting them altogether, Task Communication, Task Synchronization, Device Drivers, How to Choose an RTOS.

units.title: The Embedded System Development Environment
units.text: The Embedded System Development Environment: The Integrated Development Environment (IDE), Types of Files Generated on Cross-compilation, Disassembler/Decompiler, Simulators, Emulators and Debugging, Target Hardware Debugging, Boundary Scan.

units.title: Trends in the Embedded Industry
units.text: Trends in the Embedded Industry: Processor Trends in Embedded System, Embedded OS Trends, Development Language Trends, Open Standards, Frameworks and Alliances, RTOS examples: VxWorks/MicroOS/OS-II

units.title: Case study
units.text: Case study: DSP/microprocessor based or FPGA based system design.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
objectives: 1. To analyze different converters and control with their applications 2. To study advanced converters and switching techniques implemented in recent technology 3. To understand, simulate and design single-phase and three-phase thyristor converters.

outcomes.text: Build and test circuits using power devices such as SCR
Analyze and design controlled rectifier, DC to DC converters, DC to AC inverters
Learn how to analyze these inverters and some basic applications.

units.title: Characteristics of Semiconductor Power Devices
units.text: Characteristics of Semiconductor Power Devices: Thyristor, power MOSFET and IGBT structure, Characteristics, operation, ratings, protections and thermal considerations. Brief introduction to power devices viz. TRIAC, MOS controlled thyristor (MCT), Power Integrated Circuit (PIC) (Smart Power), Triggering/Driver, commutation and snubber circuits for thyristor, power MOSFETs and IGBTs (discrete and IC based).Concept of fast recovery and schottky diodes as freewheeling and feedback diode.

units.title: Controlled Rectifiers
units.text: Controlled Rectifiers: Principle of Phase-Controlled converter operation, Single Phase Semi Converter and Single Phase Full Converter with R, RL, RLE load. Three Phase Half Wave Converters, Three Phase Semi Converter and Three Phase Full converter with R, RL, RLE load. Design of Converter Circuits, Effect of Load and source inductances.

units.title: Choppers
units.text: Choppers: Quadrant operations of Type A, Type B, Type C, Type D and type E choppers, Control techniques for choppers – TRC and CLC, Detailed analysis of Type A chopper. Step up chopper. Multiphase Chopper

units.title: Single-phase inverters
units.text: Single-phase inverters: Principle of operation of Series and Parallel, full bridge square wave, quasi-square wave, PWM inverters and comparison of their performance. Driver circuits for above inverters and mathematical analysis of output (Fourier series) voltage and harmonic control at output of inverter (Fourier analysis of output voltage). Filters at the output of inverters, Single phase current source inverter

units.title: Switching Power Supplies
units.text: Switching Power Supplies: Analysis of fly back, forward converters for SMPS, Resonant converters - need, concept of soft switching, switching trajectory and SOAR, Load resonant converter - series loaded half bridge DC-DC converter.

units.title: Applications
units.text: Applications: Power line disturbances, EMI/EMC, power conditioners. Block diagram and configuration of UPS, salient features of UPS, selection of battery and charger ratings, and sizing of UPS. Separately excited DC motor drive. P M Stepper motor Drive.

text_books: 1. Muhammad H. Rashid, “Power electronics”, edition IV, Prentice Hall of India. 2. Ned Mohan, Robbins, “Power electronics”, edition III, John Wiley and sons. 3. P.C. Sen., “Modern Power Electronics”, edition II, Chand& Co.
reference_books: 1. V.R.Moorthi, “Power Electronics”, Oxford University Press. 2. Cyril W., Lander,” Power Electronics”, edition III, McGraw Hill. 3. G K Dubey, S R Doradla,:Thyristorised Power Controllers”, New Age International Publishers. SCR manual from GE, USA.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Mathematics – I, II, and III. Basic Knowledge of Programming
objectives: 1. To instill in prospective engineer’s knowledge of techniques in calculus, multivariate analysis and linear algebra. 2. To equip the students with intermediate to advanced level concepts and aligned tools to help them tackle advanced mathematics and related applications.

outcomes.text: Understand the concept of floating point and errors.
Identify and solve problem using numerical methods
Implement algorithm based solution for scientific computation.

units.title: Computer Arithmetic
units.text: Computer Arithmetic: Floating Point Numbers, Normalization, Properties of Floating Point System, Rounding, Machine Precision, Subnormal and Gradual Underflow, Exceptional Values, Floating-Point Arithmetic, Cancellation.

units.title: System of linear equations
units.text: System of linear equations: Linear Systems, Solving Linear Systems, Gaussian elimination, Pivoting, Gauss-Jordan, Norms and Condition Numbers, Symmetric Positive Definite Systems and Indefinite System, Iterative Methods for Linear Systems.

units.title: Eigenvalues and singular values
units.text: Eigenvalues and singular values: Eigen-values and Eigenvectors, Methods for Computing All Eigen- values, Jacobi Method, Methods for Computing Selected Eigen- values, Singular Values Decomposition, Application of SVD.

units.title: Linear least squares
units.text: Linear least squares: Data Fitting, Linear Least Squares, Normal Equations Method, Orthogonalization Methods, QR factorization, Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization, Rank Deficiency, and Column Pivoting.

units.title: Nonlinear equations
units.text: Nonlinear equations: Fixed Point Iteration, Newton’s Method, Inverse Interpolation Method Optimization: One-Dimensional Optimization, Multidimensional Unconstrained Optimization, Nonlinear Least Squares

units.title: Interpolation
units.text: Interpolation: Purpose for Interpolation, Choice of Interpolating, Function, Polynomial Interpolation, Piecewise Polynomial Interpolation

units.title: Numerical Integration and Differentiation
units.text: Numerical Integration and Differentiation: Quadrature Rule, Newton-Cotes Rule, Gaussian Quadrature Rule, Finite Difference Approximation.

units.title: Initial Value Problems for ODES, Euler’s Method, Taylor Series
units.text: Initial Value Problems for ODES, Euler’s Method, Taylor Series Method, Runga – Kutta Method, Extrapolation Methods, Boundary Value Problems for ODES, Finite Difference Methods, Finite Element Method, Eigenvalue Problems.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Knowledge of basic electronics and control theory
objectives: 1. To provide knowledge to learn essential concepts behind control system elements and operations. 2. To expose students to the topics of process control, measurement, and instrumentation to allow applications-oriented design.

outcomes.text: Learn and apply essential concepts behind control system elements and operations in hydraulics and pneumatics automation.

Identify systems approach of the process control in industry and state-of-the-art coverage of computer integrated manufacturing using PLCs and flexible manufacturing systems as applicable in industrial applications.
Develop skills in handling computer-based controllers.
Explain fundamentals of sensorics technology and modular mechatronics along with robot technology.

units.title: Introduction to Automation
units.text: Introduction to Automation Automation in Production System, Principles and Strategies of Automation, Basic Elements of an Automated System, Advanced Automation Functions, Levels of Automations.

units.title: Introduction to Fluid Power Generating/Utilizing Elements
units.text: Introduction to Fluid Power Generating/Utilizing Elements Hydraulic pumps and motor gears, vane, piston pumps-motors- selection and specification-Drive characteristics - Linear actuator -. Reservoir capacity, heat dissipation, accumulators - standard circuit symbols, circuit (flow) analysis.

units.title: Control and Regulation Elements
units.text: Control and Regulation Elements Direction flow and pressure control valves-Methods of actuation, types, sizing of ports-pressure and temperature compensation, overlapped and under lapped spool valves-operating characteristics- Electro Hydraulic System, Electro Hydraulic servo valves-Different types characteristics and performance.

units.title: Hydraulics
units.text: Hydraulics Introduction to Hydraulics, Physical Fundamentals and principles, Hydraulic components (Pump, Valves, etc.), Basic hydraulics circuits and Electro Hydraulics, Practical examples based on simple automation tasks, types of proportional control devices- Pressure relief, Flow control, Direction control, Hydraulic symbols, Spool configurations, Selection & sizing with reference to manufacturer’s data, Electrical operation, Basic electrical circuits and operation, Solenoid design, Comparison between conventional and proportional valves.

units.title: Pneumatics
units.text: Pneumatics Introduction to Pneumatics, Physical Fundamentals and principles of Pneumatics, Pneumatic Components (Compressor, Valves, Compressed Air), Basic hydraulics circuits and Electro Pneumatics, Practical examples based on simple automation tasks

units.title: Control schemes & controllers
units.text: Control schemes & controllers On/OFF control, P, PI, PID control, related terminologies, parameter adjustments and implications Electronic P, PI & PID controller. Data acquisition, set point control, direct digital control Review of Z-transform theory and its application in digital control Digital PID algorithms

units.title: PLC
units.text: PLC Introduction to Automation Technology and Programming Languages (Ladder Diagram), Interface I/O modules with PLC, Working principle of relays and contactors, Area of application, Programming with Relay and PLC

units.title: Sensorics, Robotics and Mechatronics
units.text: Sensorics, Robotics and Mechatronics Introduction to Sensorics Technology, Basics and Fundamentals, Functions of Inductive, Capacitive, Magnetic, Ultrasonic and Optical types of sensors, Introduction to Robot Technology Basics of Mechatronics and Modular Mechatronics.

text_books: 1. Johnson Curtis, Process Control Instrumentation Technology, Prentice hall of 23 India, 8th edition, 2007. 2. Mikell P. Groover, Automation, Production Systems and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing, Pearson Education, 4th edition, 2013.
reference_books: 1. IlangoSivaraman, Introduction to Hydraulics and Pneumatics, PHI Learning Pvt Ltd., 3rdedition, 2017. 2. Study Material from Bosch-Rexroth Automation Company.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Digital Time Signal Processing
objectives: 1. To understand Image fundamentals and resolutions 2. To comprehend Image processing techniques in spatial and frequency domain 3. To design techniques for filtering images and feature extraction. 4. To develop image and video processing applications in practice

outcomes.text: Apply spatial domain techniques for grey and color image enhancement.
Implement various transforms to convert and process image in frequency domain.
Understand various morphological operations and segmentation techniques for images.
Use motion estimation techniques for analysis of video signals

units.title: Image Fundamentals
units.text: Image Fundamentals: Basics of sampling and quantization, Representing Digital Image, Spatial and Gray level resolution, Basic relationships between pixels, RGB ,HSI, CMY and CMYK colour models

units.title: Image Enhancement
units.text: Image Enhancement Spatial Domain: Point Processing- Digital negative, contrast stretching, thresholding, gray level slicing, bit plane slicing, log transformation, power law transformation. Neighbourhood Processing: Smoothing spatial filters, Sharpening spatial filters. Color image enhancement: intensity transformation and spatial filters Frequency Domain: 2-D DFT and its properties, Ideal, Butterworth and Gaussian Smoothing and Sharpening filters, Homomorphic filtering Histogram processing: Histogram equalization, histogram specification.

units.title: Image Transforms
units.text: Image Transforms: Walsh transform, Hadamard transform, Discrete cosine transform, Slant transform, Discrete Wavelet Transform

units.title: Morphological Image Processing
units.text: Morphological Image Processing: Dilation, erosion, opening, closing, Hit –or-Miss transformation Basic Morphological Algorithms: Boundary extraction on binary images, Region filling , Skeletonization

units.title: Image Segmentation
units.text: Image Segmentation: Detection of discontinuities: Point, Line and Edge detection Edge linking and boundary detection: Local processing, global processing via Hough transform, Global processing via Graph Theoretic techniques. Thresholding Region based segmentation: Region growing, region splitting and merging

units.title: Fundamentals of Digital Video
units.text: Fundamentals of Digital Video Video Formation , Perception and Representation: Digital video sampling, temporal correlation, video frame classifications, I, P and B frames, Digital video quality measure.

units.title: Digital Video Processing Techniques
units.text: Digital Video Processing Techniques Fundamentals of motion estimation and compensation General methodologies in motion estimation: Motion representation, Motion Estimation Algorithms: Sequential Search Block Matching, Hierarchical Block Matching Algorithm

text_books: 1. Rafael.C. Gonzalez and Richard E. Woods, Digital Image Processing, Pearson Education, 4th Edition, 2019. 2. Oge Marques, Practical Image and Video Processing using Matlab, IEEE Press, John Wiley & Sons Publication, 2011.
reference_books: 1. Li, Ze-Nian, Drew, Mark S., Liu, Jiangchuan, “Fundamentals of Multimedia”, Springer, 2nd Edition, 2014. 2. Scotte Umbaugh, Digital Image Processing and Analysis-Human and Computer Vision Application with CVIP Tools, 2nd edition, CRC Press, 2011.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Analog Circuits, Analog and Digital communication.
objectives: 1. To provide knowledge and principle of Colour TV and Advanced TV systems. 2. To teach fundamentals of colour signal transmission and their standards. 3. To introduce principles of display technologies like LCD TV and LED TV. 4. To give an insight of the concepts of digital signal transmission and principle of Digital TV, HDTV, EDTV, IPTV and 3D TV.

outcomes.text: Understand the working principles of various colour TV systems.
Apply knowledge of basic colour TV systems for advanced TV technologies.
Analyze the principles of various display technologies.
Analyse the fundamentals of digital signal transmission.

units.title: Fundamentals of Colour Television
units.text: Fundamentals of Colour Television: Compatibility and reverse compatibility, colour perception, Three colour theory, luminance, hue and saturation, colour TV camera, generation of luminance and colour difference signals, unsuitability of (G-Y) signal for transmission. Colour signal transmission: Frequency interleaving, bandwidth, Quadrature AM, colour burst signal, weighting factors, formation of chrominance signal, colour signal Phasor diagram.

units.title: Colour TV Systems
units.text: Colour TV Systems: NTSC colour TV system: Phasor diagram of I and Q signals, colour subcarrier frequency, coder and decoder, limitations. PAL colour TV system: features, PAL burst, cancellation of phase errors, PAL-D demodulation, choice of colour subcarrier frequency, PAL coder and decoder, merits and demerits, SECAM III colour TV system: Coder and decoder, merits and demerits.

units.title: LCD
units.text: LCD : Liquid crystal display (LCD) technology, Liquid crystals, operation of Liquid crystal display, Twisted Nematic (TN) transmissive LCD, passive and active- matrix LCD’s, TFT-LCD panel drive, Backlight assembly. LED TV: LED technology, materials used for LED’s, working of LED TV, Parameters of a LED module, advantages of LED screens, comparison of LCD, edge lit LED and back lit LED TV, Organic LED TV (OLED).

units.title: Digital Television Transmission Standards
units.text: Digital Television Transmission Standards: ATSC terrestrial transmission standard, vestigial sideband modulation, DVB-T transmission standard, ISDB-T transmission standard, channel allocations, antenna height and power.

units.title: Digital TV
units.text: Digital TV: Principles of digital video broadcasting: digitization, compression and channel encoding, Standard definition (SDTV) sampling rate, video sampling, MPEG encoding: components of DTV, Video- MPEG-2 coding, MPEG video compression, Digital TV receiver, Merits of Digital TV receivers, Direct to home (DTH) Television system.

units.title: High definition TV (HDTV)
units.text: High definition TV (HDTV): Advantages of HDTV, HDTV parameters, comparison of SDTV and HDTV aspect ratio, HDTV common interface format, Introduction to Ultra HDTV, Extended definition TV.

units.title: IPTV
units.text: IPTV: Internet protocol TV technology, On-line convergence, Asymmetrical digital subscriber line (ADSL) bandwidth allocation, Bit rates, Closed IPTV network, Video on demand, comparison of IPTV and cable technology. 3 D TV: Introduction to 3 D TV technology, three dimensional video displays.

text_books: 1. Gulati R.R, Monochrome and Colour Television, New Age International, 3rd edition, 2014. 2. K.F. Ibrahim, Newnes guide to Television and Video technology, 4th edition, 2007.
reference_books: 1. Gerald w. Collins, Fundamentals of Digital Television Transmission, John Wiley & Sons, 2001. 2. Gulati R. R., Modern Television Practice: Transmission, Reception and Applications, New Age International, 5th edition, 2015. 3. Herve Benoit , Digital Television, 2nd Edition, Focal Press, 2002.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
objectives: 1. The aim of this course is to introduce students to the application of scientific procedures to the conduction of research.

outcomes.text: Comprehend the basics of research process
Recognise the importance of literature review
Write a technical report/paper.
Relate ethical guidelines to conducting research, data collection and report writing

units.title: Introduction to research
units.text: Introduction to research The importance of research, research process overview, types of research, research terminology

units.title: Literature search and review
units.text: Literature search and review Searching for existing literature on a selected topic, reviewing the papers in selected area, use of abstract and citation databases for literature search

units.title: Formulating and solving a research problem
units.text: Formulating and solving a research problem Identifying a research problem, formulation of hypothesis, research objectives and questions, different types of research designs, experimental setup, data sampling and collection, data analysis

units.title: Technical writing
units.text: Technical writing Research paper writing, referencing in proper format, tools for technical writing,

units.title: Ethics in research
units.text: Ethics in research Research integrity, plagiarism basics and checks

program: B. Tech. ( EXTC )
objectives: 1. To familiarize with basic concepts of the laws governing corporations 2. To provide knowledge of recent developments in Law at the national level 3. To facilitate social and legal awareness from legal perspective

outcomes.text: Knowledge about the basic concepts of the important business laws
Application and interpretation of the business and labour laws in the actual business environment

units.text: Indian Contract Act, 1872  Introduction to Concepts, Major Definitions under the Act  Stages to formation of a Contract  Essential Elements- o Offer & Acceptance (Essentials) o Capacity of parties (Minors, Unsound Mind, Disqualified by Law) o Free Consent (Vitiating Elements & Effects- Coercion, Undue Influence, Fraud, Misrepresentation, Mistake) o Lawful Consideration & Lawful Object o Possibility to Perform (Doctrine of Frustration) o Agreement Expressly Declared Void  Types-Valid, Void & Voidable Agreements  Performance & Discharge of Contract;  Remedies for Breach of Contract  Special Contracts: o Indemnity & Guarantee o Bailment & Pledge o Contract of Agency

Sale of Goods Act, 1979  Concept of Sale as a Contract  Essentials of contract of sale & it’s conditions  The Rule of Caveat Emptor and the Exceptions  Conditions & Warranties including implied Conditions & Warranties  Rules of Delivery, Unpaid Seller & his rights  Suits for Breach of contract

Companies Act, 2013  Introduction to Act  Administration of Company Law (NCLT/NCLAT)  Types of companies  Characteristics of a company  Essential Documents and their clause: Memorandum of Association, Articles of Association, Certificate of Incorporation  Management: Classification of directors, Key managerial personnel, Types of meetings & resolutions  Lifting of the Corporate Veil  Concept and modes of Winding Up a company

units.title: Partnership Laws
units.text: Partnership Laws A) The Partnership Act, 1932  Nature and Characteristics of Partnership  Types of Partners  Rights and Duties of Partners  Incoming and outgoing Partners  Mode of Dissolution of Partnership B) The Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008  Salient Features of LLP  Differences between LLP and Partnership, LLP and Company  LLP Agreement  Partners and Designated Partners  Partners and their Relationship

Industrial Relations  The Trade Union Act, 1926 - Emergence of Trade Unions in India and the changing trends in Trade Unionism and their politics  Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 - Industrial Strikes and Employer Lockouts  Managing Industrial conflicts - Trends and Issues in effective Labour Court Administration  Role of Conciliation Officers in the Resolution of Industrial Disputes

Intellectual Property Rights  Introduction and the need for IPR (WIPO, TRIPS)  Trade Marks Act,1999 - Registration of Trademarks; passing off and infringement  Indian Copyright Act, 1957 - Registration and infringement of copyright  Patents Act, 1970 - Meaning of patent & Inventions; Opposition proceedings & Grant of Patent  Overview of Trade secrets and Industrial Designs

Competition Act, 2002  Objectives of Competition Law  Concept of Appreciable Adverse Effect on Competition (AAEC)  Anti-Competitive Agreements (S.3)- Horizontal Agreements, Vertical Agreements, Cartels, Blanket provision for IPR  Abuse of Dominance (S.4)  Competition Commission of India – Role, Duties, Competition Advocacy  Appellate Tribunal – Role of NCLAT

Alternative Dispute Resolution  The Law and Methods of Alternative Dispute Resolution  Comparative Study of the various forms of ADR  Application of ADR Methods in Different Fields & Areas  Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996 & International Developments  Arbitration clauses, Preparation for Arbitration, Conducting an Arbitration, Seat, Venue, Examinations and its various aspects, Evidence
Universal Ethics  Nature and Essence of Ethics  Role of ethics in Governance  Business Ethics Concepts  Professional ethics
Understanding Professional Ethics  Characteristics of ethical organizations  Causes of unethical behaviour  Benefits of ethical behaviour

units.text: Applied Ethics: Unethical Practices in Businesses  Bribery, Conflict of interest and Anti-corruption behaviour  Insider-Trading; meaning and legal provisions  Sexual harassment: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013

units.title: Applied Ethics
units.text: Applied Ethics: Combating Unethical Practices in Businesses  Whistleblowing: Concept and Mechanism  Socially responsible leadership and Corporate Social Responsibility’s role in corporate governance  Alternative Dispute Resolution as a tool to overcome unethical practices

program: B Tech (EXTC)
objectives: The aim of this course is to make students acquainted with fundamentals of wireless communication systems, and understand the diversity & spatial multiplexing phenomenon in MIMO system. This course also helps to comprehend the application of multiuser access in a cellular communication scenario and the propagation mechanisms in an urban mobile communication environment for different networks.

outcomes.text: Illustrate the concept of cell structure, frequency reuse and handoff mechanism
Apply the channel path loss models for analyzing fading behavior
Explain the need of diversity and LTE techniques used in wireless communication
Explore the architecture and models of 5G.

units.title: Introduction to wireless networks
units.text: Introduction to wireless networks Regulations- ITU-T and TRAI regulations The cellular concept- Introduction to cellular system, Frequency reuse, handoff, interference, Cell Splitting, Cell sectoring, a Microcell zone concept, Introduction to Multiple Access Technologies- FDMA, TDMA and CDMA.

units.title: Mobile radio propagation
units.text: Mobile radio propagation Large scale path loss, reflection, ground reflection (2 ray) model, practical link budget design using path loss models, small scale fading and multi-path, small-scale multipath propagation, types of small scale fading.

units.title: Diversity Techniques and MIMO
units.text: Diversity Techniques and MIMO Diversity Techniques, Diversity combining techniques, introduction to Multiple Input Multiple Output systems (MIMO)- Spatial diversity in MIMO and Spatial Multiplexing in MIMO.

units.title: LTE
units.text: LTE Different features of Release 10 and onward, Carrier Aggregation, enhanced MIMO systems, Coordinated multi-point operation (CoMP) technology, Heterogeneous networks, device-to-device communication, machine-to-machine communications, Data offloading, 3D MIMO.

units.title: 5G and 6G networks
units.text: 5G and 6G networks Introduction to Femtocell and its types, 5G architecture, 5G Radio Access Technologies: Design principles, Multi-carrier with filtering, Non- orthogonal Multiple Access - Radio access for dense deployments, Radio Access for V2X Communication, Radio access for massive machine-type communication, 5G wireless propagation channel models: Modelling requirements and scenarios, Introduction to 6G networks.

Monserrat and Patrick Marsch, 5G Mobile and Wireless Communications Technology, 1st Edition, Cambridge University Press, 2016.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech / BTI [EXTC/ Information Technology/ Computer Engineering/ Computer Science/ CSE(DS)-311(VT)]
prerequisites: Signals and Systems, Discrete Time Signal Processing
objectives: This course introduces concepts, methodologies and performance metrics for still image and motion picture processing. It also helps to develop a foundation for further study and research in the signal processing domain.

outcomes.text: Apply spatial domain enhancement techniques on grey images
Analyze various frequency domain transforms to process an image
Interpret the use of various morphological operations on images
Evaluate segmentation techniques for object detection
Illustrate video processing

units.title: Image fundamentals
units.text: Image fundamentals Basics of sampling and quantization, representing digital image, spatial and gray level resolution, basic relationships between pixels.

units.title: Image enhancement
units.text: Image enhancement Point processing techniques - digital negative, contrast stretching, thresholding, gray level slicing, bit plane slicing, log transformation, power law transformation, neighborhood processing-smoothing spatial filters, sharpening spatial filters, histogram processing-histogram equalization.

units.title: Image transforms
units.text: Image transforms Walsh transform, Hadamard transform, discrete cosine transform.

units.title: Morphological image processing
units.text: Morphological image processing Dilation, erosion, opening, closing, Hit–or-Miss transformation, basic morphological algorithms- boundary extraction on binary images, skeletonization, thinning, thickening.

units.title: Image segmentation
units.text: Image segmentation Detection of discontinuities- point, line and edge detection, edge linking and boundary detection using local processing, segmentation using thresholding, region based segmentation- region growing, region splitting and merging.

units.text: Digital video processing techniques Fundamentals of motion estimation, motion estimation algorithms- exhaustive search block matching, 2D-log search method and 3 step search method.

program: B Tech (EXTC)
prerequisites: Signals and Systems, Discrete Time Signal Processing
objectives: The aim of this course is to understand the characteristics of audio and speech signals and the related time and frequency domain methods for speech and audio analysis. It helps to analyze methods available for feature extraction from audio and speech signals. The student should be able to undertake a project which involves application like speech recognition, speaker recognition etc.

outcomes.text: Comprehend the fundamentals of audio and speech signals.
Apply various feature extraction techniques for time domain, frequency domain and cepstral domain on audio and speech signals
Use of different techniques to enhance audio and speech signals
Develop various applications of audio and speech processing.

units.title: Fundamental of speech and audio signals
units.text: Fundamental of speech and audio signals Digital models for speech waveform, representation of audio and speech waveform, quasi-periodic and quasi- stationary nature of speech signal, need and technique of framing and windowing of speech signal, different types of audio and speech signal, hearing organs and mechanism of speech signal

units.title: Time domain methods for audio and speech processing

program: B Tech (EXTC)
prerequisites: Communication Theory and Systems, Electromagnetic Field Theory
objectives: The aim of this course is to familiarize students with the fundamentals of satellite communication and Radar systems and their current applications. Students will be exposed with examples of applications and trade-offs that typically occur in engineering system design with respect to spacecraft launching and detection of targets using Radar systems.

outcomes.text: Explain the structure, techniques, technology and key organizations involved in satellite communication and Radar systems.
Design and plan satellite communication links for a prescribed Quality of Service.
Classify the various satellite subsystems and their functionality and able to understand effects of scintillation.
Apply knowledge of existing satellite systems and state of the art technology to the design of future systems.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech (EXTC/ Information Technology/ Artificial Intelligence)
objectives: This course aims to acquaint students with the fundamentals of the Internet of Things (IoT) and its building blocks. It helps to understand the IoT hardware and various protocols used in IoT applications for everyday life. It also provides information on associated technologies like cloud computing and hands-on expertise in building IoT applications.

outcomes.text: Describe the fundamentals of IoT
Demonstrate appropriate use of protocols and cloud services for a given application
Distinguish the IoT data using various data analytics methods
Construct IoT based projects using suitable hardware boards.

units.title: Introduction to IoT
units.text: Introduction to IoT Introduction and definition of IoT, IoT growth – A statistical View, Application areas of IoT, Characteristics of IoT, IoT stack, Enabling Technologies – Sensors, Cloud Computing, Big data Analytics, Embedded Computing Board, Communication protocols and user interface. Internet of Things challenges, IoT levels.

units.title: IoT hardware interface

units.title: Protocols for IoT
units.text: Protocols for IoT Networking Architectures: Star, Mesh, Tree, Short distance protocols: IEEE 802.15.4, 6LowPan, Zigbee, Wi-Fi, Messaging protocols: MQTT, CoAP and REST. Addressing and Identification Protocols: IPv4, IPV6 and Uniform Resource Identifier.

units.title: Cloud for IoT

units.title: Data Analytics in IoT

Case studies on data analytics –

program: B Tech / MBA Tech (All programs)
objectives: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) or Drones are used in crucial array of applications from defense weapon systems and surveillance to providing relief and aid to distressed humanity. This course introduces hardware and software design of drones which will instill confidence to develop Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) for various applications.

outcomes.text: Describe fundamental concepts of UAV
Explain drone system design flow by considering electrical and mechanical parameters
Explain drone’s sensors and communication technologies
Implement the model of Mini Quadrotor Vehicle

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Introduction to Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), aviation history and overview of UAV systems, UAV fundamentals, Definitions and terminology , Classes and missions of UAVs, Examples of UAV systems - very small, small, medium and large, Parts of the drone - Hardware, Software and Mechanical subsystems, Ground based controllers, Use cases in Military, Industrial, Commercial applications.

units.title: Drone system design flow
units.text: Drone system design flow System Design - requirement specification, Architecture, Mechanical design – Propeller, X-frame, Mylar, MB, Shielding and TIM, Heat spreader, FPC (flexible PCB) etc. Hardware Design – Drone hardware block diagram, A typical drone system stack-up, Drone Power Architecture and Estimation - SOC power requirements, power devices – Linear regulator, Switching regulator and battery estimation, battery constraints, watt hours and energy density, battery capacity, and cost.

units.title: Drone hardware devices
units.text: Drone hardware devices UAV sensors - accelerometers, rate gyros, pressure sensors, digital compasses, GPS. Communication Module: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, fundamentals of 3G/4G mobile communication, RF communications, Drone communication system, Drone imaging system, Flight Controllers based on MCU/MPU, FPGA.

Drone security threats in areas such as terrorist attacks, illegal surveillance and reconnaissance, smuggling, electronic snooping, and mid-air collisions.

reference_books: 1. Richard K. Barnhart, Stephen B. Hottman, Douglas M. Marshall, Eric Shappee, Introduction to Unmanned Aircraft Systems, 1st ed., CRC press, 2012. 2. program: B Tech (EXTC)
objectives: The aim of this course is to make students acquainted with fundamentals of wireless communication systems, and understand the diversity & spatial multiplexing phenomenon in MIMO system. This course also helps to comprehend the application of multiuser access in a cellular communication scenario and the propagation mechanisms in an urban mobile communication environment for different networks.

outcomes.text: Illustrate the concept of cell structure, frequency reuse and handoff mechanism
Apply the channel path loss models for analyzing fading behavior
Explain the need of diversity and LTE techniques used in wireless communication
Explore the architecture and models of 5G.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech (All programs)
objectives: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) or Drones are used in crucial array of applications from defense weapon systems and surveillance to providing relief and aid to distressed humanity. This course introduces hardware and software design of drones which will instill confidence to develop Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) for various applications.

outcomes.text: Describe fundamental concepts of UAV
Explain drone system design flow by considering electrical and mechanical parameters
Explain drone’s sensors and communication technologies
Implement the model of Mini Quadrotor Vehicle

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Introduction to Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), aviation history and overview of UAV systems, UAV fundamentals, Definitions and terminology , Classes and missions of UAVs, Examples of UAV systems - very small, small, medium and large, Parts of the drone - Hardware, Software and Mechanical subsystems, Ground based controllers, Use cases in Military, Industrial, Commercial applications.

units.title: Drone system design flow
units.text: Drone system design flow System Design - requirement specification, Architecture, Mechanical design – Propeller, X-frame, Mylar, MB, Shielding and TIM, Heat spreader, FPC (flexible PCB) etc. Hardware Design – Drone hardware block diagram, A typical drone system stack-up, Drone Power Architecture and Estimation - SOC power requirements, power devices – Linear regulator, Switching regulator and battery estimation, battery constraints, watt hours and energy density, battery capacity, and cost.

units.title: Drone hardware devices
units.text: Drone hardware devices UAV sensors - accelerometers, rate gyros, pressure sensors, digital compasses, GPS. Communication Module: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, fundamentals of 3G/4G mobile communication, RF communications, Drone communication system, Drone imaging system, Flight Controllers based on MCU/MPU, FPGA. No Change

units.text: Autonomous control of a Mini Quadrotor Vehicle Introduction of Mini Quadrotor Vehicle, Description of the Experimental Platform, Embedded Control System, Sensor units, Control unit, Wireless Camera and Modem unit, Design of controller and its Modeling. Drone security threats in areas such as terrorist attacks, illegal surveillance and reconnaissance, smuggling, electronic snooping, and mid-air collisions.

program: B Tech (EXTC)
objectives: The aim of this course is to make students acquainted with fundamentals of wireless communication systems, and understand the diversity & spatial multiplexing phenomenon in MIMO system. This course also helps to comprehend the application of multiuser access in a cellular communication scenario and the propagation mechanisms in an urban mobile communication environment for different networks.

outcomes.text: Understand fundamental wireless network concepts, ITU-T & TRAI regulations, cellular system principles, and multiple access technologies.
Analyze large-scale and small-scale radio propagation effects, including path loss models and multipath fading.
Evaluate different diversity techniques and MIMO configurations for wireless communication performance enhancement.
Compare LTE advancements such as Carrier Aggregation, enhanced MIMO, CoMP, and heterogeneous networks.
Assess 5G and 6G network architectures, radio access technologies, and propagation models for next-generation communication.

units.title: Introduction to wireless networks
units.text: Introduction to wireless networks Regulations- ITU-T and TRAI regulations The cellular concept- Introduction to cellular system, Frequency reuse, handoff, interference, Cell Splitting, Cell sectoring, a Microcell zone concept, Introduction to Multiple Access Technologies- FDMA, TDMA and CDMA.

units.title: Mobile radio propagation
units.text: Mobile radio propagation Large scale path loss, reflection, ground reflection (2 ray) model, practical link budget design using path loss models, small scale fading and multi-path, small-scale multipath propagation, types of small scale fading.

units.title: Diversity Techniques and MIMO
units.text: Diversity Techniques and MIMO Diversity Techniques, Diversity combining techniques, introduction to Multiple Input Multiple Output systems (MIMO)- Spatial diversity in MIMO and Spatial Multiplexing in MIMO.

units.title: LTE
units.text: LTE Different features of Release 10 and onward, Carrier Aggregation, enhanced MIMO systems, Coordinated multi-point operation (CoMP) Electronics & Telecommunication technology, Heterogeneous networks, device-to-device communication, machine-to-machine communications, Data offloading, 3D MIMO.

units.title: 5G and 6G networks
units.text: 5G and 6G networks Introduction to Femtocell and its types, 5G architecture, 5G Radio Access Technologies: Design principles, Multi-carrier with filtering, Non- orthogonal Multiple Access - Radio access for dense deployments, Radio Access for V2X Communication, Radio access for massive machine-type communication, 5G wireless propagation channel models: Modelling requirements and scenarios, Introduction to 6G networks.

objectives: The course aims to build and enhance skills critical to future employability through a medley of activities and simulation practices. Also vital skills like persuasion, team participation, self-branding and workplace communications are developed through this course

outcomes.text: Demonstrate awareness of business networks and communicate appropriately in various contexts
Illustrate the knowledge of team dynamics to work productively in teams and participate effectively in contexts such as group discussions
Apply persuasive communication strategies to articulate themselves in situations such as personal interviews
Create social media plans and employment related documents to showcase their personal brand

units.title: Corporate Communication

units.title: Group and Team Dynamics
units.text: Group and Team Dynamics Group Discussions(GD) - speaking in GDs, discussing problems and solutions, creating a cordial and cooperative atmosphere, using persuasive strategies, being polite and firm, turn-taking strategies, effective intervention, reaching a decision, Organizational GD, GD as part of selection process: characteristics, evaluation and analysis Dynamics of group formation, the dysfunctions of groups and teams: norm violation and role ambiguity, groupthink and group-polarization, team building exercises

program: B Tech (EXTC)
prerequisites: Signals and Systems, Discrete Time Signal Processing
objectives: The aim of this course is to understand the characteristics of audio and speech signals and the related time and frequency domain methods for speech and audio analysis. It helps to analyze methods available for feature extraction from audio and speech signals. The student should be able to undertake a project which involves application like speech recognition, speaker recognition etc.

outcomes.text: Comprehend the fundamentals of audio and speech signals.
Apply various feature extraction techniques for time domain, frequency domain and cepstral domain on audio and speech signals
Use of different techniques to enhance audio and speech signals
Develop various applications of audio and speech processing.

units.title: Fundamental of speech and audio signals
units.text: Fundamental of speech and audio signals Digital models for speech waveform, representation of audio and speech waveform, quasi-periodic and quasi- stationary nature of speech signal, need and technique of framing and windowing of speech signal, different types of audio and speech signal, hearing organs and mechanism of speech signal

units.title: Time domain methods for audio and speech processing
units.text: Time domain methods for audio and speech processing Time domain parameters of speech signal and extracting methods: short time energy, average magnitude, zero crossing rate, average magnitude difference function. speech type discrimination using ZCR and energy, short time autocorrelation function, pitch period estimation using auto-correlation function

units.title: Frequency domain method for audio and speech processing
units.text: Frequency domain method for audio and speech processing Review of Fourier transform, Short Time Fourier Transform, spectrogram, concept of true vs convolved spectra , pitch and formant extraction, spectral analysis of speech using window function

units.title: Speech enhancement
units.text: Speech enhancement Different sources of speech degradation, scope and approach of speech enhancement, speech enhancement techniques: spectral subtraction method, re- synthesis method, comb filter, Wiener filter

units.title: Feature extraction techniques of speech
units.text: Feature extraction techniques of speech Linear Predictive Coding (LPC), application of LPC in pitch and formant extraction, cepstrum - homomorphic speech processing, cepstrum, Mel scale, Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) Electronics & Telecommunication

units.title: Applications of speech processing
units.text: Applications of speech processing Introduction to classifiers, speech recognition, speaker identification and verification, audio classification, emotion recognition and Audio forensics.
