program: B Tech (EXTC)
objectives: This course aims to provide knowledge on information theory for data compression and implement channel coding techniques for correcting and detecting errors in the communication channel.

outcomes.text: Illustrate the basic concepts of information, entropy, Shannon’s theorem and channel capacity
Implement and analyse various source coding techniques
Apply various channel coding techniques for error correction and analyse their performance.

units.title: Introduction to information theory
units.text: Introduction to information theory Information, Average information, Entropy, Properties of entropy, Information Rate, Discrete memory less channel- BSC, Joint and Conditional Entropies, Zero memory information source, Markov information source, Shannon’s theorem, Channel Capacity, Shannon Limit.

units.title: Source coding algorithms (Lossless compression)
units.text: Source coding algorithms (Lossless compression) Classification of codes- uniquely decodable codes, prefix codes, Kraft- McMillan inequality Shannon Fano code, Huffman code, Minimum variance Huffman code, Extended Huffman code, Adaptive Huffman code, Application in Image and Text Compression

units.title: Source coding algorithms (Lossy compression)
units.text: Source coding algorithms (Lossy compression) Classification of redundancies, Fidelity criteria Transform based coding- Discrete Cosine Transform, Discrete Walsh Hadamard Transform, Discrete Wavelet Transform, Application in Image Compression.

units.title: Channel Coding (Linear Block Codes)
units.text: Channel Coding (Linear Block Codes) Generator and parity check matrix, Error detecting and correcting capability, syndrome testing, decoding. Cyclic codes: Algebraic structure, properties, encoder and decoder, Hamming codes, Introduction to BCH codes.

units.title: Channel Coding (Convolution encoding)
units.text: Channel Coding (Convolution encoding) Systematic and Non-systematic Convolutional code Encoder - State Representation and State Diagram, The Tree Diagram Decoding problem- Maximum Likelihood Decoding, Viterbi Decoding Algorithm, Recursive Convolutional Code, Introduction to Turbo Codes. Electronics & Telecommunication

program: B Tech (EXTC)
prerequisites: Communication Theory and Systems, Electromagnetic Field Theory
objectives: The aim of this course is to familiarize students with the fundamentals of satellite communication and Radar systems and their current applications. Students will be exposed with examples of applications and trade-offs that typically occur in engineering system design with respect to spacecraft launching and detection of targets using Radar systems.

outcomes.text: Explain the structure, techniques, technology and key organizations involved in satellite communication and Radar systems.
Design and plan satellite communication links for a prescribed Quality of Service.
Classify the various satellite subsystems and their functionality and able to understand effects of scintillation.
Apply knowledge of existing satellite systems and state of the art technology to the design of future systems.

units.title: Satellite orbital mechanics and launchers
units.text: Satellite orbital mechanics and launchers Overview of satellite communication, frequency allocations, types of satellite, orbits and their applications, orbital mechanics- developing the equations of the orbit, Kepler’s three laws of planetary motion, describing the orbit of a satellite, locating the satellite in the orbit, locating the satellite with respect to the Earth, orbital elements, look angles, orbital perturbations, launching vehicles.

units.title: Satellite link design and propagation effects
units.text: Satellite link design and propagation effects Introduction, transmission theory, system noise temperature and G/T ratio, calculation of system noise temperature, noise figure, G/T for earth stations, design of downlinks, link budgets, uplink design, combining uplink and downlink carrier to noise ratios.

units.title: Satellite subsystems
units.text: Satellite subsystems Attitude and orbit control system (AOCS), telemetry, tracking, command and monitoring system (TTC&M), power systems, communication subsystems, transponders- Single conversion and double conversion, satellite antennas.

units.title: Satellite services and navigation
units.text: Satellite services and navigation Introduction to Satellite Mobile Services, Mobile Satellite (MSAT), Very small aperture terminal (VSAT) systems, Direct broadcast satellite (DBS) TV, Global positioning systems (GPS)- position location principles, GPS segments, GPS signal structure, GPS receiver, Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS).

units.title: Radar systems
units.text: Radar systems Electronics & Telecommunication Introduction to Radar set, radar frequencies, range performance, pulse repetition frequency, Radar display, Radar antennas, CW radars, FMCW radar, MTI radar, pulse doppler radar, applications.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Computer Engineering) B Tech (CSBS, EXTC, Computer Science)/ BTI Computer
objectives: This course provides a concise introduction to the fundamental concepts in machine learning from a practical perspective. Also, it covers the different learning algorithms and paradigms used in Machine Learning.

outcomes.text: Identify machine learning techniques suitable for a given problem
Solve the problems using various machine learning techniques
Develop an application using machine learning techniques
Evaluate and interpret the results of the algorithms.

units.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
units.text: Machine Learning Fundamentals Terminology, Supervised and Unsupervised Learning with examples, Underfitting / Overfitting, Bias-Variance Trade-off, Model Selection, Applications

units.title: Exploratory data Analysis
units.text: Exploratory data Analysis Missing Value Treatment, Handling Categorical data: Mapping ordinal features, Encoding class labels, Performing one-hot encoding on nominal features, Outlier Detection and Treatment. Feature Engineering: Variable Transformation and Variable Creation, Selecting meaningful features.

units.title: Regression
units.text: Regression Linear regression using Least Squares (analytical approach), Linear regression using Gradient Descent (iterative approach), Multiple linear regression, Polynomial regression

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification Performance Evaluation, Confusion Matrix, Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, ROC Curves, AUC, k-fold Cross-Validation. Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes Classifier, Support Vector Machines, Neural Networks: Perceptron, Multi-layer Perceptron, Training using Back-propagation, Applications

units.title: Tree-Based Methods
units.text: Tree-Based Methods Basics of Decision Trees, Regression Trees, Classification Trees, Trees v/s Linear Models, Advantages and Disadvantages of Trees, Ensemble techniques- Bagging, Boosting, Random forest

units.title: Unsupervised Learning
units.text: Unsupervised Learning Challenges of Unsupervised Learning, Partitioning Methods: K-Means clustering, Dimension Reduction Methods, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Hierarchical Clustering, Introduction to Recommender systems (Non-personalized and Content-based)

objectives: To impart knowledge of the fundamental theories, methods and techniques in the field of Artificial Intelligence and to design and develop AI systems.

Apply various heuristic and searching strategies to solve problems in the AI domain
Design knowledge base using expert systems and game playing
Implement supervised and unsupervised learning approaches to solve problems in the AI domain

units.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
units.text: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Definitions of AI, Applications of Artificial Intelligence, Concept of Modeling, Inference and Learning. Introduction to Machine learning and Deep learning as a subset of AI. Intelligent agents, concept of rationality, structure of agents, Environment, Properties of task environment. Real world Examples of agents and environments.

units.title: Solving problems by Searching
units.text: Solving problems by Searching Problem solving agents, searching for solutions. Uninformed Search: Breadth first search, Depth first search, Uniform cost search Informed Search: Informed search strategies, Greedy Best First Search, A* search, Hill climbing, problems with hill climbing such as Local Maxima, Plateau, Ridge, Genetic Algorithm. Adversarial Search: Introduction to the Domain of a game, optimal decisions in games, minimax algorithm, Alpha-beta pruning.

units.title: Constraint satisfaction Problem (CSP)
units.text: Constraint satisfaction Problem (CSP) Constraint satisfaction problems, Backtracking search for CSPs, variables and value ordering, propagating information through constraints, Intelligent backtracking, Local search for CSP. Case study on CSP.

units.title: Learning

units.title: Expert system

program: B Tech/MBA Tech Information Technology
objectives: This course is an introduction to Cryptography. It introduces the concepts used in traditional as well as modern cryptography. Students will learn various symmetric and asymmetric cryptographic algorithms and its application.

outcomes.text: Explain and implement various symmetric key cryptographic algorithms
Explain and implement various asymmetric key cryptographic algorithms
Describe various attacks on cryptosystems

units.title: Overview of Cryptography and Its Applications
units.text: Overview of Cryptography and Its Applications Introduction, security goals (CIA triad), Goals of cryptography, principles of modern cryptography, perfectly secret encryption, one time pad and Shannon’s theorem, cryptographic applications.

units.title: Classical cryptosystems
units.text: Classical cryptosystems Shift Ciphers, Affine Ciphers, The Vigenère Cipher, Playfair Ciphers, Substitution Ciphers, Transposition Ciphers, stream and block ciphers, Cryptanalysis.

units.title: Symmetric Key Cryptography
units.text: Symmetric Key Cryptography Integer and modular arithmetic, Extended Euclidean Algorithm, Linear Congruence, Algebraic structures (Group, Rings, and Fields), Galois Field, Modern Block Cipher and its components(D- Boxes and S-Boxes), product ciphers, stream ciphers (FSR and LFSR), attacks on stream and block ciphers, DES and AES, modes of operations.

units.title: Mathematics for Asymmetric Key Cryptography
units.text: Mathematics for Asymmetric Key Cryptography Primes, primality testing, factorization, Chinese remainder theorem, Quadratic Congruence, Fermat’s little theorem, Euler’s theorem.

units.title: Asymmetric Key Cryptography
units.text: Asymmetric Key Cryptography RSA Cryptosystem, Rabin Cryptosystem, ElGamal Cryptosystem, Elliptic Curve Cryptosystem.

units.title: Key Management
units.text: Key Management Key Distribution Centre, Needham-Schroeder Protocol, Kerberos, Diffie,-Hellman Key Agreement, Certification Authority, Public-Key infrastructure (PKI). 5. program: B Tech/MBA Tech Information Technology
objectives: This course gives an introduction to Management Information Systems. It aims at explaining how Information Technology / Information Systems help organizations to achieve competitive advantage in the market.

outcomes.text: Explain the role of Information System in business environment
Analyze existing business applications in use and design a business application for a given scenario
Describe the implications of social media on organizations
Identify the challenges in the management of global information systems and assess the security and ethical concerns

units.title: Foundations of Information systems and Management
units.text: Foundations of Information systems and Management Why Information systems? Fundamental behavioural, technical, business and managerial concepts about the components and roles of information systems, Types of information systems: Operations support systems and Management support systems, Definition, role and impact of MIS, MIS as a support to the management and a tool for management process.

units.title: Strategic Use of Information Systems
units.text: Strategic Use of Information Systems Fundamentals of strategic advantage –What is strategic advantage, brief overview of business strategy, organizational strategy and information systems strategy. Porter’s five forces model.

units.title: Using Information Technology for strategic advantage
units.text: Using Information Technology for strategic advantage Major concepts, developments, and management issues in information technology (hardware, software, networks, data resource management, and other information processing technologies such as the Internet).

units.title: Business Applications-I
units.text: Business Applications-I Major uses of information systems for the operations, management, and competitive advantage of an e-business enterprise. Electronic Business Systems – Enterprise business systems, Functional business systems Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems – What is ERP? Benefits, challenges and trends in ERP Customer relationship Management (CRM) systems - What is CRM? Three phases of CRM, Benefits, challenges and trends in CRM Supply Chain Management (SCM) systems - What is SCM? Role of SCM, Benefits, challenges and trends in SCM.

units.title: Business Applications-II
units.text: Business Applications-II Decision support systems (DSS) – Introduction, DSS components, Decision and management, information quality, Reporting, Online analytical processing, Using DSS – what-if analysis, sensitivity analysis, Goal-seeking analysis, Optimization analysis, Data mining for decision support. Knowledge Management and Business Analytics - Data, information and Knowledge, What is knowledge Management, Managing Knowledge to Business Intelligence, Why manage knowledge, Knowledge management processes, Components of business analytics.

units.title: Social Media and Organizations
units.text: Social Media and Organizations Leveraging social media for business, What to track in social media, Network effects for organizations, Social computing applications (Enterprise social computing) and implications on organizations.

units.title: Management Challenges
units.text: Management Challenges Security, Ethical and Societal Challenges Global Management of Information Systems – Cultural, political and geo- economic challenges, Global business/IT strategies and applications, Global data access issues.

reference_books: 1. Effy Oz, Management Information System, 6th Edition, Cengage Learning, 2013.

Generate summary reports
Access and manipulate data stored in excel or raw data files
Perform data transformations and iterative data processing

objectives: This course gives an introduction to Management Information Systems. It aims at explaining how Information Technology / Information Systems help organizations to achieve competitive advantage in the market.

outcomes.text: Explain the role of Information System in business environment
Analyze existing business applications in use and design a business application for a given scenario
Describe the implications of social media on organizations

program: B. Tech (Information Technology)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics.
objectives: 1. To provide a basic understanding of biological mechanisms of living organisms from the perspective of engineers. 2. To encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools.

outcomes.text: Convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are diverse.
Identify DNA as a genetic material in the molecular basis of information transfer.
Classify enzymes and distinguish between different mechanisms of enzyme action.
Apply thermodynamic principles to biological systems.
Identify and classify microorganisms.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Convey that Biology is as important a scientific discipline as Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry Bring out the fundamental differences between science and engineering by drawing a comparison between eye and camera, Bird flying and aircraft. Mention the most exciting aspect of biology as an independent scientific discipline. Why we need to study biology? Discuss how biological observations of 18th Century that lead to major discoveries. Examples from Brownian motion and the origin of thermodynamics by referring to the original observation of Robert Brown and Julius Mayor. These examples will highlight the fundamental importance of observations in any scientific inquiry.

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification: Convey that classification per se is not what biology is all about. The underlying criterion, such as morphological, biochemical or ecological be highlighted. Hierarchy of life forms at phenomenological level. A common thread weaves this hierarchy Classification. Discuss classification based on (a) cellularity- Unicellular or multicellular (b) ultrastructure- prokaryotes or eucaryotes. (c) energy and Carbon utilization -Autotrophs, heterotrophs, lithotropes (d) Ammonia excretion – aminotelic, uricoteliec, ureotelic (e) Habitata- acquatic or terrestrial (e) Molecular taxonomy- three major kingdoms of life. A given organism can come under different category based on classification. Model organisms for the study of biology come from different groups. E.coli, S.cerevisiae, D. Melanogaster, C. elegance, A. Thaliana, M. musculus

units.title: Genetics
units.text: Genetics: Convey that “Genetics is to biology what Newton’s laws are to Physical Sciences” Mendel’s laws, Concept of segregation and independent assortment. Concept of allele. Gene mapping, Gene interaction, Epistasis. Meiosis and Mitosis be taught as a part of genetics. Emphasis to be give not to the mechanics of cell division nor the phases but how genetic material passes from parent to offspring. Concepts of recessiveness and dominance. Concept of mapping of phenotype to genes. Discuss about the single gene disorders in humans. Discuss the concept of complementation using human genetics.

units.title: Biomolecules
units.text: Biomolecules: Convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are as diverse as one can imagine Molecules of life. In this context discuss monomeric units and polymeric structures. Discuss about sugars, starch and cellulose. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA. Two carbon units and lipids.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes: Convey that without catalysis life would not have existed on earth Enzymology: How to monitor enzyme catalyzed reactions. How does an enzyme catalyze reactions. Enzyme classification. Mechanism of enzyme action. Discuss at least two examples. Enzyme kinetics and kinetic parameters. Why should we know these parameters to understand biology? RNA catalysis.

units.title: Information Transfer
units.text: Information Transfer: The molecular basis of coding and decoding genetic information is universal Molecular basis of information transfer. DNA as a genetic material. Hierarchy of DNA structure- from single stranded to double helix to nucleosomes. Concept of genetic code. Universality and degeneracy of genetic code. Define gene in terms of complementation and recombination.

units.title: Macromolecular analysis
units.text: Macromolecular analysis: How to analyses biological processes at the reductionistic level Proteins- structure and function. Hierarch in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors and structural elements.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism: The fundamental principles of energy transactions are the same in physical and biological world. Thermodynamics as applied to biological systems. Exothermic and endothermic versus endergonic and exergonic reactions. Concept of Keq and its relation to standard free energy. Spontaneity. ATP as an energy currency. This should include the breakdown of glucose to CO2 + H2O (Glycolysis and Krebs cycle) and synthesis of glucose from CO2 and H2O (Photosynthesis). Energy yielding and energy consuming reactions. Concept of Energy Charge.

units.title: Microbiology
units.text: Microbiology: Concept of single celled organisms. Concept of species and strains. Identification and classification of microorganisms. Microscopy. Ecological aspects of single celled organisms. Sterilization and media compositions. Growth kinetics.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics.
objectives: 1. To provide a basic understanding of biological mechanisms of living organisms from the perspective of engineers. 2. To encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools.

outcomes.text: Convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are diverse.
Identify DNA as a genetic material in the molecular basis of information transfer.
Classify enzymes and distinguish between different mechanisms of enzyme action.
Apply thermodynamic principles to biological systems.
Identify and classify microorganisms.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Convey that Biology is as important a scientific discipline as Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry Bring out the fundamental differences between science and engineering by drawing a comparison between eye and camera, Bird flying and aircraft. Mention the most exciting aspect of biology as an independent scientific discipline. Why we need to study biology? Discuss how biological observations of 18th Century that lead to major discoveries. Examples from Brownian motion and the origin of thermodynamics by referring to the original observation of Robert Brown and Julius Mayor. These examples will highlight the fundamental importance of observations in any scientific inquiry.

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification Convey that classification per se is not what biology is all about. The underlying criterion, such as morphological, biochemical or ecological be highlighted. Hierarchy of life forms at phenomenological level. A common thread weaves this hierarchy Classification. Discuss classification based on (a) cellularity- Unicellular or multicellular (b) ultrastructure- prokaryotes or eucaryotes. (c) energy and Carbon utilization -Autotrophs, heterotrophs, lithotropes (d) Ammonia excretion – aminotelic, uricoteliec, ureotelic (e) Habitata- acquatic or terrestrial (e) Molecular taxonomy- three major kingdoms of life. A given organism can come under different category based on classification. Model organisms for the study of biology come from different groups. E.coli, S.cerevisiae, D. Melanogaster, C. elegance, A. Thaliana, M. musculus

units.title: Genetics
units.text: Genetics Convey that “Genetics is to biology what Newton‟s laws are to Physical Sciences” Mendel‟s laws, Concept of segregation and independent assortment. Concept of allele. Gene mapping, Gene interaction, Epistasis. Meiosis and Mitosis be taught as a part of genetics. Emphasis to be give not to the mechanics of cell division nor the phases but how genetic material passes from parent to offspring. Concepts of recessiveness and dominance. Concept of mapping of phenotype to genes. Discuss about the single gene disorders in humans. Discuss the concept of complementation using human genetics.

units.title: Biomolecules
units.text: Biomolecules Convey that all forms of life has the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are as diverse as one can imagine Molecules of life. In this context discuss monomeric units and polymeric structures. Discuss about sugars, starch and cellulose. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA. Two carbon units and lipids.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes Convey that without catalysis life would not have existed on earth Enzymology: How to monitor enzyme catalyzed reactions. How does an enzyme catalyze reactions. Enzyme classification. Mechanism of enzyme action. Discuss at least two examples. Enzyme kinetics and kinetic parameters. Why should we know these parameters to understand biology? RNA catalysis.

units.title: Information Transfer
units.text: Information Transfer The molecular basis of coding and decoding genetic information is universal Molecular basis of information transfer. DNA as a genetic material. Hierarchy of DNA structure- from single stranded to double helix to nucleosomes. Concept of genetic code. Universality and degeneracy of genetic code. Define gene in terms of complementation and recombination.

units.title: Macromolecular analysis
units.text: Macromolecular analysis How to analyses biological processes at the reductionistic level Proteins- structure and function. Hierarch in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors and structural elements.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism The fundamental principles of energy transactions are the same in physical and biological world. Thermodynamics as applied to biological systems. Exothermic and endothermic versus endergonic and exergonic reactions. Concept of Keq and its relation to standard free energy. Spontaneity. ATP as an energy currency. This should include the breakdown of glucose to CO2 + H2O (Glycolysis and Krebs cycle) and synthesis of glucose from CO2 and H2O (Photosynthesis). Energy yielding and energy consuming reactions. Concept of Energy Charge.

units.title: Microbiology
units.text: Microbiology Concept of single celled organisms. Concept of species and strains. Identification and classification of microorganisms. Microscopy. Ecological aspects of single celled organisms. Sterilization and media compositions. Growth kinetics.

units.title: Measurement of Pressure and Vacuum
units.text: Measurement of Pressure and Vacuum: Importance of pressure and vacuum measurement, Range of high pressure & vacuum: Bourdon tubes, Dead weight pressure gauge tester, diaphragm gauge, LVDT, Piezo-electric pressure gauge, Low vacuum gauges - McLeod gauge, thermal conductivity gauge, Pirani gauge, Ionization gauge.

units.title: Strain Gauges
units.text: Strain Gauges: Classification, electrical strain gauge: working principle and types, gauge factor (analytical treatment), analysis of Wheatstone‟s network using strain gauges, mounting of strain gauges.

units.title: Metrology
units.text: Metrology: Definition and concept of metrology, standards of measurements, methods of measurement, precision and accuracy.

units.title: Linear Measurement
units.text: Linear Measurement: Line and end standards, Wavelength standards, Slip gauges, design and manufacture of gauges, Comparators: Types, construction and working of Mechanical, Optical, Electrical, Pneumatic comparators, Interferometry:- Basic principles, source of light, Optical flats, Fringe pattern and their interpretation

units.title: Angular Measurement
units.text: Angular Measurement: Angle standards, sine bar, angle gauges, autocollimator, angle Dekker, optical square, taper measurement, universal bevel protractor Surface finish Measurement: Surface texture, assessment of surface roughness, Tomlinson surface meter, and other surface measuring devices. Screw Thread Metrology: Screw thread terminology, measurement of thread parameters, study of thread gauges, floating carriage micrometer. Gear metrology: Gear profile and measurement of parameters, Study of Tool Maker‟s microscope and profile projector

units.title: Advances in Metrology
units.text: Advances in Metrology: coordinate measuring machine, universal measuring machine, application of lasers in measurement, machine vision system, computer aided inspection.

text_books: 1. Nakra and Chowdhury (2009), “Measurement and Control”, 3 Edition, Tata McGraw Hill. 2. R. K. Jain (2012), “Engineering Metrology”, Khanna Publishers. 3. T. G. Buckwith and N. L. Beck (1991), “Mechanical Measurements”, Addison Wesley classic
reference_books: 1. A K. Sawhney (2002), “Electrical and Electronic Measurements and Instrumentation”, Dhanpat Rai and Sons. 2. E.O. Doebelin and D. N. Manik (2010), “Doebelin's Measurement Systems”, 6th Edition, Mc Graw Hill.

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives:  To understand the basics of links, mechanisms and machines.  To provide knowledge of motion analysis of mechanisms.  To impart knowledge of machine components like flywheel, belt, ropes and chains.

outcomes.text: Illustrate kinetics and kinematics, classification of pairs based on relative motion and explain inversion of chains.
Calculate the velocity and acceleration of given mechanisms graphically and analytically.
Analyze the static and dynamic forces of flywheel for reciprocating prime movers and machines.
Select the machine components like belt, ropes and chains for required mechanisms.

units.title: Kinematics
units.text: Kinematics: Basics (Mechanism and Machines, Rigid and resistant body, Link), Classification Kinematics pairs. Limitations of Grubler‟s Criteria. Mobility and range of movement - Kutzbach and Grubler’s criterion, Grashof’s criterion Inversion of chain: mechanisms, quick return mechanism, applications. Four bar chain, Single slider crank chain, Double slider crank chain. Special Mechanisms: Straight line generating Mechanisms: Paucellier‟s and Hart‟s exact Straight Line Generating Mechanisms, Watt‟s Approximate straight line mechanics, Grass-hopper mechanism. Pantograph, Hook joint- single and double, Steering gear mechanisms – Ackerman, Davis.

units.title: Synthesis of Mechanisms
units.text: Synthesis of Mechanisms: Introduction, design a mechanism to obtain specified motions (type synthesis, number synthesis and dimensional synthesis), graphical methods. Velocity and Acceleration analysis: (Graphical approach) Velocity analysis: instantaneous centre of rotation method, relative velocity method, rubbing velocities at joints, mechanical advantage. Velocity and Acceleration analysis - relative method including kinematic pairs, Coriolis components of acceleration.

units.title: Static and dynamic force analysis
units.text: Static and dynamic force analysis: slider crank mechanisms neglecting mass of connecting rod and crank, engine force analysis, Turning moment on crank shaft. Flywheel and its applications, Fluctuation in energy, function of flywheel, estimating inertia of flywheel for reciprocating prime movers and machines.

units.title: Belts and Ropes
units.text: Belts and Ropes: Types of belts, velocity ratio, slip and creep of belt, length of belt for open and cross systems, law of belting, dynamic analysis- driving tensions, centrifugal tension, initial tension, condition of maximum power transmission.

text_books: 1. Ratan S. S (2014), “Theory of Machines”, 4th Edition, Tata McGrew Hill, New Delhi. 2. Thomas Beven (2009), “Theory of Machines”, 3rd Edition, Pearson.
reference_books: 1. J. E. Shigley (2003),” Theory of Mechanisms and Machines”, 3rd Edition, University Press. 2. P. L. Ballaney (2005),”Theory of Machines and Mechanisms”, 24th Edition, Khanna Publishing, New Delhi. 3. Ghosh and Malick (1988), ” Theory of Mechanisms and Machines”, East West Press Pvt. Ltd. 4. R. S. Hartenberg, J. Denavit, (1964), “ Kinematic synthesis of linkages (Mechanical engineering Series), Mc Graw-Hill Inc., US

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives:  To provide basic understanding of different material removal processes.  To explain the mechanics of cutting with single point, multi-point and multi edge cutting tools.  To introduce the basics of different nonconventional machining processes.

outcomes.text: Illustrate the metal cutting process with tool geometry and forces of cutting.
Select appropriate type of manufacturing process for given design.
Assess different non-conventional processes for their suitability in an industrial application.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Need of Material Removing Processes; Material Removal Rate; Design for Manufacturing; Break-Even Analysis. Metal cutting: Tool Geometry, forces in single point cutting, tool wear and tool life, formation of chips and types of chips, Mechanics of orthogonal and oblique cutting, chip thickness ratio, velocity relationship in orthogonal cutting, Merchant‟s circle diagram.

units.title: Cutting tool and tool life
units.text: Cutting tool and tool life: Analysis of stresses and strains and work done during metal cutting, friction and thermal aspects of metal cutting. Faliure of cutting tools, Mechanisms and pattern of cutting tool wear and tool life. Taylor‟s tool life equation, cutting tool materials of common use, advanced cutting tool materials. Control of cutting temperature and Cutting fluid application, Types of Cutting Fluids.

Shaper and Planer: Introduction, working and operations performed on Shapers, Planers & slotters. Milling Machines: Types of milling machines, tools and their geometry, various operations on milling machine, different attachments including dividing heads and work holding devices, MRR.

units.title: Drilling Machines
units.text: Drilling Machines: Types of machines, operations such as drilling, boring, reaming, spot facing, counter boring and sinking, tapping, drill speed and feeds, MRR. Boring and Broaching Machine: Classification-horizontal and vertical boring machine, types of broaching machines, advantages, limitations and applications of broaching.

units.title: Abrasive Machining Processes
units.text: Abrasive Machining Processes: Mechanics of grinding, types and operations of grinding machines, Centreless grinding, Grinding wheel specifications and its selection, Truing and dressing of wheels, Super finishing processes such as lapping and honing. Abrasive jet machining (AJM) and Abrasive water jet machining (AWJM).

units.title: Nonconventional Machining processes
units.text: Nonconventional Machining processes: Mechanical, chemical and thermal energy based nonconventional machining processes, Electric discharge machining (EDM), Electro-chemical machining (ECM), Electron Beam Machining (EBM), applications of different Nonconventional machining processes, Laser Beam Machining.

units.title: Processing of Plastics
units.text: Processing of Plastics: General aspects, methods of processing of plastics, compression moulding, transfer moulding, injection moulding, roto-moulding, blow moulding, thermoforming, Joining of thermoplastics, rules for design of plastic parts.

text_books: 1. Rao P. N. (2013), “Manufacturing Technology- Vol II”, 4th Edition Tata McGraw Hill. 2. Sharma P. C. (2012), “A Text Book of Production Engineering”, S Chand. 3. Kalpakjian S. and Schmid S. R. (2014), “Manufacturing Engineering and Technology”, 7th Edition, Pearson.
reference_books: 1. Chapman W. A. J. (2005), “Workshop Technology-Vol I, II, and III”, ELBS Publishers. 2. Chatopadhyaya A. B (2011), “Machining and Machine Tools”, Wiley India. 3. Lal G. K. and Choudhury S.K. (2005), “Fundamentals of Manufacturing Processes”, Alpha Science International.

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Workshop / Manufacturing Practices (BTME02011), Machine Shop - I (BTME04013)
objectives:  To practices machining of flat surfaces on shaping and grinding machines.  To practices milling, boring and screw cutting operations (both on internal and external surfaces).

outcomes.text: Understand the requirements for assembling jobs with different types of operations.
Operate different types of machines such as milling, shaping and grinding.
Practice different machining operations to create an assembly of jobs.

units.text: One composite job consisting minimum four parts employing operations on lathe, precision turning, external and internal threading, boring.
Shaping, milling, grinding & Knurling operations on composite job.
Demo on machining of Glass Fiber Reinforcement Plastic (GFRP) composite material, Drilling and edge milling operation,
Demonstration and job of CNC machine.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mechanics, Materials Engineering, and Strength of Materials
objectives: This course is designed to encourage the students to apply scientific information and imagination for the development of new improved machines or mechanical systems. It also helps to design the machine components using concepts of stress analysis, theories of failure and materials science.

outcomes.text: Articulate the design procedure and selection of material for a specific application
Design machine elements such as cotter joints, knuckle joints, and levers subjected to axial loads
Apply design methodologies to develop shafts, keys, and couplings for industrial applications
Analyse different types of power screws based on their load-carrying capacity, efficiency, and application suitability
Design various springs considering strength, stiffness
Evaluate the performance of fasteners and welded joints under various loading conditions

units.title: Fundamentals of Design
units.text: Fundamentals of Design Basic procedure, sources of design data, use of standards, synthesis and creativity, material selection, factor of safety, service factor, stress concentration, theories of failure, maximum normal stress theory, maximum shear stress, maximum distortion energy theory.

units.title: Design of Simple Machine Parts
units.text: Design of Simple Machine Parts Cotter joint, knuckle joint, levers, and turn buckle.

units.title: Design of Shafts
units.text: Design of Shafts ASME code, design of shaft on strength and torsional rigidity basis, design of transmission shaft. Design of Keys Saddle, sunk, feather, and woodruff. Design of Coupling Muff, flange, flexible and bush pin coupling.

units.title: Power Screws
units.text: Power Screws Forms of thread, multiple threads, torque analysis with square and trapezoidal threads, self-locking, collar friction torque, stresses in power screw, screw jack.

units.title: Spring Design
units.text: Spring Design Types applications and material for springs, stress and deflection equation of helical spring, design of helical compression, spring in series and parallel, leaf spring design.

units.title: Design of Fasteners
units.text: Design of Fasteners Bolted joints, riveted joints, and welded joints. Design for transverse and eccentric loading.

text_books: 1. J. F. Shigley, Mechanical Engineering Design, 13th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2014. 2. V. B. Bhandari, Design of Machine Elements, 5th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Publication, 2020.
reference_books: 1. M. F. Spotts, Design of Machine Elements, 8th Edition, Pearson Publication, 2019. 2. PSG design data book PSG college-Kalaikathir Achchagam, Coimbatore, 2020.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech Mechanical Engineering
objectives: This course aims to introduce the students to the fundamentals of material removal processes including non-conventional machining processes. The students will be able to identify/control the appropriate process parameters and possible defects of manufacturing processes.

outcomes.text: Classify the metal cutting processes with tool geometry and forces of cutting
Choose appropriate method of machining, to produce required geometrical features in components
Analyze various process parameters that affect machining processes

units.title: Metal cutting
units.text: Metal cutting Tool Geometry, forces in single point cutting, tool wear and tool life, formation of chips and types of chips, mechanics of orthogonal and oblique cutting, chip thickness ratio, velocity relationship in orthogonal cutting, Merchant’s circle diagram, analysis of stresses and strains and work done during metal cutting, friction and thermal aspects of metal cutting, cutting fluids, types of cutting fluids

units.title: Shaper and Planer
units.text: Shaper and Planer Introduction, construction, working and operations performed on Shapers, Planers and slotters. Milling Machines Types of milling machines, tools and their geometry, various operations on milling machine.

units.title: Drilling Machines
units.text: Drilling Machines Types of machines, operations such as drilling, boring, reaming, spot facing, counter boring and sinking, tapping, drill speed and feeds. Boring and Broaching Machine Classification-horizontal and vertical boring machine, types of broaching machines, advantages, limitations and applications of broaching.

units.title: Non-conventional Machining Processes
units.text: Non-conventional Machining Processes Introduction, classification and overview of non-conventional machining processes, abrasive jet machining (AJM), abrasive water jet machining (AWJM), electric discharge machining (EDM), electro-chemical machining (ECM), laser beam machining and allied processes

units.title: Processing of Plastics
units.text: Processing of Plastics General aspects, methods of processing of plastics, compression moulding, transfer moulding, injection moulding, thermoforming, Joining of thermoplastic.

text_books: 1. Rao P.N, Manufacturing Technology Volume 2, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2018. 2. Kalpakjian S and Schmid S. R, Manufacturing Engineering and Technology, 7th Edition, Pearson, 2018.
reference_books: 1. Chattopadhyay A. B, Machining and Machine Tools, 2nd Edition, Wiley India, 2017. 2. DeGarmo, Black and Kosher, Materials and Process in Manufacturing, 12th Edition, Wiley India, 2017.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mechanics, Partial Differential Equations and Laplace transforms
objectives: The course is aimed at delivering detailed understanding of fluid properties and their static - dynamic nature. This course teaches the analytical techniques necessary for grasping fundamental behavior of incompressible fluids. It is designed for the students to learn the principles of laminar flow, turbulent flow, and boundary layer theory to solve important practical problems.

outcomes.text: Explain fundamental fluid properties and differentiate between various types of fluids and flow behaviour
Analyze the principles of fluid statics, buoyancy, and flotation, and apply them to real-world engineering problems
Apply fluid kinematics and dynamics principles to characterize fluid motion and solve engineering problems
Analyze laminar and turbulent flows in pipes, including velocity distribution, shear stress, and pressure losses
Estimate energy losses in pipes and pipe network performance for different flow configurations
Analyze boundary layer formation, thickness, separation, and drag forces in external flow applications

units.title: Fluid Properties
units.text: Fluid Properties Concept of continuum, fluid properties, Classification of fluid, Newton’s law of viscosity, stress-strain relationship.

units.title: Fluid Statics
units.text: Fluid Statics Basic hydrostatic equation, Pascal’s Law, application to Manometers and mechanical gauges, hydrostatic forces on plane and curved submerged surfaces. Buoyancy and Floatation Archimedes’ Principle, buoyancy force and centre of buoyancy, metacentre, metacentric height, analytical method to find metacentric height, condition of equilibrium of submerged bodies, oscillation of a floating body

units.title: Fluid Kinematics
units.text: Fluid Kinematics Description of fluid motion-Lagrangian method and Euler’s method, classification of flow types- steady and unsteady, uniform and non-uniform, laminar and turbulent, one two and three- dimensional flow, rotational and irrotational, laminar and turbulent, compressible and incompressible. Flow patterns- stream lines, path lines, stream tubes and streak lines. Continuity equation (Cartesian and polar co-ordinates), circulation and vorticity, velocity potential and stream function.

units.title: Fluid Dynamics
units.text: Fluid Dynamics Euler’s equation of motion, Bernoulli’s equation and its applications-venturimeter, orificemeter, rotameter, pitot tube, Impulse-Momentum equation and its applications, Reynolds Transport Theorem and its application. Dimensional Analysis Secondary or derived quantities, Reyleigh method, Buckingham−𝜋theorem, dimensionless numbers, Theory of similarity, Model laws.

units.title: Laminar Flow
units.text: Laminar Flow Navier-Stokes equation of motion, developing expression for flow rate, pressure drop, shear stress, friction factor. Flow of viscous fluid in circular pipes- Hagen Poiseuille law, Couette flow. Turbulent Flow Shear stresses in turbulent flow, theories of turbulent shear stress, hydro-dynamically smooth and rough surface, modeling of turbulence, Moody’s chart. Flow Through Pipes Energy losses in pipes: Minor and Major losses, Darcy-Weisbatch equation for head loss in pipes, hydraulic gradient lines, and total energy lines, pipes in series and parallel, Equivalent pipe.

units.title: Boundary Layer Theory
units.text: Boundary Layer Theory Concept of Boundary layer, Boundary layer over flat plate, Boundary Layer thickness, momentum thickness, displacement thickness and energy thickness. Boundary layer equations and their solutions. Blasius solution (without derivation), Von-Karman momentum integral equation. Laminar boundary layer and turbulent boundary layer. Separation and control and Concept of drag.

text_books: 1. Frank M. White, Fluid Mechanics, 7th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2011. 2. S.K. Som, G.Biswas, S. Chakraborty, Introduction to Fluid Mechanics and Fluid Machines, 3rd Edition (revised), TMH Delhi, 2015.
reference_books: 1. John F. Douglas, Fluid Mechanics, 6th Edition, Pearson Education, 2011. 2. K.L. Kumar, Engineering Fluid Mechanics, 3rd Edition, S. Chand, 2016. 3. P.N. Modi, S.M. Seth, Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics including Hydraulic Machines, 19th Edition, Rajsons Publications, 2015. 4. K. Subrmanyan, Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic Machines: Problems and Solutions, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2019. 5. R.V. Giles, J.B. Evett, Cheng Liu, Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics, 4th Edition, Schaum Outline Series, McGraw Hill, 2013.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to appraise the students with different types of wastes and defects during manufacturing and the remedial steps to eliminate them. It imparts knowledge associated with aligning production processes with customer expectations and benchmark with efficient business processes.

outcomes.text: Summarize the relationship between Work in Progress and cycle time
Articulate the integration of batch size, setup, manufacturing processes and waste
Apply lean manufacturing techniques to manufacturing, projects and service industries

units.title: Introduction to Lean Manufacturing
units.text: Introduction to Lean Manufacturing History of lean, fundamental purpose of lean manufacturing, comparison to other methods. The seven Wastes, their causes and the effects, Implication of lean manufacturing – traditional vs lean manufacturing.

Tools of Lean Manufacturing 5S Principles, workplace organization, Process mapping / Value stream mapping, pull Systems (Kanban and WIP systems), error proofing and set-up reduction, total quality management (TQM), total productive maintenance (TPM), Toyota production systems, Ford production systems.

units.title: Value Stream Mapping (VSM)
units.text: Value Stream Mapping (VSM) Preparation for building a current state VSM, building a current state map (principles, concepts, loops, and methodology). Application to the factory simulation scenario. Line balancing, Poka Yoke, kanban, overall equipment effectiveness.

units.title: Just - In - time Manufacturing (JIT)
units.text: Just - In - time Manufacturing (JIT) Introduction, elements of JIT, uniform production rate, pull vs push method, kanban system, small lot size, quick and inexpensive set-up, continuous Improvement, optimized production technology.

units.title: Designing for Quality
units.text: Designing for Quality Introduction to concurrent engineering, quality function deployment (QFD) and failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA), concept, methodology and application (with case studies). Quality in service sectors: Characteristics of service sectors, quality dimensions in service sectors, measuring quality in different service sectors.

units.title: Six Sigma
units.text: Six Sigma Meaning of six sigma, why six sigma? six sigma improvement model, DMAIC and DMADV principle, building six sigma organization and culture, six sigma application, case studies.

units.title: Quality Circle
units.text: Quality Circle Quality circle structure, it’s operation, characteristics of quality circle, developing quality circle in organization, basic problem-solving techniques.

text_books: 1. M.K. Khanduja, Lean Manufacturing Implementation made easy, Inversio Solutions LLP, 2021. 2. Pascal Dennis, Lean Production Simplified, 3rd Edition, CRC Press, 2015.
reference_books: 1. James Edge, Lean Six Sigma, Bravex Publications, 2020. 2. Jeffrey K. Liker, The Toyota way, 2nd Edition, McGraw Hill Publications, 2021.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course covers alternative fuels and the analysis of their properties. The course also provides a comprehensive overview of the recent advances in the production and utilization aspects of different types of liquid and gaseous alternative fuels.

outcomes.text: Understand the need for alternative fuels, their availability, and standard properties
Compare and analyze the properties, combustion characteristics, and emissions of liquid and gaseous alternative fuels
Evaluate the performance and emission characteristics of alternative fuels
Conduct an experimental analysis of alternative fuels
Assess fuel quality and properties

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Estimation of petroleum reserve, need for alternate fuels, availability and properties of alternate fuels, American Society for Testing of Materials (ASTM) standards.

units.title: Liquid Fuels
units.text: Liquid Fuels Petroleum based liquid fuels and refining. Liquid Alternative Fuels Alcohols, general use of alcohols, properties as engine fuel, gasoline and alcohol blends, performance in spark ignition engine, methanol and gasoline blend, combustion characteristics in engine, emission characteristics. algae as a source for fuels. Vegetable Oils Soybean oil, jatropha, pongamia, rice bran, mahua etc. as alternate fuel and their properties, esterification of oils, biodiesel and emulsified fuels, lubricating oils composition and effect of alternate fuels.

units.title: Gaseous Alternative Fuels
units.text: Gaseous Alternative Fuels Hydrogen production, hydrogen as an alternative fuel, fuel cell, availability of compressed natural gas, properties and modification required to use in engines, performance and emission characteristics of compressed natural and liquefied natural gas in spark ignition and compression ignition engines, dimethyl ether, and hythane as an alternative fuel.

units.title: Analysis of Gaseous Bio-fuel
units.text: Analysis of Gaseous Bio-fuel Determination of methane, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, hydrogen sulphide, hydrogen in biogas, volatile fatty acid (VFA) and its constituents, alkalinity (total and partial), biological oxygen demand (BOD), Chemical oxygen demand (COD) and conversion efficiency.

units.title: Analysis of Fuel Qualities/Properties
units.text: Analysis of Fuel Qualities/Properties Bomb calorimeter, Junker’s calorimeter, flash point, pour point, viscosity, kinematic viscosity, acid value, saponification, fatty acid composition, iodine value, cetane index, octane value, oxidative stability and shelf life determination.

text_books: 1. Sergio Capareda, Introduction to Biomass Energy Conversions, CRC Press, 2013. 2. Colin R. Ferguson, Allan T. Kirkpatrick, Internal Combustion Engines: Applied Thermosciences, Wiley, 2015.)
reference_books: 1. Sunggyu Lee, James G. Speight, Sudarshan K. Loyalka, Handbook of Alternative Fuel Technologies, CRC Press, 2018. 2. Akhilendra Pratap Singh, Avinash Kumar Agarwal, Nirendra N. Mustafi, Yogesh C. Sharma, Alternative Fuels and Their Utilization Strategies in Internal Combustion Engines, Springer Singapore, 2019. 3. Kurt Marcel, “Alternative Fuels and Petroleum Technology”, Syrawood Publishing House 2016.
lab_work: 8 to 10 Tutorial exercises based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to acquaint students with control of mechanical operations, sensors and their interfacing with microcontrollers. The course offers learning of pneumatic/hydraulic systems, electrical controls and programmable logic controllers.

outcomes.text: Identify the suitable sensors and actuators for a mechatronics systems using pneumatic and hydraulic systems and electro-pneumatic circuits
Apply suitable logic controls and develop ladder logic programming
Design an appropriate robot for given industrial applications and carryout kinematic analysis for a robot

units.title: Introduction to Automation
units.text: Introduction to Automation Definition and fundamentals of automation, reasons for automating, basic elements of an automated system, power, program and control system. Introduction of mechatronics and its block diagram representation, key elements of mechatronics, applications of mechatronics, domestic, industrial etc. Representation of mechatronic system in block diagram and concept of transfer function for each element of mechatronic system, reduction methods and its numerical treatment for represented block diagram.

units.title: Selection of Sensors and Actuators
units.text: Selection of Sensors and Actuators Criteria for selection of sensors based on requirements, principle of measurement, sensing method, performance chart etc. Displacement, temperature, acceleration, force, pressure based on static and dynamic characteristics. Actuators, selection of actuators based on principle of operation, performance characteristics, maximum loading conditions, safety etc. Principle and selection of mechano- electrical actuators, DC motors, stepper motors, solenoid actuators, servo motors, BLDC.

units.title: Pneumatics and Hydraulics
units.text: Pneumatics and Hydraulics Hydraulic and pneumatic devices, different types of valves, actuators and auxiliary elements in pneumatics and hydraulics, their applications and use of their ISO symbols, synthesis and design of circuits (up to 2 cylinders) pneumatic, electro- pneumatics and hydraulics, electrohydraulic. Discrete control system, Programming Logic Control (PLC). Introduction to PLC, architecture, ladder logic programming for different types of logic gates, latching, timers, counter, practical examples of ladder programming.

units.title: Introduction to Robotics
units.text: Introduction to Robotics Definition of robot, evolution of robots, laws of robots, international robotic standards, types of robots, selection of robots, robot classifications, degrees of freedom, robot configuration, accuracy and repeatability, specification of a robot. Robot feedback controls, point to point control and continuous path control, control system for robot joint, adaptive control, actuators and sensors, drives and transmission systems, end effectors, applications of robots.

units.title: Analysis of Robots
units.text: Analysis of Robots Grubler - kutzbach criterion, denavit - hartneberg classic algorithm for reference frames, homogeneous coordinate transformation, the homogeneous coordinate transformation matrix, the arm matrix. Kinematics of robots, forward kinematics, inverse kinematics, simple robots, 2D cartesian robot, 2D polar robot, differential robot, geared wrists and grippers.

units.title: Modeling and Simulation
units.text: Modeling and Simulation SCARA robot, deriving equations of motion, simulation of equations of motion for relevant robots. Humanoids wheeled and legged, legged locomotion and balance, arm movement and control, performance, interaction, safety and robustness, applications, case studies.

text_books: 1. W. Bolton, Mechatronics: Electronic Control Systems in Mechanical Engineering, 6th edition, Pearson education, 2015. 2. Robert J. Schilling, Fundamentals of Robotics: Analysis and Control, 1st edition, Pearson education, 2015.
reference_books: 1. Clarence W. De Silva, Farbod Khoshnoud, Saman K. Halgamuge, Maoqing Li, Mechatronics: Fundamentals and Applications, CRC press London, 2015. 2. Rany Rizk, Mariette Awad, Mechanism, Machine, Robotics and Mechatronics Sciences, Springer international publishing, 2018.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course aims to prepare students to develop self-learning attitude, practical knowledge of programming language/modern technology according to the engineering applications.

outcomes.text: Implement the use of basics Python syntax
Create Graphical user interface in Python
Implement open source numerical libraries to build engineering applications

units.title: Introduction to Python
units.text: Introduction to Python Installation and Working with Python, Understanding Python variables Python basic Operators, Understanding python blocks, Python Data Types: Declaring and using Numeric data types: integers, float, complex, Using string data type and string operations.

units.title: Control Flow
units.text: Control Flow If, if-elif-else, loops, for loop using ranges, string, Use of while loops in python, Loop manipulation using pass, continue, break and else, Programming using Python conditional and loops block, Python arrays.

units.title: Data Structures
units.text: Data Structures List Operations, Slicing, Methods; Tuples, Sets, Dictionaries, Sequences. Comprehensions, Dictionary manipulation, list and dictionary in build functions

units.title: Functions
units.text: Functions Calling Functions, Passing Arguments, Keyword Arguments, Default Arguments, Variable-length arguments, Anonymous Functions, Fruitful Functions (Function Returning Values), Scope of the Variables in a Function - Global and Local Variables. Powerful Lamda function in python.

units.title: Numpy & Pandas
units.text: Numpy & Pandas Introduction to Numpy, Create 1D array & 2D array, Introduction to pandas, Pandas data structure:- series , data frame

text_books: 1. Allen B. Downey, Think Python: How to Think Like a Computer Scientist, 2nd edition, O‘Reilly Publishers, 2016. 2. Vamsi Kurama, Python Programming: A Modern Approach, 2nd edition, Pearson, 2018.
reference_books: 1. Kenneth A. Lambert, Fundamentals of Python, 2nd edition, Course Technology Inc, 2018. 2. Mark Lutz, Learning Python, 5th edition, O’Rielly Publishers, 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The CAD Fundamental Processes course aims to introduce students to the NX platform, providing hands- on experience with its interface and essential commands. It focuses on developing an understanding of design intent, model creation, and geometry evaluation. Students will learn to generate accurate 2D drawings and explore drafting techniques. Additionally, the course covers 3D modeling, visualization, and engineering graphics concepts to enhance their CAD proficiency.

outcomes.text: Gain the experience about the NX platform.
Understand NX software its interface and command use.
Understand design intent, model development and geometry evaluation.
Learn about how to produce 2D drawings and drafting methods.
Learn about how to produce 3D views and Engineering Graphics concepts and drafting methods.

units.title: Introduction to NX and User Interface
units.text: Introduction to NX and User Interface: Work with NX part files and NX template files, understand how to effectively use the NX user interface and work space, create sketches to capture design intent, create reference geometry for model development such as datum planes, axes, and coordinate systems.

units.title: Creating Basic Features and Geometry in NX
units.text: Creating Basic Features and Geometry in NX: Create basic features by sweeping and extruding geometry, analyze feature geometry, add detail to features such as blends and drafts, produce assemblies of component parts, produce annotated 2D drawings of models.

units.title: Advanced Part Modeling and Feature Editing in NX
units.text: Advanced Part Modeling and Feature Editing in NX: Working with existing parts, datum features, swept features, trim Body, hole features, expressions.

units.title: Coordinate Systems and Part Navigation in NX
units.text: Coordinate Systems and Part Navigation in NX: Coordinate systems, part navigator, associative copies, face and edge operations, basic freeform.

units.title: NX Assembly Design
units.text: NX Assembly Design: Constraints, References, and Modifications Creating and modifying assemblies, assembly constraints, assembly arrangements, reference sets, interpart geometry and references, component arrays, reuse library, revise and replace components.

text_books: 1 Sham Tickoo, Siemens NX 12.0 for Designers, 11th Edition, CADCIM Technologies, 2018.

objectives: The course deals with the design of marine structures subjected to different types of environmental loads and also discusses the detailed design of major and sub components of offshore structures.

Relate the physical problem of the fluid–structure interaction in marine structures
Design different structural components in offshore applications

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The main objective of this course is to provide basic understanding of composite materials used in various engineering applications. The course also explains mechanical properties, micromechanics and manufacturing methods of composite materials.

outcomes.text: Relate processing, characterization and applications of various composite materials
Apply failure criteria and evaluate the results of composite materials
Evaluate the relative merits of using alternatives (corresponding to various simple and composite materials) for important engineering and other applications

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Definition, history, characteristics, concept of composite materials, comparison with metals, composite materials in engineering, industrial scenario, advantages and limitations of composites

units.title: Types of Matrix Materials and Reinforcements

units.title: Types of Composites
units.text: Types of Composites Based on matrix materials, polymer matrix composites (PMC), metal matrix composites (MMC), ceramic matrix composites (CMC), carbon fiber composites; based on reinforcements, fiber reinforced composites, fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) composites, laminated composites, particulate composites, polymer matrix composites (PMC) – processing, structure and properties, applications, metal matrix composites (MMC) – types, processing, properties, applications, ceramic matrix composites (CMC) - processing, properties, applications, carbon fiber composites - processing, properties, applications.

units.title: Micromechanics and Macromechanics of Composites

units.title: Monotonic Strength and Fracture

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course focusses on the application of classical mechanics to various biological problems by combining the fields of biology and physiology. This course is concerned with the application of principles of mechanics to the conceptualization, design, development and analysis of equipment and systems as applied to human body.

outcomes.text: Correlate mechanics, biomechanics and kinesiology and differentiate between their uses in the analysis of human movement
Relate the reference positions, planes, and axes associated with the human body
Evaluate the skeletal considerations for movement and the different mechanics involved in bones

units.title: Basic Terminology

units.title: Kinematic Concepts for Analyzing Human Motion

units.title: Applications of Statics to Biomechanics

program: B Tech (Mechanical & Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Manufacturing Processes I and II, Machine Drawing
objectives: The objective of the course is to impart introductory knowledge of Additive Manufacturing (AM) and its capabilities in the modern digital manufacturing industries. The course is structured to acquaint the students with the operating principles and applications of most prominent technologies in the field of additive manufacturing.

outcomes.text: Compare the fundamental principles of various additive manufacturing technologies in terms of material requirements, manufacturing technologies and applications
Identify critical areas where AM can be applied to create value for the product
Apply the necessary skills in selecting the right AM process for a given application

units.title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
units.text: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing Introduction to AM, history of AM, definition, distinction between AM, CNC & other digital manufacturing techniques, reasons to use AM, classifications of AM processes, design for additive manufacturing (DfAM), AM industry: present and future, AM process chain, AM file formats (STL, 3MF, AMF, PLY, VRML, and LEO), part orientation, support generation, model slicing, contour generation, machine set-up, build file preparation.

units.title: Classification of Additive Manufacturing Techniques
units.text: Classification of Additive Manufacturing Techniques Material Extrusion: Process mechanism, process parameters, extrusion of: ceramics, metals, biomaterials, composites, contour crafting, concrete printing Vat Polymerization: Process mechanism, process parameters, advantages, disadvantages, applications, Digital Light Processing (DLP), recent advances, Large-Scale Rapid Liquid Printing. Binder & material jetting processes: Binder jetting process workflow, material requirements, binder-powder interaction, binder properties. Material Jetting process workflow, thermal and piezoelectric inkjet, material jetting fluid mechanics, drop-on-demand and continuous methods of MJ. Powder bed fusion AM process: Selective laser sintering (SLS), process mechanism, process parameters, selective laser melting (SLM), process workflow and material requirements, powder melting mechanisms, electron beam melting (EBM) process. Sheet Lamination AM Processes: Process mechanism, process parameters, ultrasonic additive manufacturing (UAM), ultrasonic welding fundamentals, UAM process parameters Directed Energy Deposition (DED) Processes: Process workflow, materials feeding for DED: powder (Laser Engineered Net Shaping) and wire, process parameters, cold spray.

objectives: The advent of modern technology and fourth Industrial revolution, particularly the industrial Internet of things, has brought enormous changes to the manufacturing industry. Relate sensing principles and Wireless Sensor Network
Create IoT applications for smart machines

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The CAD Advanced Processes course aims to enhance students' proficiency in the NX platform by introducing advanced commands and modeling techniques. It focuses on transitioning from sketches to 3D models, including raster image development. Students will gain expertise in face and edge operations, along with fundamental freeform modeling. Additionally, the course covers assembly modeling and the effective use of reference sets for complex designs.

outcomes.text: Gain the experience about the NX platform on advance commands.
Sketch to model and raster image development.
Understand face and edge operations and basics of freeform.
Learn assembly in models and using reference set.

objectives: The objective of this course is to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of industrial design principles and their application in modern manufacturing and engineering systems. The course also emphasizes aesthetic concepts, including form, style, and colour, and their influence on product appeal and usability.

Apply anthropometric data for product and system design

Summarize the different sustainable mobility technologies and smart transportation solutions

objectives: This course focusses on a critical understanding and strategic importance of operations management. The students can get familiar with interactions between firms based on parameters such as information sharing, contracting and coordination in supply chain management.

outcomes.text: Evaluate the application of operations management policies and techniques to the service sector as well as manufacturing firms
Analyze and organize Global Network Logistics for trade and transport systems, sourcing and procurement
Apply the latest developments in information technology to supply chain management in order to generate greater benefit

units.title: Production Concepts
units.text: Production Concepts Introduction, meaning, nature and scope of production and operations management. Difference between production and operations management. Productivity, factors affecting productivity and productivity measurement. Work study— Method study and work measurement. Production Technology – Types of manufacturing processes. Plant location and types of plant layout.

units.title: Material and Inventory Management
units.text: Material and Inventory Management Types of production planning, process of production planning and control (PPC) – routing, scheduling and loading. Master production schedule, aggregate production planning. Types of inventories, inventory control techniques- EOQ, ABC, VED, FSN, HML and SDE (Simple numerical problems on Inventory control techniques).

units.title: Building a Strategic Framework to Analyze Supply Chain

units.text: Warehouse and Transportation Management Concept of strategic storage, Warehouse functionality, Warehouse operating principles, Developing warehouse resources, Material handling and packaging in warehouse, Transportation management, Transport functionality and principles, Transport infrastructure, Transport economics and pricing, Transport decision making

units.text: IT in Supply Chain IT framework, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Internal supply chain management, supplier Relationship Management (SRM) and transaction management. program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering and Mechanical Engineering)

objectives: The objective of this course is to familiarize the students with the electric and hybrid vehicle architecture, technologies and fundamentals. The use of tools to design and simulate electric and hybrid vehicles is also covered.

outcomes.text: Explain electric and hybrid vehicle technology
Compare motors, batteries and controllers used in electric and hybrid vehicles
Analyze the overall system performance using key metrics
Simulate electric hybrid vehicle systems
Synthesize modern EV technology with specific requirement

units.title: Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Introduction
units.text: Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Introduction EVs and hybrids, correlation of cost and emissions, some myth busting facts, EV layouts and architecture, hybrid vehicle layouts

units.title: Vehicle Dynamics
units.text: Vehicle Dynamics Introduction, Forces acting on a Rolling vehicle, Power required for rolling motion, Modeling Real-World conditions.

units.title: Motors
units.text: Motors Introduction, the Lorentz Force law, Coulomb’s, Biot-Savarts law, brush and brushless motors, reluctance Motors, Faraday’s law, AC induction motors, motor efficiency, maximum acceleration.

units.title: Batteries
units.text: Batteries Introduction, battery fundamentals, lithium-ion batteries, battery characteristics, electric vehicle charging.

units.title: Controllers
units.text: Controllers Introduction, circuit elements, step-down DC controllers, step-up/down DC controllers, AC controllers.

units.title: Incentives and Barriers
units.text: Incentives and Barriers Introduction, national incentives, state incentives, FAME-I, FAME-II, e-AMRIT. Barriers to development of EV infrastructure in India.

units.title: Modeling and Simulation of Electric and Hybrid Vehicles
units.text: Modeling and Simulation of Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Fundamentals of vehicle system modeling, HEV Modeling using simulation software.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics.
objectives: 1. To provide a basic understanding of biological mechanisms of living organisms from the perspective of engineers. 2. To encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools.

outcomes.text: Convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are diverse.
Identify DNA as a genetic material in the molecular basis of information transfer.
Classify enzymes and distinguish between different mechanisms of enzyme action.
Apply thermodynamic principles to biological systems.
Identify and classify microorganisms.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Convey that Biology is as important a scientific discipline as Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry Bring out the fundamental differences between science and engineering by drawing a comparison between eye and camera, Bird flying and aircraft. Mention the most exciting aspect of biology as an independent scientific discipline. Why we need to study biology? Discuss how biological observations of 18th Century that lead to major discoveries. Examples from Brownian motion and the origin of thermodynamics by referring to the original observation of Robert Brown and Julius Mayor. These examples will highlight the fundamental importance of observations in any scientific inquiry.

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification Convey that classification per se is not what biology is all about. The underlying criterion, such as morphological, biochemical or ecological be highlighted. Hierarchy of life forms at phenomenological level. A common thread weaves this hierarchy Classification. Discuss classification based on (a) cellularity- Unicellular or multicellular (b) ultrastructure- prokaryotes or eucaryotes. (c) energy and Carbon utilization -Autotrophs, heterotrophs, lithotropes (d) Ammonia excretion – aminotelic, uricoteliec, ureotelic (e) Habitata- acquatic or terrestrial (e) Molecular taxonomy- three major kingdoms of life. A given organism can come under different category based on classification. Model organisms for the study of biology come from different groups. E.coli, S.cerevisiae, D. Melanogaster, C. elegance, A. Thaliana, M. musculus

units.title: Genetics
units.text: Genetics Convey that “Genetics is to biology what Newton’s laws are to Physical Sciences” Mendel’s laws, Concept of segregation and independent assortment. Concept of allele. Gene mapping, Gene interaction, Epistasis. Meiosis and Mitosis be taught as a part of genetics. Emphasis to be give not to the mechanics of cell division nor the phases but how genetic material passes from parent to offspring. Concepts of recessiveness and dominance. Concept of mapping of phenotype to genes. Discuss about the single gene disorders in humans. Discuss the concept of complementation using human genetics.

units.title: Biomolecules
units.text: Biomolecules Convey that all forms of life has the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are as diverse as one can imagine Molecules of life. In this context discuss monomeric units and polymeric structures. Discuss about sugars, starch and cellulose. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA. Two carbon units and lipids.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes Convey that without catalysis life would not have existed on earth Enzymology: How to monitor enzyme catalyzed reactions. How does an enzyme catalyze reactions. Enzyme classification. Mechanism of enzyme action. Discuss at least two examples. Enzyme kinetics and kinetic parameters. Why should we know these parameters to understand biology? RNA catalysis.

units.title: Information Transfer
units.text: Information Transfer The molecular basis of coding and decoding genetic information is universal Molecular basis of information transfer. DNA as a genetic material. Hierarchy of DNA structure- from single stranded to double helix to nucleosomes. Concept of genetic code. Universality and degeneracy of genetic code. Define gene in terms of complementation and recombination.

units.title: Macromolecular analysis
units.text: Macromolecular analysis How to analyses biological processes at the reductionistic level Proteins- structure and function. Hierarch in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors and structural elements.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism The fundamental principles of energy transactions are the same in physical and biological world. Thermodynamics as applied to biological systems. Exothermic and endothermic versus endergonic and exergonic reactions. Concept of Keq and its relation to standard free energy. Spontaneity. ATP as an energy currency. This should include the breakdown of glucose to CO2 + H2O (Glycolysis and Krebs cycle) and synthesis of glucose from CO2 and H2O (Photosynthesis). Energy yielding and energy consuming reactions. Concept of Energy Charge.

units.title: Microbiology
units.text: Microbiology Concept of single celled organisms. Concept of species and strains. Identification and classification of microorganisms. Microscopy. Ecological aspects of single celled organisms. Sterilization and media compositions. Growth kinetics.

text_books: 1. Arthur T. Johnson (2011) ‘’Biology For Engineers’’ CRC Press Taylor & Francis group 2. Microbiology, Prescott, L.M J.P. Harley and C.A. Klein 2008, 7th edition McGraw- Hill Higher Education
