program: B Tech/ MBA Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: The main purpose of this course is to introduce students with renewable energy resources availability, potential and suitability as a substitute for conventional energy resources in future energy demands.

outcomes.text: Identify sustainable energy solutions for sustainable development
Analyze renewable energy resources availability and utilization
Demonstrate competency in renewable systems analysis independently

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Renewable and non-renewable energy sources, global and Indian scenario. Energy Alternatives The solar option, nuclear option, tar sands and oil shale, tidal energy, geothermal energy.

units.title: Solar Energy
units.text: Solar Energy Solar radiation, availability, measurement and estimation, solar thermal conversion devices such as flat plate collector, tubular collector, solar air collector, solar concentrator and storage. Applications Crop drying, distillation, water heating, electric power generation. Solar Photovoltaic Photovoltaic cell technologies, generations of solar cell, electrical characteristics, photovoltaic module and array, photovoltaic module system components and design.

units.title: Biomass Energy Conversion
units.text: Biomass Energy Conversion Biomass characteristics and their availability, biofuel production processes, bio-methane, bio-hydrogen, alcoholic fermentation, biodiesel, microbial fuel cell, biomass based steam power plant, combined cycle power plant, cogeneration plant, Energy from Waste.

units.title: Wind Energy
units.text: Wind Energy Wind turbines, aerodynamics, types of turbines wind energy conversion system, wind turbine generator types, advantages and disadvantages. Hydro Power Water turbines, hydroelectric system theory, measurement and components, advantages and disadvantages of hydroelectric system.

units.title: Geothermal Energy
units.text: Geothermal Energy Structure of earth, geothermal resources, exploration of geothermal energy. OTEC Principle, applications. Tidal principle, power calculation, tidal modes of operation. Wave wave motion, energy conversion and devices applications.

units.title: Economic Analysis
units.text: Economic Analysis Initial and annual costs, present worth calculation, annual savings, payback period.

text_books: 1. Vaughn C. Nelson, Kenneth L. Starcher, Introduction to Renewable Energy (Energy and the Environment, CRC Press, UK, 2016. 2. B. K Khan, Non-Conventional Energy Resources, TMH New Delhi, 2013. 3. J. A. Duffie and W. A. Beckman, Solar Engineering of Thermal Processes, John Wiley, New York, 2013.
reference_books: 1. D. Y. Goswami, F. Kreith and J. F. Kreider, Principles of Solar Engineering, Taylor and Francis, Philadelphia, 2015. 2. S. P. Sukhatme, Solar Energy - Principles of thermal collection and storage, Tata McGraw-Hill, New Delhi, 2008. (Classic Book) 3. J. Twidell and T. Weir, Renewable Energy Resources, E & F N Spon Ltd, London, 1986. (Classic Book)

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS), B Tech & MBA Tech Mechanical, B Tech Mechatronics
objectives: The objective of the course is to familiarize with basic knowledge of Additive Manufacturing (AM) and its capabilities in the modern digital manufacturing industries. It teaches about various additive manufacturing techniques.

outcomes.text: Compare the fundamental principles of various additive manufacturing technologies in terms of material requirements, manufacturing technologies and applications
Identify critical areas where AM can be applied to create value for the product
Apply the necessary skills in selecting the right AM process for a given application

units.title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
units.text: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing Introduction to AM, history of AM, definition, distinction between AM, CNC & other digital manufacturing techniques, reasons to use AM, classifications of AM processes, design for additive manufacturing (DfAM), AM industry: present and future, AM process chain, AM file formats (STL, 3MF, AMF, PLY, VRML, and LEO), part orientation, support generation, model slicing, contour generation, machine set-up, build file preparation.

units.title: Classification of Additive Manufacturing Techniques
units.text: Classification of Additive Manufacturing Techniques Material Extrusion: Process mechanism, process parameters, extrusion of: ceramics, metals, biomaterials, composites, contour crafting, concrete printing Vat Polymerization: Process mechanism, process parameters, advantages, disadvantages, applications, Digital Light Processing (DLP), recent advances, Large-Scale Rapid Liquid Printing. Binder & material jetting processes: Binder jettng process workflow, material requirements, binder-powder interaction, binder properties. Material Jetting process workflow, thermal and piezoelectric inkjet, material jetting fluid mechanics, drop-on-demand and continuous methods of MJ. Powder bed fusion AM process: Selective laser sintering (SLS), process mechanism, process parameters, selective laser melting (SLM), process workflow and material requirements, powder melting mechanisms, electron beam melting (EBM) process. Sheet Lamination AM Processes: Process mechanism, process parameters, ultrasonic additive manufacturing (UAM), ultrasonic welding fundamentals, UAM process parameters Directed Energy Deposition (DED) Processes: Process workflow, materials feeding for DED: powder (Laser Engineered Net Shaping) and wire, process parameters, cold spray.

units.title: Post- Processing
units.text: Post- Processing Product quality evaluation, need for post-processing, support material removal, surface finish improvement, aesthetic improvement, property enhancements using non-thermal and thermal techniques.

units.title: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM)
units.text: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM) Design guidelines: part orientation, support, geometry considerations, layer thickness, part size, material consideration, residual stress, topology optimization, case studies on design for AM.

units.title: Applications of AM & Industry 4.0
units.text: Applications of AM & Industry 4.0 Aerospace, biomedical, defence, automobile, rapid tooling, reverse engineering, economic consideration, Industry 4.0 for AM, case studies on application of AM in various industries.

text_books: 1. Gibson I, Rosen D W, Stucker B, Additive Manufacturing Technologies: Rapid Prototyping to Direct Digital Manufacturing, 2nd Edition, Springer, 2015. 2. Filemon Schöffer, Ben Redwood, Brian Garret, The 3D Printing Handbook: Technologies, design and applications, 3D Hubs, 2017. References Books 1. Yang, L., Hsu, K., Baughman, B., Godfrey, D., Medina, F., Menon, M., & Wiener, S., Additive manufacturing of metals: the technology, materials, design and production, Springer, Edition 2017. 2. Gebhardt, Andreas, Understanding additive manufacturing, 2nd Edition, Hanser Publication, 2018.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: The objective of this course is to help the students understand the principles and applications relevant to the planning, design, and operations of manufacturing or service firms. This course also develops an understanding about quality management practices in organizations that facilitate organizational effectiveness.

outcomes.text: Develop an understanding of manufacturing and service operations management as a subject and outline the strategic concerns involved in operations decisions
Apply the principles, philosophy underpinning inventory management techniques, just- in-time and MRP systems along with their limitations
Analyze the economic aspects related to production management

units.title: Concept of Production Management
units.text: Concept of Production Management Meaning of production, production process system, scope of production management, objectives of production management, functions and scopes of production management, scope of production management, brief history of production management, responsibilities of production manager.

units.title: Productivity
units.text: Productivity Introduction, meaning of productivity, factors affecting on productivity, productivity improvement, measurement of productivity.

units.title: Economic Analysis
units.text: Economic Analysis Factors to be considered in product design. production cost concepts; fixed cost, variable cost, break even analysis, P-V chart, and make-buy decision.

units.title: Plant Location and Plant Layout
units.text: Plant Location and Plant Layout Meaning of plant layout, objective of a good plant layout, factors to be considered in plant location, types of plant layout, process layout. techniques of plant layout, concept of group technology, group layout.

units.title: Production Planning and Control (PPC)
units.text: Production Planning and Control (PPC) Objective of PPC, functions of PPC, capacity planning, manufacturing resource planning and scheduling, JIT system, Kanban pull system of scheduling, line balancing.

units.title: Materials Management
units.text: Materials Management Bill of materials, quantity planning, inventory control, economic order quantity (EOQ), lead time, consumption rate, different ordering systems, Q system, P system, the store’s function and ABC analysis.

units.title: Quality
units.text: Quality Introduction to quality control, quality management, function of quality, quality control stages, function of inspection, statistical quality control, statistical quality control, control charts, acceptance sampling.

text_books: 1. S. N. Chary, Production and Operations Management, 6th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2019. 2. Bedi Kanishka, Production and Operations Management, 3rd Edition, Oxford University Press, 2016.
reference_books: 1. S. Gupta and M. Starr, Introduction to Production and Operations Management, RC Press, 1st Edition, 2014. 2. R. Panneerselvam, Production and Operations Management, 3rd Edition, PHI Learning, 2012.

program: B Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: This course introduces aspects of project management such as formulation, budgeting, planning, scheduling and control of projects from initiation to completion.

outcomes.text: Interpret the project feasibility and identify the role of project manager
Relate the resources and durations using scheduling tools and techniques
Plan the costs and risks of projects
Apply the tools for monitoring the progress of projects

units.title: Introduction to Project Management
units.text: Introduction to Project Management Definition, classification of project management in different environments, scope, systems approach, project feasibility, project life cycle, systems development cycle phases.

units.title: Project Organization
units.text: Project Organization Project organization, types of structures, roles of project managers and team, integration in large scale projects.

units.title: Project Planning and Scheduling
units.text: Project Planning and Scheduling Planning fundamentals, project master plan, work breakdown structure and other tools of project planning, work packages, project organization structure and responsibilities, responsibility matrix, use of Gantt charts, critical path method (CPM) and project evaluation and review technique (PERT) for scheduling and resource allocation, introduction to software tools for documentation, scheduling, analysis etc.

units.title: Cost Estimating and Budgeting
units.text: Cost Estimating and Budgeting Cost estimating process, elements of budgeting, project cost accounting and management information systems, cost schedules and forecasts.

units.title: Project Risk Management
units.text: Project Risk Management Risk concepts and identification, risk response planning, risk management methods, information monitoring, control process, cost accounting systems for project control, performance analysis.

units.title: Evaluation and Termination
units.text: Evaluation and Termination Project evaluation and reporting, closing the contract.

text_books: 1. Jack R Meredith, Samuel J Mantel, Shafer Project Management –A Managerial Approach, 8th Edition, Wiley Publications, 2017. 2. Erik W Larson, Clifford F Gray, Rohit Joshi, Project Management the Managerial Process, 8th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Dennis Lock, The Essentials of Project and Programme Management, 4th Edition, Routledge Publications, 2017. 2. Prasanna Chandra, Projects: Planning, Analysis, Selection, Financing Implementation and Review, 8th Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017.

program: B Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: This course focusses on a critical understanding and strategic importance of operations management. The students can get familiar with interactions between firms based on parameters such as information sharing, contracting and coordination in supply chain management.

outcomes.text: Evaluate the application of operations management policies and techniques to the service sector as well as manufacturing firms
Analyze and organize Global Network Logistics for trade and transport systems, sourcing and procurement
Apply the latest developments in information technology to supply chain management in order to generate greater benefit

units.title: Production Concepts
units.text: Production Concepts Introduction, meaning, nature and scope of production and operations management. Difference between production and operations management. Productivity, factors affecting productivity and productivity measurement. Work study— Method study and work measurement. Production Technology – Types of manufacturing processes. Plant location and types of plant layout.

units.title: Material and Inventory Management
units.text: Material and Inventory Management Types of production planning, process of production planning and control (PPC) – routing, scheduling and loading. Master production schedule, aggregate production planning. Types of inventories, inventory control techniques- EOQ, ABC, VED, FSN, HML and SDE (Simple numerical problems on Inventory control techniques).

units.title: Building a Strategic Framework to Analyze Supply Chain
units.text: Building a Strategic Framework to Analyze Supply Chain Supply chain stages and decision phases, Process View of Supply Chain: Supply Chain Flows, Examples of Supply Chain, Competitive and Supply Chain Strategies, achieving strategic fit: Expanding strategic scope, Drivers of supply chain performance, Framework for structuring drivers: inventory, transportation facilities, information obstacles to achieving fit.

units.title: Designing the Supply Chain Network
units.text: Designing the Supply Chain Network Distribution networking: Role, Design, Supply Chain Network (SCN): Role, Factors, framework for design decisions.

units.title: Warehouse and Transportation Management
units.text: Warehouse and Transportation Management Concept of strategic storage, Warehouse functionality, Warehouse operating principles, Developing warehouse resources, Material handling and packaging in warehouse, Transportation management, Transport functionality and principles, Transport infrastructure, Transport economics and pricing, Transport decision making

units.title: IT in Supply Chain
units.text: IT in Supply Chain IT framework, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Internal supply chain management, supplier Relationship Management (SRM) and transaction management. Coordination in supply chain: Lack of supply chain coordination and the Bullwhip effect, Obstacle to coordination, Managerial levers, Building partnership and trust, Emerging trends and issues. Vendor managed inventory 3PL-4PL, Reverse logistics: Reasons, Role, Activities; RFID systems: Components, Applications, Implementation; Lean supply chain, Implementation of Six Sigma in supply chain, Green supply chain.

text_books: 1. Sunil Chopra, Peter Meindl, Supply Chain Management Strategy, Planning and Operations, 6th Edition, Pearson, 2016. 2. Chase, R.B., Shankar, R. & Jacobs, F.R., Operations & Supply Chain Management, 14th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Robert B. Handfield, Ernest L. Nichols, Introduction to Supply Chain Management, Prentice Hall PTR, 2007. (Classic Book) 2. Bedi, Kanishka, Production & Operations Management, 3rd Edition, Oxford University Press, 2013.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering and Mechanical Engineering)/ B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Calculus, Engineering Mechanics, Classical Physics
objectives: The objective of this course is to familiarize the students with the electric and hybrid vehicle architecture, technologies and fundamentals. The use of tools to design and simulate electric and hybrid vehicles is also covered.

outcomes.text: Explain electric and hybrid vehicle technology
Compare motors, batteries and controllers used in electric and hybrid vehicles
Simulate electric hybrid vehicle systems

units.title: Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Introduction
units.text: Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Introduction EVs and hybrids, correlation of cost and emissions, some myth busting facts, EV layouts and architecture, hybrid vehicle layouts

units.title: Vehicle Dynamics
units.text: Vehicle Dynamics Introduction, Forces acting on a Rolling vehicle, Power required for rolling motion, Modeling Real-World conditions.

units.title: Motors
units.text: Motors Introduction, the Lorentz Force law, Coulomb’s, Biot-Savarts law, brush and brushless motors, reluctance Motors, Faraday’s law, AC induction motors, motor efficiency, maximum acceleration.

units.title: Batteries
units.text: Batteries Introduction, battery fundamentals, lithium-ion batteries, battery characteristics, electric vehicle charging.

units.title: Controllers
units.text: Controllers Introduction, circuit elements, step-down DC controllers, step-up/down DC controllers, AC controllers.

units.title: Incentives and Barriers
units.text: Incentives and Barriers Introduction, national incentives, state incentives, FAME-I, FAME-II, e-AMRIT. Barriers to development of EV infrastructure in India.

units.title: Modeling and Simulation of Electric and Hybrid Vehicles
units.text: Modeling and Simulation of Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Fundamentals of vehicle system modeling, HEV Modeling using simulation software.

text_books: 1. Per Enge, Nick Enge, Stephen Zoepf, Electric Vehicle Engineering, 1st Edition, McGraw Hill, 2021. 2. Tom Denton, Electric and Hybrid Vehicles, 2nd Edition, Roultedge, Taylor & Francis Group, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Amir Khajepour, Saber Fallah, Avesta Goodarzi, Electric and Hybrid Vehicles – Technologies, Modeling and Control: A Mechatronic Approach, 1st Edition, Wiley, 2014. 2. Chitra A., S. Padamanaban, Jens Bo Holm-Nielsenm S. Himavathi, Artificial Intelligent Techniques for Electric and Hybrid Electric Vehicles, 1st Edition, Scrivener Publishing - Wiley, 2020.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mechanics, Materials Engineering, and Strength of Materials
objectives: This course is designed to encourage the students to apply scientific information and imagination for the development of new improved machines or mechanical systems. It also helps to design the machine components using concepts of stress analysis, theories of failure and materials science.

outcomes.text: Articulate the design procedure and selection of material for a specific application
Design machine elements such as cotter joints, knuckle joints, and levers subjected to axial loads
Analyse different types of power screws based on their load-carrying capacity, efficiency, and application suitability
Design various springs considering strength, stiffness
Evaluate the performance of fasteners and welded joints under various loading conditions
Explain concept of group technology, computer aided quality control and computer integrated manufacturing

units.title: Fundamentals of Design
units.text: Fundamentals of Design Basic procedure, sources of design data, use of standards, synthesis and creativity, material selection, factor of safety, service factor, stress concentration, theories of failure, maximum normal stress theory, maximum shear stress, maximum distortion energy theory.

units.title: Design of Simple Machine Parts
units.text: Design of Simple Machine Parts Cotter joint, knuckle joint, levers, and turn buckle.

units.title: Design of Shafts
units.text: Design of Shafts ASME code, design of shaft on strength and torsional rigidity basis, design of transmission shaft. Design of Keys Saddle, sunk, feather, and woodruff. Design of Coupling Muff, flange, flexible and bush pin coupling.

units.title: Power Screws
units.text: Power Screws Forms of thread, multiple threads, torque analysis with square and trapezoidal threads, self-locking, collar friction torque, stresses in power screw, screw jack.

units.title: Spring Design
units.text: Spring Design Types applications and material for springs, stress and deflection equation of helical spring, design of helical compression, spring in series and parallel, leaf spring design.

units.title: Design of Fasteners
units.text: Design of Fasteners Bolted joints, riveted joints, and welded joints. Design for transverse and eccentric loading.

text_books: 1. J. F. Shigley, Mechanical Engineering Design, 13th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2014. 2. V. B. Bhandari, Design of Machine Elements, 5th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Publication, 2020.
reference_books: 1. M. F. Spotts, Design of Machine Elements, 8th Edition, Pearson Publication, 2019. 2. PSG design data book PSG college-Kalaikathir Achchagam, Coimbatore, 2020.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus. Program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering) Semester: V /IX Course: Manufacturing Processes-II Code: 702ME0C015 Teaching Scheme Evaluation Scheme Lecture (Hours per week) Practical (Hours per week) Tutorial (Hours per week) Credit

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mechanics, Partial Differential Equations and Laplace transforms
objectives: The course is aimed at delivering detailed understanding of fluid properties and their static - dynamic nature. This course teaches the analytical techniques necessary for grasping fundamental behavior of incompressible fluids. It is designed for the students to learn the principles of laminar flow, turbulent flow, and boundary layer theory to solve important practical problems.

outcomes.text: Explain fundamental fluid properties and differentiate between various types of fluids and flow behavior
Analyze the principles of fluid statics, buoyancy, and flotation, and apply them to real-world engineering problems
Apply fluid kinematics and dynamics principles to characterize fluid motion and solve engineering problems
Analyze laminar and turbulent flows in pipes, including velocity distribution, shear stress, and pressure losses
Estimate energy losses in pipes and pipe network performance for different flow configurations
Analyze boundary layer formation, thickness, separation, and drag forces in external flow applications

units.title: Fluid Properties
units.text: Fluid Properties Concept of continuum, fluid properties, Classification of fluid, Newton’s law of viscosity, stress-strain relationship.

units.title: Fluid Statics
units.text: Fluid Statics Basic hydrostatic equation, Pascal’s Law, application to Manometers and mechanical gauges, hydrostatic forces on plane and curved submerged surfaces. Buoyancy and Floatation Archimedes’ Principle, buoyancy force and centre of buoyancy, metacentre, metacentric height, analytical method to find metacentric height, condition of equilibrium of submerged bodies, oscillation of a floating body

units.title: Fluid Kinematics
units.text: Fluid Kinematics Description of fluid motion-Lagrangian method and Euler’s method, classification of flow types- steady and unsteady, uniform and non-uniform, laminar and turbulent, one two and three- dimensional flow, rotational and irrotational, laminar and turbulent, compressible and incompressible. Flow patterns- stream lines, path lines, stream tubes and streak lines. Continuity equation (Cartesian and polar co-ordinates), circulation and vorticity, velocity potential and stream function.

units.title: Fluid Dynamics
units.text: Fluid Dynamics Euler’s equation of motion, Bernoulli’s equation and its applications-venturimeter, orificemeter, rotameter, pitot tube, Impulse-Momentum equation and its applications, Reynolds Transport Theorem and its application. Dimensional Analysis Secondary or derived quantities, Reyleigh method, Buckingham−𝜋theorem, dimensionless numbers, Theory of similarity, Model laws.

units.title: Laminar Flow
units.text: Laminar Flow Navier-Stokes equation of motion, developing expression for flow rate, pressure drop, shear stress, friction factor. Flow of viscous fluid in circular pipes- Hagen Poiseuille law, Couette flow. Turbulent Flow Shear stresses in turbulent flow, theories of turbulent shear stress, hydro-dynamically smooth and rough surface, modeling of turbulence, Moody’s chart. Flow Through Pipes Energy losses in pipes: Minor and Major losses, Darcy-Weisbatch equation for head loss in pipes, hydraulic gradient lines, and total energy lines, pipes in series and parallel, Equivalent pipe.

units.title: Boundary Layer Theory
units.text: Boundary Layer Theory Concept of Boundary layer, Boundary layer over flat plate, Boundary Layer thickness, momentum thickness, displacement thickness and energy thickness. Boundary layer equations and their solutions. Blasius solution (without derivation), Von-Karman momentum integral equation. Laminar boundary layer and turbulent boundary layer. Separation and control and Concept of drag.

text_books: 1. Frank M. White, Fluid Mechanics, 7th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2011. 2. S.K. Som, G.Biswas, S. Chakraborty, Introduction to Fluid Mechanics and Fluid Machines, 3rd Edition (revised), TMH Delhi, 2015.
reference_books: 1. John F. Douglas, Fluid Mechanics, 6th Edition, Pearson Education, 2011. 2. K.L. Kumar, Engineering Fluid Mechanics, 3rd Edition, S. Chand, 2016. 3. P.N. Modi, S.M. Seth, Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics including Hydraulic Machines, 19th Edition, Rajsons Publications, 2015. 4. K. Subrmanyan, Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic Machines: Problems and Solutions, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2019. 5. R.V. Giles, J.B. Evett, Cheng Liu, Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics, 4th Edition, Schaum Outline Series, McGraw Hill, 2013.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to appraise the students with different types of wastes and defects during manufacturing and the remedial steps to eliminate them. It imparts knowledge associated with aligning production processes with customer expectations and benchmark with efficient business processes.

outcomes.text: Summarize the relationship between Work in Progress and cycle time
Articulate the integration of batch size, setup, manufacturing processes and waste
Apply lean manufacturing techniques to manufacturing, projects and service industries

units.title: Introduction to Lean Manufacturing
units.text: Introduction to Lean Manufacturing History of lean, fundamental purpose of lean manufacturing, comparison to other methods. The seven Wastes, their causes and the effects, Implication of lean manufacturing – traditional vs lean manufacturing.

Tools of Lean Manufacturing 5S Principles, workplace organization, Process mapping / Value stream mapping, pull Systems (Kanban and WIP systems), error proofing and set-up reduction, total quality management (TQM), total productive maintenance (TPM), Toyota production systems, Ford production systems.

units.title: Value Stream Mapping (VSM)
units.text: Value Stream Mapping (VSM) Preparation for building a current state VSM, building a current state map (principles, concepts, loops, and methodology). Application to the factory simulation scenario. Line balancing, Poka Yoke, kanban, overall equipment effectiveness.

units.title: Just - In - time Manufacturing (JIT)
units.text: Just - In - time Manufacturing (JIT) Introduction, elements of JIT, uniform production rate, pull vs push method, kanban system, small lot size, quick and inexpensive set-up, continuous Improvement, optimized production technology.

units.title: Designing for Quality
units.text: Designing for Quality Introduction to concurrent engineering, quality function deployment (QFD) and failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA), concept, methodology and application (with case studies). Quality in service sectors: Characteristics of service sectors, quality dimensions in service sectors, measuring quality in different service sectors.

units.title: Six Sigma
units.text: Six Sigma Meaning of six sigma, why six sigma? six sigma improvement model, DMAIC and DMADV principle, building six sigma organization and culture, six sigma application, case studies.

units.title: Quality Circle
units.text: Quality Circle Quality circle structure, it’s operation, characteristics of quality circle, developing quality circle in organization, basic problem-solving techniques.

text_books: 1. M.K. Khanduja, Lean Manufacturing Implementation made easy, Inversio Solutions LLP, 2021. 2. Pascal Dennis, Lean Production Simplified, 3rd Edition, CRC Press, 2015.
reference_books: 1. James Edge, “Lean Six Sigma”, Bravex Publications, 2020. 2. Jeffrey K. Liker, “The Toyota way”, 2nd Edition, McGraw Hill Publications, 2021. Program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering) Semester: V / IX Course: Alternative Fuels Code: 702ME0E003 Teaching Scheme Evaluation Scheme Lecture (Hours per week) Practical (Hours per week) Tutorial (Hours per week) Credit
lab_work: 8 to 10 Tutorial exercises based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to acquaint students with control of mechanical operations, sensors and their interfacing with microcontrollers. The course offers learning of pneumatic/hydraulic systems, electrical controls and programmable logic controllers.

outcomes.text: Identify the suitable sensors and actuators for a mechatronics systems using pneumatic and hydraulic systems and electro-pneumatic circuits
Apply suitable logic controls and develop ladder logic programming
Design an appropriate robot for given industrial applications and carryout kinematic analysis for a robot

units.title: Introduction to Automation
units.text: Introduction to Automation Definition and fundamentals of automation, reasons for automating, basic elements of an automated system, power, program and control system. Introduction of mechatronics and its block diagram representation, key elements of mechatronics, applications of mechatronics, domestic, industrial etc. Representation of mechatronic system in block diagram and concept of transfer function for each element of mechatronic system, reduction methods and its numerical treatment for represented block diagram.

units.title: Selection of Sensors and Actuators
units.text: Selection of Sensors and Actuators Criteria for selection of sensors based on requirements, principle of measurement, sensing method, performance chart etc. Displacement, temperature, acceleration, force, pressure based on static and dynamic characteristics. Actuators, selection of actuators based on principle of operation, performance characteristics, maximum loading conditions, safety etc. Principle and selection of mechano- electrical actuators, DC motors, stepper motors, solenoid actuators, servo motors, BLDC.

units.title: Pneumatics and Hydraulics
units.text: Pneumatics and Hydraulics Hydraulic and pneumatic devices, different types of valves, actuators and auxiliary elements in pneumatics and hydraulics, their applications and use of their ISO symbols, synthesis and design of circuits (up to 2 cylinders) pneumatic, electro- pneumatics and hydraulics, electrohydraulic. Discrete control system, Programming Logic Control (PLC). Introduction to PLC, architecture, ladder logic programming for different types of logic gates, latching, timers, counter, practical examples of ladder programming.

units.title: Introduction to Robotics
units.text: Introduction to Robotics Definition of robot, evolution of robots, laws of robots, international robotic standards, types of robots, selection of robots, robot classifications, degrees of freedom, robot configuration, accuracy and repeatability, specification of a robot. Robot feedback controls, point to point control and continuous path control, control system for robot joint, adaptive control, actuators and sensors, drives and transmission systems, end effectors, applications of robots.

units.title: Analysis of Robots
units.text: Analysis of Robots Grubler - kutzbach criterion, denavit - hartneberg classic algorithm for reference frames, homogeneous coordinate transformation, the homogeneous coordinate transformation matrix, the arm matrix. Kinematics of robots, forward kinematics, inverse kinematics, simple robots, 2D cartesian robot, 2D polar robot, differential robot, geared wrists and grippers.

units.title: Modeling and Simulation
units.text: Modeling and Simulation SCARA robot, deriving equations of motion, simulation of equations of motion for relevant robots. Humanoids wheeled and legged, legged locomotion and balance, arm movement and control, performance, interaction, safety and robustness, applications, case studies.

text_books: 1. W. Bolton, Mechatronics: Electronic Control Systems in Mechanical Engineering, 6th edition, Pearson education, 2015. 2. Robert J. Schilling, Fundamentals of Robotics: Analysis and Control, 1st edition, Pearson education, 2015.
reference_books: 1. Clarence W. De Silva, Farbod Khoshnoud, Saman K. Halgamuge, Maoqing Li, Mechatronics: Fundamentals and Applications, CRC press London, 2015. 2. Rany Rizk, Mariette Awad, Mechanism, Machine, Robotics and Mechatronics Sciences, Springer international publishing, 2018.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course aims to prepare students to develop self-learning attitude, practical knowledge of programming language/modern technology according to the engineering applications.

outcomes.text: Implement the use of basics Python syntax
Create Graphical user interface in Python
Implement open source numerical libraries to build engineering applications

units.title: Introduction to Python
units.text: Introduction to Python Installation and Working with Python, Understanding Python variables Python basic Operators, Understanding python blocks, Python Data Types: Declaring and using Numeric data types: integers, float, complex, Using string data type and string operations.

units.title: Control Flow
units.text: Control Flow If, if-elif-else, loops, for loop using ranges, string, Use of while loops in python, Loop manipulation using pass, continue, break and else, Programming using Python conditional and loops block, Python arrays.

units.title: Data Structures
units.text: Data Structures List Operations, Slicing, Methods; Tuples, Sets, Dictionaries, Sequences. Comprehensions, Dictionary manipulation, list and dictionary in build functions

units.title: Functions
units.text: Functions Calling Functions, Passing Arguments, Keyword Arguments, Default Arguments, Variable-length arguments, Anonymous Functions, Fruitful Functions (Function Returning Values), Scope of the Variables in a Function - Global and Local Variables. Powerful Lamda function in python.

units.title: Numpy & Pandas
units.text: Numpy & Pandas Introduction to Numpy, Create 1D array & 2D array, Introduction to pandas, Pandas data structure:- series , data frame

Relate the physical problem of the fluid–structure interaction in marine structures

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The main objective of this course is to provide basic understanding of composite materials used in various engineering applications. The course also explains mechanical properties, micromechanics and manufacturing methods of composite materials.

outcomes.text: Relate processing, characterization and applications of various composite materials
Apply failure criteria and evaluate the results of composite materials
Evaluate the relative merits of using alternatives (corresponding to various simple and composite materials) for important engineering and other applications

units.title: Basic Concepts
units.text: Basic Concepts Modes of Heat Transfer, its mechanism and mathematical models. Conduction Heat Transfer: Fourier’s general conduction equation in Cartesian, Cylindrical and Spherical co-ordinates (for cylindrical and spherical walls derivation of Fourier’s three-dimensional equation is not included), thermal resistance, solution of Fourier’s equation for one dimensional steady state heat conduction through various configurations such as plane, cylindrical, spherical wall, composite medium. Critical thickness of insulation and its importance. Heat Transfer from extended surfaces: Types of fins, Governing equation, fin effectiveness, efficiency of fins, concept of corrected fin length, application of fins. Unsteady State Heat Conduction: Lumped System Analysis

units.title: Convection Heat Transfer
units.text: Convection Heat Transfer: Forced and natural convection, hydrodynamic and thermal boundary layer, Convection heat transfer coefficient, Momentum and energy equation for laminar boundary layer, Laminar and Turbulent flow, principles of dimensional analysis, physical significance of dimensionless numbers, Nusselt number, Prandtl number, Reynolds number, Grashof number. Empirical relations and their use for forced internal and external convection for circular and non-circular ducts. Empirical relations and their use for free convection on vertical, horizontal flat plate and cylinders.

units.title: Boiling and Condensation
units.text: Boiling and Condensation: Physical phenomenon and Pool boiling curve

units.title: Thermal Radiation
units.text: Thermal Radiation: Introduction to physical mechanism, concept of black body, grey body and radiation properties. Microwave Heating. Basic laws of radiation; Planck’s law, Kirchoff’s law, Stefan- Boltzman law, Wein’s-displacement law and Lambert’s Cosine law, Intensity of radiation, radiosity, shape factor for simple geometries, heat exchange between non-black bodies, Radiation Shield.

units.title: Heat Exchangers
units.text: Heat Exchangers: Classification, temperature distribution in parallel and counter flow arrangement, overall heat transfer coefficient, fouling factor, log mean temperature difference method, Effectiveness-NTU method.

text_books: 1. Yunus Cengel (2008), “Heat and Mass Transfer, A Practical Approach”, 5th Ed, Tata McGraw Hill. 2. Theodore Bergman & Adrienne Lavine (2017), “Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer”, 8 th edition, Wiley Publication 3. C.P. Kothandaraman & S. Subramanyan (2009), “Heat and mass transfer data book”, 6th Edition, New Age International
reference_books: 1. P.K Nag (2016), “Heat and Mass Transfer”, 3rd Edition, Tata MCgraw Hill 2. Frank Kreith, R.M. Manglik, Mark S. Bohn (2011), “Principles of Heat Transfer” 7th Edition, Cengage Learning. 3. S. K. Som (2008), “Introduction to Heat Transfer”, PHI Learning. 4. Frank P Incropera and D.P. Dewitt (2011), “Introduction to Heat Transfer”, John Wiley & Sons. 5. N.V. Suryanarayana (2015), Engineering Heat & Mass Transfer, 2nd Edition, PENRAM.

program: B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Graphics and Design (BTME01004), Manufacturing Processes-I (BTME04012), Manufacturing Processes-II (BTME05013)
objectives: ● To introduce the basics of backend of drafting packages ● To give hands on experience on the 3D Modeling software ● To impart knowledge of NC/CNC machines and programming of CNC using machine codes ● To provide concepts of GT, CAPP, CAQC and CIM

outcomes.text: Create accurate and precise geometry of complex engineering systems and use the geometric models in different engineering applications
Apply the concepts of machining for the purpose of selection of machining parameters and cutting tools for CNC milling and turning
Understand concepts of different CAD/CAM/CIM systems and various data management systems

units.title: Introduction and Elements of interactive computer graphics
units.text: Introduction and Elements of interactive computer graphics: The design process, the role of modeling and communication. Modeling using CAD, product life cycle and CAD/CAM, Concurrent engineering in product design and development, Collaborative Engineering, Computers for design process, CAD System Architecture-Software and Hardware

units.title: Techniques for geometric modeling
units.text: Techniques for geometric modeling : Graphic standards, The parametric representation of geometry-Bezier curves, Cubic spline curve, B-Spline curve, parametric representation of line, circle, ellipse and parabola, Constructive solid geometry (CSG), Boundary representation (B-rep), Wire Frame modeling, Solid modeling, Surface modeling, feature based modeling, Assembly Modeling- Different approaches of creating an assembly, Parent child relationship

units.title: Transformation, Manipulation and Data Storage
units.text: Transformation, Manipulation and Data Storage: 2D and 3D Transformations (Translation, Rotation, Scaling and Magnification), Concatenations, Matrix representation, Problems on Transformations. Object transformation, mirror transformation, Bill of Materials from attribute data, Engineering data management system, relational data base for design, object oriental database, Design Information Systems

units.title: NC and CNC technology
units.text: NC and CNC technology: Introduction, basic components of NC system, NC procedure, NC coordinate systems, NC motion control systems, Various actuation systems and feedback devices like encoder, tachogenerator, etc. Applications, Advantages and Disadvantages of NC machines Constructional details of CNC machines, CNC programming concepts, Manual part programming methods, Various G and M codes, Absolute and incremental system, Tool length and diameter compensation, Programming of turning and milling, Use of canned cycles, subroutines Flexible Manufacturing Systems (FMS), Machining Centers and its types, Automated Material Handling and Storage Systems like Robots, Automated Guided Vehicles (AGV) and Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems

units.title: Group Technology, CAPP and CAQC
units.text: Group Technology, CAPP and CAQC: Introduction to GT, Part families, Part Classification and Coding, GT Machines cells, Benefits of GT Introduction to CAPP, Retrieval type Process Planning Systems, Generative type Process Planning Systems, Benefits of CAPP, PFA, Similarity coefficient matrix Introduction to Computer Aided Quality Control (CAQC), Computers in QC, Contact Inspection Methods, Non-Contact Inspection Methods, Integration of CAQC with CAD/CAM

Computer Integrated Manufacturing and Technology driven practices: Introduction, Evolution, Objectives, CIM Hardware and software, CIM Benefits, Nature and role of elements of CIM, Identifying CIM needs, Data base requirements of CIM, Role of CAD/CAM in CIM, Obstacles to Computer Integrated Manufacturing, CIM wheel, DFM and DFA Introduction to Rapid Prototyping, Virtual Prototyping

text_books: 1. Groover, Mikell, and E. W. J. R. Zimmers, (2008), “CAD/CAM: computer- aided design and manufacturing”, Pearson Education. 2. Ibrahim Zeid, R. Sivasubramanian (2009), “CAD/CAM, Theory and Practice”, Tata McGraw Hill Publications.
reference_books: 1. P. N. Rao (2010), “CAD/CAM Principles and Applications” Tata McGraw Hill Publications. 2. P. Radhakrishan, S. Subramanyan, V. Raju (2004), “CAD/CAM/CIM”, New Age International Publishers.

program: B. Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Machine Drawing (BTME03011), Design of Machine Elements - I (BTME05010)
objectives:  To understand the design of gears and gear systems used in the industry  To provide the knowledge of different types of bearings and their selection  To introduce concept of robust design

outcomes.text: Select appropriate gears for power transmission on the basis of given load and speed
Design gears and bearings based on given conditions
Select bearing for a given application from manufacturing catalogues

units.title: Gear Design
units.text: Gear Design: Types of gear and its applications, selection of gear materials with desirable properties, modes of Gear tooth failure and methods of gear lubrication Spur Gear: Terminology, minimum number of teeth, face width and module relation, force analysis, beam strength of gear tooth (Lewis Equation), Velocity factor, service factor, effective load on gear tooth, Wear Strength of gear tooth (Buckingham Equation), Module calculation based on beam and wear strength. Helical Gear: Terminology, transverse and normal module, Virtual number of teeth, tooth proportions, force analysis, beam and wear strength, effective load on gear tooth.

units.title: Bevel Gears
units.text: Bevel Gears: Types of Bevel gears, terminology of straight tooth bevel gear, formative number of teeth, force analysis, beam and wear strength, dynamic load and effective load, materials selection for straight bevel gear, introduction to spiral bevel gear. Worm Gear: Terminology, geometric proportions of worm gears, force analysis, friction in worm gears, efficiency of worm gears, material selection, strength rating of worm gears, wear rating of worm gears, thermal considerations.

units.title: Rolling Contact Bearing
units.text: Rolling Contact Bearing: Types of rolling contact bearings , selection of bearing type, static and dynamic load carrying capacity, Stribeck’s equation, equivalent bearing load, Load life relationship, selection of bearing life, selection of bearing from manufactures catalogue, design for cyclic loads and speeds, bearing with probability of survival other than 90 %, lubrication of rolling contact bearing, mounting of bearing, causes of failure in rolling contact bearings and remedies, use of oil seals.

units.title: Sliding Contact Bearing
units.text: Sliding Contact Bearing: Basic modes of lubrications, theory of hydrodynamic lubrication, Pressure development in oil film, hydrostatic step bearing, energy losses in hydrostatic step bearings, Reynolds equation, Somerfield number, Raimondi and Boyd method, Temperature rise, bearing design- selection of parameters, bearing materials, lubricating oils and

text_books: 1. J. E. Shigley and C.R. Mischke (2006), “Mechanical Engineering Design” McGraw Hill Publication Co. Ltd. 2. V. B. Bhandari (2013), “Design of Machine Elements”, Tata McGraw Hill, New Delhi.
reference_books: 1. M. F. Spotts and T. E. Shoup (2008), “Design of Machine Elements”, Prentice Hall International. 2. V. M. Faires (2008), “Design of Machine Element”, McMillan. 3. PSG Design Data Handbook, PSG College, Kalaikathir Achchagam, Coimbatore, 2012.

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course provides introduction to Indian traditional knowledge and its relevance in the modern society.

outcomes.text: Understand the concept of Traditional knowledge and its importance
Apply the concept of Vedic mathematics to solve problems
Understand relevance of Chanakya niti in modern management

units.text: Introduction to traditional knowledge: Define traditional knowledge, nature and characteristics, scope and importance, kinds of traditional knowledge, the physical and social contexts in which traditional knowledge develop, the historical impact of social change on traditional knowledge systems. Indigenous Knowledge (IK), characteristics, traditional knowledge vis-à-vis indigenous knowledge, traditional knowledge Vs western knowledge traditional knowledge vis-à-vis formal knowledge

units.title: Traditional knowledge in different sectors
units.text: Traditional knowledge in different sectors: Traditional knowledge and engineering, Traditional medicine system, TK and biotechnology, TK in agriculture, Traditional societies depend on it for their food and healthcare needs, Importance of conservation and sustainable development of environment, Management of biodiversity, Food security of the country and protection of TK.
Vedic mathematics: Introduction, subtraction, multiplication, division, linear and quadratic equations, simultaneous linear equations, factorizations

units.title: Chanakya and modern management
units.text: Chanakya and modern management: leadership, qualities of a leader, people management, strategy, teamwork

text_books: 1. R. Pillai, Corporate Chanakya, Jaico Publishing House: Mumbai, 2012. 2. S. B. K. Tirtha and V. S. Agrawala, Vedic Mathematics, New Delhi: Motilal Banarsidass, 2004. 3. A. Jha, Traditional Knowledge System in India, New Delhi: Atlantic Publishers and Distributors (P) Ltd, 2009.
reference_books: 1. D. Bathia, Vedic Mathematics Made Easy, Mumbai: Jaico Publishing House, 2014. 2. B. K. Mohanta and V. K. Singh, Traditional Knowledge System and Technology in India, Delhi: Pratibha Prakashan, 2012. 3. S. Bose, Vedic Mathematics, V&S Publishers: New Delhi, 2015.

course_name: Department Elective I - Advanced Manufacturing Processes
program: B. Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives:  To introduce different manufacturing processes like advance casting, welding and forming etc.  To impart knowledge of industrial applications of various processes, equipment used in advance manufacturing.

outcomes.text: Understand requirement of appropriate advanced manufacturing process.
Classify and explain the various advanced manufacturing processes.
Select appropriate advanced material process based on design of component.

units.title: Surface Treatment
units.text: Surface Treatment: Scope, Cleaners, Methods of cleaning, Surface coating types, Electro forming, Physical Vapor deposition, Chemical vapor deposition, thermal spraying, Ion implantation, diffusion coating, Diamond coating and cladding.

units.title: Advanced Casting and Forming Processes
units.text: Advanced Casting and Forming Processes: Need and classification of advanced casting process; Metal mould casting; stir casting; Squeeze casting; Vacuum mould casting; Evaporative pattern casting; Ceramic shell casting. Classification of various advanced forming processes; High energy rate forming (HERF) process; Electro-magnetic forming(EMF), explosive forming; Electro-hydraulic forming (EHF); Stretch forming; Contour roll forming.

units.title: Development in Joining Processes
units.text: Development in Joining Processes: Electron beam welding (EBW); laser beam welding (LBW); ultrasonic welding (USW); Friction Stir Welding (FSW), Under water Friction Stir Welding (UWFSW); Joining of dis-similar metals; Adhesive Bonding and its applications

units.title: Non-traditional Machining Processes
units.text: Non-traditional Machining Processes: Parametric analysis and applications of processes such as ultrasonic machining (USM); Abrasive water jet machining (AWJM); Laser jet machining (LJM); Photo chemical Machining (PCM); Electrophoretic Deposition machining (EPDM); Wire Electro Discharge machining (WEDM) and its types.

units.title: Advancement in Machining Process
units.text: Advancement in Machining Process: Theory of Machining, Material removal mechanism; Hard machining; High speed machining. Machining of Composites like Metal Matrix Composite, Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic, Carbon Fiber Reinforced Plastic etc, Nickel based Superalloys, Refractory metals, Ceramics.

units.title: Recent Trends and Applications
units.text: Recent Trends and Applications: Design for manufacturing; Rapid Prototyping; Near net Manufacturing; Additive Manufacturing; Powder based fusion process; Nano Machining; Micro Machining; Machining of Micro gear, micro nozzle, micro pins, stent, implants.

text_books: 1. Kalpakjian S. and Schmid S. R. (2016), “Manufacturing Engineering and Technology”, 7th Edition, Pearson. 2. Jain V. K., (2012) Micro Manufacturing Processes, 4th Edition CRC Press, Taylor & Francis Group.
reference_books: 1. Chapman W. A. J. (2011), “Work Shop Technology- Vol I, II, III”, ELBS Publishers. 2. John A Schey, (2008) “Introduction to Manufacturing Processes”, Mc Graw Hill.

course_name: Department Elective I - Sustainable Energy Systems
program: B. Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives:  To acquire basic knowledge on relevant energy technology.  To have an overall understanding of energy systems.  To understand the complex relationship between energy and society.  To have a basic understanding of energy and electricity markets.

outcomes.text: Understand the principles of operation of renewable energy technologies.
Explain and demonstrate design and operating principles for solar, wind, hybrid and emerging systems. Explore renewable energy storage methods and emerging renewable technologies.

units.title: Factors Promoting Renewable Energy Applications
units.text: Factors Promoting Renewable Energy Applications: Introduction; India and world energy usage for electricity generation; Factors affecting the application and use of alternative energy sources; Environmental concern and renewable energy use
Solar Radiation, Solar Thermal Energy collection; Flat Plate and focusing collectors their materials and performance, Applications – heating, cooling and Power Generation

units.title: Photovoltaic
units.text: Photovoltaic: Introduction; Solar radiation characteristics; Photovoltaic conversion; Performance evaluation of PV cells, modules, panels, and arrays; Connections of photovoltaic devices; Optimization of photovoltaic arrays; Photovoltaic systems; Applications of photovoltaics; Utility interconnection issues and requirements

units.title: Wind Energy Conversion Systems
units.text: Wind Energy Conversion Systems: Introduction; The characteristics of wind; The aerodynamic theory of windmills; Wind power profile; Basic elements of the WECS; WECS schemes for generating electricity; Siting and sizing of WECS; Applications for WECS; Levels of wind power generation in utility grid systems; Future expectation of WECS; A hybrid wind and PV energy conversion system
Energy Storage; Battery technology; Fuel cells; Compressed air

units.title: energy storage; Flywheel Storage; Hydropower; Supercapacitors
units.text: energy storage; Flywheel Storage; Hydropower; Supercapacitors (Ultracapacitors); Superconducting magnetic energy storage Emerging Renewable Energy Sources: Ocean thermal energy conversion; Tidal energy; Wave power generation systems; Geothermal energy systems; Biomass energy systems; Solar thermal energy conversion systems; Microturbines; Satellite power systems

program: B. Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives:  To introduce the field of Composite Materials used in various engineering applications  To develop a solid understanding of the properties of composite materials and their micromechanics

outcomes.text: Understand processing, characterization and applications of various composite materials
Develop a basic understanding of the use of composite materials, micromechanics of composites
Evaluate the relative merits of using alternatives (corresponding to various simple and composite materials) for important engineering and other applications

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Definition, history, characteristics, concept of composite materials, comparison with metals, composite materials in engineering, industrial scenario, advantages and limitations of composites

units.title: Types of Matrix Materials
units.text: Types of Matrix Materials: Functions of a matrix, desired properties of a matrix, Polymer Matrix (Thermosets and Thermoplastics), Metal Matrix, Ceramic Matrix, Carbon Matrix, Glass Matrix etc. Types of Reinforcements/Fibers: Role and selection of reinforcement materials, types of fibers - Glass fibers, Boron fibers, Carbon fibers, Organic fibers - Aramid fibers, Ceramic fibers - Oxide fibers and non-oxide fibers, Alumina fibers, Silicon carbide fibers, Tungsten carbide fibers, Multiphase fibers, Whiskers, Flakes etc., properties of fibers, comparison of fibers Various types of composites: Based on Matrix Material - Polymer Matrix Composites (PMC), Metal Matrix Composites (MMC), Ceramic Matrix Composites (CMC), Carbon Fiber Composites; Based on reinforcements - Fiber Reinforced Composites, Fiber Reinforced Polymer (FRP) Composites, Laminated Composites, Particulate Composites

Polymer Matrix Composites (PMC) – Processing, structure and properties, applications. Metal matrix Composites (MMC) – Types, processing, properties, applications. Ceramic Matrix Composites (CMC) - Processing, properties, applications. Carbon Fiber Composites - Processing, properties, applications.

units.title: Micromechanics and Macromechanics of Composites
units.text: Micromechanics and Macromechanics of Composites: Density, Mechanical Properties, Thermal Properties, Mechanics of load transfer from matrix to fiber, elastic constants of an isotropic material, elastic constants of a lamina, stresses and strains in laminate composites

units.title: Monotonic
units.text: Monotonic Strength and Fracture- Tensile strength of unidirectional fiber composites, compressive strength of unidirectional fiber composites, Fracture modes in composites - Single and multiple fractures, debonding and delamination fracture, short-fiber composites: critical fiber length, models for strength, models for stiffness, fatigue and creep.

units.title: Advanced Composites
units.text: Advanced Composites: Nanocomposites, hybrid composites, self- healing composites, self-reinforced composites, in-situ composites, smart composites. Industrial Applications of Composite Materials: Aerospace industries, Automobile and other surface transport industries, Packaging industries, House hold and sports components etc., Recycling of composites

text_books: 1. Composite Materials: Science and Engineering, Krishan K. Chawla, Springer, 2012. 2. Composite materials and processing, M. Balasubramanian, CRC press, 2013.
reference_books: 1. Composites Manufacturing: Materials, Product, and Process Engineering, S. Mazumdar, CRC press, 2001. 2. Manufacturing processes for advanced composites, F.C. Campbell Jr, Elsevier, 2003.

program: B. Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Manufacturing Processes - I and II (BTME04012 and BTME05013)
objectives:  To develop an understanding of the short and medium term planning and control function of production at middle and operational level.  To focus on functions for estimation and allocation of resources  To impart knowledge of procedures for meeting production and inventory targets in production organizations covering a wide range product types

outcomes.text: To develop an understanding of the short and medium term planning and control function of production at middle and operational level

Analyze planning, professional and engineering decisions within a manufacturing environment To focus on functions for estimation and allocation of resources To impart knowledge of procedures for meeting production and inventory targets in production organizations covering a wide range product types

units.title: Fundamentals of Manufacturing
units.text: Fundamentals of Manufacturing: Manufacturing definition, value adding conversion process, resources and optimum allocation; functions of production; Production Planning and Control and its interrelationship with other functions such as marketing, finance, R&D organization for production systems; job order, batch production.

units.title: Economic Analysis
units.text: Economic Analysis: Factors to be considered in product design. Economics of scales fixed Cost, variable cost, break even chart, P-V chart, multiple product P-V charts, and make-buy decision.

units.title: Plant Location and Plant Layout
units.text: Plant Location and Plant Layout: Factors to be considered in plant location, process layout. Techniques of plant layout, concept of Group technology, Group layout.

units.title: Production planning and control
units.text: Production planning and control: Scheduling, Progress monitoring, job order scheduling, dispatching rules, batch size Decision, production range; Aggregate planning, capacity planning, manufacturing resource planning and scheduling, JIT system, SMED, Kanban pull system of scheduling, line balancing.

units.title: Materials management
units.text: Materials management: Bill of materials, Quantity planning, Inventory control, Economic order quantity (EOQ), lead time, consumption rate, different ordering systems, Q system, P system, S system, Two and three bin systems, the store’s function and ABC analysis.

units.title: Introduction to Project management
units.text: Introduction to Project management: Project evaluation and review techniques, critical path method (PERT /CPM), float, three time estimates, probability of completion before due date, crashing and optimum duration, resource levelling.

text_books: 1. S. Eilon (2004), “Elements of Production Planning and Control”, Universal Publicity Corporation. 2. S. N. Chary (2009), “Production and Operations Management”, Tata McGraw Hill. 3. L. S. Srinath (2000), “PERT and CPM – Principles and Applications”, East West Press.
reference_books: 1. R. Chase (2008), “Operation Management”, Tata McGraw Hill. 2. E. S. Buffa (2007), “Modern Production /Operation Management”, Wiley Eastern. 3. B. Mahadevan (2007), “Operations Management, Theory and Practice”, Pearson Education. 4. Evans and Collier (2007), “Operation Management, An Integrated Goods and Services Approach”, Thomson/South-Western. 5. J. S. Matrinich (2008), “Production and Operation Management an Applied Modern Approach”, Wiley India.

course_name: Department Elective I - Product Design and Development
program: B. Tech. (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Manufacturing Processes – I and II (BTME04012 and BTME05013)
objectives:  To provide the understanding of the development and design aspects of products  To impart knowledge of business and technical concerns about the different methodologies of product development  To introduce concept of product life cycle and product data management

outcomes.text: Understand different stages of product development and design with modern approaches.
Apply the knowledge of Technology Forecasting using S-Curve in product development as per customers need. Benchmark products, technologies & techniques for product design.

units.title: Introduction to Product Design and Development
units.text: Introduction to Product Design and Development: Definition of product design, design by evolution and innovation, factors in product design, morphology of product design (seven phases), standardization, simplification and specialization in product design, modern approaches- concurrent design and quality function deployment, product development, product development versus product design, types of design and redesign, modern product development process, product development team and product development planning with reference to ISO standard, difference between product verification and production validation, introduction to prototyping, rapid prototyping methods.

units.title: Product
units.text: Product Development – Technical and Business Concerns: Technology Forecasting and Technology S-Curve (Technology Stage), Mission Statement and Technical Questioning, Economic Analysis of Product, Customer Needs and Satisfaction, Customer Population and Market Segmentation, Customer Needs-Types and Models, Gathering Customer Needs Information, Analysis of Gathered Information.

units.title: Product Development from Concept to Product Function
units.text: Product Development from Concept to Product Function: Generating concepts, information gathering and brainstorming, morphological analysis, concept selection-design evaluation, estimation of technical feasibility, concept selection process, Pugh’s concept, selection charts, numerical concept scoring, process of concept embodiment, system modeling, Failure Mode Effect Analysis (FMEA), functional modeling and decomposition, fast method, subtract and operate procedure, establishing system functionality, augmentation and aggregation.

units.title: Quality function deployment (QFD)
units.text: Quality function deployment (QFD): Quality function deployment studies to validate design characteristics; Affinity diagram, Tree diagram, Matrix diagram, Prioritization matrix; Design validation

units.title: Design for ‘X’ (DFX)
units.text: Design for ‘X’ (DFX): Design for manufacture, assembly, testing, maintenance, service, reliability; Product safety and hazard evaluation; Final disposal; Reverse Engineering.

text_books: 1. K. Otto and K. Wood (2009), “Product Design –Techniques in Reverse Engineering and New Product Development”, Pearson Education. 2. K. T. Ulrich and S. D. Eppinger (2008), “Product Design and Development”, Tata McGraw Hill.
reference_books: 1. R. Rosenthal (2000), “Effective Product Design and Development”, Business One- Irwin S Publication. 2. E.B. Magrab, S.K. Gupta, F. Patrick (2009), “Integrated Product and Process Design and Development-The Product Realization Process”, CRC press.

units.title: Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM) and Technology Driven
units.text: Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM) and Technology Driven Practices Introduction, evolution, objectives, CIM hardware and software, CIM benefits, nature and role of elements of CIM, identifying CIM needs, data base requirements of CIM, role of CAD/CAM in CIM, obstacles to computer integrated manufacturing, CIM wheel, design for manufacturing and design for assembly, introduction to rapid prototyping, virtual prototyping

program: B Tech/MBA Tech/ B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Thermodynamics, Applied Thermodynamics, Heat Transfer
objectives: This course focuses in detail on industrial refrigeration and air-conditioning systems, which are crucial to modern space conditioning. Additionally, it aims to impart knowledge regarding the choice of HVAC plant equipment and control systems.

outcomes.text: Apply HVAC theory in the design and selection of HVACR plant equipment
Discuss and analyze the different air conditioning and industrial refrigeration systems
Explain different components and control systems in the HVAC and refrigeration industry

units.title: Introduction

Energy-efficient HVAC design. Classification of Air Conditioning Systems Window air-conditioner, split air-conditioner, dessert Cooler, air-washer, chillers, VRV system, cassette, roof tops, FCUs.

units.title: Components of Refrigeration Plant
units.text: Components of Refrigeration Plant Types of compressors, types of evaporators, types of condensers, types of throttling devices, ventilation and air filtration, cooling towers.

units.title: Industrial Refrigeration System
units.text: Industrial Refrigeration System Vapour absorption refrigeration system- Ammonia vapor absorption system, Lithium bromide absorption system, capacity control.

Equipment Selection Chiller selection, compressor selection, condenser selection, selection of thermostatic expansion valve, pipe sizing.
