program: B Tech/MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed to give students hands-on experience on metal cutting operations. It also helps them to understand the essence of the safety practices and standard operating procedures of the power tools including machining and finishing operations.

outcomes.text: Create one composite job using different types of machining operations.
Operate different types of machines such as milling, shaping and grinding.
Illustrate common problems with tooling and fixtures in CNC programming and machining.

units.text: One composite job consisting minimum four parts employing operations on lathe, precision turning, external and internal threading, boring.
Practice Shaping, milling, grinding & Knurling operations on composite job.
Demonstration on machining of Glass Fiber Reinforcement Plastic (GFRP) composite material, Drilling and edge milling operation.
Demonstration of a job on CNC machine.

lab_work: Performing 15 week practical to complete jobs as per the syllabus.

program: B Tech/MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The objective of this course is to give the students a systematic and comprehensive understanding of various aspects related to industrial engineering and its relevance in the industrial environment.

outcomes.text: Describe the concepts of productivity and methods to improve efficiency
Apply the methods to measure parameters such as time and magnitude of activities performed
Analyze the cost effectiveness of each function of the product in terms of usefulness to the customer

units.title: Productivity
units.text: Productivity Productivity concepts. Analysing the work content of a job to identify and reduce/eliminate the excess work content. Interdependence between working conditions and productivity. Significance of theory of Scientific Management. Improving Efficiency and Productivity through Work-study, Work-study components. Relationship between Method Study and Time Study.

units.title: Method Study
units.text: Method Study Basic procedure of method study. Factors in selecting a job to a studied. Recording the facts with charts and diagrams. Questioning technique for development of new method. Role of Management and workers in implementation.

units.title: Facilities & Workplace Design
units.text: Facilities & Workplace Design Aligning the physical facilities- plant layout, equipment and work flow as per the production processes. Principles of Motion Economy. Standardization of the process.

units.title: Work Measurement
units.text: Work Measurement Significance of work measurement. Techniques of work measurement. Need of work sampling technique. Conducting work sampling study. Analytical estimation of work. Concept of rating factor. Consideration of various allowances. Standard time for work. Predetermined time standards. Use standard data. MOST for work measurement. Use of time standards.

units.title: Ergonomics
units.text: Ergonomics Field of Ergonomics. Physical and cognitive issues of ergonomics. Aims of ergonomics considerations. Working postures of operatives. Design of objects, facilities and environment. Anthropometrical details. Database of human factors. Ergonomic improvement of physical and cognitive issues. Ergonomics principals. Information input and human control of systems. Work space and arrangement. Living environment. Visual displays

units.title: Value Engineering
units.text: Value Engineering Definition of Value Engineering, Uses of Value Engineering, Reasons for unnecessary costs, Difference between Value Engineering and other cost reduction techniques. Case studies

text_books: 1. International Labour Office, Introduction to Work Study, 3rd edition, Oxford & I. B. H. Publishing Co. Ltd, 2015. 2. R. Barnes, Motion and Time Study Design and Measurement of Work, 7th edition, Asia Publishing, 2009.
reference_books: 1. M. S. Sanders & E J McCormick, Human factors in Engineering & Design, Tata McGraw Hill, 2020. 2. Merton E. Davis, William D. Falcon, Value Engineering: The Implications for Managers, American Management Association, 2002.

program: B Tech/MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed to encourage the students to understand the role of fluid power in automation. It helps them to identify the various components of an automation system and design circuits to control the physical output work.

outcomes.text: Relate hydraulic power, hydraulic actuators and motors
Analyze the different components of hydraulic systems
Identify different pneumatic controls, actuators and control valves

units.title: Introduction to Hydraulic Power
units.text: Introduction to Hydraulic Power Role of drive-in automation system, comparison of drives. Definition of hydraulic system, advantages, limitations, applications, Pascal's law, structure of hydraulic control system, problems on Pascal's law. The source of Hydraulic Power: Pumps Classification of pumps, pumping theory of positive displacement pumps, construction and working of Gear pumps and Vane pumps.

units.title: Hydraulic Systems
units.text: Hydraulic Systems Hydraulic Power Pack, Hydraulic Accumulator, Symbolic representation and working of Control Valves – Direction Control Valves, Flow Control Valves, Check valves, shuttle valves, pressure valves. Use of valves for speed and pressure control. Hydraulic circuits in power tools and other applications.

units.title: Pneumatic Systems
units.text: Pneumatic Systems Definition of pneumatic system, advantages, limitations, applications, Choice of working medium. Characteristics of compressed air. Structure of Pneumatic control System, Direction control valves, single and double acting linear actuator; direct and indirect control of DCV, Speed control circuits.

units.title: Fluid power circuits with electrical control
units.text: Fluid power circuits with electrical control Ladder Logic Diagram, Electro-hydraulic/pneumatic control, Use of relays and limit switches, Sequencing Circuits with and without electrical control, multi- cylinder circuit applications.

text_books: 1. Anthony Esposito, Fluid Power with Applications, 7th Edition, Pearson Education, 2008. 2. M. Galal Rabie, Fluid Power Engineering, 1st Edition, McGraw- Hill, 2009.
reference_books: 1. Andrew Parr, Hydraulics and Pneumatics- A technician’s and engineer’s guide, 3rd Edition, Butterworth-Heinemann Ltd, 2011. 2. Ilango Sivaraman, Introduction to Hydraulics and Pneumatics, 3rd Edition, PHI Learning Pvt. Ltd., 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech/MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course provides the understanding of the development and design aspects of products, impart knowledge of business and technical concerns about the different methodologies of product development. This course also discusses the concept of product life cycle and product data management.

outcomes.text: Identify the different stages of product development and design with modern approaches
Apply the knowledge of Technology Forecasting using S-Curve in product development as per customers need
Describe the process of benchmarking of products, technologies & techniques product design

units.title: Introduction to Product Design and Development
units.text: Introduction to Product Design and Development Definition of product design, product development versus product design, types of design and redesign, design by evolution and innovation, factors in product design, morphology of product design (seven phases), standardization, simplification and specialization in product design, product life cycle and its various phases, modern approaches- concurrent design in product development, product development team and product development planning with reference to ISO standard, new product development process/stages, difference between product verification and production validation.

units.title: Product Development – Technical and Business Concerns
units.text: Product Development – Technical and Business Concerns Technology forecasting and Technology S-curve, Kano model, Mission statement and technical questioning. Economic analysis of product, customer needs and satisfaction, customer population and market segmentation, gathering customer needs information, analysis of gathered information.

units.title: Product Development from Concept to Product Function
units.text: Product Development from Concept to Product Function Generating concepts, information gathering and brainstorming, morphological analysis, concept selection-design evaluation, estimation of technical feasibility, concept selection process, Pugh’s concept, selection charts, numerical concept scoring, process of concept embodiment, system modeling, Failure Mode Effect Analysis (FMEA), functional modeling and decomposition, fast method, subtract and operate procedure, establishing system functionality.

units.title: Quality function deployment (QFD)
units.text: Quality function deployment (QFD) Quality function deployment studies to validate design characteristics; Affinity diagram, Tree diagram, Matrix diagram, Prioritization matrix; Design validation.

units.title: Design for ‘X’ (DFX)
units.text: Design for ‘X’ (DFX) Design for manufacture, assembly, testing, maintenance, service, reliability, environmental sustainability; introduction to prototyping, rapid prototyping methods. Product safety and hazard evaluation; Final disposal; Reverse Engineering; Managing Competitiveness- benchmarking, outsourcing and mass customization.

text_books: 1. K. Otto and K. Wood, Product Design –Techniques in Reverse Engineering and New Product Development, 7th Edition, Pearson Education, 2020. 2. K. T. Ulrich and S. D. Eppinger, Product Design and Development, 6th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2015.
reference_books: 1. E. B. Magrab, S.K. Gupta, F. Patrick, Integrated Product and Process Design and Development-The Product Realization Process, 2nd Edition, CRC press, 2019.

program: B Tech/MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course provides comprehensive understanding of working principles of fluid machinery including performance characteristics, governing and similarity method for performance prediction.

outcomes.text: Articulate the working of different types of fluid machinery
Evaluate hydraulic turbines and pumps in terms of design parameters and performance Characteristics
Apply similarity methods to predict the performance of the hydraulic turbine and pumps

units.title: Principles of hydraulic machines
units.text: Principles of hydraulic machines Impacts of jet on flat plate and curved vanes, elements of a hydro power plant, types of heads and efficiencies. Theory of impulse and reaction machines, Euler’s energy equation applied to a turbine and pump, velocity triangles, expression for work done.

units.title: Impulse Turbine
units.text: Impulse Turbine Pelton Turbine Components of a Pelton turbine, velocity triangles, speed ratio, jet ratio, estimation of various parameters like head, discharge, and efficiency, determination of number of buckets. Performance curves, governing of turbine, cavitation.

units.title: Reaction Turbines
units.text: Reaction Turbines Types of reaction turbines, draft tubes. Francis Turbine Velocity triangles construction, working and performance. Kaplan Turbine Velocity triangles construction, working and performance, governing of turbine.

units.title: Pumps
units.text: Pumps Introduction, Classification of pumps-positive displacement and non - positive displacement. Reciprocating Pump Basic theory, construction, operation, Slip, Indicator diagram, use of air vessel. Rotary Pumps Basic theory, types, construction and working, variable delivery pumps.

units.title: Centrifugal pumps
units.text: Centrifugal pumps Basic Theory, velocity triangles, classification, construction, operation, characteristics, Priming of pumps, Series and parallel operation of pumps. Cavitation and NPSH (NPSHA, NPSHR).

units.title: Similarity
units.text: Similarity Similarity relations in turbines and pumps, definition of unit quantities and specific quantities.

text_books: 1. P.N. Modi, S.M. Seth, Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics including Hydraulic Machines, 22nd Edition, Rajsons Publication, 2019. 2. K. Subramanya, Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic Machines, 2nd Edition McGraw Hill Publication, 2018.
reference_books: 1. M. K. Goyal, Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic Machines, PHI Learning, 2015. 2. Y. Cengel, Fluid Mechanics-Fundamentals and Applications, 4th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2019.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech/ B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mechanics and Strength of Materials
objectives: To provide an understanding of the basics of aerodynamics in aircraft. To impart knowledge of boundary layer theory. To introduce the aerospace vehicle and space vehicle design. To introduce wind tunnel testing

outcomes.text: Analyse the basic flight mathematical aspects and potential flows
Discuss structural design of aircraft and space vehicles
Classify types of wind tunnel and describe wind tunnel testing technique

units.title: Introduction to Aerodynamics
units.text: Introduction to Aerodynamics Importance of Aerodynamic, four principles of aerodynamics, three laws of aerodynamics, six fundamentals of flight.

units.title: Applied Aerodynamics
units.text: Applied Aerodynamics Panel methods, pressure distribution, Kutta conditions, flow around airfoil (unsteady potential flow, compressible flow, axisymmetric flow) and slender body theories. Flight vehicle aerodynamics, rotor aerodynamics – low Reynolds number aerodynamics

units.title: Aircraft Vehicle Design
units.text: Aircraft Vehicle Design Design considerations for civilian and military aircraft, weight estimation, airfoil and geometry selection, thrust to weight ratio and wing loading, initial sizing, propulsion, landing gear and subsystems, aerodynamics, stability, control, and handling qualities, flight mechanics and performance issues, aircraft layout and configuration, structural aspects and constraint analysis.

units.title: Space Vehicle Design
units.text: Space Vehicle Design History of rocketry & launch vehicles, Current & future launch vehicles. Orbit/trajectory requirements and missions. Launch vehicle sizing, launch into an orbit, rocket propulsion (configuration and structural design), design for re-entry

units.title: Wind Tunnel Techniques
units.text: Wind Tunnel Techniques Introduction to wind tunnel, Classification of wind tunnels, Elements of wind tunnel, Conventional measurement techniques, wind tunnel testing technique.

text_books: 1. John D. Anderson, Fundamentals of aerodynamics, NY: McGraw-Hill Education, 6th edition, 2017. 2. Robert F. Stengel, Flight dynamics, Princeton University Press, 2nd Edition, 2022.
reference_books: 1. Bertin, J. J. and Cummings, R. M., Aerodynamics for Engineers, Prentice Hall, 6th edition, 2013. 2. Houghton, E. L., Carpenter, P. W., Collicott, S. H., and Valentine, D. T., Aerodynamics for Engineering Students, Butterworth-Heinemann, 6th Edition, 2012.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed to impart knowledge of an IC engine and the ignition systems. It also introduces the modern developments in internal combustion engines with optical measurement techniques and emission control.

outcomes.text: Explain advanced engine technologies and emission norms
Apply concepts of different alternate fuels used for SI and CI engines
Analyze environmental, social, and technological issues related to the future widespread use of internal combustion engines

units.title: Basic Characteristics of Engines
units.text: Basic Characteristics of Engines Compression ratio, energy supply to an engine, power developed by engine, specific weight and specific volume, cylinder pressures, indicated mean effective pressure determination, torque characteristics, cylinder arrangement and their relative merits. Engine Cooling Systems Types of cooling, cooling of critical engine components, re-cooling the coolant, comparison of air cooled and liquid cooled engines.

units.title: Fuel Delivery in Spark Ignition Engines
units.text: Fuel Delivery in Spark Ignition Engines Classification of fuel delivery systems, fuel transfer pumps, fixed jet carburetor, computer controlled carburetor, gasoline injection systems. Ignition Systems in Spark Ignition Engines Battery ignition system, requirements for satisfactory operation of the ignition system, ignition timing and advancing mechanisms, magneto ignition system, electronic ignition system.

units.title: Combustion and Combustion Systems in Compression Ignition Engines
units.text: Combustion and Combustion Systems in Compression Ignition Engines Air motion in compression ignition engines, delay period in compression ignition engines, types of diesel combustion systems. Scavenging and Super Charging in Compression Ignition Engines Types of scavenging systems, improved and modified scavenging systems, super charging and engine performance, methods of super charging.

units.title: Modern Developments in Internal Combustion Engines
units.text: Modern Developments in Internal Combustion Engines Exhaust gas recirculation, multi point fuel injection, gasoline direct engine, homogeneous charge compression ignition and turbo-charging. Optical Measurement Techniques and Tools Particle image velocimetry (PIV), 3D and Holographic PIV, spray visualization, phase doppler interferometry for spray characterization, optical engines and engine endoscopy, use of nanoparticles in internal combustion engines.

units.title: Automobile Emissions and Its Control
units.text: Automobile Emissions and Its Control Need for emission control, classification/ categories of emissions, major pollutants, control of emissions, evaluating vehicle emissions, European emission standards, Indian emission standards, pollution monitoring instruments and techniques, Control measures such as diesel oxidation catalyst, diesel particulate filter, selective catalytic reduction and lean NOx trap.

text_books: 1. Ganesan, V, Internal Combustion Engines, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Book Co., 2017. 2. John B. Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, 2nd Edition McGraw Hill Book, 2018.
reference_books: 1. Amitava Datta, Avinash Kumar Agarwal, Dhananjay Kumar Srivastava, Rakesh Kumar Maurya, Advances in Internal Combustion Engine Research, Springer Singapore, 2017. 2. Richard Stone, Introduction to Internal Combustion Engines, Macmillan Education UK, 2012.

program: B Tech /B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, Differential and Integral Calculus
objectives: This course is designed to provide knowledge of different modes of heat transfer with different laws of conduction, convection and radiation. It also helps to provide understanding of different applications of conduction, convection and radiation.

outcomes.text: Describe the basic laws of heat transfer
Analyse realistic problems involving different modes of heat transfer
Apply basic principles of heat transfer to design heat transfer devices

units.title: Basic Concepts
units.text: Basic Concepts Modes of Heat Transfer, its mechanism and mathematical models. Conduction Heat Transfer Fourier’s general conduction equation in Cartesian, Cylindrical and Spherical co- ordinates (for cylindrical and spherical walls derivation of Fourier’s three- dimensional equation is not included), thermal resistance, solution of Fourier’s equation for one dimensional steady state heat conduction through various configurations such as plane, cylindrical, spherical wall, composite medium. Critical thickness of insulation and its importance. Heat Transfer from Extended Surfaces Types of fins, Governing equation, fin effectiveness, efficiency of fins, concept of corrected fin length, application of fins. Unsteady State Heat Conduction Lumped System Analysis

units.title: Convection Heat Transfer
units.text: Convection Heat Transfer Forced and natural convection, hydrodynamic and thermal boundary layer, Convection heat transfer coefficient, Momentum and energy equation for laminar boundary layer, Laminar and Turbulent flow, principles of dimensional analysis, physical significance of dimensionless numbers, Nusselt number, Prandtl number, Reynolds number, Grashof number. Empirical relations and their use for forced internal and external convection for circular and non-circular ducts. Empirical relations and their use for free convection on vertical, horizontal flat plate and cylinders. Boiling and Condensation Physical phenomenon and Pool boiling curve.

units.title: Thermal Radiation
units.text: Thermal Radiation Introduction to physical mechanism, concept of black body, grey body and radiation properties. Microwave Heating. Basic laws of radiation; Planck’s law, Kirchoff’s law, Stefan-Boltzman law, Wein’s-displacement law and Lambert’s Cosine law, Intensity of radiation, radiosity, shape factor for simple geometries, heat exchange between non-black bodies, Radiation Shield.

units.title: Heat Exchangers
units.text: Heat Exchangers Classification, temperature distribution in parallel and counter flow arrangement, overall heat transfer coefficient, fouling factor, log mean temperature difference method, Effectiveness-NTU method.

text_books: 1. Theodore Bergman & Adrienne Lavine, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, 8th Edition, Wiley Publication 2017. 2. C.P. Kothandaraman & S. Subramanyan, Heat and Mass Transfer Data Book, 9th Edition, New Age International 2018.
reference_books: 1. P.K Nag, Heat and Mass Transfer, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2016. 2. Frank P Incropera and D.P. Dewitt, Introduction to Heat Transfer, John Wiley & Sons, 2011.
lab_work: 8 to 10 Experiments based on the syllabus.

Apply the concepts of machining for the purpose of selection of machining parameters and cutting tools for CNC milling and turning
Relate different CAD/CAM/CIM and various data management systems

units.text: Introduction and Elements of Interactive Computer Graphics The design process, computers for design process, product life cycle and CAD/CAM, concurrent engineering in product design and development, collaborative engineering, CAD system architecture - software and hardware, the role of modeling and communication, modeling using CAD

units.text: Value Engineering Definition of Value Engineering, Uses of Value Engineering, Reasons for unnecessary costs, Difference between Value Engineering and other cost reduction techniques. Case studies

text_books: 1. International Labour Office, Introduction to Work Study, 3rd edition, Oxford & I. B. H. Publishing Co. Ltd, 2015. 2. R. Barnes, Motion and Time Study Design and Measurement of Work, 7th edition, Asia Publishing, 2009.
reference_books: 1. M. S. Sanders & E J McCormick, Human factors in Engineering & Design, Tata McGraw Hill, 2020. 2. Merton E. Davis, William D. Falcon, Value Engineering: The Implications for Managers, American Management Association, 2002.

program: B Tech/B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed to encourage the students to understand the role of fluid power in automation. It helps them to identify the various components of an automation system and design circuits to control the physical output work.

outcomes.text: Relate hydraulic power, hydraulic actuators and motors
Analyze the different components of hydraulic systems
Identify different pneumatic controls, actuators and control valves

units.title: Introduction to Hydraulic Power
units.text: Introduction to Hydraulic Power Role of drive-in automation system, comparison of drives. Definition of hydraulic system, advantages, limitations, applications, Pascal's law, structure of hydraulic control system, problems on Pascal's law. The source of Hydraulic Power: Pumps Classification of pumps, pumping theory of positive displacement pumps, construction and working of Gear pumps and Vane pumps.

units.title: Hydraulic Systems
units.text: Hydraulic Systems Hydraulic Power Pack, Hydraulic Accumulator, Symbolic representation and working of Control Valves – Direction Control Valves, Flow Control Valves, Check valves, shuttle valves, pressure valves. Use of valves for speed and pressure control. Hydraulic circuits in power tools and other applications.

units.title: Pneumatic Systems
units.text: Pneumatic Systems Definition of pneumatic system, advantages, limitations, applications, Choice of working medium. Characteristics of compressed air. Structure of Pneumatic control System, Direction control valves, single and double acting linear actuator; direct and indirect control of DCV, Speed control circuits.

units.title: Fluid power circuits with electrical control
units.text: Fluid power circuits with electrical control Ladder Logic Diagram, Electro-hydraulic/pneumatic control, Use of relays and limit switches, Sequencing Circuits with and without electrical control, multi- cylinder circuit applications.

text_books: 1. Anthony Esposito, Fluid Power with Applications, 7th Edition, Pearson Education, 2008. 2. M. Galal Rabie, Fluid Power Engineering, 1st Edition, McGraw- Hill, 2009.
reference_books: 1. Andrew Parr, Hydraulics and Pneumatics- A technician’s and engineer’s guide, 3rd Edition, Butterworth-Heinemann Ltd, 2011. 2. Ilango Sivaraman, Introduction to Hydraulics and Pneumatics, 3rd Edition, PHI Learning Pvt. Ltd., 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech/B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course provides the understanding of the development and design aspects of products, impart knowledge of business and technical concerns about the different methodologies of product development. This course also discusses the concept of product life cycle and product data management.

outcomes.text: Identify the different stages of product development and design with modern approaches
Apply the knowledge of Technology Forecasting using S-Curve in product development as per customers need
Describe the process of benchmarking of products, technologies & techniques product design

units.title: Introduction to Product Design and Development
units.text: Introduction to Product Design and Development Definition of product design, product development versus product design, types of design and redesign, design by evolution and innovation, factors in product design, morphology of product design (seven phases), standardization, simplification and specialization in product design, product life cycle and its various phases, modern approaches- concurrent design in product development, product development team and product development planning with reference to ISO standard, new product development process/stages, difference between product verification and production validation.

units.title: Product Development – Technical and Business Concerns
units.text: Product Development – Technical and Business Concerns Technology forecasting and Technology S-curve, Kano model, Mission statement and technical questioning. Economic analysis of product, customer needs and satisfaction, customer population and market segmentation, gathering customer needs information, analysis of gathered information.

units.title: Product Development from Concept to Product Function
units.text: Product Development from Concept to Product Function Generating concepts, information gathering and brainstorming, morphological analysis, concept selection-design evaluation, estimation of technical feasibility, concept selection process, Pugh’s concept, selection charts, numerical concept scoring, process of concept embodiment, system modeling, Failure Mode Effect Analysis (FMEA), functional modeling and decomposition, fast method, subtract and operate procedure, establishing system functionality.

units.title: Quality function deployment (QFD)
units.text: Quality function deployment (QFD) Quality function deployment studies to validate design characteristics; Affinity diagram, Tree diagram, Matrix diagram, Prioritization matrix; Design validation.

units.title: Design for ‘X’ (DFX)
units.text: Design for ‘X’ (DFX) Design for manufacture, assembly, testing, maintenance, service, reliability, environmental sustainability; introduction to prototyping, rapid prototyping methods. Product safety and hazard evaluation; Final disposal; Reverse Engineering; Managing Competitiveness- benchmarking, outsourcing and mass customization.

text_books: 1. K. Otto and K. Wood, Product Design –Techniques in Reverse Engineering and New Product Development, 7th Edition, Pearson Education, 2020. 2. K. T. Ulrich and S. D. Eppinger, Product Design and Development, 6th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2015.
reference_books: 1. E. B. Magrab, S.K. Gupta, F. Patrick, Integrated Product and Process Design and Development-The Product Realization Process, 2nd Edition, CRC press, 2019. Program: B Tech/B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering) Semester: VI / X Course: Fluid Machinery Code: 702ME0E012 Teaching Scheme Evaluation Scheme Lecture (Hours per week) Practical (Hours per week) Tutorial (Hours per week) Credit
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course provides an in-depth understanding of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), commonly known as drones. This course covers the fundamental concepts, design, operation, applications, and regulations related to UAVs and various types of components, sensors, data processing, and hands- on experience in operating UAVs.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the basic principles and working mechanisms of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
Identify various types of UAVs and their applications across different industries
Analyse the challenges and safety concerns associated with UAV technology

units.title: Introduction and Fundamentals of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
units.text: Introduction and Fundamentals of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles History, evolution, and applications, types of vehicles, aerial vehicles: fixed wing, multirotor, etc. Ground vehicles Wheeled, tracked etc. Underwater vehicles Surface vessels and submerged vehicles; and associated subsystems.

units.title: UAV Flight Mechanics
units.text: UAV Flight Mechanics Coordinate frames, transformation matrices, direction cosine matrix, Euler angles, and quaternions. Kinematics and dynamics, forces and moments, general rigid body dynamics, rigid body dynamics for fixed wing, rotary wing vehicles, multi-rotors, underwater and ground vehicles

units.title: Applications of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
units.text: Applications of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Applications of UAVs in Agriculture, Environmental Monitoring, Construction and Infrastructure, Disaster Management, Surveying and Mapping, Filmmaking and Photography. Path planning Schemes for path planning, smooth trajectory generation, waypoint following Guidance Basic concepts of guidance theory, guidance design for trajectory following and tracking

units.title: UAV Regulations and Legal Considerations
units.text: UAV Regulations and Legal Considerations National and international regulations, privacy concerns, and ethical considerations. Control Design of autopilots, integrated and separate control subsystems design, constraints imposed by different types of vehicles Common sensors for unmanned autonomous vehicles, vision-guided navigation

units.title: UAV Security and Safety
units.text: UAV Security and Safety Counter-UAV measures, safety protocols, and risk management. Future Trends in UAV Technology Emerging technologies, AI integration, and beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) operations.

text_books: 1. John W. Leach and Claudio G. R. de Oliveira, UAV Fundamentals: Unmanned Aircraft and Remotely Operated Vehicles, 1st Edition, CRC Press, 2018. 2. George M. Siouris, Introduction to UAV Systems, 1st Edition, Springer, 2011.
reference_books: 1. R. Beard and T. W. McLain, Small Unmanned Aircraft: Theory and Practice, 2nd Edition, Princeton University Press, 2012. 2. Brian Halliday, Drones: Mastering Flight Techniques, 1st Edition, Crowood Press, 2017.

program: B Tech/ B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed to encourage the students to provide a distinctive skill set which is useful in securing employment globally in the automotive or intelligent mobility sectors with the growing demand for highly skilled professionals within automotive manufacturers.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the key principles of navigation and decision making algorithms
Analyze the components of an automotive control systems and its implementation
Evaluate models of vehicle interactions and the movement of groups of vehicles

units.title: Design thinking for EV
units.text: Design thinking for EV Autonomous vehicle sensors and imaging. Sensor integration architectures and multiple sensor fusion. Indoor autonomous surveillance, AI algorithms for sensing and imaging: supervised learning―neural networks.

units.title: Traffic Engineering and intelligent transportation
units.text: Traffic Engineering and intelligent transportation Traffic stream components, intelligent transportation system in India. Principles of path planning, navigation and decision making for autonomous vehicles approaches. Satellite navigation system, simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM). Application examples of path planning, navigation and decision making algorithms.

units.title: Introduction to transport systems and optimization theory
units.text: Introduction to transport systems and optimization theory Advanced optimization techniques, traffic modelling & simulation, electrified transport systems. Optimal energy management system based on driving pattern recognition.

units.title: Modern automotive architectures
units.text: Modern automotive architectures A review of modern automotive control hardware requirements and architectures. The evaluation of current and future vehicle networking technologies.

units.title: Autonomous navigation of EV
units.text: Autonomous navigation of EV An introduction to navigation systems, history, system architecture, application; modes of navigation – land.

units.title: Human-System Interface Design
units.text: Human-System Interface Design Design of safe operating systems and the human-technical interface. Computing systems for autonomous driving: state-of-the-art and challenges, Waymo’s technology.

text_books: 1. Steven Van Uytsel, Autonomous Vehicles, Springer,1st Edition, 2021 2. Ronald K. Jurgen, Autonomous Vehicles for Safer Driving, SAE International, 2013.
reference_books: 1. Shaoshan Liu LIYUN LI Jie Tang Shuang Wu Jean-Luc Gaudiot Creating Autonomous Vehicle Systems, Morgan & Claypool Publishers, 2017. 2. Anthony Raymond How Autonomous Vehicles will Change the World, Clever Gizmos LLC, 2020.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mechanics and Strength of Materials
objectives: To provide an understanding of the basics of aerodynamics in aircraft. To impart knowledge of boundary layer theory. To introduce the aerospace vehicle and space vehicle design. To introduce wind tunnel testing

outcomes.text: Analyse the basic flight mathematical aspects and potential flows
Discuss structural design of aircraft and space vehicles
Classify types of wind tunnel and describe wind tunnel testing technique

units.title: Introduction to Aerodynamics
units.text: Introduction to Aerodynamics Importance of Aerodynamic, four principles of aerodynamics, three laws of aerodynamics, six fundamentals of flight.

units.title: Applied Aerodynamics
units.text: Applied Aerodynamics Panel methods, pressure distribution, Kutta conditions, flow around airfoil (unsteady potential flow, compressible flow, axisymmetric flow) and slender body theories. Flight vehicle aerodynamics, rotor aerodynamics – low Reynolds number aerodynamics

units.title: Aircraft Vehicle Design
units.text: Aircraft Vehicle Design Design considerations for civilian and military aircraft, weight estimation, airfoil and geometry selection, thrust to weight ratio and wing loading, initial sizing, propulsion, landing gear and subsystems, aerodynamics, stability, control, and handling qualities, flight mechanics and performance issues, aircraft layout and configuration, structural aspects and constraint analysis.

units.title: Space Vehicle Design
units.text: Space Vehicle Design History of rocketry & launch vehicles, Current & future launch vehicles. Orbit/trajectory requirements and missions. Launch vehicle sizing, launch into an orbit, rocket propulsion (configuration and structural design), design for re-entry

units.title: Wind Tunnel Techniques
units.text: Wind Tunnel Techniques Introduction to wind tunnel, Classification of wind tunnels, Elements of wind tunnel, Conventional measurement techniques, wind tunnel testing technique.

text_books: 1. John D. Anderson, Fundamentals of aerodynamics, NY: McGraw-Hill Education, 6th edition, 2017. 2. Robert F. Stengel, Flight dynamics, Princeton University Press, 2nd Edition, 2022.
reference_books: 1. Bertin, J. J. and Cummings, R. M., Aerodynamics for Engineers, Prentice Hall, 6th edition, 2013. 2. Houghton, E. L., Carpenter, P. W., Collicott, S. H., and Valentine, D. T., Aerodynamics for Engineering Students, Butterworth-Heinemann, 6th Edition, 2012.

program: B Tech /B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed to impart knowledge of an IC engine and the ignition systems. It also introduces the modern developments in internal combustion engines with optical measurement techniques and emission control.

outcomes.text: Explain advanced engine technologies and emission norms
Apply concepts of different alternate fuels used for SI and CI engines
Analyze environmental, social, and technological issues related to the future widespread use of internal combustion engines

units.title: Basic Characteristics of Engines
units.text: Basic Characteristics of Engines Compression ratio, energy supply to an engine, power developed by engine, specific weight and specific volume, cylinder pressures, indicated mean effective pressure determination, torque characteristics, cylinder arrangement and their relative merits. Engine Cooling Systems Types of cooling, cooling of critical engine components, re-cooling the coolant, comparison of air cooled and liquid cooled engines.

units.title: Fuel Delivery in Spark Ignition Engines
units.text: Fuel Delivery in Spark Ignition Engines Classification of fuel delivery systems, fuel transfer pumps, fixed jet carburetor, computer controlled carburetor, gasoline injection systems. Ignition Systems in Spark Ignition Engines Battery ignition system, requirements for satisfactory operation of the ignition system, ignition timing and advancing mechanisms, magneto ignition system, electronic ignition system.

units.title: Combustion and Combustion Systems in Compression Ignition Engines
units.text: Combustion and Combustion Systems in Compression Ignition Engines Air motion in compression ignition engines, delay period in compression ignition engines, types of diesel combustion systems. Scavenging and Super Charging in Compression Ignition Engines Types of scavenging systems, improved and modified scavenging systems, super charging and engine performance, methods of super charging.

units.title: Modern Developments in Internal Combustion Engines
units.text: Modern Developments in Internal Combustion Engines Exhaust gas recirculation, multi point fuel injection, gasoline direct engine, homogeneous charge compression ignition and turbo-charging. Optical Measurement Techniques and Tools Particle image velocimetry (PIV), 3D and Holographic PIV, spray visualization, phase doppler interferometry for spray characterization, optical engines and engine endoscopy, use of nanoparticles in internal combustion engines.

units.title: Automobile Emissions and Its Control
units.text: Automobile Emissions and Its Control Need for emission control, classification/ categories of emissions, major pollutants, control of emissions, evaluating vehicle emissions, European emission standards, Indian emission standards, pollution monitoring instruments and techniques, Control measures such as diesel oxidation catalyst, diesel particulate filter, selective catalytic reduction and lean NOx trap.

text_books: 1. Ganesan, V, Internal Combustion Engines, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Book Co., 2017. 2. John B. Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, 2nd Edition McGraw Hill Book, 2018.
reference_books: 1. Amitava Datta, Avinash Kumar Agarwal, Dhananjay Kumar Srivastava, Rakesh Kumar Maurya, Advances in Internal Combustion Engine Research, Springer Singapore, 2017. 2. Richard Stone, Introduction to Internal Combustion Engines, Macmillan Education UK, 2012.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mechanics, Fluid Mechanics and Strength of Materials
objectives: This course introduces the basic concepts of vibrations and discusses free vibration of an undamped single-degree of-freedom system. This course also deals with two-degree-of-freedom systems, which require two independent coordinates to describe their motion. The modeling of continuous systems as multidegree-of-freedom systems is also presented in this course.

outcomes.text: Derive the equation of motion of a single-degree-of-freedom system
Solve two-degree-of-freedom free- and forced-vibration problems
Formulate the equations of motion of multidegree-of-freedom systems

units.title: Fundamentals of Vibration
units.text: Fundamentals of Vibration Basic Concepts of Vibration, Classification of Vibration, Vibration Analysis Procedure, Spring Elements, Mass or Inertia Elements, Damping Elements, Harmonic Motion, Harmonic Analysis

units.title: Single-Degree-of-Freedom Systems
units.text: Single-Degree-of-Freedom Systems Free Vibration of an Undamped Translational System, Free Vibration of an Undamped Torsional System, Free Vibration with Viscous Damping, Free Vibration with Coulomb Damping.

units.title: Two-Degree-of-Freedom Systems
units.text: Two-Degree-of-Freedom Systems Equations of Motion for Forced Vibration, Free Vibration Analysis of an Undamped System, Torsional System, Forced-Vibration Analysis.

units.title: Multidegree-of-Freedom Systems
units.text: Multidegree-of-Freedom Systems Modeling of Continuous Systems as Multi degree of Freedom Systems, Equations of Motion, Influence Coefficients, Generalized Coordinates and Generalized Forces, Lagrange s Equations, Equations of Motion of Undamped Systems in Matrix Form, Eigenvalue Problem

text_books: 1. S. S. Rao, Mechanical Vibration, Addison Wesley, 2004. 2. Michel Géradin and Daniel J. Rixen, Mechanical Vibrations Theory and Application to Structural Dynamics, John Wiley & Sons, 2015.
reference_books: 1. J. S. Rao, Advanced Theory of Vibration, New Age international, 1994. 2. S. Graham Kelley (2000), Fundamentals of Mechanical Vibrations, McGraw Hill, 2000.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: The main purpose of this course is to introduce students with renewable energy resources availability, potential and suitability as a substitute for conventional energy resources in future energy demands.

outcomes.text: Identify sustainable energy solutions for sustainable development
Analyze renewable energy resources availability and utilization
Demonstrate competency in renewable systems analysis independently

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Renewable and non-renewable energy sources, global and Indian scenario. Energy Alternatives The solar option, nuclear option, tar sands and oil shale, tidal energy, geothermal energy.

units.title: Solar Energy
units.text: Solar Energy Solar radiation, availability, measurement and estimation, solar thermal conversion devices such as flat plate collector, tubular collector, solar air collector, solar concentrator and storage. Applications Crop drying, distillation, water heating, electric power generation. Solar Photovoltaic Photovoltaic cell technologies, generations of solar cell, electrical characteristics, photovoltaic module and array, photovoltaic module system components and design.

units.title: Biomass Energy Conversion
units.text: Biomass Energy Conversion Biomass characteristics and their availability, biofuel production processes, bio-methane, bio-hydrogen, alcoholic fermentation, biodiesel, microbial fuel cell, biomass based steam power plant, combined cycle power plant, cogeneration plant, Energy from Waste.

units.title: Wind Energy
units.text: Wind Energy Wind turbines, aerodynamics, types of turbines wind energy conversion system, wind turbine generator types, advantages and disadvantages. Hydro Power Water turbines, hydroelectric system theory, measurement and components, advantages and disadvantages of hydroelectric system.

units.title: Geothermal Energy
units.text: Geothermal Energy Structure of earth, geothermal resources, exploration of geothermal energy. OTEC Principle, applications. Tidal principle, power calculation, tidal modes of operation. Wave wave motion, energy conversion and devices applications.

units.title: Economic Analysis
units.text: Economic Analysis Initial and annual costs, present worth calculation, annual savings, payback period.

text_books: 1. Vaughn C. Nelson, Kenneth L. Starcher, Introduction to Renewable Energy (Energy and the Environment, CRC Press, UK, 2016. 2. B. K Khan, Non-Conventional Energy Resources, TMH New Delhi, 2013. 3. J. A. Duffie and W. A. Beckman, Solar Engineering of Thermal Processes, John Wiley, New York, 2013.
reference_books: 1. D. Y. Goswami, F. Kreith and J. F. Kreider, Principles of Solar Engineering, Taylor and Francis, Philadelphia, 2015. 2. S. P. Sukhatme, Solar Energy - Principles of thermal collection and storage, Tata McGraw-Hill, New Delhi, 2008. (Classic Book) 3. J. Twidell and T. Weir, Renewable Energy Resources, E & F N Spon Ltd, London, 1986. (Classic Book)

program: B Tech / MBA Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS), B Tech & MBA Tech Mechanical, B Tech Mechatronics
objectives: The objective of the course is to familiarize with basic knowledge of Additive Manufacturing (AM) and its capabilities in the modern digital manufacturing industries. It teaches about various additive manufacturing techniques.

outcomes.text: Compare the fundamental principles of various additive manufacturing technologies in terms of material requirements, manufacturing technologies and applications
Identify critical areas where AM can be applied to create value for the product
Apply the necessary skills in selecting the right AM process for a given application

units.title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
units.text: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing Introduction to AM, history of AM, definition, distinction between AM, CNC & other digital manufacturing techniques, reasons to use AM, classifications of AM processes, design for additive manufacturing (DfAM), AM industry: present and future, AM process chain, AM file formats (STL, 3MF, AMF, PLY, VRML, and LEO), part orientation, support generation, model slicing, contour generation, machine set-up, build file preparation.

units.title: Classification of Additive Manufacturing Techniques
units.text: Classification of Additive Manufacturing Techniques Material Extrusion: Process mechanism, process parameters, extrusion of: ceramics, metals, biomaterials, composites, contour crafting, concrete printing Vat Polymerization: Process mechanism, process parameters, advantages, disadvantages, applications, Digital Light Processing (DLP), recent advances, Large-Scale Rapid Liquid Printing. Binder & material jetting processes: Binder jettng process workflow, material requirements, binder-powder interaction, binder properties. Material Jetting process workflow, thermal and piezoelectric inkjet, material jetting fluid mechanics, drop-on-demand and continuous methods of MJ. Powder bed fusion AM process: Selective laser sintering (SLS), process mechanism, process parameters, selective laser melting (SLM), process workflow and material requirements, powder melting mechanisms, electron beam melting (EBM) process. Sheet Lamination AM Processes: Process mechanism, process parameters, ultrasonic additive manufacturing (UAM), ultrasonic welding fundamentals, UAM process parameters Directed Energy Deposition (DED) Processes: Process workflow, materials feeding for DED: powder (Laser Engineered Net Shaping) and wire, process parameters, cold spray.

units.title: Post- Processing
units.text: Post- Processing Product quality evaluation, need for post-processing, support material removal, surface finish improvement, aesthetic improvement, property enhancements using non-thermal and thermal techniques.

units.title: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM)
units.text: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM) Design guidelines: part orientation, support, geometry considerations, layer thickness, part size, material consideration, residual stress, topology optimization, case studies on design for AM.

units.title: Applications of AM & Industry 4.0
units.text: Applications of AM & Industry 4.0 Aerospace, biomedical, defence, automobile, rapid tooling, reverse engineering, economic consideration, Industry 4.0 for AM, case studies on application of AM in various industries.

text_books: 1. Gibson I, Rosen D W, Stucker B, Additive Manufacturing Technologies: Rapid Prototyping to Direct Digital Manufacturing, 2nd Edition, Springer, 2015. 2. Filemon Schöffer, Ben Redwood, Brian Garret, The 3D Printing Handbook: Technologies, design and applications, 3D Hubs, 2017. References Books 1. Yang, L., Hsu, K., Baughman, B., Godfrey, D., Medina, F., Menon, M., & Wiener, S., Additive manufacturing of metals: the technology, materials, design and production, Springer, Edition 2017. 2. Gebhardt, Andreas, Understanding additive manufacturing, 2nd Edition, Hanser Publication, 2018.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: The objective of this course is to help the students understand the principles and applications relevant to the planning, design, and operations of manufacturing or service firms. This course also develops an understanding about quality management practices in organizations that facilitate organizational effectiveness.

outcomes.text: Develop an understanding of manufacturing and service operations management as a subject and outline the strategic concerns involved in operations decisions
Apply the principles, philosophy underpinning inventory management techniques, just- in-time and MRP systems along with their limitations
Analyze the economic aspects related to production management

units.title: Concept of Production Management
units.text: Concept of Production Management Meaning of production, production process system, scope of production management, objectives of production management, functions and scopes of production management, scope of production management, brief history of production management, responsibilities of production manager.

units.title: Productivity
units.text: Productivity Introduction, meaning of productivity, factors affecting on productivity, productivity improvement, measurement of productivity.

units.title: Economic Analysis
units.text: Economic Analysis Factors to be considered in product design. production cost concepts; fixed cost, variable cost, break even analysis, P-V chart, and make-buy decision.

units.title: Plant Location and Plant Layout
units.text: Plant Location and Plant Layout Meaning of plant layout, objective of a good plant layout, factors to be considered in plant location, types of plant layout, process layout. techniques of plant layout, concept of group technology, group layout.

units.title: Production Planning and Control (PPC)
units.text: Production Planning and Control (PPC) Objective of PPC, functions of PPC, capacity planning, manufacturing resource planning and scheduling, JIT system, Kanban pull system of scheduling, line balancing.

units.title: Materials Management
units.text: Materials Management Bill of materials, quantity planning, inventory control, economic order quantity (EOQ), lead time, consumption rate, different ordering systems, Q system, P system, the store’s function and ABC analysis.

units.title: Quality
units.text: Quality Introduction to quality control, quality management, function of quality, quality control stages, function of inspection, statistical quality control, statistical quality control, control charts, acceptance sampling.

text_books: 1. S. N. Chary, Production and Operations Management, 6th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2019. 2. Bedi Kanishka, Production and Operations Management, 3rd Edition, Oxford University Press, 2016.
reference_books: 1. S. Gupta and M. Starr, Introduction to Production and Operations Management, RC Press, 1st Edition, 2014. 2. R. Panneerselvam, Production and Operations Management, 3rd Edition, PHI Learning, 2012.

program: B Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: This course introduces aspects of project management such as formulation, budgeting, planning, scheduling and control of projects from initiation to completion.

outcomes.text: Interpret the project feasibility and identify the role of project manager
Relate the resources and durations using scheduling tools and techniques
Plan the costs and risks of projects
Apply the tools for monitoring the progress of projects

units.title: Introduction to Project Management
units.text: Introduction to Project Management Definition, classification of project management in different environments, scope, systems approach, project feasibility, project life cycle, systems development cycle phases.

units.title: Project Organization
units.text: Project Organization Project organization, types of structures, roles of project managers and team, integration in large scale projects.

units.title: Project Planning and Scheduling
units.text: Project Planning and Scheduling Planning fundamentals, project master plan, work breakdown structure and other tools of project planning, work packages, project organization structure and responsibilities, responsibility matrix, use of Gantt charts, critical path method (CPM) and project evaluation and review technique (PERT) for scheduling and resource allocation, introduction to software tools for documentation, scheduling, analysis etc.

units.title: Cost Estimating and Budgeting
units.text: Cost Estimating and Budgeting Cost estimating process, elements of budgeting, project cost accounting and management information systems, cost schedules and forecasts.

units.title: Project Risk Management
units.text: Project Risk Management Risk concepts and identification, risk response planning, risk management methods, information monitoring, control process, cost accounting systems for project control, performance analysis.

units.title: Evaluation and Termination
units.text: Evaluation and Termination Project evaluation and reporting, closing the contract.

text_books: 1. Jack R Meredith, Samuel J Mantel, Shafer Project Management –A Managerial Approach, 8th Edition, Wiley Publications, 2017. 2. Erik W Larson, Clifford F Gray, Rohit Joshi, Project Management the Managerial Process, 8th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Dennis Lock, The Essentials of Project and Programme Management, 4th Edition, Routledge Publications, 2017. 2. Prasanna Chandra, Projects: Planning, Analysis, Selection, Financing Implementation and Review, 8th Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017.

program: B Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS)
objectives: This course focusses on a critical understanding and strategic importance of operations management. The students can get familiar with interactions between firms based on parameters such as information sharing, contracting and coordination in supply chain management.

outcomes.text: Evaluate the application of operations management policies and techniques to the service sector as well as manufacturing firms
Analyze and organize Global Network Logistics for trade and transport systems, sourcing and procurement
Apply the latest developments in information technology to supply chain management in order to generate greater benefit

units.title: Production Concepts
units.text: Production Concepts Introduction, meaning, nature and scope of production and operations management. Difference between production and operations management. Productivity, factors affecting productivity and productivity measurement. Work study— Method study and work measurement. Production Technology – Types of manufacturing processes. Plant location and types of plant layout.

units.title: Material and Inventory Management
units.text: Material and Inventory Management Types of production planning, process of production planning and control (PPC) – routing, scheduling and loading. Master production schedule, aggregate production planning. Types of inventories, inventory control techniques- EOQ, ABC, VED, FSN, HML and SDE (Simple numerical problems on Inventory control techniques).

units.title: Building a Strategic Framework to Analyze Supply Chain
units.text: Building a Strategic Framework to Analyze Supply Chain Supply chain stages and decision phases, Process View of Supply Chain: Supply Chain Flows, Examples of Supply Chain, Competitive and Supply Chain Strategies, achieving strategic fit: Expanding strategic scope, Drivers of supply chain performance, Framework for structuring drivers: inventory, transportation facilities, information obstacles to achieving fit.

units.title: Designing the Supply Chain Network
units.text: Designing the Supply Chain Network Distribution networking: Role, Design, Supply Chain Network (SCN): Role, Factors, framework for design decisions.

units.title: Warehouse and Transportation Management
units.text: Warehouse and Transportation Management Concept of strategic storage, Warehouse functionality, Warehouse operating principles, Developing warehouse resources, Material handling and packaging in warehouse, Transportation management, Transport functionality and principles, Transport infrastructure, Transport economics and pricing, Transport decision making

units.title: IT in Supply Chain
units.text: IT in Supply Chain IT framework, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Internal supply chain management, supplier Relationship Management (SRM) and transaction management. Coordination in supply chain: Lack of supply chain coordination and the Bullwhip effect, Obstacle to coordination, Managerial levers, Building partnership and trust, Emerging trends and issues. Vendor managed inventory 3PL-4PL, Reverse logistics: Reasons, Role, Activities; RFID systems: Components, Applications, Implementation; Lean supply chain, Implementation of Six Sigma in supply chain, Green supply chain.

text_books: 1. Sunil Chopra, Peter Meindl, Supply Chain Management Strategy, Planning and Operations, 6th Edition, Pearson, 2016. 2. Chase, R.B., Shankar, R. & Jacobs, F.R., Operations & Supply Chain Management, 14th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Robert B. Handfield, Ernest L. Nichols, Introduction to Supply Chain Management, Prentice Hall PTR, 2007. (Classic Book) 2. Bedi, Kanishka, Production & Operations Management, 3rd Edition, Oxford University Press, 2013.

program: B Tech /B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, Differential and Integral Calculus
objectives: This course is designed to provide knowledge of different modes of heat transfer with different laws of conduction, convection and radiation. It also helps to provide understanding of different applications of conduction, convection and radiation.

outcomes.text: Identify and explain different modes of heat transfer
Applying heat transfer principles to calculate heat transfer rates in steady and transient state conditions in different geometries and fins
Analysing forced and natural convection heat transfer, including the use of empirical correlations to determine convection heat transfer
Apply radiation heat transfer principles to calculate heat exchange between surfaces with different emissivity and geometries
Apply basic principles of heat transfer to design heat transfer devices
Analyze real-world engineering problems using heat transfer principles

units.title: Basic Concepts
units.text: Basic Concepts Modes of Heat Transfer, its mechanism and mathematical models. Conduction Heat Transfer Fourier’s general conduction equation in Cartesian, Cylindrical and Spherical co- ordinates (for cylindrical and spherical walls derivation of Fourier’s three- dimensional equation is not included), thermal resistance, solution of Fourier’s equation for one dimensional steady state heat conduction through various configurations such as plane, cylindrical, spherical wall, composite medium. Critical thickness of insulation and its importance. Heat Transfer from Extended Surfaces Types of fins, Governing equation, fin effectiveness, efficiency of fins, concept of corrected fin length, application of fins. Unsteady State Heat Conduction Lumped System Analysis

units.title: Convection Heat Transfer
units.text: Convection Heat Transfer Forced and natural convection, hydrodynamic and thermal boundary layer, Convection heat transfer coefficient, Momentum and energy equation for laminar boundary layer, Laminar and Turbulent flow, principles of dimensional analysis, physical significance of dimensionless numbers, Nusselt number, Prandtl number, Reynolds number, Grashof number. Empirical relations and their use for forced internal and external convection for circular and non-circular ducts. Empirical relations and their use for free convection on vertical, horizontal flat plate and cylinders. Boiling and Condensation Physical phenomenon and Pool boiling curve.

units.title: Thermal Radiation
units.text: Thermal Radiation Introduction to physical mechanism, concept of black body, grey body and radiation properties. Microwave Heating. Basic laws of radiation; Planck’s law, Kirchoff’s law, Stefan-Boltzman law, Wein’s- displacement law and Lambert’s Cosine law, Intensity of radiation, radiosity, shape factor for simple geometries, heat exchange between non-black bodies, Radiation Shield.

units.title: Heat Exchangers
units.text: Heat Exchangers Classification, temperature distribution in parallel and counter flow arrangement, overall heat transfer coefficient, fouling factor, log mean temperature difference method, Effectiveness-NTU method.

text_books: 1. Theodore Bergman & Adrienne Lavine, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, 8th Edition, Wiley Publication 2017. 2. C.P. Kothandaraman & S. Subramanyan, Heat and Mass Transfer Data Book, 9th Edition, New Age International 2018.
reference_books: 1. P.K Nag, Heat and Mass Transfer, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2016. 2. Frank P Incropera and D.P. Dewitt, Introduction to Heat Transfer, John Wiley & Sons, 2011.
lab_work: 8 to 10 Experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech /B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Graphics and Design, Manufacturing Processes-I, Manufacturing Processes-II
objectives: The principal objective of this course is to introduce basics of backend of drafting packages and to give hands on experience on the 3D modeling software. The course has been structured to impart knowledge of NC/CNC machines and programming of CNC using machine codes along with providing concepts of GT, CAPP, CAQC and CIM.

outcomes.text: Understand the application of computers in design process and product life cycle management
Demonstrate mathematical models to represent various curves
Apply the CAD modeling knowledge for modeling of mechanical parts and assemblies
Analyze various geometric transformation and manipulation techniques
Develop CNC part programs to manufacture industrial components
Explain concept of group technology, computer aided quality control and computer integrated manufacturing

units.title: Introduction and Elements of Interactive Computer Graphics
units.text: Introduction and Elements of Interactive Computer Graphics The design process, computers for design process, product life cycle and CAD/CAM, concurrent engineering in product design and development, collaborative engineering, CAD system architecture - software and hardware, the role of modeling and communication, modeling using CAD

units.title: Techniques for Geometric Modeling
units.text: Techniques for Geometric Modeling Graphic standards, the parametric representation of geometry - Bezier curves, cubic spline curve, B-spline curve, parametric representation of line, circle, ellipse and parabola, constructive solid geometry (CSG), boundary representation (B-rep), wire frame modeling, solid modeling, surface modeling, feature based modeling, assembly modeling - different approaches of creating an assembly, parent child relationship

Transformation, Manipulation and Data Storage 2D and 3D transformations (translation, rotation, scaling and magnification), concatenations, matrix representation, problems on transformations. object transformation, mirror transformation, bill of materials from attribute data, engineering data management system, relational data base for design, object oriental database, design information systems

units.title: NC and CNC Technology
units.text: NC and CNC Technology Introduction, basic components of NC system, NC procedure, NC coordinate systems, NC motion control systems, various actuation systems and feedback devices like encoder, tachogenerator etc., applications, advantages and disadvantages of NC machines, constructional details of CNC machines, CNC programming concepts, manual part programming methods, various G and M codes, absolute and incremental system, tool length and diameter compensation, programming of turning and milling, use of canned cycles, subroutines, flexible manufacturing systems (FMS), machining centers and its types, automated material handling and storage systems like robots, automated guided vehicles (AGV) and automated storage and retrieval systems

units.title: Group Technology (GT), CAPP and CAQC
units.text: Group Technology (GT), CAPP and CAQC Introduction to GT, part families, part classification and coding, GT machines cells, benefits of GT introduction to computer aided process planning (CAPP), retrieval type process planning systems, generative type process planning systems, benefits of CAPP, production flow analysis (PFA), similarity coefficient matrix, introduction to computer aided quality control (CAQC), computers in QC, contact inspection methods, non-contact inspection methods, integration of CAQC with CAD/CAM

units.title: Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM) and Technology Driven
units.text: Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM) and Technology Driven Practices Introduction, evolution, objectives, CIM hardware and software, CIM benefits, nature and role of elements of CIM, identifying CIM needs, data base requirements of CIM, role of CAD/CAM in CIM, obstacles to computer integrated manufacturing, CIM wheel, design for manufacturing and design for assembly, introduction to rapid prototyping, virtual prototyping

text_books: 1. P. N. Rao, CAD/CAM Principles and Applications, Tata McGraw Hill Publications, 3rd edition, 2017. 2. Groover, Mikell, and E. W. J. R. Zimmers, CAD/CAM: computer-aided design and manufacturing, Pearson Education., 1st edition, 2003.
reference_books: 1. Ibrahim Zeid, R. Sivasubramanian, CAD/CAM, Theory and Practice, Tata McGraw Hill Publications. 2nd edition, 2009. 2. P. Radhakrishan, S. Subramanyan, V. Raju, CAD/CAM/CIM, New Age International Publishers, 1st edition, 2007.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech/ B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Thermodynamics, Applied Thermodynamics, Heat Transfer
objectives: This course focuses in detail on industrial refrigeration and air-conditioning systems, which are crucial to modern space conditioning. Additionally, it aims to impart knowledge regarding the choice of HVAC plant equipment and control systems.

outcomes.text: Apply HVAC theory in the design and selection of HVACR plant equipment
Analyze the different air conditioning and industrial refrigeration systems
Explain different components and control systems in the HVAC and refrigeration industry

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Introduction of HVACR, requirement of a space conditioning, Psychrometric chart, psychrometric processes, Cooling/heating load, latent heat/ sensible heat load, cooling load calculations. Energy-efficient HVAC design. Classification of Air Conditioning Systems Window air-conditioner, split air-conditioner, dessert Cooler, air-washer, chillers, VRV system, cassette, roof tops, FCUs.

units.title: Components of Refrigeration Plant
units.text: Components of Refrigeration Plant Types of compressors, types of evaporators, types of condensers, types of throttling devices, ventilation and air filtration, cooling towers.

units.title: Industrial Refrigeration System
units.text: Industrial Refrigeration System Vapour absorption refrigeration system- Ammonia vapor absorption system, Lithium bromide absorption system, capacity control.

units.title: Controls in HVAC Systems
units.text: Controls in HVAC Systems Operating controls, temperature controls, humidistats and air stats, primary and secondary controllers pneumatic control, variable frequency drive, safety controls, pressure switches, antifreeze thermostat. Equipment Selection Chiller selection, compressor selection, condenser selection, selection of thermostatic expansion valve, pipe sizing.

text_books: 1. Frank Kreith, Shan K. Wang, Paul Norton, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Engineering, CRC Press, 2018. 2. P. N. Ananthanarayanan, Basic Refrigeration and Air Conditioning, McGraw-Hill Education, 2005.
reference_books: 1. Wilbert F. Stoecker, Jerold W. Jones, Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning, 1982 (Classic Book). 2. Javed Khazaii, Energy-efficient HVAC design, Springer 2014.

program: B Tech/B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The objective of this course is to give the students a systematic and comprehensive understanding of various aspects related to industrial engineering and its relevance in the industrial environment.

outcomes.text: Describe the concepts of productivity and methods to improve efficiency
Apply the methods to measure parameters such as time and magnitude of activities performed
Analyze the cost effectiveness of each function of the product in terms of usefulness to the customer

units.title: Productivity
units.text: Productivity Productivity concepts. Analysing the work content of a job to identify and reduce/eliminate the excess work content. Interdependence between working conditions and productivity. Significance of theory of Scientific Management. Improving Efficiency and Productivity through Work-study, Work-study components. Relationship between Method Study and Time Study.

units.title: Method Study
units.text: Method Study Basic procedure of method study. Factors in selecting a job to a studied. Recording the facts with charts and diagrams. Questioning technique for development of new method. Role of Management and workers in implementation.

units.title: Facilities & Workplace Design
units.text: Facilities & Workplace Design Aligning the physical facilities- plant layout, equipment and work flow as per the production processes. Principles of Motion Economy. Standardization of the process.

units.title: Work Measurement
units.text: Work Measurement Significance of work measurement. Techniques of work measurement. Need of work sampling technique. Conducting work sampling study. Analytical estimation of work. Concept of rating factor. Consideration of various allowances. Standard time for work. Predetermined time standards. Use standard data. MOST for work measurement. Use of time standards.

units.title: Ergonomics
units.text: Ergonomics Field of Ergonomics. Physical and cognitive issues of ergonomics. Aims of ergonomics considerations. Working postures of operatives. Design of objects, facilities and environment. Anthropometrical details. Database of human factors. Ergonomic improvement of physical and cognitive issues. Ergonomics principals. Information input and human control of systems. Work space and arrangement. Living environment. Visual displays

units.title: Value Engineering
units.text: Value Engineering Definition of Value Engineering, Uses of Value Engineering, Reasons for unnecessary costs, Difference between Value Engineering and other cost reduction techniques. Case studies

text_books: 1. International Labour Office, Introduction to Work Study, 3rd edition, Oxford & I. B. H. Publishing Co. Ltd, 2015. 2. R. Barnes, Motion and Time Study Design and Measurement of Work, 7th edition, Asia Publishing, 2009.
reference_books: 1. M. S. Sanders & E J McCormick, Human factors in Engineering & Design, Tata McGraw Hill, 2020. 2. Merton E. Davis, William D. Falcon, Value Engineering: The Implications for Managers, American Management Association, 2002.

program: B Tech/B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed to encourage the students to understand the role of fluid power in automation. It helps them to identify the various components of an automation system and design circuits to control the physical output work.

outcomes.text: Relate hydraulic power, hydraulic actuators and motors
Analyze the different components of hydraulic systems
Identify different pneumatic controls, actuators and control valves

units.title: Introduction to Hydraulic Power
units.text: Introduction to Hydraulic Power Role of drive-in automation system, comparison of drives. Definition of hydraulic system, advantages, limitations, applications, Pascal's law, structure of hydraulic control system, problems on Pascal's law. The source of Hydraulic Power: Pumps Classification of pumps, pumping theory of positive displacement pumps, construction and working of Gear pumps and Vane pumps.

units.title: Hydraulic Systems
units.text: Hydraulic Systems Hydraulic Power Pack, Hydraulic Accumulator, Symbolic representation and working of Control Valves – Direction Control Valves, Flow Control Valves, Check valves, shuttle valves, pressure valves. Use of valves for speed and pressure control. Hydraulic circuits in power tools and other applications.

units.title: Pneumatic Systems
units.text: Pneumatic Systems Definition of pneumatic system, advantages, limitations, applications, Choice of working medium. Characteristics of compressed air. Structure of Pneumatic control System, Direction control valves, single and double acting linear actuator; direct and indirect control of DCV, Speed control circuits.

units.title: Fluid power circuits with electrical control
units.text: Fluid power circuits with electrical control Ladder Logic Diagram, Electro-hydraulic/pneumatic control, Use of relays and limit switches, Sequencing Circuits with and without electrical control, multi- cylinder circuit applications.

text_books: 1. Anthony Esposito, Fluid Power with Applications, 7th Edition, Pearson Education, 2008. 2. M. Galal Rabie, Fluid Power Engineering, 1st Edition, McGraw- Hill, 2009.
reference_books: 1. Andrew Parr, Hydraulics and Pneumatics- A technician’s and engineer’s guide, 3rd Edition, Butterworth-Heinemann Ltd, 2011. 2. Ilango Sivaraman, Introduction to Hydraulics and Pneumatics, 3rd Edition, PHI Learning Pvt. Ltd., 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech/B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course provides the understanding of the development and design aspects of products, impart knowledge of business and technical concerns about the different methodologies of product development. This course also discusses the concept of product life cycle and product data management.

outcomes.text: Identify the different stages of product development and design with modern approaches
Apply the knowledge of Technology Forecasting using S-Curve in product development as per customers need
Describe the process of benchmarking of products, technologies & techniques product design

units.title: Introduction to Product Design and Development
units.text: Introduction to Product Design and Development Definition of product design, product development versus product design, types of design and redesign, design by evolution and innovation, factors in product design, morphology of product design (seven phases), standardization, simplification and specialization in product design, product life cycle and its various phases, modern approaches- concurrent design in product development, product development team and product development planning with reference to ISO standard, new product development process/stages, difference between product verification and production validation.

units.title: Product Development – Technical and Business Concerns
units.text: Product Development – Technical and Business Concerns Technology forecasting and Technology S-curve, Kano model, Mission statement and technical questioning. Economic analysis of product, customer needs and satisfaction, customer population and market segmentation, gathering customer needs information, analysis of gathered information.

units.title: Product Development from Concept to Product Function
units.text: Product Development from Concept to Product Function Generating concepts, information gathering and brainstorming, morphological analysis, concept selection-design evaluation, estimation of technical feasibility, concept selection process, Pugh’s concept, selection charts, numerical concept scoring, process of concept embodiment, system modeling, Failure Mode Effect Analysis (FMEA), functional modeling and decomposition, fast method, subtract and operate procedure, establishing system functionality.

units.title: Quality function deployment (QFD)
units.text: Quality function deployment (QFD) Quality function deployment studies to validate design characteristics; Affinity diagram, Tree diagram, Matrix diagram, Prioritization matrix; Design validation.

units.title: Design for ‘X’ (DFX)
units.text: Design for ‘X’ (DFX) Design for manufacture, assembly, testing, maintenance, service, reliability, environmental sustainability; introduction to prototyping, rapid prototyping methods. Product safety and hazard evaluation; Final disposal; Reverse Engineering; Managing Competitiveness- benchmarking, outsourcing and mass customization.

text_books: 1. K. Otto and K. Wood, Product Design –Techniques in Reverse Engineering and New Product Development, 7th Edition, Pearson Education, 2020. 2. K. T. Ulrich and S. D. Eppinger, Product Design and Development, 6th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2015.
reference_books: 1. E. B. Magrab, S.K. Gupta, F. Patrick, Integrated Product and Process Design and Development-The Product Realization Process, 2nd Edition, CRC press, 2019.
