program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course provides an in-depth understanding of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), commonly known as drones. This course covers the fundamental concepts, design, operation, applications, and regulations related to UAVs and various types of components, sensors, data processing, and hands- on experience in operating UAVs.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the basic principles and working mechanisms of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
Identify various types of UAVs and their applications across different industries
Analyse the challenges and safety concerns associated with UAV technology

units.title: Introduction and Fundamentals of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
units.text: Introduction and Fundamentals of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles History, evolution, and applications, types of vehicles, aerial vehicles: fixed wing, multirotor, etc. Ground vehicles Wheeled, tracked etc. Underwater vehicles Surface vessels and submerged vehicles; and associated subsystems.

units.title: UAV Flight Mechanics
units.text: UAV Flight Mechanics Coordinate frames, transformation matrices, direction cosine matrix, Euler angles, and quaternions. Kinematics and dynamics, forces and moments, general rigid body dynamics, rigid body dynamics for fixed wing, rotary wing vehicles, multi-rotors, underwater and ground vehicles

units.title: Applications of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
units.text: Applications of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Applications of UAVs in Agriculture, Environmental Monitoring, Construction and Infrastructure, Disaster Management, Surveying and Mapping, Filmmaking and Photography. Path planning Schemes for path planning, smooth trajectory generation, waypoint following Guidance Basic concepts of guidance theory, guidance design for trajectory following and tracking

units.title: UAV Regulations and Legal Considerations
units.text: UAV Regulations and Legal Considerations National and international regulations, privacy concerns, and ethical considerations. Control Design of autopilots, integrated and separate control subsystems design, constraints imposed by different types of vehicles Common sensors for unmanned autonomous vehicles, vision-guided navigation

units.title: UAV Security and Safety
units.text: UAV Security and Safety Counter-UAV measures, safety protocols, and risk management. Future Trends in UAV Technology Emerging technologies, AI integration, and beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) operations.

text_books: 1. John W. Leach and Claudio G. R. de Oliveira, UAV Fundamentals: Unmanned Aircraft and Remotely Operated Vehicles, 1st Edition, CRC Press, 2018. 2. George M. Siouris, Introduction to UAV Systems, 1st Edition, Springer, 2011.
reference_books: 1. R. Beard and T. W. McLain, Small Unmanned Aircraft: Theory and Practice, 2nd Edition, Princeton University Press, 2012. 2. Brian Halliday, Drones: Mastering Flight Techniques, 1st Edition, Crowood Press, 2017.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course objectives focus on developing expertise in Teamcenter architecture, organizational management, workflow configuration, BMIDE-based data model setup, and utility usage for various system requirements.

outcomes.text: Gain in depth knowledge of Teamcenter 2 tier and 4 tier architectures
Use organization application to create company organization (employee, user, group, role)
Create workflow process template and monitor them
Configure Teamcenter using BMIDE data model configuration
Use utilities for various requirement

units.title: Creating and Managing Volumes in Teamcenter
units.text: Creating and Managing Volumes in Teamcenter: Teamcenter 2 tier and 4 tier Architecture, Teamcenter Directories (TC_DATA, TC_ROOT, TC Volume. etc), Organization (Creating Person, User, Role, Groups), Creating Volumes, setting Default Volumes, BMIDE user Interface views (Object/Class/Extension/Navigator/Console), Classes and Attributes, Custom/COTS Objects and Properties (Persistant, Compound, Relation, Table), Server Connection Profile, POM Schema, Template Project Creation, Project Export/Import, Hot/Tem Deployment.

units.title: Advanced LOV Management and Rule-Based Configurations
units.text: Advanced LOV Management and Rule-Based Configurations: List Of Value (LOV) Concept and Types (Classic, Dynamic), Creating LOV and attaching to Properties, Filter Cascading, Interdependent LOV, Batch LOV, Display Rule, Naming Rule, Deep Copy Rule, GRM Rule, Condition (Create, Search).

units.title: Importing and Exporting Queries in Teamcenter
units.text: Importing and Exporting Queries in Teamcenter: Teamcenter Query Concept, Query Builder Interface, Creating Queries for objects or workflow, Executing Queries in advanced Search, Import/export Queries • Creating Reports, viewing reports, Access manager Rule/Object based protection, Editing the Rule tree, Export /Import Access manager rule tree, creating new Rule, Verifying Rule.

units.title: Project Activation, Deactivation, and Object Assignment
units.text: Project Activation, Deactivation, and Object Assignment: Project Concept, Creating Project, Privilege for Project Admin, Project Team Lead, Member, Activation and Deactivation of project, Assigning Object to Project, Process Term and functionality, Process template and task Template, Creating Workflow Process, Single and Multi-task process, Tasks in Process Template (Do Task, Task, Review Task, OR Task. etc), Resource Pool. Importing /Exporting Workflow Processes.

units.title: Attribute Management and Key LOV Dictionary in Teamcenter
units.text: Attribute Management and Key LOV Dictionary in Teamcenter: Classification Admin Interface, Creating Group, Classes, Views. Creating and managing attribute, Key LOV dictionary, classify object and verify. Utilities Concept and how to use. Make user, clear locks, dataset cleanup etc.

text_books: 1 Uthayan Elangovan, Teamcenter Engineering and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), 1st Edition, CRC press, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Stephen M. Samuel, Eric D. Weeks And Mark A. Kelley, Teamcenter Engineering and Product Lifecycle Management Basics, 1st Edition, Design Visionaries, 2006.

It introduces robotics and automation in production lines while providing exposure to standard engineering manufacturing simulations. The course emphasizes practical applications across multiple domains, including automotive, aerospace, product manufacturing, and FMCG industries.

outcomes.text: Understand Simulation Environment
Replicate Actual Manufacturing Process.
Understand Robotics and Automation in Production Line.
Learn the standard engineering manufacturing process in Simulation Environment.
Understand multiple domains like Automotive, Aerospace, Product Manufacturing, FMCG Industries and more.

units.title: Introduction to NX Simulation and Visualization
units.text: Introduction to NX Simulation and Visualization: Basic environment, study creation, creating sequences of simulative operations, collision detection, section cutting, video and picture output.

units.title: Introduction to Kinematic Devices in NX
units.text: Introduction to Kinematic Devices in NX: Defining kinematic devices, navigating the Motion Simulation environment, setting up kinematic constraints and joints.

units.title: Advanced Spot-Welding Techniques
units.text: Advanced Spot-Welding Techniques: Pneumatic and Servo Guns: Defining and simulating robotic spot welding, pneumatic and servo gun definition and usage, pedestrial welding and gun on robot path development.

units.title: Simulating Robotic Grinding and Welding Processes
units.text: Simulating Robotic Grinding and Welding Processes: Defining and simulating robotic continuous applications, arc welding and grinding path development.

units.title: Simulating Robotic Material Handling Processes
units.text: Simulating Robotic Material Handling Processes: Defining and simulating robotic material handling, gripper definition and usage, pick and place path development, Multi-robot simulation (i.e. interference zones), swept volumes, 7th axis, etc.

program: B Tech/ B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed to encourage the students to provide a distinctive skill set which is useful in securing employment globally in the automotive or intelligent mobility sectors with the growing demand for highly skilled professionals within automotive manufacturers.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the key principles of navigation and decision making algorithms
Analyze the components of an automotive control systems and its implementation
Evaluate models of vehicle interactions and the movement of groups of vehicles

units.title: Design thinking for EV
units.text: Design thinking for EV Autonomous vehicle sensors and imaging. Sensor integration architectures and multiple sensor fusion. Indoor autonomous surveillance, AI algorithms for sensing and imaging: supervised learning―neural networks.

units.title: Traffic Engineering and intelligent transportation
units.text: Traffic Engineering and intelligent transportation Traffic stream components, intelligent transportation system in India. Principles of path planning, navigation and decision making for autonomous vehicles approaches. Satellite navigation system, simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM). Application examples of path planning, navigation and decision making algorithms.

units.title: Introduction to transport systems and optimization theory
units.text: Introduction to transport systems and optimization theory Advanced optimization techniques, traffic modelling & simulation, electrified transport systems. Optimal energy management system based on driving pattern recognition.

units.title: Modern automotive architectures
units.text: Modern automotive architectures A review of modern automotive control hardware requirements and architectures. The evaluation of current and future vehicle networking technologies.

units.title: Autonomous navigation of EV
units.text: Autonomous navigation of EV An introduction to navigation systems, history, system architecture, application; modes of navigation – land.

units.title: Human-System Interface Design
units.text: Human-System Interface Design Design of safe operating systems and the human-technical interface. Computing systems for autonomous driving: state-of-the-art and challenges, Waymo’s technology.

text_books: 1. Steven Van Uytsel, Autonomous Vehicles, Springer,1st Edition, 2021 2. Ronald K. Jurgen, Autonomous Vehicles for Safer Driving, SAE International, 2013.
reference_books: 1. Shaoshan Liu LIYUN LI Jie Tang Shuang Wu Jean-Luc Gaudiot Creating Autonomous Vehicle Systems, Morgan & Claypool Publishers, 2017. 2. Anthony Raymond How Autonomous Vehicles will Change the World, Clever Gizmos LLC, 2020.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mechanics and Strength of Materials
objectives: To provide an understanding of the basics of aerodynamics in aircraft. To impart knowledge of boundary layer theory. To introduce the aerospace vehicle and space vehicle design. To introduce wind tunnel testing

outcomes.text: Analyse the basic flight mathematical aspects and potential flows
Discuss structural design of aircraft and space vehicles
Classify types of wind tunnel and describe wind tunnel testing technique

units.title: Introduction to Aerodynamics
units.text: Introduction to Aerodynamics Importance of Aerodynamic, four principles of aerodynamics, three laws of aerodynamics, six fundamentals of flight.

units.title: Applied Aerodynamics
units.text: Applied Aerodynamics Panel methods, pressure distribution, Kutta conditions, flow around airfoil (unsteady potential flow, compressible flow, axisymmetric flow) and slender body theories. Flight vehicle aerodynamics, rotor aerodynamics – low Reynolds number aerodynamics

units.title: Aircraft Vehicle Design
units.text: Aircraft Vehicle Design Design considerations for civilian and military aircraft, weight estimation, airfoil and geometry selection, thrust to weight ratio and wing loading, initial sizing, propulsion, landing gear and subsystems, aerodynamics, stability, control, and handling qualities, flight mechanics and performance issues, aircraft layout and configuration, structural aspects and constraint analysis.

units.title: Space Vehicle Design
units.text: Space Vehicle Design History of rocketry & launch vehicles, Current & future launch vehicles. Orbit/trajectory requirements and missions. Launch vehicle sizing, launch into an orbit, rocket propulsion (configuration and structural design), design for re-entry

units.title: Wind Tunnel Techniques
units.text: Wind Tunnel Techniques Introduction to wind tunnel, Classification of wind tunnels, Elements of wind tunnel, Conventional measurement techniques, wind tunnel testing technique.

text_books: 1. John D. Anderson, Fundamentals of aerodynamics, NY: McGraw-Hill Education, 6th edition, 2017. 2. Robert F. Stengel, Flight dynamics, Princeton University Press, 2nd Edition, 2022.
reference_books: 1. Bertin, J. J. and Cummings, R. M., Aerodynamics for Engineers, Prentice Hall, 6th edition, 2013. 2. Houghton, E. L., Carpenter, P. W., Collicott, S. H., and Valentine, D. T., Aerodynamics for Engineering Students, Butterworth-Heinemann, 6th Edition, 2012.

program: B Tech /B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed to impart knowledge of an IC engine and the ignition systems. It also introduces the modern developments in internal combustion engines with optical measurement techniques and emission control.

outcomes.text: Explain advanced engine technologies and emission norms
Apply concepts of different alternate fuels used for SI and CI engines
Analyze environmental, social, and technological issues related to the future widespread use of internal combustion engines

units.title: Basic Characteristics of Engines
units.text: Basic Characteristics of Engines Compression ratio, energy supply to an engine, power developed by engine, specific weight and specific volume, cylinder pressures, indicated mean effective pressure determination, torque characteristics, cylinder arrangement and their relative merits. Engine Cooling Systems Types of cooling, cooling of critical engine components, re-cooling the coolant, comparison of air cooled and liquid cooled engines.

units.title: Fuel Delivery in Spark Ignition Engines
units.text: Fuel Delivery in Spark Ignition Engines Classification of fuel delivery systems, fuel transfer pumps, fixed jet carburetor, computer controlled carburetor, gasoline injection systems. Ignition Systems in Spark Ignition Engines Battery ignition system, requirements for satisfactory operation of the ignition system, ignition timing and advancing mechanisms, magneto ignition system, electronic ignition system.

units.title: Combustion and Combustion Systems in Compression Ignition Engines
units.text: Combustion and Combustion Systems in Compression Ignition Engines Air motion in compression ignition engines, delay period in compression ignition engines, types of diesel combustion systems. Scavenging and Super Charging in Compression Ignition Engines Types of scavenging systems, improved and modified scavenging systems, super charging and engine performance, methods of super charging.

units.title: Modern Developments in Internal Combustion Engines
units.text: Modern Developments in Internal Combustion Engines Exhaust gas recirculation, multi point fuel injection, gasoline direct engine, homogeneous charge compression ignition and turbo-charging. Optical Measurement Techniques and Tools Particle image velocimetry (PIV), 3D and Holographic PIV, spray visualization, phase doppler interferometry for spray characterization, optical engines and engine endoscopy, use of nanoparticles in internal combustion engines.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)

objectives: This course introduces the basic concepts of vibrations and discusses free vibration of an undamped single-degree of-freedom system. This course also deals with two-degree-of-freedom systems, which require two independent coordinates to describe their motion. The modeling of continuous systems as multidegree-of-freedom systems is also presented in this course.

Solve two-degree-of-freedom free- and forced-vibration problems
Formulate the equations of motion of multidegree-of-freedom systems

units.title: Two-Degree-of-Freedom Systems

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics.
objectives: 1. To provide a basic understanding of biological mechanisms of living organisms from the perspective of engineers. 2. To encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering tools.

outcomes.text: Convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are diverse.
Identify DNA as a genetic material in the molecular basis of information transfer.
Classify enzymes and distinguish between different mechanisms of enzyme action.
Apply thermodynamic principles to biological systems.
Identify and classify microorganisms.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Convey that Biology is as important a scientific discipline as Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry Bring out the fundamental differences between science and engineering by drawing a comparison between eye and camera, Bird flying and aircraft. Mention the most exciting aspect of biology as an independent scientific discipline. Why we need to study biology? Discuss how biological observations of 18th Century that lead to major discoveries. Examples from Brownian motion and the origin of thermodynamics by referring to the original observation of Robert Brown and Julius Mayor. These examples will highlight the fundamental importance of observations in any scientific inquiry.

units.title: Classification
units.text: Classification Convey that classification per se is not what biology is all about. The underlying criterion, such as morphological, biochemical or ecological be highlighted. Hierarchy of life forms at phenomenological level. A common thread weaves this hierarchy Classification. Discuss classification based on (a) cellularity- Unicellular or multicellular (b) ultrastructure- prokaryotes or eucaryotes. (c) energy and Carbon utilization -Autotrophs, heterotrophs, lithotrophs (d) Ammonia excretion – aminotelic, uricotelic, ureotelic (e) Habitat- acquatic or terrestrial (e) Molecular taxonomy- three major kingdoms of life. A given organism can come under different category based on classification. Model organisms for the study of biology come from different groups. E.coli, S.cerevisiae, D.Melanogaster, C.elegance, A. Thaliana, M.musculus

units.title: Genetics
units.text: Genetics Convey that “Genetics is to biology what Newton’s laws are to Physical Sciences” Mendel’s laws, Concept of segregation and independent assortment. Concept of allele. Gene mapping, Gene interaction, Epistasis. Meiosis and Mitosis be taught as a part of genetics. Emphasis to be give not to the mechanics of cell division nor the phases but how genetic material passes from parent to offspring. Concepts of recessiveness and dominance. Concept of mapping of phenotype to genes. Discuss about the single gene disorders in humans. Discuss the concept of complementation using human genetics.

units.title: Biomolecules
units.text: Biomolecules Convey that all forms of life have the same building blocks and yet the manifestations are as diverse as one can imagine Molecules of life. In this context discuss monomeric units and polymeric structures. Discuss about sugars, starch and cellulose. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleotides and DNA/RNA. Two carbon units and lipids.

units.title: Enzymes
units.text: Enzymes Convey that without catalysis life would not have existed on earth Enzymology: How to monitor enzyme catalyzed reactions. How does an enzyme catalyze reactions? Enzyme classification. Mechanism of enzyme action. Discuss at least two examples. Enzyme kinetics and kinetic parameters. Why should we know these parameters to understand biology? RNA catalysis.

units.title: Information Transfer
units.text: Information Transfer The molecular basis of coding and decoding genetic information is universal Molecular basis of information transfer. DNA as a genetic material. Hierarchy of DNA structure- from single stranded to double helix to nucleosomes. Concept of genetic code. Universality and degeneracy of genetic code. Define gene in terms of complementation and recombination.

units.title: Macromolecular analysis
units.text: Macromolecular analysis How to analyse biological processes at the reductionistic level Proteins- structure and function. Hierarch in protein structure. Primary secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure. Proteins as enzymes, transporters, receptors and structural elements.

units.title: Metabolism
units.text: Metabolism The fundamental principles of energy transactions are the same in physical and biological world. Thermodynamics as applied to biological systems. Exothermic and endothermic versus endergonic and exergonic reactions. Concept of Keq and its relation to standard free energy. Spontaneity. ATP as an energy currency. This should include the breakdown of glucose to CO2 + H2O (Glycolysis and Krebs cycle) and synthesis of glucose from CO2 and H2O (Photosynthesis). Energy yielding and energy consuming reactions. Concept of Energy Charge.

units.title: Microbiology
units.text: Microbiology Concept of single celled organisms. Concept of species and strains. Identification and classification of microorganisms. Microscopy. Ecological aspects of single celled organisms. Sterilization and media compositions. Growth kinetics.

text_books: 1. Arthur T. Johnson (2011) ‘’Biology for Engineers’’ CRC Press Taylor & Francis group. 2. Microbiology, Prescott, L.M J.P. Harley and C.A. Klein 2008, 7th edition McGraw-Hill Higher Education.
reference_books: 1. Biology: A global approach: Campbell, N. A.; Reece, J. B.; Urry, Lisa; Cain, M, L.; Wasserman, S. A.; Minorsky, P. V.; Jackson, R. B. Pearson Education Ltd 2. program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To introduce thermodynamic concepts, thermodynamic properties and thermodynamic definitions of heat and work. 2. To make students aware of laws of thermodynamics and their applications to engineering problems. 3. To introduce the broad-based understanding of different modes of heat transfer. 4. To impart knowledge of different applications of conduction, convection and radiation.

outcomes.text: Know the fundamental concepts of engineering thermodynamics.
Analyze closed systems, steady and unsteady flow open systems based on first law of thermodynamics(energy), second law of thermodynamics(entropy).

Proficiently apply heat transfer principles (conduction, convection and radiation) to modeling and solution of engineering problems including analytical and numerical solutions to governing equations.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Definition, and basic concepts of engineering thermodynamics; description of matter – macroscopic description and microscopic description; thermodynamic system, surroundings and the system boundary; thermodynamic properties, processes and cycles; homogeneous and heterogeneous systems; thermodynamic equilibrium; quasi-static process; pure substance; concepts of continuum. Pressure, Volume and Temperature: definition of pressure, volume and temperature and their measurements; Thermal equilibrium; Zeroth law of thermodynamics; – thermometric property, scale of temperature, reference points, comparison of different types of thermometers; ideal gas; gas thermometers; ideal gas temperature; Celsius temperature scale; illustrative Examples.

units.title: First Law of Thermodynamics
units.text: First Law of Thermodynamics: Definition of the first law; Application of first law for a closed system undergoing a cyclic and non-cyclic process; different forms of stored energy; pure substance; specific heats,

units.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics
units.text: Second Law of Thermodynamics: Limitations of first law; Kelvin-Planck statement of second law; Clausius statement of second law; equivalence between the two statements; reversibility and irreversibility- definition of a reversible heat engine; Statement of Third Law of Thermodynamics and its importance

units.title: Entropy
units.text: Entropy: Introduction; Clausius inequality (or Clausius theorem); Entropy as a property of a system; Temperature – entropy plot and its usefulness in analyzing thermodynamic processes; entropy change for an irreversible process; principle of increase of entrop; Carnot cycle, entropy generation in closed and open systems; Tds relations and their significance(first and second law combined), Isentropic process.

units.title: Basic Concepts
units.text: Basic Concepts Modes of Heat Transfer, its mechanism and mathematical model. Conduction Heat Transfer: Fourier’s general conduction equation in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical co-ordinates, thermal resistance, Solution of Fourier’s equation for one dimensional steady state heat conduction through various configurations such as plane, cylindrical, spherical wall, composite medium.( for cylindrical and spherical walls derivation of Fourier’s three-dimensional equation is not included), Critical thickness of insulation and its importance Heat Transfer from extended surfaces: Types of fins, Governing equation, fin effectiveness, efficiency of fin, concept of corrected fin length, application of fins.

units.title: Unsteady State Heat Conduction
units.text: Unsteady State Heat Conduction: Lumped System Analysis, Heat Transfer in Semi Infinite solids, Use of Transient-Temperature Charts. Convection Heat Transfer: Classification of convection heat transfer- Forced & Natural, Hydrodynamic and thermal boundary layer, Momentum and energy equation for laminar boundary layer, Laminar and Turbulent flow. Convection heat transfer coefficient, Boundary layer similarities

units.title: Thermal Radiation
units.text: Thermal Radiation: Introduction to Physical Mechanism, concept of black body, and grey body, radiation properties. Basic laws of radiation- Planck’s law, Kirchoff’s law, Stefan-Boltzman law, Wein’s-displacement law and Lambert’s Cosine law

text_books: 1. P. K. Nag, “Engineering Thermodynamics”, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008 2. Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer (2017) by Theodore Bergman & Adrienne Lavine, 8th edition, Wiley Publication
reference_books: 1. Y. Cengel and M. Boles, “Thermodynamics -An Engineering Approach”, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. Introduction to Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer by Yunus A. Cengel McGraw-Hill,.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To learn the fundamental science and engineering relevant to materials 2. To introduce the concept of mechanical deformation in metals 3. To impart the knowledge of various failure mechanisms in materials and the theories and design modifications to avoid them.

outcomes.text: Design a process, microstructure and components to satisfy the system requirements.
Analyze the root cause of failure in different types of materials.
Understand formation of alloys and their applications.
Select appropriate materials for various applications depending on the structural requirements.

units.title: Mechanical Behaviour of Metals
units.text: Mechanical Behaviour of Metals: Deformation: Definition, elastic and plastic deformation and significance in design and shaping deformation in single crystal and polycrystalline materials, critical stress for deformation. Material Testing: Destructive Testing: Basic mechanical properties, tensile testing, hardness testing, Impact testing. Non Destructive Testing: Dye Penetrant, magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing Strain Hardening: Definition and importance, dislocation theory, effect of strain hardening on engineering behaviour of material. Recrystallization annealing, recovery, recrystallization and grain growth.

units.title: Failure of Metals
units.text: Failure of Metals: Fracture: Definition and types, Griffth’s theory of fracture, Orowan’s Modification. Fatigue: Definition and significance of cyclic stress, mechanism of fatigue and theories of fatigue failure, S-N curve and its interpretation, Notch effect, surface effect, Corrosion and thermal fatigue. Creep: Definition and significance of creep, analysis of classical creep curve, creep resistant materials

units.title: Phase Diagrams
units.text: Phase Diagrams: Concept of solidification of metals, Solidification of pure metals, solid solutions, nucleation, growth of the new phase, solidification of alloys, progressive and directional solidification. phases and structural constituent of phase diagram, Gibb’s phase rule, Lever rule. Coring and dendritic segregation, Eutectic and eutectoid system.

units.title: Fe-Fe3C Equilibrium Diagram
units.text: Fe-Fe3C Equilibrium Diagram: Importance of iron as engineering material, Allotropic forms of irons, Fe-Fe3C diagram: phases, reactions, and critical temperatures Solidification and microstructure of different steels Effect of Alloying Elements in Steels: Limitation of plain carbon steels. Significance of alloying elements. Cast irons: White, gray and malleable cast iron, Nodular and mottled cast iron, Alloy cast iron

units.title: Heat Treatment of Steel
units.text: Heat Treatment of Steel: Definition and significance of heat treatment, Time temperature transformation diagrams (TTT), Continuous cooling Transformation (CCT). Annealing: Process, properties and applications of full annealing, diffusion annealing, process Annealing and cyclic annealing. Normalizing: Hardening and Tempering.

units.title: Powder Metallurgy
units.text: Powder Metallurgy: Characteristics and production of metal powders, blending and mixing, compacting, pre-sintering and sintering secondary operations

units.title: Engineering Alloys
units.text: Engineering Alloys Ferrous Alloys: Classification, stainless steel, Tool Steel. Non-ferrous alloys: Copper alloys: Brass, bronzes (Tin, Beryllium and Silicon), Aluminium and its alloys. Composite Materials Definition, Characteristics and applications of composite materials Introduction of Advance and Smart Materials.

text_books: 1. Willam D. Callister, Jr., Adopted by R. Balsubramanium (2012), “Material science and Engineering”, Wiley India (P) Ltd. 2. S. H. Avner (2012), “Introduction to Physical Metallurgy”, Tata McGraw Hill.
reference_books: 1. V.D. Kodgire, S.V. Kodgire (2003) “Material science and Metallurgy” Everest Publishing House, Pune. 2. K.G. Budinksi & M.K. Budinksi (2016), “Engineering materials Properties and Selection”, Pearson India Education Service Pvt. Ltd.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart the knowledge of structure and properties of fluid and appreciate the complexities in solving fluid problems. 2. To provide understanding of various flow measurement techniques. 3. To impart the knowledge of characteristics of the components of fluid machines.

outcomes.text: Understand fluid properties, and their static-dynamic nature
Apply fundamentals of laminar and turbulent flow, boundary layer theory in solving real life problem
Analyze the flow in water pumps and turbines

units.title: Fluid Properties
units.text: Fluid Properties: Concept of continuum, fluid properties, Classification of fluid, Newton’s law of viscosity, stress-strain relationship. Fluid Statics: Basic hydrostatic equation, Pascal’s Law, application to Manometers and mechanical gauges, hydrostatic forces on plane and curved submerged surfaces. Buoyancy and Floatation: Archimedes’ Principle, buoyancy force and center of buoyancy, metacenter, metacentric height, analytical method to find metacentric height, condition of equilibrium of submerged bodies, oscillation of a floating body

units.title: Fluid Kinematics
units.text: Fluid Kinematics: Description of fluid motion-Lagrangian method and Euler’s method, classification of flow types- steady and unsteady, uniform and non-uniform, laminar and turbulent, one two and three- dimensional flow, rotational and irrotational, laminar and turbulent, compressible and incompressible.

units.title: Fluid Dynamics
units.text: Fluid Dynamics: Euler’s equation of motion, Bernoulli’s equation and its applications-Venturimeter, orifice meter, rotameter, pitot tube, Impulse-Momentum equation and its applications, Reynolds Transport Theorem and its application.

units.title: Laminar Flow
units.text: Laminar Flow: Navier-Stokes equation of motion, developing expression for flow rate, pressure drop, shear stress, friction factor. Flow of viscous fluid in circular pipes. Turbulent Flow: Shear stresses in turbulent flow, theories of turbulent shear stress, hydro-dynamically smooth and rough surface, modeling of turbulence. Flow through pipes: Energy losses in pipes: Minor and Major losses, Darcy-Weisbatch equation for head loss in pipes, hydraulic gradient lines, and total energy lines, pipes in series and parallel.

units.title: Principles of hydraulic machines
units.text: Principles of hydraulic machines: Impacts of jet on flat plate and cured vanes, elements of a hydro power plant, types of heads and efficiencies. Theory of impulse and reaction machines, Euler’s energy equation applied to a turbine and pump, velocity triangles, expression for work done.

units.title: Impulse Turbines & Reaction Turbines
units.text: Impulse Turbines & Reaction Turbines Construction, working and performance of Pelton turbine, Francis Turbine and Kaplan Turbine

units.title: Pumps
units.text: Pumps: Introduction, Classification of pumps - positive displacement and non - positive displacement. Reciprocating Pump: Basic theory, construction, operation, Slip, Indicator diagram. Types of reciprocating pumps, use of air vessel. Rotary Pumps: Basic theory, types, construction and working, variable delivery pumps. Centrifugal pumps: Basic Theory, Euler’s equation and velocity triangles, classification, construction, operation, characteristics Priming of pumps and NPSH Theory, Construction and working of Air lift pump, Jet pump and Hydraulic Ram.

text_books: 1. Frank M. White (2008), “Fluid Mechanics”, 6th Edition, McGraw Hill. 2. S.K. Som, Biswas G., "Introduction to Fluid Mechanics and Fluid Machines", Tata McGraw-Hill, 2nd Edition, 2008 3. Yunus A. Cengel and John Cimbala (2008), “Fluid Mechanics”, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill.
reference_books: 1. John F. Douglas, Janusz Gasiorek (2001), “Fluid Mechanics”, 4th Edition, Pearson Education. 2. P. N. Modi and S.M. Seth(2015), Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic Machinery, Standard Book House, 22nd Edition.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To create awareness about the OSI reference model. 2. To acquaint the students with the different types of networks at various levels such as sensor level, device network and control network. 3. To provide sufficient knowledge about the HART. 4. To impart the fundamentals of foundation field bus.

outcomes.text: Examine the importance of OSI, TCP/IP model, various networking components.
Compare the different types of networks at various levels of field communication.
Use HART for communication
Establish Foundation fieldbus communication.
Investigate the various wireless devices.

units.title: Introduction to Networks
units.text: Introduction to Networks: OSI reference model, TCP/IP model, Transmission media, UTP-STP cable, co-axial cable, N/W components: Repeaters, bridge, hub, switch, router, gateways.

units.title: Open Control Network
units.text: Open Control Network: RS232, RS422, EIA485 , Modbus Structure, Implementation, GPIB, Proprietary Control N/Modbus Plus.

units.title: Networks at different levels
units.text: Networks at different levels: Sensor level network: AS-i, CAN, Device net, Interbus and LON Device networks: Foundation Fieldbus H1-HART Profibus-PA Control Network: BACnet, control-net, FF-HSE, Profibus-DP.

units.title: HART
units.text: HART: Architecture, Physical, Data Link, Application, Communication Technique, Normal and burst mode of communication, Troubleshooting, Benefits of HART

units.title: Foundation Fieldbus
units.text: Foundation Fieldbus: Fieldbus requirement, features, advantages, fieldbus components, types, architecture–physical, data link, application layer, system and network management, wiring, segment functionality checking, installation in safe and hazardous area and troubleshooting, function block application process.

units.title: Wireless Technologies
units.text: Wireless Technologies: Satellite systems, Wireless LANs (WLANs), WiFi, VPAN, 6LoWPAN, ZigBee/IEEE 802.15.4 protocol, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), GPRS and – their comparison, limitations and characteristics.

text_books: 1. Deon Reynders, Steve Mackay, Edwin Wright, Practical Industrial Data Communication, 1st edition ELSEVEIR, 2005. 2. Lawrence M Thompson, Industrial Data Communication, 2nd edition, 1997.
reference_books: 1. Daniel T Miklovic, Real Time Control Networks, ISA 1993. 2. Bela G Liptak, Process Software and Digital Networks,3rd edition2002. 3. Andrew S. Tanenbaum, Computer Networks, 4th edition, PHI/Pearson Education,2002. 4. Behrouz A. Forouzan, Data Communications and Networking, 2nd edition, Tata McGraw Hill Publishing Company, New Delhi, 2000. 5. Douglas E.Corner, Computer Networks and Internets, 2nd edition, Pearson Education Asia, 5th Indian reprint, 2001.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To know the basics of algorithmic problem solving 2. To develop Python programs with conditionals and loops. 3. To define Python functions and call them. 4. To use Python data structures and input/output with files in Python.

outcomes.text: Develop algorithmic solutions to simple computational problems
Decompose a Python program into functions.
Represent compound data using Python lists, tuples, dictionaries.
Read and write data from/to files in Python Programs.

units.title: Algorithm Problem Solving
units.text: Algorithm Problem Solving: Algorithms, building blocks of algorithms (statements, state, control flow, functions), notation (pseudo code, flow chart, programming language), algorithmic problem solving, simple strategies for developing algorithms (iteration, recursion). Illustrative problems: find minimum in a list, insert a card in a list of sorted cards, guess an integer number in a range, Towers of Hanoi.

units.title: Data, Expressions, Statements
units.text: Data, Expressions, Statements: Python interpreter and interactive mode; values and types: int, float, boolean, string, and list; variables, expressions, statements, tuple assignment, precedence of operators, comments; modules and functions, function definition and use, flow of execution, parameters and arguments; Illustrative programs: exchange the values of two variables, circulate the values of n variables, distance between two points.

units.title: Control Flow, Functions
units.text: Control Flow, Functions: Conditionals: Boolean values and operators, conditional (if), alternative (if-else), chained conditional (if-elif-else); Iteration: state, while, for, break, continue, pass; Fruitful functions: return values, parameters, local and global scope, function composition, recursion; Strings: string slices, immutability, string functions and methods, string module; Lists as arrays. Illustrative programs: square root, gcd, exponentiation, sum an array of numbers, linear search, binary search.

units.title: Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries
units.text: Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries: Lists: list operations, list slices, list methods, list loop, mutability, aliasing, cloning lists, list parameters; Tuples: tuple assignment, tuple as return value; Dictionaries: operations and methods; advanced list processing - list comprehension; Illustrative programs: selection sort, insertion sort, merge sort, histogram.

units.title: Files, Modules, Packages
units.text: Files, Modules, Packages: Files and exception: text files, reading and writing files, format operator; command line arguments, errors and exceptions, handling exceptions, modules, packages; Illustrative programs: word count, copy file.

text_books: 1. Allen B. Downey, Think Python: How to Think Like a Computer Scientist, 2nd edition, Updated for Python 3, Shroff/O’Reilly Publishers, 2016. 2. Guido van Rossum and Fred L. Drake Jr, An Introduction to Python – Revised and updated for Python 3.2, Network Theory Ltd., 2011.
reference_books: 1. Robert Sedgewick, Kevin Wayne, Robert Dondero, ―Introduction to Programming in Python: An Inter-disciplinary Approach, Pearson India Education Services Pvt. Ltd., 2016. 2. Timothy A. Budd, ―Exploring Python‖, Mc-Graw Hill Education (India) Private Ltd.,, 2015. 3. Kenneth A. Lambert, ―Fundamentals of Python: First Programs‖, CENGAGE Learning, 2012. 4. Charles Dierbach, ―Introduction to Computer Science using Python: A Computational Problem-Solving Focus, Wiley India Edition, 2013.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To provide knowledge of analog domain signals and systems for time and frequency domain analysis. 2. To study various continuous and discrete time transforms.

outcomes.text: Define and identify various types of signals and systems.
Apply mathematical operations to analyze signals and systems.
Apply various mathematical transforms for continuous time signal and systems.
Use various transforms to analyze discrete time signal and systems.

units.title: Signals
units.text: Signals: Signals, classification of signals, elementary signals - analog and discrete signals, Basic operation of signals, systems.

Time domain representation for linear time invariant systems (analog & discrete): Classification of systems, series and parallel connection of systems, causal, non-causal, memory less and with memory, stable invertible systems. Convolution. Impulse, step response for first and second order LTI systems.

units.title: Fourier Series for continuous time and discrete time signals
units.text: Fourier Series for continuous time and discrete time signals: Representation of signals in terms of orthogonal functions, orthonormal signals, Types Fourier series – Exponential and Trigonometric Fourier Series. Dirichlet Conditions. Gibb’s Phenomenon.

units.title: Fourier Transform for continuous time signals
units.text: Fourier Transform for continuous time signals: Fourier transform, their properties, Fourier transform representation of periodic signals. Frequency response of continuous time system. Relation between Fourier and Laplace Transform.

units.title: Analysis of continuous time system using Laplace transforms
units.text: Analysis of continuous time system using Laplace transforms: Introduction to bidirectional Laplace transforms and ROC, its properties, Application of LT in electrical circuit , LT of elementary signals unilateral Laplace transform Inversion of Laplace transform, Using L.T. with or without initial conditions, Transfer function of system.

units.title: Analysis of discrete time system using Z transforms
units.text: Analysis of discrete time system using Z transforms: Introduction, Z transform of elementary signals, ROC, Properties of Z transform, Inversion of Z transform, system function, solution of difference equation, unilateral Z transform.

text_books: 1. Tarun Kumar Rawat, Signals and Systems, Oxford University Press, July-2010. 2. Nagoor Kani , Signals and Systems, McGraw-Hill publication, 1st Edition, March-2010.
reference_books: 1. Oppenheim & Willsky, Signal and Systems, Prentice Hall of India publication, 2nd edition, 2008. 2. Simon Haykin & Barry van veen, Signal and Systems, John Wiley publication. 2nd edition, 2008. 3. H. P. HSU, Signals and Systems, Schaum’s Outlines, McGraw-Hill publication, 3rd Edition, 2013.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Electronic Systems
objectives: The primary objective of this course is to familiarize students with the operation of power semiconductor devices and various types of electric drives. The design aspect of DC and AC drives used in industrial applications is emphasized.

outcomes.text: Identify and apply power electronic devices for industrial applications
Design electric drive for an industrial application
Analyze the performance of electric drives

units.title: Power Devices
units.text: Power Devices Construction, static, dynamic characteristics and ratings of SCR, GTO, IGBT, TRIAC Methods of turning on of SCR- Gate triggering circuit using UJT Methods of turning off-Natural and Forced Commutation circuits

units.title: DC Converter Drives
units.text: DC Converter Drives Basic characteristics of DC motors – Operating modes. Concept of controlled rectifier. Single Phase Drives-Half wave converter drives, semi converter drives, full converter drives, dual converter drives. Three Phase Drives-Half wave converter drives, semi converter drives, full converter drives, dual converter drives

units.title: DC Chopper Drives
units.text: DC Chopper Drives Principle of Power Control, Principle of Regenerative Brake Control, Principle of Rheostatic Brake Control, two/four quadrant chopper drives Closed loop control of DC drives- Open loop transfer function, closed loop transfer function, phase locked loop control, microcomputer control of DC drives, performance analysis and stability of variable speed dc drives

units.title: AC Drives
units.text: AC Drives Introduction, induction motor drives, performance characteristics, stator voltage control, rotor voltage control, slip power recovery, frequency control, voltage and frequency control, current control, voltage, current and frequency control, current source inverter fed induction motor drive, forced commutated inverter fed induction motor drives, flux vector control

units.title: Synchronous Motor Drives
units.text: Synchronous Motor Drives Cylindrical rotor motors, salient-pole motors, reluctance motors, permanent-magnet motors, switched reluctance motors, self-controlled synchronous motor drives and traction drives, brushless DC and AC motor drives

text_books: 1. M. Rashid, Power Electronics, 3rd Edition, Prentice Hall of India Publication, 2010. 2. M. D. Singh & K. B. Khanchandani, Power Electronics, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2006. 3. Dubey G.K, Fundamentals of Electrical Drives, 2nd Edition, Narosa Press, 2002.
reference_books: 1. Ned Mohan, Undeland, Robbins, Power Electronics, 3rd Edition, John Wiley Publication year, 2009.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course will help students to understand the fundamental concepts of control systems and system stability. The course also helps to analyze and evaluate the system design pertaining to the system performance, stability criterion, controllability and observability.

outcomes.text: Explain the basic functioning and components of feedback control systems
Analyse first and second orders systems, their dynamic and steady state response
Apply different stability analysis criterion
Construct system models using state space analysis

units.title: Concept of Open loop and Closed Loop Systems
units.text: Concept of Open loop and Closed Loop Systems Examples and applications of open and closed loop systems, classifications of control systems, control system components and its functioning.

units.title: Mathematical Modeling of Physical Systems
units.text: Mathematical Modeling of Physical Systems Differential equation of physical system, mechanical system, translational systems, electrical system, pneumatic system, block diagram reduction technique, signal flow graph method.

units.title: State Variable Analysis
units.text: State Variable Analysis Concept of state, state variables and state model, concept of state space, state trajectory and vector matrix representation of state model, transfer function from state model, laplace Transform solution of state equation, concept of controllability and observability.

units.title: Time Response Analysis
units.text: Time Response Analysis Time response analysis of first order and second order systems, characteristic equations, response to step, ramp and parabolic inputs, steady state error and error constants.

units.title: Stability Analysis of the System
units.text: Stability Analysis of the System Absolute stability and relative stability, routh hurwitz’s stability criterion and limitations, stability analysis from root locus, effect of addition of poles and zeros.

units.title: Frequency Response Analysis
units.text: Frequency Response Analysis Nyquist stability criterions, nyquist plot, gain and phase margins, bode plot of magnitude and phase and determination of stability margins.

units.title: Feedback System Performance
units.text: Feedback System Performance Performance specifications in frequency domain, correlation between frequency domain and time domain specifications, introduction to pid controller.

text_books: 1. Norman Nise, Control Systems Engineering, 6th Edition, Wiley Publication, 2011. 2. I.G. Nagrath & M. Gopal, Control System Engineering, 5th Edition, New Age International Publication, 2008.
reference_books: 1. Richard C. Drof and Robert H. Bishop, Modern Control System, 13th Edition, Person Int., 2016. 2. Katsuhiko Ogata, Modern Control Engineering, 5th Edition, Person Int., 2009.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: This course helps student to develop in-depth understanding of various traditional and non- traditional manufacturing processes. The course also imparts knowledge on various process equipments and tools required for a manufacturing.

outcomes.text: Explain various types of metal casting and forming processes
Experiment with the tool geometry and operations of lathe, milling and drilling machines
Choose appropriate joining processes for practical applications

units.title: Metal Casting
units.text: Metal Casting Fundamentals of casting process, pattern materials, pattern types, allowances, foundry practices, gating system, molding sand- composition and properties, cores, moulding processes- shell moulding, CO2 moulding, investment casting, die casting, centrifugal casting and continuous casting, casting defects and their remedies.

units.title: Forming
units.text: Forming Fundamentals of metal forming, cold and hot working, forging, rolling, extrusion, wire drawing and tube drawing, press tools relevant defects and remedies.

units.title: Welding
units.text: Welding Riveting, soldering and brazing, fusion welding, gas and arc welding, submerged arc welding-inert gas welding, electro slag welding, thermit welding, welding equipment, miscellaneous welding processes, weld joint types, weldability.

units.title: Machining Operations
units.text: Machining Operations Cutting tool nomenclature, geometry, principle of machining, lathe, drilling, milling and boring and broaching machine and their operations, cutting tools used, different attachments, work holding devices, classifications, advantages, limitations and applications.

text_books: 1. Amitabha Ghosh, Asok K. Mallik, Manufacturing Science, 2nd Edition, East-West Press Pvt. Ltd., 2010. 2. E. Paul De Garmo, J. T. Black, Ronald A. Kohser, Materials and Processes in Manufacturing, 13th Edition, Wiley Publication, 2019.
reference_books: 1. G. K. Lal, Fundamentals of Manufacturing Processes, Alfa Science International, 2010. 2. W. A. J. Chapman, Work Shop Technology- Vol I, II, III, ELBS Publishers, 2011. 3. P. N. Rao, Manufacturing Technology-Vol I & Vol II, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Physics, Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
objectives: The course develops an understanding of mathematical aspects of representing motion. The emphasis is on the techniques for analysis of dynamic system models using theoretical methods. The students learn to synthesize solutions for offline applications in industrial robotics.

outcomes.text: Describe the theoretical concepts in simulation of mathematical models
Analyze the given dynamic systems models using theoretical methods
Synthesize dynamic systems using modelling and analytical methods

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Review of dynamic modelling, dynamic models of engineering systems, financial systems, biological systems, ecological and epidemiological systems, Robot Offline Programming and Simulation in industrial robotics

units.title: Time Domain Methods
units.text: Time Domain Methods Classification of ODEs, continuous time systems, discrete time systems, scalar and vector differential equation solutions in the state space form

units.title: Laplace Transform Method
units.text: Laplace Transform Method Solving second order equations, solving the equations in the state space form, partial fractions, response to pulsed excitations

units.title: Sampled Data Systems
units.text: Sampled Data Systems Minimum sampling frequency, aliasing, stability relationship between continuous and discrete time systems, relationship between poles, conversion between continuous and discrete time transfer functions

units.title: Model Validation
units.text: Model Validation Model validation using Monte-Carlo simulation, basic case studies, statistical confidence intervals

units.title: Analogy between Mechanical and Electrical Systems
units.text: Analogy between Mechanical and Electrical Systems Dynamic stiffness, flexibility, admittance, impedance, wave impedance for sound radiation, effect of mounted sensor mass on the measurement of the base motion

units.title: Introduction to System Identification
units.text: Introduction to System Identification Basics of reverse engineering systems from data, computational methods, logarithmic decrement and external resonance as identification tools

text_books: 1. M. Driels, Linear Control Systems Engineering, McGraw-Hill, 1996. (Classic Book) 2. D. Inman, Engineering Vibration, 4th Edition, Pearson, 2014.
reference_books: 1. N. Nise, Control Systems Engineering, 7th Edition, Wiley, 2014. 2. H. Gurocak, Industrial Motion Control, Wiley, 2015.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course introduces students to optimization methodology as a valuable decision making tool. The emphasis is on developing skills in building and solving optimization algorithms for various practical engineering problems.

outcomes.text: Apply concepts of Linear Programming
Solve assignment problems, transportation problems and project scheduling
Implement dynamic programming, gaming theory and Queuing theory
Demonstrate use of Inventory control and Simulation Methodology

units.title: Introduction to Operations Research
units.text: Introduction to Operations Research Origin of OR and its definition, concept of optimizing performance measure, types of OR problems, phases of OR problem approach, problem formulation, building mathematical model, deriving solutions, validating model, controlling and implementing solution, applications of OR

units.title: Linear Programming
units.text: Linear Programming Linear programming – examples from industrial cases, formulation & definitions. implicit assumptions of LPP Convex set, convex polyhedron, extreme points, basic feasible solutions Geometric method: two-variable case Simplex Algorithm – slack, surplus & artificial variables, computational details, Big-M method, Two Phase method, identification and resolution of special cases through simplex iterations Special cases – infeasibility, unboundedness, redundancy & degeneracy, sensitivity analysis Duality – formulation, results, fundamental theorem of duality, dual-simplex and primal-dual algorithms

units.title: Transportation and Assignment problems
units.text: Transportation and Assignment problems Transportation Problems - examples, definitions – decision variables, supply & demand constraints, formulation, balanced & unbalanced situations, solution methods – NWCR, minimum cost and VAM, test for optimality (MODI method), degeneracy and its resolution Assignment Problems - examples, definitions – decision variables, constraints, formulation, balanced & unbalanced situations, solution methods – Hungarian, test for optimality (MODI method), degeneracy & its resolution

units.title: PERT – CPM
units.text: PERT – CPM Project definition, project scheduling techniques – Gantt chart, PERT & CPM, determination of critical paths, estimation of Project time and its variance in PERT using statistical principles, concept of project crashing/time-cost trade- off

units.title: Dynamic Programming and Game Theory
units.text: Dynamic Programming and Game Theory Dynamic programming under certainty, Game theory- Definitions- Number of Players, sum of gains and losses, strategy. Two-person Zero Sum Games, pure strategies: games with saddle point

units.title: Queuing Theory
units.text: Queuing Theory Definitions – queue (waiting line), waiting costs, characteristics (arrival, queue, service discipline) of queuing system, Kendall’s notation, Little’s law, steady state behavior, Poisson’s Process & queue, models with examples - M/M/1 and its performance measures

units.title: Application of Simulation
units.text: Application of Simulation Definition and steps of simulation, random number, random number generator, Monte-Carlo Simulation, Flow Shop System, Job Shop System, Simple Fixed Period Inventory System

text_books: 1. H.A. Taha, Operations Research: An Introduction, 10th Edition, Pearson Education, 2019. 2. J. K. Sharma, Operations Research: Theory and Applications, 3rd Edition, Macmillan India Limited, 2006.
reference_books: 1. K.G. Murthy, Linear Programming, John Wiley & Sons, 1983. (Classic Book) 2. G. Hadley, Linear Programming, 3rd Edition, Narosa, 2002. 3. H.M. Wagner, Principles of OR with Application to Managerial Decisions, Prentice Hall India Learning Pvt., 1980. (Classic Book) 4. F.S. Hiller and G.J. Lieberman, Introduction to Operations Research”, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course teaches the impact of various types of stresses on machine and structural components. It also introduces the fundamental concepts of designing simple machine components.

outcomes.text: Illustrate the importance of materials in design and select appropriate materials for safe design
Apply the principle and basic procedure of machine components design
Design of various machine components like shafts, couplings, joints, gears and belts

units.title: Stress Analysis
units.text: Stress Analysis Design process, selection of materials, preferred numbers, fits and tolerances, direct, bending and shear stress-combined stresses-eccentric loading on machine members-stress concentration and notch sensitivity

units.title: Design of Shafts and Couplings
units.text: Design of Shafts and Couplings Design of solid shafts based on strength, rigidity, design of muff coupling and rigid flange coupling

units.title: Design of Joints
units.text: Design of Joints Design of bolted joints including axial and tensile loading, knuckle joints, cotter joints, bolt of uniform strength

units.title: Design of Gears
units.text: Design of Gears Design of spur gear based on contact stress and beam strength, and based on Lewis and Buckingham equations

units.title: Design of Flexible Drives
units.text: Design of Flexible Drives Design of flat belt and ‘V’ belt for simple power transmission between shafts

text_books: 1. J. F. Shigley, Mechanical Engineering Design, 8th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. V. B. Bhandari, Design of Machine Elements, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2010.
reference_books: 1. Hall, Holowenko, Laughen, Machine Design, Schaum’s Outline Series, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. M. F. Spotts, Design of Machine Elements, 8th Edition, Pearson, 2004. 3. PSG Design Data Handbook
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course elaborates the fundamental concepts of various modes of heat transfer. It emphasizes the mathematical modelling of conduction, convection and radiation. The focus of the course is on teaching the analytical techniques in solving practical heat transfer problems.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental principles and laws of heat transfer.
Design heat transfer systems with the application of these principles.
Develop the problem-solving skills essential to practice heat transfer in real-world applications.

units.title: Conduction
units.text: Conduction Heat transfer in conduction and convection, Fourier’s law of conduction, Problems on 1D heat conduction through plain walls, composite walls, cylinder walls, spheres. Extended surfaces: Fins. Problems on heat transfer through Fins, fin efficiency, fin effectiveness.

units.title: Convection
units.text: Convection Heat transfer in convection, Free and forced convection, Flow and thermal boundary layer equations, laminar flow through circular pipe, constant heat flux and constant wall temperature conditions, Overall heat transfer coefficient.

units.title: Radiation
units.text: Radiation Heat transfer in radiation, Stefan-Boltzmann Law, black body, grey body, shape factor

Identify the different interaction models for interfacing
Analyze the communication and collaboration model
Synthesize practical systems with HMI modelling for real time applications

objectives: The course elaborates detailed treatment of industrial networks and their requirements. It emphasizes various serial communication standards and various industrial protocols required for communication. The course also teaches students the basics of wireless communication.

Compare various types of serial communication standards
Illustrate various Industrial protocols and wireless communications
Design and program for CAN Network

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course introduces students rigorously to the working mechanisms of fluid machines used mainly in power generation. The students are required to analyze the essential underlying mechanisms using constitutive principles to understand and grasp the failure modes of fluid machines.

outcomes.text: Explain the working and governing of various types of fluid machines
Evaluate the performance of hydraulic turbines and pumps, in terms of design parameters and performance characteristics
Apply similarity methods to predict the performance of the hydraulic turbines and pumps

units.title: Principles of Hydraulic Machines
units.text: Principles of Hydraulic Machines Impacts of jet on flat plate and curved vanes, elements of a hydro power plant, types of heads and efficiencies. Theory of impulse and reaction machines, Euler’s energy equation applied to a turbine and pump, velocity triangles, expression for work done.

units.title: Hydraulic Machines
units.text: Hydraulic Machines Construction, working and performance of Pelton turbine, Francis Turbine and Kaplan Turbine. Concept performance and operating characteristics, efficiency curves, model testing.

units.title: Hydraulic Pumps
units.text: Hydraulic Pumps Classification, centrifugal, mixed and axial flow pumps, head, power and efficiency calculations, system losses and system head, impeller slip and slip factors, fans and compressors, internal and stage efficiency, stalling.

units.title: Hydrostatic Machines
units.text: Hydrostatic Machines Principle of positive displacement machines, working principle of reciprocating pumps and compressors, indicator diagram, volumetric efficiency, slip, effect of friction and acceleration. Concept of air vessels, two throw and three throw pumps, constant and variable delivery, rotary pumps and compressors, Fluid coupling and torque converter, hydraulic jack, press, crane, pressure accumulator and intensifier.

units.title: Maintenance of Hydraulic Systems
units.text: Maintenance of Hydraulic Systems Causes of Hydraulic system problems, preventive maintenance, maintaining and disposing of fluids, Filters, strainers, prevention of problems caused by gases, probable causes.

objectives: The course emphasizes the importance and applicability of supervisory control with acquired data using industrial communication protocols. It introduces and reinforces the concept of a virtual instrument on a suitable computational platform using graphical programming. It also introduces students to the design of basic industrial control systems.

outcomes.text: Apply the fundamentals of Supervisory Control, Virtual Instrumentation and data Acquisition
Analyze the hardware-in-loop simulations
Synthesize a VI system to solve real time problems using data acquisition

objectives: The course develops an understanding of the web browser and desktop tasks automation process using an open source software platform. The course introduces students to designing practical drag and drop scripts to automate routine and time-consuming processes on desktop computers. The students also learn to design automation bots using an automation platform.

outcomes.text: Describe the concepts in web browser and desktop task automation
Design the basic building block automation processes
Develop mechanical bots for automating processes

Select the correct components for practical automation systems
Develop the basic framework of the automation process

Illustrate the use of hardware that enables design and implementation of VR & AR systems
Apply the concepts of the visual perceptions in VR-AR technologies

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Electronic Systems
objectives: The primary objective of this course is to familiarize students with the operation of power semiconductor devices and various types of electric drives. The design aspect of DC and AC drives used in industrial applications is emphasized.

outcomes.text: Identify and apply power electronic devices for industrial applications
Design electric drive for an industrial application
Analyze the performance of electric drives

units.title: Power Devices
units.text: Power Devices Construction, static, dynamic characteristics and ratings of SCR, GTO, IGBT, TRIAC Methods of turning on of SCR- Gate triggering circuit using UJT Methods of turning off-Natural and Forced Commutation circuits

units.title: DC Converter Drives
units.text: DC Converter Drives Basic characteristics of DC motors – Operating modes. Concept of controlled rectifier. Single Phase Drives-Half wave converter drives, semi converter drives, full converter drives, dual converter drives. Three Phase Drives-Half wave converter drives, semi converter drives, full converter drives, dual converter drives

units.title: DC Chopper Drives
units.text: DC Chopper Drives Principle of Power Control, Principle of Regenerative Brake Control, Principle of Rheostatic Brake Control, two/four quadrant chopper drives Closed loop control of DC drives- Open loop transfer function, closed loop transfer function, phase locked loop control, microcomputer control of DC drives, performance analysis and stability of variable speed dc drives

units.title: AC Drives
units.text: AC Drives Introduction, induction motor drives, performance characteristics, stator voltage control, rotor voltage control, slip power recovery, frequency control, voltage and frequency control, current control, voltage, current and frequency control, current source inverter fed induction motor drive, forced commutated inverter fed induction motor drives, flux vector control

units.title: Synchronous Motor Drives
units.text: Synchronous Motor Drives Cylindrical rotor motors, salient-pole motors, reluctance motors, permanent-magnet motors, switched reluctance motors, self-controlled synchronous motor drives and traction drives, brushless DC and AC motor drives

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course will help students to understand the fundamental concepts of control systems and system stability. The course also helps to analyze and evaluate the system design pertaining to the system performance, stability criterion, controllability and observability.

outcomes.text: Explain the basic functioning and components of feedback control systems
Analyse first and second orders systems, their dynamic and steady state response
Apply different stability analysis criterion
Construct system models using state space analysis

units.title: Concept of Open loop and Closed Loop Systems
units.text: Concept of Open loop and Closed Loop Systems Examples and applications of open and closed loop systems, classifications of control systems, control system components and its functioning.

units.title: Mathematical Modeling of Physical Systems
units.text: Mathematical Modeling of Physical Systems Differential equation of physical system, mechanical system, translational systems, electrical system, pneumatic system, block diagram reduction technique, signal flow graph method.

units.title: State Variable Analysis
units.text: State Variable Analysis Concept of state, state variables and state model, concept of state space, state trajectory and vector matrix representation of state model, transfer function from state model, laplace Transform solution of state equation, concept of controllability and observability.

units.title: Time Response Analysis
units.text: Time Response Analysis Time response analysis of first order and second order systems, characteristic equations, response to step, ramp and parabolic inputs, steady state error and error constants.

units.title: Stability Analysis of the System
units.text: Stability Analysis of the System Absolute stability and relative stability, routh hurwitz’s stability criterion and limitations, stability analysis from root locus, effect of addition of poles and zeros.

units.title: Frequency Response Analysis
units.text: Frequency Response Analysis Nyquist stability criterions, nyquist plot, gain and phase margins, bode plot of magnitude and phase and determination of stability margins.

units.title: Feedback System Performance
units.text: Feedback System Performance Performance specifications in frequency domain, correlation between frequency domain and time domain specifications, introduction to pid controller.

text_books: 1. Norman Nise, Control Systems Engineering, 6th Edition, Wiley Publication, 2011. 2. I.G. Nagrath & M. Gopal, Control System Engineering, 5th Edition, New Age International Publication, 2008.
reference_books: 1. Richard C. Drof and Robert H. Bishop, Modern Control System, 13th Edition, Person Int., 2016. 2. Katsuhiko Ogata, Modern Control Engineering, 5th Edition, Person Int., 2009.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: This course helps student to develop in-depth understanding of various traditional and non- traditional manufacturing processes. The course also imparts knowledge on various process equipments and tools required for a manufacturing.

outcomes.text: Explain various types of metal casting and forming processes
Experiment with the tool geometry and operations of lathe, milling and drilling machines
Choose appropriate joining processes for practical applications

units.text: Metal Casting Fundamentals of casting process, pattern materials, pattern types, allowances, foundry practices, gating system, molding sand- composition and properties, cores, moulding processes- shell moulding, CO2 moulding, investment casting, die casting, centrifugal casting and continuous casting, casting defects and their remedies.

units.title: Forming
units.text: Forming Fundamentals of metal forming, cold and hot working, forging, rolling, extrusion, wire drawing and tube drawing, press tools relevant defects and remedies.

units.title: Welding
units.text: Welding Riveting, soldering and brazing, fusion welding, gas and arc welding, submerged arc welding-inert gas welding, electro slag welding, thermit welding, welding equipment, miscellaneous welding processes, weld joint types, weldability.

units.title: Machining Operations
units.text: Machining Operations Cutting tool nomenclature, geometry, principle of machining, lathe, drilling, milling and boring and broaching machine and their operations, cutting tools used, different attachments, work holding devices, classifications, advantages, limitations and applications.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Physics, Linear Algebra and Differential Equations

outcomes.text: Describe the theoretical concepts in simulation of mathematical models
Analyze the given dynamic systems models using theoretical methods
Synthesize dynamic systems using modelling and analytical methods

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Review of dynamic modelling, dynamic models of engineering systems, financial systems, biological systems, ecological and epidemiological systems, Robot Offline Programming and Simulation in industrial robotics

units.title: Time Domain Methods
units.text: Time Domain Methods Classification of ODEs, continuous time systems, discrete time systems, scalar and vector differential equation solutions in the state space form

units.title: Laplace Transform Method
units.text: Laplace Transform Method Solving second order equations, solving the equations in the state space form, partial fractions, response to pulsed excitations

units.title: Sampled Data Systems

units.title: Model Validation
units.text: Model Validation Model validation using Monte-Carlo simulation, basic case studies, statistical confidence intervals

units.title: Analogy between Mechanical and Electrical Systems
units.text: Analogy between Mechanical and Electrical Systems Dynamic stiffness, flexibility, admittance, impedance, wave impedance for sound radiation, effect of mounted sensor mass on the measurement of the base motion

units.title: Introduction to System Identification
units.text: Introduction to System Identification Basics of reverse engineering systems from data, computational methods, logarithmic decrement and external resonance as identification tools

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course introduces students to optimization methodology as a valuable decision making tool. The emphasis is on developing skills in building and solving optimization algorithms for various practical engineering problems.

outcomes.text: Apply concepts of Linear Programming
Solve assignment problems, transportation problems and project scheduling
Implement dynamic programming, gaming theory and Queuing theory
Demonstrate use of Inventory control and Simulation Methodology

units.title: Introduction to Operations Research
units.text: Introduction to Operations Research Origin of OR and its definition, concept of optimizing performance measure, types of OR problems, phases of OR problem approach, problem formulation, building mathematical model, deriving solutions, validating model, controlling and implementing solution, applications of OR

units.title: Linear Programming
units.text: Linear Programming Linear programming – examples from industrial cases, formulation & definitions. implicit assumptions of LPP Convex set, convex polyhedron, extreme points, basic feasible solutions Geometric method: two-variable case Simplex Algorithm – slack, surplus & artificial variables, computational details, Big-M method, Two Phase method, identification and resolution of special cases through simplex iterations Special cases – infeasibility, unboundedness, redundancy & degeneracy, sensitivity analysis Duality – formulation, results, fundamental theorem of duality, dual-simplex and primal-dual algorithms

units.title: Transportation and Assignment problems
units.text: Transportation and Assignment problems Transportation Problems - examples, definitions – decision variables, supply & demand constraints, formulation, balanced & unbalanced situations, solution methods – NWCR, minimum cost and VAM, test for optimality (MODI method), degeneracy and its resolution Assignment Problems - examples, definitions – decision variables, constraints, formulation, balanced & unbalanced situations, solution methods – Hungarian, test for optimality (MODI method), degeneracy & its resolution

units.title: PERT – CPM
units.text: PERT – CPM Project definition, project scheduling techniques – Gantt chart, PERT & CPM, determination of critical paths, estimation of Project time and its variance in PERT using statistical principles, concept of project crashing/time-cost trade- off

units.title: Dynamic Programming and Game Theory
units.text: Dynamic Programming and Game Theory Dynamic programming under certainty, Game theory- Definitions- Number of Players, sum of gains and losses, strategy. Two-person Zero Sum Games, pure strategies: games with saddle point

units.title: Queuing Theory
units.text: Queuing Theory Definitions – queue (waiting line), waiting costs, characteristics (arrival, queue, service discipline) of queuing system, Kendall’s notation, Little’s law, steady state behavior, Poisson’s Process & queue, models with examples - M/M/1 and its performance measures

units.title: Application of Simulation

objectives: The objective of this course is to introduce students to the concepts, principles, and practical applications of virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) technologies. Emphasizing the design and development of interactive VR and AR experiences, this course covers the historical context, fundamental theories, and various interaction techniques in these fields.
