program: B Tech (EXTC/IT/MTRX) and MBA Tech (IT)
objectives: This course helps to develop and analyse continuous and discrete time signals and systems. It also forms the foundation for further studies in the areas such as speech/audio processing, image processing, and communication systems.

outcomes.text: Classify the continuous time and discrete time signals and systems
Apply various mathematical operations to analyze signals and systems
Analyze the continuous time signals and systems using various transforms
Determine the frequency spectrum of discrete time signals and systems response

units.title: Introduction to Signals and Systems
units.text: Introduction to Signals and Systems Signals - definitions, classification, elementary continuous and discrete time signals, operations on continuous and discrete time signals, system and its classification.

units.title: Linear Time Invariant System
units.text: Linear Time Invariant System Continuous and discrete time LTI systems, convolution integral and convolution sum, interconnection of systems, series, parallel and mixed.

units.title: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Signals
units.text: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Signals Introduction to different types of Fourier series representation, Exponential Fourier Series representation of continuous time periodic signal, magnitude and phase spectrum.

units.title: Fourier Transform
units.text: Fourier Transform Fourier transform of elementary signals and its frequency spectrum, properties of Fourier transform, inverse Fourier transform, analysis of LTI continuous time system in frequency domain.

units.title: Laplace Transform
units.text: Laplace Transform Limitations of Fourier transform, introduction to Laplace transform, ROC and its properties, Laplace transform of elementary signals, properties of Laplace transform, inverse Laplace transform, solution of differential equation.

units.title: Z-transforms
units.text: Z-transforms Introduction to Z transform, Z transform of elementary signals, ROC, properties of Z transform, inverse Z transform, solution of difference equation.

text_books: 1. Tarun Kumar Rawat, Signals and Systems, 1st Edition, Oxford University Press, 2010. 2. Nagoor Kani, Signals and Systems, 1st Edition, McGraw-Hill publication, 2010.
reference_books: 1. Oppenheim & Willsky, Signal and Systems, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall of India publication, 2008. (Classic Book) 2. Simon Haykin & Barry Van Veen, Signal and Systems, 2nd Edition, John Wiley publication, 2008.
lab_work: 8 to 10 practical exercises (and a practicum) based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Physics, Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
objectives: The course develops an understanding of mathematical aspects of representing motion. The emphasis is on the techniques for analysis of dynamic system models using theoretical methods. The students learn to synthesize solutions for offline applications in industrial robotics.

outcomes.text: Describe the theoretical concepts in simulation of mathematical models
Analyze the given dynamic systems models using theoretical methods
Synthesize dynamic systems using modelling and analytical methods

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Review of dynamic modelling, dynamic models of engineering systems, financial systems, biological systems, ecological and epidemiological systems, Robot Offline Programming and Simulation in industrial robotics

units.title: Time Domain Methods
units.text: Time Domain Methods Classification of ODEs, continuous time systems, discrete time systems, scalar and vector differential equation solutions in the state space form

units.title: Laplace Transform Method
units.text: Laplace Transform Method Solving second order equations, solving the equations in the state space form, partial fractions, response to pulsed excitations

units.title: Sampled Data Systems
units.text: Sampled Data Systems Minimum sampling frequency, aliasing, stability relationship between continuous and discrete time systems, relationship between poles, conversion between continuous and discrete time transfer functions

units.title: Model Validation
units.text: Model Validation Model validation using Monte-Carlo simulation, basic case studies, statistical confidence intervals

units.title: Analogy between Mechanical and Electrical Systems
units.text: Analogy between Mechanical and Electrical Systems Dynamic stiffness, flexibility, admittance, impedance, wave impedance for sound radiation, effect of mounted sensor mass on the measurement of the base motion

units.title: Introduction to System Identification
units.text: Introduction to System Identification Basics of reverse engineering systems from data, computational methods, logarithmic decrement and external resonance as identification tools

text_books: 1. M. Driels, Linear Control Systems Engineering, McGraw-Hill, 1996. (Classic Book)
reference_books: 1. N. Nise, Control Systems Engineering, 7th Edition, Wiley, 2014. 2. H. Gurocak, Industrial Motion Control, Wiley, 2015.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course introduces students to optimization methodology as a valuable decision making tool. The emphasis is on developing skills in building and solving optimization algorithms for various practical engineering problems.

outcomes.text: Apply concepts of Linear Programming
Solve assignment problems, transportation problems and project scheduling
Implement dynamic programming, gaming theory and Queuing theory
Demonstrate use of Inventory control and Simulation Methodology

units.title: Introduction to Operations Research
units.text: Introduction to Operations Research Origin of OR and its definition, concept of optimizing performance measure, types of OR problems, phases of OR problem approach, problem formulation, building mathematical model, deriving solutions, validating model, controlling and implementing solution, applications of OR

units.title: Linear Programming
units.text: Linear Programming Linear programming – examples from industrial cases, formulation & definitions. implicit assumptions of LPP Convex set, convex polyhedron, extreme points, basic feasible solutions Geometric method: two-variable case Simplex Algorithm – slack, surplus & artificial variables, computational details, Big-M method, Two Phase method, identification and resolution of special cases through simplex iterations Special cases – infeasibility, unboundedness, redundancy & degeneracy, sensitivity analysis Duality – formulation, results, fundamental theorem of duality, dual-simplex and primal-dual algorithms

units.title: Transportation and Assignment problems
units.text: Transportation and Assignment problems Transportation Problems - examples, definitions – decision variables, supply & demand constraints, formulation, balanced & unbalanced situations, solution methods – NWCR, minimum cost and VAM, test for optimality (MODI method), degeneracy and its resolution Assignment Problems - examples, definitions – decision variables, constraints, formulation, balanced & unbalanced situations, solution methods – Hungarian, test for optimality (MODI method), degeneracy & its resolution

units.title: PERT – CPM
units.text: PERT – CPM Project definition, project scheduling techniques – Gantt chart, PERT & CPM, determination of critical paths, estimation of Project time and its variance in PERT using statistical principles, concept of project crashing/time-cost trade- off

units.title: Dynamic Programming and Game Theory
units.text: Dynamic Programming and Game Theory Dynamic programming under certainty, Game theory- Definitions- Number of Players, sum of gains and losses, strategy. Two-person Zero Sum Games, pure strategies: games with saddle point

units.title: Queuing Theory
units.text: Queuing Theory Definitions – queue (waiting line), waiting costs, characteristics (arrival, queue, service discipline) of queuing system, Kendall’s notation, Little’s law, steady state behavior, Poisson’s Process & queue, models with examples - M/M/1 and its performance measures

units.title: Application of Simulation
units.text: Application of Simulation Definition and steps of simulation, random number, random number generator, Monte-Carlo Simulation, Flow Shop System, Job Shop System, Simple Fixed Period Inventory System

text_books: 1. H.A. Taha, Operations Research: An Introduction, 10th Edition, Pearson Education, 2019. 2. J. K. Sharma, Operations Research: Theory and Applications, 3rd Edition, Macmillan India Limited, 2006.
reference_books: 1. K.G. Murthy, Linear Programming, John Wiley & Sons, 1983. (Classic Book) 2. G. Hadley, Linear Programming, 3rd Edition, Narosa, 2002. 3. H.M. Wagner, Principles of OR with Application to Managerial Decisions, Prentice Hall India Learning Pvt., 1980. (Classic Book) 4. F.S. Hiller and G.J. Lieberman, Introduction to Operations Research”, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course teaches the impact of various types of stresses on machine and structural components. It also introduces the fundamental concepts of designing simple machine components.

outcomes.text: Illustrate the importance of materials in design and select appropriate materials for safe design
Apply the principle and basic procedure of machine components design
Design of various machine components like shafts, couplings, joints, gears and belts

units.title: Stress Analysis
units.text: Stress Analysis Design process, selection of materials, preferred numbers, fits and tolerances, direct, bending and shear stress-combined stresses-eccentric loading on machine members-stress concentration and notch sensitivity

units.title: Design of Shafts and Couplings
units.text: Design of Shafts and Couplings Design of solid shafts based on strength, rigidity, design of muff coupling and rigid flange coupling

units.title: Design of Joints
units.text: Design of Joints Design of bolted joints including axial and tensile loading, knuckle joints, cotter joints, bolt of uniform strength

units.title: Design of Gears
units.text: Design of Gears Design of spur gear based on contact stress and beam strength, and based on Lewis and Buckingham equations

units.title: Design of Flexible Drives
units.text: Design of Flexible Drives Design of flat belt and ‘V’ belt for simple power transmission between shafts

text_books: 1. J. F. Shigley, Mechanical Engineering Design, 8th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. V. B. Bhandari, Design of Machine Elements, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2010.
reference_books: 1. Hall, Holowenko, Laughen, Machine Design, Schaum’s Outline Series, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. M. F. Spotts, Design of Machine Elements, 8th Edition, Pearson, 2004. 3. PSG Design Data Handbook
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course introduces the students to the design parameters for Human Machine Interface. It emphasizes various contemporary interaction models. The course teaches the students to design GUI interfaces using programming language.

outcomes.text: Describe the fundamental approaches for HMI
Identify the different interaction models for interfacing
Analyze the communication and collaboration model
Synthesize practical systems with HMI modelling for real time applications

units.title: Foundations of Human Machine Interface
units.text: Foundations of Human Machine Interface What is HMI – design, models, evaluation, need to understand people, computers and methods, basic human abilities - vision, hearing, touch, memory Computers – speed, interfaces, widgets, and effects on interaction Humans – memory, attention span, visual perception, psychology, ergonomics, understanding users

units.title: The Design Process
units.text: The Design Process Interaction Design Basics, interaction styles, HCI in the Software Process, HCI design principles and rules: design principles, principles to support usability, golden rules and heuristics, HCI patterns, design rules, HCI design standards

units.title: Implementation
units.text: Implementation Implementation Tools, technology and change designing for the Web, designing for portable devices, handling errors and designing help, prototyping and UI software

units.title: Users Models
units.text: Users Models Predictive models, cognitive models, interaction with natural languages, next generation interface, socio-organizational issues and stakeholder requirements, heuristic evaluation, evaluation with cognitive models, evaluation with users

units.title: Software Tools
units.text: Software Tools Nextion Editor, Nextion instruction set, assignment statements, operational commands, HMI designing commands, color code constants, system variables

text_books: 1. Alan J, Dix. Janet Finlay, Russell Beale, Human Computer Interaction, 3rd Edition, Pearson Education, 2004, ISBN 81-297-0409-9. 2. Jenny Preece, Rogers, Sharp, “Interaction Design-beyond human-computer interaction”, WILEY-INDIA, 2019, ISBN 81-265-0393-9.
reference_books: 1. Jonathan Lazar, Jinjuan Feng, Harry Hochheiser, Research Methods in Human-Computer Interaction, 3rd Edition, Morgan Kaufmann, 2017, ISBN: 9780128053904. 2. Mary Beth Rosson and John M. Carroll, Usability Engineering: Scenario-Based Development of Human-Computer Interaction, Morgan Kaufmann, 2001, ISBN-13: 978-1558607125.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course Introduces various industrial engineering tools for enhancing productivity. It elaborates on the concepts of ergonomics, value engineering and emphasizes productivity improvement techniques. It teaches students the use of the analytical techniques to solve practical problems.

outcomes.text: Apply work-study techniques for improving productivity
Plan an effective work place layout using industrial engineering tools
Understand the fundamentals of value engineering to reduce unnecessary costs
Design work platforms using principles of ergonomics

units.title: Productivity
units.text: Productivity Definition, productivity in enterprise, task of management, productivity of materials, land, building, machine, and labor, measurement of productivity, factors affecting productivity, improving efficiency and productivity through work-study, work-study components, productivity improvement techniques, 5s, Poka-Yoke, Kaizen and Kanban

units.title: Method study
units.text: Method study Basic procedure of method study, factors in selecting a job study, recording techniques using charts and diagrams, questioning technique for development of new method, visual and micro motion study, principles of motion economy

units.title: Workplace design
units.text: Workplace design Selection of plant location and layout, types of plant layout, material flow patterns, tools and techniques for effective plant layout, use of analytical and computational techniques including simulation for plant layout design

units.title: Work Measurement
units.text: Work Measurement Objectives, significance, work measurement techniques - Time Study, Work Sampling, Pre-determined Motion Time Standards (PMTS), determination of Time Standards, Observed Time, Basic Time, Normal Time, rating factors, allowances, and Standard Time

units.title: Value Engineering
units.text: Value Engineering Definition of Value Engineering, uses of Value Engineering, unnecessary costs, difference between Value Engineering and other cost reduction techniques, Function Analysis System Techniques (FAST) diagram

units.title: Ergonomics
units.text: Ergonomics Ergonomics, history of ergonomics, human-machine relations, displays and controls, human-computer interaction. anthropometry Cognitive ergonomics, workspace design for standing and seating postures

text_books: 1. International Labor Office, Geneva, Introduction to Work Study, 3rd Edition, Oxford and IBH, 2015. 2. A. B. Badiru, Handbook of Industrial and Systems Engineering, 2nd Edition, CRC Press, 2014.
reference_books: 1. J. L. Riggs, Production systems: Planning, Analysis and Control, 4th Edition, Wiley, 1987. (Classic Book) 2. M. Telsang, Industrial Engineering and Production management, 3rd Edition, S. Chand, 2018.
lab_work: 8 to 10 Tutorial exercises based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Electronic Systems, Microprocessor Systems and Interfacing
objectives: The course elaborates detailed treatment of industrial networks and their requirements. It emphasizes various serial communication standards and various industrial protocols required for communication. The course also teaches students the basics of wireless communication.

outcomes.text: Examine the importance of OSI, TCP/IP model and various networking requirements
Compare various types of serial communication standards
Illustrate various Industrial protocols and wireless communications
Design and program for CAN Network

units.title: Introduction to Networks, Cables, Noise and Error Detection
units.text: Introduction to Networks, Cables, Noise and Error Detection OSI reference model, TCP/IP model, Ethernet, LoRaWAN, Network cables, sources of electrical noise, origin of errors, types of error detection, control, and correction

units.title: Serial communication standards
units.text: Serial communication standards RS232, RS422, RS-485 interface standard, troubleshooting and testing with RS-485, GPIB standard, USB interface

units.title: HART
units.text: HART Architecture, physical, data link, applications, communication technique, troubleshooting, benefits of HART

units.title: Controller Area Networks
units.text: Controller Area Networks Introduction, CAN frame formats, CAN bus arbitration, CAN interrupts and CAN modes, programming CAN Network

units.title: Open Industrial Fieldbus and Device net Systems
units.text: Open Industrial Fieldbus and Device net Systems AS-I, Device Net, Profibus-PA and Profibus-DP Foundation Fieldbus: Fieldbus requirements, features, advantages, components, types, and architecture

units.title: Radio and Wireless Communication
units.text: Radio and Wireless Communication Satellite systems, Wi-Fi, ZigBee, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and GPRS

text_books: 1. J. Park, S. McKay and E. Wright, Practical Data Communication for Instrumentation and Control, Elsevier, 2008. 2. Lawrence M Thompson, “Industrial Data Communication”, 2nd Edition, 1997. (Classic Book)
reference_books: 1. D. T. Miklovic, Real Time Control Networks, ISA, 1993. (Classic Book) 2. B. G. Liptak, Process Software and Digital Networks, 3rd Edition, 2002. 3. A. S. Tanenbaum, Computer Networks, 4th Edition, PHI/Pearson Education, 2002. 4. B. A. Forouzan, Data Communications and Networking, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, New Delhi, 2000. 5. D. E. Corner, Computer Networks and Internet, 2nd Edition, Pearson Education Asia, Fifth Indian reprint, 2001.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech and MBA Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS), B Tech Mechatronics
objectives: The course emphasizes the importance and power of supervisory control with acquired data using industrial communication protocols. It introduces and reinforces the concept of a virtual instrument on a suitable computational platform using graphical programming. It also introduces students to the design of basic industrial control systems.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of Virtual Instrumentation and data Acquisition
Create the hardware-in-loop simulations
Analyze and evaluate the performance of Virtual Instrumentation Systems
Create a VI system to solve real time problems using data acquisition

units.title: Fundamentals of Virtual Instrumentation
units.text: Fundamentals of Virtual Instrumentation Historical perspective, advantages, block diagrams and architecture of a virtual instrument, data-flow techniques, graphical programming in data flow, comparison with conventional programming Software Overview LabVIEW, Graphical User Interface - controls and indicators data types, data flow programming, editing, debugging and running a virtual instrument, graphical programming pallets, their configuration, VIs and sub-Vis, typical examples

units.title: Programming Structure
units.text: Programming Structure FOR loops, WHILE loop, CASE structure, formula node, sequence structures Introduction to Arrays and Clusters Array operations, cluster functions, graphs and charts, local and global variables

units.title: State Machines
units.text: State Machines Introduction, definition of State Machine, a simple State Machine, event structures File Input/Output Introduction, file formats, file I/O functions, path functions, sample VIs to demonstrate file WRITE and READ function String Handling Introduction, string functions, LabVIEW string formats, typical examples

units.title: Basics of Data Acquisition
units.text: Basics of Data Acquisition Introduction to data acquisition, classification of Signals, analog interfacing connecting signal to the board, analog input/output techniques, digital I/O, counters and timers DAQ Hardware configuration Introduction, Measurement and Automation Explorer, DAQ assistants, analysis assistants, interfacing instruments

units.title: GPIB and RS232
units.text: GPIB and RS232 Introduction, RS232 Vs. GPIB, handshaking, GPIB interfacing, RS232C/RS485 interfacing, standard commands for programmable instruments, VISA Standard bus architectures ISA, PCI, VME and PXI.

units.title: Advanced Topics in Lab View
units.text: Advanced Topics in Lab View Use of analysis tools and application of VI, Fourier Transforms, power spectrum, correlation methods, windowing & flittering Simulation of systems using VI Development of control system, image acquisition and processing, motion control

text_books: 1. Jovitha Jerome, Virtual instrumentation Using LabVIEW, 4th Edition, PHI Learning, 2010, ISBN: 978-8120340305. 2. Sanjay Gupta and Joseph John, Virtual Instrumentation Using Lab View, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, New Delhi, 2010, ISBN : 978-0070700284.
reference_books: 1. Lisa. K. Wills, LabVIEW for Everyone, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall of India, 2008, ISBN: 978- 0132681940. 2. Garry Johnson and Richard Jennings, LabVIEW Graphical Programming, 4th Edition, McGraw Hill Professional, 2006, ISBN No-978-1259005336.

program: B Tech and MBA Tech programs except B Tech CSBS and B Tech CSE (DS), B Tech Mechatronics, B Tech and MBA Tech AI, DS
objectives: The course develops an understanding of the web browser and desktop tasks automation process using an open source software platform. The course introduces students to designing practical drag and drop scripts to automate routine and time-consuming processes on desktop computers. The students also learn to design automation bots using an automation platform.

outcomes.text: Describe the concepts in web browser and desktop task automation
Design the basic building block automation processes
Develop mechanical bots for automating processes

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction History of RPA, Processes and Flowcharts, Programming constructs in RPA, UiPath Community version download and installation, Studio, Robot, and Orchastrator, overview of the Studio components

units.title: Workflow Sequencing
units.text: Workflow Sequencing Variables, Flowchart, and control flow

units.title: Data Manipulation
units.text: Data Manipulation Scalar variables, collections, tables, interfacing with Excel

units.title: Images and Text Automation
units.text: Images and Text Automation Optical character recognition, screen scraping, data scraping, recording and advanced UI interaction

units.title: Case Studies
units.text: Case Studies Testing, exception handling, integration with AI and ML, Onboarding Bot, Invoice Processing Bot

text_books: 1. N. Mullakara and A. K. Asokan, Robotic Process Automation Projects, Packt>, 2020. 2. A. M. Tripathi, Learning Robotic Process Automation, Packt>, 2018.
reference_books: 1. T. Taulli, The Robotic Process Automation Handbook, Apress, 2021. 2. R. Murdoch, Robotic Process Automation, Independently Published, 2018.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To introduce fundamentals of Data conversion, PLC and SCADA. 2. To impart knowledge for designing PLC based sequencing applications.

outcomes.text: Understand the basics of data conversion, data acquisition, PLC and SCADA.
Analyze the performance of data converters.
Apply PLC for sequence control.
Create PLC Ladder logic programs for industrial applications.

units.title: Data Converters
units.text: Data Converters: Introduction to signal conditioning and its elements, Sampling Theorem, Sampling process, Quantization, Encoding, Aliasing, Sample and hold circuit. DACs – basic DAC technique, weighted resister, R -2R ladder and inverted R -2R ladder types of DACs. ADCs – parallel feedback ADC, dual slope ADC, frequency based ADC and their comparison. DAC/ADC Specifications, Typical ICs for ADC and DAC. Design examples on ADCs and DACs.

units.title: Data Acquisition Systems (DAS)
units.text: Data Acquisition Systems (DAS): Introduction, definition and need for data acquisition systems. Objectives of DAS, Single Channel DAS, Multiplexer – multiplexed channel operation, Multichannel DAS, Interfacing DAS with computer.

units.title: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)
units.text: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC): Evolution of PLCs, Discrete State Control, Block Diagram of PLC, Classification of PLCs. Description of PLC components: Power Supply, Input and Output Modules , Discrete Input and Output Modules, Analog Input and output Modules, Programming Devices, CPU, I/O module specifications. Typical PLC specifications. Different Addressing modes.

units.title: PLC Programming
units.text: PLC Programming: Memory Organization, Program Files, Data Files, Program Scan Cycle. Types of programming languages used in PLCs: Ladder logic, Functional block diagram, Sequential flow chart, Instruction List, Structured Text. Rules for ladder logic Programming, Relay Logic Instructions, Latching, Interlocking, Triggers, Logic gates programming in PLC. Timer Instructions: On Delay, Off Delay and Pulse Timers. Counter Instructions: Up counter and Down Counter. Data manipulation instructions, Mathematical instructions, Sequence and Shift register instructions. Analog Module programming.

units.title: Application Development
units.text: Application Development: Interfacing of various inputs & outputs to PLC- Electromagnetic Control Relays, Contactors, Motor Starters, Manually operated switches, Mechanically operated switches, Proximity sensors, Encoders, Decoders. Interfacing Remote I/O s with PLC. Design of Tank level control System, Sequential switching of motors, Motor starters, Temperature control, Conveyor belt control, Pneumatic Cylinder control, Automatic Bottle filler. Industrial case studies.

units.title: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA)
units.text: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA): Introduction to supervisory control, Need of SCADA, Architecture of SCADA. Components of SCADA: MTU, RTU and HMI. Wireless SCADA, Interfacing of SCADA with PLC.

text_books: 1. Curtis D. Johnson, “Process control Instrumentation Technology”, Prentice Hall, 8th Edition, June 2005. 2. M.Mitra and S.Gupta, “Programmable logic controllers and Industrial Automation: An Introduction”, Penram International Publishing (India) Pvt. Ltd., 2nd Edition, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Petreuzeulla, “Programmable Controllers”, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2nd Edition, 2005. 2. G. B. Clayton, “Data Converters”, Palgrave Macmillan Press, 4th Edition, 2012.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical Engineering (BTMA01002), Physics (BTMA01003), Digital Electronics (BTMA03009)
objectives: 1. To develop basic skills required for measurements of mechanical and process parameters. 2. To impart knowledge about applications and working of various metrological instruments. 3. To study different types of sensors and transducers used in industrial applications.

outcomes.text: Understand the significance of calibration, specifications and characteristics of different measuring instruments.
Analyze the impact of factors like surface finish on performance of machines.
Select and Apply sensors and transducers for various physical parameters.
Analyze the performance of different bridge circuits for measurement of Resistance, Inductance and Capacitance.

units.title: Introduction to Metrology and measurement system
units.text: Introduction to Metrology and measurement system: Definition and concept of metrology, standards of measurements, methods of measurement. Configuration of Generalized measurement system. Performance characteristics of measuring instruments, Static characteristics- Error, Accuracy, Precision, Span, Range, Sensitivity, Linearity, Reliability and Resolution. Dynamic characteristics- Dynamic error, Speed of response, Fidelity and Lag.

units.title: Linear Measurements
units.text: Linear Measurements: Line and end standards, Wavelength standards, slip gauges, design and manufacturing of gauges. Comparators: Types, construction and working of Mechanical, Optical, Electrical, Pneumatic Comparators. Interferometry: Basic principles, source of light, Optical flats, Fringe pattern and their interpretation

units.title: Angular
units.text: Angular Measurement: Angle standards, sine bar, angle gauges, autocollimator, angle Dekker, optical square, taper measurement, universal bevel protractor Surface finish Measurement: Surface texture, assessment of surface roughness, Tomlinson surface meter, and other surface measuring devices.

units.title: Modern Optical Measurement and Metrology
units.text: Modern Optical Measurement and Metrology: Tool Maker’s Microscope, Profile Projector, Optical Square. Basics of Optical Interference and Interferometry, Optoelectronic measurements.

units.title: Sensors and Transducers
units.text: Sensors and Transducers: Principles, Classification and applications. Transducer Selection Criteria for Mechatronics applications. Pressure Transducers: Bellows, Diaphragm, Bourdon tubes, Pirani Gauge, Ionization Gauge, Piezoelectric transducer and Strain Gauge. Flow Transducers: Orifice Plate, Pitot tube, Ventury tube, Rotameter, Ultrasonic Flow meter, Electromagnetic flow meter. Temperature Transducers: RTD, Thermistor, Thermocouple, Pyrometers. Displacement/Position Transducers: LVDT, Hall effect transducers, Optical encoders. Resonant Sensor, Optical Fiber based sensor, Grating Leakage.

units.title: Proximity Sensors
units.text: Proximity Sensors: Basic Principle, Construction, Working and applications of Inductive, Capacitive, Ultrasonic, Magnetic and Photoelectric proximity sensors. Modes of operation of Photoelectric proximity sensors. Performance Comparison and Specifications of different Proximity sensors.

units.title: Measurement of R, L, C
units.text: Measurement of R, L, C: Measurement of Resistance, low, medium and high. Kelvin’s double bridge, Wheatstone’s bridge and Megger. AC bridge circuits for measurement of inductance and capacitance, Maxwell’s, Hay's, Schering's and Wein bridge.

text_books: 1. Nakra and Chowdhury, “Measurement and Control”, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2009. 2. H.S. Kalsi," Electronic Instrumentation", Tata McGraw Hill, 3rd Edition, 2010. 3. R. K. Jain, “Engineering Metrology”, Khanna Publishers, 2009.
reference_books: 1. A. K. Sawhney , “Electrical and Electronic Measurements and Instrumentation”, Dhanpat Rai and Co.,2012 2. E.O. Doebelin and D. N. Manik, “Doebelin's Measurement Systems”, 6" Edition, McGraw Hill, 2010.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. The aim of this course is to introduce students to the application of scientific procedures to the conduction of research.

outcomes.text: Comprehend the basics of research process
Recognise the importance of literature review
Write a technical report/paper.
Relate ethical guidelines to conducting research, data collection and report writing

units.title: Introduction to research
units.text: Introduction to research The importance of research, research process overview, types of research, research terminology

units.title: Literature search and review
units.text: Literature search and review Searching for existing literature on a selected topic, reviewing the papers in selected area, use of abstract and citation databases for literature search

units.title: Formulating and solving a research problem
units.text: Formulating and solving a research problem Identifying a research problem, formulation of hypothesis, research objectives and questions, different types of research designs, experimental setup, data sampling and collection, data analysis

units.title: Technical writing
units.text: Technical writing Research paper writing, referencing in proper format, tools for technical writing,

units.title: Ethics in research
units.text: Ethics in research Research integrity, plagiarism basics and checks

text_books: -- 1. Research Methodology: Methods and techniques, C R Kothari, New Age International (P) Limited Publishers. 2. Research Methodology a step by step guide for beginners, Ranjit Kumar, Pearson Publications
reference_books: -- 1. Smart Melville, Wayne Goddard, Research Methodology: An introduction or Science and Engineering Students, Juta &Co. Ltd.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To introduce the basics of backend of drafting packages. 2. To give hands on experience on the 3D Modeling software. 3. To impart knowledge of NC/CNC machines and programming of CNC using machine codes. 4. To provide concepts of GT, CAPP, CAQC and CIM.

outcomes.text: Create accurate and precise geometry of complex engineering systems and use the geometric models in different engineering applications.
Apply the concepts of machining for the purpose of selection of machining parameters and cutting tools for CNC milling and turning.
Understand concepts of different CAD/CAM/CIM systems and different data management systems.

units.title: Introduction and Elements of interactive computer graphics
units.text: Introduction and Elements of interactive computer graphics: The design process, the role of modeling and communication. Modeling using CAD, product life cycle and Computer-Aided Design (CAD)/ Computer-Aided Manufacturing(CAM), Concurrent engineering in product design and development, Collaborative Engineering, Computers for design process, CAD System Architecture-Software and Hardware.

units.title: Techniques for geometric modeling
units.text: Techniques for geometric modeling : Graphic standards, The parametric representation of geometry-Bezier curves, Cubic spline curve, B-Spline curve, parametric representation of line, circle, ellipse and parabola, Constructive solid geometry (CSG), Boundary representation (B-rep), Wire Frame modeling, Solid modeling, Surface modeling, feature based modeling, Assembly Modeling- Different approaches of creating an assembly, Parent child relationship.

units.title: Transformation, Manipulation and Data Storage
units.text: Transformation, Manipulation and Data Storage: 2D and 3D Transformations (Translation, Rotation, Scaling and Magnification), Concatenations, Matrix representation, Problems on Transformations. Object transformation, mirror transformation, Bill of Materials from attribute data, Engineering data management system, relational data base for design, object oriental database, Design Information Systems.

units.title: NC and CNC technology
units.text: NC and CNC technology: Introduction, basic components of Numeric Control (NC) system, NC procedure, NC coordinate systems, NC motion control systems, Various actuation systems and feedback devices like encoder, tachogenerator, etc. Applications, Advantages and Disadvantages of NC machines. Constructional details of Computer Numeric Control (CNC) machines, CNC programming concepts, Manual part programming methods, Various G and M codes, Absolute and incremental system, Tool length and diameter compensation, Programming of turning and milling, Use of canned cycles, subroutines. Flexible Manufacturing Systems (FMS), Machining Centers and its types, Automated Material Handling and Storage Systems like Robots, Automated Guided Vehicles (AGV) and Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems (AS/RS)

units.title: Group Technology, CAPP and CAQC
units.text: Group Technology, CAPP and CAQC: Introduction to Group Technology (GT), Part families, Part Classification and Coding, GT Machines cells, Benefits of GT. Introduction to Computer Aided Process Planning (CAPP), Retrieval type Process Planning Systems, Generative type Process Planning Systems, Benefits of CAPP, PFA, Similarity coefficient matrix. Introduction to Computer Aided Quality Control (CAQC), Computers in QC, Contact Inspection Methods, Non-Contact Inspection Methods, Integration of CAQC with CAD/CAM

units.title: Computer
units.text: Computer Integrated Manufacturing and Technology driven practices: Introduction, Evolution, Objectives, CIM Hardware and software, CIM Benefits, Nature and role of elements of CIM, Identifying CIM needs, Data base requirements of CIM, Role of CAD/CAM in CIM, Obstacles to Computer Integrated Manufacturing, CIM wheel, Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA). Introduction to Rapid Prototyping, Virtual Prototyping. Introduction to Smart Manufacturing and Smart Design Concept.

text_books: 1. Mikell P. Groover and Emory W. Zimmers, Jr.,“CAD/CAM Computer Aided and Manufacturing” Eastern Economy Edition, PHI. 2. Ibrahim Zeid, R. Sivasubramanian (2009), “CAD/ CAM, Theory and Practice” Tata McGraw Hill Publications.
reference_books: 1. P. N. Rao (2010), “CAD/CAM Principles and Applications” Tata McGraw Hill Publications. 2. P. Radhakrishan, S. Subramanyan, V. Raju (2004), “CAD/CAM/CIM”, New Age International Publishers.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To provide an exposure on how to simulate a system.

outcomes.text: Evaluate decisions by optimization using simulation techniques.
Select the right method of simulation as per the system.

units.text: System – ways to analyze the system – Model - types of models – Simulation – Definition – Types of simulation models – steps involved in simulation – Advantages & Disadvantages. Monte Carlo Simulation. Parameter estimation – estimator – properties – estimate – point estimate – confidence interval estimates – independent – dependent – hypothesis – types of hypothesis- steps – types 1& 2 errors – Framing – strong law of large numbers.

Building of Simulation model – validation – verification – credibility – their timing – principles of valid simulation Modeling – Techniques for verification – statistical procedures for developing credible model. Modeling of stochastic input elements – importance – various procedures – theoretical distribution – continuous – discrete – their suitability in modeling.

Generation of random variates – factors for selection – methods – inverse transform – composition – convolution – acceptance – rejection – generation of random variables – exponential – uniform – weibull – normal Bernoulli – Binomial – uniform – poisson. Simulation languages – comparison of simulation languages with general purpose languages – Simulation languages vs Simulators – software features – statistical capabilities – G P S S – SIMAN- SIMSCRIPT –Simulation of M/M/1 queue – comparison of simulation languages.
Output data analysis – Types of Simulation w.r.t output data analysis – warmup period- Welch algorithm – Approaches for Steady – State Analysis – replication – Batch means methods – comparisons
Applications of Simulation – flow shop system – job shop system – M/M/1 queues with infinite and finite capacities – Simple fixed period inventory system – New boy paper problem

text_books: 1. Law & Kelton (2000) ,”Simulation Modeling and Analysis”, 3rd Edition., McGraw-Hill Inc.
reference_books: 1. Carrie A. & Wiley (1990), Simulation of Manufacturing Systems, NY, 1990.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mathematics - I, II and III (BTAB01001, BTAB02001 and BTMA03001), Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer (BTMA05012)
objectives: 1. To understand physical systems e.g. mechanical, electrical, thermal and fluid systems and converting them to mathematical models. 2. To understand the mathematical Modeling and response analysis of dynamic systems that is required in Mechanical engineering. 3. To learn the use of any mathematical software.

outcomes.text: Design the mathematical models of the physical systems.
Analyse the response of the systems and also modify the systems as per the requirements using mathematical software.

units.text: Introduction to system dynamics: Introduction, Mathematical Modeling of Dynamic System, Analysis and Design of Dynamic Systems.

units.title: The Laplace transform
units.text: The Laplace transform: Introduction, Complex Numbers, Complex Variables, and Complex Functions, Laplace Transformation, Inverse Laplace Transformation, Solving Linear, Time-Invariant Differential Equations, Example Problems and Solutions, Problems.

units.title: Mechanical systems
units.text: Mechanical systems: Introduction, Mechanical Elements, Mathematical modeling of simple Mechanical systems, Work, Energy, and Power, Example Problems and Solutions, Problems.

Transfer-Function approach to modeling dynamic system: Introduction, Block Diagrams, Partial-Fraction Expansion with MATLAB, Transient-Response Analysis with MATLAB, Example Problems and Solutions, Problems.

units.title: State-Space approach to modeling dynamic system
units.text: State-Space approach to modeling dynamic system: Introduction, Transient-Response Analysis OF Systems in State-Space Form with MATLAB, State-Space Modeling of System with Input Derivatives, Transformation of Mathematical Models with MATLAB, Example Problems and Solutions, Problems.

units.title: Electrical systems and electromechanical systems
units.text: Electrical systems and electromechanical systems: Introduction, Fundamentals of Electrical Circuits, Mathematical Modeling of Electrical Systems, Analogous Systems, Mathematical Modeling of Electromechanical Systems, Mathematical Modeling of Operational- Amplifier Systems

units.title: Fluid systems and thermal systems
units.text: Fluid systems and thermal systems: Introduction, Mathematical Modeling of Liquid-Level Systems, Mathematical Modeling of Pneumatic Systems, Linearization of Nonlinear Systems, Mathematical Modeling of Hydraulic Systems, Mathematical Modeling of Thermal Systems

text_books: 1. Oghata (2007), “System Dynamics” Pearson Publications. 2. Norman Nise (2008), “Control System Engineering” Wiley.
reference_books: 1. Close, Fredrik (2001), “Modeling and Analysis of Dynamic System” Wiley. 2. Narsico, George Julius (2005), “Modeling and Control of Dynamic System” Thomson.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To impart the knowledge of the basics of the automobiles. 2. To introduce the different automobile systems like suspension, axles and steering and transmission systems in the Automobiles.

outcomes.text: Understand the types of engines used in automobile and their characteristics, selections of suitable rear axle, gear etc.
Analyze the chassis layout, steering geometry, types of suspensions, and clutch and gear mechanism of vehicle.
Understand the clutch and braking mechanisms.

units.title: Vehicle Performance
units.text: Vehicle Performance: Types of engines used in automobiles, their characteristics and selections, resistance to motion of vehicle, air, rolling and gradient resistances, power requirement for acceleration and tradability, selection of suitable rear axle and gear ratios.

units.title: Chassis
units.text: Chassis: Chassis layout, power plant location, types of automobiles, weight distribution stability, type of frame, materials.

units.title: Steering
units.text: Steering: Steering geometry, wheel alignment and wheel balancing, center point Steering, Ackerman and Davis steering, cornering force slip angle, scrub radius, steering conventional layout of steering system. Steering systems for independent suspension, wheel wobble and shimmy, power steering. Axle: Axle material, load and stresses on front axle design, steering heads, axle bearing wheel alignment, differential and their types, rear axle arrangements, two speed rear axle, single, double and triple reduction rear axles. Tires: Function, construction, types of tires, tubeless tire.

units.title: Suspension System
units.text: Suspension System: types of suspensions, materials, shackles and mountings, types of springs, shock absorbers, sprung weight and un sprung weight, conventional suspension system, independent suspension, air suspension, hydra-gas suspension, rubber suspension, interconnected suspension, self- leveling suspension

units.title: Drive mechanisms
units.text: Drive mechanisms: Torque reaction, driving thrust, propeller shaft, universal joints, and constant velocity universal joints. Differential, action of differential, constructional details, types of rear axles, materials, bearing loads, double reduction and two speed axle, front wheel drive, all-wheel drive, introduction to continuous variable transmission (CVT).

units.title: Clutch and braking mechanisms
units.text: Clutch and braking mechanisms: Clutch: Clutch mechanism-wet/dry clutch- constant pressure, constant wear type, back up plate, cone clutch, centrifugal clutch, multi-plate clutch, clutch materials, influence of temperature on the performance, torque limiter. Numerical Examples. Braking Systems: types and construction, mechanical, hydraulic system, diagonal braking system, antilock braking system. Numerical Examples.

text_books: 1. K. K. Jain and Asthana (2002), “Automobile Engineering”, TTI Publications. 2. R.K. Rajput (2007), “A Text Book of Automobile Engineering”, Laxmi Publications. 3. S. Kripal (2009), “Automobile Engineering Vol I”, New Chand Jain.
reference_books: 1. G. Genta, Morello (2009), “The Automotive Chassis: System Design”, Springer. 2. Society of Automotive Engineering (1997), “Automotive Engineering”. 3. D. Crolla (2009), “Automotive Engineering: Powertrain, Chassis System, Vehicle, Body”, Butterworth- Heinemann.

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. To understand the impact of different types of stresses on components 2. To introduce the fundamental concepts of design of simple machine parts.

outcomes.text: Understand the importance of materials in design and select appropriate materials for safe design.
Apply the principle and basic procedure of machine components design.
Analyze the different types of loads and stresses acting on components.
Design of various machine components like shafts, couplings, springs, joints, gears and belts.

units.title: Stress Analysis
units.text: Stress Analysis: Design process-Selection of materials-preferred numbers, fits and tolerances, direct, bending and shear stress-combined stresses-eccentric loading on machine members-stress concentration and notch sensitivity.

units.title: Design of Shafts, Coupling and Springs
units.text: Design of Shafts, Coupling and Springs: Design of solid shafts based on strength, rigidity. Design of muff coupling and rigid flange coupling, Design of coil springs.

units.title: Design of Joints
units.text: Design of Joints: Design of bolted joints including axial and tensile loading, Knuckle joints, Cotter joints, Bolt of uniform strength, Thread locking devices, Design of riveted joints for structures.

units.title: Design of Gears
units.text: Design of Gears: Design of spur gear based on contact stress and beam strength and based on Lewis and Buckingham equations.

units.title: Design of Flexible Drives
units.text: Design of Flexible Drives: Design of flat belt and V-belt drives.

text_books: 1. J. F. Shigley (2008), “Mechanical Engineering Design”, 8th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill 2. V. B. Bhandari (2010), “Design of Machine Elements”, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill
reference_books: 1. Hall, Holowenko, Laughen, (2008) “Machine Design” Schaum’s outline series Tata McGraw Hill Publication. 2. M. F. Spotts (2004), “Design of Machine Elements”, 8th Edition, Pearson Publication. 3. PSG design data book

program: B. Tech. (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: 1. Acquire introductory knowledge of Additive Manufacturing (AM) and its capabilities in the modern digital manufacturing industry. 2. To get acquainted with the operating principles and applications of most prominent technologies in the field of Additive Manufacturing. 3. Explore the Design for Additive Manufacturing capabilities of each AM process and to identify and create complex and novel designs.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental principles of various Additive Manufacturing (AM) technologies, material requirements and cost considerations with regards to each AM process.
Identify critical areas where AM can be applied to create value for the entire product life- cycle.
Select the right AM process for a given application.
Develop an enterprising perspective concerning the application of AM in the design of a product, either entirely or partly.

units.title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
units.text: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing: Introduction to AM, history of AM, definition, distinction between AM, CNC & other digital manufacturing techniques, reasons to use AM, classifications of AM processes, design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM), AM industry: present and future, AM process chain, CAD and file formats for AM. Introduction to Metal Additive Manufacturing. Laser Cutting vs Water jet cutting.

units.title: Extrusion based AM processes
units.text: Extrusion based AM processes: Fused deposition Modeling(FDM), history of FDM, material requirements, workflow: material loading, liquefaction, bonding, solidification, support generation, nozzle dynamics, applications, benefits and limitations, post-processing, material characterization, extrusion of: ceramics, metals, biomaterials, composites, non-planer systems, contour crafting, concrete printing.

units.title: Vat Polymerization AM process
units.text: Vat Polymerization AM process: Stereolithography apparatus(SLA), history of SLA, material requirements, workflow: SLA chemistry, reaction mechanism, scan patterns, applications, benefits and limitations, other liquid polymer- based systems: Solid Ground Curing (SGC), Microstreolithography, Digital Light Processing (DLP), Continuous Liquid Interface Production (CLIP), Large-Scale Rapid Liquid Printing.

units.title: Sheet Lamination AM Processes
units.text: Sheet Lamination AM Processes: Laminated Object Manufacturing (LOM), LOM of paper, polymer and composite sheets, LOM mechanism: gluing, adhesive bonding, bond then from, from then bond, thermal bonding, sheet metal clamping, Ultrasonic Additive Manufacturing(UAM), ultrasonic welding fundamentals, UAM process parameters, material characterization.

units.title: Powder Bed Fusion AM Process
units.text: Powder Bed Fusion AM Process: Selective Laser Sintering (SLS): process workflow and material requirements, powder production methods, powder fusion mechanism, polymer ageing and recycling, High Speed Sintering(HSS), Multi-Jet Fusion(MJF), polymer powder characterization and selection, Selective Laser Melting (SLM): process workflow and material requirements, powder melting mechanism, melt pool dynamics, laser scan patterns, post- processing, powder production, handling and recycling, Electron Beam Melting (EBM) Process.

units.title: Binder Jetting (BJ) & Material Jetting AM Process
units.text: Binder Jetting (BJ) & Material Jetting AM Process: workflow, thermal and piezoelectric inkjet, material requirements, material jetting fluid mechanics, drop-on-demand and continuous methods of MJ, material jetting of metals, ceramics, nanomaterial, BJ AM Process: process workflow, material requirements, powder characterization for BJ process, binder-powder interaction, binder properties.

units.title: Directed Energy Deposition (DED) Processes
units.text: Directed Energy Deposition (DED) Processes: Process workflow, materials feeding for DED: powder (Laser Engineered Net Shaping) & wire, process parameters and optimization, Electron Beam Additive Manufacturing (EBAM) plasma-based DED, Cold Spray.

units.title: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM)
units.text: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM): Key process-specific DfAM guidelines, AM file formats (STL, 3MF, AMF, PLY, VRML, LEO): processing, conversion and repair algorithms, tool path generation, topology optimization, generative design, slicing and support generation.

text_books: 1. Gibson I, Rosen D W, Stucker B (2015), “Additive Manufacturing Technologies: Rapid Prototyping to Direct Digital Manufacturing”, Springer.
reference_books: 1. Yang, L., Hsu, K., Baughman, B., Godfrey, D., Medina, F., Menon, M., & Wiener, S. (2017). “Additive manufacturing of metals: the technology, materials, design and production”, Springer. 2. Gebhardt, Andreas. (2011). "Understanding additive manufacturing." Hanser Publication 3. Bártolo, P. J. (Ed.). (2011). Stereolithography: materials, processes and applications. Springer Science & Business Media.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at developing the detailed understanding of various mechanism used in devices or machines. This course focuses on analysis of the motion of mechanisms and to design mechanisms that yield the desired motion. The course is designed for the students to understand and master the concepts of displacement, velocity and acceleration of simple mechanisms and machine components. These include cam profile and its analysis, gear kinematics with gear train calculations, belt drives and chain drives, and friction clutches and brakes.

outcomes.text: Describe the fundamentals of links, mechanisms, machines, brakes and clutches
Analyse planar mechanism for displacement, velocity and acceleration graphically and analytically
Construct various type of Cam profiles and analyze the standard motion of the follower
Illustrate the machine components like belt, ropes and chains for required mechanisms
Estimate the performance and efficiency of brakes and clutches, considering frictional forces and their impact on machine operation
Evaluate simple, compound, reverted, and epicyclic gear trains to determine velocity ratios

units.title: Introduction of Mechanisms and Machines
units.text: Introduction of Mechanisms and Machines Concepts of Kinematics and Dynamics, Mechanisms and Machines, Planar and Spatial Mechanisms, Kinematic Pairs, Kinematic Chains, Kinematic Diagrams, Kinematic Inversion, four bar chain, single and double Slider Crank Mechanisms and their Inversions, Degrees of Freedom, Mobility and range of movement - Kutzbach and Grubler’s criterion, Number Synthesis, Grashof’s criterion, straight line mechanisms.

units.title: Velocity and Acceleration Analysis
units.text: Velocity and Acceleration Analysis Velocity and Acceleration analysis: (Graphical approach) Velocity analysis: instantaneous centre of rotation method, relative velocity method for four bar pin jointed linkages and four bar slider crank linkages. Velocity and Acceleration analysis - relative method four bar pin jointed linkages and four bar slider crank linkages.

units.title: CAM
units.text: CAM Types of cams, Types of followers, Follower displacement programming, Derivatives of follower Motion, Motions of follower, Layout of cam profiles. 4. Belt, Ropes and Chains Types of belt drive, Velocity ratio, Slip, Pulley arrangement, Length of belt, Law of belting, Ratio of friction tension, Power transmitted, Centrifugal effects on belts, Maximum power transmitted, Creep, Chains, Chain length, Angular speed ratio, Classification of chains. 5. Friction Clutches and Brakes Introduction to friction clutches, Rolling Friction, Types of Clutches, Types of brakes, Block and Shoe brakes, Differential band brake, Internal expanding shoe brake. 6. Gears and Gear Trains Terminology, Law of Gearing, Characteristics of involute and cycloidal action, Interference and undercutting, centre distance variation, minimum number of teeth, contact ratio, spur, helical, spiral bevel and worm gears, problems. Gear Trains: Synthesis of Simple, compound & reverted gear trains, Analysis of epicyclic gear trains

text_books: 1. Thomas Beven, Theory of Machines, 3rd Edition, Pearson, 2009. 2. S. S. Rattan, Theory of Machines, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, New Delhi, 2009.
reference_books: 1. John Uicker, G R Pennock J. E. Shigley, Theory of Mechanisms and Machines, 3rd Edition, University Press, 2010. 2. P. L. Ballaney, Theory of Machines and Mechanisms, 24th Edition, Khanna Publishing, New Delhi, 2005.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech /B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course describes the application of Engineering Thermodynamics to model the energy conversion phenomenon. With this course one can impart knowledge of air compressors and components of steam power system. This course provides basics of I.C engines, refrigeration systems and air conditioning systems and also build a bridge for these courses.

outcomes.text: Analyse the working principles and performance parameters of reciprocating and rotary air compressors
Evaluate the design, efficiency, and critical pressure conditions in nozzles and diffusers
Apply thermodynamic principles to assess the performance of steam generators and turbines
Examine the performance and working conditions of condensers and cooling towers
Assess different refrigeration and air-conditioning systems, including refrigerants, cycles, and working principles
Evaluate the performance of internal combustion (IC) engines, including heat balance calculations and valve/port timing diagrams

units.title: Reciprocating Air Compressors
units.text: Reciprocating Air Compressors Working principle, work done, Effect of clearance volume, Single and multistage compressors, Volumetric efficiency, Intercooling in multistage compressors, calculation of power requirement, Rotary compressors. Review of Thermodynamics, Vapour Power cycles, Binary Vapour Cycle, Combined Cycle and Co-generation.

units.title: Steam Generators
units.text: Steam Generators Fire Tube Boilers, Water Tube Boilers, Boiler Mountings and Accessories, High Pressure Boilers. Draught, Performance of Boilers, Combustion of Fuel.

units.title: Nozzles and Diffusers
units.text: Nozzles and Diffusers Theory and Design, Efficiency and Critical Pressure, General Relationship and supersaturated Flow. Steam Turbines Impulse and Reaction turbine Principles - Compounding – Types - Velocity diagrams for simple and multistage turbines - Speed regulations – Governors.

units.title: Condensers and Cooling Towers
units.text: Condensers and Cooling Towers Classification of condenser, air leakage, condenser performance parameters. Cooling tower design.

units.title: Refrigeration
units.text: Refrigeration Refrigeration cycles, Reversed Carnot cycle, Vapour compression system, Vapour absorption refrigeration system. Refrigerants Their classification and desirable properties. Air-Conditioning Principles of air-conditioning, Types of Air- conditioning Systems, Summer and Winter air -conditioning. Cryogenics Introduction and applications.

units.title: IC Engines
units.text: IC Engines Classification, Working of SI & CI engine, Port timing and Valve timing diagram, Performance testing of I.C Engines, Heat balance calculations.

text_books: 1. P. K. Nag, Basics and Applied Thermodynamics, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. P. K. Nag, Power Plant Engineering, 4th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2016. 3. Vanwvylen & Sonntag, Classical Thermodynamics, 5th Edition, Wiley Eastern, 1994.
reference_books: 1. Y. Cengel and M. Boles, Thermodynamics -An Engineering Approach, 6th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008. 2. M. J. Moran, H. N. Shapiro, D. D. Boettner, M. B. Bailey, Fundamentals of Engineering Thermodynamics, 7th Edition, John Wiley and Sons, 2011.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech / B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course is aimed at training the students on lathe machine with different turning operations like such as plain, taper turning along with operations like facing, thread cutting, grooving, knurling and wire drawing die on metals.

outcomes.text: Apply different operations on lathe like plain, taper turning, facing, grooving and knurling
Operate different operations like screw cutting and threading
Perform different operation on lathe like drilling, boring, counter boring, internal taper turning

units.text: Job on lathe performing plain and taper turning.
Job on precision turning and screw cutting.
Assembly of Two pieces using operations like drilling, boring, counter boring, internal taper turning and broaching operations.

lab_work: Performing 15 week practical to complete jobs as per the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course nurtures the practical product development aptitude in students by requiring them to conceptualize and ideate a product or a method and then test its feasibility. It requires students to gather extensive information on the current available designs and their functionality. The final proposal details a product or a method distinguishing itself from the current availability.

outcomes.text: Initiate a product or methodology development process
Analyze the basic feasibility criteria and stress testing of their proposal
Develop an understanding of various aspects in contemporary system design

units.text: Initiating and Ideation
Conceptualization
Literature Review and Preliminary Design
Rigorous Analysis and Feasibility
Proposed Design and Approval
Testing, Validation, Implementation
Presentation and Report

lab_work: Lab work consists of the full stack development of experimental open-ended mini-projects concerning general aspects of mechatronic systems.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course emphasizes the importance and applicability of supervisory control with acquired data using industrial communication protocols. It introduces and reinforces the concept of a virtual instrument on a suitable computational platform using graphical programming. It also introduces students to the design of basic industrial control systems.

outcomes.text: Apply the fundamentals of Supervisory Control, Virtual Instrumentation and data Acquisition
Create the hardware-in-loop simulations
Create a VI system to solve real time problems using data acquisition

units.title: Introduction to Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA)
units.text: Introduction to Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Introduction to supervisory control, Need of SCADA, Architecture of SCADA. Components of SCADA: MTU, RTU and HMI. Interfacing of SCADA with PLC.

units.title: Fundamentals of Virtual Instrumentation
units.text: Fundamentals of Virtual Instrumentation Historical perspective, advantages, block diagrams and architecture of a virtual instrument, data-flow techniques, graphical programming in data flow, comparison with conventional programming Software Overview LabVIEW, Graphical User Interface - controls and indicators data types, data flow programming, editing, debugging and running a virtual instrument, graphical programming pallets, their configuration, VIs and sub-Vis, typical examples

units.title: Programming Structure
units.text: Programming Structure FOR loops, WHILE loop, CASE structure, formula node, sequence structures Introduction to Arrays and Clusters Array operations, cluster functions, graphs and charts, local and global variables

units.title: State Machines
units.text: State Machines Introduction, definition of State Machine, a simple State Machine, event structures File Input/Output Introduction, file formats, file I/O functions, path functions, sample VIs to demonstrate file WRITE and READ function String Handling Introduction, string functions, LabVIEW string formats, typical examples

units.title: Basics of Data Acquisition
units.text: Basics of Data Acquisition Introduction to data acquisition, classification of Signals, analog interfacing connecting signal to the board, analog input/output techniques, digital I/O, counters and timers DAQ Hardware configuration Introduction, Measurement and Automation Explorer, DAQ assistants, analysis assistants, interfacing instruments

units.title: GPIB and RS232
units.text: GPIB and RS232 Introduction, RS232 Vs. GPIB, handshaking, GPIB interfacing, RS232C/RS485 interfacing, standard commands for programmable instruments, VISA Standard bus architectures ISA, PCI, VME and PXI.

text_books: 1. Jovitha Jerome, Virtual instrumentation Using LabVIEW, 4th Edition, PHI Learning, 2010, ISBN: 978-8120340305. 2. Sanjay Gupta and Joseph John, Virtual Instrumentation Using Lab View, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, New Delhi, 2010, ISBN : 978-0070700284.
reference_books: 1. Lisa. K. Wills, LabVIEW for Everyone, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall of India, 2008, ISBN: 978- 0132681940. 2. Garry Johnson and Richard Jennings, LabVIEW Graphical Programming, 4th Edition, McGraw Hill Professional, 2006, ISBN No-978-1259005336.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Electronic systems, Introduction to Digital systems, Microprocessors and Microcontroller
objectives: The course is designed to introduce the students in depth with various sensors and transducers used in industrial situations. It also emphasizes the hardware and programming aspects of PLCs for industrial applications.

outcomes.text: Select and Apply sensors and transducers for mechatronics application
Design PLC based sequential control mechanisms
Create PLC Ladder logic programs for industrial applications

units.title: Sensors and Transducers
units.text: Sensors and Transducers Principles, Classification and applications. Transducer Selection Criteria for Mechatronics applications. Pressure Transducers Bellows, Diaphragm, Bourdon tubes, Pirani Gauge, Ionization Gauge, Piezoelectric transducer and Strain Gauge. Flow Transducers Orifice Plate, Pitot tube, Ventury tube, Rota meter, Ultrasonic Flow meter, Electromagnetic flow meter. Temperature Transducers RTD, Thermistor, Thermocouple, Pyrometers. Displacement/Position Transducers LVDT, Hall effect transducers, Optical encoders, Resonant sensor.

units.title: Proximity Sensors
units.text: Proximity Sensors Basic Principle, Construction, Working and applications of Inductive, Capacitive, Ultrasonic, Magnetic and Photoelectric proximity sensors. Modes of operation of Photoelectric proximity sensors. Performance comparison and Specifications of different Proximity sensors.

units.title: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)
units.text: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) Evolution of PLCs, Discrete State Control, Block Diagram of PLC, Classification of PLCs. Description of PLC components: Power Supply, Input and Output Modules, Discrete Input and Output Modules, Analog Input and output Modules, Programming Devices, CPU, I/O module specifications. Typical PLC specifications. Different Addressing modes.

units.title: PLC Programming
units.text: PLC Programming Memory Organization of PLC, Program Files, Data Files, Program Scan Cycle. Types of programming languages used in PLCs: Ladder logic, Functional block diagram, Sequential flow chart, Instruction List, Structured Text. Rules for ladder logic Programming. Relay Logic Instructions, Latching, Interlocking, Triggers, Logic gates programming in PLC. Timer Instructions: On Delay, Off Delay and Pulse Timers. Counter Instructions: Up counter and Down Counter. Data manipulation instructions, Mathematical instructions, Sequence and Shift register instructions. Analog Module programming.

units.title: Application Development
units.text: Application Development Interfacing of various inputs & outputs to PLC (Electromagnetic Control Relays, Contactors, Motor Starters, Manually operated switches, Mechanically operated switches, Proximity sensors), Interfacing Remote I/O s with PLC. Design of Tank level control System, Sequential switching of motors, Motor starters, Temperature/Pressure control, Conveyor belt control, Pneumatic Cylinder sequencing, Automatic Bottle filler. Industrial case studies.

text_books: 1. Curtis D. Johnson, Process control Instrumentation Technology, 8th illustrated Edition, Prentice Hall, 2013. 2. M.Mitra and S. Gupta, Programmable logic controllers and Industrial Automation: An Introduction, 2nd Edition, Penram International Publishing (India) Pvt. Ltd., 2017.
reference_books: 1. Petreuzeulla, Programmable Controllers, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2005. 2. D. Patranabis, Principal of Industrial Instrumentation, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2010.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of Control Systems, Computer Programming, Calculus, Linear Algebra and Probability, Programming Knowledge and Statistics.
objectives: The primary objective of the course is to introduce students to the building blocks of Artificial Intelligence, fuzzy logic, and its techniques to distinguish from conventional techniques. The course also lays emphasis on the application of supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms for real-world systems.

outcomes.text: Apply basic principles of AI in problem solving, inference, perception, knowledge representation and learning.
Interpret and apply fuzzy logic for various real-world applications.
Recognize the characteristics of machine learning that makes it useful to solve real-world problems.

units.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
units.text: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Meaning and definition of AI, significance and role of AI, application of AI, history of AI. Search Techniques- Introduction to informed and uninformed search, State space search: Depth first search, Breadth first search, Heuristic search: Best first search, Intelligent Agent

units.title: Artificial Neural Network
units.text: Artificial Neural Network Basic concepts of neural network; Overview of learning rules and parameters, activation functions, single layer perceptron and multilayer perceptron, Multilayer feed forward network, Backpropagation networks: Architecture and algorithm.

units.title: Fuzzy Logic
units.text: Fuzzy Logic Concepts of uncertainty, properties and operations on classical sets and fuzzy sets, classical & fuzzy relations, Membership functions and its types, fuzzification, fuzzy rule-based systems, defuzzification, fuzzy propositions, fuzzy inference system, recent applications.

units.title: Introduction to machine learning

objectives: This course emphasizes the understanding of embedded systems and real-time operating systems that can help identify and define design problems and challenges of real-time operating systems. The course elaborates the design of embedded system applications to process inputs and gather data in real time to produce desired output.

outcomes.text: Grasp the concept of embedded systems and its design requirements for various applications
Implement embedded system communication protocols
Use the Real Time Operating System (RTOS) and its multitasking functionality

units.text: Introduction to Embedded systems and its Design aspects Architecture of Embedded Systems, Design Metrics, Examples of embedded systems, hardware/software co-design, Embedded micro controller cores (ARM, RISC, CISC, and SOC), embedded memories, sensors, and interfacing techniques

units.title: Hardware Software Co-Design and Program Modeling

Analyze the workings of life saving and life support systems used in the real world
Grasp the basic principles and working of the health monitoring equipment

It introduces and reinforces the concept of a virtual instrument on a suitable computational platform using graphical programming. It also introduces students to the design of basic industrial control systems.

outcomes.text: Apply the fundamentals of Supervisory Control, Virtual Instrumentation and data Acquisition
Create the hardware-in-loop simulations
Create a VI system to solve real time problems using data acquisition

objectives: The course is designed to introduce the students in depth with various sensors and transducers used in industrial situations. It also emphasizes the hardware and programming aspects of PLCs for industrial applications.

outcomes.text: Select and Apply sensors and transducers for mechatronics application
Design PLC based sequential control mechanisms
Create PLC Ladder logic programs for industrial applications

units.title: Sensors and Transducers
units.text: Sensors and Transducers Principles, Classification and applications. Transducer Selection Criteria for Mechatronics applications. Pressure Transducers Bellows, Diaphragm, Bourdon tubes, Pirani Gauge, Ionization Gauge, Piezoelectric transducer and Strain Gauge. Flow Transducers Orifice Plate, Pitot tube, Ventury tube, Rota meter, Ultrasonic Flow meter, Electromagnetic flow meter. Temperature Transducers RTD, Thermistor, Thermocouple, Pyrometers. Displacement/Position Transducers LVDT, Hall effect transducers, Optical encoders, Resonant sensor.

units.text: Proximity Sensors Basic Principle, Construction, Working and applications of Inductive, Capacitive, Ultrasonic, Magnetic and Photoelectric proximity sensors. Modes of operation of Photoelectric proximity sensors. Performance comparison and Specifications of different Proximity sensors.

units.title: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)
units.text: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) Evolution of PLCs, Discrete State Control, Block Diagram of PLC, Classification of PLCs. Description of PLC components: Power Supply, Input and Output Modules, Discrete Input and Output Modules, Analog Input and output Modules, Programming Devices, CPU, I/O module specifications. Typical PLC specifications. Different Addressing modes.

units.title: PLC Programming
units.text: PLC Programming Memory Organization of PLC, Program Files, Data Files, Program Scan Cycle. Types of programming languages used in PLCs: Ladder logic, Functional block diagram, Sequential flow chart, Instruction List, Structured Text. Rules for ladder logic Programming. Relay Logic Instructions, Latching, Interlocking, Triggers, Logic gates programming in PLC. Timer Instructions: On Delay, Off Delay and Pulse Timers. Counter Instructions: Up counter and Down Counter. Data manipulation instructions, Mathematical instructions, Sequence and Shift register instructions. Analog Module programming.

units.title: Application Development
units.text: Application Development Interfacing of various inputs & outputs to PLC (Electromagnetic Control Relays, Contactors, Motor Starters, Manually operated switches, Mechanically operated switches, Proximity sensors), Interfacing Remote I/O s with PLC. Design of Tank level control System, Sequential switching of motors, Motor starters, Temperature/Pressure control, Conveyor belt control, Pneumatic Cylinder sequencing, Automatic Bottle filler. Industrial case studies.

reference_books: 1. Petreuzeulla, Programmable Controllers, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2005. 2. D. Patranabis, Principal of Industrial Instrumentation, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2010.

The course elaborates the design of embedded system applications to process inputs and gather data in real time to produce desired output.

outcomes.text: Grasp the concept of embedded systems and its design requirements for various applications
Implement embedded system communication protocols
Use the Real Time Operating System (RTOS) and its multitasking functionality

units.title: Introduction to Embedded systems and its Design aspects
units.text: Introduction to Embedded systems and its Design aspects Architecture of Embedded Systems, Design Metrics, Examples of embedded systems, hardware/software co-design, Embedded micro controller cores (ARM, RISC, CISC, and SOC), embedded memories, sensors, and interfacing techniques

units.title: Hardware Software Co-Design and Program Modeling
units.text: Hardware Software Co-Design and Program Modeling Fundamental Issues in Hardware Software Co-Design, Embedded communication protocols (Xbee, RS-232, I2C and CAN) Computational Models in Embedded Design, Introduction to Unified Modeling Language, Higher level programming models.

units.title: Embedded Firmware & Hardware Design and Development
units.text: Embedded Firmware & Hardware Design and Development Embedded Firmware Design Approaches, Embedded Firmware Development Languages, Programming in Embedded C, Hardware Design: Analog electronics and digital electronics components, Electronic design automation (EDA) tools, PCB layout design.

units.title: The Embedded System Development Environment
units.text: The Embedded System Development Environment The Integrated Development Environment (IDE), Types of Files Generated on Cross Compilation, Disassembler/Decompiler, Simulators, Emulators and Debugging, Target Hardware Debugging, Boundary Scan.

units.title: Real-Time Operating System (RTOS) and current OS trends
units.text: Real-Time Operating System (RTOS) and current OS trends Operating System Basics, Types of OS, Tasks, Process and Threads, Multiprocessing and Multitasking, Task Scheduling, Threads and Processes Scheduling: Putting them altogether, Task Communication, Task Synchronization, Device Drivers, Embedded OS Trends, RTOS example: VxWorks.

units.title: Case study
units.text: Case study DSP/microprocessor-based, micro-controller-based, or FPGA-based system design.

text_books: 1. Raj Kamal, Embedded Systems, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Education Private Limited, 2017. 2. Shibu K. V., Introduction to Embedded Systems, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Education Private Limited, 2009.
reference_books: 1. James K Peckol, Embedded Systems - A Contemporary Design Tool, John Wiley Publication, 2015. 2. Frank Vahid, and Tony Givargis, Embedded System Design, John Wiley Publication, 2014.
