program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Electronic systems, Signals and Systems
objectives: This course helps the students to understand the basic principles and working of various biomedical monitoring devices. It is aimed at developing the core competency and skill to design and develop new health care systems.

outcomes.text: Summarize the working of various biomedical devices
Analyze the workings of life saving and life support systems used in the real world
Grasp the basic principles and working of the health monitoring equipment

units.title: Basic principle, working and technical specifications of
units.text: Basic principle, working and technical specifications of ECG, EMG and EEG machines, LEAD configurations, 10-20 electrode system measuring techniques for EOG, ERG and phonocardiography, Patient Safety: Electric shock hazards, leakage currents, safety codes for electromedical equipment.

units.title: Cardiac Pacemakers
units.text: Cardiac Pacemakers Need for a pacemaker, modes of operation, classification codes for pacemaker, external and implantable pacemaker, programmable pacemaker, Power sources for pacemakers, leads and electrodes, recent developments of Implantable Pacemakers.

units.title: Patient Monitoring Systems and Telemetry
units.text: Patient Monitoring Systems and Telemetry Measurement of heart rate, pulse rate, blood pressure, temperature and respiration rate, apnea detector. Heart rate variability measurement, Basics of Telemetry, Multi-channel Telemetry Point of care devices and their design considerations for homecare devices: glucometer, pulse oximeter

units.title: Basic principle and working of Audiometers and hearing aid
units.text: Basic principle and working of Audiometers and hearing aid Basic audiometer, pure tone and speech audiometer, evoked response audiometry, introduction to hearing aids and cochlear implants.

units.title: Basic principle and working of Fetal and Neonatal Monitoring System
units.text: Basic principle and working of Fetal and Neonatal Monitoring System Cardiotocograph, methods of monitoring of fetal heart rate, monitoring of labour activity, incubator and infant warmer

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course emphasizes the use of software platforms used in the real world for computer aided design, analysis and manufacturing, and computer aided manufacturing. The process of culmination of computer aided engineering drawing into Computer Numerically Controlled machine programming is elaborated in the course.

outcomes.text: Create accurate and precise geometry of complex engineering systems and use the geometric models in various engineering applications
Apply the concepts of machining for the purpose of selection of machining parameters and cutting tools for CNC milling and turning
Program the four-axis CNC simulator and the actual CNC machine for creating a finished specimen with a given geometry

units.title: Introduction and Elements of Interactive Computer Graphics
units.text: Introduction and Elements of Interactive Computer Graphics The design process, the role of modeling and communication. Modeling using CAD, product life cycle and Computer-Aided Design (CAD)/ Computer- Aided Manufacturing(CAM), Concurrent engineering in product design and development, Collaborative Engineering, CAD System Architecture-Software and Hardware.

units.title: Techniques for Geometric Modeling
units.text: Techniques for Geometric Modeling Graphic standards, The parametric representation of geometry-Bezier curves, Cubic spline curve, B-Spline curve, parametric representation of line, circle, ellipse and parabola, Constructive solid geometry (CSG), Boundary representation (B-rep), Wire Frame modeling, Solid modeling, Surface modeling, feature based modeling, Parent child relationship.

Transformation, Manipulation and Data Storage 2D and 3D Transformations (Translation, Rotation, Scaling and Magnification), Concatenations, Matrix representation, Problems on Transformations. Object transformation, mirror transformation, Bill of Materials from attribute data, Engineering data management system, relational data base for design, object oriental database, Design Information Systems.

units.title: NC and CNC Technology
units.text: NC and CNC Technology Introduction, basic components of Numeric Control (NC) system, NC procedure, NC coordinate systems, NC motion control systems, Various actuation systems and feedback devices like encoder, tachogenerator, etc. Applications, Advantages and Disadvantages of NC machines. Constructional details of Computer Numeric Control (CNC) machines, computer-assisted numerical control programming, Manual part programming methods, Various G and M codes Flexible Manufacturing Systems (FMS), Automated Material Handling and Storage Systems like Robots, Automated Guided Vehicles (AGV) and Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems (AS/RS)

units.title: CNC Simulations
units.text: CNC Simulations Four-axis CNC simulator operation and programming, creating complex geometries, simulations on a software simulation platform

units.title: Testing and Validation
units.text: Testing and Validation Hands-on testing and programming of an actual CNC machine, complex geometries and G-code/M-code generation

text_books: 1. Mikell P. Groover and Emory W. Zimmers, Jr., CAD/CAM Computer Aided and Manufacturing, Prentice Hall, PHI, 1984. (Classic Book) 2. Ibrahim Zeid, R. Sivasubramanian, CAD/ CAM, Theory and Practice, Tata McGraw Hill Publications, 2nd Edition, 2009.
reference_books: 1. P. N. Rao, CAD/CAM Principles and Applications, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Publications, 2010. 2. P. Radhakrishan, S. Subramanyan, V. Raju, CAD/CAM/CIM, 2nd Edition, New Age International Publishers, 2004.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Manufacturing Processes, Probability and Statistics, Management Accounting for Engineers
objectives: The course is designed to introduce students to the concept of total quality management and technical skills required to lead for quality improvement. The course also elaborates tools and techniques for quality improvement.

outcomes.text: Apply various techniques of quality management for improving quality and productivity
Analyze data and interpret results using various total quality tools and statistical techniques
Identify the importance of teamwork, empowerment and motivation in quality management

units.title: Introduction to Total Quality in Organizations
units.text: Introduction to Total Quality in Organizations Importance of Quality. The concept of Quality. Quality in manufacturing. Quality in services. Principles of total quality. Comparison of total quality with traditional management practices. Total Quality and organizational models.

units.title: Approaches to Total Quality
units.text: Approaches to Total Quality Deming’s management philosophy, Deming’s 14 principles of management. The Juran philosophy. The Crosby philosophy. ISO 9000 standards: Structure, registration and perspectives. Quality awards. Six sigma: Concept, Principle, Methodology, Scope, Advantage and limitations.

text_books: 1. Dale Besterfield, Carol Besterfield-Michna, Glen Besterfield, Mary Besterfield-Sacre, Hemant Urdhwareshe, Rashmi Urdhwareshe, Total Quality Management, 5th Edition, Pearson, 2018. 2. reference_books: 1. P. N. Mukherjee, Total Quality Management, Prentice Hall India Learning, 2006. 2. John S. Oakland, Total Quality Management and Operational Excellence, 4th Edition, Routledge, 2014.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course nurtures the practical product development aptitude in students by requiring them to conceptualize and ideate a product or a method and then test its feasibility. It requires students to gather extensive information on the current available designs and their functionality. The final proposal details a product or a method distinguishing itself from the current availability.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental concepts of DC circuits, including Kirchhoff’s laws and network theorems
Interpret the principles of AC circuit analysis, including resonance and three-phase systems
Illustrate the working principles of transformers and different types of electrical machines
Explain the basic operation of analog electronic components, including rectifiers, transistors and operational amplifiers
Make use of logic gates and Boolean expressions for digital circuits

units.text: Initiating and Ideation
Conceptualization
Literature Review and Preliminary Design
Rigorous Analysis and Feasibility
Proposed Design and Approval
Testing, Validation, Implementation
Presentation and Report

lab_work: Lab work consists of the full stack development of experimental open-ended mini-projects concerning general aspects of mechatronic systems.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course emphasizes the importance and applicability of supervisory control with acquired data using industrial communication protocols. It introduces and reinforces the concept of a virtual instrument on a suitable computational platform using graphical programming. It also introduces students to the design of basic industrial control systems.

outcomes.text: Apply the fundamentals of Supervisory Control, Virtual Instrumentation and Data Acquisition
Create the hardware-in-loop simulations
Create a VI system to solve a real time problem using data acquisition
Analyze and apply industrial communication protocols such as RS232, RS485 and GPIB
Evaluate the performance of the SCADA-based control systems

units.title: Introduction to Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA)
units.text: Introduction to Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Introduction to supervisory control, Need of SCADA, Architecture of SCADA. Components of SCADA: MTU, RTU and HMI. Interfacing of SCADA with PLC.

units.title: Fundamentals of Virtual Instrumentation
units.text: Fundamentals of Virtual Instrumentation Historical perspective, advantages, block diagrams and architecture of a virtual instrument, data-flow techniques, graphical programming in data flow, comparison with conventional programming Software Overview LabVIEW, Graphical User Interface - controls and indicators data types, data flow programming, editing, debugging and running a virtual instrument, graphical programming pallets, their configuration, VIs and sub-Vis, typical examples

units.title: Programming Structure
units.text: Programming Structure FOR loops, WHILE loop, CASE structure, formula node, sequence structures Introduction to Arrays and Clusters Array operations, cluster functions, graphs and charts, local and global variables

units.title: State Machines
units.text: State Machines Introduction, definition of State Machine, a simple State Machine, event structures File Input/Output Introduction, file formats, file I/O functions, path functions, sample VIs to demonstrate file WRITE and READ function String Handling Introduction, string functions, LabVIEW string formats, typical examples

units.title: Basics of Data Acquisition
units.text: Basics of Data Acquisition Introduction to data acquisition, classification of Signals, analog interfacing connecting signal to the board, analog input/output techniques, digital I/O, counters and timers DAQ Hardware configuration Introduction, Measurement and Automation Explorer, DAQ assistants, analysis assistants, interfacing instruments

units.title: GPIB and RS232
units.text: GPIB and RS232 Introduction, RS232 Vs. GPIB, handshaking, GPIB interfacing, RS232C/RS485 interfacing, standard commands for programmable instruments, VISA Standard bus architectures ISA, PCI, VME and PXI.

text_books: 1. Jovitha Jerome, Virtual instrumentation Using LabVIEW, 4th Edition, PHI Learning, 2010, ISBN: 978-8120340305. 2. Sanjay Gupta and Joseph John, Virtual Instrumentation Using Lab View, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, New Delhi, 2010, ISBN : 978-0070700284.
reference_books: 1. Lisa. K. Wills, LabVIEW for Everyone, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall of India, 2008, ISBN: 978- 0132681940. 2. Garry Johnson and Richard Jennings, LabVIEW Graphical Programming, 4th Edition, McGraw Hill Professional, 2006, ISBN No-978-1259005336.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Electronic systems, Introduction to Digital systems, Microprocessors and Microcontroller
objectives: The course is designed to introduce the students in depth with various sensors and transducers used in industrial situations. It also emphasizes the hardware and programming aspects of PLCs for industrial applications.

outcomes.text: Select and apply sensors and transducers for industrial applications
Analyze and compare the working principles, specifications, and performance of proximity sensors
Describe the architecture, components, and addressing modes of PLCs
Create PLC ladder logic programs for sequential control mechanisms
Design and implement PLC-based automation solutions

units.title: Sensors and Transducers
units.text: Sensors and Transducers Principles, Classification and applications. Transducer Selection Criteria for Mechatronics applications. Pressure Transducers Bellows, Diaphragm, Bourdon tubes, Pirani Gauge, Ionization Gauge, Piezoelectric transducer and Strain Gauge. Flow Transducers Orifice Plate, Pitot tube, Ventury tube, Rota meter, Ultrasonic Flow meter, Electromagnetic flow meter. Temperature Transducers RTD, Thermistor, Thermocouple, Pyrometers. Displacement/Position Transducers LVDT, Hall effect transducers, Optical encoders, Resonant sensor.

units.title: Proximity Sensors
units.text: Proximity Sensors Basic Principle, Construction, Working and applications of Inductive, Capacitive, Ultrasonic, Magnetic and Photoelectric proximity sensors. Modes of operation of Photoelectric proximity sensors. Performance comparison and Specifications of different Proximity sensors.

units.title: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)
units.text: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) Evolution of PLCs, Discrete State Control, Block Diagram of PLC, Classification of PLCs. Description of PLC components: Power Supply, Input and Output Modules, Discrete Input and Output Modules, Analog Input and output Modules, Programming Devices, CPU, I/O module specifications. Typical PLC specifications. Different Addressing modes.

units.title: PLC Programming
units.text: PLC Programming Memory Organization of PLC, Program Files, Data Files, Program Scan Cycle. Types of programming languages used in PLCs: Ladder logic, Functional block diagram, Sequential flow chart, Instruction List, Structured Text. Rules for ladder logic Programming. Relay Logic Instructions, Latching, Interlocking, Triggers, Logic gates programming in PLC. Timer Instructions: On Delay, Off Delay and Pulse Timers. Counter Instructions: Up counter and Down Counter. Data manipulation instructions, Mathematical instructions, Sequence and Shift register instructions. Analog Module programming.

units.title: Application Development
units.text: Application Development Interfacing of various inputs & outputs to PLC (Electromagnetic Control Relays, Contactors, Motor Starters, Manually operated switches, Mechanically operated switches, Proximity sensors), Interfacing Remote I/O s with PLC. Design of Tank level control System, Sequential switching of motors, Motor starters, Temperature/Pressure control, Conveyor belt control, Pneumatic Cylinder sequencing, Automatic Bottle filler. Industrial case studies.

text_books: 1. Curtis D. Johnson, Process control Instrumentation Technology, 8th illustrated Edition, Prentice Hall, 2013. 2. M.Mitra and S. Gupta, Programmable logic controllers and Industrial Automation: An Introduction, 2nd Edition, Penram International Publishing (India) Pvt. Ltd., 2017.
reference_books: 1. Petreuzeulla, Programmable Controllers, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2005. 2. D. Patranabis, Principal of Industrial Instrumentation, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill publication, 2010.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Fundamental Knowledge of Control Systems, Computer Programming, Calculus, Linear Algebra and Probability, Programming Knowledge and Statistics.
objectives: The primary objective of the course is to introduce students to the building blocks of Artificial Intelligence, fuzzy logic, and its techniques to distinguish from conventional techniques. The course also lays emphasis on the application of supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms for real-world systems.

outcomes.text: Apply basic principles of AI in problem solving, inference, perception, knowledge representation and learning
Understand and apply basic principles of artificial neural networks in real world problems
Interpret and apply Fuzzy Logic for various real world applications
Recognize the characteristics of machine learning that makes it useful to solve real-world problems
Apply the basic principles of Supervised and Unsupervised learning algorithms to solve real world applications

units.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
units.text: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Meaning and definition of AI, significance and role of AI, application of AI, history of AI. Search Techniques- Introduction to informed and uninformed search, State space search: Depth first search, Breadth first search, Heuristic search: Best first search, Intelligent Agent

units.title: Artificial Neural Network
units.text: Artificial Neural Network Basic concepts of neural network; Overview of learning rules and parameters, activation functions, single layer perceptron and multilayer perceptron, Multilayer feed forward network, Backpropagation networks: Architecture and algorithm.

units.title: Fuzzy Logic
units.text: Fuzzy Logic Concepts of uncertainty, properties and operations on classical sets and fuzzy sets, classical & fuzzy relations, Membership functions and its types, fuzzification, fuzzy rule-based systems, defuzzification, fuzzy propositions, fuzzy inference system, recent applications.

units.title: Introduction to machine learning
units.text: Introduction to machine learning Regression, Classification, Bias-Variance trade off, Linear Regression, Multivariate Regression, Hidden Markov models, Gaussian Processes, Bayesian decision theory. 5. Supervised and Unsupervised learning LMS, Logistic regression, Naïve Bayes, Support vector machines, Decision Trees (ID3 Algorithm). Unsupervised learning: Clustering criteria, K-means, Fuzzy C-means, Hierarchical clustering 6. Applications of Machine Learning in Robotics Developmental Robotics, Cognitive Robotics, Evolutionary Robotics

Mehryar Mohri, Afshin Rostamizadeh and Amet Talwalkar, Foundation of Machine Learning, MIT Press 2012. 3. Timothy Ross, Fuzzy Logic with Engineering Application, Wiley, 3rd Edition, 2011.
reference_books: 1. Christopher Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, Springer, 2011. 2. Simon Haykin, Neural Networks and Learning Machines, Pearson, 3rd Edition, 2010. 3. Ethem Alpaydin, Introduction to Machine Learning, 2nd Edition, MIT Press, 2010. 4. S. Rajasekaran, G.A. Vijayalakshmi Pai, Neural Networks, Fuzzy Logic and Genetic Algorithms, 3rd Edition, PHI, 2011. 5. K. Mehrotra, C.K. Mohan and Sanjay Ranka, Elements of Artificial Neural Networks, MIT Press, 1997. program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: This course is designed for the students to grasp the underlying mathematics and its application in modern control systems. The students are required to analyze practical control engineering problems using classical and modern methods. The course also emphasizes synthesizing solutions using scripting on a computational platform.

outcomes.text: Use the theoretical concepts in classical and modern control theory
Analyze the performance of a control methodology
Develop theoretical designs for controllers using modern methods
Analyze control designs for motion control
Synthesize the motion control and motion logic control solutions to practical problems

units.title: Classical Control Theory

units.title: Controller Design
units.text: Controller Design Open loop control, state feedback control, PID control in Laplace domain, gain and phase compensators

units.title: Introduction to Modern Control Theory

units.title: Discrete Time Systems
units.text: Discrete Time Systems Discrete time systems, discretized continuous systems, time domain analysis, Kalman filter

units.title: Performance Specifications
units.text: Performance Specifications Performance specifications, tracking and regulation, motion control with trapezoidal velocity profile

units.title: Introduction to Advanced Topics
units.text: Introduction to Advanced Topics Optimal Control, H∞ Control, Linear Matrix Inequalities, semidefinite programming

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: This course aims at introducing idea of discrete time signals, systems and their classification. An image is a discrete time signal, which is analyzed by certain algorithms for digital image processing, to develop a foundation that provides deep insights into this field. This fact is also emphasized in the course.

outcomes.text: Apply various transforms for Discrete Time signals
Apply spatial domain techniques for grey and color image enhancement
Synthesize various morphological operations and segmentation techniques for images
Analyze the important parameters and their impact on filtered signals
Synthesize digital filters for basic operations

units.title: Transforms for Discrete Time Signals

units.title: Introduction and Elements of Interactive Computer Graphics

Modeling using CAD, product life cycle and Computer-Aided Design (CAD)/ Computer- Aided Manufacturing (CAM), Concurrent engineering in product design and development, Collaborative Engineering, CAD System Architecture-Software and Hardware.

units.text: Techniques for Geometric Modeling Graphic standards, The parametric representation of geometry-Bezier curves, Cubic spline curve, B-Spline curve, parametric representation of line, circle, ellipse and parabola, Constructive solid geometry (CSG), Boundary representation (B-rep), Wire Frame modeling, Solid modeling, Surface modeling, feature based modeling, Parent child relationship.

Transformation, Manipulation and Data Storage 2D and 3D Transformations (Translation, Rotation, Scaling and Magnification), Concatenations, Matrix representation, Problems on Transformations. Object transformation, mirror transformation, Bill of Materials from attribute data, Engineering data management system, relational data base for design, object oriental database, Design Information Systems.

units.title: NC and CNC Technology
units.text: NC and CNC Technology Introduction, basic components of Numeric Control (NC) system, NC procedure, NC coordinate systems, NC motion control systems, Various actuation systems and feedback devices like encoder, tachogenerator, etc. Applications, Advantages and Disadvantages of NC machines. Constructional details of Computer Numeric Control (CNC) machines, computer-assisted numerical control programming, Manual part programming methods, Various G and M codes Flexible Manufacturing Systems (FMS), Automated Material Handling and Storage Systems like Robots, Automated Guided Vehicles (AGV) and Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems (AS/RS)

units.title: CNC Simulations
units.text: CNC Simulations Four-axis CNC simulator operation and programming, creating complex geometries, simulations on a software simulation platform

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
prerequisites: Manufacturing Processes, Probability and Statistics, Management Accounting for Engineers
objectives: The course is designed to introduce students to the concept of total quality management and technical skills required to lead for quality improvement. The course also elaborates tools and techniques for quality improvement.

outcomes.text: Apply various techniques of quality management for improving quality and productivity
Analyze data and interpret results using various total quality tools and statistical techniques
Identify the importance of teamwork, empowerment and motivation in quality management
Analyze the impact of application of TQM tools and techniques
Synthesize optimal techniques and tools for a given problem

units.title: Introduction to Total Quality in Organizations
units.text: Introduction to Total Quality in Organizations Importance of Quality. The concept of Quality. Quality in manufacturing. Quality in services. Principles of total quality. Comparison of total quality with traditional management practices. Total Quality and organizational models.

units.title: Approaches to Total Quality
units.text: Approaches to Total Quality Deming’s management philosophy, Deming’s 14 principles of management. The Juran philosophy. The Crosby philosophy. ISO 9000 standards: Structure, registration and perspectives. Quality awards. Six sigma: Concept, Principle, Methodology, Scope, Advantage and limitations.

text_books: 1. Dale Besterfield, Carol Besterfield-Michna, Glen Besterfield, Mary Besterfield-Sacre, Hemant Urdhwareshe, Rashmi Urdhwareshe, Total Quality Management, 5th Edition, Pearson, 2018. 2. James R. Evans, James W. Dean Jr, Total Quality: Management, Organization and Strategy, 4th Edition, Thomson, 2004.

objectives: The course emphasizes the importance and applicability of supervisory control with acquired data using industrial communication protocols. It introduces and reinforces the concept of a virtual instrument on a suitable computational platform using graphical programming. It also introduces students to the design of basic industrial control systems.

outcomes.text: Apply the fundamentals of Supervisory Control, Virtual Instrumentation and data Acquisition
Analyze the hardware-in-loop simulations
Synthesize a VI system to solve real time problems using data acquisition

units.title: Fundamentals of Virtual Instrumentation
units.text: Fundamentals of Virtual Instrumentation Historical perspective, advantages, blocks diagram and architecture of a virtual instrument, data-flow techniques, graphical programming in data flow, comparison with conventional programming Software Overview Lab VIEW, Graphical user interfaces - Controls and Indicators Data types - Data flow programming - Editing - Debugging and Running Virtual instrument - Graphical programming pallets - and their configuration VIs and sub-VIs Typical examples-VIs

units.title: Programming Structure

units.title: State Machines

units.title: Basics of Data Acquisition
units.text: Basics of Data Acquisition Introduction to data acquisition Classification of Signals, Analog Interfacing Connecting signal to board, Analog Input/output techniques digital I/O, counters and timers DAQ Hardware configuration Introduction, Measurement and Automation Explorer, DAQ Assistants, Analysis Assistants Interfacing Instruments

units.title: GPIB and RS232
units.text: GPIB and RS232 Introduction, RS232 Vs. GPIB, Handshaking, GPIB Interfacing, RS232C/RS485 Interfacing, Standard commands for Programmable Instruments, VISA Standard bus architectures ISA, PCI, VME and PXI

units.title: Advanced Topics in Lab View
units.text: Advanced Topics in Lab View Use of analysis tools and application of VI: Fourier transforms Power spectrum, Correlation methods, windowing & flittering Simulation of systems using VI Development of Control system, Image acquisition and processing, Motion control
