units.title: Construction practices
units.text: Construction practices Modern methods of construction of concrete, steel and composite bridges, their impact on analysis and design, construction stage analysis. Introduction to analysis and design of long span bridges: suspension and cable stayed bridges, balanced cantilever construction, segmental construction.

text_books: 1. N. Krishna Raju, Design of Bridges, 5th Edition, Oxford and IBH, 2019. 2. Victor D. J, Essentials of Bridge Engineering, 6th Edition Oxford, 2019. 3. T.R Jagdeesh & M.A Jayaram, Design of Bridge Structures, 3rd Edition, Prentice Hall India Private Ltd., 2020.
reference_books: 1. Ponnuswamy S, Bridge Engineering, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw-Hill Education, 2017. 2. Raina V.K, Raina’s Concrete Bridge Practice Construction, Maintenance and Rehabilitation, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill, 2019. 3. Tomlinson M. J., Foundation Design and Construction, 7th Edition, Pearson, 2017.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course aims to bring the students to such a level so as to enable them to take the appropriate decision in respect of choice of prestressed section over R. C. C. as a civil engineer. Also to make the candidate to understand the analysis of Prestressed Concrete sections and losses in prestress. This course focuses to make the candidate able to understand and implement the guidelines of Indian Standard code for analysis and design sections using limit state philosophy.

outcomes.text: Understand the concept of pre-stressing its casting techniques and applications, behaviour of the pre-stressed structures vis-à-vis that of the RCC structure
Apply the concept to take the decision with respect to the choice of pre-stressed section over RCC
Analyse the various pre-stressed components of the structure and design the same using relevant IS Code

units.title: Introduction, Prestressing Systems and Material Properties
units.text: Introduction, Prestressing Systems and Material Properties Basic concept, early attempts of prestressing, brief history, development of building materials. Definitions, advantages of prestressing, limitations of prestressing, types of prestressing, source of prestressing force. External or internal prestressing, pre- tensioning or post-tensioning, linear or circular prestressing, full, limited or partial prestressing, uniaxial, biaxial or multiaxial prestressing. Prestressing systems and devices. Constituents of concrete and hardened concrete, prestressing steel, codal provisions.

units.title: Losses in Prestressed Concrete Section
units.text: Losses in Prestressed Concrete Section Notations, Losses in prestress, elastic shortening, pre-tensioned and post-tensioned axial and flexural members. Friction loss, anchorage slip loss, force variation diagram. Losses due to creep and shrinkage of concrete, relaxation of steel, total time-dependent loss

units.title: Analysis of Members
units.text: Analysis of Members Analysis of members under axial load and flexure, analysis at service loads, stress concept, force concept, load balancing concept. Cracking moment, kern point, pressure line. Ultimate Strength, analysis of rectangular sections, flanged sections, partially prestressed sections, un-bonded post-tensioned beams.

units.title: Design of Members
units.text: Design of Members Design of members for axial tension and flexure, design of prestressing force. Final design, final design for Type – I and Type – II members. Choice of sections, determination of limiting zone, post-tensioning in stages, Magnel’s graphical method, detailing requirements for flexure, Shear and torsion.

units.title: Analysis and Design for Shear and Torsion
units.text: Analysis and Design for Shear and Torsion Limit state of collapse for shear, maximum permissible shear stress, design of transverse reinforcement, detailing requirement for shear, general comments, design steps, design of stirrups for flange. Limit state of collapse for torsion, design of longitudinal reinforcement, design of transverse reinforcement, detailing requirement for shear, general comments, design steps.

units.title: Calculations of Deflection and Crack Width
units.text: Calculations of Deflection and Crack Width Calculation of deflection, deflection due to gravity load, deflection due to prestressing force, total deflection, limits of deflection, determination of moment of inertia, limits of span-to-effective depth ratio, calculation of crack width, limits of crack width.

units.title: Transmission of Prestress
units.text: Transmission of Prestress Introduction, Pre-tensioned members, transmission length, development length, end zone reinforcement, post-tensioned members, end zone reinforcement, bearing plate.

units.title: Continuous Beams
units.text: Continuous Beams Continuous Beams, introduction, analysis, incorporation of moment due to reactions, pressure line due to prestressing force, concordant cable profile, cable profiles, partially continuous beams, analysis at ultimate limit state, moment redistribution

units.title: Special Topics
units.text: Special Topics Circular prestressing, introduction, general analysis and design, prestressed concrete pipes, liquid storage tanks, ring beams

text_books: 1. N. Krishna Raju, Prestressed Concrete, 6th Edition, McGraw Hill, New York, 2018. 2. T. Y. Lin, N.H. Burns, Design of Prestressed Concrete Structures, 3rd Edition, John Willey, New York, 2010.
reference_books: 1. N. Rajgopalan, Prestressed Concrete, 3rd Edition, Narosa Publishing House, 2010. 2. Dayaratnam, P, Prestressed Concrete Structures, 6th Edition, Oxford and IBH, 2017. 3. Sinha, N.C., S.K. Roy, Fundamentals of Prestressed Concrete, 3rd Edition, S.C. Chand and Company, 2011. 4. S. Ramamurtham, Prestressed Concrete, 5th Edition, Dhanpat Rai and Son's, 2016. 5. Relevant latest IS codes (IS:1343)

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course focusses on the basics of structural dynamics. It also focusses on the evaluation of dynamic properties of structures and their response subjected to dynamic loads and earthquake loads as per the requirements of Indian standard codal provisions

outcomes.text: Determine the natural properties of SDOF and MDOF Systems
Evaluate the response of SDOF and MDOF systems
Analyze the structure using IS code method and response spectrum

units.title: Single Degree of Freedom (SDOF) Systems
units.text: Single Degree of Freedom (SDOF) Systems Definitions of basic problems in dynamics, static v/s dynamic loads, different types of dynamic loads, un-damped vibration of SDOF system, natural frequency and periods of vibration, damping in structure. Response to periodic loads, response to general dynamic load, response of structure subject to ground motion, use of Fourier series for periodic forces.

units.title: Multiple Degree of Freedom (MDOF) Systems
units.text: Multiple Degree of Freedom (MDOF) Systems Direct determination of frequencies and mode shapes, orthogonality principle, approximate methods for determination of frequencies and mode shapes. Forced vibration of MDOF system, modal analysis, applications to multistoried rigid frames subject to lateral dynamic loads including ground motion

units.title: Seismological Background
units.text: Seismological Background Seismicity of a region, earthquake faults and waves, structure of earth, plate tectonics, elastic-rebound theory of earthquake, intensity and magnitude of earthquake, measurement of ground motion, seismogram, earthquake frequency, local site effects, seismotectonics and Seismicity of India.

units.title: Characterization of Ground Motion
units.text: Characterization of Ground Motion Earthquake response spectra, factors influencing response spectra, design response spectra for elastic systems, peak ground acceleration, response spectrum shapes, deformation, pseudo-velocity, pseudo-acceleration response spectra. peak structural response from the response spectrum, response spectrum characteristics, construction site specific response spectra.

units.title: Deterministic Earthquake Response
units.text: Deterministic Earthquake Response Types of earthquake excitation, lumped SDOF elastic systems. translational excitation, lumped MDOF elastic systems, translational excitation, time history analysis, multistoried buildings with symmetric plans, multi storied buildings with un-symmetric plans, torsional response of symmetric plan building, distributed - parameter elastic systems, translational excitation, combining maximum modal responses using mean square response of a single mode, SRSS and CQC combination of modal responses.

units.title: IS Code Method of Seismic Analysis
units.text: IS Code Method of Seismic Analysis Seismic co-efficient method and its limitation, response spectrum method, IS 1893-part 1 - 2016 provisions for seismic analysis of buildings

units.title: Introduction to Ductile Detailing of Structures
units.text: Introduction to Ductile Detailing of Structures Provisions of IS 13920: 2016 for ductile detailing of structures

text_books: 1. A. K. Jain, Dynamics of Structures with Matlab Applications, 1st Edition, Pearson Education India, 2016.
reference_books: 1. Roy R. Craig & Andrew J. Kurdila, Fundamentals of Structural Dynamics, 2nd Edition, John Wiley & Sons, 2011 (Classic Book). 2. Clough & Penzein, Dynamics of Structures, 2nd Edition, CBS, 2015. 3. Anil K. Chopra, Dynamics of Structures, 5th Edition, Pearson Education, 2020. 4. IS 1893 (Part 1): 2016, BIS Publications. 5. IS 13920: 2006, BIS Publications

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course focusses on advance geotechnical analysis including evaluation of stability of slopes, analyses of earth retaining structures and estimation of stresses in soil. The course also focuses on estimation of field bearing capacity of footing and design of group piles based on Indian Standards.

outcomes.text: Estimate stresses in soil using appropriate theories
Distinguish between types of slope failures, and analyze the stability of earth slopes
Analyse of earth retaining structures like gravity retaining walls
Estimation of field bearing capacity and settlement of shallow and pile foundations

units.title: Stress Distribution in Soils
units.text: Stress Distribution in Soils Introduction, Boussinesq’s theory, vertical stress distribution diagrams, construction of isobars, Pressure bulbs, Influence coefficients, vertical stresses beneath loaded areas - point load, line load, uniformly loaded rectangular and circular areas, Newmark’s influence chart, Westergaard’s analysis

units.title: Stability of Slopes
units.text: Stability of Slopes Introduction, types of slope failure, different factors of safety, analysis of infinite slopes, Stability of finite slopes- plane failure, Swedish circle method, friction circle method, stability numbers and charts

units.title: Field Estimation of Bearing Capacity for Footing
units.text: Field Estimation of Bearing Capacity for Footing Plate load test in detail with reference to IS: 1888 and its applications and estimation of settlements, bearing capacity based on standard penetration tests

units.title: Analysis of Group of Pile Foundations
units.text: Analysis of Group of Pile Foundations Pile load test as per IS: 2911 specifications, negative skin friction, pile groups, installation of pile, ultimate capacity of groups, settlement of pile groups in sand and in clays as per IS 2911 and critical depth method, Introduction to piled raft foundation, NDT for piles.

units.title: Earth Pressure on Retaining Structures
units.text: Earth Pressure on Retaining Structures Analysis of gravity retaining wall

units.title: Braced Cuts
units.text: Braced Cuts Lateral earth pressure distribution, apparent pressure diagrams, estimation of strut forces and loads in deep cuts in stiff clay, sand, saturated clay. Bjerrum and Eide method of analysis, use of touch piles, secant piles, anchors for shoring system

text_books: 1. Dr. Alam Singh, Soil Engineering in Theory and Practice, Vol-I, 4th Edition, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd., 2018. 2. VNS Murthy, Text Book of Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd., 2018.
reference_books: 1. Hans Winterkorn and Hsai-Yang Fang, Foundation Engineering Handbook, Publisher in India- Galgotia Booksource, 1986 (Classic Book). 2. B. M. Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering, 7th Edition, Cengage Learning, 2011. 3. Relevant IS Codes, BIS Publications

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course will allow students to evaluate the importance of geology in rock mechanics practice, classify rocks and predict their mechanical behaviour and integrate laboratory and field techniques to determine stress-strain and strength of rocks to assess rock failure and its importance in civil engineering.

outcomes.text: Assess importance of geology in rock mechanics practice
Classify rocks based on various classification methods and predict their mechanical behavior
Interpret laboratory and field techniques to determine stress –strain, modulus and strength behaviour of rocks

units.title: Elements of Structural Geology
units.text: Elements of Structural Geology Elements of Structural geology, advanced concepts of plate tectonic theory, geological site investigations in rocks and engineering characteristics of rock masses, mapping basics; Introduction to MOVE, FieldClino MOVE and FieldMOVE softwares (Petex).

units.title: Engineering Classification of Rocks and Rock Masses
units.text: Engineering Classification of Rocks and Rock Masses Classification of intact rocks, rock mass classifications {rock quality designation, rock structural rating, geomechanics classification (RMR)}, strength and modulus from classifications, classification based on strength and modulus, Geoengineering, classification, Deere and Miller’s Engineering classification.

In-situ stress measurement in Rocks and Rock testing a) In-situ stress measurement in rocks Flat Jack method, Bore-hole deformation method, Core discing method, Hydraulic Fracturing method. b) Rock testing 1. Laboratory testing: Compression test, Effect of L/D ratio, Determination of Modulus of Elasticity and Poisson's Ratio, Direct and Indirect (Brazilian) Tensile tests, Shear tests (including hollow cylinder test). 2. In-situ testing: Plate load test, Block shear test, Cable Jacking test, Pressuremeter test.

units.title: Strength, Modulus and Stress-Strain Responses of Rocks
units.text: Strength, Modulus and Stress-Strain Responses of Rocks Factors influencing rock responses, strength criteria for isotropic intact rocks, modulus of isotropic intact rocks with confining pressure, uni-axial compressive strength of intact anisotropic rocks, strength due to induced anisotropy in rocks, compressive strength and modulus from SPT, stress-strain models (constitutive models, elastic stress-strain model, elasto-plastic stress-strain model, equivalent material concept), influence of intermediate principal stress

units.title: Bearing Capacity of Rocks
units.text: Bearing Capacity of Rocks Estimation of bearing capacity (foundation on intact rock, heavily fractured rock, UBC with Hoek-Brown criterion, foundation on slope), stress distribution in rocks, factor of safety, strengthening measures (concrete shear keys, bored concrete piles, tensioned cable anchors, concrete block at toe), settlement in rocks (from joint factor, for horizontal joints, from field tests)

units.title: Stability of Rock Slopes
units.text: Stability of Rock Slopes Modes of failure, rotational failure, plane failure, wedge method of analysis, buckling failure, toppling failure, improvement of slope stability and protection

units.title: Rock Bolting and Grouting
units.text: Rock Bolting and Grouting Opening in Rocks, Rock Bolting and Grouting Introduction to theory of elasticity, lines and unlined tunnels, pressure tunnels and tunnels for other purposes. Grouting in rocks, objectives, contact grouting, consolidation grouting, process of grouting, grout requirement, types of grout, stage grouting, grout curtain. Rock bolts, rock bolt types and applications, theory of rock bolting, rock anchors, modes of failure, uplift capacity

text_books: 1. J. C. Jaeger and N. G. W. Cook, Fundamentals of Rock Mechanics, Oxford Press, 2007. 2. T. Ramamurthy (Editor), Engineering in Rocks, Prentice Hall. 2007
reference_books: 1. K. G. Stagg and O. C. Zienkiewicz, Rock Mechanics in Engineering Practice, John Willey & Sons, 1968 (Classic Book). 2. Alfred Jumikis, Rock Mechanics-Vol. I & II, Trans Tech Publication, 1979 (Classic Book).

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The objective of this course is to provide the knowledge about the methods of design for flexible and rigid highway and airport pavements. The course aims to give the knowledge of pavement condition, low-cost roads, concrete roads and plant and machinery needed for construction of pavements.

outcomes.text: Discuss different pavement structures and their functions
Estimate stresses for and design the different pavement structures
Identify methodology for evaluation and strengthening of pavements
Appraise low-cost roads, concrete roads, road making machinery

units.title: Pavement Structure and Functional Attributes
units.text: Pavement Structure and Functional Attributes Factor affecting pavement design, types of wheel loads for highways and airports, development of design method for highway and airport pavements.
Stresses in Flexible Pavements 1-layer, 2-layer, 3-layers theories, EWLF, ESWL Stresses in Rigid pavement: load and temperature stresses, combined stresses.

units.title: Flexible Pavement Design
units.text: Flexible Pavement Design Airport pavement: Corps of Engineer’s method, FAA method, CDOT method, Asphalt institute method. Highway Pavement: Empirical methods using no soil strength criteria, empirical method based on soil strength criteria: CBR method as specified by IRC, Road note 29 methods, AASHTO method, Asphalt institute method. Fatigue and rutting as a failure criterion.

units.title: Rigid Pavement Design
units.text: Rigid Pavement Design Airport pavements: PCA methods, corps of Engineer’s method, FAA method. Joints and reinforcement requirement. Highway pavement: Current British procedure, IRC method.

units.title: Evaluation and Strengthening
units.text: Evaluation and Strengthening Flexible and rigid pavement distresses, condition and evaluation surveys, present serviceability index, roughness measurement, Benkaleman beam deflections, design of overlays, skid resistance and measurement.

units.title: Concrete Road Construction
units.text: Concrete Road Construction Mix design, concrete strength, size of aggregates, gradation, and workability, preparation of base form work, placing of reinforcement, compaction, and finishing, curing, joints.

units.title: Low-Cost Roads (rural areas)
units.text: Low-Cost Roads (rural areas) Classification of low-cost roads, construction of low-cost roads, stabilization of subgrade, base and its advantages, construction of granular base courses, macadam surface, macadam bases, low-cost materials and methods used for highway construction, suitability of different types of roads under different situation. Soils.

units.title: Road Making Machinery
units.text: Road Making Machinery Role of labour versus machinery, in road construction, earth work machinery, rock excavation machinery, aggregate transportation and watering equipment, wet mix WMM Plant, Asphalt plant, (computerized), drum mix, Continuous batch mix, compaction equipment, bituminous equipment, storage, heating and spraying equipment, hot mix plants, cold mix plants, paver, finisher, concrete road making machinery, equipment usage rates, factors affecting usage rate.

text_books: 1. L. R. Kadiyali and Dr. N. B. Lal, Principles and Practices of Highway Engineering, Khanna Publication, New Delhi, 2017.
reference_books: 1. Khanna & Justo, Highway Engineering, 10th Edition, New Chand & Brothers, Roorkee, 2018. 2. Yoder, E. J., Principles of Pavement Design, 2nd Edition, John Wiley & Sons, Inc., New York, 1975 (Classic Book).

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course covers identification, characterization, quantification, treatment and management of wastewater, solid waste, emission and noise from the industry.

outcomes.text: Discuss industrial waste treatment strategy based on waste type
Evaluate type and quantity of industrial waste
Design of various units of Effluent Treatment Plant

units.title: Industrial Wastewater - Introduction
units.text: Industrial Wastewater - Introduction Wastewater streams, their characteristics, generation and recycling of waste water in manufacturing processes in engineering and non-engineering industry

units.title: Industrial Wastewater Treatment and Management
units.text: Industrial Wastewater Treatment and Management Estimation of wastewater, Industry specific physio-chemical and biological treatment requirements, alternatives and their evaluation with respect to treatment. Neutralization, equalization, Engineering precipitation and solidification. Economic feasibility of joint treatment of raw industrial effluent with municipal sewage. Need for assessment and design of common effluent treatment plant for industrial estates. Standards for disposal of treated industrial wastewaters into water bodies, municipal sewer and land, Concept of Integrated wastewater treatment facilities. Case Studies

units.title: Industrial Solid Waste Treatment and Management techniques
units.text: Industrial Solid Waste Treatment and Management techniques Industrial waste generation and their characteristics, variation in its Quality and quantity, Collection, Segregation, Storage, Treatment Methodology and Standards for Disposal of industrial solid wastes. Methods of waste reduction, process modification, volume and strength reduction, segregation, reuse, recycle, material conservation, good housekeeping etc. Case Studies

units.title: Industrial Emission Management
units.text: Industrial Emission Management Introduction - types of air emission on basis of types of industry, emission monitoring and sampling, ambient air quality standards, emission control devices. Case Studies

text_books: 1. Rose Marie O. Mendoza, Industrial Waste Management, 1st Edition, Arcler Education Inc. 2018. 2. Patwardhan A. D., Industrial Waste Water Treatment, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall of India, 2020.
reference_books: 1. Metcalf & Eddy, George Tchobanoglous, Franklin Burton, H. David Stensel, Wastewater Engineering: Treatment and Reuse, 4th Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2017. (Classic Book) 2. Soli J. Arceivala, Asolekar S.R., Waste Water Treatment for Pollution Control and Reuse, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Professional, 2017. (Classic Book)

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
prerequisites: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics, Hydraulics and Fluid Machinery
objectives: This course focusses on the analysis and design of hydraulic structures like dams, spillways and energy dissipaters. This course provides demonstration and understanding of advanced fluid mechanics and geotechnical engineering principles.

outcomes.text: Estimate various forces on hydraulic structures
Design different dam structures, spillways and energy dissipaters
Analyse small bridges, surplus weirs, causeways and culverts

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Introduction, classification, comparative study of various types of dams, selection of site of dam, preliminary and final investigations of dam sites, fixation of storage capacity, reservoir losses, sedimentation in reservoirs and density currents.

units.title: Gravity Dams
units.text: Gravity Dams Criteria for selection of dam site, construction material, forces acting on gravity dam, modes of failure, stability analysis, safety criteria, methods of design, stress analysis and stress contours, galleries, instrumentation, joints, keys, water seals, temperature control in concrete dams, foundation treatment.

units.title: Arch and Buttress Dams
units.text: Arch and Buttress Dams Types of arch dams, forces on an arch dam, design. Types of buttress dams.

units.title: Earth and Rockfill Dams
units.text: Earth and Rockfill Dams Advantages and limitations, foundation of earth dams, causes and failures of earth dams, design criteria, design considerations in earthquake regions, seepage line for different conditions, filters, upstream blankets, stability analysis, Swedish circle method with pore pressure, details of construction and maintenance, types of rockfill dams, stability analysis, advantages.

units.title: Spillways and Flood Control Works
units.text: Spillways and Flood Control Works Factors affecting design of spillway, types of spillways, design principles of ogee spillway, chute spillway, siphon spillway and shaft spillway. Design of bucket type energy dissipater and stilling basin, flood mitigation reservoirs. Crest gates, types, advantages, choice, design of radial gate. Outlet works through dams, intake structures.

units.title: Miscellaneous Hydraulic Structures
units.text: Miscellaneous Hydraulic Structures Analysis of small bridges and culverts, data collection, high flood discharge, linear waterway calculation, scour depth, causeways and culverts

text_books: 1. Modi P.N., Irrigation Water Resources and Water Power Engineering, 11th Edition, Standard Book House, 2019.
reference_books: 1. Garg S.K., Irrigation Engineering and Hydraulic Structures, 38th Edition, Khanna Publishers, 2023. 2. Punmia B.C., Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics, 22nd Edition, Laxmi Publications, 2019.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
prerequisites: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics; Hydraulics and Fluid Machinery
objectives: This course focuses on various analyse & design procedures and optimization techniques for Water distribution systems (WDS). It also focuses on pumps, valves in WDS.

outcomes.text: Analyse and design WDS with different methods
Demonstrate pump, reservoir & valve behavior and rising main design in WDS
Optimize WDS with various methods

units.title: General Hydraulic Principles
units.text: General Hydraulic Principles Head loss formulae- Darcy- Waisbach formula, Hazen – Williams formula, Modified Hazen- Williams formula, Series and Parallel connection of Pipes, Equivalent Pipes, Analysis of branched Water Distribution Networks.

units.title: Analysis of WDS
units.text: Analysis of WDS Analysis of flow in looped networks using Hardy Cross, Newton-Raphson and Linear Theory method

units.title: Reservoirs, Pumps and Valves
units.text: Reservoirs, Pumps and Valves Check valve, flow control valve and pressure reduces valve in Water distribution systems. Flow dependent analysis of multi-reservoir systems, Introduction to head-dependent analysis. Rising main design.

units.title: Node Flow Analysis of Water Distribution Networks
units.text: Node Flow Analysis of Water Distribution Networks Node head – discharge relationships, Direct and Indirect methods, Application of NFA technique to serial networks.

units.title: Design of Water Distribution Networks
units.text: Design of Water Distribution Networks Critical path method, Formulation of optimization model, Application of Cost- head loss ratio method and linear programming technique to optimal design of branched networks.

text_books: 1. Bhave, P.R. and Gupta R., Analysis of water distribution Networks, 1st Edition, Narosa Publishing Co, New Delhi, 2019. 2. Bhave P.R., Optimal Design of Water Distribution Networks, 1st Edition, Narosa Publishing Co, New Delhi, 2003. (Classic Book)
reference_books: 1. Manual on Water Supply and Treatment, CPHEEO, Ministry of Urban Development.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The objective of this course is to expose the students to various types of contracts and practices including international contracts, legal aspects of contracts, tendering and special contracts. The course also provides information about the arbitration and other alternate dispute resolution methods.

outcomes.text: Explain different types of tenders and contracts in construction
Describe various mechanisms of alternative dispute resolution including arbitration
Summarize various laws related to construction

units.title: Construction Contracts
units.text: Construction Contracts Indian Contracts Act, elements of contracts, types of contracts, features, suitability, design of contract documents, international contract document, standard contract document, Torts, FIDIC forms of contract

units.title: Tenders
units.text: Tenders Prequalification, bidding, accepting, evaluation of tender from technical, contractual and commercial perspective, contract formation and interpretation, potential contractual problems, World Bank procedures and guidelines

units.title: Claims and Claims Management
units.text: Claims and Claims Management Claims, common claims in construction, claims from contractor and from employer, Causes of disputes and importance of role of various stakeholders in prevention of disputes, Alternate Dispute Resolution methods- mediation, conciliation, negotiation and Dispute Resolution Boards.

units.title: Arbitration
units.text: Arbitration Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996, Comparison of actions and laws, agreements, subject matter, violations, appointment of arbitrators, conditions of arbitration, powers and duties of arbitrator, rules of evidence, enforcement of award, costs

units.title: Legal requirements
units.text: Legal requirements Insurance in construction, laws governing sale, purchase and use of urban and rural land, and revenue codes, custom duties and their influence on construction costs, legal requirements for planning, Property Law, Agency Law, Local Government Laws for approval, statutory regulations

Injunctions and Bailment a) Injunctions- Types, temporary, perpetual, mandatory. b) Indemnity & Guarantee- difference between the two; Contracts of Guarantee & Indemnity. Consideration for Guarantee, Surety’s liability, discharge of surety. Bailment- Nature of transaction, delivery of bailee.

text_books: 1. Patil. B. S. & Woodhouse S.P., Building and Engineering Contracts, 7th Edition, CRC Press, 2019.
reference_books: 1. Julian Bailey, Construction Law, 2nd Edition, 3 Vol., Taylor and Francis, 2021. 2. Indian Contracts Act, 1872.

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course covers the approach and methodology for Environmental Impact Assessment and developing the Environmental Management Plan. It also covers the Environmental Auditing of various projects.

outcomes.text: Discuss Environmental Impact Assessment and process
Draft EIA documentation
Develop Environmental Auditing methodology

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Definitions and concepts, rationale and historical development of EIA, Significance of EIA, Role of EIA in planning & decision making process, objectives of EIA. EIA for Civil Engineers.

units.title: Environmental Assessment Process
units.text: Environmental Assessment Process Assessment methodology, Socioeconomic impact assessment, Air quality impact analysis, Noise impact analysis, Energy impact analysis, Water quality impact analysis, Vegetation & wild life impact analysis, Cumulative impact assessment, Ecological impact assessment, Risk assessment.

units.title: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)
units.text: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Basic concept behind Environmental Impact Statement (EIS), Stages in EIS production: Screening, scoping, prediction, evaluation, reducing impact, monitoring, conclusions, typical EIS outline.

units.title: EIA Documentation and Case Studies
units.text: EIA Documentation and Case Studies Preparation of Rapid/Baseline and Comprehensive EIA report for any five projects of different sectors of construction industry.

units.title: Environmental Auditing
units.text: Environmental Auditing Definition, aims and objectives, audit principles, incentives to undertake audit, partial environmental audits, stages of environmental audits, scope of audit, provisions of various environmental acts in India

text_books: 1. Ramandran S., Environmental Impact Assessment, 1st Edition, Airwalk Publications, 2019. 2. Raman N. S. and Rao Y.R., Environmental Impact Assessment, 1st Edition, Laxmi Publications Pvt Ltd., 2018.
reference_books: 1. Kumar and Hosetti B.B., Environmental Impact Assessment and Management, Daya Publishing House, 2024. 2. Barthwal R. R., Environmental Impact Assessment, 2nd Edition, New Age International Publisher, 2012. (Classic Book)

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The objective of this course is to understand the quality control aspects in planning, systems, management and assurance. The course also focusses on evaluating the quality in construction and techniques for quality improvement.

outcomes.text: Describe the quality control aspects in planning, systems, management, assurance
Evaluate quality assurance in construction
Elucidate the quality improvement techniques in construction

units.title: Quality Management
units.text: Quality Management Introduction, definitions and objectives, factors influencing construction quality, responsibilities and authority, quality plan, quality management guidelines, quality circles

units.title: Quality Systems
units.text: Quality Systems Introduction, quality system standard, ISO 9000 family of standards, requirements, preparing quality system documents, quality related training, implementing a quality system, Third party certification

units.title: Quality Planning
units.text: Quality Planning Quality policy, objectives and methods in construction industry, consumer’s satisfaction, Ergonomics, time of completion, statistical tolerance, Taguchi’s concept of quality, codes and standards, documents, contract and construction programming, inspection procedures, processes and products, total QA / QC program and cost implication, Ishikawa fishbone diagram, source event diagram.

units.title: Quality Control and Assurance
units.text: Quality Control and Assurance Objectives, regularity agent, owner, design, contract and construction oriented objectives, methods, techniques and needs of QA/QC, different aspects of quality, appraisals, factors influencing construction quality, critical, major failure aspects and failure mode analysis, stability methods and tools, optimum design, reliability testing, reliability coefficient and reliability prediction, cost of quality

units.title: Quality Improvement Techniques
units.text: Quality Improvement Techniques Selection of new materials, influence of drawings, detailing, specification, standardization, bid preparation, construction activity, safety, social and environmental factors, natural causes and speed of construction on quality of delivery. Life cycle costing.

text_books: 1. James, J. O’ Brian, Construction Inspection Handbook – Total Quality Management, Van Nostrand, 2012. (Classic Book)
reference_books: 1. John L. Ashford, The Management of Quality in Construction, 2nd Edition, E & F. N. Spon, 2020. 2. Juran Frank, J. M. and Gryna, F. M., Quality Planning and Analysis, 5th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2001. (Classic Book)

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: This course covers groundwater hydrology and well hydraulics for understanding the groundwater processes. It also focuses on groundwater modelling for flow and contaminant transport.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the occurrence, distribution and characteristics of sub-surface water
Analyse groundwater flow-transport phenomenon for groundwater modelling
Appraise remedial measures for groundwater contamination

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction General water balance, regional groundwater balance, distribution of sub- surface water, different types of aquifers, occurrence of groundwater in hydrogeologic formations, structures and types of wells, components of groundwater studies

units.title: Aquifer Characteristics
units.text: Aquifer Characteristics Darcy’s law, determination of in situ hydraulic conductivity, flow through fractured medium. Governing equations of groundwater flow in aquifers, consideration of various recharge and discharge terms, Dupuit’s theory of free surface flow

units.title: Groundwater Flow Modelling

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The objective of this course is to understand the concepts in economics and finance in construction industry, analyze investment alternatives, manage funds for projects and the fundamentals of accounting.

outcomes.text: Interpret financial statements
Assess the investment alternatives
Summarize funds allocation and its management for construction projects

units.title: Overview of Finance Management
units.text: Overview of Finance Management Overview, finance functions, relevance of finance management in construction industry.

units.title: Financial Statements and Analysis
units.text: Financial Statements and Analysis Necessity of preparing financial statements, Income statement and Balance Sheet structure, terminologies associated, concept of depreciation, financial ratios and analysis, construction accounting.

units.title: Time Value of Money
units.text: Time Value of Money Principle of equivalence, Cash Flow diagram – Nominal and effective interest- continuous interest. Compounding and discounting concepts, future value, present value, annuity, perpetuity.

units.title: Comparing Alternative Proposals
units.text: Comparing Alternative Proposals Capital budgeting principles and process, discounting and non-discounting techniques for evaluation and comparison of proposals, payback period, ARR, NPV, IRR, Replacement analysis, IROR, benefit-cost analysis, break even analysis.

units.title: Working Capital Management
units.text: Working Capital Management Concept of working capital, factors affecting working capital, working capital cycle and calculating working capital cycle, calculation of working capital, Sources of working capital.

units.title: Funds Management
units.text: Funds Management Project Financing principles, balance sheet and off balance sheet finance, working out project cash flows, sources of long term finance, project appraisal.

reference_books: 1. Collier C. and Gola C., Engineering Economics & Cost Analysis, 3rd Edition, Addison Wesley Education Publishers, 1998. (Classic Book)

program: B Tech (Civil Engineering)
objectives: The objective of this course is to illustrate the various types of harbors, their components and the impact of tides, and waves on harbor design. It also covers the importance of soil survey procedure involving various dredging equipment, marine structures, and marine surveys.

outcomes.text: Illustrate the different types of harbors and their components
Explain the impact of tides and waves on harbor design
Distinguish between the different types of breakwaters, docks, and berthing structures
Describe the different dredging equipment, marine structures, and marine surveys

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Factors affecting modes of transportation, advantages and disadvantages of water transportation, important terminologies in harbours and ports, difference between harbour and port, classification of harbours, size of harbour, harbour entrances and turning basins

units.title: Impact of Tides, Waves, and Wind on Design of Harbour
units.text: Impact of Tides, Waves, and Wind on Design of Harbour Introduction to tides and waves, types of tides, basic definitions, types of beaches, littoral drift, and its prevention, wind and waves, height of waves, wave action, wave differentiation, estimation of static and dynamic wave pressures on inside and outside of vertical wall, breaking wave action, wave action on piles and estimation of drag and inertial force on piles, wave reflection, Windrose diagram, Beufort’s scale

units.title: Breakwaters
units.text: Breakwaters Introduction, classification of breakwaters – upright, mound with superstructure, heap, or mound breakwater

units.title: Docks
units.text: Docks Introduction to docks, different shapes of docks, repairs dock and its types, dock entrances and entrance locks, types of lock gates, forces acting on lock gates, caissons for dock entrances, turning basins, design of entrance channels

units.title: Berthing Structures
units.text: Berthing Structures Forces acting on quay walls, design of quay walls, construction of quay walls, dwarf quay wall, Necessity of wharf, open type wharves, Necessity and their functions, Types of piers.

units.title: Dredging
units.text: Dredging Necessity, disposal of the dredged material, types of dredging devices and their operations

units.title: Marine Structures
units.text: Marine Structures Basic terms, navigational signals, types of signals, beacon lights, light house and its construction, light ships, buoys and its types, transit shades and warehouses

units.title: Marine Surveys
units.text: Marine Surveys Necessity, types- hydrographic and topographic, soil investigations, hydraulic models

text_books: 1. R. Srinivasan, Harbour, Dock and Tunnel Engineering, 29th Edition, Charotar Publishing House Pvt. Ltd., 2018.
reference_books: 1. Hasmukh Oza and Gautam Oza, Principles and Practices of Highway Engineering, 8th Edition(reprint), Charotar Publishing House Pvt. Ltd., 2023. 2. S. P. Bindra, Harbour, Dock and Tunnel Engineering, Dhanpat Rai Publications, 2015. (Classic Book)

Analyze computations in deep neural networks.
Implement deep neural networks models for different applications using convolutional neural networks.

units.title: Recurrent Neural Networks

units.title: Applications of Deep Learning

objectives: This course focuses on the fundamentals of neural networks along with a practical perspective of advanced topics such as convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and long short-term memory with their real-world applications.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamentals of deep learning.
Apply optimization and regularization for tuning the parameters of deep neural networks.

Apply recurrent neural networks architectures for various applications.

program: B Tech/MBA Tech Artificial Intelligence, Computer Engineering, Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering) B Tech (AI and DS and CSBS)
objectives: This course introduces concepts in cryptography and computer security and discusses both their theoretical foundations and practical applications. It also provides fundamental knowledge on various aspects of network and system Security

outcomes.text: Explain and analyze symmetric key encryption and decryption
Use asymmetric key cryptography for data encryption
Describe various techniques of network security

units.title: Network Security

reference_books: 1. Wade Trappe and Lawrence C Washington, Introduction to Cryptography with Coding Theory, 3rd Edition, Pearson Education, 2020. 2. Wanbo Mao, Modern Cryptography: Theory and Practice, 4th Edition, Pearson Education, 2011.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering, AI and ML, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Engineering, CSE (DS)) MBA Tech (Artificial Intelligence & Computer Engineering)
objectives: The course aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) by covering its foundational concepts and advanced applications. Students will gain insight into the historical development and evolution of RPA, along with a deep appreciation for the benefits and challenges of its implementation. By delving into RPA tools and their features, students will learn to harness workflow automation, create apps, grasp the distinctions between attended and unattended bots, and comprehend the symbiotic relationship between RPA and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

outcomes.text: Demonstrate understanding of fundamental RPA concepts, historical evolution, benefits and process analysis and selection

Leverage the concept for deciding financial angle of IT projects

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Introduction to Business Analytics and Business Intelligence.
objectives: Students will be familiar with basic concepts of cognitive and analytical learning and will be able to use them in problem solving. The purpose of this course is to give students a broad understanding of the field of cognitive science. The course discusses models of cognition that are based on empirical studies of human behaviour and computer models of artificial intelligence. They will gain an in-depth understanding of the computational properties of natural languages and the commonly used algorithms for processing linguistic information.

outcomes.text: Understand the concepts of analytics and areas of cognitive learning.
Analyse the various data and cognitive analytical techniques.
Apply various artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning approaches and methodologies in real life work.

units.title: Foundational Areas of Analytics
units.text: Foundational Areas of Analytics Introduction to Analytics: Definition, Description & Evolution of Analytics, History of Analytics, and Applicability of Analytics with development of Technology and Computer, How Analytics entered mainstream Concepts of Analytics: Various overlapping concepts and fields of Analytics such as Data Mining, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence and Simulation Emerging Areas in Analytics: Understanding of emerging research areas of Analytics: Mathematical programming, Evolutionary computation, Simulation, Machine learning/data mining, Logic-based models, and, Combinations of categories Value Chain of Analytics: Descriptive Analytics Covering Exploratory Data Analysis & Basic of Statistics, Diagnostics Analytics: BI/Analysis, Trend, Pattern, Simultaneous Relationship, Predictive Analytics: Cause-Effect Relationship and Futuristic prediction in terms of probabilities, Continuous & Categorical Predictions, Simulation, Optimization, Multi-faceted Intelligent Technology driven Analytics combining Machine Intelligence with Human Brain Processing Abilities

units.title: Foundational Areas of Cognitive Science
units.text: Foundational Areas of Cognitive Science Introduction & Evolution of Cognitive Science: Introduction to the study of cognitive sciences, Brief history of cognitive science development and Methodological concerns in philosophy Understand Brain and Sensory Motor Information: Fundamentals of Neuro Science, Processing of sensory information in the brain, and Brain Imaging Elements Language & Linguistic Knowledge: Background and details of Syntax & Semantics, Understanding of Generative Linguistic Memory & Processing: Theory of Information Processing, Fundamentals of Short term Memory

units.title: Data Theory & Taxonomy Of Data
units.text: Data Theory & Taxonomy Of Data Data as a whole: Understanding of Data as a whole for distinguishing and relating various types of data and Categorization of Data: Structured, Unstructured Data, Quantitative & Qualitative Data Views of Data: Understanding Data as an interdisciplinary framework for learning methodologies: covering statistics, neural networks, and fuzzy logic Measurement & Scaling Concepts: Measurement of variables and commonly used statistical tools: Number of procedures for measurement of the variables, Categorization procedures, Scale construction procedures and Techniques of data processing for qualitative as well as quantitative data; Various types of Scales: Nominal, Ordinal, Interval & Ratio Scales

units.title: Multivariate Data Analytics & Cognitive Analytics
units.text: Multivariate Data Analytics & Cognitive Analytics Overview: High level overview of Categorization of Techniques: Inter- dependence Relationship Techniques and Dependence Relationship Techniques Overview of Commonly Used Inter-dependence Techniques: Factor Analysis, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Cluster Analysis Overview of Commonly Used Dependence Techniques: Regression, Logistic Regression Analytics Value Chain & Application of Analytics across Value Chain: Basic statistical concepts such as Descriptive & Diagnostics statistics, concept of random variables, discrete and continuous random variables, confidence interval, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance and correlation. Predictive analytics techniques such as multiple linear regression, logistic regression, decision tree learning Clustering and forecasting techniques. Prescriptive analytics Concepts: linear programming, integer programming, goal programming & stochastic models ,Cognitive analytics Concepts: Text Analytics, Learning Analytics, Data Mining, Cognitive Systems, Cognitive Computing, Learning Data Science, Machine Learning, Big data Analytics and Business analytics

units.title: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
units.text: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence: Various areas of AI: Knowledge: Text Analytics, Topic Modelling, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Natural Language Generation (NLG), Natural Language Understanding (NLU), Named-entity recognition (NER)

units.title: Perception
units.text: Perception: Image Analytics, Video Analytics & Audio Analytics Memory: Cognitive Engagement: BOTs, Virtual & Digital Assistants, Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, Mixed Reality Learning: Intelligent Automation Spectrum of AI Reactive Machine: Low memory, works on Known rules, such as Object Detection/Games/Recommendations specific to known Rules Limited Memory: Memory used to learn and improve continuously such as Most ML Models, Automated VehiclesTheory of Mind: Machine Understands and responds such as BoTs/Virtual/Digital Assistants Self-Aware: Human like intelligence such as Super Robots in Space etc Approach & Methodology: World Standard Methodology: CRISP-DM Methodology, SEMMA Methodology Real Life Work around Multi-Variate Analytics: A few Selected Commonly used Techniques: Predictive & Classification Models, Regression, Clustering Real Life Work around Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Deep Learning: A few Selected Commonly used Techniques & Algorithms: ANN (Artificial Neural Network), CNN (Convolutional Neural Network), RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) RN Architecture: LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM, Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), CTRNN (Continuous Time RNN) CNN Architectures: VGG16, Alexnet, InceptionNet, RestNet, Googlenet Object Detection models: R-CNN, Fast R-CNN, Faster R-CNN, cascade R-CNN. Mask RCNN, Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) ,You Only Look Once (YOLO), Single-Shot Refinement Neural Network for Object Detection (RefineDet), Retina-Net Autoencoders: Denoising Autoencoder, GAN Transformers: Attention based Encoder and Decoder: Eg- BERT(Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), Generative Pretrained Transformers GPT-3, GPT-2, BERT, XLNet, and RoBERTa

program: B. Tech (Computer Science & Business Systems)
prerequisites: Computer Networks, Operating Systems , Computer Organization and Architecture
objectives: This course will help students to understand basic principles and concepts of Internet-of-Things use cases, applications, architecture and technologies. It will help them to get an overview of an end to end IoT system encompassing the edge, cloud and application tiers and assist the to create an end-to- end IoT application.

outcomes.text: Identify the components, techniques and frameworks for IoT
Analyse the processes and design methodology for IoT networking and communication
Demonstrate the various techniques of IoT data processing and applications

units.title: Introduction to IoT and Use cases
units.text: Introduction to IoT and Use cases: Understanding basic concepts of IoT, Consumer IoT vs Industrial Internet, Fundamental building blocks, Use Cases of IoT in various industry domains

units.title: Architecture
units.text: Architecture: IoT reference architectures, Industrial Internet Reference Architecture, Edge Computing, IoT Gateways, Data Ingestion and Data Processing Pipelines, Data Stream Processing

units.title: Sensors and Industrial Systems
units.text: Sensors and Industrial Systems: Introduction to sensors and transducers, integrating sensors to sensor processing boards, introduction to industrial data acquisition systems, industrial control systems and their function

units.title: Networking and Communication for IoT

Message encoding (JSON, Protocol Buffers)

units.title: IoT Data Processing and Storage
units.text: IoT Data Processing and Storage: Time Series Data and their characteristics, time series databases, basic time series analytics, data summarization and sketching, dealing with noisy and missing data, anomaly and outlier detection

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: This course provides an introduction to the theory and practice of quantum computation. Topics covered include: physics of information processing, quantum logic, quantum algorithms including Shor's factoring algorithm and Grover's search algorithm, quantum error correction, quantum communication, and cryptography.

outcomes.text: Describe States, Operators, Measurements in Quantum computing.
Implement and apply Quantum Algorithms in real world problems.
Apply Quantum True Random Number Generators and Quantum key distribution (QKD) in real world problem.
Review the topics from Post-Quantum Cryptography.

units.text: Introduction to Quantum Information: States, Operators, Measurements, Quantum Entanglement: Quantum Teleportation, Super-dense coding, CHSH Game, Quantum gates and circuits

units.title: Quantum Algorithms
units.text: Quantum Algorithms: Deutsch-Jozsa, Simon, Grover, Shor, Implication of Grover’s and Simon’s algorithms towards classical symmetric key cryptosystems, Implication of Shor’s algorithm towards factorization and Discrete Logarithm based classical public key cryptosystems

course_name: Advanced Social, Text and Media Analytics
program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Data Mining, Machine Learning, Python Programming
objectives: The objective of this course is to impart knowledge of Application Programming Interface (API) services to collect data and analyze structures or unstructured data - primarily textual comments - for sentiments expressed in them. To Use different tools for collecting, analyzing, and exploring social media data for research and development purposes.

outcomes.text: Understand various techniques for Text Mining and carry out Pattern Discovery, Predictive Modelling
Explore the use of social network analysis to understand the growing connectivity and complexity in the world around us on different scales – ranging from small groups to the World Wide Web
Develop social network analysis model to identify important social actors, subgroups (i.e., clusters), and network properties in social media sites such as Twitter, Facebook, and YouTube

units.title: Text Mining
units.text: Text Mining: Introduction, Core text mining operations, Pre-processing techniques, Categorization, Clustering, Information extraction, Probabilistic models for information extraction, Text mining applications Methods & Approaches: Content Analysis; Natural Language Processing; Clustering & Topic Detection; Simple Predictive Modeling; Sentiment Analysis; Sentiment Prediction

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Operating Systems, Object Oriented Programming and Computer Networks
objectives: To educate students with wide knowledge in Mobile Computing

outcomes.text: Describe the mobile computing architecture and applications.
Compare location and handoff techniques.
Analyse wireless transmission networks and assess mobile ad-hoc, WSNs and cognitive radio networks.
Identify issues related to recent communication technologies for cellular network i.e. 5G network.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Overview of wireless and mobile infrastructure; Preliminary concepts on cellular architecture; Design objectives and performance issues; Radio resource management and interface; Propagation and path loss models; Channel interference and frequency reuse; Cell splitting; Channel assignment strategies; Overview of generations:- 1G to 5G.

units.title: Location and handoff management
units.text: Location and handoff management: Introduction to location management (HLR and VLR); Mobility models characterizing individual node movement (Random walk, Fluid flow, Markovian, Activity based); Mobility models characterizing the movement of groups of nodes (Reference point based group mobility model, Community based group mobility model); Static (Always vs. Never update, Reporting Cells, Location Areas) and Dynamic location management schemes (Time, Movement, Distance, Profile Based); Terminal Paging (Simultaneous paging, Sequential paging); Location management and Mobile IP; Overview of handoff process; Factors affecting handoffs and performance evaluation metrics; Handoff strategies; Different types of handoffs (soft, hard, horizontal, vertical)

units.title: Wireless transmission fundamentals
units.text: Wireless transmission fundamentals: Introduction to narrow and wideband systems; Spread spectrum; Frequency hopping; Introduction to MIMO; MIMO Channel Capacity and diversity gain; Introduction to OFDM; MIMO-OFDM system; Multiple access control (FDMA, TDMA, CDMA, SDMA); Wireless local area network; Wireless personal area network (Bluetooth and ZigBee)

units.title: Mobile Ad-hoc networks
units.text: Mobile Ad-hoc networks: Characteristics and applications; Coverage and connectivity problems; Routing in MANETs. Wireless sensor networks: Concepts, basic architecture, design objectives and applications; Sensing and communication range; Coverage and connectivity; Sensor placement; Data relaying and aggregation; Energy consumption; Clustering of sensors; Energy efficient Routing (LEACH). Cognitive radio networks: Fixed and dynamic spectrum access; Direct and indirect spectrum sensing; Spectrum sharing; Interoperability and co-existence issues; Applications of cognitive radio networks.

units.title: D2D communications in 5G cellular networks
units.text: D2D communications in 5G cellular networks: Introduction to D2D communications; High level requirements for 5G architecture; Introduction to the radio resource management, power control and mode selection problems; Millimeter wave communication in 5G.

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Introduction to Business Analytics and Business Intelligence, Machine Learning.
objectives: Students will be familiar with basic concepts of cognitive and analytical learning and will be able to use them in problem solving. The purpose of this course is to give students a broad understanding of the field of cognitive science. The course discusses models of cognition that are based on empirical studies of human behaviour and computer models of artificial intelligence. They will gain an in-depth understanding of the computational properties of natural languages and the commonly used algorithms for processing linguistic information.

outcomes.text: Understand the concepts of analytics and areas of cognitive learning
Analyse the various data and cognitive analytical techniques
Apply various artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning approaches and methodologies in real life work

units.title: Foundational Areas of Analytics
units.text: Foundational Areas of Analytics Introduction to Analytics: Definition, Description & Evolution of Analytics, History of Analytics, and Applicability of Analytics with development of Technology and Computer, How Analytics entered mainstream Concepts of Analytics: Various overlapping concepts and fields of Analytics such as Data Mining, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence and Simulation Introduction of Emerging Areas in Analytics: Understanding of emerging research areas of Analytics: Mathematical programming, Evolutionary computation, Simulation, Machine learning/data mining, Logic-based models, and, Combinations of categories Introduction of Value Chain of Analytics: Descriptive Analytics Covering Exploratory Data Analysis & Basic of Statistics, Diagnostics Analytics: BI/Analysis, Trend, Pattern, Simultaneous Relationship, Predictive Analytics: Cause-Effect Relationship and Futuristic prediction in terms of probabilities, Continuous & Categorical Predictions, Simulation, Optimization, Multi-faceted Intelligent Technology driven Analytics combining Machine Intelligence with Human Brain Processing Abilities

units.title: Foundational Areas of Cognitive Science
units.text: Foundational Areas of Cognitive Science Introduction & Evolution of Cognitive Science: Introduction to the study of cognitive sciences, Brief history of cognitive science development and Methodological concerns in philosophy Understand Brain and Sensory Motor Information: Fundamentals of Neuro Science, Processing of sensory information in the brain, and Brain Imaging Elements Language & Linguistic Knowledge: Background and details of Syntax & Semantics, Understanding of Generative Linguistic Memory & Processing: Theory of Information Processing, Fundamentals of Short term Memory

units.title: Data Theory & Taxonomy Of Data
units.text: Data Theory & Taxonomy Of Data Data as a whole: Understanding of Data as a whole for distinguishing and relating various types of data and Categorization of Data: Structured, Unstructured Data, Quantitative & Qualitative Data Views of Data: Understanding Data as an interdisciplinary framework for learning methodologies: covering statistics, neural networks, and fuzzy logic, Various types of Scales: Nominal, Ordinal, Interval & Ratio Scales

units.title: Multivariate Data Analytics & Cognitive Analytics
units.text: Multivariate Data Analytics & Cognitive Analytics Overview: High level overview of Categorization of Techniques: Inter-dependence Relationship Techniques and Dependence Relationship Techniques Analytics Value Chain & Application of Analytics across Value Chain: Basic statistical concepts such as Descriptive & Diagnostics statistics, concept of random variables, discrete and continuous random variables, confidence interval, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance and correlation. Introduction of Prescriptive analytics Concepts: linear programming, integer programming, stochastic models. Cognitive analytics Concepts: Text Analytics, Learning Analytics, Data Mining, Cognitive Systems

units.title: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
units.text: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence: Various areas of AI: Knowledge: Text Analytics, Topic Modelling, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Natural Language Generation (NLG), Natural Language Understanding (NLU), Named-entity recognition (NER) Perception: Image Analytics, Video Analytics & Audio Analytics Memory: Cognitive Engagement: BOTs, Virtual & Digital Assistants, Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, Mixed Reality Learning: Intelligent Automation, Spectrum of AI Reactive Machine: Low memory, works on Known rules, such as Object Detection/Games/Recommendations specific to known Rules Limited Memory: Memory used to learn and improve continuously such as Most ML Models, Automated VehiclesTheory of Mind: Machine Understands and responds such as BoTs/Virtual/Digital Assistants Self-Aware: Human like intelligence such as Super Robots in Space etc

units.title: Approach & Methodology
units.text: Approach & Methodology: World Standard Methodology: CRISP-DM Methodology, SEMMA Methodology Real Life Work around Multi-Variate Analytics: A few Selected Real Life Work around Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Deep Learning: A few Selected Commonly used Techniques & Algorithms: ANN (Artificial Neural Network), CNN (Convolutional Neural Network), RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) RN Architecture: LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM, Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), CTRNN (Continuous Time RNN) Object Detection models: Faster R-CNN, cascade R-CNN. Mask RCNN, Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) ,You Only Look Once (YOLO), Retina-Net Autoencoders: Denoising Autoencoder, GAN Transformers: Attention based Encoder and Decoder: Eg- BERT(Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), Generative Pretrained Transformers GPT-3, GPT-2

Hurwitz, Marcia Kaufman, Adrian Bowles ,Cognitive Computing and Big Data Analytics, Learning from data : concepts, theory, and methods, John Wiley &Publication, 2007.

Topics covered include: physics of information processing, quantum logic, quantum algorithms including Shor's factoring algorithm and Grover's search algorithm, quantum error correction, quantum communication, and cryptography.

Apply Quantum True Random Number Generators and Quantum key distribution (QKD) in real world problem.
Review the topics from Post-Quantum Cryptography.

prerequisites: Data Mining, Machine Learning, Python Programming
objectives: The objective of this course is to impart knowledge of Application Programming Interface (API) services to collect data and analyze structures or unstructured data - primarily textual comments - for sentiments expressed in them. To Use different tools for collecting, analyzing, and exploring social media data for research and development purposes.

outcomes.text: Understand various techniques for Text Mining and carry out Pattern Discovery, Predictive Modelling

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Operating Systems, Object Oriented Programming and Computer Networks
objectives: To educate students with wide knowledge in Mobile Computing

outcomes.text: Describe the mobile computing architecture and applications.
Compare location and handoff techniques.
Analyse wireless transmission networks and assess mobile ad-hoc, WSNs and cognitive radio networks.
Identify issues related to recent communication technologies for cellular network i.e. 5G network.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Overview of wireless and mobile infrastructure; Preliminary concepts on cellular architecture; Design objectives and performance issues; Radio resource management and interface; Propagation and path loss models; Channel interference and frequency reuse; Cell splitting; Channel assignment strategies; Overview of generations:- 1G to 5G.

units.title: Location and handoff management
units.text: Location and handoff management: Introduction to location management (HLR and VLR); Mobility models characterizing individual node movement (Random walk, Fluid flow, Markovian, Activity based); Mobility models characterizing the movement of groups of nodes (Reference point based group mobility model, Community based group mobility model); Static (Always vs. Never update, Reporting Cells, Location Areas) and Dynamic location management schemes (Time, Movement, Distance, Profile Based); Terminal Paging (Simultaneous paging, Sequential paging); Location management and Mobile IP; Overview of handoff process; Factors affecting handoffs and performance evaluation metrics; Handoff strategies; Different types of handoffs (soft, hard, horizontal, vertical)

units.title: Wireless transmission fundamentals
units.text: Wireless transmission fundamentals: Introduction to narrow and wideband systems; Spread spectrum; Frequency hopping; Introduction to MIMO; MIMO Channel Capacity and diversity gain; Introduction to OFDM; MIMO-OFDM system; Multiple access control (FDMA, TDMA, CDMA, SDMA); Wireless local area network; Wireless personal area network (Bluetooth and ZigBee)

units.title: Mobile Ad-hoc networks
units.text: Mobile Ad-hoc networks: Characteristics and applications; Coverage and connectivity problems; Routing in MANETs. Wireless sensor networks: Concepts, basic architecture, design objectives and applications; Sensing and communication range; Coverage and connectivity; Sensor placement; Data relaying and aggregation; Energy consumption; Clustering of sensors; Energy efficient Routing (LEACH). Cognitive radio networks: Fixed and dynamic spectrum access; Direct and indirect spectrum sensing; Spectrum sharing; Interoperability and co-existence issues; Applications of cognitive radio networks.

units.title: D2D communications in 5G cellular networks
units.text: D2D communications in 5G cellular networks: Introduction to D2D communications; High level requirements for 5G architecture; Introduction to the radio resource management, power control and mode selection problems; Millimeter wave communication in 5G.

prerequisites: Operating Systems, Object Oriented Programming and Computer Networks
objectives: To educate students with wide knowledge in Mobile Computing

outcomes.text: Describe the mobile computing architecture and applications.
Compare location and handoff techniques.
Analyse wireless transmission networks and assess mobile ad-hoc, WSNs and cognitive radio networks.
Identify issues related to recent communication technologies for cellular network i.e. 5G network.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Overview of wireless and mobile infrastructure; Preliminary concepts on cellular architecture; Design objectives and performance issues; Radio resource management and interface; Propagation and path loss models; Channel interference and frequency reuse; Cell splitting; Channel assignment strategies; Overview of generations:- 1G to 5G.

units.title: Location and handoff management
units.text: Location and handoff management: Introduction to location management (HLR and VLR); Mobility models characterizing individual node movement (Random walk, Fluid flow, Markovian, Activity based); Mobility models characterizing the movement of groups of nodes (Reference point based group mobility model, Community based group mobility model); Static (Always vs. Never update, Reporting Cells, Location Areas) and Dynamic location management schemes (Time, Movement, Distance, Profile Based); Terminal Paging (Simultaneous paging, Sequential paging); Location management and Mobile IP; Overview of handoff process; Factors affecting handoffs and performance evaluation metrics; Handoff strategies; Different types of handoffs (soft, hard, horizontal, vertical)

Able to identify characteristics and nature of Services
Comprehend ways to design Services and evaluate them using Service qualities
Understand how various methods can be used to operate and manage Service businesses

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To understand human behaviour through the lens of social preferences, heuristics and norms and its application in decision making in contrast to neo-classical / standard model.

outcomes.text: To understand how individuals behave and how thoughts and emotions affect individual decision-making.
To examine how beliefs, heuristics and biases affect decisions.
To Understand aspects of decision-making under uncertainty and solve analytical problems.
To analyse individual preferences in social context.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction The neoclassical/standard model and behavioral economics in contrast; historical background; behavioral economics and other social sciences; theory and evidence in the social sciences and in behavioral economics; applications – gains and losses, money illusion, charitable donation.

units.title: Basics of choice theory
units.text: Basics of choice theory Revisiting the neoclassical model; utility in economics and psychology; models of rationality; connections with evolutionary biology and cognitive neuroscience; policy analysis – consumption and addiction, environmental protection, retail therapy; applications – pricing, valuation, public goods, choice anomalies

units.title: Beliefs, heuristics and biases
units.text: Beliefs, heuristics and biases: Revisiting rationality; causal aspects of irrationality; different kinds of biases and beliefs; self-evaluation and self- projection; inconsistent and biased beliefs; probability estimation; trading applications – trade in counterfeit goods, financial trading behavior, trade in memorabilia

units.title: Choice under uncertainty
units.text: Choice under uncertainty: Background and expected utility theory; prospect theory and other theories; reference points; loss aversion; marginal utility; decision and probability weighting; applications – ownership and trade, income and consumption, performance in sports.

units.title: Intertemporal choice
units.text: Intertemporal choice: Geometric discounting; preferences over time; anomalies of inter-temporal decisions; hyperbolic discounting; instantaneous utility; alternative concepts – future projection, mental accounts, heterogeneous selves, procedural choice; policy analysis – mobile calls, credit cards, organization of government; applications – consumption and savings, clubs and membership, consumption planning

units.title: Strategic choice

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Business Strategy, Financial & Cost Accounting, Financial Management
objectives: This course will help the students to get an overview of the traditional financial theories of portfolio management, calculus models, and optimization techniques.

outcomes.text: Understand existing financial models in a quantitative and mathematical way.
Apply these quantitative tools to solve complex problems in the areas of portfolio management, risk management and financial engineering.
Explain the approaches required to calculate the price of options.
Identify the methods required to analyse information from financial data and trading systems.

units.text: Numerical methods relevant to integration, differentiation and solving the partial differential equations of mathematical finance: examples of exact solutions including Black Scholes and its relatives, finite difference methods including algorithms and question of stability and convergence, treatment of near and far boundary conditions, the connection with binomial models, interest rate models, early exercise, and the corresponding free boundary problems, and a brief introduction to numerical methods for solving multi-factor models.

units.title: Black-Scholes framework
units.text: Black-Scholes framework: Black-Scholes PDE: simple European calls and puts; put-call parity. The PDE for pricing commodity and currency options. Discontinuous payoffs - Binary and Digital options. The Greeks: theta, delta, gamma, vega & rho and their role in hedging. The mathematics of early exercise - American options: perpetual calls and puts; optimal exercise strategy and the smooth pasting condition. Volatility considerations - actual, historical, and implied volatility; local vol and volatility surfaces. Simulation including random variable generation, variance reduction methods and statistical analysis of simulation output. Pseudo random numbers, Linear congruential generator, Mersenne twister RNG. The use of Monte Carlo simulation in solving applied problems on derivative pricing discussed in the current finance literature. The technical topics addressed include importance sampling, Monte Carlo integration, Simulation of Random walk and approximations to diffusion processes, martingale control variables, stratification, and the estimation of the “Greeks.”

units.title: Financial Products and Markets
units.text: Financial Products and Markets: Introduction to the financial markets and the products which are traded in them: Equities, indices, foreign exchange, and commodities. Options contracts and strategies for speculation and hedging.

Application areas include the pricing of American options, pricing interest rate dependent claims, and credit risk. The use of importance sampling for Monte Carlo simulation of VaR for portfolios of options.

units.title: Statistical Analysis of Financial Returns
units.text: Statistical Analysis of Financial Returns: Fat-tailed and skewed distributions, outliers, stylized facts of volatility, implied volatility surface, and volatility estimation using high frequency data.

Copulas, Hedging in incomplete markets, American Options, Exotic options, Electronic trading, Jump Diffusion Processes, High-dimensional covariance matrices, Extreme value theory, Statistical Arbitrage.

objectives: The course will serve as an introduction to the implementation of enterprise systems within organizations. Functionalities and purposes of enterprise systems will be presented and analyzed, including enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, and supply chain management (SCM) systems.
