program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: The objective of the course is to understand the growing significance and impact of services on the growth and economy and the scientific ways to run the operations so as to optimize the business and brand returns.

outcomes.text: Understand concepts about Services and distinguish it from Goods
Able to identify characteristics and nature of Services
Comprehend ways to design Services and evaluate them using Service qualities
Understand how various methods can be used to operate and manage Service businesses
Understand how innovation can be approached from Services point of view

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Introduction to the course, Introduction to service operations, Role of service in economy and society, Introduction to Indian service sector. Nature of Services and Service Encounters: Differences between services and operations, Service package, characteristics, various frameworks to design service operation system, Kind of service encounter, importance of encounters. Service-Dominant Logic: From Goods-Dominant logic to Service-Dominant logic, Value Co-creation.

units.title: Service Strategy and Competitiveness
units.text: Service Strategy and Competitiveness: Development of Strategic Service Vision (SSV), Data Envelopment Analysis. New Service Development: NSD cycle, Service Blueprinting, Elements of service delivery system. Service Design: Customer Journey and Service Design, Design Thinking methods to aid Service Design. Locating facilities and designing their layout: models of facility locations (Huff's retail model), Role of service-scape in layout design. Service Quality: SERVQUAL, Walk through Audit, Dimensions of Service quality & other quality tools.

units.title: Service Guarantee & Service Recovery
units.text: Service Guarantee & Service Recovery: How to provide Service guarantee? How to recover from Service failure?

units.title: Forecasting Demand for Services
units.text: Forecasting Demand for Services: A review of different types of forecasting methods for demand forecasting. Managing Capacity and Demand: Strategies for matching capacity and demand, Psychology of waiting, Application of various tools used in managing waiting line in services. Managing Facilitating Goods: Review of inventory models, Role of inventory in services. Managing service supply relationship: Understanding the supply chain/hub of service, Strategies for managing suppliers of service. Vehicle Routing Problem: Managing after sales service, Understanding services that involve transportation of people and vehicle, Techniques for optimizing vehicle routes.

units.title: Service Innovation
units.text: Service Innovation: Services Productivity, Need for Services Innovation. Student Project: Option 1: Choose any service organization around and present it from the perspective of: nature of service, classification of service, blueprint or service design analysis, service quality, and any additional perspective you would like to add. Option 2: Choose any latest research paper in services and explain your understanding and feedback on the same.

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
objectives: To understand human behaviour through the lens of social preferences, heuristics and norms and its application in decision making in contrast to neo-classical / standard model.

outcomes.text: To understand how individuals behave and how thoughts and emotions affect individual decision-making.
To examine how beliefs, heuristics and biases affect decisions.
To Understand aspects of decision-making under uncertainty and solve analytical problems.
To analyse individual preferences in social context.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction The neoclassical/standard model and behavioral economics in contrast; historical background; behavioral economics and other social sciences; theory and evidence in the social sciences and in behavioral economics; applications – gains and losses, money illusion, charitable donation.

units.title: Basics of choice theory
units.text: Basics of choice theory Revisiting the neoclassical model; utility in economics and psychology; models of rationality; connections with evolutionary biology and cognitive neuroscience; policy analysis – consumption and addiction, environmental protection, retail therapy; applications – pricing, valuation, public goods, choice anomalies

units.title: Beliefs, heuristics and biases
units.text: Beliefs, heuristics and biases: Revisiting rationality; causal aspects of irrationality; different kinds of biases and beliefs; self-evaluation and self- projection; inconsistent and biased beliefs; probability estimation; trading applications – trade in counterfeit goods, financial trading behavior, trade in memorabilia

units.title: Choice under uncertainty
units.text: Choice under uncertainty: Background and expected utility theory; prospect theory and other theories; reference points; loss aversion; marginal utility; decision and probability weighting; applications – ownership and trade, income and consumption, performance in sports.

units.title: Intertemporal choice
units.text: Intertemporal choice Geometric discounting; preferences over time; anomalies of inter-temporal decisions; hyperbolic discounting; instantaneous utility; alternative concepts – future projection, mental accounts, heterogeneous selves, procedural choice; policy analysis – mobile calls, credit cards, organization of government; applications – consumption and savings, clubs and membership, consumption planning

units.title: Strategic choice
units.text: Strategic choice Review of game theory and Nash equilibrium – strategies, information, equilibrium in pure and mixed strategies, iterated games, bargaining, signaling, learning; applications – competitive sports, bargaining and negotiation, monopoly and market entry

Individual preferences; choice anomalies and inconsistencies; social preferences; altruism; fairness; reciprocity; trust; learning; communication; intention; demographic and cultural aspects; social norms; compliance and punishment; inequity aversion; policy analysis – norms and markets, labor markets, market clearing, public goods; applications – logic and knowledge, voluntary contribution, compensation design

text_books: 1. An Introduction to Behavioral Economics, by N. Wilkinson and M. Klaes
reference_books: 1. Colin Cramer, George Loewenstien, Mathew Rabin , Advances in Behavioral Economics, Princeton University Press

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Business Strategy, Financial & Cost Accounting, Financial Management
objectives: This course will help the students to get an overview of the traditional financial theories of portfolio management, calculus models, and optimization techniques.

outcomes.text: Understand existing financial models in a quantitative and mathematical way.
Apply these quantitative tools to solve complex problems in the areas of portfolio management, risk management and financial engineering.
Explain the approaches required to calculate the price of options.
Identify the methods required to analyse information from financial data and trading systems.

units.text: Numerical methods relevant to integration, differentiation and solving the partial differential equations of mathematical finance: examples of exact solutions including Black Scholes and its relatives, finite difference methods including algorithms and question of stability and convergence, treatment of near and far boundary conditions, the connection with binomial models, interest rate models, early exercise, and the corresponding free boundary problems, and a brief introduction to numerical methods for solving multi-factor models.

units.title: Black-Scholes framework
units.text: Black-Scholes framework: Black-Scholes PDE: simple European calls and puts; put-call parity. The PDE for pricing commodity and currency options. Discontinuous payoffs - Binary and Digital options. The Greeks: theta, delta, gamma, vega & rho and their role in hedging. The mathematics of early exercise - American options: perpetual calls and puts; optimal exercise strategy and the smooth pasting condition. Volatility considerations - actual, historical, and implied volatility; local vol and volatility surfaces. Simulation including random variable generation, variance reduction methods and statistical analysis of simulation output. Pseudo random numbers, Linear congruential generator, Mersenne twister RNG. The use of Monte Carlo simulation in solving applied problems on derivative pricing discussed in the current finance literature. The technical topics addressed include importance sampling, Monte Carlo integration, Simulation of Random walk and approximations to diffusion processes, martingale control variables, stratification, and the estimation of the “Greeks.”

units.title: Financial Products and Markets
units.text: Financial Products and Markets: Introduction to the financial markets and the products which are traded in them: Equities, indices, foreign exchange, and commodities. Options contracts and strategies for speculation and hedging.

Application areas include the pricing of American options, pricing interest rate dependent claims, and credit risk. The use of importance sampling for Monte Carlo simulation of VaR for portfolios of options.

units.title: Statistical Analysis of Financial Returns
units.text: Statistical Analysis of Financial Returns: Fat-tailed and skewed distributions, outliers, stylized facts of volatility, implied volatility surface, and volatility estimation using high frequency data.

Copulas, Hedging in incomplete markets, American Options, Exotic options, Electronic trading, Jump Diffusion Processes, High-dimensional covariance matrices, Extreme value theory, Statistical Arbitrage.

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Introduction to Innovation, IP Management & Entrepreneurship
objectives: To introduce students to the content areas of industrial psychology and the application of psychological theory to organizational issues. Topics include employment law, job analysis, recruitment and selection, training, performance appraisal and discipline, employee motivation, and workplace safety. Using an applied approach, this course will help prepare students for their roles as employees and managers.

outcomes.text: Become conversant about the major content areas of Industrial Psychology (i.e., job analysis, recruitment, selection, employment law, training, performance management, and health/well- being issues in the workplace).
Gain further comfort with statistical concepts in the context of making personnel decisions to reinforce content learned in PSY203 or an equivalent introductory statistics course.
Gain practical experience by completing a series of hands-on projects involving job analysis, selection decisions, training programs, and employee well-being.
Deepen your understanding of tests and measurements so that you can collect accurate information and make sound data-based decisions.
Prepare for other focused seminar courses in Industrial/Organizational Psychology or Human Resource Management.

objectives: To understand human behaviour through the lens of social preferences, heuristics and norms and its application in decision making in contrast to neo-classical / standard model.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction The neoclassical/standard model and behavioral economics in contrast; historical background; behavioral economics and other social sciences; theory and evidence in the social sciences and in behavioral economics; applications – gains and losses, money illusion, charitable donation.

units.title: Basics of choice theory
units.text: Basics of choice theory Revisiting the neoclassical model; utility in economics and psychology; models of rationality; connections with evolutionary biology and cognitive neuroscience; policy analysis – consumption and addiction, environmental protection, retail therapy; applications – pricing, valuation, public goods, choice anomalies

units.title: Beliefs, heuristics and biases

units.title: Choice under uncertainty
units.text: Choice under uncertainty: Background and expected utility theory; prospect theory and other theories; reference points; loss aversion; marginal utility; decision and probability weighting; applications – ownership and trade, income and consumption, performance in sports.

units.title: Intertemporal choice
units.text: Intertemporal choice Geometric discounting; preferences over time; anomalies of inter-temporal decisions; hyperbolic discounting; instantaneous utility; alternative concepts – future projection, mental accounts, heterogeneous selves, procedural choice; policy analysis – mobile calls, credit cards, organization of government; applications – consumption and savings, clubs and membership, consumption planning

Individual preferences; choice anomalies and inconsistencies; social preferences; altruism; fairness; reciprocity; trust; learning; communication; intention; demographic and cultural aspects; social norms; compliance and punishment; inequity aversion; policy analysis – norms and markets, labor markets, market clearing, public goods; applications – logic and knowledge, voluntary contribution, compensation design

program: B. Tech (Computer Science and Business Systems)
prerequisites: Business Strategy, Financial & Cost Accounting, Financial Management
objectives: This course will help the students to get an overview of the traditional financial theories of portfolio management, calculus models, and optimization techniques.

outcomes.text: Understand existing financial models in a quantitative and mathematical way.
Apply these quantitative tools to solve complex problems in the areas of portfolio management, risk management and financial engineering.
Explain the approaches required to calculate the price of options.
Identify the methods required to analyse information from financial data and trading systems.

units.text: Numerical methods relevant to integration, differentiation and solving the partial differential equations of mathematical finance: examples of exact solutions including Black Scholes and its relatives, finite difference methods including algorithms and question of stability and convergence, treatment of near and far boundary conditions, the connection with binomial models, interest rate models, early exercise, and the corresponding free boundary problems, and a brief introduction to numerical methods for solving multi-factor models.

units.title: Black-Scholes framework
units.text: Black-Scholes framework: Black-Scholes PDE: simple European calls and puts; put-call parity. The PDE for pricing commodity and currency options. Discontinuous payoffs - Binary and Digital options. The Greeks: theta, delta, gamma, vega & rho and their role in hedging. The mathematics of early exercise - American options: perpetual calls and puts; optimal exercise strategy and the smooth pasting condition. Volatility considerations - actual, historical, and implied volatility; local vol and volatility surfaces. Simulation including random variable generation, variance reduction methods and statistical analysis of simulation output. Pseudo random numbers, Linear congruential generator, Mersenne twister RNG. The use of Monte Carlo simulation in solving applied problems on derivative pricing discussed in the current finance literature. The technical topics addressed include importance sampling, Monte Carlo integration, Simulation of Random walk and approximations to diffusion processes, martingale control variables, stratification, and the estimation of the “Greeks.”

units.title: Financial Products and Markets
units.text: Financial Products and Markets: Introduction to the financial markets and the products which are traded in them: Equities, indices, foreign exchange, and commodities. Options contracts and strategies for speculation and hedging.

Application areas include the pricing of American options, pricing interest rate dependent claims, and credit risk. The use of importance sampling for Monte Carlo simulation of VaR for portfolios of options.

units.title: Statistical Analysis of Financial Returns
units.text: Statistical Analysis of Financial Returns: Fat-tailed and skewed distributions, outliers, stylized facts of volatility, implied volatility surface, and volatility estimation using high frequency data.

Copulas, Hedging in incomplete markets, American Options, Exotic options, Electronic trading, Jump Diffusion Processes, High-dimensional covariance matrices, Extreme value theory, Statistical Arbitrage.

objectives: DevSecOps automatically bakes in security at every phase of the software development lifecycle, enabling development of secure software at the speed of Agile and DevOps. program: B. Tech CSE (Cybersecurity)
objectives: Image and video evidence is a growing concern during an investigation as more and more of our lives are captured in some form. From cell phones to CCTV security cameras in public places to cell phone cameras, our everyday activities are constantly being recorded. This evidence, when properly collected and analysed, can be crucial in solving crimes. This course will introduce students to the concepts of video and image forensics. The course will cover how to properly identify, collect, and handle digital video and image evidence in a way that maintains evidence integrity and is consistent with best practices in the field.

outcomes.text: Forensically extract image and video evidence from given media
Perform image and video authentication and detect tampering
Create and detect deepfake

objectives: DevSecOps automatically bakes in security at every phase of the software development lifecycle, enabling development of secure software at the speed of Agile and DevOps. program: B. Tech Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity)
objectives: Image and video evidence is a growing concern during an investigation as more and more of our lives are captured in some form. From cell phones to CCTV security cameras in public places to cell phone cameras, our everyday activities are constantly being recorded. This evidence, when properly collected and analysed, can be crucial in solving crimes. This course will introduce students to the concepts of video and image forensics. The course will cover how to properly identify, collect, and handle digital video and image evidence in a way that maintains evidence integrity and is consistent with best practices in the field.

outcomes.text: Forensically extract image and video evidence from given media
Perform image and video authentication and detect tampering
Create and detect deepfake

objectives: This course gives you an introduction to modeling methods and simulation tools for a wide range of natural phenomena. program: B. Tech– Data Science (Business Analytics)
objectives: This course gives you an introduction to modeling methods and simulation tools for a wide range of natural phenomena. The different methodologies that will be presented here can be applied to very wide range of topics such as  Fluid motion, stellar dynamics, population evolution etc.  This course does not intend to go deeply into any numerical method or process and does not provide any recipe for the resolution of a particular problem  It is rather a basic guideline towards different methodologies that can be applied to solve any kind of problem and help you pick the one best suited for you. The assignments of this course will be made as practical as possible in order to allow you to actually create from scratch short programs that will solve simple problems. Although programming will be used extensively in this course we do not require any advanced programming experience in order to complete it.

outcomes.text: Explain the differences between machine learning systems in research and production, and describe the components and needs of ML systems in real-world scenarios.
Apply fundamental concepts of data systems including data sources, formats, models, and processing frameworks to enable machine learning workflows.
Analyze the processes of data sampling, labeling, handling class imbalance, and feature engineering in the design of ML systems.
Evaluate deployment strategies such as batch and online prediction, and assess the trade-offs in cloud vs. edge deployment.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech Data Science
objectives: The aim of this course is to deep dive into details of neural-network based learning methods for computer vision. It will cover neural learning algorithms and practical engineering tricks for training and fine-tuning networks for visual recognition tasks. It will enable the students to learn advanced concepts of computer vision and utilize them to implement vision algorithms efficiently for use in research and industry.

outcomes.text: Analyze visual content using feature extraction techniques such as edge, corner, blob detection, and descriptors like SIFT, SURF, HoG, and LBP for effective image representation and matching.
Apply Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image classification, recognition, and training using advanced architectures such as AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, and Inception.

Evaluate object detection and segmentation methods (e.g., YOLO, Mask R-CNN, U-Net), and visualize CNN features using techniques like DeepDream and Style Transfer.
Design and implement advanced deep learning models for generative and self-supervised tasks using GANs, VAEs, contrastive learning, and video understanding using 3D CNNs and multimodal systems.

program: B Tech / MAB Tech Data Science, B Tech CSE (DS)

objectives: The aim of the course is to introduce the students with fundamentals of Quantum Machine Learning. It will enable students to relate elements from classical Machine Learning techniques with Quantum computing.

outcomes.text: Understand key concepts of quantum computing including qubits, gates, measurement, and quantum parallelism.

objectives: The capstone project is designed to provide a culminating design experience to the final-year students’ learning with essentially required hands-on experience to ensure that they graduate with the required practical and soft skills. objectives: The aim of the course is to provide an iterative framework for developing real-world machine learning systems that are deployable, reliable, and scalable. outcomes.text: Explain the differences between machine learning systems in research and production, and describe the components and needs of ML systems in real-world scenarios.

Analyze the processes of data sampling, labeling, handling class imbalance, and feature engineering in the design of ML systems.
Evaluate deployment strategies such as batch and online prediction, and assess the trade-offs in cloud vs. edge deployment.
Design an end-to-end ML production pipeline including model monitoring, diagnosis of failures, and resource management.

objectives: The aim of this course is to deep dive into details of neural-network based learning methods for computer vision. It will cover neural learning algorithms and practical engineering tricks for training and fine-tuning networks for visual recognition tasks. It will enable the students to learn advanced concepts of computer vision and utilize them to implement vision algorithms efficiently for use in research and industry.

outcomes.text: Analyze visual content using feature extraction techniques such as edge, corner, blob detection, and descriptors like SIFT, SURF, HoG, and LBP for effective image representation and matching.
Apply Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image classification, recognition, and training using advanced architectures such as AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, and Inception.
Demonstrate the integration of CNN and RNN models for spatio-temporal tasks including video-based action recognition, image captioning, and sequence-to-sequence problems.
Evaluate object detection and segmentation methods (e.g., YOLO, Mask R-CNN, U-Net), and visualize CNN features using techniques like DeepDream and Style Transfer.
Design and implement advanced deep learning models for generative and self-supervised tasks using GANs, VAEs, contrastive learning, and video understanding using 3D CNNs and multimodal systems.

program: B. Tech– Data Science (Business Analytics)
objectives: This course gives you an introduction to modeling methods and simulation tools for a wide range of natural phenomena. The different methodologies that will be presented here can be applied to very wide range of topics such as  Fluid motion, stellar dynamics, population evolution etc.  This course does not intend to go deeply into any numerical method or process and does not provide any recipe for the resolution of a particular problem  It is rather a basic guideline towards different methodologies that can be applied to solve any kind of problem and help you pick the one best suited for you. The assignments of this course will be made as practical as possible in order to allow you to actually create from scratch short programs that will solve simple problems. Although programming will be used extensively in this course we do not require any advanced programming experience in order to complete it.

3GPP LTE and 4G 3GPP LTE: Introduction, system overview: Frequency bands and spectrum, network structure, and protocol structure, Physical layer: Frame slots and symbols Logical and Physical Channels: Mapping of data on to logical sub- channels physical layer procedures: establishing a connection, retransmission and reliability, scheduling, power control, handover. 4G: Introduction, features and architecture-Multi antenna Technologies: MIMO.

units.title: Emerging Technologies
units.text: Emerging Technologies: 5G Characteristics envisioned for 5G, specifications and architecture SDN (Software Defined Network) - Objective and architecture.

text_books: 1. Theodore S. Rappaport, “Wireless Communications”, Prentice Hall of India, PTR publication, 2nd edition, 2011. 2. Andreas F. Molisch , “Wireless Communications”, Wiley, 2nd edition, 2010
reference_books: 1. Jochen H. Schiller, “Mobile Communication”, Pearson, 2nd edition, 2010. 2. Gary J. Mullet, “Introduction to wireless telecommunications systems and networks”, Cengage learning, 1st edition, 2011.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Digital Communication and Computer networks
objectives: 1. To provide knowledge of basic Telephony and characterise the traffic in telephone network. 2. To study various types of digital switching and signalling techniques and ISDN with B-ISDN. 3. To understand the need and process of transition from traditional communication networks to broadband communication networks. 4. To explore Voice over IP and the functionality of different building blocks of broadband technology.

outcomes.text: Explain the basic concepts of telephony.
Analyse and characterize the traffic in telephone network and Broadband Access Technologies.
Compare the different broadband network access techniques of cable modem service, optical fiber based access, and broadband wireless access techniques of Wi-Fi and Wi- MAX networks.
Describes the voice coding techniques and different protocols used for VoIP.

units.title: Telephony Background
units.text: Telephony Background: Analogue networks, subscriber loop design, calculating resistance Limit, calculating loss limit, Transmission Impairments in Subscriber loop.

units.title: Telephone traffic theory
units.text: Telephone traffic theory: Traffic characterization, arrival and holding time, Erlang formula and Tables, loss systems, lost calls, network blocking probabilities, delay systems, measurement of traffic congestion, lost calls and grade of service.

units.title: Digital switching and Synchronisation
units.text: Digital switching and Synchronisation: Voice digitization Multi channel PCM, Frame/multiframe/signalling formats, Higher order multiplexing, Line codes, Space division switching, time division switching, time space time (TST) switch, space time space (STS) switch, comparison of TST and STS switches, Blocking and Non-blocking switches. Network Synchronization: Need for synchronization, Methods for synchronization Timing recovery (PLL), Clock Instability, Elastic stores, Timing inaccuracies, Slips, Pulse Stuffing. Signalling: Types of Signalling, Channel Associated signalling, Common Channel Signalling, SS7.

units.title: Integrated service digital network (ISDN)
units.text: Integrated service digital network (ISDN): ISDN overview, ISDN interfaces and functions, transmission structure, Broadband ISDN (B - ISDN): (B - ISDNS) standards, architecture protocol reference model, B- ISDN lower layers.

units.title: The Basics of Broadband Technology
units.text: The Basics of Broadband Technology: Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL, HDSL, RADSL, VDSL, G.lite), Access network architecture (DSLAM), Modulation technologies (DMT), CAP

units.title: Voice over IP
units.text: Voice over IP: Voice coding, properties of speech, waveform coding, vocoding, hybrid coding, VoIP architecture, VoIP Protocols: Resource reservation protocol (RSVP), Multi Protocol Label Switching (MPLS), real time protocol (RTP), session initiation protocol (SIP). H.323 standard media gateway control protocol, business aspects of VoIP routes

units.title: Broadband ATM Switching & Transmission
units.text: Broadband ATM Switching & Transmission: Broadband IP Switching over ATM, Broadband Transmission Network for LAN & WAN, SONET/ SDH. 6. Broadband Access Technologies: Cable Modem Service: Head end and regional network architecture, Cable Modem Termination System, CMTS, Hybrid Fiber Coax networks HFC, Cable Labs initiatives (DOCSIS. PacketCable, CableHome), Optical Fiber-based Networks: Passive Optical Network (PON) architecture (Optical line termination, optical network terminals), Standards (BPON, GPON, EPON) Fixed and Mobile WiMAX: Architecture, Standards (IEEE 802.11, 802.15, 802.16), Services, Comparison of broadband access techniques.

text_books: 1. John C. Bellamy, “Digital Telephony”, Wiley India, 3rd edition, 2011. 2. William Stalling, “ISDN and Broadband ISDN with Frame Relay and ATM”, Pearson education Asia publication, 4th Edition, 2002. 3. Leonhard Korowajczuk, “LTE, WiMAX and WLAN Network Design, Optimization and Performance Analysis”, John Willey Publication, 1st edition, 2011. 4. Alberto Leon-Garcia, “Communication Networks”, Tata McGraw Hill Publication, Second edition, 2004.
reference_books: 1. Roger L. Freeman, “Fundamentals of Telecommunication”, John Wiley and Sons, Inc., Publication, 2nd edition, 2013. 2. Andy Valder, “Understanding telecommunication network”, IET, 1st Edition 2007. 3. Ray Horak, “Telecommunications and Data Communications Handbook”, John Wiley and Sons, Inc., Publication, 2nd edition, 2008

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of solid state electronics.
objectives: 1. To provide the foundation for state-of-the-art CMOS design. 2. To provide the basics of design and layout of CMOS VLSI circuits. 3. To study the essential physics required for understanding of VLSI circuits and VLSI design rules. 4. To implement the full VLSI design flow for IC design and chip level issues.

outcomes.text: Undersatnd the IC fabrication process.
Understand advanced VLSI CMOS design flow used in the semiconductor industry using EDA tools.
Determine the performance of VLSI circuits like inverters, super buffers and sequential circuits.
Implement CMOS Logic from transistor level schematic to layout using design rules using CAD tools.

units.title: Fabrication of ICs
units.text: Fabrication of ICs: Crystal growth, Diffusion of impurities, Ion implantation, Oxidation, CVD, Lithography, Epitaxy, Metallization and Packaging. Fabrication of NPN, PNP and lateral Transistors. Parasitic Transistor, Fabrication of IC Diodes, Resistor and capacitors, Isolation. Field Effect Transistor: General physical consideration, MOSFET Threshold voltage, flat band condition, threshold adjustment, linear and saturated operation, FET capacitance mobility saturation and thermal variations, Short channel effect and hot electron effects electro migration, Aluminium spikes and contact resistance.

units.title: Processing Scaling and Reliability
units.text: Processing Scaling and Reliability: Silicon gate NMOS CMOS process, silicon patterning, mask generation, active area definition, transistor formation contacts, metallization, chip packaging process limitations scaling factor of MOS circuits, scaling, functional limitations of scaling, scaling of wires and interconnections, latch up in scaled CMOS circuits, device reliability, soft errors, noise margins, lead inductance, gate oxide reliability, Polysilicon resistance and input protection.

units.title: Design rules and Layout
units.text: Design rules and Layout : The purpose of design rules, NMOS rules, CMOS design rules, passive load NMOS inverter , active load NMOS inverter, NMOS NAND & NOR gates, CMOS inverter, CMOS NAND & NOR gates, interlayer contacts, butting and buried contacts.

units.title: MOS inverters
units.text: MOS inverters : MOSFET aspect and inverter ratio, enhancement & depletion mode pull ups, enhancement Vs depletion mode pull ups, standard CMOS inverter, NMOS threshold voltage and inverter ratio transit and switching speed of NMOS & CMOS inverter.

units.title: Super Buffer
units.text: Super Buffer : CMOS & steering logic, RC delay lines, NMOS & CMOS super buffer, NMOS tri-state super buffer and PAD drivers. CMOS gates, dynamic ratio-less inverter with large capacitive buffer load, designing pass transistor logic. Dynamic CMOS design.

units.title: CMOS Digital Gates/Sequential Circuits
units.text: CMOS Digital Gates/Sequential Circuits: NMOS and CMOS Super Buffer, Tri-State buffer and PAD Drivers, CMOS Gates, Dynamic CMOS Design, Charge Sharing, Pseudo- NMOS PMOS, Flip-Flops, Setup and Hold Time, Race Around Condition, Sequential Digital Circuits, Power Analysis and Estimation, Different Process Corners, Slow and Fast Transistors, High and Low Threshold Voltage Transistors.

units.title: CAD Tools and Methodology
units.text: CAD Tools and Methodology Introduction to VLSI CAD tools, ASIC, Full-Custom flow, RTL-to- GDSII flow.

units.title: Packaging and Testing
units.text: Packaging and Testing: Packaging of ICs. Different types of packages. Design for Testability – requirement & cost of testing, test pattern generation, fault models, test generation and methodology

text_books: 1. Neil H. E. Weste, and Kamran Eshraghian, “Principles of CMOS VLSI Design a System Perspective”, Addison Wesley, 3rd edition, 2003. 2. E. D Fabricius, “Introduction to VLSI Design”, McGraw-Hill, 3rd edition, 1990.
reference_books: 1. Carver Mead and Lynn Conway, “Introduction to VLSI Systems”, Addison-Wesley, 5th Edition, 1980 2. D. A. Pucknell, Kamran Eshraghian, “Basic VLSI Design”, Prentice Hall, 3rd edition. 2010. 3. Andrew Bros, “VLSI Circuits & System in Silicon”, McGraw Hill International Edition, 3rd edition, 1991. 4. “Cadence Design Manual, Cadence Design Systems”, CA, USA Publication, 3rd Edition, July 2005.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Basic Engineering Mathematics, Automation and Control.
objectives: 1. To impart knowledge about industrial robots for their control and design. 2. To understand and analyse the various applications of robots. 3. To provide knowledge to learn essential concepts behind control system elements and operations.

outcomes.text: Perform kinematic and dynamic analyses with simulation.
Understand image representation for robotic movement.
Understand usage of various controllers, sensors and actuators in the system.
Learn and apply essential concepts behind control system elements and operations in hydraulics automation.

units.title: Introduction to Robotics
units.text: Introduction to Robotics Automation and Robots, Classification, Application, Specification, Social issues and safety

units.title: Direct and Inverse Kinematics
units.text: Direct and Inverse Kinematics Co-ordinate frames, Rotations, Homogeneous Coordinates, Link co-ordinates, Arm equation (3 ,4 and 5 axes robots). General properties of inverse kinematic solution, Tool configuration, Inverse kinematics of three axis, four axis and five axis robots.

units.title: Robot Vision
units.text: Robot Vision: Image representation and analysis, Template matching, Polyhedral objects, Shape Analysis, Segmentation.

units.title: Introduction to automation
units.text: Introduction to automation: Automation in production system. Principles and strategies of automation, Basic elements of an automation system, Advanced automation Functions, Levels of automation.

units.title: Sensor and Actuation Systems
units.text: Sensor and Actuation Systems Sensor: Contact and Proximity, Position, Velocity, Force, Tactile etc. Actuators: Electric, Hydraulic and Pneumatic; Transmission: Gears, Timing Belts and Bearings, Parameters for selection of sensors and actuators.

Introduction to Hydraulics, Physical Fundamentals and principles, Hydraulic components (Pump, Valves, etc.), Basic hydraulics circuits and Electro Hydraulics, Practical examples based on simple automation tasks, types of proportional control devices- Pressure relief, Flow control, Direction control, Hydraulic symbols, Spool configurations, Selection & sizing with reference to manufacturer's data, Electrical operation, Basic electrical circuits and operation, Solenoid design, Comparison between conventional and proportional valves.

units.title: PLC
units.text: PLC Introduction to Automation Technology and Programming Languages (Ladder Diagram), Interface I/O modules with PLC, Design of logic Gates using Ladder diagram, Working principle of relays and contactors, Area of application Programming with Relay and PLC

text_books: 1. Robert Schilling, “Fundamentals of Robotics- Analysis and control”, Prentice Hall of India, 4/e, 2011. 2. Johnson Curtis, “Process Control Control Instrumentation Technology”, Prentice hall of India, 8th edition, 2007.
reference_books: 14 1. John J Craig, “Introduction to Robotics: Mechanics & Control”, Pearson Education India, 3/e, 2008. 2. Dale R. Patrick and Stephen Fardo, “Industrial Process Control System”, 2nd Edition, Prentice hall, 2011.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Analog and digital communication systems, Digital Television Systems, Electromagnetic Field Theory.
objectives: 1. Understand and provide knowledge of principle of Satellite communication and Radar communication. 2. To study various types and application of Radar systems for navigation and remote sensing. 3. Study of different types of satellite orbits, Orbital parameters and launching techniques, spacecraft subsystems and satellite services. 4. To provide knowledge of wave propagation and satellite link design.

outcomes.text: Apply concepts of Satellite and Radar communication in numerous applications.
Determine orbital parameters and apply concepts for launching various satellites.
Analyze the parameters of wave propagation and calculate link budget.
Evaluate the performance of various Satellite and Radar systems.

units.title: Satellite Communication
units.text: Satellite Communication: General background, basic satellite system, frequency allocations for satellite services, types of satellite, system design considerations, and applications.

units.title: Satellite Orbits
units.text: Satellite Orbits: Types of Orbits and their applications, Orbital Mechanics: Developing the equations of the orbit, Kepler’s three laws of planetary motion, describing the orbit of a satellite, locating the satellite in the orbit, locating the satellite with respect to the Earth, orbital elements, look angle determination, orbital perturbations, launching techniques and launch vehicle, orbital effects in communications systems performance.

units.title: Wave Propagation And Link Design
units.text: Wave Propagation And Link Design: Introduction, atmospheric losses, ionospheric effects, rain attenuation, other impairments, antenna polarization, polarization of satellite signals, cross polarization discrimination, ionospheric depolarization, rain depolarization, ice depolarization. Transmission losses, link power budget equation, system noise temperature, carrier to noise ratio for uplink and down link, combined uplink and downlink carrier to noise ratio, inter modulation noise.

units.title: Satellite Subsystems
units.text: Satellite Subsystems: Attitude and orbit control system, Telemetry, tracking command and monitoring system, power system, communication system: Single and double conversion transponder, satellite antennas, Equipment reliability and space qualification.

units.title: Satellite Services
units.text: Satellite Services: Introduction to Satellite Mobile Services, MIMO systems, Multiple antenna based satellite communication, Hybrid satellite‐terrestrial communication system. Very small aperture terminal (VSAT) systems: Network architectures, RadarSat. Direct broadcast satellite (DBS) TV: C-Band and Ku-Band Home Satellite TV, Digital DBS TV, DBS-TV receiving antennas, DBS-TV receiver, Installation of DBS-TV antennas, Low noise block converter (LNBC).

units.title: Satellite Navigation
units.text: Satellite Navigation: Global positioning systems (GPS): GPS position location principles, GPS segments, GPS receiver, GPS signal structure, Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS): Architecture and frequencies, IRNSS Receiver. GPS Aided Geo Augmented Navigation (GAGAN).

units.title: Radar System
units.text: Radar System: Introduction, Radar set, radar frequencies and radar applications. Range performance, minimum detectable signal, receiver noise, transmitter power, pulse repetition frequency, pulse duration, Radar display, Radar antenna scanning & Tracking system, Radar system losses, Radar clutters, Radar cross-section of targets: Simple Targets: Sphere, Long thin wire or Rod, flat plate and corner reflector, Cone – sphere, Effect of target shape, complex targets.

units.title: Classification Of Radar Systems
units.text: Classification Of Radar Systems: Principles, operation, performance, limitations and applications : CW radars, FMCW radar, MTI radar, Pulse Doppler radar. Introduction to Radar Applications: Synthetic Aperture radar (SAR), Phased array radar, Ground Penetrating radar (GPR), Weather radar, Tracking radar, 3D Radar, Automotive radar and Distance measuring equipment (DME).

text_books: 1. Timothy Pratt, Satellite Communication, Wiley Publication, 2nd edition, 2007. 2. M. I. Skolnik, Introduction to Radar System, Mc-Graw Hill publication, 3rd edition, 2009.
reference_books: 1. Dennis Roddy, Satellite Communication, McGraw Hill, 4th edition, 2006. 2. M Richharia, Mobile Satellite Communication – Principles and trends, Wiley, 2nd edition 2014. 3. G. Kennedy, B. Davis, S.R.M. Prasanna, Electronics communication systems, McGraw Hill Education private ltd., 6th edition, 2017. 4. http://irnss.isro.gov.in/ 5. Recent research papers on MIMO satellite and hybrid satellite‐terrestrial communication. 6. E. G. Larsson and P. Stoica, Information Theory, Space‐Time Block Coding for Wireless Communications, Cambridge University Press, 2003.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Objectives: 1. To apply concept of information theory for data compression 2. To implement channel coding techniques for correcting and detecting errors in the channel.
objectives: 1. To apply concept of information theory for data compression 2. To implement channel coding techniques for correcting and detecting errors in the channel.

outcomes.text: Understand the concept of information, entropy, Shannon’s theorem and channel capacity.
Implement and analyse various source coding techniques.
Apply various channel coding techniques for error correction and analyse their performance.

units.text: Introduction to information theory: Information, Average information, Entropy, Properties of entropy, Information Rate, Discrete memory less channel- BSC, Joint and Conditional Entropies, Mutual information, Information sources, Zero memory information source, Markov information source, Shannon’s theorem, Channel Capacity, Shannon Limit.

units.title: Source coding algorithms (Lossless compression)
units.text: Source coding algorithms (Lossless compression): Classification of codes- uniquely decodable codes, prefix codes, Kraft- McMillan inequality Shannon Fano code, Huffman code, Minimum variance Huffman code, Extended Huffman code, Adaptive Huffman code, Arithmetic codes, RLE, Golomb codes, Dictionary techniques-LZ77,LZ78, LZW, Application in Image and Text Compression

units.title: Source coding algorithms (Lossy compression)
units.text: Source coding algorithms (Lossy compression): Classification of redundancies, Fidelity criteria Transform based coding: Discrete Cosine Transform, Discrete Walsh Hadamard Transform, Discrete Wavelet Transform, Application in Image Compression-JPEG Baseline, JPEG 2000.

units.title: Channel Coding (Linear Block Codes)
units.text: Channel Coding (Linear Block Codes): Generator matrix, parity check matrix, Error detecting and correcting capability, syndrome testing, decoding, Cyclic codes: Algebraic structure, properties, encoder and decoder, Hamming codes, Introduction to BCH codes.

units.title: Channel Coding (Convolution encoding)
units.text: Channel Coding (Convolution encoding) Systematic and Non-systematic Convolutional code Encoder: State Representation and State Diagram, The Tree Diagram, The Trellis Diagram Decoding problem: Maximum Likelihood Decoding, Viterbi Decoding Algorithm, Distance Properties, code rate, coding gain Recursive Convolutional Code, Introduction to Turbo Codes.

text_books: 1. Thomas M. Cover, Joy A. Thomas, “Elements of Information Theory”, Wiley Publication, 2nd Edition, 2016 2. Ranjan Bose, “Information Theory and Coding”, McGraw Hill Publication, 3rd Edition, July 2016 3. Rafael.C. Gonzalez and Richard E. Woods, “Digital Image Processing”, Pearson Education, 4th Edition, 2019. 4. Bernard Sklar, Pabitra Kumar Ray, “Digital Communications Fundamentals and Applications”, Pearson Education, 2nd Edition, 2009
reference_books: 1. Shu Lin and D.J. Costello Jr., “Error Control Coding”, Prentice Hall, 2nd Edition, 2011. 2. Khalid Sayood, “Introduction to Data Compression”, Morgan Kaufmann, 5th Edition, 2017.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Knowledge of calculus and basic probability and statistics
objectives: 1. To provide knowledge of the basic concepts of machine learning. 2. To introduce basic theory and algorithms of machine learning to solve real-world problems.

outcomes.text: Analyze and apply different Statistical tools for Data Modelling.
Analyze and Design Simple Machine Learning applications.
To analyze and apply Regression and classification models.
To apply Supervised, Unsupervised learning algorithm for model assessment and validation.

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Machine learning, History of machine learning, Types of Machine Learning Supervised, Unsupervised and Reinforcement Learning, AI vs Machine learning, Machine Learning Vs Data Science.

units.title: Data Cleaning and Transformation
units.text: Data Cleaning and Transformation Understanding Data, Types of data, Pre-processing, Feature Extraction, Feature Scaling: Min-Max, Log scaling, Standardization, Mean normalization.

units.title: Linear and Logistic Regression
units.text: Linear and Logistic Regression: Model representation, Hypothesis Function, Simple Linear Regression Multiple Linear Regression, Cost Function, Gradient Descent algorithm, Over fitting, Under fitting. Mean Square Error and R squared value. Logistic Regression Algorithm, Model representation, Hypothesis Function, Decision Boundary, Cost Function, Gradient Descent Algorithm. Multiclass Classification: One vs All,

units.title: Supervised Machine Learning Classifiers
units.text: Supervised Machine Learning Classifiers Linear discriminant analysis (LDA), Decision tree, Random Forest, Naïve Bayes, XgBoost, Adaboost Algorithm for classification, Confusion matrix, Evaluation metrics like Accuracy, Precision, FDR, ROC, AUC, Mathew correlation coefficient, and Youden’s index

units.title: Multilayer (Neuron/Perceptron) Network and Support Vector
units.text: Multilayer (Neuron/Perceptron) Network and Support Vector Machine: Model Representation, Network Training: Feed Forward Algorithm, Error Back Propagation algorithm, Model Selection, Bias -Variance Trade off, Catalysts for Overfitting, Algorithm Optimization SVM: Maximum Margin Classification, hyperplane design, Lagrange Duality, Kernels, Penalization method, Function Estimation.

units.title: Unsupervised Learning
units.text: Unsupervised Learning: Introduction, K-mean Clustering, hierarchical clustering,DBSCAN clustering, K-Nearest Neighbor Classifier, Dimension Reduction: Principal Component Analysis, Maximum Variance Formulation, Application of PCA

units.title: Application of Machine Learning
units.text: Application of Machine Learning: Applications of supervise and unsupervised machine learning algorithm in the field of Biomedical, Economics and Telecommunication Domain

text_books: 1. Alpaydin Ethem, “Introduction to Machine Learning”, MIT Press, 4th Edition, 2020 2. Andreas C. Müller and Sarah Guido, “Introduction to Machine Learning with Python”, O'Reilly Media, 2nd Edition, 2018
reference_books: 1. Aurelien Geron, “Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow:”, O'Reilly Media, Inc, 2nd Edition ,2019 2. Christopher M. Bishop, “Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning” Springer publication, 2nd Edition, 2017.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
objectives: 1. To develop the concepts associated with the understanding of energy storage system. 2. To be able to understand the classification and applications of energy storage system.

outcomes.text: Remember the historical perspective and technical methods of energy storage system.
Compare the different types of energy storage system.
Understand the basics of electrical and electrochemical energy storage system.
Analyze the performance factors of energy storage systems.

units.title: Energy Storage Through the Ages
units.text: Energy Storage Through the Ages: Renewable Energy Before the Industrial Revolution, Wood, Peat, and Energy Crops—Using Stored Solar Energy, Fossil Energy in the Fossil Age, Use and Emissions of Fossil Energy: Status Quo, Transitioning to an Age of Renewables.

units.title: Definition and Classification of Energy Storage Systems
units.text: Definition and Classification of Energy Storage Systems: Energy storage definition and application, The Use of Storage Systems, Classification of Storage Systems, Calculation of Relevant (power & energy) parameters, Economic Classification.

units.title: Electrical Energy Storage
units.text: Electrical Energy Storage: Supercapacitors, Fundamental Features of a Capacitor, Charging and Discharging, Losses, Efficiency, and Other Characteristic Values, Service Life, Application. Superconducting Electromagnetic-Energy Storage Systems: Principles of Superconduction, Superconducting Electromagnetic Energy Storage (SMES) System, Applications.

units.title: Electrochemical Energy Storage Systems
units.text: Electrochemical Energy Storage Systems: Basic Physical Principles, Energy Storage Parameters, Lead-Acid Batteries, Charging Lead Batteries, Aging Mechanisms, Nickel Batteries, Nickel-Cadmium Batteries, Nickel Metal Hydride Batteries, Lithium Batteries, Energy Density, Power Density, and Efficiency

units.title: Mechanical Energy Storage
units.text: Mechanical Energy Storage: Compressed Air Energy Storage Power Plants, Compressed Air Energy Storage Volumes, Pumped-Storage Plants, Flywheel Storage Facilities, Flywheel Designs, Mechanical Stored Energy Systems, Applications.

units.title: Comparison of Storage Systems
units.text: Comparison of Storage Systems: Load-Management, Comparison of Costs, Efficiency Levels and Energy Densities, Strengths and Weaknesses of the Various Technologies, Future Potential and Public Acceptance of Energy Storage Systems.

text_books: 1. Michael Sterner, Ingo Stadler, Handbook of Energy Storage: Demand, Technologies, Integration, Springer-Verlag Berlin Heidelberg, 1st Edition, 2019 2. Detlef Stolten,“Hydrogen and Fuel Cells: Fundamentals, Technologies and Applications”, Wiley, 3rd Edition, 2010. 3. Jiujun Zhang, Lei Zhang, Hansan Liu, Andy Sun, Ru-Shi Liu, Electrochemical Technologies for Energy Storage and Conversion, John Wiley and Sons, 2nd Eedition, 2012.
reference_books: 1. Francois Beguin and Elzbieta Frackowiak, Super capacitors, Wiley, 1st Edition, 2013. 2. Doughty Liaw, Narayan and Srinivasan, Batteries for Renewable Energy Storage, The Electrochemical Society, New Jersy, 2010.

course_name: Industrial IoT Markets and Project Planning
program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
objectives: 1. To understand the IIoT perspective in thinking and building solutions 2. To learn and introduce the tools and techniques that enable IIoT solutions.

outcomes.text: Understand IOT, IIOT and project planning.
Develop off the shelf hardware and software components used in IIoT.
Understand various IIoT layers, platforms, security and privacy.
Design concepts of design thinking, project planning, networking and implementation of IIoT applications.

units.title: Introduction of Industrial IoT (IIoT) and project planning
units.text: Introduction of Industrial IoT (IIoT) and project planning What is industry 4.0 and factors enables IIoT, Key skill required for IIoT, Various platforms and market information on software and services, Application area: for example, Automotive, Transportation, Industrial Manufacturing, Building Automation, Oil & Gas, and Agriculture etc. Operating systems used in IIoT.

units.title: IIoT Platforms, Software and Services
units.text: IIoT Platforms, Software and Services Overview of IOT components, Various architectures of IOT and IIOT, Advantages & disadvantages, Industrial Internet - Reference Architecture; IIOT System components: Sensors, Gateways, Routers. Cloud brokers, servers and its integration, IIoT platforms and the leading suppliers of platforms. Examples such as building automation deployment and how a platform forms the "glue" that ties the entire system together. Software and services market in IIoT.

units.title: Real time Operating Systems and application areas
units.text: Real time Operating Systems and application areas RTOS used in IIoT, RTOS features and supervising control systems, Various application area such as Automotive and Transportation, Industrial Manufacturing, Building Automation, Oil & Gas and Agriculture) and considerations involved in selecting a real-time operating system for an IIoT node (think: a single board computer attached to a manufacturing machine like a lathe).

units.title: IIoT Networking
units.text: IIoT Networking Networking concepts, network functions virtualization and software defined networks. Back-end Application Designing Apache for handling HTTP Requests, PHP & MySQL for data processing, JSON lib for data processing.

units.title: IIoT Project Planning
units.text: IIoT Project Planning How to execute project, how to build the bill of material for a product, calibrate sensors and validate sensor measurement, how hard drive and sloid state drive operate, file systems and file system used for big data storage and visualization in IIoT.

text_books: 1. Ovidiu Vermesam and Peter Friess, “Internet of Things – from research and innovatin to market deployment”, River Publisher, 3rd edition, 2017. 2. Olivier Hersent, David Boswarthick, Omar Elloumi, “The Internet of Things: Key Applications and Protocols”, 2nd Edition, Wiley Publications, 2016
reference_books: 1. Hakima Chaouchi, “The Internet of Things Connecting Objects to the Web”, Wiley Publications, Wiley publication, 2013. 2. Adrian McEwen, Hakim Cassimally, “Designing the Internet of Things”, Wiley publication, 3rd edition, 2016.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
objectives: 1. To provide the basic understanding of measurement and instrumentation systems and the insight of the resistive sensors and its applications in real life. 2. To introduce the concept of the reactive sensors and self-generating sensors and its applications in real life. 3. To familiarize the characteristics, working principle and application of special purpose transducers. 4. To impart the importance of smart sensors, sensor interface standards for wearable device applications and to provide a brief overview of the wearable technology and its impact on social life

outcomes.text: Understand the basic idea of measurements, characteristics and the errors associated with measurements.
Demonstrate and realize the concept of resistive and reactive sensors to be employed for real life applications
Understand the working principle of special purpose sensors and the need for developing smart sensors.
Describe the taxonomy of the wearable devices and its design constraints for measuring physical and biological signals.

units.title: Introduction to Measurements and Sensors
units.text: Introduction to Measurements and Sensors: Functional Elements of a Measurement System and Instruments, Applications and Classification of Instruments, Types of measured Quantities, Measures of Dispersion, Sample deviation and sample mean, Units and standards, Calibration and errors . General concepts and terminology of Sensor systems, Transducers classification-sensors and actuators, General input-output configurations, Static and dynamic characteristics of measurement system.

units.title: Resistive Sensors
units.text: Resistive Sensors: Resistive sensors- Potentiometers, strain gages (piezo-resistive effect), resistive temperature detectors (RTD), thermistors, magneto-resistors, light dependent resistor (LDR), resistive hygrometers, resistive gas sensors. Wearable applications: Strain sensor for monitoring Physiological signals, body movement.

units.title: Reactive Sensors
units.text: Reactive Sensors:: Inductive sensors - variable reluctance sensors, Hall effect, Eddy current sensors, Linear variable differential transformers (LVDT), variable transformers, magneto-elastic, magneto-resistive, and magnetostrictive sensors. Capacitive sensors- variable capacitor, differential capacitor. Wearable applications: Body/textile antennas for wireless data transmission.

units.title: Self generating Sensors
units.text: Self generating Sensors:: Thermoelectric sensors, piezoelectric sensors, pyroelectric sensors, photovoltaic sensors, electrochemical sensors, Wearable applications: temperature sensitive fabric, electrochemical sensors

units.title: Mechanical transducers
units.text: Mechanical transducers: Accelerometers: Characteristics and working principle, Types- Capacitive, Piezo resistive, piezoelectric; Gyroscopes: Characteristics and working principle, Rotor Gyroscope; Diaphragm Pressure Sensor –resistive & capacitive type (micro press sensor). Wearable applications: Motion sensors for fall detection, hemiplegic and PD (Parkinson’s disease) patients.

units.title: Smart Sensors for application in wearable technology
units.text: Smart Sensors for application in wearable technology: Integrated and Smart sensors, IEEE 1451 standard & Transducer Electronic Datasheets (TEDs), Overview of various smart sensors: Digital temperature sensor (DS1621, TMP36GZ), Humidity sensor (DHT11, DHT22, FC28), IR sensor (FC51), Gas sensor (MQ2, MQ8), Pressure sensors (BMP180), Accelerometers (ADXL335), etc; Structural health monitoring sensors, Introduction to MEMS and Flexible sensors.

units.title: Scope of Wearable Devices
units.text: Scope of Wearable Devices: Role of Wearables, Attributes of Wearables, The Meta Wearables – Textiles and clothing, Social Aspects: Interpretation of Aesthetics, Adoption of Innovation, On-Body Interaction; Case Study: Google Glass, health monitoring, Wearables: Challenges and Opportunities, Future and Research Roadmap.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
objectives: 1. To study fundamentals of cloud computing fundamentals. 2. To understand the service deployed from cloud architecture. 3. To learn about specialized cloud models based on applications.

outcomes.text: Analyze the components of cloud computing.
Evaluate the deployment of web services from cloud architecture.
Learn the consistency of services deployed from a cloud architecture
Analyze case studies to derive the best practice model for developing and deploying cloud based applications.

units.title: Cloud computing fundamentals
units.text: Cloud computing fundamentals Cloud Computing definition, private, public and hybrid cloud. Cloud types; IaaS, PaaS, SaaS. Benefits and challenges of cloud computing, public vs private clouds, role of virtualization in enabling the cloud; Business Agility: Benefits and challenges to Cloud architecture. Data privacy in Cloud - Internet access security, server access security, program access security, and database security are the main security issues in the cloud. Application availability, performance, security and disaster recovery; next generation Cloud Applications.

units.title: Cloud web services
units.text: Cloud web services Technologies and the processes required when deploying web services; Deploying a web service from inside and outside a cloud architecture, advantages and disadvantages

units.title: Management of cloud services
units.text: Management of cloud services Reliability, availability and security of services deployed from the cloud. Performance and scalability of services, tools and technologies used to manage cloud services deployment. Cloud Economics: Cloud Computing infrastructures for implementing cloud based services. Economics of choosing a Cloud platform for an organization based on application requirements, economic constraints and business needs (e.g Amazon, Microsoft and Google, Salesforce, Ubuntu and Redhat)

units.title: Application development
units.text: Application development Service creation environments to develop cloud based applications. Development environments for Amazon, Azure, and Google App for service environment.

units.title: Cloud IT Models
units.text: Cloud IT Models Analysis of Case Studies when deciding to adopt cloud computing architecture. How to decide if the cloud is right for your requirements. Cloud based service, applications and development platform deployment so as to improve the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO).

text_books: 1. Gautam Shroff, “Enterprise Cloud Computing Technology Architecture Applications”, Cambridge University Press; 1st edition, 2017. 2. Toby Velte, Anthony Velte, Robert Elsenpeter, “Cloud Computing, A Practical Approach” McGraw-Hill Osborne Media; 1st edition [ISBN: 0071626948], 2015.
reference_books: 1. Dimitris N. Chorafas, “Cloud Computing Strategies” CRC Press; 1st edition [ISBN: 1439834539], 2010. 2. Thomas Erl, Zaigham Mahmood, and Ricardo Puttini, Cloud Computing Concepts, Technology & Architecture, Prentice Hall, 2013

program: B. Tech. ( EXTC )
objectives: 1. To do literature survey in the topic selected for major project. 2. To explore the feasibility of the project. 3. To design and formulate the work to be carried out in next phase.

outcomes.text: Select an appropriate problem statement.
Analyze different designing parameters.
Formulate the feasible design model. Activities to be done in phase I:
The Project group to be formed consisting of not more than 3 students.
The Project area and topic is to be selected in consultation with Project Mentors, alternatively students can propose the topics.
The Names of the students and the topic of the Project to be submitted in the first week of the semester along with Name of the Mentor.
The first phase of the project will involve Literature Survey, feasibility study, Design and Part Implementation.

Student is required to submit a 1-2 pages weekly report on the work done to the mentor. Attendance will be given on the report. There would continuous evaluation based on the weekly report submitted for 50 marks.
Report primarily containing Literature Survey, feasibility study, Design and Part Implementation is to be submitted at the end of the Semester. (Spiral Bound Report)
Presentation (about 30 minutes) of the work done during the Semester to be evaluated by External Examiner and Project Mentor. 40

program: B Tech / MBA Tech (EXTC)
objectives: The objective of this course is to introduce digital switching and signaling techniques. It provides knowledge about the transition process from traditional to broadband communication networks and explores Voice over IP.

outcomes.text: Outline the basic concepts of telephone traffic theory
Classify network synchronization and signalling techniques
Describe the voice coding techniques and different protocols used for VoIP
Compare broadband access technologies

units.title: Telephone traffic theory
units.text: Telephone traffic theory Traffic characterization, arrival and holding time, Erlang formula and Tables, loss systems, lost calls, network blocking probabilities, delay systems, Measurement of traffic congestion, lost calls and grade of service.

units.title: Network Synchronization
units.text: Network Synchronization Need for synchronization, Methods for synchronization timing recovery (PLL), Clock instability, Elastic stores, Timing inaccuracies, Slips, Pulse stuffing. Signaling - Types of Signaling, Channel associated signaling, Common channel signaling and SS7.

units.title: Voice over IP
units.text: Voice over IP Voice digitization Multi channel PCM, Voice coding, properties of speech, waveform coding, vocoding, hybrid coding, VoIP architecture, VoIP Protocols: Resource Reservation Protocol (RSVP), Multi-Protocol Label Switching (MPLS), Real Time Protocol (RTP), Session Initiation Protocol (SIP). H.323 standard media gateway control protocol, business aspects of VoIP routes

units.title: The Basics of Broadband Technology
units.text: The Basics of Broadband Technology Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL, HDSL, RADSL, VDSL, G. Lite), Access network architecture (DSLAM), Modulation technologies (DMT), CAP.

units.title: Broadband Access Technologies
units.text: Broadband Access Technologies Cable Modem Service: Head end and regional network architecture, Cable Modem Termination System, cable Modem Termination System (CMTS), Hybrid Fiber Coax networks HFC, Cable Labs initiatives (data-over-cable Service Interface Specification (DOCSIS), Packet Cable, Cable Home), Optical Fiber-based Networks: Passive Optical Network (PON) architecture, Optical line termination, Optical network terminals, Standards (Broadband PON (BPON), Gigabit (GPON), Ethernet (EPON), Long-Range Wide-Area Network (LoRaWAN) and Narrowband IoT (NB-IoT), Comparison of broadband access techniques.

text_books: 1. Willian Flanagan, VoIP and Unified Communications: Internet Telephony and the Future Voice Network, 1st Edition, Wiley publication, 2012. 2. Leonhard Korowajczuk, LTE, WiMAX and WLAN Network Design, Optimization and Performance Analysis, 1st Edition, John Willey Publication, 2011.
reference_books: 1. Roger L. Freeman, Fundamentals of Telecommunication, 2nd Edition, John Wiley and Sons, Inc., Publication, 2013. 2. William Stalling, ISDN and Broadband ISDN with Frame Relay and ATM, 4th Edition, Pearson education Asia publication, 2002. 3. Ray Horak, Telecommunications and Data Communications Handbook, 2nd Edition, John Wiley and Sons, Inc., Publication, 2008
lab_work: 8 to 10 practical exercises (and a practicum) based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech (EXTC)
prerequisites: Basic Engineering Mathematics, Control System Engineering.
objectives: The primary purpose of this course is to impart knowledge about industrial robots for their control and design. It also helps to develop an automated system using sensors, hydraulics, pneumatics and programmable logic controllers.

outcomes.text: Classify various robots using direct and inverse kinematic analysis
Make use of image processing algorithms for representation of robotic tool movement
Explain various sensors, actuators, and hydraulic, pneumatic and PLC components used in automation
Design automated systems for simple tasks

units.title: Introduction to Robotics
units.text: Introduction to Robotics Automation and robots, classification, application, specification.

units.title: Direct and Inverse Kinematics
units.text: Direct and Inverse Kinematics Co-ordinate frames, rotations, Homogeneous Coordinates, Link co-ordinates, Arm equation (3 and 4 axes robots), General properties of inverse kinematic solution, Tool configuration, Inverse kinematics of three axis, four axis robots.

units.title: Robot Vision
units.text: Robot Vision Image representation and analysis, Template matching, Polyhedral objects, shape analysis and segmentation with basic applications.

units.title: Introduction to automation
units.text: Introduction to automation Principles and strategies of automation, Basic elements of an automation system, Advanced automation functions, Levels of automation.

units.title: Sensor and Actuation Systems
units.text: Sensor and Actuation Systems Types of Sensors, sensor contact and proximity, position, velocity, Electrics actuators, Transmission gears, timing belts and bearings, parameters for selection of sensors and actuators.

units.title: Introduction to Hydraulics & Pneumatic Systems
units.text: Introduction to Hydraulics & Pneumatic Systems Fundamentals and principles of Hydraulic and Pneumatic system, components used in hydraulic and Pneumatic systems (pump, valves, etc.), Basic hydraulics circuits and Electro hydraulics, practical examples based on simple automation tasks.

units.title: PLC
units.text: PLC Introduction to Automation technology and Programming languages (Ladder Diagram), interface I/O modules with PLC, design of logic gates using Ladder diagram.

text_books: 1. Dale R. Patrick and Stephen Fardo, Industrial Process Control System, 2nd Edition, River Publication, 2019. 2. Robert Schilling, Fundamentals of Robotics Analysis and Control, 1st Edition, Person India, 2015.
reference_books: 1. John J Craig, Introduction to Robotics: Mechanics & Control, 4th Edition, Pearson Education India, 2017. 2. Johnson Curtis, Process Control Instrumentation Technology, 8th Edition, Prentice Hall of India, 2007.
lab_work: 8 to 10 exercises (and a practicum) based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech (Computer Engineering, EXTC, AI ) / B Tech (AI and DS )
objectives: This course is designed to cover Biometric Identification Science and Technology.

outcomes.text: Understand the importance of biometric based system
Apply Image Processing techniques in designing the Biometric based solution
Design and develop various biometric recognition systems considering their ethical responsibility
Understand the multimodal Biometric based recognition system.

units.title: Introduction to Biometrics
units.text: Introduction to Biometrics Biometric attributes, Biometric data, System overview, Privacy and its challenges, Biometric matching basics, authentication, identification.

units.title: Types of Biometrics
units.text: Types of Biometrics Biometric systems based on fingerprint recognition, Iris recognition, Face identification and localization in images, Retina recognition methods, Human identification based on gait, Speech as biometric data.

units.title: Multimodal Systems
units.text: Multimodal Systems Advantages of multimodal system, Types of multimodal system, Combination techniques: Feature level fusion, score level fusion, decision level fusion. Performance Testing and reporting, Errors in the test set, matching issues.

units.title: Biometric Performance hierarchy
units.text: Biometric Performance hierarchy The statistical basis of biometric system, hypothesis testing, The False Match, False Non-Match and Equal Error Rates, ROC curves, DET curves, Identification - CMC curve, verification, Dealing with uncertainty, Systematic Errors, Sampling Errors, Confidence Interval Interpretation, Computing Confidence Intervals, Parametric Techniques, Non-parametric Bootstrapping, Statistical measures of Biometrics, Comparison of privacy factor in different biometrics technologies.

units.title: Biometrics for Network Security Applications
units.text: Biometrics for Network Security Applications Iris Recognition, Fingerprint Recognition, Surveillance Systems.

text_books: 1. Ted Dunstone and Neil Yager, Biometric System and Data Analysis: Design, Evaluation, and data Mining, Springer,2009. 2. R. M. Bolle, J. H. Connell, S. Pankanti, N. K. Ratha, and A. W. Senoir, Guide to Biometrics, Springer,2006.
reference_books: 1. A. K. Jain, R. Bolle and S. Pankanti, Personal Identification in Networked society, Kluwer Academic Publishers,2005 2. John Vacca, Biometrics Technologies and verification Systems, Elsevier Inc Inc., 2007
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments (and a practicum where applicable) based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech/MBA Tech Artificial Intelligence, Computer Engineering, Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering) B Tech (AI and DS)
objectives: This course introduces concepts in cryptography and computer security and discusses both their theoretical foundations and practical applications. It also provides fundamental knowledge on various aspects of network and system Security

outcomes.text: Explain and analyze symmetric key encryption and decryption
Use asymmetric key cryptography for data encryption
Describe various techniques of network security
Discuss various system security mechanisms

units.title: Introduction of Data Encryption
units.text: Introduction of Data Encryption Need for Data encryption, Goal of Security: confidentiality, integrity, authentication, Security attacks: Active, Passive attacks, Cryptanalytic and non-cryptanalytic. Classical techniques: Substitution ciphers, Transposition ciphers, Symmetric and asymmetric encryption.

units.title: Symmetric Key encryption
units.text: Symmetric Key encryption Data Encryption Standard (DES) Structure, Key generation, Encryption and Decryption, 2-DES, triple DES, confusion and Diffusion, Avalanche attack. Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) Algebraic structures, GF(28) fields, AES structure, round functions, key expansion, Encryption and Decryption, AES Security: Avalanche attack, confusion and Diffusion Key management: Kerberos

units.title: Asymmetric Key encryption
units.text: Asymmetric Key encryption Number theory and Modular arithmetic: Primality testing Fermat's and Euler's theorems, Order of a number, Primitive roots, Euclidean and Extended Euclidean Algorithm Principles of public key cryptosystems, RSA algorithm, Diffie-Hellman key exchange

units.title: Message Integrity and message Authentication
units.text: Message Integrity and message Authentication Message authentication codes (MAC), Hash functions, SHA-512, digital

units.title: Network Security
units.text: Network Security Need for Security of Computer Networks, Transport layer security: Secure Socket Layer (SSL), IP Security: transport and tunnel modes, E-mail Security: PGP and S/MIME.

units.title: System Security
units.text: System Security Users, Trust and Trusted systems, Buffer overflow and malicious software, worms, viruses, denial of service attacks, Firewalls: construction and working principals, Intrusion detection systems, Introduction to SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) technology.

text_books: 1. William Stallings, Cryptography and Network Security, 7th edition, Pearson Publication, 2017. 2. Behrouz A. Forouzan and Debdeep Mukhopadhyay, Cryptography and Network Security, 3rd edition, Mc Graw Hill, 2015.
reference_books: 1. Wade Trappe and Lawrence C Washington, Introduction to Cryptography with Coding Theory, 3rd Edition, Pearson Education, 2020. 2. Wanbo Mao, Modern Cryptography: Theory and Practice, 4th Edition, Pearson Education, 2011.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments (and a practicum where applicable) based on the syllabus

program: B Tech/MBA Tech. (Artificial Intelligence, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering) B Tech (AI and ML)
objectives: This course focuses on the fundamentals of neural networks along with a practical perspective of advanced topics such as convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and long short-term memory with their real-world applications.

outcomes.text: Explain the fundamentals of deep learning.
Apply optimization and regularization for tuning the parameters of deep neural networks.
Build convolutional neural networks architectures for various applications.
Apply recurrent neural networks architectures for various applications.

units.title: Introduction to Deep Learning
units.text: Introduction to Deep Learning What is deep learning, motivation for using deep learning, Applications of deep learning in various domains.

units.title: Neural Networks
units.text: Neural Networks Basics of Neural network, Perceptron, Multilayer perceptron, Feedforward neural network, back-propagation, Activation functions, Loss functions, Gradient descent for neural networks.

units.title: Optimization and Regularization for Deep Learning
units.text: Optimization and Regularization for Deep Learning Stochastic GD, Mini Batch SGD, Momentum Based GD, Nesterov Accelerated GD, AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam, L1 and L2 Regularization, Early stopping, drop out.

units.title: Convolutional Neural Networks
units.text: Convolutional Neural Networks Convolution operation, pooling, striding, convolution over volume, parameters of CNN, Fully connected networks v/s CNN, Deep convolutional architectures: AlexNet, Inception Network, ResNet. Transfer learning using CNN, Applications of CNN.

units.title: Recurrent Neural Networks
units.text: Recurrent Neural Networks Vanilla RNN, Back-propagation through time, Vanishing and Exploding gradients, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Applications of RNN.

text_books: 1. Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio and Aaron Courville, Deep Learning, 1st Edition, MIT Press Book, 2017 2. Charu Agarwal, Neural Networks and Deep Learning: A Textbook, 1st Edition, Springer, 2018
reference_books: 1. François Chollet, Deep Learning with Python, 1st Edition, Manning Publication, 2017 2. Aurelien Geron, Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, 2nd Edition, O’Reilly, 2019.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments (and a practicum where applicable) / based on the syllabus
