program: B Tech (EXTC)
objectives: This course imparts fundamental knowledge of Ad hoc Networks and design issues at different layers. It also provides information about the WiFi, WiMAX standards and UWB air interface with IEEE 802.20 for IP & roaming in high-speed mobile environments.

outcomes.text: Describe the concepts, architectures and applications of Ad hoc Network
Analyse the design issues of protocols used in Ad hoc networks at MAC, network and transport layers
Compare WiFi and WiMAX standards for wireless broadband access

units.title: Introduction to Ad hoc Network
units.text: Introduction to Ad hoc Network Introduction to generations in wireless systems, Introduction to wireless/Mobile Ad-Hoc Networks (MANETs), Classification of mobile data networks, MANET issues, and Wireless channel related issues.

units.title: MAC layer issues in Ad hoc Networks
units.text: MAC layer issues in Ad hoc Networks Introduction, Issues in designing a Media Access Control (MAC) Protocol, Carrier Sense Multiple Access (CSMA) with hidden and exposed terminal issues, Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance (MACA) and Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance for Wireless (MACAW) protocols.

units.title: Network layer issues in Ad hoc Networks
units.text: Network layer issues in Ad hoc Networks Introduction to routing algorithm, Issues in designing a routing protocol for Ad hoc Networks, Table-Driven and Hybrid routing protocols, Wireless Routing Protocol – Cluster head Gateway Switch Routing Protocol (CGSR) protocols, Location aided, Hybrid protocols, Multicast protocols.

units.title: Transport Layer issues
units.text: Transport Layer issues Introduction, Issues in designing a transport layer protocol for Ad hoc Networks, data flow control mechanisms, congestion control protocols, security aspects.

units.title: Multimodal Sub-GigaHertz Communication
units.text: Multimodal Sub-GigaHertz Communication Mutimodal communication for IoT - SigFox UL, SigFox DL, NB-IoT, IEEE 802.15.4g, IEEE 802.11.ah, DASH, Multimodel communication and management.

units.title: WiMAX – IEEE 802.16 Standards
units.text: WiMAX – IEEE 802.16 Standards Various 802.16 (a to e) protocols, Worldwide Interoperability for Microwave Access (WiMAX) air interface / Physical layer, WiMAX architecture, WiMAX and WiFi Interworking, WiMAX modes - TDD and FDD, QoS in WiMAX.
UWB - Ultra Wide Band (UWB) air Interface and IEEE 802.20 (standard for mobile broadband wireless access) and beyond

program: B Tech (EXTC)
objectives: The aim of this course is to investigate brain function using mathematical tools and theories. It includes methods of neuron encoding and decoding and concept of synaptic plasticity. It also helps to comprehend the functioning of brain by creating different computational models.

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of structural and functional neuroscience
Examine the various modalities of brain research
Create descriptive, Mechanistic and Interpretative models of brain
Interpret computational models using biophysics of neurons

units.title: Introduction to Computational Neuroscience
units.text: Introduction to Computational Neuroscience What is computational neuroscience, Brain areas and their functions, Types of neurons, electrical characteristics of neuron, Synapses, challenges in brain research and Brouwer’s recommendations.

units.title: Modalities of Brain
units.text: Modalities of Brain Types of indirect and direct modality of brain research, their working principle, advantages, disadvantages. Feature extractions of EEG wave using various time domain and frequency domain transforms.

units.title: Computational Models
units.text: Computational Models To understand the functioning of brain by creating Descriptive models, Mechanistic models, Interpretative model for light and audio stimulus.

units.title: Neural encoding and decoding
units.text: Neural encoding and decoding Feature selection, Finding relevant features, Binomial spiking , Interspike interval distribution, the generalized linear model, Time rescaling theorem, neural decoding and signal detection theory, population coding and Bayesian estimation, stimulus reconstruction, Entropy and spike trains.

units.title: Neuron Modelling
units.text: Neuron Modelling Hodgkin-Huxley model of action potential (spike) generation, Equivalent circuit model of neuron, dynamics of activation and inactivation, Anatomy of spikes, forest of dendrites, Modeling the networks of neuron.

units.title: Synaptic plasticity
units.text: Synaptic plasticity Long term potentiation (LTP), Hebb’s rule, unsupervised learning of brain, sparse and predictive coding.

text_books: 1. Michael A. Arbib & James J. Bonaiuto, From Neuron to Cognition via Computational Neuroscience, MIT press, 2016. 2. Hanspeter A Mallot , Computational Neuroscience: A First Course, Springer Science & Business Media, 2013. 3. Robert H. Clewley, Fundamentals of Computational Neuroscience, Oxford press, 2009.
reference_books: 1. Britt Anderson, Computational Neuroscience and Cognitive Modelling: A Student's Introduction Methods and Procedures, Sage Publications Ltd, 2014. 2. Patricia S. Church land and Terrence J. Sejnowski, The Computational Brain, MIT press, 1992. 3. Randolph Parks, Fundamentals of Neural Network Modeling Neuropsychology and Cognitive Neuroscience (Computational Neuroscience Series, MIT press, 1999.

program: B Tech (EXTC)
objectives: This course aims to introduce the basic concepts of Next Generation Wireless Systems such as 6G and beyond, massive MIMO techniques and their limitations. It also helps to provide knowledge about Terahertz Communications and its antenna design to predict performance.

outcomes.text: Explain the evolution of next generation wireless systems
Describe massive MIMO techniques and its multi antenna systems
Elaborate on Terahertz Transceiver devices and Channel Modelling
Design and simulate Terahertz Antennas

units.title: Technology evolution of wireless communications
units.text: Technology evolution of wireless communications Introduction, Historical Background and Evolution of Wireless Systems, Application Scenarios of Next Generation Wireless Systems, Need for 6G and Beyond, Enabling Technologies of Next Generation Wireless Systems.

Massive Multiple Input Multiple Outputs (MIMO) Techniques Introduction, MIMO techniques, Multi-User MIMO Maturing, Massive MIMO, Limiting Factors of Massive MIMO, MIMO implementations, Radio Propagation and Orthogonality of Channel Responses.

units.title: Multi antenna Systems - Large-Scale MIMO and Massive MIMO
units.text: Multi antenna Systems - Large-Scale MIMO and Massive MIMO Introduction, Massive MIMO Uplink and Downlink, Spectral Efficiency (SE), Area Throughput, Precoding, Single-Cell (SC) Precoding Techniques, Precoding Techniques for the Downlink of Multicell Scenario, Hybrid Precoding, Massive MIMO with Linear Precoding and Detection, Energy Efficiency (EE).

units.title: Terahertz Transceiver and Devices
units.text: Terahertz Transceiver and Devices Terahertz communications with resonant tunneling diodes: Status and Perspectives Characterization of Emitters and Detectors. Terahertz Channel Characteristics and Modelling Fundamentals of interference modelling by stochastic geometry in THz networks, Terahertz communication channel characteristics and measurements, An overview of the Terahertz communication networks and Line-of-Sight (LOS) and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) Propagation Techniques.

units.title: Terahertz Antenna Design
units.text: Terahertz Antenna Design Advancements in Terahertz Antenna Design and Their Performance, Antenna Misalignment and Blockage in THz Communications, Hybrid Beamforming in Wireless Terahertz Communications, Ultra- Massive MIMO in THz Communications: Concepts, Challenges and Applications, Design of Passive Components for Microwave Photonics- based Millimetre Wave Systems

text_books: 1. Mohammed Usman, Mohd Wajid and Mohd Dilshad Ansari, Enabling Technologies for Next Generation Wireless Communications, 1st Edition, CRC press, 2021. 2. Saim Ghafoor, Mubhasir Husain, and Alan Davy, Next Generation Wireless Terahertz Communication Networks, CRC Press, 2021.
reference_books: 1. Neill Wilkinson, Next Generation Networks Services, Technologies and Strategies, 3rd Edition, Wiley Publications, 2002.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Digital Signal Processing , Probability and Stochastic Processes
objectives: 1. To understand the need and applications of Adaptive signal Processing 2. To study and develop FIR, LMS, RLS filters

outcomes.text: Understand the need for adaptive filtering
Demonstrate the knowledge of FIR filters and LMS algorithm
Understand signal space and vector space concept
Develop recursive least square filters

units.text: General concept of adaptive filtering and estimation, applications and motivation. Review of probability, random variables and stationary random processes, Correlation structures, properties of correlation matrices.
Optimal FIR (Wiener) filter, Method of steepest descent, LMS algorithm (real, complex), Convergence Analysis, Weight Error Correlation Matrix, Mis-adjustment and Excess MSE

units.title: Variants of the LMS algorithm
units.text: Variants of the LMS algorithm: the sign LMS family, normalized LMS algorithm, block LMS and FFT based realization, frequency domain adaptive filters, Sub-band adaptive filtering.

Signal space concepts - Introduction to finite dimensional vectors pace theory, subspace, basis, dimension, linear operators, rank and nullity, inner product space, orthogonality, Gram- Schmidt orthogonalization, concepts of orthogonal projection, orthogonal decomposition of vector spaces. Vector space of random variables, correlation as inner product, forward and backward projections, Stochastic lattice filters, recursive updating of forward and backward prediction errors, relationship with AR modeling, joint process estimator, gradient adaptive lattice

Introduction to recursive least squares (RLS), vector space formulation of RLS estimation, pseudo-inverse of a matrix, time updating of inner products, development of RLS lattice filters, RLS transversal adaptive filters. Advanced topics: affine projection and subspace based adaptive filters, partial update algorithms, QR decomposition and systolic array.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
prerequisites: Linear Algebra, Probability and Statistic, Machine Learning
objectives: 1. This topics course aims to present the mathematical, statistical and computational challenges of building stable representations for high- dimensional data, such as images, text and data. 2. We will examine into selected topics of Deep Learning, discussing recent models from both supervised and unsupervised learning. 3. Special emphasis will be on convolutional architectures, invariance learning, and unsupervised learning.

outcomes.text: Understand the key notions of deep learning, such as learning regimes, model types, optimization and training methodologies.
Apply deep learning algorithms to real-world data and problems.
Understand and apply deep-learning frameworks to implement models and algorithms.

units.title: Application based on Deep Neural Network
units.text: Application based on Deep Neural Network Image Classification, Time Series Prediction, Language Translation, Speech Recognition.

course_name: Industrial IoT Markets and Project Planning
program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
objectives: 1. To understand the IIoT perspective in thinking and building solutions 2. To learn and introduce the tools and techniques that enable IIoT solutions.

outcomes.text: Understand IOT, IIOT and project planning.
Understand and develop off the shelf hardware and software components used in IIoT.
Understand various IIoT layers, platforms, security and privacy.
Understand and design concepts of design thinking, project planning, networking and implementation of IIoT applications.

units.title: Introduction of Industrial IoT (IIoT) and project planning
units.text: Introduction of Industrial IoT (IIoT) and project planning What is industry 4.0 and factors enables IIoT, Key skill required for IIoT, Various platforms and market information on software and services, Application area: for example, Automotive, Transportation, Industrial Manufacturing, Building Automation, Oil & Gas, and Agriculture etc. Operating systems used in IIoT.

units.title: IIoT Platforms, Software and Services
units.text: IIoT Platforms, Software and Services Overview of IOT components, Various architectures of IOT and IIOT, Advantages & disadvantages, Industrial Internet - Reference Architecture; IIOT System components: Sensors, Gateways, Routers. Cloud brokers, servers and its integration, IIoT platforms and the leading suppliers of platforms. Examples such as building automation deployment and how a platform forms the "glue" that ties the entire system together. Software and services market in IIoT.

units.title: Real time Operating Systems and application areas
units.text: Real time Operating Systems and application areas RTOS used in IIoT, RTOS features and supervising control systems, Various application area such as Automotive and Transportation, Industrial Manufacturing, Building Automation, Oil & Gas and Agriculture) and considerations involved in selecting a real-time operating system for an IIoT node (think: a single board computer attached to a manufacturing machine like a lathe).

units.title: IIoT Networking

units.title: IIoT Project Planning

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
objectives: 1. To provide the basic understanding of measurement and instrumentation systems and the insight of the resistive sensors and its applications in real life. 2. To introduce the concept of the reactive sensors and self-generating sensors and its applications in real life. 3. To familiarize the characteristics, working principle and application of special purpose transducers. 4. To impart the importance of smart sensors, sensor interface standards for wearable device applications and to provide a brief overview of the wearable technology and its impact on social life

outcomes.text: Gain the basic idea of measurements, characteristics and the errors associated with measurements.
Demonstrate and realize the concept of resistive and reactive sensors to be employed for real life applications
Understand the working principle of special purpose sensors and the need for developing smart sensors.
Describe the taxonomy of the wearable devices and its design constraints for measuring physical and biological signals.

units.title: Introduction to Measurements and Sensors
units.text: Introduction to Measurements and Sensors: Functional Elements of a Measurement System and Instruments, Applications and Classification of Instruments, Types of measured Quantities, Measures of Dispersion, Sample deviation and sample mean, Units and standards, Calibration and errors . General concepts and terminology of Sensor systems, Transducers classification-sensors and actuators, General input- output configurations, Static and dynamic characteristics of measurement system.

units.title: Resistive Sensors
units.text: Resistive Sensors: Resistive sensors- Potentiometers, strain gages (piezo-resistive effect), resistive temperature detectors (RTD), thermistors, magnetoresistors, light dependent resistor (LDR), resistive hygrometers, resistive gas sensors. Wearable applications: Strain sensor for monitoring Physiological signals, body movement.

units.title: Reactive Sensors
units.text: Reactive Sensors:: Inductive sensors - variable reluctance sensors, Hall effect, Eddy current sensors, Linear variable differential transformers (LVDT), variable transformers, magneto-elastic, magneto-resistive, and magnetostrictive sensors. Capacitive sensors- variable capacitor, differential capacitor. Wearable applications: Body/textile antennas for wireless data transmission.

units.title: Self generating Sensors
units.text: Self generating Sensors:: Thermoelectric sensors, piezoelectric sensors, pyroelectric sensors, photovoltaic sensors, electrochemical sensors, Wearable applications: temperature sensitive fabric, electrochemical sensors

units.title: Mechanical transducers
units.text: Mechanical transducers: Accelerometers: Characteristics and working principle, Types- Capacitive, Piezoresistive, piezoelectric; Gyroscopes: Characteristics and working principle, Rotor Gyroscope; Diaphragm Pressure Sensor –resistive & capacitive type (micro press sensor). Wearable applications: Motion sensors for fall detection, hemiplegic and PD (Parkinson’s disease) patients.

units.title: Smart Sensors for application in wearable technology
units.text: Smart Sensors for application in wearable technology: Integrated and Smart sensors, IEEE 1451 standard & Transducer Electronic Datasheets (TEDs), Overview of various smart sensors: Digital temperature sensor (DS1621, TMP36GZ), Humidity sensor (DHT11, DHT22, FC28), IR sensor (FC51), Gas sensor (MQ2,MQ8), Pressure sensors (BMP180), Accelerometers (ADXL335), etc; Structural health monitoring sensors, Introduction to MEMSand Flexible sensors.

units.title: Scope of Wearable Devices
units.text: Scope of Wearable Devices: Role of Wearables, Attributes of Wearables, The Meta Wearables – Textiles and clothing, Social Aspects: Interpretation of Aesthetics, Adoption of Innovation, On-Body Interaction; Case Study: Google Glass, health monitoring, Wearables: Challenges and Opportunities, Future and Research Roadmap.

program: B. Tech. (EXTC)
objectives: 1. To study fundamentals of cloud computing fundamentals. 2. To understand the service deployed from cloud architecture. 3. To learn about specialized cloud models based on applications.

outcomes.text: Analyze the components of cloud computing showing how business agility in an organization can be created
Evaluate the deployment of web services from cloud architecture.
Learn the consistency of services deployed from a cloud architecture
Analyze case studies to derive the best practice model for developing and deploying cloud based applications.

units.title: Cloud computing fundamentals
units.text: Cloud computing fundamentals Cloud Computing definition, private, public and hybrid cloud. Cloud types; IaaS, PaaS, SaaS. Benefits and challenges of cloud computing, public vs private clouds, role of virtualization in enabling the cloud; Business Agility: Benefits and challenges to Cloud architecture. Data privacy in Cloud - Internet access security, server access security, program access security, and database security are the main security issues in the cloud. Application availability, performance, security and disaster recovery; next generation Cloud Applications.

units.title: Cloud applications
units.text: Cloud applications Technologies and the processes required when deploying web services; Deploying a web service from inside and outside a cloud architecture, advantages and disadvantages.

units.title: Management of cloud services
units.text: Management of cloud services Reliability, availability and security of services deployed from the cloud. Performance and scalability of services, tools and technologies used to manage cloud services deployment; Cloud Economics: Cloud Computing infrastructures available for implementing cloud based services. Economics of choosing a Cloud platform for an organization, based on application requirements, economic constraints and business needs (e.g Amazon, Microsoft and Google, Salesforce.com, Ubuntu and Redhat)

units.title: Application development
units.text: Application development Service creation environments to develop cloud based applications. Development environments for service development; Amazon, Azure, Google App.

units.title: Cloud IT Model
units.text: Cloud IT Model Analysis of Case Studies when deciding to adopt cloud computing architecture. How to decide if the cloud is right for your requirements. Cloud based service, applications and development platform deployment so as to improve the total cost of ownership (TCO).

program: B Tech (EXTC)
prerequisites: Knowledge of all core and elective courses completed till semester VII.
objectives: This course provides a culminating design experience to the final-year students’ learning with essentially required hands-on experience to ensure that they graduate with the required practical and soft skills. It aims to expose the students to the entire product development life cycle starting from literature review, feasibility study, analysis, design, development and validation so as to enhance the technical skill sets in the chosen field. The course also provides an opportunity to the students for the development of their academic skills and logical thinking, oral communication skills, teamwork and planning.

outcomes.text: Select an appropriate problem statement after reviewing the literature and identifying the research gaps.
Formulate the different use cases/feasible design model.
Implement the prototype/proof of concept, test and validate the results.
Work efficiently in a team environment. Summarize the topic into a technical report.

program: B Tech / MBA Tech (EXTC)
objectives: This course imparts fundamental knowledge of Ad hoc Networks and design issues at different layers. It also provides information about the WiFi, WiMAX standards and UWB air interface with IEEE 802.20 for IP & roaming in high-speed mobile environments.

outcomes.text: Describe the concepts, architectures and applications of Ad hoc Network
Analyse the design issues of protocols used in Ad hoc networks at MAC, network and transport layers
Compare WiFi and WiMAX standards for wireless broadband access

units.title: Introduction to Ad hoc Network
units.text: Introduction to Ad hoc Network Introduction to generations in wireless systems, Introduction to wireless/Mobile Ad-Hoc Networks (MANETs), Classification of mobile data networks, MANET issues, and Wireless channel related issues.

units.title: MAC layer issues in Ad hoc Networks
units.text: MAC layer issues in Ad hoc Networks Introduction, Issues in designing a Media Access Control (MAC) Protocol, Carrier Sense Multiple Access (CSMA) with hidden and exposed terminal issues, Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance (MACA) and Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance for Wireless (MACAW) protocols.

units.title: Network layer issues in Ad hoc Networks
units.text: Network layer issues in Ad hoc Networks Introduction to routing algorithm, Issues in designing a routing protocol for Ad hoc Networks, Table-Driven and Hybrid routing protocols, Wireless Routing Protocol – Cluster head Gateway Switch Routing Protocol (CGSR) protocols, Location aided, Hybrid protocols, Multicast protocols.

units.title: Transport Layer issues
units.text: Transport Layer issues Introduction, Issues in designing a transport layer protocol for Ad hoc Networks, data flow control mechanisms, congestion control protocols, security aspects.

units.title: Multimodal Sub-GigaHertz Communication

units.title: WiMAX – IEEE 802.16 Standards

UWB - Ultra Wide Band (UWB) air Interface and IEEE 802.20 (standard for mobile broadband wireless access) and beyond

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)
prerequisites: Computer networks, Basic programming skills, Basic electronics skills
objectives: The basic idea of the Internet of Things is that virtually every physical thing in this world can also become a computer that is connected to the Internet. When they do so they are often called smart things, because they can act smarter than things that have not been tagged. Students will gain advanced knowledge of key theories and concepts of the Internet of Things. They will acquire specialised problem-solving skills, being able to analyse and design new solutions based on Internet of Things technology.

outcomes.text: Understand typical applications of IoT
Understand IoT solution design approach
Analyze and design IoT solutions for specific problems
Understand data analytics frameworks and security concepts for IoT.

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)

program: B. Tech. (Information Technology)
prerequisites: Software Engineering, Object Oriented Analysis & Design
objectives: This course introduces concepts, metrics, and models in software quality assurance. The course covers components of software quality assurance systems before, during, and after software development. The course will include case studies and hands on experiences. Students will develop an understanding of software quality and approaches to assure software quality.

outcomes.text: Understand the quality factors
Understand and comprehend SQA architecture and its Components
Identify the Software Defects and defects removal
Evaluate on the basis of Software quality metrics and the standards

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction: Software quality challenge, software errors, faults and failures, causes of software errors, software quality and software quality assurance definition

units.title: Software quality factors
units.text: Software quality factors: Need for software quality requirements, classification of software requirements into software quality factors, product operation, revision and transition software quality factors, alternative models of software quality factors, software compliance with quality factor

units.title: Components of SQA
units.text: Components of SQA: SQA system architecture, pre project software quality components, software project lifecycle components, infrastructure components for error prevention and improvement, Management SQA components, SQA standards, system certification and assessment components, human component

units.title: Defect removal effectiveness
units.text: Defect removal effectiveness: Software development methodologies, factors affecting QA activities in development process, Verification, validation and qualification, model for SQA defect removal effectiveness and cost, reviews

units.title: Software testing
units.text: Software testing: Definition and objectives, testing process, strategies, software test classification, black box and white box, test case design, automated testing techniques & Tools, Security Testing, Alpha and Beta site testing programs

units.title: Maintenance and external participants
units.text: Maintenance and external participants: Pre maintenance software quality components, Maintenance software quality assurance tools, types of external participants, risks and benefits, assuring quality of external participants, SQA tools for assuring quality of external participants contribution

units.title: Standards
units.text: Standards: Overview of standards for interoperability, acceptability, and quality management: ISO 9001, ISO 9000- 3, CMM and CMMI, Boot strap methodology, ISO/IEC 15504 model, IEEE STD 12207, IEEE STD 1012, IEEE STD 1028, ISO 27001 standard for security

units.title: Software quality metrics
units.text: Software quality metrics: Objective and classification of software quality metrics, process metrics and product metrics, implementation and limitation of software quality metrics.

units.title: Naming

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Engineering Mechanics (BTAB01005 and BTME02004), Design of Machine Elements - I and II (BTME05003, BTME06003)
objectives:  To provide the understanding of detailed design of mechanical systems and their uses in different application under different load conditions and safety limits.  To impart knowledge of the fundamentals of design of some important mechanical systems.

outcomes.text: Understand design of pressure vessels and belt conveyor.
Design of Design of mechanical systems like pressure vessel and conveyor.
Analyze Design of main components of I C Engines.
Demonstrate basics of optimization in design.

units.title: Cylinders and pressure vessels
units.text: Cylinders and pressure vessels: Thin cylinders, thin spherical vessels. Thick cylinders and principal stresses, Lames’s, Clavarino’s and Birnie’s equations. Cylinder with external pressure, auto frottage, compound cylinders. Gasket and gasketed joints, uniform pressure vessels, end closers, openings in pressure vessels

units.title: I.C. Engine components
units.text: I.C. Engine components: Main parts of IC engine, design of piston, piston rings, piston pin, cylinder, cylinder head, connecting rod, crank shaft, end bearings and end caps, valve gear mechanism.

units.title: Design of hoisting mechanism
units.text: Design of hoisting mechanism: Design of snatch block assembly including rope selection, sheave, hook, bearing for hook, cross piece, axle for sheave and shackle plate. Design of belt conveyors: Power requirement, selection of belt, design of tension take up unit, idler pulley Optimum Design: Objectives of optimum design, optimum design of mechanical elements using differential calculus and Lagrange multiplier method, concept of adequate design. Johnson’s method: primary, subsidiary and limit equations, case of normal specifications, redundant and incompatible specifications.

text_books: 1. J. E. Shigley and C. R. Mischke (2008), “Mechanical Engineering Design”, McGraw Hill Pub. Co. Ltd. 2. V. B. Bhandari (2013), “Design of Machine Element”, McGraw Hill Education Pvt. Ltd, New Delhi.
reference_books: 1. N. C. Pandya and C. S. Shah (2006), “Machine Design” Charotar Publishing house Pvt LTD, Anand. 2. V. M. Faires (2008), “Design of Machine Element”, McMillan.

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Thermodynamics (BTME03002), Thermal Engineering (BTME05001), Heat Transfer (BTME06001)
objectives:  To impart the knowledge of working of vapour compression and vapour absorption refrigeration systems.  To provide the understanding of different processes in psychrometry used in air- conditioning, and introduce cooling load calculations  To introduce duct design methods.  To introduce the applications of refrigeration and air conditioning.

outcomes.text: Understand the working and applications of different refrigeration systems.
Understand the properties of refrigerants used for different cooling applications.
Estimate the designing criterion for Air- Conditioning systems using psychrometry.

units.title: Introduction To Refrigeration
units.text: Introduction To Refrigeration: Methods of refrigeration, Carnot refrigerator, Carnot heat pump, co- efficient of performance(COP), unit of refrigeration(TR), Energy efficiency ratio(EER) Air-craft refrigeration systems; Need for air-craft refrigeration and Simple air-cooling system.

units.title: Vapor Compression Refrigeration System
units.text: Vapor Compression Refrigeration System: Simple vapor compression cycle (VCC); T-s, h-s and p-h diagrams for VCC, COP calculation from T-s and h-s charts for different conditions, Theoretical and actual cycle, Wet versus dry compression, pressure losses and their effects on the VCC, Effect of suction and delivery pressure on VCC. Vapor compression refrigeration (VCR) systems with multiple evaporators and compressors.

units.title: Absorption Refrigeration System
units.text: Absorption Refrigeration System: Ammonia-water vapor absorption refrigeration (VAR) system. Enthalpy- concentration, analysis of the system. Lithium bromide- water absorption refrigeration system, Introduction to Electrolux refrigeration system.

units.title: Refrigerants
units.text: Refrigerants: Desirable properties of refrigerants, designation system for refrigerants, thermodynamic, chemical and physical properties, secondary refrigerants, selection of refrigerants, ODP, GWP and TEWI

units.title: Psychrometry
units.text: Psychrometry: Psychrometric properties, Dalton’s law of partial pressure, chart and processes, psychrometer, By-pass factor, Apparatus dew point temperature

units.title: Air – Conditioning
units.text: Air – Conditioning: Human comfort- Requirement of comfort air conditioning, thermodynamics of human body, effective temperature, comfort chart, comfort zone, economic considerations for selecting the comfort points Mixing process, basic processes in conditioning of air, psychrometric processes in air conditioning equipment, Different classes of air conditioning system, summer air-conditioning, winter air conditioning. Cooling load calculations.

units.title: Duct Design
units.text: Duct Design Friction chart for circular ducts. Equivalent diameter of a circular duct for rectangular ducts. Static pressure regain and equal pressure drop methods of duct design. Fans and blowers. Introduction to AHU- design/selection.

units.title: Applications of Refrigeration
units.text: Applications of Refrigeration: Food processing and preservation, typical examples of food processing by refrigeration and storage, transport refrigeration. Applications of Air Conditioning: Industrial, commercial, residential hospital requirement and transport.

text_books: 1. Arora C. P. (2006), “Refrigeration and Air Conditioning”, 2nd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill. 2. Dossat Roy J. and Horan Thomas J. (2012), “Principles of Refrigeration”, 10th Edition, Prentice Hall.
reference_books: 1. Ashrae, “Handbook: Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning Applications” (2010), American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers. 2. Prasad Manohar (2006), “Refrigeration and Air Conditioning” 2nd Edition. New Age International. 3. Ananthanarayanan P. (2005): Basic Refrigeration and air-conditioning, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Publication.

program: B. Tech.(Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Integral and Vector Calculus (BTAB01001), Differential Equations (BTME02001)
objectives:  To provide the understanding of basics of finite element methods and analysis.  To impart knowledge of one dimensional and two dimensional Finite element analysis  To introduce the applications of FEA in structural and thermal domains.

outcomes.text: Understand the basics and mathematical aspect of FEA.
Apply concept of nodes and elements on structural one dimensional and two dimensional engineering problems.
Implement FEM procedures to analyse heat conduction and fluid flow problems using a general purpose software ANSYS.

units.title: Introduction to Finite Element Analysis
units.text: Introduction to Finite Element Analysis: Introduction to FEA, history of FEM, general FEM procedures, applications of FEM in various fields, advantages and disadvantages of FEM and software packages of FEA.

units.title: Mathematical aspects of FEA
units.text: Mathematical aspects of FEA: Newton Cotes formula, Gauss quadrature formula in one and two dimensional, non-Weak form Galerkin approach, Sub domain method, finite difference method, Weak form–Rayleigh-Ritz Method.

units.title: Finite Element Types
units.text: Finite Element Types: One dimensional element such as two nodded and three nodded bars and beams, discretization, element shape, interpolation function, shape function and application of boundary conditions.

units.title: One Dimensional Problems
units.text: One Dimensional Problems: Element and global stiffness matrix, developing EME and GME for different fields like thermal, fluid etc., Discretization of domain, element equations, imposition of boundary conditions, introduction to constant strain triangle elements (CST elements).

units.title: Application to Field Problems
units.text: Application to Field Problems: Plane trusses, application with one dimensional and two dimensional heat conduction, fins and fluid flow problems.

text_books: 1. J. N. Reddy (2006), “An Introduction to the Finite Element Method”, 3rd Edition, McGraw-Hill Higher Education. 2. S. S. Rao (2005), “The Finite Element in Engineering”, 4th edition Butterworth Heinemann.
reference_books: 1. J. T. Oden and J. N. Reddy (2011), “An Introduction to the Mathematical Theory of Finite Elements”, Dover Publications, 2. P. Seshu (2010), “Textbook of FEA”, Prentice Hall. 3. S. Desai and J.F. Abel (2000), “Introduction to Finite Elements Methods”, CBS Publications.

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: All Mechanical Engineering subjects till semester VI
objectives:  To inculcate the ability to gather information for the seminar topic with presentations and report

outcomes.text: Apply the use of knowledge of basic Mechanical Engineering subjects Carry out literature review for the seminar topic
Develop presentation and communication skills

units.text: Each student will select a topic in the area of Mechanical engineering and related area in the state of art area and technical development, The topic will be decided by the student, guide and departmental research committee. Literature collection related to the topic selected by individual student. Objective should be defined before end of Semester.

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mechanics (BTAB01005 and BTME02004), Materials Engineering (BTME04004) and Design of Machine Elements – I & II (BTME05003 and BTME06003).
objectives:  To introduce the fundamental physical principles of the classical theory of friction, wear and lubrication.  To demonstrate basic understanding of friction, lubrication and wear processes  To understand the fundamental principles of high contact stresses (Hertz stresses), fatigue-failure, and Elasto-hydrodynamic (EHD) lubrication in rolling bearings and gears.

outcomes.text: Understand the principles for selecting compatible materials for minimizing friction and wear in machinery.
Understand the principles of bearing selection and bearing arrangement in machines.
Analyze the requirements for selecting bearings in machines.

units.title: Introduction to Tribology
units.text: Introduction to Tribology: Tribology in design and industry, economic considerations of tribology. Lubrication: Lubrication types, lubricants and its properties, types of additives, Lubricating oils, Sliding contact bearings, classification and comparison

units.title: Friction and wear
units.text: Friction and wear: Friction: Laws of friction, friction types and causes, friction measurement, theories of friction. Wear: Wear types, major and minor modes of wear. Theories of wear and influencing factors, control methods, wear measurements. Surface topology, characterization, integrity, surface films, temperature, load, compatibility. Friction and wear in polymers and ceramics.

units.title: Hydrostatic lubrication
units.text: Hydrostatic lubrication: Basic concepts, advantages, limitations and applications, viscous flow through rectangular slot, hydrostatic step bearing analysis and energy losses, optimum design of step bearing. Temperature rise in hydrostatic step bearing. Introduction of Hydrostatic squeeze film bearing and gas lubrication

units.title: Hydrodynamic lubrication
units.text: Hydrodynamic lubrication: Theory of hydrodynamic lubrication, mechanism of pressure development in oil film, lubrication regimes, Reynold’s equation for hydrodynamic lubrication, hydrodynamic journal bearing, analysis of journal bearing, Petroff’s equation, Sommerfeld number, bearing design parameters, hydrodynamic thrust bearing and its types.

units.title: Hydrodynamic
units.text: Hydrodynamic Thrust Bearing: Mechanism of pressure development, types of hydrodynamic thrust bearing and their analysis for pressure distribution and load carrying capacity. Basic concept of Elasto-hydrodynamic lubrication, bearing materials and properties, oil seals, shield and gaskets.

text_books: 1. G. Stachowiak (2005), “Engineering Tribology”, 3rd Edition, Elsevier Butterworth- Heinemann. 2. Bharat Bhushan (2004), “Introduction to Tribology”, John Wiley and Sons.
reference_books: 1. B. Bhushan, B.K. Gupta (2000), “Handbook of Tribology: Materials, Coatings and surface Treatments”, Krieger Publications. 2. J. Davis (2001), “Surface Engineering for Corrosion and Wear Resistance”, ASM International.

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Theory of Machines - II (BTME04006), I. C. Engine (BTME06002), Design of Machine Elements - I and II (BTME05003 and BTME06003)
objectives:  To impart the knowledge of the basics of the automobiles.  To introduce the different automobile systems like suspension, axles and steering and transmission systems in the Automobiles.  To introduce the different electrical system, charging system, starting system and electronic control module, electronic spark control, electronic fuel injector and electronic sensors in automobile

outcomes.text: Understand various engines, characteristics and selections.
Analyse the working of various parts and drive mechanism of vehicle.
Understand the electrical and electronic control systems of an automobile.

units.title: Vehicle Performance
units.text: Vehicle Performance: Types of engines used in automobiles, their characteristics and selections, resistance to motion of vehicle, air, rolling and gradiant resistances, power requirement for acceleration and tradability, selection of suitable rear axle and gear ratios.

units.title: Chassis
units.text: Chassis: Chassis layout, power plant location, types of automobiles, weight distribution stability, type of frame, materials.

units.title: Steering
units.text: Steering: Steering geometry, wheel alignment and wheel balancing, center point Steering, Ackerman and Davis steering, cornering force slip angle, scrub radius, steering conventional layout of steering system. steering systems for independent suspension, wheel wobble and shimmy, power steering. Axle: Axle material, load and stresses on front axle design, steering heads, axle bearing wheel alignment, rear axle arrangements, two speed rear axle, single, double and triple reduction rear axles. Drive line: Propeller shafts and universal joints, types and construction, different types of universal joints and constant velocity joints. Live axle and differential: Final drive, spiral, bevel, hypoid, and worm drives, Types of live axles, semi, three quarter and full floating axles, Necessity of differential, conventional and non slip differential, Trouble shooting and remedies

units.title: Suspension System
units.text: Suspension System: Objects of suspension, Basic requirements, Springs- leaf and coil spring, Air suspension and its feature, Independent suspension, Forces acting in independent suspension, sprung and un-sprung mass, pitching, rolling and bouncing, shock absorbers. Wheel and Tyres: Requirements of wheels and tyres, constructional features, Types of tyres, Inflation pressure and its importance, application to ride and stability, trouble shooting and remedies

units.title: Electrical system
units.text: Electrical system: Battery: Types of battery, lead acid, Alkline, ZEBRA, sodium sulphur and swing, ratings, charging, maintance and testing of lead acid battery Electronic Ignition System: Capacitor, Discharge ignition system, Distributor less ignition system, Direct ignition system, Hall effect pulse generator, Inductive pulse generators, constant dwell system, constant energy system. Charging system: Dynamo: Principle of operation, construction, working, Regulators, combined current and voltage regulators. Alternator: Principle of operation, construction, working, rectification from AC to DC Starting system: Requirements, various torque terms used, starter motors drives, Bendix, Follo through, Barrel, Rubber compression, compression spring, friction clutch, overrunning clutch, Dyer, starter motor solenoids and switches, glow plugs

units.title: Recent trends in Automobiles
units.text: Recent trends in Automobiles: Electronic control module (ECM), operating modes of ECM ( closed loop and open loop), Input required and output signals from ECM, electronic spark control, Air management system, Idle speed control, Multipoint fuel injection system and single point fuel injection, Electronic fuel injectors, principle of operation, construction, working and application of temperature sensors, inductive sensors. Position sensors(rotary, linear), pressure sensors, knock sensors, Hot wire and thin film air flow sensors, vertex flow/turbine sensors, optical sensor, oxygen sensors, light sensors, methanol sensors, rain sensor, New development in sensors technology

text_books: 1. K. K. Jain and Asthana (2002), “Automobile Engineering”, TTI Publications. 2. R.K. Rajput (2007), “A Text Book of Automobile Engineering”, Laxmi Publications. 3. S. Kripal (2009), “Automobile Engineering Vol I”, New Chand Jain. 4. Joseph Heitner (2017), 2 edition, “Automotive Mechanics”, McGraw Hill Education.
reference_books: 1. G. Genta, Morello (2009), “The Automotive Chassis: System Design”, Springer. 2. Society of Automotive Engineering (1997), “Automotive Engineering”. 3. D. Crolla (2009), “Automotive Engineering: Powertrain, Chassis System, Vehicle, Body”, Butterworth- Heinemann. 4. Tom Denton (2004), “Automobile Electrical and Electronics” Elsvier.

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives:  To provide the understanding of new areas of nano-materials.  To impart the knowledge of various measurement techniques for the nano- materials  To generate interest of students and introduce the students to the new areas of upcoming research

outcomes.text: Understand the basic of nanotechnology and its applications in various fields of science and engineering.
Evaluate new techniques of Nano size measurement like SEM, TEM etc.
Apply new areas of research like fuel cells, solar cells to solve engineering problems.

units.title: Basic Solid State Physics
units.text: Basic Solid State Physics: Crystal structures, size dependence of properties, semiconductors, energy bands, excitations.

units.title: Measurement of properties
units.text: Measurement of properties: particle size, TEM, SEM, STM, AFM, Spectroscopy and magnetic resonance Properties of individual nanoparticles – Metal nanocrystals, magic numbers and theoretical modeling, geometric structure, semiconducting nanoparticles, carbon nanoparticles.

Synthesis and characterization Bulk nanocrystals- synthesis methods thin film deposition, multilayers, magnetic nanoparticles, spin valve, giant and colossal magnetoresistance, ferrofluids Quantum wells, wires and dots

Carbon nanostructures, carbon molecules, carbon clusters, Carbon nanotubes: Fabrication, structure, Electrical properties, vibration properties, Mechanical properties. Application of carbon Nanotubes; Field emission and shielding, Computers, Fuel cells, Chemical sensors, Catalysis, Mechanical Reinforcement.

Organic compounds and polymers-forming and characterization, size effects, supramolecules, micelles Biological materials – biological building blocks, DNA double nanowire, genetic code, biological nanostructures (proteins, miscelles and vescilles), multilayer films, Unsteady One-dimensional Flow Two and Three-dimensional Situations Over relaxation and Under relaxation MEMS, NEMS: design, fabrication and applications. (Nanostereolithography, Plasma CVD), coating of nanoparticles.

text_books: 1. Charles P Poole Jr. and Frank J Owens (2003), “Introduction to Nanotechnology”, Wiley 2. Hari Singh Nalwa (Editor), “Nanostructured Materials and Nanotechnology” Concise Edition, Academic. 3. William A Goddard, Donald W Brenner, Sergey Edward Lyshevski, Goddard III (2012), “Handbook of Nanoscience, Engineering, and Technology”, CRC Press.
reference_books: 1. David Sellmyer and R Skomski Ed. (2006), “Advanced Magnetic Nanostructures”, Springer. 2. Gabriel O Shonaike, Suresh G Advani (2003), “Advanced Polymeric Materials” CRC Press.

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives:  To introduce aspects of project management such as formulation, planning, scheduling and control of project.  To provide with a high level overview of project management.  To impart knowledge associated with planning, budgeting, scheduling, controlling, and terminating a project.

outcomes.text: Evaluate project requirements for determining its feasibility.
Analyse the various systems involved in the projects.
Analyse resources using quantitative techniques like CPM/ PERT.

units.title: Introduction to project management
units.text: Introduction to project management: Definition, Function, evolution of project management , classification of project management in different environments
The project management systems, methodologies and systems development cycle: Scope, systems approach, project feasibility, project life cycle, the phases of systems development cycle.

units.title: Project Planning
units.text: Project Planning: Planning fundamentals, project master plan, work breakdown structure and other tools of project planning, work packages project organization structure and responsibilities, responsibility matrix.

units.title: Project Scheduling
units.text: Project Scheduling: Use of Gantt charts and network diagrams, activity of node diagrams, activity on arrow diagrams the critical path, time based networks.
PERT, CPM, Resource Allocation Introduction to Tools and techniques for scheduling development, crashing of networks, time- cost relationship, Resource leveling multiple project scheduling.

units.title: Cost Estimating and Budgeting
units.text: Cost Estimating and Budgeting: Cost estimating process elements of budgeting, Project cost accounting and management information systems, cost schedules and forecasts.

units.title: Managing Risks in Projects
units.text: Managing Risks in Projects: Risk concepts and identification, risk assessment, risk priority, risk response planning, risk management methods.

units.title: Project Control
units.text: Project Control: Information monitoring, internal and external project control, cost accounting systems for project control, control process, performance analysis, variance limits, issues in project management software (MS Projects).

units.title: Project Evaluation, Reporting and termination
units.text: Project Evaluation, Reporting and termination: Project reviews and reporting, closing the contract.

units.title: Project organization structure and integration
units.text: Project organization structure and integration :Requirement of project organizations, different structure and integration in large scale projects, roles of project manager and project team

text_books: 1. John M. Nicholas (2001), “Project Management for Business and Technology”, 2nd Edition, Pearson Education Asia. 2. Jack R Meredith, Samuel J Mantel (2000), “Project Management –A Managerial Approach”, 4th Edition, JW and Sons. References Books: 1. Norman R Howes (2001), “Modern Project Management”, Amacom. 2. Prasanna Chandra (2004), “Projects: Planning, Analysis, Selection, Implementation and Review”, 5th Edition, Tata McGraw Hill. 3. Gido and Clements (2003), “Successful Project Management”, 2nd Edition, Thomson. 4. Choudhury (2006) “Project Management”, Tata McGraw Hill.

program: B. Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Engineering Physics (BTAB01002), Engineering Thermodynamics (BTME03002) and Thermal Engineering (BTME05001)
objectives:  To provide the understanding of basics energy scenario and need for non conventional energy sources.  To make students familiarize with different non-conventional energy sources and their use.  To motivate students to work on non-conventional energy tapping techniques.

outcomes.text: Conclude the need for alternative energy sources based on an understanding of the global energy crisis.
Implement the techniques to harness non-conventional energy sources – solar, wind, geothermal, biomass, ocean and chemical.
Develop the working of devices such as solar heaters, photovoltaic cells, wind turbines, biogas plants and fuel cells etc.

units.title: Energy Requirement – of India and World
units.text: Energy Requirement – of India and World: Present energy scenario, conventional energy sources- World's production and reserves, India's production and reserves. Global energy crises, shortcomings and limitations to the existing energy sources, need for alternative energy sources.

units.title: Solar Energy
units.text: Solar Energy: Solar radiation- Terrestrial and extraterrestrial. Energy potential of sun, simple flat plate collector, design of liquid flat plate collector, selective coatings, Application of LFPC performance, analysis of LFPC. Concentrating collectors, solar ponds, solar distillators, solar satellite power system, solar cooker, solar air heaters, solar driers, photovoltaic direct energy conversion, solar cells, solar thermal power system, solar energy storage.

units.title: Wind Energy
units.text: Wind Energy: History, principle of wind power, Betz model, wind mills- horizontal axis and vertical axis, horizontal axis wind turbines, their components. Operation, recent developments and their site characteristics. Vertical axis- Magnus effect, Madaras and Darrieus turbine. Application of wind energy.

units.title: Geothermal Energy
units.text: Geothermal Energy: History and future, origin and types of geothermal energy regions, dry rock and hot Aquifer analysis, vapor dominated and liquid nominated geothermal systems, operational and environmental problems.

units.title: Ocean Energy
units.text: Ocean Energy: Types of ocean energy sources, Ocean temperature difference, OTEC cycles-closed and open. Comparison with normal thermal power cycles. Ocean waves-Wave motion, Energy power from waves, Wave energy Conversion devices. Tidal Power-Formation and causes of tides, power from tides, Tidal power devices.

units.title: Biomass Energy
units.text: Biomass Energy: Various forms of biomass as a potential energy source, energy plantation, Bio-fuel production processes, Biogas plants, Gassifiers, principle, construction and design of gassifiers, individual and community bio and gobar gas plants, Types of gobar gas plants.

units.title: Chemical Energy Sources
units.text: Chemical Energy Sources: Fuel cells-principle, classification, advantage and disadvantage, application and recent development

text_books: 2. John W. Twidell and Anthony D. Weir (2006), “Renewable Energy Sources”, 2nd Edition, Taylor and Francis. 3. G. D. Rai (2009), “Non-Conventional Energy Sources”, Standard Publisher.
reference_books: 1. G. N. Tiwari and M. K. Ghosal (2005), “Renewable Energy Resources: Basic Principles and Applications”, Narosa Publishing House. 2. S. P. Sukhatme, J. K. Nayak (2008), “Solar Energy - Principle of Thermal Collection and Storage”, Tata McGraw Hill. 3. P. H. Henderson (2005), “India-The Energy Sector”, Oxford university Press. 4. D. A. Ray (2000), “Industrial Energy Conservation”, Pergamon Press.

outcomes.text: To understand physical systems e.g., mechanical, electrical, thermal and fluid systems and converting them to mathematical models.
Develop the mathematical Model and evaluate the response analysis of dynamic systems that is required in Mechanical engineering.

outcomes.text: Understand the theoretical concepts of mass and stiffness matrix, conduction matrix for basic mechanical engineering continuum problems
Understand scripting for FEA on a computational platform
Develop an understanding of solving practical problems on a versatile commercially available platform

units.title: 1-D Solid Mechanics
units.text: 1-D Solid Mechanics: 1-D bars, trusses, elemental stiffness matrix, assembly, boundary conditions, penalty method, stress-strain and reaction calculations

units.title: Analysis of Flexural elements
units.text: Analysis of Flexural elements: Classical beam, elemental stiffness matrix, global stiffness matrix, analysis of frames,

units.title: 2-D Solid Mechanics

units.title: 1-D Heat Transfer
units.text: 1-D Heat Transfer: 1-D heat conduction matrix, boundary conditions, penalty method, 1-D fins

units.title: 2-D Heat Transfer
units.text: 2-D Heat Transfer: Triangular heat elements, 2-D heat conduction matrix, boundary conditions, penalty method, 2-D fins

units.title: Structural Dynamics

objectives: To inculcate the ability to gather relevant information and evaluate the feasibility of the project presenting it in the form of report.

outcomes.text: Apply knowledge of Mechanical Engineering for problem identification.
Analyze literature for feasibility study of the topic chosen.
Develop and evaluate solutions for defined problem. Present the proposed methodology with report.

program: B.Tech.(Mechanical)
prerequisites: Fluid Mechanics (BTME04010), Mathematics-I & II (BTME01001& BTME02008), Physics (BTME01003)
objectives:  To provide understanding of working principles of fluid machines  To impart the knowledge of characteristics of the components of fluid machines  To introduce hydrostatic and hydrokinetic systems

outcomes.text: Understand and articulate the working and governing of different types of fluid machineries.
Evaluate hydraulic turbines and pumps, in terms of design parameters and performance characteristics. Applying similarity methods to predict the performance of the hydraulic turbines and pumps.

units.title: Principles of hydraulic machines
units.text: Principles of hydraulic machines: Impacts of jet on flat plate and cured vanes, elements of a hydro power plant, types of heads and efficiencies. Theory of impulse and reaction machines, Euler’s energy equation applied to a turbine and pump, velocity triangles, expression for work done.

units.title: Impulse Turbine
units.text: Impulse Turbine: Pelton Turbine: Components of a Pelton turbine, velocity triangles speed ratio, jet ratio, estimation of various parameters like head, discharge, and efficiency etc., determination of number of buckets. Performance curves, governing of turbine.

units.title: Reaction Turbines
units.text: Reaction Turbines: Types of reaction turbines - inward and outward flow, radial mixed and axial; elements of the turbine, estimation of various parameters, draft tubes. Francis Turbine – velocity triangles construction, working and performance, Kaplan Turbine – velocity triangles construction, working and performance, governing of turbine.

units.title: Similarity
units.text: Similarity: Similarity relations in turbines, definition of unit quantities and specific quantities

units.title: Pumps
units.text: Pumps: Introduction, Classification of pumps - positive displacement and non - positive displacement.

units.title: Reciprocating Pump
units.text: Reciprocating Pump: Basic theory, construction, operation, Slip, Indicator diagram. Types of reciprocating pumps, indicator diagram, use of air vessel. Rotary Pumps: Basic theory, types, construction and working, variable delivery pumps Centrifugal pumps: Basic Theory, Euler’s equation and velocity triangles, classification, construction, operation, characteristics. Priming of pumps. Series and parallel operation of pumps. Cavitations and NPSH (NPSHA, NPSHR) Other water lifting devices (Theory, Construction and operation) (a) Air lift pump. (b) Jet Pump. (c) Hydraulic Ram.

units.title: Cavitation
units.text: Cavitation: Cavitation in turbines - causes, effects and remedies, Thoma's cavitation parameter σ. Use of σ Vs specific speed graphs.

Hydrostatic systems, their function, components and application such as Hydraulic press, lift, crane and fluid drive for machine tools. Intensifier and accumulator. Hydrokinetic systems: Fluid couplings and torque converter.

text_books: 1. K. Subrmanya (2013), “Hydraulic Machines”, Tata McGraw Hill. 2. Yunus A. Cengel and John Cimbala (2008), “Fluid Mechanics”, Tata McGraw Hill, 2nd Edition.
reference_books: 1. P.N. Modi, S.M. Seth (2015), “Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics including Hydraulic Machines”, Rajsons Publications. 2. G.K. Sahu (2013), “ Pumps”, New Age International. 3. Frank M. White (2008), “Fluid Mechanics”, McGraw Hill, 6th Edition. 4. Som and Biswas (2003), “Fluid Mechanics and Machinery”, TMH Delhi. 5. Jagdish Lal (2000), “Hydraulic Machines”, Metropolitan Book Co.

course_name: Department Elective II - Mechatronic Systems Design
program: B.Tech.(Mechanical)
objectives:  To develop an understanding of the principles of a multi-disciplinary approach in the development of mechatronic systems  To develop an understanding of hydraulic, pneumatic and PLC controlled systems employed in modern manufacturing industry  To develop an understanding of control engineering concepts applied to mechatronics

outcomes.text: Understand the principles of mechatronic sensors and actuators
Demonstrate the ability to understand basic hydraulic circuits, pneumatic circuits and ladder logic diagrams
Synthesize mechatronic systems using appropriate analysis methods

units.title: Sensors & Actuators
units.text: Sensors & Actuators: Significance of sensor measurements, classification of sensors, analog vs digital sensors, sensors for displacement, acceleration, proximity sensors, ultrasonic sensors. optical sensors, linear motion drives. electrical actuators - DC Motors, stepper motors, servo motors, induction motors

units.title: Hydraulic & Pneumatic Systems
units.text: Hydraulic & Pneumatic Systems: Fundamentals of hydraulics, Pascal’s law, ISO symbols, accumulators, design of typical hydraulic circuits - regenerative circuit, meter in and meter out circuit, sequence circuit, bleed-off circuits, counter balancing circuits, sequencing circuits using electro-pneumatics and electro-hydraulics

units.title: Introduction to Control Systems
units.text: Introduction to Control Systems: Classification of control system, state feedback, mathematical modeling of control systems, transfer functions, block diagram algebra, signal flow graphs Stability analysis and Root Locus Technique: Introduction to concepts of stability, Routh and Hurwitz stability criteria, frequency response analysis, Bode plots

units.title: PID Controllers
units.text: PID Controllers: PID controllers, closed loop response of a PID controlled system

units.title: Industrial Motion Control
units.text: Industrial Motion Control: Indexing, flying shear, pick and place, motion system layout

units.title: Programmable Logic Controllers
units.text: Programmable Logic Controllers: Basic building block and function, advantages over hard-wired control, programming of PLC, Ladder logic diagram, PLC timers and counters, simple ladder logic problems.

units.title: Applications in Mechatronics
units.text: Applications in Mechatronics: Sensors for condition monitoring, mechatronic control in automated manufacturing

text_books: 1. Mechatronics: A Multidisciplinary Approach, W. Bolton, Pearson Education, 2008. 2. Introduction to Mechatronics and Measurement Systems, D. C. Alciatore and M. B. Histand, Tata McGraw-Hill, 2007.
reference_books: 1. N. Nise (2004), “Control System Engineering", John Wiley & Sons. 2. S. H. Crandall, D. C. Karnopp, E.F. Kurtz Jr. and D. C. Pridmore-Brown (1968), “Dynamics of Mechanical and Electromechanical Systems”, McGraw Hill.

program: B.Tech.(Mechanical)
prerequisites: Manufacturing Processes I and II (BTME04012 & BTME05002), Machine Drawing (BTME03011), CAD/CAM/CIM (MBME06003)
objectives: ● To acquire introductory knowledge of Additive Manufacturing (AM) and its capabilities in the modern digital manufacturing industry. ● To get acquainted with the operating principles and applications of most prominent technologies in the field of Additive Manufacturing. ● To explore the Design for Additive Manufacturing capabilities of each AM process and to identify and create complex and novel designs.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental principles of various Additive Manufacturing (AM) technologies, material requirements and cost considerations with regards to each AM process
Identify critical areas where AM can be applied to create value for the entire product life-cycle
Apply the necessary skills in selecting the right AM process for a given application
Develop an enterprising perspective concerning the application of AM in the design of a product, either entirely or partly

units.title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
units.text: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing: Introduction to AM, history of AM, definition, distinction between AM, CNC & other digital manufacturing techniques, reasons to use AM, classifications of AM processes, design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM), AM industry: present and future, AM process chain, CAD and file formats for AM.

units.title: Extrusion based AM processes
units.text: Extrusion based AM processes: Fused deposition Modelling(FDM), history of FDM, material requirements, workflow: material loading, liquefaction, bonding, solidification, support generation, nozzle dynamics, applications, benefits and limitations, post-processing, material characterization, extrusion of: ceramics, metals, biomaterials, composites, non-planer systems, contour crafting, concrete printing.

units.title: Vat Polymerization AM process
units.text: Vat Polymerization AM process: Stereolithography apparatus(SLA), history of SLA, material requirements, workflow: SLA chemistry, reaction mechanism, scan patterns, applications, benefits and limitations, other liquid polymer-based systems: solid ground curing SGC, Microstreolithography, Digital Light Processing DLP, Continuous Liquid Interface Production CLIP, Large-Scale Rapid Liquid Printing.

units.title: Sheet Lamination AM Processes
units.text: Sheet Lamination AM Processes: Laminated Object Manufacturing (LOM), LOM of paper, polymer and composite sheets, LOM mechanism: gluing, adhesive bonding, bond then from, from then bond, thermal bonding, sheet metal clamping, Ultrasonic Additive Manufacturing(UAM), ultrasonic welding fundamentals, UAM process parameters, material characterization.

units.title: Powder Bed Fusion AM Process
units.text: Powder Bed Fusion AM Process: Selective Laser Sintering (SLS): process workflow and material requirements, powder production methods, powder fusion mechanism, polymer ageing and recycling, High Speed Sintering(HSS), Multi-Jet Fusion(MJF), polymer powder characterization and selection, Selective Laser Melting (SLM): process workflow and material requirements, powder melting mechanism, melt pool dynamics, laser scan patterns, post-processing, powder production, handling and recycling, Electron Beam Melting (EBM) Process.

units.title: Binder Jetting (BJ) & Material Jetting AM Process
units.text: Binder Jetting (BJ) & Material Jetting AM Process: workflow, thermal and piezoelectric inkjet, material requirements, material jetting fluid mechanics, drop-on-demand and continuous methods of MJ, material jetting of metals, ceramics, nanomaterial, BJ AM Process: process workflow, material requirements, powder characterization for BJ process, binder-powder interaction, binder properties.

units.title: Directed Energy Deposition (DED) Processes
units.text: Directed Energy Deposition (DED) Processes: Process workflow, materials feeding for DED: powder (Laser Engineered Net Shaping) & wire, process parameters and optimization, Electron Beam Additive Manufacturing (EBAM) plasma-based DED, Cold Spray.

units.title: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM)
units.text: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM): Key process-specific DfAM guidelines, AM file formats (STL, 3MF, AMF): processing, conversion and repair algorithms, tool path generation, topology optimization, generative design, slicing and support generation.

text_books: 1. Gibson I, Rosen D W, Stucker B (2015), “Additive Manufacturing Technologies: Rapid Prototyping to Direct Digital Manufacturing”, Springer. 2. Chua, C. L., Lim, K., (2003), “Rapid Prototyping: Principles and Applications”, World Scientific Publishing Co. Pte. Ltd. Other References: 1. Yang, L., Hsu, K., Baughman, B., Godfrey, D., Medina, F., Menon, M., & Wiener, S. (2017), “Additive manufacturing of metals: the technology, materials, design and production”, Springer. 2. Gebhardt, Andreas, (2011), "Understanding additive manufacturing." Hanser Publication. 3. Bártolo, P. J. (Ed.), (2011), Stereolithography: materials, processes and applications. Springer Science & Business Media.

objectives:  To develop an understanding of linear and nonlinear differential equations and their use as equations of motion for dynamic systems  To develop an understanding of solution process using numerical integration  To develop an understanding of state space methods of analysis of dynamic systems

outcomes.text: Understand modeling of dynamic systems in diverse disciplines
Demonstrate ability to analyze dynamic systems
Synthesize dynamic systems using appropriate methods of analysis

units.title: Dynamic System Applications
units.text: Dynamic System Applications: Dynamic systems in ecology, prey- predator systems, disease modeling, Kalman filtering in finance, MEMs, resonant sensors, analog filters and amplifiers used in sound amplification, use of vibration in musical instruments, dynamic systems in robotic manipulation, 3-D printer head motion modeling

units.title: Modeling Dynamic Systems
units.text: Modeling Dynamic Systems: Degrees of freedom, Newton’s laws, single and multiple degrees of freedom, linear and nonlinear equations of motion

units.title: Solving Linear Equations of Motion
units.text: Solving Linear Equations of Motion: Solving linear differential equations using Laplace transforms, solving equations in the second order and the state space form using Laplace transforms

units.title: Solving LTV and Nonlinear Equations of Motion
units.text: Solving LTV and Nonlinear Equations of Motion: Solving nonlinear equations with small nonlinearities using perturbation, numerical solutions of time varying and general nonlinear equations of motion

units.title: Modeling and Analysis of Piecewise Linear Systems
units.text: Modeling and Analysis of Piecewise Linear Systems: Modeling of piecewise linear systems, variation of parameters formula and its application in solving PLS

units.title: Case Studies
units.text: Case Studies: Dynamic analysis and control of 3-D printer drive train, model development, control logic, control algorithm design, implementation

text_books: 1. William J. Palm, (2017), “System Dynamics”, John Wiley and Sons, 3rd Edition. 2. Jerry H. Ginsberg (1995), “Advanced Engineering Dynamics”, Cambridge University Press 2nd Edition.
reference_books: 1. N. Nise (2004), “Control System Engineering”, John Wiley & Sons. 2. S. H. Crandall, D. C. Karnopp, E.F. Kurtz Jr., and D. C. Pridmore-Brown (1968), “Dynamics of Mechanical and Electromechanical Systems”, McGraw Hill.

course_name: Department Elective II - Refrigeration and Air Conditioning
program: B.Tech.(Mechanical)
objectives:  To impart the knowledge of working of vapour compression and vapour absorption refrigeration systems  To provide the understanding of different processes in psychrometry used in air- conditioning, and introduce cooling load calculations  To introduce duct design methods  To introduce the applications of refrigeration and air conditioning

outcomes.text: Understand the working and applications of different refrigeration systems with their refrigerants
Analyze the concept of human comfort and air- conditioning systems
Estimate the designing criterion for air- conditioning systems using psychrometry

units.title: A. Introduction to Refrigeration
units.text: A. Introduction to Refrigeration: Methods of refrigeration, Carnot refrigerator, Carnot heat pump, co- efficient of performance (COP), unit of refrigeration (TR), Energy efficiency ratio (EER), Applications of Refrigeration and air- conditioning B. Refrigerants: Desirable properties of refrigerants, thermodynamic, chemical and physical properties, designation system for refrigerants, secondary refrigerants, selection of refrigerants, ODP, GWP and TEWI

units.title: A. Air Refrigeration System
units.text: A. Air Refrigeration System: Reverse Brayton cycle, Need for air-craft refrigeration, Air-craft refrigeration systems; Simple air-cooling system. B. Vapor Compression Refrigeration System: Simple vapor compression cycle (VCC); T-s, h-s and p-h diagrams for VCC, COP calculation from T-s and h-s charts for different conditions, Theoretical and actual cycle, Wet versus dry compression, pressure losses and their effects on the VCC, Effect of suction and delivery pressure on VCC. Vapor compression refrigeration (VCR) systems with multiple evaporators and compressors, cascade refrigeration system. Absorption Refrigeration System: Ammonia-water vapor absorption refrigeration (VAR) system, Electrolux refrigeration system, Lithium bromide- water absorption refrigeration system, enthalpy- concentration analysis of the system. Psychrometry: Psychrometric properties, psychrometric processes, Sling psychrometer, By-pass factor, apparatus dew point temperature, Air- washer and its applications, adiabatic mixing of air streams. Human comfort: Requirement of comfort air conditioning, thermodynamics of human body, effective temperature, comfort chart, comfort zone, economic considerations for selecting the comfort points. Air –Conditioning: RSHF, GSHF, ESHF, cooling load estimations, different classes of air conditioning system, design of summer and winter air conditioning systems. Air Distribution systems: Friction chart for circular ducts, equivalent diameter of a circular duct for rectangular ducts. Static pressure regain and equal pressure drop methods of duct design. Fans and blowers. Introduction to AHU- design/selection.

text_books: 1. Arora C. P. (2009), “Refrigeration and Air Conditioning”, Tata McGraw Hill, 3rd Edition. 2. Dossat Roy J. and Horan Thomas J. (2012), “Principles of Refrigeration”, Prentice Hall, 10th Edition.
reference_books: 1. A. V. Domkundwar and Dr. V. M. Domkundwar (2014),” Refrigeration and Air- Conditioning Data book, 2nd Edition. Dhanpat Rai and Co.(P) LTD. 2. Ashrae, “Handbook: Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning Applications” (2010), American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers. 3. Prasad Manohar (2006), “Refrigeration and Air Conditioning” 2nd Edition. New Age International. 4. Ananthanarayanan P. (2005): Basic Refrigeration and air-conditioning, 3rd Edition, Tata McGraw Hill Publication.

program: B.Tech.(Mechanical)

objectives: 1. To introduce the concept of vibration of mechanical systems. 2. To impart the knowledge of free and forced vibration. 3. To provide understanding of the concepts of natural frequency and resonance for a dynamic system.

outcomes.text: Understand the equations of motion of vibrating systems and ascertain the response of the systems along with the calculation of natural frequency
Compute vibratory response and design the systems to minimize vibration transmissibility

Apply safety and occupational health and environment in industry

Design of different types of heat exchangers like shell and tube type, plate heat exchanger, compact heat exchanger

The course covers strategic planning methods to optimize workflows, ensuring efficient and scalable factory operations.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental principles of plant layout optimization and its impact on operational efficiency.
Analyze factory throughput to identify bottlenecks and opportunities for efficiency improvement.
Evaluate the effectiveness of different automation strategies in enhancing factory performance.
Create innovative layout solutions by integrating optimization, throughput analysis, and automation principles

objectives: This course provides the understanding of key drivers of supply chain performance and their inter- relationship with strategy. This course also introduces design issues and helps students understand how information technology is used in supply chain optimization.

outcomes.text: Describe the functions of supply chain network and its process
Evaluate the various model of supply chain management
Illustrate complexity involved in supply chain analytics

units.title: Strategic Framework, Supply Chain Network and Ware house management
units.text: Strategic Framework, Supply Chain Network and Ware house management Introduction of supply chain analytics, supply chain stages, types of supply chain- horizontal and vertical, supply chain flows, process view of supply chain - cycle view and push/pull view. Role of distribution in supply chain network, factors involved in designing the distribution network, design options for a distribution network, factors influencing network design decisions. Concept of strategic storage, types of warehouses, warehouse functionality, warehouse operating principles, material handling and packaging in warehouse.

units.title: Modelling in Supply Chain Management
units.text: Modelling in Supply Chain Management Introduction, analytics framework based on SCOR model, supplier selection analytics, analytical hierarchy processing method, technique of order preference by similarity to ideal solution method (TOPSIS), VIKOR method.

units.title: Supply chain Analytics
units.text: Supply chain Analytics Demand forecasting in supply chain, Bullwhip effect and time series analysis, exponential smoothening method of forecasting, measures of forecasting errors, inventory management, safety stock and reorder level, Economic Order Quality (EOQ), multi echelon inventory management, optimum level of product availability in supply chain, predictive modeling in forecasting in supply chain.

units.title: IT in Supply Chain
units.text: IT in Supply Chain IT framework, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Internal supply chain management, Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) and transaction management, RFID systems, Lean supply chain, Reverse logistics, Green supply chain.

Select appropriate sensor for a manufacturing process
Comprehend the processing of sensor data

program: B Tech /B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: Nanotechnology has found many applications in mechanical engineering and is projected to be of greater relevance to mechanical systems in future. The main objective of the course is to expose students with emerging manufacturing techniques for producing micro and nano level products. The course is aimed at giving in-depth idea of the different techniques used in micro and nano machining/manufacturing.

outcomes.text: Relate micro and nano mechanical systems and their applications in mechanical engineering.
Demonstrate machinability studies using traditional and advanced micromachining, joining, and deposition processes.
Recognize the need and identify suitable applications of nano and micromachining in industry.

units.title: Micro and Nano Mechanical Systems
units.text: Micro and Nano Mechanical Systems An overview of micro and nano mechanical systems and their applications in Mechanical Engineering, Nano-machines, Nano-mechanics, Nano-metrology, Nano-tribology, Nano-fluidics, Nano-manufacturing

units.title: Conventional Processes
units.text: Conventional Processes: Micro-turning, Micro-drilling and Micro-milling Introduction, micro-turning, micro-drilling, micro-milling, product quality in micromachining Micro-grinding and Ultra‐Precision Processes Introduction, micro and nano-grinding, nano-grinding tools

units.title: Non‐Conventional Processes
units.text: Non‐Conventional Processes: Laser Micromachining Fundamentals of lasers, laser microfabrication, laser nanofabrication, micro-EDM, micro-ECM. Micro Forming Techniques Laser micro-bending, micro-deep drawing, and micro-extrusion

units.title: Micro and Nano Finishing Processes
units.text: Micro and Nano Finishing Processes Need for nano finishing, magnetic abrasive finishing, magnetorheological finishing, elastic emission finishing, magnetic float polishing, Ion beam finishing.

units.title: Micro Joining
units.text: Micro Joining Introduction to micro joining, challenges, micro resistance welding, ultrasonic welding, micro TIG welding.

units.title: Applications of Nano and Micromachining in Industry
