objectives: The principal objective of this course is to provide brief introduction of CFD along with analysis of heat transfer and fluid flow problems.

outcomes.text: Explain the need for modelling and simulation as well as the working of CFD software
Apply standard direct and iterative techniques to solve a system of linear algebraic equation
Analyze the heat transfer and fluid flow problems using techniques of CFD

units.text: Introduction to Modeling and Simulation Experimental and analytical approach, Modeling in engineering, scope and application of CFD, solution methodology of CFD software - preprocessing, solver, post processing. Mathematical Modeling Concept of mathematical modeling, basic conservation equation (continuity equation, momentum equation, energy Equation). Initial and boundary conditions

units.title: Discretization Methods
units.text: Discretization Methods Introduction to Finite Difference method, Finite Element method and Finite Volume method. Central, Forward and Backward difference. Von Neumann stability analysis, grid generation, uniform and non-uniform grids, structured and unstructured grids, Explicit and Implicit schemes of Finite Difference Method.

units.title: Solution Methods of Linear Algebraic Equations
units.text: Solution Methods of Linear Algebraic Equations Direct methods: Gauss elimination, Tri-diagonal Matrix Algorithm (TDMA) etc. Iterative methods: Gauss Seidel method

Application of CFD to Conductive and Convective Heat Flow Steady one- and two-dimensional conduction, unsteady one and two dimensional conduction. Steady one-dimensional and two-dimensional convection-diffusion, unsteady one and two-dimensional convection- diffusion.

units.title: Application of CFD to Incompressible Fluid Flow
units.text: Application of CFD to Incompressible Fluid Flow Stream function-vorticity method, determination of pressure for viscous flow. The SIMPLE, SIMPLER Algorithm, basic theories of turbulence, Introduction to turbulence models.

Describe some of the approximations essential in finite element solutions
Solve a heat transfer problem by the finite element method

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The objective of this course is to develop awareness and basic skills necessary for the reliable measurements and measuring instruments and impart knowledge on methods of measurement of different engineering parameters such as pressure, temperature, displacement, etc. and different metrological instruments for linear, angular, taper and surface finish measurements.

outcomes.text: Describe the measurement terminologies and the concept of generalized measurement systems.
Select sensors, devices and methods for measurement of specific parameters with required accuracy.
Analyze the impact of various factors on the measurement process.

units.title: Introduction to Measurement
units.text: Introduction to Measurement Need of measurement, Study of instruments, measurement methods, generalized measurement system & its functional elements, instrument characteristics - static & dynamic characteristics, calibration.

units.title: Temperature and Pressure Measurement
units.text: Temperature and Pressure Measurement Thermometry Overview of thermometry, thermometers, thermo-electric temperature measurement, resistance thermometry, pyrometer. Pressure Measurement Bourdon tubes, dead weight pressure gauge tester, diaphragm gauge, LVDT, Piezo-electric pressure gauge, Low vacuum gauges - McLeod gauge, thermal conductivity gauge, Pirani gauge, ionization gauge, comparison of different pressure measuring instruments.

units.title: Strain Gauges
units.text: Strain Gauges Classification, electrical strain gauge: working principle and types, gauge factor (analytical treatment), analysis of Wheatstone’s network using strain gauges, mounting of strain gauges.

units.title: Measurement Standards, Comparators and Angular Measurement
units.text: Measurement Standards, Comparators and Angular Measurement Definition and concept of metrology, measurement standards, types and sources of errors, accuracy and precision, introduction to uncertainty in measurement, Calibration Concept and procedure. Length Standards Line and end standards, slip gauges and linear measuring instruments. Angular Measurement Angle standards, sine bar, angle gauges, autocollimator, angle dekkor, optical square, taper measurement, universal bevel protractor. Interferometry Basic principles, source of light, optical flats, fringe pattern and their interpretation.

units.title: Comparators, Thread and Gear Metrology, Surface Roughness Measurement

Gear Metrology Gear profile and measurement of parameters, study of tool maker’s microscope and profile projector. Surface Roughness Measurement Surface texture, assessment of surface roughness, Tomlinson surface meter, and other surface measuring devices.

Nano Metrology Introduction to nano metrology.

objectives: This course is designed to encourage the students to apply aesthetics and ergonomics in product design. It also helps to impart knowledge on ergonomic principles to recognize, evaluate, and control work place conditions that cause or contribute to employee safety and productivity issues.

outcomes.text: Explain the basics of ergonomics and aesthetics in product design
Select aesthetic concepts such as colour code, styles controls while designing product
Apply safety and occupational health and environment in industry

Anthropometric data and its applications in ergonomic, design, limitations of anthropometric data. Case study on anthropometric data.

units.title: Aesthetic Concepts
units.text: Aesthetic Concepts Concept of unity, concept of order with variety, concept of purpose style and environment, Aesthetic expressions. Style components of style, house style, observation style in capital goods, case study.

units.title: Colour

units.text: Ergonomics and Industrial Design Introduction, general approach to the man-machine relationship, workstation design-working position and posture. An approach to industrial design, elements of design structure for industrial design in engineering applications in manufacturing systems.

units.title: Control and Displays

units.title: Safety & Occupational Health and Environment

Environmental Safety; Occupational Health – Health and Safety consideration; Personal protective Equipment

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Basic Electrical Engineering, Engineering Mechanics and Strength of Materials
objectives: This course presents an introduction to wind energy and wind turbines. It introduces the current challenges in modern wind turbine analysis, design, and development and provides a comprehensive examination of state-of-the-art technologies.

outcomes.text: Categorize various types of wind turbines and its principal components
Determine the mechanical power, types of stresses and the control parameters
Analyze the economics, effects on the environment, safety in operation and the potential hazards

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Importance of renewable, technical issues, wind farm development, wind turbine siting, new and future technologies, energy in a moving object and moving fluid, power in the wind, power absorption by a turbine, wind speed variation, force from wind, aerodynamic force, lift and drag coefficients, airfoils.

units.title: Types and Components of Wind Turbine
units.text: Types and Components of Wind Turbine Turbine classification, propeller wind turbine, The H-rotor, Darrieus turbine, Savonius rotor, mechanical components - tower, foundation, rotor, nacelle, gearbox, turbine brake, electrical components - generators, transformers and anemometer.

units.title: Propeller
units.text: Propeller Mechanical power, diagrams, mechanical power in a turbine, turbine power variation with angular speed, daily energy production by a turbine, annual energy production.

units.title: Wind Turbine Design
units.text: Wind Turbine Design Power accord with the wind speed, wind speed measurement, power calculations, output power quality and requirement, blade pitch control, turbine operating power curve, yaw control, parking brake, fault control, various operational states of a turbine, loads on the rotor, aerodynamic loads on the blade, other blade loads, vibrations, blade fatigue, blade construction.

units.title: Economics, Environmental Concerns and Safety
units.text: Economics, Environmental Concerns and Safety Fundamentals of economics, initial costs of a wind energy project, operating cost, comparison with other energy sources, cost per unit, onshore wind farms, noise, view, landscape, effects on birds, RF interference and effect on communications, offshore wind farms, effects on birds and marine animals, safety and working with wind turbines, effect of temperature and environmental changes, protection from lightning, ice forming on the blades, wind energy in urban areas, working environment, possible hazards, commonsense safety rules, standardized safety rules, and official regulations, climbing gear, minimizing the risk .

text_books: 1. Weifei Hu, Advanced Wind Turbine Technology, 1st Edition, Springer, 2018. 2. Ahmad Hemami, Wind Turbine Technology, 1st Edition, Cengage Learning, 2012.
reference_books: 1. Trevor M. Letcher, Wind Energy Engineering-A Handbook for Onshore and Offshore Wind Turbines, 1st Edition, Elsevier Inc., 2017. 2. Wei Tong, Wind Power Generation and Wind Turbine Design, 1st Edition, WIT Press, 2010.

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer
objectives: The present course aims at developing a familiarity with various types of heat exchangers, their construction and applications. Conventional methods of heat exchanger analysis; brief design methodology of typical heat exchangers.

outcomes.text: Analyze the fundamentals and design procedure of heat exchanger
Design of different types of heat exchangers like shell and tube type, plate heat exchanger, compact heat exchanger
Articulate performance enhancement of heat exchanger

units.title: Introduction to Heat Exchangers
units.text: Introduction to Heat Exchangers Background, Application, Classification, Common terminologies. Basic design methods for recuperators and regenerators: F-LMTD and effectiveness-NTU method. Forced convection correlations, pressure drop, fouling in heat exchangers.

units.title: Shell and Tube Heat Exchangers
units.text: Shell and Tube Heat Exchangers Basic design procedure, Kern method, Bell-Delaware method, stream analysis method. TEMA code.

units.title: Heat Transfer
units.text: Heat Transfer Enhancement of heat transfer, extended surface or Fin, fundamental of extended surface heat transfer, Fin tube heat exchanger

units.title: Plate Heat Exchangers
units.text: Plate Heat Exchangers Types, construction, design, application. Compact Heat Exchangers Construction, design, application.

units.title: Heat Pipes
units.text: Heat Pipes Construction, working principle, application, analysis. Special heat pipes. Thermal Design of Condensers and Evaporators, Micro/Nano Heat Transfer.

text_books: 1. R. K. Shah, Dusan P. Sekulic, Fundamentals of Heat Exchanger Design, 1st Edition, Wiley & Sons, 2003. (Classic) 2. Sadik Kakac, Hongtan Liu, Heat Exchangers: Selection, Rating, and Thermal Design, 3rd Edition, CRC Press, 2020.
reference_books: 1. John E Hesselgreaves, Compact Heat Exchangers Selection: Design and Operation, 1st Edition, Elsevier Science, 2001. (Classic) 2. Wilfried Roetzel, Xing Luo, Dezhen Chen, Design and Operation of Heat Exchangers and Their Networks, Netherlands: Elsevier Science, 2019.

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Knowledge of Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Management and Basic Manufacturing processes.
objectives: The objective of this course is to provide students with the knowledge and techniques required to improve product quality and process efficiency by identifying and measuring production process variability, which, if not successfully addressed can lead to inconsistent product quality, costly wastage, and other reliability and productivity problems.

outcomes.text: Explain quality management concepts and diagnose quality problems
Apply the tool and techniques of quality management as a means to diagnose, reduce and eliminate causes of variation
Analyze the sources of variation for improving quality and desired performance

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Fundamentals of TQM, historical developments, quality gurus, quality planning, quality statement, TQM implementation stages, leadership, vision/mission/strategy.

units.title: TQM Principles and Practices
units.text: TQM Principles and Practices Customer satisfaction, customer perception of quality, customer complaints, employee involvement, continuous process improvement, Juran Trilogy, PDSA cycle, 5S, Kaizen, DMAIC concept, Cost of Quality.

units.title: TQM Tools and Techniques
units.text: TQM Tools and Techniques Benchmarking, Quality Function Deployment, Failure Mode and Effect Analysis,

text_books: 1. D.H. Besterfield, C. Besterfield, Total Quality Management, 5th Edition, Pearson Education Asia, 2018. 2. D.C. Montgomery, Introduction to Statistical Quality Control, 8th Edition, Wiley, 2020. 3. R. Ticker, Quality Management Systems: A Practical Guide to Standards Implementation, 1st Edition, Routledge, 2019.
reference_books: 1. D. Natarajan, ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems, 1st Edition, Springer, 2017. 2. W. Lindsay, J. Evans, An Introduction to Six Sigma & Process Improvement, 5th Edition, Cengage learning, 2014.

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: This course provides the understanding of key drivers of supply chain performance and their inter- relationship with strategy. This course also introduces design issues and helps students understand how information technology is used in supply chain optimization.

outcomes.text: Describe the functions of supply chain network and its process
Evaluate the various model of supply chain management
Illustrate complexity involved in supply chain analytics

units.title: Strategic Framework, Supply Chain Network and Ware house management
units.text: Strategic Framework, Supply Chain Network and Ware house management Introduction of supply chain analytics, supply chain stages, types of supply chain- horizontal and vertical, supply chain flows, process view of supply chain - cycle view and push/pull view. Role of distribution in supply chain network, factors involved in designing the distribution network, design options for a distribution network, factors influencing network design decisions. Concept of strategic storage, types of warehouses, warehouse functionality, warehouse operating principles, material handling and packaging in warehouse.

units.title: Modelling in Supply Chain Management
units.text: Modelling in Supply Chain Management Introduction, analytics framework based on SCOR model, supplier selection analytics, analytical hierarchy processing method, technique of order preference by similarity to ideal solution method (TOPSIS), VIKOR method.

units.title: Supply chain Analytics
units.text: Supply chain Analytics Demand forecasting in supply chain, Bullwhip effect and time series analysis, exponential smoothening method of forecasting, measures of forecasting errors, inventory management, safety stock and reorder level, Economic Order Quality (EOQ), multi echelon inventory management, optimum level of product availability in supply chain, predictive modeling in forecasting in supply chain.

units.title: IT in Supply Chain
units.text: IT in Supply Chain IT framework, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Internal supply chain management, Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) and transaction management, RFID systems, Lean supply chain, Reverse logistics, Green supply chain.

text_books: 1. Sunil Chopra, Peter Meindl and D. V. Karla, Supply Chain Management Strategy, Planning and Operations, 6th Edition, Pearson Education, 2016. 2. Cecill Bozarth and Robett B. Handfield, Introduction to Operations and Supply Chain Management , 5th Edition, Pearson Education, 2018.
reference_books: 1. Robert B. Handfield, Ernest L. Nichols, Supply Chain Management, Prentice Hall PTR, 2007.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The course is aimed at imparting knowledge of role of the elements of automation in manufacturing industry.

outcomes.text: Recognize the working principle and components of an automation system
Select appropriate sensor for a manufacturing process
Comprehend the processing of sensor data

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Types of Automation , automation in production systems, principles of material handling, automated guided vehicle Systems (AGVs), conventional and automated storage systems , types of layout, flexible manufacturing systems (FMS).

units.title: Sensor working and applications
units.text: Sensor working and applications Definition, application and differentiation, roles of sensors, Construction and principle of working of sensors in automated systems for manufacturing, types and classification of sensors, type of actuators.

units.title: Principles of Selection for Manufacturing
units.text: Principles of Selection for Manufacturing Proximity Sensor, Motion Sensors, Velocity Sensor, and Pressure Sensors. Encoder-Optical, Magnetic, Inductive, Capacitive, Accelerometer –GPS, Bluetooth, Range Sensors, Magnetic Sensors and Hall Effect Sensors.

units.title: Programmable Automation
units.text: Programmable Automation Processing data from sensors, interfacing sensors with microcontroller and simple programs for basic operations, sensor selection and justification for industrial applications. Simple programs for sensors using microcontrollers. Simple circuits for Electrical control of fluid power actuators.

text_books: 1. Mikell P. Groover, Automation, Production Systems, Computer-Integrated Manufacturing, 4th Edition, Pearson India, 2016. 2. S. Vijayachitra , Transducers Engineering, 2nd Edition, Prentice Hall India, 2016. 3. Simon Monk, Programming Arduino, 2ND Edition, McGraw Hill Education, 2018.
reference_books: 1. R.K. Rajput, Robotics and Industrial Automation, 2nd Edition, S. Chand., 2014. 2. Paul P.L. Regtien, Sensors for Mechatronics, 1st Edition, Elsevier Inc., 2012. 3. D.V.S. Murty, Transducers and Instrumentation, 1st Edition, Prentice Hall India, 2012.

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: Nanotechnology has found many applications in mechanical engineering and is projected to be of greater relevance to mechanical systems in future. The main objective of the course is to expose students with emerging manufacturing techniques for producing micro and nano level products. The course is aimed at giving in-depth idea of the different techniques used in micro and nano machining/manufacturing.

outcomes.text: Relate micro and nano mechanical systems and their applications in mechanical engineering.
Demonstrate machinability studies using traditional and advanced micromachining, joining, and deposition processes.
Recognize the need and identify suitable applications of nano and micromachining in industry.

units.title: Micro and Nano Mechanical Systems
units.text: Micro and Nano Mechanical Systems An overview of micro and nano mechanical systems and their applications in Mechanical Engineering, Nano-machines, Nano-mechanics, Nano-metrology, Nano-tribology, Nano-fluidics, Nano-manufacturing

units.title: Conventional Processes
units.text: Conventional Processes: Micro-turning, Micro-drilling and Micro-milling Introduction, micro-turning, micro-drilling, micro-milling, product quality in micromachining Micro-grinding and Ultra‐Precision Processes Introduction, micro and nano-grinding, nano-grinding tools

units.title: Non‐Conventional Processes
units.text: Non‐Conventional Processes: Laser Micromachining Fundamentals of lasers, laser microfabrication, laser nanofabrication, micro-EDM, micro-ECM. Micro Forming Techniques Laser micro-bending, micro-deep drawing, and micro-extrusion

units.title: Micro and Nano Finishing Processes
units.text: Micro and Nano Finishing Processes Need for nano finishing, magnetic abrasive finishing, magnetorheological finishing, elastic emission finishing, magnetic float polishing, Ion beam finishing.

units.title: Micro Joining
units.text: Micro Joining Introduction to micro joining, challenges, micro resistance welding, ultrasonic welding, micro TIG welding.

units.title: Applications of Nano and Micromachining in Industry
units.text: Applications of Nano and Micromachining in Industry Typical machining methods, applications in optical manufacturing, semiconductor and electronics related applications, Recent advances in micro & nanofabrication

text_books: 1. V. K. Jain, Micro-manufacturing Processes, 1st Edition, CRC Press, 2012. 2. Yi Qin, Micro-manufacturing Engineering and Technology, 2nd Edition, William Andrew, 2015
reference_books: 1. Kapil Gupta, Micro and Precision Manufacturing, 1st Edition, Springer, 2018 2. N. P. Mahalik, Micromanufacturing and nanotechnology, 1st Edition, Springer, 2006 (Classic)

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Differential and Integral Calculus, Fluid Mechanics, Heat Transfer
objectives: The principal objective of this course is to provide brief introduction of CFD along with analysis of heat transfer and fluid flow problems.

outcomes.text: Explain the need for modelling and simulation as well as the working of CFD software
Apply standard direct and iterative techniques to solve a system of linear algebraic equation
Analyze the heat transfer and fluid flow problems using techniques of CFD

units.title: Introduction to Modeling and Simulation
units.text: Introduction to Modeling and Simulation Experimental and analytical approach, Modeling in engineering, scope and application of CFD, solution methodology of CFD software - preprocessing, solver, post processing. Mathematical Modeling Concept of mathematical modeling, basic conservation equation (continuity equation, momentum equation, energy Equation). Initial and boundary conditions

units.title: Discretization Methods
units.text: Discretization Methods Introduction to Finite Difference method, Finite Element method and Finite Volume method. Central, Forward and Backward difference. Von Neumann stability analysis, grid generation, uniform and non-uniform grids, structured and unstructured grids, Explicit and Implicit schemes of Finite Difference Method.

units.title: Solution Methods of Linear Algebraic Equations
units.text: Solution Methods of Linear Algebraic Equations Direct methods: Gauss elimination, Tri-diagonal Matrix Algorithm (TDMA) etc. Iterative methods: Gauss Seidel method

Application of CFD to Conductive and Convective Heat Flow Steady one- and two-dimensional conduction, unsteady one and two dimensional conduction. Steady one-dimensional and two-dimensional convection-diffusion, unsteady one and two-dimensional convection- diffusion.

units.title: Application of CFD to Incompressible Fluid Flow
units.text: Application of CFD to Incompressible Fluid Flow Stream function-vorticity method, determination of pressure for viscous flow. The SIMPLE, SIMPLER Algorithm, basic theories of turbulence, Introduction to turbulence models.

text_books: 1. J. D. Anderson, Computational Fluid Dynamics-The Basics with Applications, McGraw Hill, 2017. 2. Suhas V. Patankar, Numerical Heat Transfer Fluid Flow, Hemisphere Publishing Corporation, 2013.
reference_books: 1. P. Niyogi, M.K. Laha, S. K. Chakrabarty, Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics, Pearson Education, India, 2013. 2. T.J. Chung, Computational Fluid Dynamics, Cambridge University Press, 2014.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Mathematics I, Mathematics II, Engineering Mechanics, Strength of Materials, Heat Transfer
objectives: This course presents an introduction to the finite element methods. The guidelines for selecting displacement functions and the concepts that should be considered when modeling are discussed as the course progresses. This course describes how to treat different types of forces for two-dimensional elements and to solve one-dimensional heat transfer problems.

outcomes.text: Derive the stiffness matrix for the beam and Constant-Strain Triangular element
Describe some of the approximations essential in finite element solutions
Solve a heat transfer problem by the finite element method

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Brief history, matrix notation, general steps, applications and advantages of the FEM, computer programs for the FEM, stiffness matrix for a spring element, spring assemblage, direct stiffness method, boundary conditions.

units.title: Truss
units.text: Truss Stiffness matrix for a bar element, displacement function, transformation of vectors in two dimensions, global stiffness matrix for bar arbitrarily oriented in the plane, computation of stress for a bar in the x – y plane, solution of a plane truss, use of symmetry in structures, inclined supports.

units.title: Beam and Frame
units.text: Beam and Frame Beam stiffness, assemblage of beam stiffness matrices, direct stiffness method, distributed loading, beam element with nodal hinge, two-dimensional arbitrarily oriented beam element, rigid plane frame, skewed supports, beam element arbitrarily oriented in space, concept of substructure analysis

units.title: Plane Stress and Plane Strain
units.text: Plane Stress and Plane Strain Concepts of Plane Stress and Plane Strain, Constant-Strain Triangular Element Stiffness Matrix, Body and Surface Forces, Plane Stress Problem, Bilinear Rectangle, Comparison of Elements

units.title: Practical Considerations in Modeling
units.text: Practical Considerations in Modeling Finite Element Modeling, Equilibrium and Compatibility of Finite Element Results, Convergence of Solution and Mesh Refinement.

units.title: Heat Transfer and Mass Transport
units.text: Heat Transfer and Mass Transport Basic Differential Equation, Heat Transfer with Convection, Thermal Conductivities, Heat Transfer Coefficients, One-Dimensional and Two- Dimensional Finite Element Formulation, Line or Point Sources, One- Dimensional Heat Transfer with Mass Transport

text_books: 1. Daryl L. Logan, A First Course in the Finite Element Method, 6th Edition, Cengage Learning, 2017. 2. A. Belegundu and T. Chandrupatla, Introduction to Finite Elements in Engineering, 4th Edition, Prentice Hall, 2015.
reference_books: 1. R. D. Cook, D. S. Malkus, M. E. Plesha, R. J. Witt, Concepts and Applications of Finite Element Method 4𝑡ℎ edition, Wiley, 2007. 2. Ioannis Koutromanos, Fundamentals of Finite Element Analysis, 1st Edition, John Wiley & Sons Ltd, 2018.
lab_work: 8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

program: B Tech /MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
objectives: The objective of this course is to develop awareness and basic skills necessary for the reliable measurements and measuring instruments and impart knowledge on methods of measurement of different engineering parameters such as pressure, temperature, displacement, etc. and different metrological instruments for linear, angular, taper and surface finish measurements.

outcomes.text: Describe the measurement terminologies and the concept of generalized measurement systems.
Select sensors, devices and methods for measurement of specific parameters with required accuracy.
Analyze the impact of various factors on the measurement process.

units.title: Introduction to Measurement
units.text: Introduction to Measurement Need of measurement, Study of instruments, measurement methods, generalized measurement system & its functional elements, instrument characteristics - static & dynamic characteristics, calibration.

units.title: Temperature and Pressure Measurement
units.text: Temperature and Pressure Measurement Thermometry Overview of thermometry, thermometers, thermo-electric temperature measurement, resistance thermometry, pyrometer. Pressure Measurement Bourdon tubes, dead weight pressure gauge tester, diaphragm gauge, LVDT, Piezo-electric pressure gauge, Low vacuum gauges - McLeod gauge, thermal conductivity gauge, Pirani gauge, ionization gauge, comparison of different pressure measuring instruments.

units.title: Strain Gauges
units.text: Strain Gauges Classification, electrical strain gauge: working principle and types, gauge factor (analytical treatment), analysis of Wheatstone’s network using strain gauges, mounting of strain gauges.

units.title: Measurement Standards, Comparators and Angular Measurement
units.text: Measurement Standards, Comparators and Angular Measurement Definition and concept of metrology, measurement standards, types and sources of errors, accuracy and precision, introduction to uncertainty in measurement, Calibration Concept and procedure. Length Standards Line and end standards, slip gauges and linear measuring instruments. Angular Measurement Angle standards, sine bar, angle gauges, autocollimator, angle dekkor, optical square, taper measurement, universal bevel protractor. Interferometry Basic principles, source of light, optical flats, fringe pattern and their interpretation.

units.title: Comparators, Thread and Gear Metrology, Surface Roughness Measurement
units.text: Comparators, Thread and Gear Metrology, Surface Roughness Measurement Comparators Types, construction and working of Mechanical, Optical, Electrical, Pneumatic comparators. Screw Thread Metrology Screw thread terminology, measurement of thread parameters, study of thread gauges, floating carriage micrometer. Gear Metrology Gear profile and measurement of parameters, study of tool maker’s microscope and profile projector. Surface Roughness Measurement Surface texture, assessment of surface roughness, Tomlinson surface meter, and other surface measuring devices.

units.title: Advances in Metrology
units.text: Advances in Metrology Coordinate measuring machine (CMM) Fundamental features of CMM, role of CMMs, types of CMM and applications, types of probe. Laser Metrology Basic concepts of lasers, advantages of lasers, laser interferometers, types, applications. Machine Vision Systems Vision system measurement, multisensory systems. Nano Metrology Introduction to nano metrology.

reference_books: 1. E.O. Doebelin and D. N. Manik, Doebelin's, Measurement Systems, 6th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2010. 2. A K Bewoor and V A Kulkarni, Metrology and Measurement, 13th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2017.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Knowledge of all core and elective courses completed till 3rd year.
objectives: The capstone project is designed to provide a culminating design experience to the final-year students’ learning with essentially required hands-on experience to ensure that they graduate with the required practical and soft skills. The course aims to encourage students to think critically, solve challenging problems, do a feasibility study and develop written and oral communication skills, teamwork and planning. The students may also work in interdisciplinary areas which will help broaden their scope and learning in different domains.

outcomes.text: Select an appropriate problem statement after reviewing the literature and identifying the research gaps.
Formulate the different use cases/feasible design model.
Implement the prototype/proof of concept, test and validate the results.
Manage a team project.
Summarize the topic into a technical report.

program: B Tech/ MBA Tech (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Engineering Mechanics, Materials Engineering, Strength of Materials, Design of Machine Elements
objectives: This course is designed to impart knowledge of the principles and procedures for the design of mechanical power transmission components. It also helps to understand the standard procedure available for design of transmission of mechanical elements.

outcomes.text: Articulate the design of belt drives and selection of belt, rope and chain drives
Analyze forces to design spur gears and helical gears
Design bevel and worm gears

units.title: Bevel, Worm and Cross Helical Gears
units.text: Bevel, Worm and Cross Helical Gears Straight bevel gear: Tooth terminology, tooth forces and stresses, equivalent number of teeth. objectives: The principal objective of this course is to provide brief introduction of CFD along with analysis of heat transfer and fluid flow problems.

outcomes.text: Explain the need for modelling and simulation as well as the working of CFD software
Apply standard direct and iterative techniques to solve a system of linear algebraic equation
Analyze the heat transfer and fluid flow problems using techniques of CFD

units.title: Introduction to Modeling and Simulation
units.text: Introduction to Modeling and Simulation Experimental and analytical approach, Modeling in engineering, scope and application of CFD, solution methodology of CFD software - preprocessing, solver, post processing. program: B Tech /B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Mathematics I, Mathematics II, Engineering Mechanics, Strength of Materials, Heat Transfer
objectives: This course presents an introduction to the finite element methods. The guidelines for selecting displacement functions and the concepts that should be considered when modeling are discussed as the course progresses. This course describes how to treat different types of forces for two-dimensional elements and to solve one-dimensional heat transfer problems.

outcomes.text: Understanding the basic principles of FEA, including discretization, element types and shape functions
Derive the stiffness matrix for the beam and Constant-Strain Triangular element
Illustrate FEA characteristic equations to analyze plain stress, plain strain and derive element matrices for CST elements
Develop FEA Characteristic equations for Isoparamteric problems and heat transfer problem
Analyze solution accuracy by performing error estimation, mesh refinement studies, and convergence analysis to improve simulation reliability
Use ANSYS in real-world mechanical, thermal, and structural engineering problems to analyze their behavior

units.title: Introduction
units.text: Introduction Brief history, matrix notation, general steps, applications and advantages of the FEM, computer programs for the FEM, stiffness matrix for a spring element, spring assemblage, direct stiffness method, boundary conditions.

units.title: Truss
units.text: Truss Stiffness matrix for a bar element, displacement function, transformation of vectors in two dimensions, global stiffness matrix for bar arbitrarily oriented in the plane, computation of stress for a bar in the x – y plane, solution of a plane truss, use of symmetry in structures, inclined supports.

units.title: Beam and Frame
units.text: Beam and Frame Beam stiffness, assemblage of beam stiffness matrices, direct stiffness method, distributed loading, beam element with nodal hinge, two-dimensional arbitrarily oriented beam element, rigid plane frame, skewed supports, beam element arbitrarily oriented in space, concept of substructure analysis

units.title: Plane Stress and Plane Strain
units.text: Plane Stress and Plane Strain Concepts of Plane Stress and Plane Strain, Constant-Strain Triangular Element Stiffness Matrix, Body and Surface Forces, Plane Stress Problem, Bilinear Rectangle, Comparison of Elements

units.title: Practical Considerations in Modeling
units.text: Practical Considerations in Modeling Finite Element Modeling, Equilibrium and Compatibility of Finite Element Results, Convergence of Solution and Mesh Refinement.

units.title: Heat Transfer and Mass Transport
units.text: Heat Transfer and Mass Transport Basic Differential Equation, Heat Transfer with Convection, Thermal Conductivities, Heat Transfer Coefficients, One-Dimensional and Two- Dimensional Finite Element Formulation, Line or Point Sources, One- Dimensional Heat Transfer with Mass Transport

program: B Tech /B Tech Integrated (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: Knowledge of all core and elective courses completed till 3rd year.
objectives: The capstone project is designed to provide a culminating design experience to the final-year students’ learning with essentially required hands-on experience to ensure that they graduate with the required practical and soft skills. The course aims to encourage students to think critically, solve challenging problems, do a feasibility study and develop written and oral communication skills, teamwork and planning. The students may also work in interdisciplinary areas which will help broaden their scope and learning in different domains.

outcomes.text: Select an appropriate problem statement after reviewing the literature and identifying the research gaps
Formulate a feasible design model
Develop the prototype/proof of concept, test and validate the results
Create, work in team and apply the solution in practical way to specific problem
Summarize the major findings to compile a technical report

units.title: Spur Gears and Parallel Axis Helical Gears

units.title: Bevel, Worm and Cross Helical Gears

Estimating the dimensions of pair of straight bevel gears. Worm Gear: Merits and demerits terminology. Thermal capacity, materials-forces and stresses, efficiency, estimating the size of the worm gear pair. Cross helical: Terminology- helix angles-Estimating the size of the pair of cross helical gears.

program: B Tech (Mechanical Engineering)

objectives: This course provides a culminating design experience to the final-year students’ learning with essentially required hands-on experience to ensure that they graduate with the required practical and soft skills. It aims to expose the students to the entire product development life cycle starting from literature review, feasibility study, analysis, design, development and validation so as to enhance the technical skill sets in the chosen field. The course also provides an opportunity to the students for the development of their academic skills and logical thinking, oral communication skills, teamwork and planning.

outcomes.text: Select an appropriate problem statement after reviewing the literature and identifying the research gaps.
Formulate the different use cases/feasible design model.

prerequisites: Physics, Fundamentals of Control Systems, Microprocessor Systems and Interfacing, Industrial Drives, PLCs and Instrumentation
objectives: The main goal of the course is for the students to understand basic elements of mechatronic systems. The students learn to analyze motion control and design aspects of mechatronic systems before taking the next step to synthesize system functionality using analysis tools.

outcomes.text: Understand the design process and describe key elements of mechatronic systems
Develop and simulate block diagram models of electrical, mechanical, and fluid systems
Describe the architecture, functioning and working principles of smart sensors
Analyze and compare various types of actuators used in mechatronic systems
Design and tune controllers used for mechatronic applications

units.title: Mechatronic Design Process
units.text: Mechatronic Design Process Comparison of mechatronic system with electro-mechanical system, Integrated design issues, steps in designing mechatronic systems, Hardware in the loop simulation, Key elements of mechatronic systems. Advanced mechatronic applications: Model-based manufacturing, Supervisory control structures, and Open architecture mechatronic model.

units.title: Modelling and Simulation
units.text: Modelling and Simulation Block Diagrams, Manipulations and simulation. Block diagram modelling: Transfer function approach, Conversion from mechanical illustration, Modified analogy approach. Modelling of electrical systems, Mechanical translational systems, Mechanical rotational systems and Fluid systems.

units.title: Smart Sensors
units.text: Smart Sensors Criteria for Sensor selection in mechatronic applications, Architecture of smart sensors, Pattern recognition and classification, Biometric sensors, Architecture of CISS sensor, Interfacing CISS sensor for data acquisition and control, Sensor Noise suppression techniques.

units.title: Actuation Systems
units.text: Actuation Systems Electromagnetic actuators Solenoids, Permanent magnet DC motor, Permanent magnet stepper motor, Variable reluctance stepper motor, Applications of Brushless DC motor in mechatronic systems. Comparison between different types of motors. Fluid Power actuators Configuration of Hydraulic and Pneumatic actuation system. Non-conventional actuators Piezoelectric actuators, Magnetostrictive actuators.

units.title: Controllers
units.text: Controllers Continuous and Discrete Processes, Control modes. Principle and Configuration of On-Off controller, Proportional, Proportional Integral and Proportional Integral Derivative controller, Inverse Derivative Controller, Adaptive Controller, Model predictive controller. Use of Fuzzy logic and Neural network in controller design. Controller Tuning methods.

program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering)
objectives: The course elaborates the basic elements of robot motion with its mathematical modelling. The students learn to analyze motion control aspects of robotics before advancing to the task of synthesizing robot motion using mathematical and software tools.

Evaluate robotic simulation results using the tool configuration vector and then the equation of motion

objectives: The capstone project is designed to provide a culminating design experience to the final-year students’ learning with essentially required hands-on experience to ensure that they graduate with the required practical and soft skills. program: B Tech (Mechatronics Engineering, AI and ML, Artificial Intelligence & Computer Engineering) MBA Tech (Artificial Intelligence & Computer Engineering)
objectives: The course aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) by covering its foundational concepts and advanced applications. Students will gain insight into the historical development and evolution of RPA, along with a deep appreciation for the benefits and challenges of its implementation. By delving into RPA tools and their features, students will learn to harness workflow automation, create apps, grasp the distinctions between attended and unattended bots, and comprehend the symbiotic relationship between RPA and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

outcomes.text: Demonstrate understanding of fundamental RPA concepts, historical evolution, benefits and process analysis and selection
Analyze RPA tools, design bot workflows, and apply decision-making strategies, constructing optimized automation processes
Create user-centric app interfaces, develop integrated app functionalities aligned with RPA workflows, and deploy applications within operational frameworks
Evaluate ethical considerations, including data security and privacy, ensuring compliant RPA implementations, and making informed decisions regarding automation practices.

units.text: Advanced RPA Concepts Integrating with APIs and web services, Automating email communication and document processing, Handling unstructured data using OCR (Optical Character Recognition), Advanced error handling and recovery strategies, Using triggers and event-based automation.

program: MBA Tech./ B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)

units.text: Case Studies of Existing Smart cities of the world Like Singapore, London – UK, Barcelona etc.

units.title: Project work begins
units.text: Project work begins : Students get divided into teams, each team will study one of the ten aspects of Smart city- Transport, Infrastructure, Water Management , energy, health, hygiene & sanitation, education, governance, social & cultural fabric and disaster management: Project work begins - Briefing to students on the sub-themes and allotted projects related to any one area for an in- depth study by each team. The stage gates and timelines for the project defined along with the evaluation criteria at each deliverable. 10. Sector analysis - Project wise: Presentation of secondary research on the specific area picked up by the student teams 11. Primary Research work - Project wise: Expert interviews, focus group discussions, ethnographic study to understand the needs and aspirations of people from the future cities. 12. Ideation for Innovative concept proposals for resolving issues in Smart cities: Observation on post-it notes, Clustering, Analysis and ideation for new concept ideas 13. Initial Concept development for solutions: Students develop concepts around proposed solutions for various pain points identified in their respective domain areas 14. Feasibility Analysis of the Concepts developed: Concepts developed initially put through feasibility tests and refined subsequently 15. Exhibiting/ Presenting the Innovative solution Concepts generated

program: MBA Tech./ B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)

objectives: 1. Interpret multidisciplinary scientific bases of climatic change: basic mechanisms that govern the climate system and its responses to drivers of change 2. Analyse paleo-climatic change and assess recent historical variability to project future climate projections 3. Investigate the impact of climate change on communities of human population and global economy 4. Gain insight into legal and Financial aspects of Climate change 5. Investigate fundamentals of the fields of Geo-engineering

Investigate climate projections from the past and predict possible future climate change on Earth
Analyse how human activities are influencing Climate Change and Global Warming
Evaluate global climate change policy and its implementation, options for mitigation and adaptation
Evaluate aspects of Climate change finance

program: MBA(Tech)/ B. Tech. Mechanical Engineering
objectives: ● Acquire introductory knowledge of 3D Printing (3DP) and its capabilities in the modern digital manufacturing industry. ● To get acquainted with the operating principles and applications of most prominent technologies in the field of 3D Printing ● Explore the Design for 3D printing capabilities of each 3D printing process and to identify and create complex and novel designs.

outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental principles of various 3D Printing technologies, material requirements and cost considerations about each 3DP process.
Identify critical areas where 3DP can be applied to create value for the entire product life cycle.
Apply the necessary skills in selecting the right 3DP process for a given application.
Develop an enterprising perspective concerning the application of 3DP in the design of a product, either entirely or partly.

units.title: Introduction to 3D Printing
units.text: Introduction to 3D Printing: Introduction to 3DP, history of 3DP, definition, distinction between 3DP, AM, CNC & other digital manufacturing techniques, reasons to use 3DP, classifications of 3DP processes, design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM), 3DP industry: present and future, 3DP process chain, CAD and file formats for 3DP.

units.title: Extrusion based 3DP processes
units.text: Extrusion based 3DP processes: Fused deposition Modelling(FDM), history of FDM, material requirements, workflow: material loading, liquefaction, bonding, solidification, support generation, nozzle dynamics, applications, benefits and limitations, post-processing, material characterization, extrusion of: ceramics, metals, biomaterials, composites, non-planer systems, contour crafting, concrete printing.

units.title: Vat Polymerization 3DP process
units.text: Vat Polymerization 3DP process: Stereo lithography apparatus(SLA), history of SLA, material requirements, workflow: SLA chemistry, reaction mechanism, scan patterns, applications, benefits and limitations, other liquid polymer-based systems: solid ground curing SGC, Micro stereolithographic, Digital Light Processing DLP, Continuous Liquid Interface Production CLIP, Large-Scale Rapid Liquid Printing.

units.title: Sheet Lamination 3DP Processes
units.text: Sheet Lamination 3DP Processes: Laminated Object Manufacturing (LOM), LOM of paper, polymer and composite sheets, LOM mechanism: gluing, adhesive bonding, bond then from, from then bond, thermal bonding, sheet metal clamping, Ultrasonic Additive Manufacturing(UAM), ultrasonic welding fundamentals, UAM process parameters, material characterization.

units.title: Powder Bed Fusion 3DP Process
units.text: Powder Bed Fusion 3DP Process: Selective Laser Sintering (SLS): process workflow and material requirements, powder production methods, powder fusion mechanism, polymer ageing and recycling, High Speed Sintering(HSS), Multi-Jet Fusion(MJF), polymer powder characterization and selection, Selective Laser Melting (SLM): process workflow and material requirements, powder melting mechanism, melt pool dynamics, laser scan patterns, post-processing, powder production, handling and recycling, Electron Beam Melting (EBM) Process.

units.title: Binder Jetting (BJ) & Material Jetting 3DP Process
units.text: Binder Jetting (BJ) & Material Jetting 3DP Process: workflow, thermal and piezoelectric inkjet, material requirements, material jetting fluid mechanics, drop-on-demand and continuous methods of MJ, material jetting of metals, ceramics, nanomaterial, BJ AM Process: process workflow, material requirements, powder characterization for BJ process, binder-powder interaction, binder properties.

units.title: Directed Energy Deposition (DED) Processes
units.text: Directed Energy Deposition (DED) Processes: Process workflow, materials feeding for DED: powder (Laser Engineered Net Shaping) & wire, process parameters and optimization, Electron Beam Additive Manufacturing (EBAM) plasma-based DED, Cold Spray.

units.title: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM)
units.text: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM): Key process-specific DfAM guidelines, various AM file formats: processing, conversion and repair algorithms, tool path generation, topology optimization, generative design, slicing and support generation.

objectives: This course focuses on the multidisciplinary scientific bases for climate change, paleo-climatic change and impact on communities. It also focuses on the legal and financial aspects of climate change, adaptation and mitigation.

outcomes.text: Explain the climate system and global circulation
Investigate climate projections from the past
Discuss global climate change policy and its implementation, mitigation & adaptations

Future trends and Impacts of Climate Change: Projected future trends and impacts of climate change on surface temperature, precipitation, ocean pH.

Global Ocean Circulation: Origin of the Gulf Stream, The Deep Atlantic Conveyor, El Niño and its Effects, Global ice sheet degradation.

Kyoto Protocol, Paris Agreement, COP Simulation, India’s role in climate change mitigation.

Role of non-governmental organizations and corporate initiatives, voluntary commitments and actions, disclosure-based initiatives, social cost of carbon, Short term and Long Term Mitigation

Identify and measure requirements of a smart city.
